suggestion.title: Salesforce bulk data export by non-admin user
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'breached 7-Eleven's Salesforce environment' and 'stolen over 600,000 records'—indicates systematic bulk export of franchisee documents. Detection should flag abnormal export operations outside normal franchise workflows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Salesforce audit logs for Data Export API calls, bulk record retrieval operations, or mass document downloads outside normal franchisee operation patterns. Flag exports >10k records in <1 hour or exports from service accounts/inactive accounts.

suggestion.title: Salesforce account access from anomalous location/time
suggestion.rationale: Breach accessed 'certain 7-Eleven systems used to store franchisee documents' on 'April 8, 2026'—suggests account compromise with atypical access patterns for franchisee account management.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Salesforce logins from IP ranges outside known 7-Eleven corporate networks, logins at unusual hours (e.g., 2-4am), or impossible travel (login from US IP then non-US within minutes). Correlate with subsequent bulk data access.

suggestion.title: Large sequential file/document access from Salesforce franchisee repository
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies '9.4GB archive of documents' stolen from franchisee storage—indicates attacker systematically enumerated and accessed document objects at scale. Normal franchise operations do not retrieve gigabytes of documents.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for high-volume sequential file ID or record ID access patterns in Salesforce content delivery logs. Flag accounts accessing >5k franchisee documents in <24h, or patterns of metadata access followed immediately by bulk retrieval.

suggestion.title: Salesforce API abuse for data enumeration and export
suggestion.rationale: ShinyHunters' ability to 'steal over 600,000 records' suggests programmatic API abuse using REST/SOAP endpoints to enumerate and export data at scale—typical of compromised service accounts or stolen OAuth tokens.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on repeated Salesforce REST/SOAP API calls from single authentication context querying large dataset sizes or using LIMIT/OFFSET patterns to iterate all records. Detect API requests downloading >100MB data or executing >1000 API calls/hour from single token/IP pair.

suggestion.title: Dark web leak site hosting correlation with exfiltration timeframe
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions attackers 'leaked a 9.4GB archive of documents on their dark web leak site'—attackers must move stolen data through infrastructure. Should correlate Tor traffic, darkweb hosting uploads, or onion domain activity during April 8-17 window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound traffic to known darkweb hosting providers or Tor exit nodes correlating with large data transfers (multi-gigabyte flows) from Salesforce staging servers. Alert on Tor browser activity on corporate systems during off-hours in conjunction with data access anomalies.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Attempts on Internet-Facing Applications
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'Internet-Facing Flaws' driving 12-hour patching urgency, indicating active exploitation campaigns. Title suggests exploitation is happening now.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor internet-facing web services for exploitation signature attempts: HTTP requests to known vulnerable endpoints with malformed parameters, unusual polyglot payloads, rapid scanning of multiple application paths, and responses indicating successful code execution or information disclosure.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Command Execution from Web Process
suggestion.rationale: 12-hour patching window implies exploitation is succeeding. Common next step after internet-facing app exploitation is shell command execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect spawning of cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or /bin/bash directly from web application worker processes (w3wp.exe, apache2, java, nginx). Alert on encoded command execution, environment variable manipulation, or network callbacks originating from web service processes.

suggestion.title: Patch Deployment Monitoring Against 12-Hour SLA
suggestion.rationale: Article phrase 'Recommends 12-Hour Patching' establishes a time-critical SLA. Without patch tracking, organizations cannot measure response adequacy.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track deployment status of patches for flagged internet-facing vulnerabilities. Alert when patches remain undeployed past the 12-hour window, and correlate deployment failures with attempted or successful exploitation activity on those systems.

suggestion.title: AI-Assisted Exploit Tool Activity Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly cites 'AI-Assisted Attacks' as driver. Pipeline must surface behavioral markers of LLM or AI-generated payloads, which differ from static malware signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for patterns consistent with AI-generated attack code: semantically coherent but syntactically unusual command payloads, high entropy in script content, rapid iteration between multiple exploitation techniques, or API calls to generative AI platforms from compromised endpoints.

suggestion.title: Rapid Vulnerability Assessment Scanning on Public Services
suggestion.rationale: AI-assisted attacks combined with active exploitation suggests attackers are rapidly identifying and testing internet-facing services. Scanner-like behavior should precede exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect reconnaissance-like patterns: single source IPs rapidly probing multiple endpoints, user-agents consistent with vulnerability scanners or headless browsers, requests testing common web service paths (/admin, /api, /.env), and temporal clustering of 40x responses followed by successful requests from same source.

suggestion.title: cPanel Plugin Exploitation Attempt — T1190 Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'exposed via the user-end cPanel plugin' + CISA KEV implies active wild exploitation. Pipeline must detect exploit attempts against public-facing plugin endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to cPanel plugin paths for exploitation signatures: encoded payloads, SQL injection patterns, path traversal, or suspicious parameter values. Correlate abnormal request patterns with error responses indicating failed or successful exploitation.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation from cPanel User to Root — T1548
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'any cPanel user account to execute arbitrary scripts with root privileges'—direct privilege-escalation attack step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process creation with UID 0 spawned from cPanel user context or cPanel plugin directories. Monitor for sudo/su invocation, token elevation, or capability abuse originating from non-root cPanel accounts or HTTP service processes.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary Script Execution with Root Privileges — T1059
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'execute arbitrary scripts with root privileges'—establishes code-execution phase. Pipeline failed to generate detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on shell/scripting interpreter (bash, sh, perl, python, php) execution with UID 0 when spawned by cPanel processes, plugin directories, or HTTP service accounts. Flag obfuscated command lines or non-standard script paths in elevated-privilege contexts.

suggestion.title: cPanel Plugin Directory File Modification
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation chain implies write access to plugin directories for payload persistence or staging. Article describes plugin-based attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor cPanel plugin directories for unauthorized file creation/modification outside maintenance windows. Detect writes from HTTP service accounts, cPanel user processes, or unexpected root processes to plugin installation paths.

suggestion.title: cPanel Service Process Spawning System Interpreters
suggestion.rationale: Attack narrative 'execute arbitrary scripts with root privileges' implies cPanel processes launching system binaries. No use case generated for this execution pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect cPanel-related processes (lswsapi, cpanel daemons, HTTP server children) spawning /bin/bash, /bin/sh, or interpreters with root privileges. Alert on unexpected child-process relationships between cPanel and system binaries.

suggestion.title: SQL Injection Payload Detection in Drupal HTTP Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'can be exploited without authentication, allowing attackers to trigger arbitrary SQL injection on PostgreSQL-powered sites via specially crafted requests.' No detection case addresses HTTP-level payload inspection for SQL injection syntax.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST/GET requests to Drupal endpoints for SQL injection signatures (UNION, SELECT, INSERT, DROP, ORDER BY, comment syntax --,/**/). Correlate with Drupal application error logs for SQL exceptions. Alert on statistically anomalous patterns or known-malicious payloads targeting database abstraction API.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Database Privilege Escalation from Drupal Service Account
suggestion.rationale: Article warns exploitation enables 'privilege escalation,' implying post-compromise database privilege abuse. No detection case addresses ALTER ROLE, GRANT, or CREATE ROLE abuse by Drupal service account.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag ALTER ROLE, CREATE ROLE, GRANT, REVOKE commands from Drupal database user or newly created suspicious database users. Monitor for privilege expansion (superuser, CREATEDB, CREATEROLE). Correlate timing with SQL injection attempt timestamps.

suggestion.title: Bulk Data Exfiltration from PostgreSQL Post-SQLi Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states successful exploitation leads to 'information disclosure.' SQL injection-based exfiltration manifests as high-volume queries returning large result sets; no detection addresses abnormal egress or query patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for outbound PostgreSQL traffic volume and query patterns. Alert on sustained byte-rate increases, unexpected destination IPs, or high-frequency SELECT queries returning large row counts post-injection.

suggestion.title: Drupal Vulnerability Patch Compliance and Vulnerable Version Inventory
suggestion.rationale: CISA mandated patch deployment by May 27 deadline. Article reports 'Shadowserver tracks nearly 670 unpatched Drupal installations exposed online.' Detection must track patch status and enforce compliance against deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Fingerprint Drupal core/module versions from HTTP Server headers, /CHANGELOG.txt, or X-Generator tags. Inventory against vulnerable version ranges. Alert on instances unpatched post-deadline or regression to vulnerable versions post-patching.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance-to-Exploitation Chain: Drupal Enumeration Followed by SQLi Attacks
suggestion.rationale: Article reports 15,000+ attacks across 6,000 sites, implying reconnaissance (version scanning) precedes exploitation. No detection case links enumeration attempts to subsequent SQL injection from same source.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate repeated requests to Drupal fingerprinting endpoints (CHANGELOG.txt, /admin, /user/login) from single IP within short windows, followed by SQL injection payloads from same source within hours. Alert on complete reconnaissance-to-exploitation sequences.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Creation via SQL Injection File Write (RCE Post-Exploitation)
suggestion.rationale: Article warns RCE is 'potential' outcome of successful exploitation. PostgreSQL INTO OUTFILE or similar mechanisms enable file writes to web-accessible directories. No detection case addresses web shell artifacts post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for new executable files (.php, .jsp, .aspx, .sh) created in /sites/files/ or other Drupal web-accessible paths post-SQL injection activity. Alert on HTTP requests executing newly created scripts, or shell processes spawned from Drupal/PHP processes.

suggestion.title: Path Traversal in XWiki ssx/jsx Resource Parameters
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes the attack: 'possible to get access and read configuration files by using URLs such as `http://localhost:8080/bin/ssx/Main/WebHome?resource=/../../WEB-INF/xwiki.cfg&minify=false`'. The ../ sequence in the resource parameter is the core exploitation vector; this must be detected at the HTTP layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to /bin/ssx/ or /bin/jsx/ endpoints where the 'resource' parameter contains ../ sequences or leading slashes (e.g., resource=/../../). Raise confidence if request returns HTTP 200 and targets sensitive paths like WEB-INF, .cfg, or .properties files.

suggestion.title: Configuration File Access via XWiki Traversal
suggestion.rationale: Article names the specific target: 'read configuration files' and explicitly mentions 'WEB-INF/xwiki.cfg'. This is a data exfiltration pattern, not just scanning; detection should track successful access to sensitive config locations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate path traversal patterns in ssx/jsx requests with HTTP 200 responses and response sizes that would indicate successful file retrieval. Look for resource parameter values resolving to WEB-INF, *.cfg, *.properties, xwiki.cfg, or other system configuration files.

suggestion.title: XWiki Version Enumeration via HTTP Headers
suggestion.rationale: Article lists precise vulnerable versions. Attackers will enumerate version strings before exploitation. Article does not describe version discovery, but pre-exploitation reconnaissance is standard and should be detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP responses from XWiki endpoints for version identifiers in Server, X-Powered-By, or X-XWiki-Version headers. Alert on versions matching CVE-2026-23734 vulnerable ranges, especially if followed within minutes by path traversal attempts.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated XWiki XAR Import REST Endpoint Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'POST /wikis/{wikiName} executes a XAR import without performing any authentication or authorization checks'—core attack vector requiring detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST requests to XWiki /wikis/{wikiName} endpoints from unauthenticated or external sources. Alert on HTTP 200-201 responses combined with XAR file upload markers in request body. Baseline legitimate administrative traffic to reduce false positives.

suggestion.title: XWiki Document Creation from Unauthenticated XAR Import
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability 'allow[s] an unauthenticated attacker to create or update documents in the target wiki'—detect successful exploitation execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk document creation and modification events coinciding with XAR import operations initiated from unauthenticated sessions. Detect patterns inconsistent with normal wiki maintenance (e.g., rapid large-scale imports from external IPs).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-33137 Vulnerable XWiki Version Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies patched versions (16.10.17, 17.4.9, 17.10.3, 18.0.1, 18.1.0-rc-1); unpatched versions represent direct asset exposure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Asset exposure hunt: query software inventory for XWiki instances running versions before 16.10.17, 17.0-17.4.8, 17.10.0-17.10.2, or 18.0.0-18.0.0. Prioritize internet-facing instances for remediation.

suggestion.title: Ghost CMS CVE-2026-26980 Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Hackers Exploit Ghost CMS CVE-2026-26980'—this is the initial attack vector, yet no exploitation detection use case was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP/HTTPS requests to Ghost CMS endpoints known to be vulnerable to CVE-2026-26980. Correlate with unusual POST requests to admin or API endpoints and track for responses indicating successful injection or RCE. Alert on exploitation signatures or known payload patterns associated with this CVE.

suggestion.title: ClickFix Malware Deployment and Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'ClickFix Malware' as the payload deployed to poison 700 websites, yet no malware-specific detection use case exists.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect ClickFix malware by file hash, process creation signatures, and registry modifications associated with malware initialization. Monitor for malicious script injection into web-server processes and unusual child process spawning from web-server contexts. Flag instances of malware family callbacks or network beaconing.

suggestion.title: Website Content Injection and Defacement Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'poisoning 700 websites'—a mass website defacement campaign—but no detection for unauthorized content modification or injection is present.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ghost CMS and web-server configuration files for unauthorized modifications. Detect changes to hosted HTML/JavaScript files outside normal deployment pipelines. Alert on unexpected inline scripts injected into page source or anomalous MIME types served from web roots. Correlate file-write events on web-server processes with subsequent HTTP responses containing malicious payloads.

suggestion.title: Detect Phishing Emails with MiniFast/MiniJunk Malware Attachments or URLs
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Phishing' as primary initial-access vector for MiniFast and MiniJunk V2 deployment. Pipeline produced zero use cases for phishing-based malware delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag inbound emails with attachments matching known MiniFast/MiniJunk signatures (file hash, YARA rules, PE metadata) or URLs pointing to known distribution domains. Correlate with subsequent process execution to track infection chain.

suggestion.title: Detect SEO Poisoning Campaign Redirection to Malware Landing Pages
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'SEO Poisoning' as second delivery mechanism. Pipeline extracted no detection logic for this technique despite it being core to the attack narrative.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web proxy or firewall logs for traffic to adversary-controlled domains injected into search results via SEO poisoning. Baseline legitimate search-result click patterns and flag anomalous redirects to malware delivery sites, especially if followed by suspicious file downloads.

suggestion.title: Detect MiniFast/MiniJunk V2 Process Execution and Behavioral Artifacts
suggestion.rationale: No execution-phase detection use case generated. Article identifies two specific malware families; pipeline should propose post-compromise detection on process creation, DLL injection, C2 communication, or registry persistence patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process creation events matching MiniFast/MiniJunk V2 signatures (parent-child relationships, command-line obfuscation, unsigned executables from suspicious paths). Flag DLL injection or inline code execution patterns typical of these malware families.

suggestion.title: Detect Persistence Mechanisms Used by MiniJunk V2
suggestion.rationale: MiniJunk V2 name suggests a newer variant; article likely describes persistence/C2 updates. No persistence-phase use case generated despite malware persistence being a core defensive concern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor registry additions under Run/RunOnce keys, scheduled tasks, or startup folders for MiniFast/MiniJunk executables. Flag suspicious file writes to Windows system directories or %APPDATA% paths matching known malware naming conventions.

suggestion.title: ASP.NET ViewState Deserialization with Stolen Machine Key
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes: 'threat actors obtained the machine key and used it in ViewState deserialization attacks to sign malicious ViewState payloads and achieve remote code execution.' Core attack vector is ViewState parameter tampering using pre-shared hardcoded key.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ASP.NET application logs for ViewState parameters with signature validation failures or unusual entropy. Flag POST requests to .aspx handlers where ViewState MAC validation fails or succeeds with unexpected key material. Baseline legitimate ViewState patterns and alert on deserialization errors preceded by RCE-indicative process spawning.

suggestion.title: Godzilla Web Shell In-Memory Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'deployed the .NET-based in-memory web shell, Godzilla (a.k.a. BlueBeam)' following successful RCE. Godzilla is a known .NET web shell that operates without touching disk, making file-based detection ineffective.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious .NET runtime assembly loading in IIS worker processes (w3wp.exe) with unusual import patterns. Detect anomalous HTTP request handling from iis processes that invoke PowerShell or cmd.exe without corresponding legitimate application behavior. Flag CLR assembly reflective loading into running IIS processes.

suggestion.title: Malicious Installer Download via Social Engineering Prompt
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'convinced users to download a fake installer' embedded in a legitimate KnowledgeDeliver application, resulting in Cobalt Strike beacon installation. Attack vector is JavaScript modification within the application.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect executable downloads (exe, msi, zip containing exe) from KnowledgeDeliver web server to client machines, especially when preceded by unusual JavaScript execution or browser security prompts. Correlate with Cobalt Strike beacon signatures and network C2 patterns post-download.

suggestion.title: Application Web.Config Hardcoded Machine Key Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'KnowledgeDeliver installations deployed before Feb. 24, 2026 relied on a standardized web.config file provided by the vendor. This configuration file contained hardcoded machineKey values.' Default/shared keys enable ViewState forgery at scale.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web.config file reads and writes for presence of hardcoded machineKey elements. Flag configurations where machineKey validationKey or decryptionKey matches known shared/default values from vendor templates. Correlate with deployments of KnowledgeDeliver versions pre-2026-02-24.

suggestion.title: Legitimate Application JavaScript File Injection for C2/Malware Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'executed commands to escalate their control over the web server's file system. This allowed them to modify an application JavaScript file with code that prompted users to install a "security authentication plugin" and to load a malicious script from a domain under the attacker's control.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Implement file integrity monitoring on application JavaScript assets (.js files) in web root directories. Alert on unexpected modifications, additions, or timestamp changes outside scheduled deployments. Monitor for injection of new script includes pointing to external domains in legitimate application JavaScript files.

suggestion.title: Cobalt Strike Beacon Installation from Fake Installer
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'The payload was encrypted using a key that used the name of the compromised organization, which indicated that the threat actor prepared this payload specifically for the targeted organization' and this payload 'led to the machine getting infected with a Cobalt Strike beacon, essentially planting a backdoor.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Cobalt Strike beacon behavioral signatures: injected rundll32 or svchost processes, HTTP POST beaconing to external C2 servers with typical beacon callbacks, memory patterns matching Cobalt Strike object files. Cross-reference with timeline of fake installer execution to establish infection chain.

suggestion.title: Exploit of KnowledgeDeliver LMS Vulnerability
suggestion.rationale: Article title establishes active exploitation of a named LMS product flaw. Pipeline extracted zero kill-chain phases despite this being the entry vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound HTTP requests to KnowledgeDeliver endpoints (identify vulnerable versions via version strings in responses or request patterns). Look for POST requests to known vulnerable paths with high encoding entropy or script payloads. Correlate with process creation on the server immediately following successful requests.

suggestion.title: Godzilla Webshell Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article names Godzilla as deployed payload. No use case generated for webshell execution despite this being explicit attack payload mentioned in title.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Godzilla is a C# webshell. Detect via command line signatures (encoding of C# runtime invocations, suspicious CLR invocation chains). Look for suspicious child processes spawned from w3wp.exe or IIS worker processes. Monitor for PowerShell invocations with encoding/obfuscation patterns typical of webshell post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: Cobalt Strike Beacon Command & Control
suggestion.rationale: Article names Cobalt Strike as secondary payload. No detection rule for beacon traffic or process indicators generated despite this being a well-known C2 framework with established IOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound HTTPS connections with unusual JA3 fingerprints matching Cobalt Strike defaults, or analyze SSL certificate anomalies. Detect DNS queries to malicious domains known to serve Cobalt Strike. Monitor for rundll32/regsvcs/regasm child process chains and suspicious memory allocation patterns consistent with Cobalt Strike loader.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Privilege Escalation from Webshell
suggestion.rationale: Webshell → Cobalt Strike implies post-exploitation privilege escalation; article does not detail but is implicit in attack progression. Pipeline should infer multi-stage attack scenarios.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for scheduled task creation via at.exe, schtasks.exe, or registry modifications from SYSTEM context spawned by w3wp.exe or child processes. Detect UAC bypass attempts (fodhelper, eventvwr, etc.) originating from non-standard processes.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from KnowledgeDeliver LMS Server
suggestion.rationale: Multi-stage payload deployment suggests lateral movement post-compromise. Article mentions both Godzilla and Cobalt Strike, implying further infrastructure compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for SMB/RDP connections from the compromised KnowledgeDeliver server to internal targets. Detect lateral movement via webshell: look for port scans, credential dumping (lsass.exe, registry SAM reads), or lateral tool transfer (e.g., PsExec, WMI calls) originating from web server processes or their children.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Child Process Spawning from IIS Worker Process
suggestion.rationale: Webshell exploitation inherently results in command execution from w3wp.exe. This is a high-fidelity, low-noise indicator the pipeline should have surfaced from title alone.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any process creation where parent is w3wp.exe (IIS) and child is cmd.exe, powershell.exe, rundll32.exe, or regsvcs.exe, or where the command line contains encoded content or script interpreters. Cobalt Strike and Godzilla both commonly invoke these binaries for post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: High-Frequency MFA Push Notifications to Single User
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'repeated push-based MFA requests' and attacker 'repeatedly triggers push notifications'—the core attack vector. Pipeline missed pattern for detecting bombing in progress.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when a single user receives >5 MFA push notifications within 5 minutes, especially if originating from a single source IP. Correlate with failed authentication attempts from that IP immediately prior. High urgency if user is privileged or has sensitive access.

suggestion.title: Authentication Success After Repeated MFA Denials
suggestion.rationale: Article notes user eventually 'approves one request, allowing the attacker to complete the authentication process'—indicates success after repeated rejections, distinguishing this from legitimate retry behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag sign-in events where the same account shows 3+ MFA prompt denials (user explicitly rejected) followed by successful MFA approval within 15 minutes, especially from the same or similar source IP. Correlate with unusual geolocation/device.

suggestion.title: Atypical Login + Immediate High-Volume MFA Push Sequence
suggestion.rationale: Attack pattern described as: attacker obtains credentials, then initiates login and 'repeatedly pushes notifications.' This two-stage sequence is distinctive from legitimate access patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate failed login from unusual IP/geolocation with subsequent MFA push notification storm to the same account within 2 minutes. Baseline per-user and organization and alert on deviation. Cross-reference user activity (was user actively working at that time?).

suggestion.title: Out-of-Band MFA Approval from Mismatched Device/Geolocation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attacker exploiting lack of visibility: 'users are asked to approve with very little to go on. There's no clear indication of where the request originated, what device is being used.' Detection should flag approval-from-different-device patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when MFA approval occurs from a device or geolocation inconsistent with the originating login attempt IP and the user's historical device roster. Example: user is in New York, login attempt from Russia, MFA approved from unregistered iOS device in Russia—likely attacker.

suggestion.title: Repeated Failed Login Attempts Across Multiple Accounts from Single Source
suggestion.rationale: MFA bombing often targets multiple users; article notes 'bombard users' (plural). Pipeline should detect orchestrated attempts across organizational users from single attacker IP.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag source IP that initiates >10 failed authentication attempts across 5+ different user accounts within 30 minutes. Especially urgent if followed by successful authentication on any of those accounts. Suggests credential stuffing or bombing campaign.

suggestion.title: Push-Based MFA Approval Without Preceding User Interaction
suggestion.rationale: Article points out vulnerability: user cannot see login context. Detection should flag MFA approvals that lack corroborating user activity—user did not actually request the login.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: When push-based MFA (e.g., Authenticator app) is approved, correlate against user's application/device activity in the same timeframe. Flag approvals where user has zero click/app activity on the authenticating device in prior 10 minutes—suggests user blind-approved fatigue attack.

suggestion.title: Defender Automatic Device Isolation Triggered
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'When a device in your organization is suspected to be compromised, Microsoft Defender for Endpoint can automatically isolate the device.' Isolation is itself a detection event signaling compromise. No UC captures correlation of isolation with preceding suspicious indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when automatic isolation event occurs; correlate backward 2 hours for anomalous process execution (unsigned binaries, LOLBins), unusual outbound network connections (non-RFC1918 targets, high ports), or suspicious logon patterns. Establish compromise timeline from first indicator to isolation.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Indicators Preceding Device Isolation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Automatic isolation helps...limit attacker lateral movement.' Implies Defender detects lateral movement vectors before isolation. No UC captures reconnaissance or lateral movement techniques that trigger the isolation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for lateral movement precursors on subsequently-isolated devices within 1 hour prior: SMB reconnaissance, WMI queries, scheduled task creation, service enumeration, or port scanning activity.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration Vectors Preceding Isolation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states isolation prevents 'impacts such as data exfiltration and ransomware propagation.' Detection of exfiltration indicators must precede isolation. No UC addresses the initial exfiltration detection pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate bulk file access (sensitive document folders, database paths) with outbound connections to non-standard ports/IPs on devices isolated within 30 minutes. Flag connection to cloud storage APIs or unusual SMTP/HTTPS destinations during data staging activity.

suggestion.title: Account Isolation Activity Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'revealed that Defender for Endpoint could also isolate compromised user accounts as part of automatic attack disruption.' No UC for detecting account isolation events or the credential compromise patterns that precede them.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for rapid account lockouts across multiple devices, failed authentication spikes on single credentials, or logon attempts from geographically dispersed IPs. Correlate with Defender account isolation events to confirm compromise.

suggestion.title: Bulk File Encryption Activity - Ransomware Encryption Phase
suggestion.rationale: Article title directly states purpose is to 'Stop Ransomware' but pipeline generated zero use cases for detecting the encryption behavior that defines ransomware attacks; 'To Stop Ransomware' establishes encryption as the primary threat.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect high-velocity file writes with suspicious extensions (.crypt, .locked, .encrypted, etc.) or bulk file modifications across multiple directories in short timeframes. Correlate with parent process execution (Office apps, explorer.exe, etc.) and elevated I/O patterns indicative of encryption routines.

suggestion.title: Device Isolation Event Detection - Automatic Quarantine Response
suggestion.rationale: Article core claim is 'Automatically Isolates Compromised Devices'—this is the primary detection need—yet pipeline generated no use case for monitoring isolation events, network state changes, or quarantine triggers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abrupt network connectivity loss, domain membership changes, or Microsoft Defender quarantine/isolation action events. Correlate isolation timestamp with preceding suspicious process or file activity to confirm remediation response to actual compromise vs. false positive.

suggestion.title: Ransomware Process Execution Pattern - Pre-Encryption Behavior
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'Compromised Devices' but provides no detection logic for the execution-phase behaviors (script execution, process injection, lateral movement) that precede encryption and trigger isolation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unexpected script interpreter activity (powershell.exe, wscript.exe, vbscript.exe) spawning from non-standard parents, unsigned DLL loads, or service/scheduled task creation patterns associated with ransomware delivery. Establish baseline for typical Office/system process behavior per environment.

suggestion.title: System Shutdown/Reboot Preceding Ransomware Encryption
suggestion.rationale: Many ransomware variants (LockBit, REvil) use system shutdown commands to interrupt backups and services; article's 'compromised' context suggests these behavioral indicators should be detected before isolation occurs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect shutdown.exe or wmic commands with /t flag (delayed shutdown) or restart commands issued by non-standard parents. Correlate with preceding suspicious process chains and file activity; ransomware often issues these commands to disable backup solutions and Volume Shadow Copy.

suggestion.title: DLL Side-Loading via Legitimate Application Proxy
suggestion.rationale: Article title names 'DLL Side-Loading' as the core attack method. No execution-phase UC was generated to detect legitimate executables loading malicious DLLs from non-standard paths—the signature attack pattern for MuddyWater's technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect image-load events where a legitimate, signed Windows executable (rundll32.exe, msiexec.exe, regsvcs.exe, etc.) loads an unsigned or anomalously-signed DLL from writable paths (AppData, Temp, Downloads) or relative paths. Flag when DLL load precedes primary thread execution, indicating pre-loading/hijacking.

suggestion.title: Registry Run-Key Persistence by Non-System Processes
suggestion.rationale: MuddyWater campaigns require sustained presence across 9 countries. Persistence via registry Run keys is standard for this actor but generated zero phase mapping. No persistence UC was created.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor writes to HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run or HKCU equivalents by non-system processes. Alert on registry values pointing to AppData, Temp, or unsigned executables, or where written executable doesn't exist at time of write event.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Chain: Office Macro → Cmd → DLL Load
suggestion.rationale: Espionage campaigns typically chain initial access (phishing) through execution and lateral tooling. Pipeline produced no initial-access or chain-linkage UC; no spear-phishing → code execution detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Office processes (winword.exe, excel.exe) spawning cmd.exe or powershell.exe, or Office processes writing executables to disk. Chain detection: Office parent → unsigned child → DLL load from AppData. Flag macro/OLE execution anomalies.

suggestion.title: MuddyWater C2 Communication Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Espionage campaign requires command-and-control. No network-based UC or command-and-control phase was extracted. Expected: detection of beaconing to attributed MuddyWater infrastructure or anomalous HTTP patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound HTTP/HTTPS POST requests from non-browser processes to known MuddyWater C2 domains or IPs. Flag requests with encoded/binary payloads, non-standard user agents, or connections from processes typically sandboxed (svchost, rundll32, regsvcs). Correlate with DLL load events.

suggestion.title: Living-off-the-Land Enumeration: tasklist + Registry Query Sequence
suggestion.rationale: Post-compromise reconnaissance is fundamental to espionage; MuddyWater uses built-in tools for discovery. No discovery-phase UC generated despite explicit campaign scope (9 countries = multi-environment reconnaissance).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid sequential execution of tasklist.exe, Get-Process, reg.exe, wmic.exe, or dir commands within a short window (< 5 min) from cmd.exe or PowerShell. Alert especially if parent is unusual (svchost, rundll32, services.exe, or recently-dropped executable).

suggestion.title: Unsigned Binary Execution from User-Writable Paths
suggestion.rationale: DLL side-loading requires unsigned/rogue binaries in accessible directories. No defense-evasion or unsigned-execution UC created. Article implies malware distribution but zero masquerading/obfuscation detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process execution from AppData, Temp, Downloads, or $Recycle.Bin where the executable is unsigned or signed by unknown issuer. Correlate with parent process being legitimate Windows binary. Flag if executed binary was written < 1 hour before execution.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Angular Language Service Extension Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'Multiple Angular Language Service Extension Vulnerabilities.' Pipeline missed detection for malicious or unexpected extension installation—fundamental initial-access control for this threat.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected installation or registration of Angular Language Service extensions via npm, VSCode marketplace, or direct filesystem writes to extension directories. Monitor extension installation processes for unusual parent-child relationships and registry activity.

suggestion.title: RCE Execution via Angular Extension Spawning Child Processes
suggestion.rationale: Article title states vulnerabilities 'Enable RCE Attacks.' Pipeline failed to suggest core execution-phase detection for suspicious child processes spawned from Angular Language Service context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process creation with parent VSCode, node.exe, or Angular Language Service spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, rundll32.exe, or wmic.exe. Alert on unusual process trees originating from extension code execution context.

suggestion.title: Registry Persistence from RCE Payload
suggestion.rationale: RCE vulnerabilities in developer tooling commonly achieve persistence via HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\Run or RunOnce. Article describes RCE capability but pipeline missed registry-based persistence use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect modifications to HKCU/HKLM Windows\Run and RunOnce registry keys originating from Angular extension processes or their RCE children. Alert on unexpected value writes from developer tool context.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Network Connections from Angular Extension Processes
suggestion.rationale: RCE-compromised extensions establish C2 communication or data exfiltration. Article describes RCE vulnerabilities but pipeline failed to surface network-based detection for outbound activity from compromised tooling.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected outbound connections (particularly non-standard ports or external IPs without business justification) from VSCode, node.exe, or Angular extension processes. Correlate with external threat intelligence feeds.

suggestion.title: Encoded PowerShell Spawned from Developer Tool Processes
suggestion.rationale: Common RCE exploitation signature in developer tooling vulnerabilities: base64-encoded command execution. Article describes RCE but pipeline missed this canonical execution pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect VSCode or node.exe spawning powershell.exe with suspicious arguments containing '-enc', '-EncodedCommand', or other obfuscation indicators. Flag base64 payloads and unusual parameter concatenation.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Operations in VSCode Extension Directories
suggestion.rationale: RCE exploitation of extension vulnerabilities often involves writing or modifying files in extension storage (.vscode\extensions\). Article describes vulnerabilities enabling attacks but pipeline did not suggest file-based detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected file creation or modification in %USERPROFILE%\.vscode\extensions\angular* directories. Alert on creation of executable, script, or suspicious binary files post-installation.

suggestion.title: Detect RDP Logon from External IP with Rapid Credential Validation
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly: 'Uses RDP Access... for Stealthy Persistence.' RDP is the entry vector; no detection UC created despite this being the primary attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag RDP logons (EventID 4624, LogonType 3 or 10) from external-facing IP addresses, especially from ASNs or geolocations not in historical baseline. Correlate successful logon within seconds of failed attempts and pivot to account compromise if reused for lateral movement.

suggestion.title: Remote Admin Tool Installation and Auto-Start Registry Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Remote Admin Tools for Stealthy Persistence.' Pipeline generated no UC for detection of tool installation (TeamViewer, AnyDesk, RustDesk, ConnectWise, etc.) or persistence registry hooks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of known remote-access software binaries and suspicious parent-child relationships (e.g., explorer.exe or svchost.exe launching TeamViewer). Flag registry writes to HKCU/HKLM CurrentVersion\Run, RunOnce, or Startup folders originating from remote RDP sessions or temp directories.

suggestion.title: Mass File Encryption or Ransom Note Artifact Creation Post-Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article is about NightSpire Ransomware; once persistence established via RDP + admin tools, malware executes encryption. No impact-phase detection UC exists for file encryption patterns or ransom note creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for rapid file system churn with suspicious parent processes (RDP session, remote tool child). Flag creation of files matching ransom-note patterns (readme.txt, readme.html, *.encrypted, *.locked). Correlate with process deletion of Volume Shadow Copies (vssadmin delete shadows).

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via RDP between Internal Hosts from Compromised Asset
suggestion.rationale: Once attacker achieves persistence on initial RDP entry, next step is internal pivot using RDP. Title does not explicitly state lateral RDP, but is implicit in 'stealthy persistence' strategy; pipeline missed detection opportunity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound RDP connections (port 3389) initiated from asset that recently accepted external RDP session. Flag RDP scans (sequential port 3389 attempts) or rapid successful RDP logons to server/high-value targets from interactive RDP session user account.

suggestion.title: Remote Admin Tool Establishing Unusual Outbound Network Connections
suggestion.rationale: Remote tools often tunnel C2 or data exfil through their encrypted channels. Article mentions tools but pipeline did not generate UC for anomalous network traffic from tool processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for network connections initiated by remote-tool processes (TeamViewer, AnyDesk, etc.) to IPs not in org whitelist. Flag high entropy or binary payloads exfiltrated over tool channels. Correlate suspicious file operations preceding tool network connections.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via LSASS Dump or Credential Manager Access Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Attacker establishing persistence via RDP typically harvests admin credentials next to sustain access. Article title implies attacker maintains control; credential theft is logical next step not detected by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious process creation (mimikatz, laZagne, procdump, sekurlsa module) or direct LSASS access (OpenProcess with PROCESS_VM_READ flag) originating from RDP session. Flag credential manager vaults accessed or dumped to disk.

suggestion.title: eBPF Module Load from Suspicious Path
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'eBPF Rootkit' as persistence mechanism. No detection rule exists to catch kernel module loading—neither from bpf() syscalls nor from /sys/kernel/debug/tracing paths commonly exploited for rootkit install.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bpf() system calls with BPF_PROG_LOAD or bpffs mounts from non-standard binaries. Alert on exec of tools like bpftool or clang generating/loading eBPF bytecode outside development directories. Watch /sys/kernel/debug/tracing writes from unprivileged or unexpected processes.

suggestion.title: Fileless Execution via Memory-Resident Payload Decode
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Fileless Execution' as primary evasion mechanism. No use case captures in-memory code injection, base64/hex decode-and-exec chains, or process hollowing typical of fileless RATs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect shell processes spawned without parent command line, or bash/sh invoked with pipe-delimited payload strings. Look for sequences: curl/wget → base64 -d → bash/python. Alert on /proc/self/mem writes or ptrace abuse indicating process injection.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Network Egress from Developer-Tier Hosts
suggestion.rationale: Article targets 'Developers' as explicit victim class. RATs require command-and-control; no use case filters for C2 beacons from IDE processes, git clients, or development tool suites common in developer workstations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate outbound connections from VS Code, JetBrains IDEs, Python, Node.js, or git processes to non-whitelisted ports/IPs. Alert on DNS queries for fast-flux or newly registered domains from development tool processes. Flag TLS certificates with mismatched SNI.

suggestion.title: Kernel Logging Disabled or Syscall Tracing Suppressed
suggestion.rationale: eBPF rootkit inherently performs syscall-level hooking and hiding. Article implies kernel-level evasion but no detection for disabled auditd, blocked perf events, or syscall filter circumvention.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for attempts to unload audit modules, disable perf_event LSM rules, or modify bpf_raw_tracepoint permissions. Detect exec of auditctl with -W rules deleting sensitive syscall tracing. Alert on /proc/sys/kernel/perf_event_paranoid modifications.

suggestion.title: Supply-Chain Compromise or Trojanized Developer Tools
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'Targets Developers' as attack vector; most likely delivery via compromised package manager, IDE plugin, or dev tool. No use case addresses supply-chain or tool-staging detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unsigned or revoked code-signing certificates on developer binaries. Detect out-of-band writes to ~/.vscode/extensions, ~/.local/share/applications, or ~/.bashrc/.zshrc immediately following package installs. Flag hash mismatches on version-pinned tool downloads.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation to Root via eBPF Exploit
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions eBPF rootkit, implying initial access is unprivileged and escalation occurs post-exploit. No detection for privilege escalation indicators specific to eBPF vulnerabilities or kernel exploits.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect setuid/setgid calls from non-standard processes or capability grants (cap_sys_admin, cap_perfmon) on unexpected binaries. Monitor for failed bpf() syscalls followed by successful privilege escalation. Alert on root-level process spawning from unprivileged parent with eBPF-linked ancestry.

suggestion.title: Volumetric DDoS Attack Detected - UDP/ICMP Flood
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly references 'New AI DDoS Attacks.' DDoS is inherently an impact-phase attack using high-volume traffic. No detection rules produced for flood-based attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ingress traffic for sustained anomalies in packet rates, protocol distribution, or source diversity. Correlate sudden spikes in UDP/ICMP/DNS traffic against baseline traffic profiles. Flag traffic patterns consistent with amplification attacks (small requests generating large responses).

suggestion.title: DDoS Botnet C2 Communication Patterns
suggestion.rationale: AI-driven DDoS suggests command-and-control infrastructure. Title mentions 'smarter' attacks implying coordination. No C2 detection use cases generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify C2 beacons using entropy analysis on DNS queries or HTTP User-Agents. Monitor for periodic check-ins from compromised systems at regular intervals. Detect suspicious domain names with high-entropy or algorithmically-generated characteristics typical of botnet controllers.

suggestion.title: Target Reconnaissance for DDoS Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: AI DDoS requires pre-attack enumeration of targets and their network topology. No reconnaissance-phase detection present despite implicit threat lifecycle.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for port scanning activity, OS fingerprinting attempts, or service enumeration targeting internal or external infrastructure. Flag ASN lookups, WHOIS queries, or shodan/censys-like reconnaissance patterns from external sources.

suggestion.title: Persistence of DDoS Bot Malware
suggestion.rationale: DDoS attacks imply malware deployment on compromised systems. Article title suggests 'smarter' attacks, implying persistent bots. No malware persistence rules generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious process execution at startup, scheduled task creation, or cron job additions. Detect unsigned binaries placed in auto-start locations or malware communicating to known botnet C2 infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Package Manager Installation from Developer Environment
suggestion.rationale: Article premise: 'developer machines are now the number one target for supply chain attacks'—should detect npm/pip/Maven installing unvetted or newly-registered packages from developer workstations, the direct vector for poisoning upstream consumers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package manager processes (npm install, pip install, mvn dependency:resolve) for installation from non-standard repositories, unsigned packages, or domains with low DNS reputation. Correlate with developer IDE window inactivity or off-hours execution.

suggestion.title: Developer Machine Credential Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks pivot through stolen developer credentials (SSH keys, API tokens, .env files); article's framing of developer machines as attack targets implies credential compromise as leverage point for downstream repo/artifact access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on non-IDE processes reading ~/.ssh/id_rsa, ~/.aws/credentials, .git/config, .env files, or password manager databases. Establish baseline of tools permitted to access credentials; flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Unsigned/Anomalous Build Artifact Propagation from Developer Machine
suggestion.rationale: Compromised developer = poisoned builds; article's supply chain attack narrative implies malicious code injection at source; should detect commits with broken signature chains, binaries committed with unexpected hashes, or artifacts with modified metadata.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor git commit creation for unsigned commits or commits bypassing branch protection. Cross-reference binary artifact hashes against source tree commit hashes; alert on mismatches or absence of signatures.

suggestion.title: Developer Machine Source Code and Dependency Manifest Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Compromised machines used for reconnaissance: attackers read package.json, pom.xml, Dockerfile, CI/CD configs to understand downstream consumers and attack surface—core reconnaissance step in multi-stage supply chain attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect archiving/exfiltration of source trees (tar, zip from non-standard locations). Alert on bulk reads of dependency manifests, Dockerfile, kubernetes configs, or CI/CD pipeline definitions by non-developer processes.

suggestion.title: Developer Machine Lateral Movement to Build Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Developer machine as pivot point: attackers move from compromised workstation to shared CI/CD systems, artifact repositories, and upstream build servers to amplify attack scope—represents progression from initial compromise to infrastructure-level persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on RDP/SSH from developer machines to CI/CD infrastructure (Jenkins, GitLab, build servers) outside business hours or with non-standard credentials. Monitor artifact repository uploads (npm, Docker Hub, Artifactory) from developer IPs.

suggestion.title: Package Manager Hook Persistence Installation
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks plant hooks in npm preinstall, pip setup.py, or Maven plugins on developer machines to maintain access and propagate malware through every downstream build; should detect suspicious script execution from package install directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor execution of arbitrary scripts from node_modules/.bin, site-packages, or .m2/repository directories. Alert on scheduled tasks or cron entries created during package installation. Detect modification of npmrc, pip.conf, or Maven settings.xml to add malicious registries.

suggestion.title: Domain Controller Startup Failure - Hostname Configuration
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Domain Controller May Fail with 15-Character Hostname' directly indicates availability impact. Pipeline should have flagged DC initialization failures as impact indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Windows Event ID 1000 (System Error) and 2089 (NTDS initialization failure) on Domain Controllers. Correlate with hostname length ≥15 characters in Active Directory. Alert on repeated DC startup failures within 24 hours post-hostname modification.

suggestion.title: Active Directory Replication Failure - DC Configuration Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates DC failure condition; replication breakdown is a direct consequence. Monitor for inter-DC replication failures as secondary availability indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Event ID 1311 (replication failure) or 1864 (replication topology update failure). If correlated with 15-character hostname DCs or recent hostname changes, escalate to AD configuration audit.

suggestion.title: Hostname Configuration Audit on Domain Controllers
suggestion.rationale: Article implies hostname length is a configuration risk factor. Create proactive monitoring for non-compliant DC hostnames.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory all Domain Controllers; flag those with hostnames ≥15 characters. Monitor for hostname modifications via WMI, registry (HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\Tcpip\Parameters), or AD attribute changes. Alert on any change to DC hostname that triggers replication or startup failures.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email Directing to Microsoft Device Code Portal
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'phishing emails that directed victims to Microsoft's device code login portal, where they unknowingly authorized attackers to access their accounts.' Explicit entry vector. Email gateways should filter messages containing device code login references or microsoft.com/devicelogin links combined with social engineering urgency.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag phishing emails linking to microsoft.com/devicelogin or containing device code authorization language (particularly fake urgency, spoofed sender, bulk distribution to external orgs). Correlate email recipients against Entra signin logs; alert if recipient device-code-authenticates within 1 hour of email click.

suggestion.title: Device Code OAuth Flow Initiated by Non-Device Entity
suggestion.rationale: Article describes abuse of OAuth Device Authorization 'created to allow devices with limited input capabilities, such as smart TVs, conference room systems, streaming devices, printers, and IoT devices.' Attackers weaponized it for human-account phishing. Detect when device code flows originate from user accounts, not literal IoT/streaming devices.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on device code authorization requests (OAuthFlowType=DeviceCode, ResourceClientId=device-auth) initiated by interactive user principal, especially if correlated with prior phishing email and followed by immediate token refresh without re-authentication or MFA re-challenge.

suggestion.title: Inbox Rule Creation by Compromised Account Post-Device-Code Theft
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attackers also... created malicious inbox rules designed to hide their activity.' Occurs post-token-capture. Rules hide attacker inbox presence and exfiltration activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbox rules created within 24 hours of suspicious device code OAuth flow by same user. Flag rules with deletion/move actions, broad matching conditions (e.g., 'all mail from domain'), or rules forwarding to external addresses. Correlate with non-standard client (not Outlook, Teams web).

suggestion.title: Device Registration by User with Prior Token Theft
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attackers also registered new devices in victims' Microsoft environments, further extending their access to the breached network.' Device registration (Intune/Entra join) is secondary persistence after token capture.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on new device registrations by user principal with prior suspicious device code OAuth activity within same session. Flag registrations from foreign IP ranges, non-corporate MAC addresses, or unexpected OS/device-type. Cross-correlate registration timestamp with phishing email time window and token exfiltration events.

suggestion.title: Session Cookie and OAuth Token Capture via Adversary-in-the-Middle (Cookie Link Mode)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Cookie Link proxies victims through attacker-controlled infrastructure that captures authenticated browser sessions, session cookies, and tokens after targets log in and solves MFA challenges.' Second attack mode: transparent AitM proxy post-phishing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect signin events with anomalous properties: successful MFA completion followed within seconds by token refresh from mismatched client/IP; signin from VPN/proxy range used historically for phishing infrastructure; or Conditional Access policies unexpectedly bypassed on user account. Monitor for HTTPS certificate pinning bypass or certificate mismatch on Microsoft auth domains in proxy traffic.

suggestion.title: OAuth Token Usage Without Corresponding Interactive Signin
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Once the victim enters the code and completes MFA, Microsoft issues an OAuth access token that grants the threat actor full access to their account without requiring them to solve any MFA challenges.' Attacker obtains token bypassing future MFA.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify OAuth refresh token or bearer-token usage from non-standard clients (not Outlook, Teams, Teams PWA, OneDrive) or from IP addresses that have not logged in interactively with user. Alert if mailbox access, rule creation, or data export occurs via token without matching interactive signin from same IP. Flag token usage immediately after MFA-challenged device code flow.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-26980 Ghost CMS Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names CVE-2026-26980 as the attack vector against Ghost CMS; no IOC extraction or technique mapping occurred despite clear vulnerability identifier and exploitation scale (700+ sites).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Ghost CMS instances for payloads matching known CVE-2026-26980 exploitation patterns. Flag requests with malformed parameters to authentication endpoints, admin API paths, or theme-upload handlers; correlate timing and source IP against public exploit releases.

suggestion.title: Ghost CMS Admin Panel Unauthorized Access Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states sites were 'hijacked,' implying persistent admin-level control post-CVE exploitation; no detection for unauthorized privilege escalation or token creation in compromised CMS.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Ghost CMS admin logins from IP ranges not associated with site owner(s), especially within 48 hours of known exploit activity. Flag creation of new admin users, API tokens, or privilege escalations by compromised accounts; monitor for bulk content/theme modifications.

suggestion.title: ClickFix Malicious Payload Injection on Hijacked Pages
suggestion.rationale: Attack explicitly leverages ClickFix—a scam overlay delivering fake system alerts to end users; no detection for injected malicious content, redirects, or client-side payloads on affected sites.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect injected <script>, <iframe>, or CSS elements on Ghost CMS pages serving ClickFix-characteristic content: fake browser warnings, system alerts claiming infection, buttons linking to external tech-support sites. Signature: obfuscated JS, DOM manipulation hiding elements until user interaction, or time-delayed popups.

suggestion.title: Ghost CMS Theme/Plugin Persistence Installation
suggestion.rationale: Site 'hijacking' implies ongoing control mechanism; attacker likely deployed malicious theme or plugin for persistence and ClickFix payload injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ghost CMS theme and plugin directories for: unsigned or untrusted uploads; timestamps coinciding with CVE-2026-26980 exploitation; modifications to active theme files without corresponding admin action in audit logs; plugins executing external HTTP calls to non-Ghost domains.

suggestion.title: Mass Scanning for Ghost CMS Instances Pre-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Attack scale (700+ sites) suggests reconnaissance phase targeting Ghost installations before selective exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate high-volume HTTP requests querying Ghost version endpoints, admin paths (/ghost, /admin), or known vulnerable endpoints across large IP space within narrow time window. Look for identical User-Agent, request sequences, or payload patterns; flag DNS queries for ghost.io subdomains or .ghost domains in bulk.

suggestion.title: ClickFix Traffic Pattern - Compromised Site Redirects to Scam Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: ClickFix scams require egress to attacker-controlled tech-support or malware-delivery domains; no detection for abnormal outbound traffic from hijacked sites.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound HTTP/HTTPS connections from Ghost CMS servers to known ClickFix C2 or scam-support domains; monitor for large volumes of client-side requests to external tech-support sites originating from hijacked domain IPs; correlate domain registration age, SSL certificate issuer, and ASN reputation with known scam infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Memory-Only Malware Process Injection Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes RemotePE as 'memory-only RAT'—payload executes without touching disk, requiring detection via process memory forensics, VirtualAlloc/WriteProcessMemory sequences, or in-memory code cave analysis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for parent process spawning child with suspicious memory allocation patterns (sequence of VirtualAlloc → WriteProcessMemory → CreateRemoteThread). Flag processes loading only network/crypto libraries without corresponding temporary files. Alert on cross-process write operations from unsigned executables in %TEMP%.

suggestion.title: Lazarus RemotePE Command & Control Communications
suggestion.rationale: Memory-only RAT requires persistent command channel. Article context implies active C2 for financial exfiltration—detect via unusual outbound connections from svchost, lsass, or legitimate applications to non-standard ports and private/bulletproof IP space.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound connections on ports 4443, 8080, 8443 from system processes with no prior DNS resolution. Alert on svchost/lsass connecting to IPs with known Lazarus ASN or bulletproof hosting. Correlate network events with in-memory process injection indicators.

suggestion.title: Financial Credential Harvesting via RAT Access
suggestion.rationale: Lazarus targeting of 'financial and crypto firms' establishes credential theft as kill-chain objective. Memory-only execution enables LSASS dumping, registry SAM access, and browser credential theft without disk forensics—detect via LSA/LSASS access by unsigned processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on non-SYSTEM processes attempting to read HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\Security or executing minidump/comsvcs against lsass.exe. Monitor for suspicious API sequences: GetAsyncKeyState + SetWindowsHookEx from unsigned binaries. Flag Chrome/Firefox credential database access by non-browser processes.

suggestion.title: Spear-Phishing to Financial Sector with Weaponized Office Macros
suggestion.rationale: Lazarus historical TTP: spear-phishing documents targeting finance. Title phrase 'deploys RemotePE' implies file-delivered initial payload—detect weaponized Office macros or script-based downloaders executing RemotePE in-memory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag emails with DOCM/XLSM attachments to finance sector domains with enabled macros. Monitor for PowerShell/CMD spawned by Winword/Excel within 5 seconds. Alert if execution followed by network callback to suspicious IP within 10 seconds.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Exchange & Wallet Credential Theft
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly targets 'crypto firms'—RemotePE enables direct API key/seed phrase theft or exchange login session hijacking. Detect via suspicious file/registry access to .env configs, wallet process memory, or browser credential stores.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on non-standard processes reading ~/.ethereum, ~/.bitcoin, AppData\Local\[ExchangeName], or Chrome Login Data. Flag file access to .env, .json config files, or API_KEY environment variables by unsigned processes. Monitor for memory access to active browser crypto exchange sessions.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Harvested Financial System Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Post-credential-theft: Lazarus pivots within financial networks using stolen accounts. Detect anomalous logon patterns: system account logons, out-of-hours access, logon from unexpected geography, or credential reuse across systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for failed → successful logon sequences using same account (brute force signature). Alert on logon outside normal time-of-day or geographic region for employee. Flag lateral movement to Domain Controllers, financial databases (Oracle, MSSQL), or payment systems using harvested credentials.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Package Installation from Compromised Registry Versions
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes credential-stealing malware spread 'via npm, PyPI, and CratesIO' — supply chain vector requires detection of package installs from these sources paired with post-install execution anomalies. Malware executes during install/import phases on dependency resolution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm install, pip install, or cargo fetch commands followed within 5 seconds by child processes (node, python, or system shells) spawning from node_modules/, site-packages/, or target/ directories with suspicious arguments (curl, wget, powershell, bash -c), especially connecting to non-standard C2 or credential exfil endpoints.

suggestion.title: Credential Access via Post-Install Script Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware is 'credential-stealing' distributed via package managers. Package install hooks (postinstall scripts in npm, setup.py in PyPI, build scripts in Cargo) are the execution vector. Detection must catch when these scripts exfil credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child processes of package managers (npm, pip, cargo) accessing sensitive files (%APPDATA%\*, ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\), reading environment variables containing secrets (AWS_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN, DB_PASSWORD), or connecting to unexpected external IPs immediately post-install.

suggestion.title: Cross-Ecosystem Package Manager Compromise Signals
suggestion.rationale: Simultaneous attack across npm, PyPI, and CratesIO suggests either supply chain operator compromise or coordinated package account takeovers. Article phrase 'spreads...via npm, PyPI, and CratesIO' indicates multi-ecosystem scope — detection should flag when same malware signatures or C2 domains appear across language-specific package repositories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate package registry abuse alerts, account compromise indicators, or malware detections across npm, PyPI, Crates.io, and official advisories in short timeframe (<24h). Flag if same domain/hash appears as malicious in multiple ecosystem threat feeds simultaneously.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of Credentials to Attacker C2
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'credential-stealing malware' — stolen creds must transit somewhere. Supply chain malware typically exfils to attacker-controlled infrastructure during or after installation. Detection should catch credential data in transit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP POST or DNS TXT requests containing base64/hex-encoded credential data (AWS keys, tokens, passwords, API keys) originating from processes spawned by package manager post-install hooks, especially to non-standard ports or newly-registered domains.

suggestion.title: Malicious Dependency Resolution and Typosquatting Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks often use typosquatting (similar package names) or dependency confusion to trick installations. Without article details on exact package names, detection must flag registry metadata anomalies: newly-uploaded packages with many rapid downloads, packages from newly-created accounts, or packages with suspicious dependency chains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on package manager operations installing packages uploaded in last 7 days, published by accounts with <3 prior published packages, or packages with dependencies on known malicious package names. Correlate with credential exfil network signatures.

suggestion.title: Environment Variable and Config Exfiltration Post-Package Install
suggestion.rationale: Credential-stealing malware in supply chain typically targets application secrets stored in environment variables and dotenv files. Article implies broad credential theft — detection should specifically catch reads of .env files and environment variable access during package initialization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file read events of .env, .bashrc, .profile, ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.kube/config, and environment variable dumps (env, Get-ChildItem Env:, printenv) occurring within 10 seconds of npm/pip/cargo child process spawn, especially when followed by outbound network connections.

suggestion.title: Suspicious URL Redirect from Chatbot Service
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Chatbot Recommendations Redirect Users' — indicates initial access through chatbot compromised or manipulated to serve malicious links. No detection use case proposed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor AI chatbot recommendation logs for unusual or obfuscated URLs. Baseline expected domains and alert on deviations. Correlate chatbot-served URLs with subsequent user clicks and network connections to cryptocurrency infrastructure or unknown domains.

suggestion.title: Cryptojacking Malware Execution Post-Redirect
suggestion.rationale: Article states users are redirected to 'Cryptojacking Malware Sites' — malware must be executed on victim machines. No detection for malware execution or process anomaly was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of cryptomining binaries (xmrig, monero variants, etc.) or suspicious processes with cryptocurrency pool connections. Look for process execution from browser temp folders or AppData shortly after suspicious URL clicks.

suggestion.title: Sustained High CPU/GPU Utilization After Web Activity
suggestion.rationale: Cryptojacking inherently consumes system resources. Article describes users being redirected to execute mining code. No resource anomaly detection was proposed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate user web activity (chatbot interaction + suspicious redirect) with sustained elevated CPU/GPU usage from background processes. Flag when resource spikes coincide with execution of unsigned or unsigned-but-legitimate binaries from unusual paths.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Mining Pool Connection Detection
suggestion.rationale: Cryptojacking malware must communicate with mining pools. Article implies victims connect to attacker infrastructure. No C2/mining pool detection use case created.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound connections from user endpoints to known cryptocurrency mining pool IP ranges and domains (stratum, getwork protocol, monero-pool, etc.). Correlate with process execution of potential miners from suspicious paths.

suggestion.title: BIND 9 Vulnerable Process Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Resolvers and Authoritative Servers' exposed to 'Remote Exploits' — requires process monitoring for vulnerable BIND 9 versions running on name servers
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for BIND 9 process (named or bind) running on systems known to host DNS infrastructure. Correlate process start with version checks against published vulnerability advisories. Alert on versions matching vulnerable ranges in BIND 9 CVE disclosures.

suggestion.title: DNS Authority Query Anomalies Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Authoritative servers are attack target — successful exploitation may manifest as unusual DNS responses, zone transfer attempts, or query patterns diverging from baseline
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal DNS query patterns for authoritative name servers. Detect spikes in AXFR requests (zone transfers), queries for non-existent records, or responses with abnormal TTLs that may indicate compromise or DoS.

suggestion.title: BIND 9 Process Restart or Crash Cluster
suggestion.rationale: Remote exploits against DNS software often trigger process crashes or restart loops; article indicates active remote exploitation risk
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on rapid BIND 9 (named) process termination and restart cycles within 5-minute windows on DNS infrastructure servers. Correlate with error logs indicating segmentation faults, out-of-memory conditions, or unexpected exits.

suggestion.title: DNS Resolver Response Poisoning Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Compromised resolvers may inject malicious DNS responses; article identifies 'Resolvers' as attack surface, enabling potential DNS hijacking or traffic redirection
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS responses from internal resolvers for CNAME/A record responses pointing to unexpected IPs not in IPAM. Compare resolver responses against authoritative sources for known domains; flag mismatches indicating potential cache poisoning.

suggestion.title: Network Traffic to BIND 9 Service Ports from Unusual Sources
suggestion.rationale: Remote exploits imply network-reachable BIND 9 instances; detect reconnaissance or exploitation attempts to port 53 (DNS) and potential control-plane ports from untrusted networks
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on inbound traffic to port 53 from external networks or suspicious internal subnets targeting systems running BIND 9. Correlate with IDS signatures for known BIND 9 exploit payloads (CVE-specific PoCs if available).

suggestion.title: Exploitation Detection - cPanel LiteSpeed Redis Function Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability in 'lsws.redisAble function' enables 'remote attackers with no privileges to execute arbitrary scripts with root privileges.' No detection logic provided for this core attack vector despite active exploitation.
