suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes exploitation chains as critical attack path: 'chained vulnerabilities, where a couple of mediums and highs combine into a critical exploit path.' Implies sequential low-level auth/data-access flaws combined into privilege escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate multiple failed/marginal authorization attempts (403s, token rejections) followed by successful lateral access to higher-privilege resource. Look for attacker using intermediate-privilege identity to escalate rather than direct admin access; sequential auth test patterns.

suggestion.title: Cross-Tenant or Cross-Identity Data Access
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 'cross-tenant data leakage' as primary context-dependent attack: 'none of these have a heuristic signature...only humans could acquire the contextual understanding required.' Defenders need behavioral detection since signature matching fails.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on data access spanning multiple tenant IDs, organization boundaries, or user contexts in single session. Detect requests for resources tagged with different org/owner attributes than the calling identity. Look for systematic retrieval of invoices, PII, or configuration belonging to different business units.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated or Weakly Authenticated API Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article describes probing/observation cycle as core attack pattern: 'probe, observe, infer' applied by AI against APIs. Weak auth on API endpoints enables continuous low-friction reconnaissance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag API endpoints accepting requests without Authorization header or with expired/low-privilege tokens, followed by parameter/object ID enumeration. Correlate unauthenticated access to sensitive API paths (e.g., /admin, /users, /billing) with parameter fuzzing patterns.

suggestion.title: Callback Phishing Email + Unexpected RDP Session Initiation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'SRG actors either directly call or send phishing emails to urge employees to call the SRG actor posing as IT support. While on the phone, the SRG actor directs the employee to grant access to a remote desktop session.' No detection addresses the correlation between phishing delivery and RDP grant in a compressed timeframe.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate phishing email to user with mstsc.exe or RDP client invocation within 30 minutes. Escalate if RDP target is external IP, non-standard port, or from VPN/residential range. Flag if no corresponding IT ticket exists.

suggestion.title: USB / External Storage Device Insertion with Concurrent Bulk File Access
suggestion.rationale: Article describes physical data theft: 'the malicious actors can steal data by connecting USB drives or external hard drives to the victim's computer.' No detection pairs USB insertion events with suspicious file enumeration or data staging.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on external USB device insertion (Sysmon Event 23 or equivalent) immediately preceding large file reads across sensitive shares. Correlate with process execution touching >50 files in <10 minutes from non-standard process.

suggestion.title: Remote Desktop Protocol Access from Non-Corporate Network
suggestion.rationale: Article states SRG 'direct[s] the employee to grant access to a remote desktop session' without employee verification of source. No detection for RDP connections from untrusted or unrecognized external networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag inbound RDP (TCP 3389) or RDP Gateway traffic from VPN services, residential ISPs, or geographically inconsistent locations. Escalate if RDP session precedes file transfers to removable media or unusual process spawning.

suggestion.title: Typosquatted Domain Registration and Phishing Email Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'the attackers register domains to impersonate IT helpdesk or support portals for major U.S. law firms and financial services firms, using typosquatted patterns.' No detection monitors domain registration or email sourcing from look-alike domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DNS queries to typosquatted variants of org domain (remove/swap characters: orgname-it.com, org-namesupport.com). Alert on emails claiming IT origin but sent from unregistered or newly-registered domain. WHOIS-check domains for privacy service registration or bulk registrant patterns.

suggestion.title: Bulk File Access and Data Staging for Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'SRG uses the stolen data to extort the victims'—indicating data collection and preparation phase. Attack involves gathering files before exfiltration, but no detection captures abnormal access volume or staging patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect single account or process accessing >100 files across multiple sensitive directories in <15 minutes. Escalate if files subsequently staged to single temp location, compressed (.zip/.rar), or queued for transfer to removable device or network share.

suggestion.title: Unidentified Individual Requesting Physical Computer Access and IT Impersonation
suggestion.rationale: Article lists as indicator: 'the presence of unidentified or unauthorized individuals claiming to be IT support and attempting to access computers, as possible indicators of an SRG attack.' Physical security breach that requires detective controls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-correlate badge access logs (who accessed building/floor) with visitor sign-in records. Alert on unscheduled access by unidentified individual to IT-restricted areas on dates when phishing/helpdesk scam reports filed. Review security camera footage for individuals handling computers.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized ChangeMissionDatabase privilege assignment or MDB mutation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'authenticated user with the ChangeMissionDatabase privilege can exploit this.' Detection should monitor for privilege escalation, role assignments, or privilege abuse preceding algorithm modifications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor authentication logs and authorization events for ChangeMissionDatabase permission grants to unexpected principals or existing users. Correlate with subsequent MDB writes. Alert on privilege escalation attempts targeting Yamcs administrative roles.

suggestion.title: Janino expression compilation anomalies in Yamcs algorithm factory
suggestion.rationale: The vulnerability exploits 'JavaExprAlgorithmExecutionFactory' using 'Janino Expression Engine' without sandbox. Article indicates dynamic compilation of user-controlled text; should detect abnormal JVM bytecode instrumentation or Janino compilation errors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor JVM logs for Janino compiler errors, class definition anomalies, or reflection-based code generation patterns. Detect when algorithm submissions contain Java syntax fragments (import, class, method, Runtime.exec) instead of pure expression language.

suggestion.title: Suspicious algorithm text containing Java Runtime or code execution patterns
suggestion.rationale: The exploitation vector is malicious 'algorithm text' submitted via PATCH. Should specifically detect algorithm payloads containing Java code execution primitives (Runtime.exec, ProcessBuilder, Script, reflection calls).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect PATCH request bodies to /api/mdb/*/algorithms/* for Java code patterns: 'Runtime', 'exec', 'ProcessBuilder', 'reflection', 'System.', 'invoke'. Flag submissions containing these keywords as potential injection payloads.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Private Container Images
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'exposes private container images without authentication'—the core attack vector. Pipeline missed the fundamental detection of auth-bypass access to image registries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to Gitea container registry endpoints (e.g., /v2/, /api/v1/repos) that succeed (2xx responses) with missing or invalid Authorization headers. Alert on requests that enumerate or pull private image manifests/blobs without prior successful authentication.

suggestion.title: Enumerate Private Repositories via Gitea API Without Auth
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates 'private' images are exposed; discovery of what images exist is a prerequisite for exploitation. Pipeline did not capture the enumeration phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Gitea /v2/_catalog or /api/v1/repos endpoints for LIST/enumeration requests from unauthenticated sources. Threshold on sequential repo enumeration requests from single IP or subnet lacking auth tokens.

suggestion.title: Bulk Container Image Download/Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability 'exposes' images—attackers can download them. Article implies data loss scenario. Pipeline missed exfiltration detection signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous volume of container image layer downloads (blob GET requests) from single unauthenticated source within short time window. Alert on image manifests pulled without corresponding push operations (unidirectional flow).

suggestion.title: Gitea Instance with Exposed Container Registry Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Attack requires a Gitea instance running a vulnerable version with accessible registry API. Pipeline should have surfaced scanning/discovery of vulnerable Gitea deployments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Gitea instances responding to /v2/ or container registry probes. Flag instances returning image metadata without authentication challenges. Correlate with known CVE version patterns if version endpoint is exposed.

suggestion.title: GitHub Enterprise Server Exploitation Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Critical Vulnerabilities' in GHE 3.20.3; no detection use case was generated despite clear vulnerability disclosure scenario requiring exploitation detection
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub Enterprise Server instances for HTTP requests with suspicious parameter encoding, malformed JSON to API endpoints, or exploitation signatures targeting known GHE vulnerability classes. Alert on unauthorized access to admin endpoints and repository manipulation API calls from non-authenticated sources.

suggestion.title: GitHub Enterprise Server Post-Exploitation Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: Critical vulnerabilities in application servers commonly result in RCE; no detection logic for suspicious process spawning or file modification within GHE contexts
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual child processes spawned by git-daemon, github-unicorn, or other GHE service accounts; monitor for web shell creation in repository directories or SSH key enumeration within GHE user contexts.

suggestion.title: Malicious VS Code / OpenVSX Extension Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'malicious OpenVSX and Microsoft VS Code extensions that stole cryptocurrency wallets and developer credentials' as primary delivery mechanism. Pipeline identified no extraction for this attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for VS Code extension installations from untrusted or newly-created publisher accounts. Track extension activation events and correlate with credential file access. Alert on extensions that remain dormant then activate during extension update cycles.

suggestion.title: Solana Blockchain Transaction Queries for C2 Resolution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'C2 server addresses are encoded in the memo fields of blockchain transactions, creating an immutable, publicly accessible dead drop.' Pipeline extracted no detection for this evasion-resistant C2 channel.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTPS connections to Solana RPC endpoints or blockchain explorers from developer workstations. Detect base58-encoded wallet address resolution. Alert on memo field parsing and Base64 decoding of transaction data.

suggestion.title: BitTorrent DHT Configuration Retrieval
suggestion.rationale: Article documents 'GlasswormRAT queries the BitTorrent peer-to-peer network for configuration data stored against hardcoded public keys, leveraging a global decentralized network with no single point of failure.' This critical C2 resilience mechanism was completely missed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for DHT protocol activity or BitTorrent node connections from non-torrent processes, especially VS Code or developer tools. Monitor for repeated queries to the same hardcoded DHT public keys. Flag unusual peer-to-peer communication from isolated development environments.

suggestion.title: Google Calendar Dead Drop Configuration
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Glassworm uses Google Calendar event titles as dead-drop locations for Base64-encoded C2 paths.' No cloud service abuse detection for C2 infrastructure was generated despite explicit description.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Google Calendar API read operations from developer machines. Detect Base64 decoding of calendar event title content. Alert on suspicious calendar event patterns (specific naming conventions, specific times, rapid sequential reads).

suggestion.title: Dormant Extension Post-Update Activation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'dormant extensions on OpenVSX that would activate the malicious component after an update.' This time-delayed execution technique in a supply chain context was not detected or mapped.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor VS Code extension directories for dormant/inert-looking extensions that spawn child processes or access credential stores immediately following extension update operations. Correlate extension metadata and manifest timestamps with execution events.

suggestion.title: npm Package and GitHub Repository Supply Chain Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'Later attack waves extended to GitHub repositories and npm packages, with one campaign in March impacting more than 400 software artifacts.' This supply chain delivery method was not mapped to detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install and yarn operations for packages from newly-registered or recently-compromised maintainers. Track GitHub clone operations and correlate with suspicious commit patterns or branch names. Alert on post-install script execution in node_modules folders.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email with Google Domain Redirect to Attacker Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article title establishes the core attack: 'hackers abuse trusted Google domains to hide phishing links' — indicates emails containing Google service URLs (Forms, Drive, Sites, Mail, Sheets) as redirectors to attacker-controlled final destinations. Pipeline extracted zero use cases despite this being the primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag emails where URLs point exclusively to Google first-party domains (docs.google.com, forms.google.com, drive.google.com, accounts.google.com) with short URLs, unusual query parameters, or where email body requests credential entry or urgent action. High-fidelity if Google domain appears legitimate but resolves to recently-registered domain post-click.

suggestion.title: Email Gateway Reputation Bypass via Trusted Domain Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states abuse tactic: 'hide phishing links from email gateways' — indicates adversaries leveraging Google's whitelisted IP reputation and URL filtering exemptions to bypass email security controls. Zero detection logic generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on emails delivered with zero blocks/quarantines that contain Google-domain-wrapped URLs with high-entropy query parameters or obfuscated payloads. Cross-reference against security appliance logs for allow-listing of Google IPs carrying phishing payloads post-delivery.

suggestion.title: Recursive URL Redirect Chain with Google Domains
suggestion.rationale: Abusing trusted domains as redirectors inherently requires multi-hop chains. Article pattern suggests adversaries chain Google service → intermediary → final phishing site. Standard email URL inspection may not follow chains starting with trusted domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enforce recursive detonation of all email URLs including those starting with Google domains. Flag chains where Google service resolves to newly-observed, low-reputation, or typosquatted domains. Baseline Google → Google legitimate chains to identify anomalies.

suggestion.title: Google Form as Phishing Social Engineering Hook
suggestion.rationale: Google Forms are high-trust abuse targets for phishing. Article subtitle pattern ('hide phishing links') suggests Forms may be used to capture credentials. Pipeline missed social-engineering angle despite clear attack description.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify emails requesting form completion with urgency language ('verify now', 'confirm identity', 'update credentials') containing *only* a Google Forms URL with no additional context. Flag if same Forms URL distributed to multiple organizations in short window, or if query parameters suggest cloned legitimate forms.

suggestion.title: High-Velocity Phishing Campaign via Google Service URLs
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates coordinated abuse of Google domains suggests campaign-level activity. Pipeline should have detected volume patterns of emails using trusted-domain wrapping tactics.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect spikes in emails containing Google service URLs (forms.google.com, docs.google.com, drive.google.com, accounts.google.com) as primary/only URLs, particularly if shared across multiple recipients, organizations, or threat feeds in same timeframe. Correlate with known phishing reporter feeds.

suggestion.title: Suspicious APK Installation with Device Admin Request
suggestion.rationale: Article title establishes malware 'lets attackers remotely control Android devices'—remote control on Android typically requires DeviceAdmin permissions or privileged access. Pipeline missed initial compromise detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for APK installations requesting DeviceAdmin, accessibility services, or call/SMS permissions. Correlate with app installation events and identify packages signed with unknown certificates. High-risk if permissions requested before standard permissions appear in manifest.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Device Configuration Changes Post-Installation
suggestion.rationale: Remote control capability implies malware alters device state—'remotely control' suggests changes to settings, permissions, or network config. No UC surfaced detection of configuration drift.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track unexpected changes to device settings: Wi-Fi/Bluetooth toggling, proxy configuration, USB debugging state, accessibility settings activation, or permission changes after app installation. Baseline per device class and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated or Unsigned Native Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: Android malware delivering 'remote control' capability often uses native libraries (NDK) and code obfuscation—article title implies sophisticated payload. Pipeline did not suggest native code execution detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag execution of .so (native) libraries from within app sandbox, especially from unusual paths (/data/local/tmp, /cache). Monitor for dex2oat or runtime compilation. Correlate with obfuscated class names or stripped symbols.

suggestion.title: C2 Communication from Trusted App Package
suggestion.rationale: Remote control malware requires command channel—article states 'remotely control' implying bidirectional C2. Pipeline did not generate UC for C2 exfiltration or C2 traffic patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of expected egress IPs/domains per app. Alert on unexpected HTTPS traffic, DNS queries to newly registered domains, or connections to residential IP ranges. Monitor for traffic during unusual hours or data exfiltration patterns (sustained outbound).

suggestion.title: Call/SMS Interception or Call State Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Android remote control malware often abuses call/SMS APIs—title emphasizes 'remotely control devices' which includes telephony. Pipeline missed call/SMS behavior detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for app calls to TelephonyManager.answerRingingCall(), endCall(), or SMS receiver registration without user interaction. Alert on outbound SMS to premium numbers. Track state changes in CallState events correlated to app execution.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Unpatched Kernel Exploit
suggestion.rationale: Remote control capability on Android typically requires root or SELinux bypass—common BTMOB/similar families exploit CVEs. Article does not explicitly state this but remote control at scale implies privilege escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for execve() or ioctl() syscalls associated with known Android kernel exploits (Qualcomm, MediaTek, etc.). Alert on unexpected elevation of app UID to system (1000) or root (0). Track SELinux denial patterns that precede successful privilege escalation.

suggestion.title: ROADtools Binary or Module Execution
suggestion.rationale: Title names 'ROADtools' explicitly as attack vehicle ('ROADtools Misused in Cloud Attacks'). No detection use case provided despite tool-specific execution being the entry point to downstream attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for spawning of ROADtools binaries (roadrecon.exe, roadtx.exe, or Python roadtools modules) or suspicious PowerShell/Python child processes invoking ROADtools libraries. Alert on process names/command-lines containing 'roadtools', 'roadrecon', or 'roadtx' from non-admin contexts.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Token Extraction and Unauthorized Token Usage
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attack objective 'Steal Tokens' in title. No detection for token cache theft or anomalous token validation/usage post-theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process access to credential stores (DPAPI keys, token caches in %APPDATA%\Microsoft\*) and unusual token validation patterns. Flag tokens used from geographically impossible locations or by service principals that never previously accessed them.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Microsoft Graph API Calls by Compromised Accounts
suggestion.rationale: ROADtools core functionality abuses MS Graph API to enumerate/access cloud resources ('cloud attacks'). No detection for suspicious Graph API enumeration or mail/directory reads by compromised identities.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Graph API calls for bulk user/group enumeration (filter: users, groups, servicePrincipals) and mail/OneDrive access from tokens with unexpected IP geolocations or user-agents. Correlate with prior token-theft signals.

suggestion.title: MFA Factor Removal or Suspicious Re-enrollment
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly calls out 'Bypass MFA Controls' objective in title. No detection for MFA tampering, factor removal, or unauthorized device registration post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on removal of MFA methods (phone, software token, passwordless sign-in) from high-privilege accounts shortly after suspicious token activity. Flag re-enrollment of MFA to new devices from unusual locations.

suggestion.title: Excessive App Permission Consent or Service Principal Role Assignment
suggestion.rationale: ROADtools attackers grant persistent access by adding service principals or assigning roles post-compromise. Article describes 'Cloud Attacks' implying infrastructure persistence, but no detection for app consent abuse or excessive role grants.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect admin consent grants to applications by compromised low-privilege accounts, especially for high-risk scopes (Mail.Read, Directory.ReadWrite, Application.ReadWrite.All). Flag role assignments elevating service principals to Global Admin or Tenant Admin during suspicious sign-in windows.

suggestion.title: Unsigned DLL loaded by signed Fortemedia binary
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'Seedworm APT Abuses Signed Fortemedia...Binaries for DLL Sideloading' — canonical DLL sideloading pattern using legitimate signed executable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Fortemedia executables loading unsigned or misaligned DLLs. Monitor for image loads where DLL publisher does not match binary publisher. DLL sideloading typically loads malicious DLLs from same directory as legitimate executable.

suggestion.title: Unsigned DLL loaded by signed SentinelOne binary
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly names SentinelOne binary abuse for DLL sideloading — attackers abuse endpoint security vendor binaries to bypass defenses.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect SentinelOne executables loading unsigned or anomalous DLLs. Alert on image load events where DLL signature does not match expected publisher or signer is absent.

suggestion.title: Legitimate signed binary execution from unusual directory
suggestion.rationale: DLL sideloading requires placing legitimate binaries outside standard paths to load attacker-controlled DLLs. Title indicates systematic abuse of Fortemedia and SentinelOne binaries suggests coordinated binary placement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Fortemedia or SentinelOne executables launched from non-standard directories (outside Program Files, Windows\System32, etc.). Establish process baseline for legitimate application paths and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: DLL sideloading via Seedworm cluster behavior
suggestion.rationale: Article attributes attack to Seedworm APT specifically — pipeline should establish threat-actor-specific patterns. Title alone establishes coordinated technique abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate process execution of Fortemedia or SentinelOne binaries with suspicious unsigned DLL loads on same system within short time window. Seedworm operations likely show clustering of this behavior across multiple targets.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Kernel Memory Modification Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'attackers to modify kernel memory counters'; no detection logic provided for this core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes attempting privileged memory operations targeting kernel address space (e.g., NtWriteVirtualMemory, NtMapViewOfSection with KERNEL_MODE targets). Flag kernel memory access from user-mode processes without legitimate drivers.

suggestion.title: Kernel Counter Value Baseline Deviation
suggestion.rationale: Attack centers on modifying kernel counters; no telemetry for detecting anomalous counter states post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for system counters (memory allocations, I/O operations, context switches). Alert when counters show impossible or anomalous patterns (e.g., negative values, sudden resets, or flat-line behavior on high-activity systems).

suggestion.title: Unsigned or Out-of-Tree Kernel Driver Loading
suggestion.rationale: Kernel memory modification almost always requires driver injection; no monitoring for malicious driver installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for kernel drivers loaded without valid Microsoft signatures, from non-standard paths (%System32%\drivers), or with mismatched timestamps. Alert on Driver Signature Enforcement (DSE) bypass attempts or DSE disable commands.

suggestion.title: Salesforce Unauthorized API/Bulk Export Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers 'gained access to certain 7-Eleven systems' and 'breaching 7-Eleven's Salesforce environment,' then 'stolen over 600,000 records.' No UC captured the mass data movement from SaaS platform.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Salesforce Data Loader, Bulk API, or export tooling for unusual high-volume data access by service accounts or newly-created users. Correlate large exports (>10k records/hour) from franchisee document stores against baseline access patterns. Alert on exports to unfamiliar IP ranges or consecutive queries spanning entire customer/franchisee datasets.

suggestion.title: Salesforce Credential Compromise (Lateral Recon Post-Breach)
suggestion.rationale: Intrusion implies credential theft or weak auth to Salesforce (article: 'unauthorized third party gained access'). Pipeline should surface detection for anomalous Salesforce logins, MFA bypass, or token hijacking preceding mass data theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag failed Salesforce login bursts followed by successful logins from new geolocations, TOR exits, or datacenter IPs. Alert on API token creation or refresh anomalies, especially for service accounts. Detect Salesforce session hijacking via user-agent/IP mismatches on sensitive org endpoints.

suggestion.title: Known Threat Actor IOC Correlation – ShinyHunters
suggestion.rationale: ShinyHunters explicitly claimed the breach and posted to 'dark web leak site.' Article documents actor reuse pattern across 'hundreds of companies' and Salesforce-specific campaigns. No actor name or known infrastructure IOCs surfaced by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest ShinyHunters' known C2 IPs, leak site domains, and Salesforce exploit signatures from threat feeds. Correlate customer Salesforce access logs and Salesforce-instance metadata against ShinyHunters' historically-targeted customer segments. Alert on Salesforce instances matching known victim profile (franchisee operations, multi-tenant environments).

suggestion.title: Dark Web Data Leak Site Upload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states cybercriminals 'leaked a 9.4GB archive of documents on their dark web leak site.' No detection for threat-actor exfiltration infrastructure or leak-site uploads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTPS uploads to known ShinyHunters leak-site domains or newly-registered Tor hidden services matching ShinyHunters' naming/UI patterns. Correlate large outbound data transfers (multi-GB) to Tor/proxy infrastructure with prior Salesforce activity anomalies. Detect DNS queries to dark web hosting providers and marketplace sites associated with extortion campaigns.

suggestion.title: Ransomware/Extortion Demand Communication Detection
suggestion.rationale: ShinyHunters 'claimed responsibility' and demanded ransom; article notes 'FBI advised ShinyHunters' victims not to give in.' Pipeline should surface use case for detecting extortion communications and ransom demands.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor email inbound for ransom notes and extortion threats referencing specific stolen data (franchisee names, address counts, data volumes). Search for Dark Web marketplace posts or leak-site announcements matching compromised organization identity. Alert on adversary Telegram/Discord channels posting victim data samples.

suggestion.title: Third-Party SaaS Provider Compromise Blast Radius
suggestion.rationale: Article notes ShinyHunters 'has been targeting Salesforce customers for the past year and breached hundreds of companies.' Single Salesforce compromise can affect multiple customers. No UC for detecting lateral spread within multi-tenant SaaS.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-tenant Salesforce orgs: detect simultaneous unusual activity (logins, exports, permission changes) across unrelated customer instances. Monitor for Salesforce org-to-org data flows or shared API token usage. Alert when a single source IP spawns authenticated activity across multiple customer Salesforce instances in short time window.

suggestion.title: Android Accessibility Services Permission Abuse for Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'it abuses Android Accessibility Services to gain elevated permissions and grant itself further system access without additional user interaction.' This is the primary privilege escalation vector and should generate immediate detection on unauthorized permission elevation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for third-party apps requesting Accessibility Service permissions followed by subsequent elevation of sensitive capabilities (contacts, SMS, location, call recording) granted without additional explicit user consent in the same session. Flag apps that hold both Accessibility and multi-sensitive-permission combinations.

suggestion.title: Phishing Landing Page Mimicking Legitimate App Stores
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Operators send victims to phishing websites that pose as streaming services, cryptocurrency mining platforms or other familiar online services. From there, victims are pushed toward fake app stores that mimic legitimate repositories.' This is initial access via social engineering to deceptive store clones.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect URLs with domain typosquatting or visual similarity to official Google Play Store, Apple App Store, or regional app marketplaces. Correlate click events from mass phishing campaigns with navigation to fake store domains. Cross-reference landing page visual similarity using image hashing against known legitimate store assets.

suggestion.title: Malicious APK Installation from Non-Official Source
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'fake app stores that mimic legitimate repositories and prompt them to install a malicious APK' and later 'stick to the official app store.' Side-loaded APK installation from non-Play Store sources is execution mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for APK package installations originating from domains not whitelisted as legitimate app repositories. Correlate app installation timestamp with prior navigation to phishing/fake-store domains. Flag APKs with suspicious or obfuscated package names and code-signing certificates not tied to known vendors.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Exfiltration via Remote Access Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article describes RAT capabilities as: 'exfiltrate a range of sensitive data, capture screenshots and record activity on the device, and ultimately take remote control of it.' Post-compromise data theft is the impact phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual outbound network connections from device with high entropy payloads to non-standard ports. Correlate screen recording/screenshot API calls with exfiltration-sized network transfers. Monitor for processes accessing contacts, calendar, SMS, and email databases simultaneously with outbound connection attempts.

suggestion.title: Regional Government Agency Impersonation Campaign
suggestion.rationale: Article reports: 'researchers Johnk3r and Merl recently spotted campaigns that spread BTMOB while impersonating Argentina's tax and customs authorities.' Nation-state themed phishing lures are campaign-specific initial access indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sender spoofing or look-alike domains impersonating tax authorities, customs agencies, or revenue departments by country. Monitor for localized phishing lures with government agency logos and official language variants. Correlate timing of campaigns with regional government notification deadlines (tax filing windows, regulatory submissions).

suggestion.title: Rapid Malware Payload Variant Generation from MaaS Builder
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'As new variants can be generated quickly, defenders should expect rapid payload turnover... roughly 15 samples of BTMOB v2.5 had been spotted since late January of that year, i.e., in a mere two or so weeks.' High-velocity variant production is signature of commercialized tooling.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cluster APK submissions with identical or near-identical behavioral characteristics (same C2 infrastructure, permission requests, functionality) but distinct code signatures and file hashes. Flag 10+ unique APK hashes with matching internal version strings (e.g., 'v2.5') submitted within 14-day window. Cross-reference against ESET detection names (MSIL/BtmobRat, Android/Spy.Agent.EED/EIJ/EIK).

suggestion.title: Bulk Customer Data Export from Salesforce
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'used this access to export millions of consumer and business customer records from the company's Salesforce instance'—core exfiltration step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Salesforce for bulk export operations (large SOQL queries, report generation, data export API calls) from single account in short timeframe, especially accounts with previously low activity or from anomalous IP/location.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Multi-SaaS Access Post-SSO Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'After gaining access to a corporate SSO account, the threat actors steal data from connected SaaS applications such as Salesforce, Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, SAP, Slack, Adobe, Atlassian, Zendesk, Dropbox'—cascading SaaS access pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag sequential or rapid authentication to multiple SaaS platforms (3+ distinct services) from single user account within short window (minutes/hours), especially if user has no historical access to those services.

suggestion.title: Microsoft Entra Account Compromise via Voice Phishing
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'breached Charter on April 1 through a voice phishing (vishing) attack that compromised an employee's Microsoft Entra account'—post-vishing account anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Entra logins from new geolocation/IP immediately after failed authentication attempts, MFA bypass events, or new device registration on account; correlate with external reports of targeted vishing campaigns.

suggestion.title: Large-Scale Customer PII and CPNI Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'stolen 40 million records containing the personal information of consumer and business customers'—data discovery phase before exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on large-result SOQL queries or bulk report generation targeting customer PII fields (names, emails, addresses, phone numbers, CPNI) from single Salesforce user in short timeframe, especially queries returning thousands+ rows.

suggestion.title: Cross-Platform Customer Record Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'stolen customer support ticket data' plus Salesforce records—exfiltration spans multiple systems (Salesforce, Zendesk).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate bulk export events across multiple platforms (Salesforce + Zendesk + support ticketing) within same timeframe from same user; flag concurrent downloads of customer records and support tickets as coordinated exfiltration.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48172 Vulnerable Asset Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Standard asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in [...asset-exposure].' Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this direct recommendation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify cPanel instances running vulnerable LiteSpeed plugin versions. Cross-reference vulnerability scan results against asset inventory for CVE-2026-48172. Prioritize internet-facing instances.

suggestion.title: cPanel User Privilege Escalation to Root
suggestion.rationale: Article core attack: 'any cPanel user account to execute arbitrary scripts with root privileges.' Privilege escalation path is entirely undetected by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor cPanel audit logs for unexpected privilege transitions. Detect process creation where parent context is cPanel/web process but child executes as root/UID 0. Flag standard user accounts initiating root-level commands.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary Script Execution via LiteSpeed Plugin
suggestion.rationale: Core exploit mechanism: 'execute arbitrary scripts with root privileges' via plugin exposure. Execution detection layer completely missing from pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect shell/script interpreter invocations (bash, sh, perl, python) originating from LiteSpeed cPanel plugin execution path or web-process context with root privileges. Correlate unexpected script file creation in plugin directories.

suggestion.title: cPanel User Account Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Attack explicitly leverages 'any cPanel user account' as attack vector. Credential-abuse angle (using valid, non-privileged accounts maliciously) not detected despite being core to attack narrative.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal cPanel user behavior. Flag deviations: user accounts performing privilege-escalation attempts, execution of administrative functions inconsistent with role history, or accounts interacting with plugin/core cPanel functions they never previously accessed.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Lateral Movement from Compromised cPanel
suggestion.rationale: Once root access achieved, attacker has unrestricted pivot capability. Article implies active exploitation but pipeline provides zero post-exploitation detection coverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Following successful CVE-2026-48172 exploitation, monitor for lateral movement indicators: SSH key generation, credential enumeration, network scanning, unexpected outbound connections, or reconnaissance of internal systems from the compromised cPanel host.

suggestion.title: SQL Injection Attempts Against Drupal Database Abstraction API
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability allows attackers to 'trigger arbitrary SQL injection on PostgreSQL-powered sites via specially crafted requests' with '15,000 attack attempts targeting almost 6,000 individual sites' observed — core attack pattern entirely unmapped.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST requests to Drupal core database layer endpoints (or any database query parameter injection points). Flag SQL operators (UNION, SELECT, OR, DROP, HAVING, xp_cmdshell, system()) in request parameters, especially when paired with PostgreSQL error responses or unusual response delays.

suggestion.title: Abnormal Database Query Execution from Web Process
suggestion.rationale: Article notes successful exploitation 'can potentially lead to information disclosure, privilege escalation, and even remote code execution' — the execution phase of SQL injection resulting in data access or command execution not captured in detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate web service process execution (apache, www-data, nginx) with PostgreSQL query logs. Flag queries containing UNION, SELECT INTO, or script execution functions executed from web tier that differ from baseline application behavior. Monitor for process spawning from database connections.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Drupal User Table Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'privilege escalation' as documented impact of CVE-2026-9082 exploitation but no detection for post-SQL-injection lateral privilege gain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for modifications to Drupal user credential tables (drupal.users, drupal.sessions, drupal.users_roles) via SQL injection patterns. Flag cases where unprivileged web service accounts insert, update, or delete rows that assign elevated roles (admin, authenticated user) or reset password hashes.

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution Post-SQL Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'remote code execution' as potential impact of CVE-2026-9082 but pipeline provides zero detection for shell command execution following database compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for command-line process execution spawned from Drupal web service account (apache, www-data, postgres backend processes). Flag bash, cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or system command invocations that immediately follow suspicious database queries or within Drupal request lifecycle.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance of Drupal Installations via Version Fingerprinting
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'Shadowserver now tracks nearly 670 unpatched Drupal installations exposed online' — implies active scanning/reconnaissance phase before targeted exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to Drupal fingerprinting endpoints (CHANGELOG.txt, README.txt, /misc/drupal.js, /sites/default/settings.php) originating from external sources. Correlate multiple requests to different targets from same source to identify mass reconnaissance campaigns.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration via SQL Injection Result Output
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'information disclosure' is outcome of successful exploitation but no detection for data being extracted through HTTP responses or out-of-band channels following SQL injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP response sizes and content following SQL injection attempts. Flag unusually large response payloads or base64-encoded data in responses after database query injection. Correlate with Drupal database schema to detect extraction of user tables, configuration, or sensitive content.

suggestion.title: Suspicious ScreenConnect Process Execution with Cryptominer Payload
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly covers 'cryptojacking campaign abusing ScreenConnect.' Pipeline generated zero UCs for ScreenConnect abuse. Should detect ScreenConnect spawning child processes associated with mining or downloading mining executables.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: ScreenConnect executable (scplugin.exe, scviewer.exe) spawning child processes or writing suspicious binaries to disk, especially processes associated with GPU mining libraries (CUDA, OpenCL) or known miner binaries. Focus on unexpected code execution paths initiated by RMM tools.

suggestion.title: Poisoned Search Result Landing & Malicious Site Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article headline: 'poisoned search results' and 'malicious sites also surfaced through AI chatbots'—this is initial access vector. Pipeline has no detection for browser-driven compromise or landing on attacker infrastructure from search result clicks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Unexpected network connections from browser processes to domains with characteristics of poisoned results (newly registered, typosquatting legitimate download sites, high entropy names). Correlate failed HTTPS validation attempts or user agent mismatches.

suggestion.title: GPU Mining Process Detection via Resource Consumption & Crypto Signatures
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'GPU mining' as impact payload. No UC for detecting miners themselves. Should monitor sustained high GPU utilization, known miner process names, crypto libraries, or pool communication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Long-running processes with high sustained GPU/CPU utilization spawned from user temp directories or %AppData%. Look for crypto mining library imports (cuDNN, clBLAS), pool connections on non-standard ports, or stratum protocol traffic.

suggestion.title: Suspicious .NET Utility Execution for Evasion or Living-off-the-Land
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'abusing Microsoft .NET utilities'—implies .NET tools (likely csc.exe, msbuild.exe, powershell.exe with .NET) misused for staging or evasion. No UC for this tactic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: csc.exe, msbuild.exe, or dotnet.exe executing from non-standard paths, with command-line arguments including obfuscation markers, parent process anomalies (e.g., launched by browser), or writing to suspicious locations. Correlate with child processes spawning mining binaries.

suggestion.title: Malicious Domain Generation & SEO Poisoning Infrastructure Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'poisoned search results' implying attacker-controlled or compromised SEO infrastructure. Pipeline missed detection for C2/infrastructure domains that would be seeding malicious results.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: DNS/HTTP requests to newly registered domains with SEO keywords in hostnames, typosquatting patterns, or subdomains associated with legitimate software download pages. Detect beaconing patterns post-compromise to attacker-controlled infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via ScreenConnect Post-Initial Compromise
suggestion.rationale: ScreenConnect is a remote management tool—once installed via poisoned search, likely used for lateral movement within network. Pipeline has no UC for ScreenConnect lateral movement abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: ScreenConnect establishing connections to multiple internal hosts, especially to high-value targets (servers, workstations). Monitor for RDP-like behavior from ScreenConnect or authenticated lateral movement post-installation.

suggestion.title: XWiki unauthenticated XAR import via REST POST /rest/wikis/{wikiName}
suggestion.rationale: Article provides explicit behavioral detection hunt with Splunk SPL for the primary attack path. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this hunt being detailed in the 'Recommended hunts' section with regex-refined endpoint matching and status-code filtering (200, 202). Article explicitly states: 'POST /wikis/{wikiName} executes a XAR import without performing any authentication or authorization checks.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthenticated POST requests to /rest/wikis/ endpoint matching /rest/wikis/[wikiName]/ with HTTP 200 or 202 responses. These indicate successful XAR import execution on target wiki without prior authentication.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email with SEO Poisoning Link Click
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'via Phishing and SEO Poisoning' as delivery mechanism. No detection for this primary initial-access vector was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect clicks on links pointing to compromised or malicious SEO-poisoned search results. Correlate with phishing email metadata (sender, subject keywords for MiniFast/MiniJunk). Alert on navigations to download sites hosting these malware families.

suggestion.title: MiniFast/MiniJunk V2 Malware Execution and Process Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes malware 'deployment' but pipeline captured no execution-phase detection. Malware family names provide specific signatures for process behavior and file artifacts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process creation with parent-child relationships typical of dropper→payload execution (e.g., rundll32, regsvcs, mshta launching suspicious child processes). Detect file writes matching known MiniFast/MiniJunk V2 signatures or behavioral patterns (process hollowing, DLL injection).

suggestion.title: Infostealer Credential Harvesting and Browser Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: MiniJunk/MiniFast naming convention strongly suggests credential-stealing malware ('Mini' + suffix common in infostealer families), yet no credential-access or collection-phase detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect infostealer-characteristic behaviors: (1) child processes spawned from malware parent accessing LSASS, WinLogon, or credential manager processes; (2) suspicious reads of browser profile directories; (3) input capture APIs or screen capture code execution.

suggestion.title: C2 Communication from Compromised Host
suggestion.rationale: Malware deployment necessitates command-and-control, a standard kill-chain phase completely absent from pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous outbound HTTPS traffic from processes spawned by or executing malware (MiniFast/MiniJunk): unusually high volume, non-standard ports, certificate mismatches, or to known attacker infrastructure. Monitor for DNS queries to domains registered by Iranian threat actors.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
suggestion.rationale: Infostealer malware inherently exfiltrates stolen credentials and browser data. No exfiltration-phase detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect large or suspicious outbound data transfers from compromised hosts running infostealer malware. Alert on encrypted C2 traffic containing credential-like patterns, Base64-encoded password dumps, or browser cookie/session data being transmitted to attacker-controlled IPs.

suggestion.title: Iranian APT Infrastructure Attribution
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies threat actor as Iranian. Pipeline output included no actor-attribution or infrastructure mapping. Should correlate known Iranian APT C2 domains, ASNs, and hosting patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference observed C2 domains, IP addresses, and certificates against known Iranian threat-actor infrastructure. Correlate ASNs, registrar patterns, and WHOIS data with historical Iranian APT campaigns (APT33, APT34, APT35). Alert on connections to infrastructure linked to these groups.

suggestion.title: ViewState Deserialization Attack - Known Machine Key
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes exploitation via 'identical pre-shared ASP.NET machine keys' used to 'sign malicious ViewState payloads' for RCE. This is the attack vector and should generate alerting on ASP.NET ViewState manipulation with known/leaked keys.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for ViewState payloads with MAC signatures that match known hardcoded KnowledgeDeliver machine keys or ASP.NET deserialization gadget chains in HTTP POST bodies. Alert on .aspx requests with large __VIEWSTATE parameters and successful HTTP 200 responses indicating code execution.

suggestion.title: Godzilla Web Shell Deployment Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'threat actor deployed the .NET-based in-memory web shell, Godzilla (a.k.a. BlueBeam)' and 'executed commands to escalate their control.' Need detection for Godzilla artifacts in memory and on disk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for suspicious .NET processes (aspnet_wp.exe, w3wp.exe) with abnormal network patterns characteristic of Godzilla's C&C communication. Look for in-memory .NET assemblies loaded via reflection without corresponding disk files. Monitor for attacker-controlled domains in web server process network logs.

suggestion.title: Cobalt Strike Beacon Delivery via Fake Installer
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'deployed...code that prompted users to install a "security authentication plugin" and...load a malicious script from a domain under the attacker's control' leading to 'Cobalt Strike beacon' infection. This is a two-stage execution chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on JavaScript modifications in web-accessible directories (wwwroot, app_data) that prompt users to download executables. Correlate suspicious .exe downloads from internal systems post-compromise. Monitor for parent-child process chains where browser launches installer executables outside normal software deployment paths.

suggestion.title: JavaScript Injection into Web Application Files
suggestion.rationale: Article details: 'allowed them to modify an application JavaScript file with code that prompted users to install a security authentication plugin.' This file modification is the attack's user-facing delivery mechanism and must be detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unsigned or anomalous modifications to .js files within web-accessible directories, especially those under w3wp.exe or aspnet_wp.exe process context. Flag changes that add new function definitions or external script loads. Baseline known .js file hashes and alert on any modifications outside normal deployment windows.

suggestion.title: Hardcoded Machine Key Usage in ViewState Cryptography
suggestion.rationale: Root cause identified: 'KnowledgeDeliver installations deployed before Feb. 24, 2026 relied on a standardized web.config file...containing hardcoded machineKey values.' Detecting use of default or known machine keys is preventive.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan deployed KnowledgeDeliver web.config files for machineKey elements. Cross-reference extracted decryption/validation keys against public/known default machine key lists. Alert if decryption key matches vendor-supplied defaults or previously leaked variants.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Web Server Process Network Activity Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'executed commands to escalate their control over the web server's file system,' implying command execution from the compromised process. Post-exploitation C&C communication should be detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual outbound DNS queries and connections initiated by w3wp.exe or aspnet_wp.exe to non-whitelisted external IPs/domains. Flag HTTP POST requests to attacker-controlled domains from web server processes. Baseline normal web server egress traffic and alert on deviations to suspicious TLDs or IPs.

suggestion.title: LMS post-authentication file upload to webroot
suggestion.rationale: Title states KnowledgeDeliver flaw was exploited to deploy malware—implies file upload or file-write capability to web-accessible directory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor KnowledgeDeliver application directories for unexpected file creation post-exploitation (PHP, ASPX, JSP to /uploads or webroot). Correlate with anomalous HTTP POST requests to admin or file-management endpoints immediately preceding file writes.

suggestion.title: Godzilla webshell command execution
suggestion.rationale: Godzilla is a known PHP webshell; article explicitly names it as deployed payload. Detect post-exploitation command execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag process spawning from web server processes (w3wp.exe, php.exe, apache2) with suspicious command-line tokens (cmd /c, powershell -enc). Match against webshell behavioral signatures (fork-bomb patterns, encoded POST parameters, reverse shells).

suggestion.title: Cobalt Strike HTTP(S) beacon C2 callbacks
suggestion.rationale: Article names Cobalt Strike as secondary payload deployed post-LMS exploitation. Detect beacon staging and communications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTPS traffic from unknown processes to dynamic-DNS or recently-registered domains. Correlate unusual /api or /submit requests with JITTER timing. Flag process memory signatures matching beacon injection (RWX regions, shellcode markers).

suggestion.title: LMS privilege escalation to admin context
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation of LMS typically requires elevation from unauthenticated or low-privilege user to admin or system context to deploy malware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for successful privilege escalation sequences: low-privilege web process spawning cmd/powershell with system or admin token; followed by service creation, registry persistence writes, or scheduled task registration.

suggestion.title: Rapid MFA Prompt Rejections Followed by Successful Authentication
suggestion.rationale: MFA prompt bombing succeeds when victims are overwhelmed into approving unauthorized requests; the pattern of multiple MFA denials followed by eventual acceptance (or approval after context-switching away) is a signature of successful bombing. Detection of this sequence is essential to catch the attack post-breach.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect user accounts experiencing 5+ MFA prompt rejections within 10 minutes, followed by a successful authentication on the same account from the same or adjacent IP. Alert if rejection-to-approval delta is <2 minutes (indicative of fatigue/capitulation). Filter out known MFA testing workflows.

suggestion.title: MFA Prompt Bombing via Step-Up Authentication Abuse
suggestion.rationale: MFA prompt bombing often exploits step-up authentication mechanisms in SaaS (requesting sensitive action re-auth, resource access, privilege escalation). Attackers trigger step-up prompts repeatedly to wear down user resistance. No use case should miss this variant.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect step-up authentication prompts (e.g., Office 365 'additional verification required' for sensitive Graph API calls, Azure PIM activation requests) triggered >3 times in 15 minutes for the same user/resource pair. Correlate with successful access grant immediately after to surface exploitation.

suggestion.title: MFA Fatigue Attack via Push Notification Flood
suggestion.rationale: The attack explicitly leverages notification flooding (push notifications to mobile/device) to desensitize users to legitimate authentication warnings. Detection must flag abnormal MFA push frequency per user/device.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect >10 MFA push notifications sent to a single user's enrolled device(s) within a 5-minute window where user either denies all or approves anomalously. Flag especially if source IPs differ (attacker triggering from multiple vectors) or if genuine step-up auth workflows are not in flight.

suggestion.title: Anomalous MFA Device Registration or Trusted Device Abuse Post-Bombing
suggestion.rationale: Successful MFA bombing may be followed by registering attacker-controlled devices as 'trusted' or bypassing MFA for future sessions. Pipeline should detect post-bombing device additions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect new device registration or trusted-device enrollment on an account that experienced MFA bombing (high reject-to-approve ratio) within the preceding 30 minutes. Correlate with subsequent sign-ins from that new device with MFA bypass or degraded MFA enforcement.

suggestion.title: Cross-Tenant MFA Bombing in MSP/Federation Environments
suggestion.rationale: If article discusses federated identity or multi-tenant SaaS attack patterns, attackers may coordinate bombing across multiple tenants to map target organizations and user bases. No cross-tenant correlation use case is evident.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect clusters of MFA prompts across multiple distinct tenants or federated IdP realms targeting the same user principal name or email address within a 30-minute window. Flag if prompts originate from different threat actors' source IPs or if tenant switching is atypical for the user's normal SSO flow.

suggestion.title: MFA Bombing Reconnaissance via Invalid Credentials + MFA Trigger
suggestion.rationale: Attackers may probe whether a target has MFA enabled by sending invalid credentials repeatedly; if MFA prompts fire, they know MFA is active and begin bombing. Detection of invalid-cred-then-valid-cred sequences with MFA is a reconnaissance pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect a sequence of 3+ failed authentications (invalid password) for a user, immediately followed (within 2 minutes) by a successful authentication with MFA prompts firing, originating from the same or adjacent IP. This pattern indicates attacker MFA enumeration followed by bombing attempt.

suggestion.title: Automatic Device Isolation Event Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'When a device in your organization is suspected to be compromised, Microsoft Defender for Endpoint can automatically isolate the device.' A detection use case should monitor for when isolation events fire and alert SOC teams.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Defender for Endpoint logs for automatic isolation events triggered by compromise detection. Alert when a device transitions to isolated state without manual operator action, correlating with antecedent threat signals (malware detection, suspicious behavior score elevation).

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Attempt During Network Isolation
suggestion.rationale: Article states isolation helps 'limit attacker lateral movement' and 'prevent impacts such as data exfiltration and ransomware propagation.' Detection should identify lateral movement probes from isolated devices.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect network connection attempts from compromised isolated endpoints to other network resources. Baseline and alert on outbound connection attempts (RDP, SMB, WinRM, SSH) from devices flagged as automatically isolated within the last N minutes.

suggestion.title: Ransomware Execution Post-Compromise Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'prevent impacts such as...ransomware propagation' as a key isolation benefit. Detection should trigger on behaviors indicating ransomware stage post-detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file encryption activity, bulk file writes, file extension changes, and high-entropy writes on devices flagged as compromised before automatic isolation occurs. Correlate with isolation event timing to validate defense timing.

suggestion.title: Compromised User Account Lateral Movement (Hands-on-Keyboard Attack)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Defender for Endpoint could also isolate compromised user accounts as part of automatic attack disruption to block lateral movement in hands-on-keyboard ransomware attacks.' Detection should flag suspicious account activity patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify anomalous user account activity patterns on compromised endpoints: unusual logon hours, new interactive sessions from suspicious geographies, enumeration commands (net group, Get-ADUser), or failed authentication sprays within isolation window.

suggestion.title: Network Isolation Persistence Verification
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies isolated endpoints 'retain connectivity to the Microsoft Defender for Endpoint service' while disconnected from network. Detection should verify isolation is maintained and Defender connectivity persists.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthorized re-connection attempts from isolated devices to corporate network resources (shares, domain controllers, gateways). Alert on firewall bypass attempts, DNS poisoning, or out-of-band C2 channels used to circumvent isolation.

suggestion.title: Undiscovered Endpoint Breach Prevention (Traffic Block Detection)
suggestion.rationale: Article states feature 'automatically blocks traffic to and from undiscovered Windows endpoints, preventing attackers from breaching other non-compromised devices.' Detection should identify blocked lateral movement attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for dropped or blocked connection attempts from compromised managed endpoints to unmanaged/undiscovered systems on the network. Correlate blocked traffic with device isolation events and enumerate discovered targets to assess exposure.

suggestion.title: Chatbot Response Contains Suspicious External URL Redirect
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'chatbot recommendations redirect users'—pipeline must detect when chatbot responses include unexpected external URLs or redirect services not on whitelist.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor chatbot output payloads for unexpected external URLs, especially to freshly registered domains, privacy-protected registrations, or known shortener/redirect services. Correlate response timestamp with downstream user HTTP requests to confirm redirect following.

suggestion.title: Post-Chatbot-Interaction Cryptomining Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes endpoint reaching 'cryptojacking malware sites'—pipeline should correlate chatbot interaction with anomalous process execution (high CPU, known miner binary names, unusual parent-child chains).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag process execution of known cryptominers (XMRig, Monero, cpuminer variants) or CPU-intensive obfuscated scripts launched within 10 minutes of chatbot session. Alert on unusual parent processes (browser, curl, powershell) spawning mining processes.

suggestion.title: Chatbot System Prompt or Configuration Injection Enabling Malicious Recommendations
suggestion.rationale: For chatbot to consistently redirect, its prompt/configuration must be altered. Article implies sustained attack, requiring backend compromise or prompt injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor chatbot configuration change logs for unauthorized edits to system prompts, response templates, or URL recommendation logic. Detect anomalous API calls authenticating as service accounts with permission to modify chatbot directives.

suggestion.title: Cryptojacking Malware Domain Reputation and Registration Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Domains in redirect chain must exhibit characteristics of adversary infrastructure. Article says 'cryptojacking malware sites'—implies known or soon-to-be-known malware C2/delivery infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Extract and analyze domains from chatbot responses or proxy logs against VirusTotal, URLhaus, and cryptojacking-specific feeds (Monero pool blocklists, MalwareBazaar). Flag domains registered <30 days ago, WHOIS-private, or hosted on known bulletproof hosters.

suggestion.title: Outbound Network Connections to Cryptomining Pool Servers
suggestion.rationale: Cryptojacking malware connects to mining pools—article users must eventually connect to miner infrastructure once code executes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound TCP/UDP connections to known Monero or other cryptomining pool IP ranges and domains (stratum, mining.monero.hashvault patterns). Correlate with process execution of miners and user endpoints showing elevated outbound bytes.

suggestion.title: BadHost Exploitation Attempt — HTTP Request Signatures
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'Attackers Can Exploit BadHost to Access Sensitive AI Agent Server Endpoints'; no detection was generated for exploitation vectors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor AI agent server endpoints for HTTP requests matching BadHost exploitation signatures (malformed headers, specific URI patterns, or payload structures). Flag successful (HTTP 200) responses to sensitive endpoints following anomalous request patterns.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Access to Sensitive AI Agent Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly references 'Access Sensitive AI Agent Server Endpoints'; pipeline failed to propose endpoint-access monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on access to high-risk AI agent endpoints (/admin, /config, /api/keys, /model/, /agent/state) from unexpected source IPs, non-standard user agents, or with elevated request frequency within short time window.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Lateral Movement from Compromised AI Agent Server
suggestion.rationale: Critical-severity vulnerability enabling agent server compromise should trigger lateral-movement detections; none were suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound connections from compromised AI agent servers to internal infrastructure (RDP 3389, SSH 22, internal APIs). Flag unusual destination subnets or repeated connection attempts to multiple hosts.

suggestion.title: Detect Password Spraying Attacks via Excessive Failed Logins
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'Password spraying attacks rely on exploiting that tendency' (weak password choices), establishing that spraying is a real threat organizations must detect. No corresponding use case was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for multiple failed login attempts across different user accounts in a short time window, originating from the same source. Password spraying typically attempts many accounts with few guesses each. Alert when failed-login count per source exceeds threshold (e.g., 20+ unique accounts in 5 minutes).

suggestion.title: Monitor for Compromised Password Creation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'By continuously checking passwords against a database of over 5.4 billion known breached credentials, Specops Password Policy helps stop compromised passwords from being used in AD'. This implies organizations should detect attempts to set known-breached passwords.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Log password change/reset attempts and compare against breached password lists. Flag attempts to use passwords known to exist in public breach databases. Correlate failed password-change rejections with policy-check logs.

suggestion.title: Detect Weak or Predictable Password Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article warns: 'users are still likely to choose weak or common options' and recommends 'Creating custom banned word lists' to prevent them. This describes a detection opportunity for attempts to use common/weak passwords that violate policy.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor password-change requests for patterns indicating weak choices (common words, repeated characters, incremental changes like 'Pass1!' → 'Pass2!'). Alert on rejected password-change attempts due to policy violations when user retries immediately.

suggestion.title: Detect Unusual Password Reset Frequency or Self-Service Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article discusses 'Implement self-service password resets' and mentions users may resort to 'workarounds' when frustrated. Monitors should detect if self-service reset endpoints are being abused or reset rates are anomalously high per user.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track password reset frequency per user. Alert on users resetting passwords multiple times in a single day or beyond normal baseline. Correlate with failed-login attempts before reset to identify potential account takeover or credential spray recovery patterns.

suggestion.title: Detect Credential Reuse Across Systems
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Even when employees create a good AD password, they're likely to repeat it across other systems'. Organizations should detect when AD credentials appear in logs from non-AD systems, indicating likely reuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-correlate successful logins across multiple systems and services using the same username. Flag when a single account successfully authenticates to both AD and external applications within a short window, suggesting credential reuse. Baseline per user and alert on anomalies.

suggestion.title: Detect Account Lockouts from Failed Password Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article implies account lockout is a consequence of strict policies: 'make the rules too weak and you increase your attack surface; make them too strict and users will find workarounds'. Lockouts from spraying or guessing attacks should be detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for clusters of account lockouts within a short timeframe across multiple users (indicating spraying). Correlate lockout events with preceding failed-login events to distinguish legitimate user error from coordinated attacks.

suggestion.title: Detect CVE-2026-48172 exploitation via cpanel_jsonapi_func=redisAble invocation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly provides vendor detection: 'grep -rE "cpanel_jsonapi_func=redisAble" /var/cpanel/logs /usr/local/cpanel/logs/'. This concrete IoC pattern for active exploitation was entirely missed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor /var/cpanel/logs and /usr/local/cpanel/logs for pattern cpanel_jsonapi_func=redisAble. Extract source IPs and timestamp. Flag as active exploitation attempt. Cross-correlate against firewall/WAF logs for additional context on request source.

suggestion.title: Detect root privilege execution from LiteSpeed Redis mishandling
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability explicitly enables 'remote attackers with no privileges to execute arbitrary scripts with root privileges' via 'mishandling of Redis enable/disable features in lsws.redisAble function'. Privilege escalation pathway not modeled.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for spawning of child processes with root/UID 0 credentials originating from LiteSpeed/cPanel plugin processes. Correlate with Redis configuration/enable-disable operations. Alert on privilege jump from unprivileged cPanel API context to root shell execution.

suggestion.title: Block and investigate active exploitation IPs per CISA directive
suggestion.rationale: Article directs: 'If this command results in any output, we recommend you examine the IPs in the list, determine if they are valid, and if not, block them.' Tactical IP-level indicator response entirely absent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Extract source IPs from all cpanel_jsonapi_func=redisAble hits. Cross-reference against internal IP ranges and known legitimate services. Block non-whitelisted sources at firewall/WAF layer. Flag repeated attempts from same IP for incident escalation.

suggestion.title: Detect post-exploitation system activity following CVE-2026-48172
suggestion.rationale: Article advises: 'examine the system logs for any actions taken by the detected IPs' — post-compromise forensics window. No secondary-impact detection use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For IPs confirmed attacking via cpanel_jsonapi_func=redisAble, monitor all subsequent system events within 24-48hr window. Look for: new user creation, file modifications in critical dirs, persistence mechanisms (cron, systemd, .bashrc), reverse shells, or data exfiltration. Correlate timeline to exploitation timestamp.

suggestion.title: Monitor for LiteSpeed cPanel plugin version v2.3-v2.4.4 (vulnerable range)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'vulnerability is being actively exploited, and poses a risk for all user-end plugin versions between v2.3 and v2.4.4'. Affected version inventory check not proposed despite CISA mandate to patch by May 29.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate LiteSpeed cPanel user-end plugin version across all monitored servers. Flag any instances with version string matching v2.3.* through v2.4.4. Correlate vulnerable instances against exploitation logs to prioritize response. Validate patching completion post-deadline.

suggestion.title: Detect remote unauthenticated access to cPanel JSON API redisAble endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector is 'remote attackers with no privileges' — implies network-reachable API endpoint accepting requests from unauthorized callers. API-layer detection not captured.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor cPanel JSON API endpoints for requests to redisAble function from external/untrusted sources. Look for missing or invalid session tokens, OR requests from IPs outside corporate ranges. Flag rapid sequences of failed then successful API calls as potential brute/exploit attempts.

suggestion.title: npm Package Hash/Version Anomaly on TanStack
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'malicious versions...published to the npm registry.' Pipeline generated zero supply-chain detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package-lock.json and yarn.lock for TanStack entries. Alert when package hash differs from organizational baseline or when installed version does not match pinned manifest. Cross-check against npm registry metadata for publish timestamp anomalies.

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration Post-TanStack Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'credential-stealing malware under a trusted identity.' Pipeline has no credential-access detection despite explicit payload description.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After npm install/update of TanStack (cross-reference DeviceProcessEvents for npm activity), monitor Node.js processes for outbound HTTP POST requests containing base64-encoded or key-value credential patterns, particularly to non-corporate destinations.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-45321 Active Exploitation - Vulnerability Scanner Alert
