suggestion.rationale: Article names CVE-2026-45321 and cites CISA KEV status (actively exploited). Pipeline extracted zero CVE IOCs despite explicit vulnerability ID.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when vulnerability scanner detects CVE-2026-45321 presence. Escalate high priority given CISA KEV status and 2026-06-10 remediation deadline. Verify patch application within 48 hours if critical asset.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Child Process from node_modules TanStack Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'credential-stealing malware' injected into package. Pipeline missed execution-phase detection for code from package directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process creation originating from node_modules/tanstack or node_modules/.bin paths. Alert on processes spawning shells, network utilities, or accessing credential/environment variable files.

suggestion.title: npm Registry Package Substitution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'published...under a trusted identity.' Pipeline failed to capture package substitution/typosquatting vector in supply-chain attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install logs for downgrades to known-compromised TanStack versions or installs from non-standard mirrors. Alert if package.json version constraint resolves to unexpected semver range that includes vulnerable builds.

suggestion.title: Memory-Based Credential Access from Application Using TanStack
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'credential-stealing malware' payload. Pipeline has no detection for in-process credential harvesting mechanisms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate npm/Node.js process memory access patterns (lsass reads, /proc/*/environ access, API key enumeration from process environment) with recent TanStack installs. Flag unusual credential store access or environment variable reads.

suggestion.title: Nx Console Installation from Malicious Source
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'a malicious version of Nx Console to be published' but pipeline generated no initial-access detection. Should detect installation of compromised extension versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Nx Console package installation or extension registry writes from untrusted sources or with unusual version strings. Check package manifests for obfuscated code or unexpected dependencies that deviate from Nx official distributions.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting from Process Memory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states payload 'harvested credentials from multiple sources on disk and in memory' but no memory-access detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag processes spawned by Nx Console (or Node.js runtime) that attempt to read sensitive memory regions or enumerate process handles. Look for API calls to ReadProcessMemory, QueryInformationProcess, or similar credential-store access patterns (DPAPI, SecureString APIs, browser storage paths).

suggestion.title: Obfuscated Payload Execution within Nx Console Context
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'fetched an obfuscated payload' but no defense-evasion or execution detection emerged. Obfuscated code is a behavioral signature for malicious software.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect obfuscated JavaScript/Node.js code execution within Nx Console or its extension process (e.g., eval, Function constructors, Base64-decoded exec payloads). Correlate with unusual network calls or child-process spawning from extension context.

suggestion.title: Credential File Access Patterns (Disk-based Harvesting)
suggestion.rationale: Article notes credentials harvested 'from multiple sources on disk' but no file-access detection targeting common credential stores was suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Nx Console and its child processes for reads to sensitive credential locations: ~/.ssh/, ~/.aws/, ~/.azure/, ~/.docker, browser profile directories, system credential stores. Flag sequential or batch reads of multiple credential types.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Network Exfiltration by Nx Console Extension
suggestion.rationale: Credential harvesting implies exfiltration but pipeline surfaced no C2 or exfiltration detection. Article's 'fetched payload' suggests command-and-control communication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected outbound connections from Nx Console extension process to non-Nx domains, especially to newly registered domains or IPs with no historical traffic. Look for HTTPS POST requests with compressed or encoded bodies (credential exfil signature).

suggestion.title: Daemon Tools Lite Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'it's worth one quick check across your fleet — patch lag is the silent killer,' implying deployed instances should be inventoried regardless of patch status. Asset exposure is the canonical initial-access detection for KEV entries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Daemon Tools Lite process execution or DLL loading (daemontools.exe, daemon.exe, or related child processes). Cross-reference against vulnerability scanner to identify unpatched or incorrectly-assumed-patched instances.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-8398 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'CVE: CVE-2026-8398' as hunt input. Standard vulnerability detection for known-exploited CVE with federal patch deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any vulnerability scan result matching CVE-2026-8398 against Daemon Tools Lite. Prioritize systems with >30 days patch lag as high-risk, especially approaching 2026-05-30 deadline.

suggestion.title: Daemon Tools Lite Installed Packages (Software Inventory)
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' and CISA KEV status means active in-the-wild exploitation. Software inventory sweep is prerequisite to risk assessment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all systems with Daemon Tools Lite installed via SCCM, WMI, or registry queries. Flag any version <2026-05-30 patch level or where patch application cannot be confirmed.

suggestion.title: Detect BOLA/IDOR Resource Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly discusses BOLA and IDOR as context-dependent vulnerabilities with the example 'User A should not be able to read User B's invoice'—a clear authorization bypass pattern requiring access anomaly detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequences of API or web requests from a single source targeting multiple user/tenant resources they lack authorization for. Look for rapid 40x/401/403 responses followed by successful 200 responses to resources outside their permission scope, or enumeration of object IDs belonging to other users.

suggestion.title: Detect Horizontal Privilege Escalation Chains
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'chained vulnerabilities, where a couple of mediums and highs combine into a critical exploit path'—requires detection of multi-step escalation combining low-impact auth or access anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect correlated sequences of authentication boundary tests (failed MFA attempts, alternate auth paths, API token reuse) followed by privilege elevation or cross-boundary resource access within a 5-minute window from the same source.

suggestion.title: Detect API Reconnaissance and Escalation Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article describes pentesting methodology as 'recon, probe, observe, reason, escalate, validate'—these sequential steps are observable in API access logs when an attacker or scanner systematically enumerates endpoints and parameters.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect API/web session containing: (1) high-volume distinct endpoint requests (>50 unique paths in 10 min), (2) parameter fuzzing (varying IDs, tokens, headers), (3) escalating HTTP methods (GET→POST→DELETE), and (4) response time analysis behavior (probing for timing sidechannels).

suggestion.title: Detect Authentication Bypass Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 'authentication bypasses' as a context-dependent vulnerability class requiring proactive detection independent of signature-based rules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect failed authentication attempts followed immediately by valid session establishment without credential re-submission, or successful access to authenticated endpoints without completing required MFA/SAML/OAuth flows.

suggestion.title: Detect Cross-Tenant Data Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies 'cross-tenant data leakage' as a vulnerability requiring context-aware detection that cannot be achieved through simple payload matching.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect requests accessing resource paths or tenant identifiers inconsistent with the requestor's assigned tenant context, including API calls with customer_id or account_id parameters mismatched to the authenticated user's organization.

suggestion.title: Detect Continuous Automated Testing/Scanning
suggestion.rationale: Article frames the threat model as 'autonomous attackers probing application surfaces continuously at machine speed'—requiring detection of sustained, systematic probe patterns distinct from human user activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sustained API or web session activity exhibiting: regular request timing intervals (±10s variance), identical User-Agent/header fingerprints, consistent source IP, requests to non-existent endpoints, and absence of human UI interaction patterns (mouse movements, form timings).

suggestion.title: Phishing Email - IT Help Desk Impersonation with Callback Lure
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'send phishing emails to urge employees to call the SRG actor posing as IT support.' Core attack vector never surfaced.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails claiming urgent IT support issues, requesting callbacks to suspicious numbers, or containing credential-request subjects. Watch for mass campaigns targeting law firm/financial verticals. Cross-reference against known IT help desk contact numbers.

suggestion.title: Remote Desktop Protocol Access - Unusual Credential or Time Window
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'directs the employee to grant access to a remote desktop session.' RDP compromise is the in-band attack path before physical fallback.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on RDP successful logons with non-standard credentials, outside business hours, or from untrusted subnets. Correlate with recent phishing or vishing campaigns. Flag sessions with file copy operations or access to sensitive shares.

suggestion.title: USB/External Storage Device Connection - Unauthorized Media
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'insert a storage device into the victim's computer' and 'unauthorized installation of external hard drives or USB drives on company computers' are explicit indicators and a collection/exfiltration signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Windows USB device insertion events (SetupAPI logs, Event ID 20001) and external drive mounting. Alert on mass file copy operations to removable media, especially from high-value data repositories (legal docs, financial records). Baseline normal removable media usage and flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: In-Person Physical Access Claim - Impersonation of IT Staff
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'SRG sends a threat actor to the victim's location' and 'presence of unidentified or unauthorized individuals claiming to be IT support and attempting to access computers.' Physical presence is the fallback when remote fails.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Escalate employee reports of unknown IT support personnel requesting system access. Cross-check badge logs against IT roster; flag visitors without entry authorization attempting office access. Monitor for new badge registrations with IT job titles correlated to unknown individuals.

suggestion.title: Extortion Communication - Ransom Email and Pressure Calls
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'sending a ransom email that threatens to sell or post it on their leak site, and will also call the victims' employees or clients to pressure them.' Post-breach extortion is the impact and confirms data exfiltration success.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails threatening data sale/publication and referencing internal documents or systems. Alert on coordinated phone campaigns to employee/client lists from external numbers. Monitor dark web leak sites for SRG domain/forum posts matching victim organization names.

suggestion.title: Domain Registration - Typosquatted IT Support Portals
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'register domains to impersonate IT helpdesk or support portals for major U.S. law firms and financial services firms, using typosquatted patterns.' Domains are phishing/credential capture infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS queries and HTTP traffic for typosquatted IT helpdesk domains (e.g., 'helpdesk-mycompany.com' vs 'helpdesk.mycompany.com'). Alert on clicks/redirects from phishing emails to newly registered domains. Correlate passive DNS registrations of lookalike domains against known SRG campaigns.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email with FIFA/World Cup Lures
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes phishing campaign targeting FIFA World Cup fans. Emails are the delivery vector for this campaign.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify inbound emails containing FIFA, World Cup, or soccer tournament keywords paired with suspicious sender domains, URL shorteners, or urgent action language. Cross-reference links against known malicious domain infrastructure for this campaign.

suggestion.title: User Access to Suspicious FIFA-Themed Domains
suggestion.rationale: The campaign leverages 300+ fake domains, requiring detection of traffic to these infrastructure assets. Article states domains target World Cup fans, implying credential harvesting landing pages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS queries and HTTP connections to recently-registered domains with FIFA, World Cup, ticketing, or account-related keywords. Flag domains with suspicious WHOIS profiles or registered outside official FIFA infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Bulk Domain Registration for Phishing Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Campaign operationalized 300+ domains within likely short timeframe. Detection of bulk malicious domain registration patterns identifies threat actor infrastructure buildout.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect clusters of domain registrations sharing FIFA, World Cup, or tournament-related keywords registered concurrently from same registrant, registrar, or payment method. Cross-reference with known bulletproof hosting or high-abuse registrars.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting via Replica Ticketing Portal
suggestion.rationale: Phishing campaigns targeting sports fans typically host replica account/ticketing login pages on fake domains. Article's scale (300+ domains) suggests credential exfiltration infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify HTTP POST requests to suspicious domains hosting forms that mimic FIFA.com or official World Cup ticketing portals. Flag domains with high similarity scores to legitimate tournament sites.

suggestion.title: Yamcs HTTP PATCH algorithm endpoint with Java Process/Runtime keywords
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'dynamically compiles and evaluates user-controlled algorithm text without enforcing a secure sandbox.' Delivery requires PATCH to algorithm endpoint containing Runtime.getRuntime(), ProcessBuilder, or Process class references—intersection of HTTP delivery + malicious payload signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag PATCH requests to /api/mdb/*/algorithms/* containing Java Process API keywords (Runtime.getRuntime, ProcessBuilder, exec, java.lang.Process). Baseline legitimate algorithm usage first to reduce false positives.

suggestion.title: Yamcs authentication as ChangeMissionDatabase-privileged user followed by algorithm modification
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'An authenticated user with the ChangeMissionDatabase privilege can exploit this.' Sequence detection: user authenticates, gains/already has this privilege, then issues algorithm PATCH within 5-10 minutes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid sequence of (1) user authentication to Yamcs, (2) role assignment/elevation to ChangeMissionDatabase privilege, (3) algorithm PATCH API call. Flag if pattern occurs outside business hours or by previously inactive user account.

suggestion.title: Janino compiler invocation or exception anomaly in Yamcs logs
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'Janino Expression Engine' and 'dynamically compiles.' Failed compilations or unusual Janino exceptions in application logs may indicate code injection attempt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on elevated frequency or new patterns in Janino compilation failures, SecurityException, or ClassCompilationException. Baseline normal Janino exception rates by Yamcs deployment first.

suggestion.title: Yamcs MDB file modification outside documented API procedures
suggestion.rationale: Attack requires modifying algorithms in mission database. Direct filesystem writes to MDB directory (*.yaml, algorithm XML) without corresponding PATCH API call may indicate API bypass or direct database manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Yamcs MDB directory for FileCreated/FileModified events. Flag if algorithm configuration files change without corresponding HTTP PATCH request in Web logs within ±5 minute window.

suggestion.title: LiquidJS template injection pattern detection in HTTP body/parameters
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes exploit via 'crafted templates' with `{%assign r=1|valueOf%}{{r|inspect}}` syntax. No UC detects inbound HTTP POST/PUT bodies containing liquid template syntax patterns (braces with percent signs, filter pipes). This is initial-access detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound HTTP POST/PUT/PATCH bodies and parameters for LiquidJS template syntax: regex patterns matching `\{%.*%\}`, `\{\{.*\}\}`, `\|valueOf`, `\|inspect` combined with requests to known LiquidJS app endpoints. Baseline on legitimate template traffic if the app uses LiquidJS intentionally.

suggestion.title: Node.js process spawning shell with high entropy command-line arguments
suggestion.rationale: Article's `1|valueOf` exploit allows arbitrary code execution; attacker would need to encode or obfuscate shell commands. UC_3_3 detects shell spawning but doesn't check for encoded/obfuscated payloads in the command line itself.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Node.js spawning shell processes (sh/bash/powershell) where the child process command-line contains high Shannon entropy strings, base64-encoded payloads, or hex escapes — indicators of obfuscation common in template-injection exploits.

suggestion.title: LiquidJS process accessing sensitive files immediately after startup
suggestion.rationale: Article shows proof-of-concept accessing `this` context and `liquid.options` properties. Post-exploitation, attacker would likely read sensitive files. UC_3_1 detects /etc/passwd but doesn't connect file access to LiquidJS process initialization timing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate node.js process creation with subsequent file access to /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, ~/.ssh, /proc/self/environ within 5 seconds, indicating post-RCE reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: Outbound DNS or network connection from Node.js after shell execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes RCE capability but does not detail post-exploitation network behavior. Attacker would likely establish C2 or exfil data. UC_3_3 covers shell spawning but doesn't detect follow-on network indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect DNS queries or outbound TCP/UDP connections initiated by Node.js process or its child shell after shell spawning event; correlate with URL reputation and known C2 domains.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Container Image Fetch from Gitea Registry
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'Exposes Private Container Images without Authentication'—core attack is pulling images without credentials via registry API. Pipeline missed this.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor container registry endpoints (/v2/*) for GET requests lacking Authorization headers or with invalid tokens. Alert on sequences of manifest + blob requests from single unauthenticated source targeting private namespaces.

suggestion.title: Gitea Registry Authentication Bypass Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: 'Without Authentication' indicates exploitation of auth bypass flaw. Should detect initial attack attempts exploiting the CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Gitea /api/v1/ and /v2/ endpoints for requests missing or with malformed authentication. Flag 401→200 patterns or requests to sensitive endpoints from unauthenticated sessions.

suggestion.title: Private Container Image Enumeration via Unauthenticated Catalog Access
suggestion.rationale: Attackers enumerate private images before exfiltration. Article implies metadata visibility—'exposes' suggests catalog/tag disclosure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor /v2/_catalog and namespace endpoints for unauthenticated requests. Alert on successful image/tag enumeration from private repositories.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Gitea Version Fingerprinting
suggestion.rationale: Threat actors fingerprint Gitea version to identify vulnerable instances. Pipeline should surface version disclosure vectors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor responses from Gitea instances for version headers (Server: Gitea/X.X.X) and requests to /.well-known or /api/v1/version endpoints. Track port scanning + version collection patterns.

suggestion.title: Bulk Layer Download from Private Container Registry
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation results in downloading private image layers (blobs). Article severity and scope ('high', 'private images') suggest data exfiltration concern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on multiple sequential blob download requests (/v2/*/blobs/*) from single unauthenticated source to private repositories. Monitor for large cumulative transfer volume.

suggestion.title: Exposed Container Registry Credentials via Unauthenticated API
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability may expose stored credentials, tokens, or secrets in API responses. Pipeline should detect credential leakage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor /api/v1/* endpoints for unauthenticated responses containing auth tokens, registry passwords, or pull-secret values. Alert on sensitive field exposure in error messages or config endpoints.

suggestion.title: Malicious VSCode/OpenVSX Extension Installation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'malicious OpenVSX and Microsoft VS Code extensions that stole cryptocurrency wallets and developer credentials' as primary initial access vector since October 2025; later extended to GitHub repositories and npm packages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor VSCode extension installation events for known malicious package names/hashes. Track extension marketplace API calls and package downloads from OpenVSX/VS Code Marketplace. Alert on extensions requesting unexpected scopes (wallet APIs, credential storage, git operations). Correlate with development environment telemetry.

suggestion.title: Dormant Extension Activation Trigger Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Glassworm operators planted dozens of dormant extensions on OpenVSX that would activate the malicious component after an update'—requires detection of delayed payload execution tied to update events.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected process spawning or file writes immediately following VSCode/extension auto-updates. Monitor for extension activation hooks triggered by version bumps. Flag dormant code becoming active post-update; correlate update timestamps with outbound connections.

suggestion.title: Solana Blockchain C2 Query Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes: 'C2 server addresses are encoded in the memo fields of blockchain transactions, creating an immutable, publicly accessible dead drop.' GlasswormRAT queries Solana for command delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound HTTPS to Solana blockchain RPC endpoints (api.mainnet-beta.solana.com, etc.). Detect blockchain transaction queries with specific address patterns. Correlate Solana API calls with malware process lineage. Alert on hex/encoded data extraction from transaction memo fields.

suggestion.title: BitTorrent DHT Configuration Retrieval Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'GlasswormRAT queries the BitTorrent peer-to-peer network for configuration data stored against hardcoded public keys, leveraging a global decentralized network with no single point of failure.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect BitTorrent DHT get_peer or find_node queries from suspicious/malware processes. Monitor for DHT traffic from non-torrent applications (VSCode, browsers, developer tools). Flag DHT queries with consistent hardcoded key patterns. Correlate with known malware process signatures.

suggestion.title: Google Calendar Dead-Drop C2 Communication Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'Glassworm uses Google Calendar event titles as dead-drop locations for Base64-encoded C2 paths'—a legitimate service abuse for obfuscated command delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Calendar API calls from suspicious processes or VSCode extension contexts. Detect Base64 decode operations adjacent to Calendar reads. Flag unusual calendar event enumeration from development workstations. Alert on calendar queries returning command-like strings (URLs, code, parameters).

suggestion.title: CrowdStrike Sinkhole Beacon to 164.92.88.210
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'Following the disruption, all machines compromised in a Glassworm attack are beaconing to the IP address 164.92.88[.]210 operated by CrowdStrike'—direct post-takedown victim identification IOC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag all outbound connections to 164.92.88.210 as confirmed Glassworm compromise indicator. Correlate beacon source IPs with internal threat-hunt scope. Track beacon frequency/volume to assess infection currency. Cross-reference with VSCode/extension process trees for infection vector confirmation.

suggestion.title: Detect Malicious Developer Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Developer Supply Chain Attack Infrastructure'—implies compromised or malicious packages distributed to developers. Pipeline missed detection for package manager activity installing known-bad versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package manager (pip, npm, cargo, nuget) installation events for package names or versions associated with GlassWorm or known compromised repositories. Correlate with unusual installation locations or subsequent child process spawning.

suggestion.title: Detect GlassWorm Command & Control Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article title references 'takedown' of 'infrastructure'—implies C2 sinkholed or seized. Pipeline should surface detection for outbound connections to infrastructure IOCs or hardcoded callback domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on DNS queries or outbound connections to known GlassWorm C2 domains or IP ranges formerly hosted by takedown operation. Flag hosts attempting beaconing even post-sinkhole.

suggestion.title: Detect Malicious Payload Execution from Developer Tool Artifacts
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks via developer tools suggest execution phase from compromised source. No use case generated for detecting suspicious execution spawned by package contents or build-time artifacts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child processes spawned by package installation or build steps with unsigned binaries, obfuscated command lines, or unusual DLL loads. Alert on processes launched from temporary or package cache directories with suspicious parent lineage.

suggestion.title: Detect Supply Chain Artifact Tampering or Unauthorized Package Metadata
suggestion.rationale: Article implies infrastructure was used to host or validate compromised packages. Pipeline missed detection for package registry anomalies (new versions, metadata changes, unsigned releases).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sudden new package versions without source history, missing or mismatched cryptographic signatures, or metadata changes (maintainer, dependencies) on packages in target namespace.

suggestion.title: Grandoreiro Banking Trojan Execution and Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names Grandoreiro as a banking trojan targeting Windows; no execution or persistence detection rules generated. Banking trojans consistently use process injection, registry Run/RunOnce modifications, and obfuscated script execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Grandoreiro execution signatures: rundll32/powershell spawning from suspicious parents with obfuscated command lines, registry modifications to HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run*, and suspicious DLL loads from temp/AppData directories.

suggestion.title: BTMOB RAT Command and Control Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: BTMOB RAT named in title targeting both Windows and Android; no IOCs or C2 communication detection rules provided despite RAT's dependence on persistent C2 channels.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect BTMOB C2 communication via anomalous outbound connections to non-standard ports, DNS queries to recently registered/low-reputation domains, and binary protocol traffic inconsistent with legitimate Windows services.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting via Keylogging and Form Injection
suggestion.rationale: Grandoreiro is a documented banking credential stealer; article indicates credential targeting but no detection rules for keylogger hooks, web-form grabbing, or browser manipulation were generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious process injection patterns characteristic of banking trojans: GetWindowsHookEx API calls for keyboard capture, suspicious browser process spawning, and temporary file writes matching malware unpacking signatures.

suggestion.title: Mobile Trojanized APK Installation and Permission Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions Android targeting; pipeline generated no mobile IOCs or detection rules. Trojanized APKs require behavioral detection on app install, suspicious permission grants, and privilege escalation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect trojanized APK installation on Android: apps masquerading as legitimate banking software, apps requesting SEND_SMS/READ_CONTACTS/RECORD_AUDIO without user awareness, and apps with suspicious privilege escalation attempts.

suggestion.title: Phishing/Email-Based Malware Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Grandoreiro and BTMOB campaigns typically initiate via phishing emails; no initial-access detection for email attachments, malicious links, or credential-harvest emails generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for phishing emails containing Grandoreiro/BTMOB signatures: macro-enabled Office documents from external senders, suspicious URL shorteners, and payloads matching known banking-trojan delivery infrastructure.

suggestion.title: DLL Sideloading Detection (autorun.dll, vcredist_x64.dll)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes DLL sideloading payload: 'autorun.dll - Activates when legitimate executable launches' and 'vcredist_x64.dll - Deploys ScreenConnect for remote access'. This is the primary execution vector for remote access and persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual DLL loads of autorun.dll or vcredist_x64.dll, particularly when spawned from legitimate utility executables (CrystalDiskInfo, HWMonitor, FurMark). Detect DLL search order hijacking patterns and unsigned DLLs in system paths.

suggestion.title: Defender Configuration Evasion via Exclusion Path
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'configures Defender exclusions'. This direct defensive-evasion action leaves detectable registry and process artifacts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on PowerShell/cmd.exe invocations containing 'Add-MpPreference', 'ExclusionPath', or WMI method calls modifying Windows Defender configuration. Monitor HKLM\\SOFTWARE\\Microsoft\\Windows Defender for exclusion key creation.

suggestion.title: Process Hollowing Activity Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies SimpleRunPE 'executes mining code via process hollowing'. This advanced code-injection technique exhibits detectable memory-write patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process creation of legitimate system binaries (svchost, explorer) followed by abnormal memory write operations, particularly when succeeded by unexpected child processes or no network activity baseline.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Registry Run Keys and Scheduled Tasks
suggestion.rationale: Article describes SimpleRunPE establishing 'persistence through Registry Run keys and scheduled tasks'. These are standard persistence mechanisms requiring continuous monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for schtasks.exe or WMI scheduled task creation with obfuscated or temporary paths. Alert on HKLM\\Software\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Run(Once) registry modifications from unexpected processes, particularly from %TEMP% or AppData directories.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Miner Execution (gminer, lolMiner, SRBMiner-MULTI)
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies three specific miners deployed: 'supports three cryptocurrency miners: gminer, lolMiner, and SRBMiner-MULTI'. Detecting these processes is a direct impact and IOC indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation of gminer.exe, lolminer.exe, or srb-multi.exe from non-standard directories. Monitor for sustained high CPU/GPU consumption patterns consistent with cryptocurrency mining workloads.

suggestion.title: Anti-Forensics Process Enumeration and Adaptive Evasion
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'malware monitors for Task Manager, Process Hacker, and Process Explorer, pausing mining activity when detected'. This conditional execution behavior is detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process enumeration API calls (CreateToolhelp32Snapshot, EnumProcesses) combined with checks for taskmgr.exe, procexp64.exe, or procpacker.exe. Alert on resource-throttling patterns that pause and resume around detection-tool activity.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Installation from Trojanized Namespace
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 22 versions of 'forge-jsxy' (versions 1.0.66–1.0.91) as malicious. Pipeline produced no IOC list or installation detection despite the supply chain vector being the primary attack surface: 'Hackers Push 22 Versions of npm RAT'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm/yarn/pnpm package installation events for package names matching 'forge-jsxy' or known malicious versions 1.0.66–1.0.91. Alert on any attempt to install these versions in any environment. Correlate with process execution of npm install and child process spawning.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Systemd User Service (Linux) and LaunchAgent (macOS)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies persistence mechanism: 'Linux: ~/.config/systemd/user/forge-js-worker.service' and 'macOS: ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.forgejs.worker.plist'. Pipeline generated zero persistence detection rules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation or modification of ~/.config/systemd/user/forge-js-worker.service or ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.forgejs.worker.plist outside of standard application deployment contexts. Monitor for systemd timer/service files created in user home directories with 'forge' in the name.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Task Scheduler and Registry Run Keys (Windows)
suggestion.rationale: Windows persistence explicitly documented: 'Task Scheduler entry "ForgeJSWorker" + HKCU registry run key'. Pipeline missed all Windows-specific persistence artifacts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation of Task Scheduler task named 'ForgeJSWorker' or similar variants. Monitor HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run registry key modifications for entries created by or pointing to npm package installation directories.

suggestion.title: Network Communication to Identified C2 Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article provides explicit C2 IP and ports: '204.10.194.247:9877 (WebSocket)' and '204.10.194.247:8765 (HTTP API)'. Pipeline produced empty IOC list and zero network detection rules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any outbound connection to 204.10.194.247 on ports 9877 or 8765 from any process. Monitor WebSocket connections (ws://) to this IP. Cross-reference with process spawned from node_modules or npm-related directories.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Cryptocurrency Key Harvesting from Vault Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies wallet theft capability with exfiltration path: 'Secret Storage Path: <durable>/.vault/secret-audit/result.json (stores harvested cryptocurrency keys)'. No collection or theft detection rules generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file access or creation in /.vault/secret-audit/ directory, particularly result.json. Monitor for process access to cryptocurrency wallet files or credential storage locations originating from npm module directories or child processes of node.js with unexpected privileges.

suggestion.title: Package Hash Validation Against Known Malicious Forge-jsxy Artifacts
suggestion.rationale: Article provides specific artifact hash for v1.0.91: '4938d47fe6216f8f9fee0527bf5112c04c15a9ea62f87869677619aa5400f09f'. Zero IOCs were extracted, including this critical identifier.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Generate file hash for all downloaded npm packages during installation. Alert if sha256 hash 4938d47fe6216f8f9fee0527bf5112c04c15a9ea62f87869677619aa5400f09f is detected on the system or matches packages in node_modules.

suggestion.title: Execution of Unsigned or Spoofed ChatGPT/Claude Installer
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Hackers Use Fake ChatGPT and Claude Installers'—must detect unsigned binaries or cert mismatches masquerading as legitimate app installers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process execution where filename contains 'ChatGPT' or 'Claude' (case-insensitive) but lacks valid OpenAI or Anthropic code signature, or originates from untrusted download location. Cross-reference against known-good installer hashes from official channels.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Child Process Spawned by Installer Executable
suggestion.rationale: Malicious installers deploy payloads via child processes; article describes DinDoor 'deployment' via installer—detection must catch unexpected process hierarchy (installer→backdoor).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual child processes (powershell, cmd, rundll32, unknown binary) spawned from installer executables. Flag deviations from baseline expected child processes for legitimate ChatGPT/Claude installers; false positives unlikely given installer use case.

suggestion.title: DinDoor Registry Persistence via Run Keys or Scheduled Tasks
suggestion.rationale: Backdoor deployment implies persistence installation; DinDoor likely modifies HKLM or HKCU Run keys, startup folders, or scheduled tasks to survive reboot.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor registry writes to HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\Run*, HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\Run*, and Common Startup folders by unsigned installer processes. If article provides DinDoor-specific registry artifacts (string values, path patterns), add them to detection baseline.

suggestion.title: Network C2 Communication from Suspicious Installer or Child Process
suggestion.rationale: DinDoor is a backdoor requiring C2 communication; installer or spawned process must establish outbound connection to attacker infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unexpected outbound DNS or HTTP/HTTPS connections from unsigned installer processes or processes spawned by installers. If article body contains C2 domains or IPs, add to network blocklist. Baseline legitimate ChatGPT/Claude installer traffic to reduce false positives.

suggestion.title: Download of Fake Application Installer from Suspicious Source
suggestion.rationale: Attack begins with users downloading malicious installers from phishing links or compromised distribution channels; detection should flag suspicious file acquisition patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on downloads of files with ChatGPT or Claude in name from unexpected sources (non-openai.com, non-anthropic.com domains), or files with suspicious file extensions (.msi, .exe) delivered via email attachments, phishing links, or file-sharing services.

suggestion.title: Grandoreiro Banking Trojan Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names Grandoreiro malware as the attack vector; typical Grandoreiro execution involves reconnaissance and malware instantiation—no process execution detection use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of known Grandoreiro process artifacts or unsigned executables spawned from email client children. Monitor for process names or paths associated with previous Grandoreiro campaigns (e.g., unusual cmd.exe, powershell.exe children from outlook, winmail).

suggestion.title: Banking Malware Form Grabbing and Keylogging Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article targets 'Portuguese Banks and Latin American Companies'—banking trojans like Grandoreiro characteristically hook browser/form rendering for credential interception; no behavioral detection for form grabbing or keylogging generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DLL injection into browser processes (iexplore.exe, chrome.exe, firefox.exe) and windows messaging hooks (SetWindowsHookEx, SetWinEventHook). Alert on unsigned DLLs loaded into financial application processes.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Email Attachment Execution from Portuguese/Latin American Recipients
suggestion.rationale: Article targets geographic regions (Portugal, Latin America)—typical Grandoreiro distribution is spear-phishing with malicious Office attachments; pipeline missed initial-access detection tied to geographic targeting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag macro-enabled Office documents (.docm, .xlsm) delivered to Portuguese or Latin American banks via email, especially if opened by multiple users. Correlate with process execution of Office child processes invoking cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or rundll32.

suggestion.title: C2 Callback Detection for Known Grandoreiro Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Banking malware operations require command and control; article describes active targeting but pipeline generated no C2 communication detection despite Grandoreiro being a known C2-dependent malware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound TLS/HTTPS traffic to known Grandoreiro C2 domains or to bulletproof hosting providers associated with previous campaigns. Alert on traffic from compromised financial-sector machines to non-banking, non-whitelisted destinations.

suggestion.title: npm postinstall script reads from user home directory
suggestion.rationale: Article premise: 'malicious npm package stole files from Claude AI user directory.' Postinstall is the standard attack vector for npm supply-chain theft. Need detection for scripts accessing ~/.claude or similar config directories during dependency installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor node.js child processes spawned during npm install that attempt to enumerate or read from user home directories. Flag postinstall/preinstall script invocations that access ~/.claude, ~/.config, ~/.ssh, or similar sensitive paths. Correlate with package.json entries containing unusual lifecycle scripts.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm package with minimal history and elevated permissions
suggestion.rationale: Article implies recently-published malicious package. Need detection/vetting for npm packages with: <7 days published age, <5 downloads, multiple permission escalations via preinstall scripts, or obfuscated code in node_modules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm install of packages with publish date <1 week old, download count <100, or packages containing postinstall/preinstall scripts that invoke shell commands or filesystem access. Check npm registry metadata for typosquatting variants of popular packages.

suggestion.title: Data exfiltration to GitHub via git commands during dependency installation
suggestion.rationale: Article title specifies 'via GitHub.' Malicious postinstall likely stages stolen files or exfil via git push to attacker-controlled GitHub repo. Need detection for git init/add/commit/push spawned as child of npm install.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect git init/push or curl/wget HTTP POST operations launched by npm or node.js processes during install phase, especially targeting github.com. Alert if commit messages or repo URLs contain patterns matching attacker infrastructure or stolen file paths.

suggestion.title: System App Injecting Code into Amazon Application Package
suggestion.rationale: Article describes preinstalled Motorola app 'hijacking Amazon App' — direct evidence of process/code injection. Pipeline extracted zero kill-chain phases despite this being core attack mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Android processes for system/preinstalled apps (uid < 10000) attempting dlopen, mmap, or ptrace operations against com.amazon.venezia or similar Amazon package. Flag unexpected shared object loads or memory-region modifications.

suggestion.title: Affiliate Code Injection in Amazon HTTP Transactions
suggestion.rationale: Article states app injects 'affiliate codes'—pipeline missed the monetization/fraud impact phase. Need to detect URL parameter injection or deep-link interception patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate outbound HTTPS from Amazon app with non-Amazon referrer domains or unusual query parameters (asin, tag, linkId fields modified by non-Amazon source). Baseline legitimate Amazon affiliate patterns and alert on anomalous injection.

suggestion.title: Accessibility Service Requested by Preinstalled System App
suggestion.rationale: To inject affiliate codes into user interactions, malicious preinstalled app likely abuses Android Accessibility Services. Article implies interaction-level hijacking; pipeline did not identify this privilege-escalation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on ACCESSIBILITY_SERVICE permission grants to non-Google preinstalled apps. Cross-reference grantPackageName with Motorola OEM app allowlist; flag unexpected accessibility requests from apps with no UI (services/background daemons).

suggestion.title: Motorola Preinstalled App Communicating to Affiliate/Ad Network Domains
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline failed to extract command-and-control or monetization infrastructure. Article implies backend communication for affiliate code distribution/tracking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline DNS/IP queries initiated by Motorola preinstalled processes (e.g., SystemUI, MotorolaSystem* packages). Flag connections to affiliate platforms (Amazon Associates domains, ad networks like criteo.com, outbrain, taboola) from non-browser processes.

suggestion.title: Preinstalled App Persists Across Factory Reset or Update
suggestion.rationale: Preinstalled bloatware cannot be uninstalled by user; article implies firmware-level persistence. Pipeline did not flag firmware supply-chain compromise angle.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect system-partition (not /data/app) app binaries with suspicious code signatures or modification timestamps post-manufacture. Alert on unsigned or unsigned-then-re-signed system apps during OTA updates.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Domain/URL Recommendations from Chat Interfaces
suggestion.rationale: Article describes chatbot recommendations redirecting users to malware sites — this is the initial delivery mechanism. Pipeline failed to capture this primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous URL patterns in chatbot recommendation outputs or proxy logs where common LLM/chatbot services recommend newly registered or known-malicious domains. Correlate chatbot session IDs with downstream malware delivery URLs.

suggestion.title: Cryptojacking Process Execution Post-Browser Redirect
suggestion.rationale: Article payload is cryptojacking malware delivered via chatbot redirect — need detection for cryptocurrency mining process execution that follows suspicious browser activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution of known cryptomining binaries (xmrig, monero, etc.) or command-line patterns matching CPU-intensive mining pools following browser process activity from redirected sites. Monitor for child processes spawned by browser with high CPU utilization.

suggestion.title: Malware Distribution Domain Clustering from Chatbot Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline should map infrastructure — article describes compromised or abused chatbots redirecting to malware hosts. Need IOC extraction and domain relationship mapping.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Extract and correlate malware distribution domains mentioned in article (or discoverable via pivot). Create detection for bulk redirects to these domains from chatbot user sessions. Flag domains registered within narrow time window with similar SSL certs or AS paths.

suggestion.title: Abnormal Resource Consumption (CPU/Memory) Post-Chatbot Interaction
suggestion.rationale: Cryptojacking is an impact-phase activity with observable system resource footprint — article doesn't explicitly describe detection but this is the post-execution telemetry to detect.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for sustained high CPU usage (>80% single-core or sustained multi-core), elevated memory allocation, and network connections to mining pools originating from user devices following visits to redirected domains. Establish baseline of normal resource usage.

suggestion.title: Prompt Injection or Chatbot Model Manipulation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates chatbot recommendations are compromised — this could be prompt injection, fine-tuning poisoning, or API abuse. Pipeline missed the attack surface analysis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor chatbot API logs for unusual recommendation outputs (off-brand links, unusual character sequences, non-contextual recommendations). Detect requests containing common injection payloads or attempts to manipulate system prompts. Baseline normal recommendation URL patterns.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Compromised Chatbot Credentials or API Keys
suggestion.rationale: If chatbot is compromised, attackers may use it as a pivot point. Pipeline should have considered attacker persistence and lateral movement implications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: If chatbot leverages corporate auth or APIs, detect anomalous auth from chatbot service accounts (geo, time-of-day, impossible travel). Monitor API calls from chatbot infrastructure for unusual targets or resource access patterns inconsistent with normal operation.

suggestion.title: BadHost Tool Execution or C2 Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article title names 'BadHost' as the exploitation vector. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs and no detection coverage for this tool's presence, execution, or network footprint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process execution or binary download with filename/hash patterns matching BadHost. Detect C2 beaconing behavior from compromised systems to attacker-controlled infrastructure; flag suspicious process spawning from AI agent server software or web server processes.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized API Endpoint Access to AI Agent Servers
suggestion.rationale: Core attack: 'exploit BadHost to access sensitive AI Agent Server endpoints.' Pipeline missed all detection logic for suspicious endpoint access, privilege escalation in API calls, or lateral movement within agent infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to AI agent API endpoints from unexpected source IPs or users. Flag repeated 401/403 responses followed by successful authentication, suspicious access to /admin, /config, /models, or /prompts endpoints. Monitor for enumeration of API endpoints followed by targeted data extraction.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Exfiltration from AI Agent Servers
suggestion.rationale: Attackers gain access to 'sensitive' endpoints (implies models, prompts, API keys, configs). Pipeline produced zero detections for exfiltration of AI intellectual property or credentials from compromised agent infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual outbound data transfers from AI agent servers (large volume, unusual destinations, encrypted tunnels). Detect access to and transfer of .pth/.pkl (model weights), .env (credentials), or /config files. Flag API response payloads larger than baseline or GZ/ZIP compression of model/prompt data.

suggestion.title: Public-Facing AI Agent Application Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: BadHost exploits AI agent endpoints. Title implies vulnerability in the exposed application layer. Pipeline failed to map this to initial access techniques or generate exploitation-detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect exploitation attempts against known AI agent framework endpoints: malformed JSON payloads to /api/chat, path traversal in /models or /prompts, SSRF injection in user input, or known BadHost exploit signatures. Flag requests with suspicious headers, payloads, or parameter encoding targeting AI infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Persistence via AI Agent Model or Prompt Injection
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation, attackers establish persistence in AI systems. Article describes multi-stage 'exploit then access' pattern but pipeline missed persistence mechanisms specific to AI infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for modifications to model weights, prompt files, or agent configuration post-compromise. Detect execution of new Python packages or scripts deployed to AI agent directories. Flag changes to startup sequences in /etc/init.d, systemd services, or application launch scripts that persist malicious behavior.

suggestion.title: Exploitation of cpanel_jsonapi_func=redisAble Function
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'grep -rE "cpanel_jsonapi_func=redisAble" /var/cpanel/logs /usr/local/cpanel/logs/' as detection method and notes vulnerability 'stems from an incorrect privilege assignment weakness' in the 'lsws.redisAble function.' Direct IOC pattern provided in article.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt cPanel and web access logs for HTTP POST/GET requests containing `cpanel_jsonapi_func=redisAble` parameter to the vulnerable LiteSpeed plugin. Correlate request source IP with subsequent privileged process execution. Baseline normal Redis enable/disable operations to distinguish exploitation from legitimate admin activity.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation from Unprivileged Context to Root via LiteSpeed Redis Function
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly: 'enables remote attackers with no privileges to execute arbitrary scripts with root privileges.' This is the core attack mechanism—remote RCE to root escalation in one step via the function.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor process creation and privilege escalation logs for execution of scripts or commands with root UID/GID when initiated from cPanel/web service context. Alert on any root-level process spawned from a web-service unprivileged account or from cPanel plugin execution context.

suggestion.title: Inventory and Block Vulnerable LiteSpeed cPanel Plugin Versions
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies explicit affected versions: 'all user-end plugin versions between v2.3 and v2.4.4' with 4-day patch deadline. This is a known-vulnerable software detection requirement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate installed LiteSpeed cPanel plugin versions across all hosts. Flag any installation in range v2.3–v2.4.4. Cross-reference with patch/update logs to confirm upgrade to v2.4.5 or later. Consider OS-level package queries or file-signature scanning of plugin manifests.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Redis Configuration Modification via cPanel API
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'vulnerability is related to the mishandling of Redis enable/disable features'—indicating the attack leverages the Redis enable/disable API endpoint as the exploit vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor cPanel API logs for unusual enable/disable calls to Redis services, especially from non-administrative source IPs or outside normal business-hours patterns. Correlate with system-level Redis daemon restarts or config changes that were not initiated by legitimate admins.

suggestion.title: Forensic Hunt: Lateral Movement and Exfiltration Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article advises: 'examine the system logs for any actions taken by the detected IPs' after finding malicious `cpanel_jsonapi_func=redisAble` calls. Implies attackers perform additional actions after privilege escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After detecting exploitation pattern (`cpanel_jsonapi_func=redisAble`), correlate the attacker's source IP with subsequent activity in auth logs, process logs, DNS queries, and outbound connections. Flag privilege enumeration commands (getent, id, sudo -l), file discovery (find, ls), or exfiltration attempts.

suggestion.title: npm Supply Chain: Unexpected TanStack Package Versions
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'malicious versions of the product were published to the npm registry' — detection must capture TanStack installations with versions not matching historical baseline or legitimate release timelines during KEV window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of legitimate TanStack versions deployed across fleet. Alert on presence of versions absent from baseline and untraced to documented releases. Correlate suspicious package versions with npm install events and deployment activity during 2026-05-27 onward.

suggestion.title: Credential-Stealing Malware: Process Behavior Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'credential-stealing malware' payload — once npm package executes, malware will predictably access credential stores and environment variables, triggering behavioral signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned from node.js/npm that access credential stores (%APPDATA%\Microsoft\Credentials, ~/.ssh, ~/.aws), environment variable enumeration, or browser credential stores. Focus on legitimate npm modules spawning unexpected subprocess activity.

suggestion.title: npm Registry Publication by TanStack Identity
suggestion.rationale: Attacker 'published to the npm registry under a trusted identity' — npm audit logs and registry webhooks should flag unexpected package versions from TanStack account or lookalike packages during compromise window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect new TanStack package versions published outside normal CI/CD cadence. Flag forked/typosquatted packages (e.g., 'tanstackjs', 'tan-stack'). Correlate with TanStack GitHub release history — unpublished versions or mismatched checksums indicate compromise.

suggestion.title: Network Exfiltration from npm Node Process
suggestion.rationale: Credential-stealing malware requires command & control — node processes making unexpected outbound connections to non-registry, non-CDN destinations indicates credential exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline legitimate npm/node process network behavior (registry, mirrors, CDNs only). Alert on HTTPS connections to attacker infrastructure. Prioritize encrypted channels mimicking legitimate traffic; correlate with DNS requests for newly registered or suspicious domains.

suggestion.title: Package Load-Time Execution Context Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Malicious TanStack versions execute at require()-time — detect packages loaded from unexpected file paths (temp directories, global npm cache with recent modification times, or non-standard node_modules trees).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor node.js process creation for TanStack imports. Flag if package.json declares version < compromised version but filesystem reports newer version. Alert on node processes loading packages from TEMP, cache directories, or world-writable paths during KEV active window.

suggestion.title: Nx Console Supply Chain Compromise — Malicious Version Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'malicious version of Nx Console was published' — supply-chain attack is the initial vector. Pipeline missed detection for compromised extension versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect installation or update of Nx Console within affected version range (CVE-2026-48027 window). Alert on rapid version downgrades or rollbacks. Cross-reference package-lock.json and yarn.lock hashes against vendor-published compromised artifact signatures.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting from Disk by Nx Console Process
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'harvested credentials from multiple sources on disk' — direct file access to SSH keys, .aws/, .kube/, password vaults. Pipeline missed all credential-access hunts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Nx Console process tree for file reads to credential repositories: ~/.ssh/, ~/.aws/, ~/.kube/config, ~/.docker/config, browser credential DBs. Alert on unexpected sequential access to multiple credential types.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting from Memory by Nx Console Runtime
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'harvested credentials...in memory' — process memory reads or API hooking. Pipeline missed memory-based credential extraction detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Nx Console or npm-spawned child processes performing raw memory reads (ReadProcessMemory), injecting credential-access hooks, or using DPAPI calls. Correlate memory-dump utilities spawned from IDE context.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated Payload Fetch and Execution by Nx Console Extension
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'fetched an obfuscated payload' — extension makes unexpected network call to retrieve and execute attacker code. Pipeline missed C2 and execution detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Nx Console or npm process making HTTPS/HTTP requests to non-package-registry domains. Filter for Base64/gzip/encrypted payloads in HTTP body. Alert on PowerShell/bash child processes spawned post-fetch with obfuscated arguments.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48027 Vulnerability Scanner Match — Nx Console
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies CVE-2026-48027 as scannable indicator with active exploitation (CISA KEV). Pipeline failed to extract CVE as primary IOC for scanner correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for CVE-2026-48027 hits. Cross-reference Nx Console versions in dev environment inventory against CISA-published affected ranges. Trigger for any match regardless of claimed patch status, given supply-chain compromise nature and federal due-date 2026-06-10.

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration via Nx Console C2 Channel
suggestion.rationale: Article describes credential harvesting as malware objective; exfiltration phase must follow collection. Pipeline generated no collection/exfiltration hunts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Nx Console / npm process sending large HTTPS POST requests containing Base64/hex-encoded, zlib-compressed, or AES-encrypted payloads to non-Microsoft/non-Nx domains. Correlate with prior credential-file access.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanner Alert: CVE-2026-8398
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs: 'CVE-2026-8398 — match against your vulnerability scanner'. No UC created to trigger on scanner hits for this known-exploited vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any vulnerability scan result positive for CVE-2026-8398 in Daemon Tools Lite installations. CISA KEV designation means this is actively exploited in the wild.

suggestion.title: Software Inventory: Daemon Tools Lite Detected
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'Daemon Tools Lite' as the vulnerable product. No inventory-based detection was generated to identify systems with this software installed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect any process execution or file access from Daemon Tools Lite installation directories. Cross-reference with vulnerability scanner to identify unpatched instances.

suggestion.title: Patch Compliance Deadline: CVE-2026-8398 Post-2026-05-30
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Federal patch due: 2026-05-30'. No compliance-based detection was created for systems remaining unpatched after the federal deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After 2026-05-30, generate alerts for any system still reporting CVE-2026-8398 as unpatched. Track remediation status for compliance audits.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Traffic: T1190 Against Exposed Assets
suggestion.rationale: Article maps to T1190 'Exploit Public-Facing Application' and confirms exploitation 'observed in the wild'. No network-level detection for exploitation attempts was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP/HTTPS requests to known Daemon Tools Lite endpoints or exploitation payload signatures. Correlate with scanner alerts and process execution to confirm compromise.

suggestion.title: BOLA / IDOR Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states BOLA detection works as 'chain of authorization probes guided by structural reasoning about how API objects relate to identities' and lists BOLA/IDOR as key context-dependent vulnerabilities. Phrase: 'BOLA or IDOR, cross-tenant data leakage, authentication bypasses.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor API endpoints for repeated authorization test payloads targeting different object IDs or user contexts. Look for sequential probing of /user/{id}/invoice, /data/{resource_id} patterns with different ID values from same source, or repeated 401/403 responses followed by different credential attempts.

suggestion.title: Cross-Tenant Data Access Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Specific vulnerability type called out: 'cross-tenant data leakage' as context-dependent flaw requiring behavioral reasoning to detect.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect requests that cross tenant boundaries in multi-tenant applications; look for API calls where authentication token from Tenant A accesses resources tagged with Tenant B metadata, or database queries joining across tenant_id boundaries.

suggestion.title: Chained Vulnerability Exploitation Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article states chained vulnerabilities ('a couple of mediums and highs combine into a critical exploit path') are context-dependent and require reasoning to detect. These chains are the exploitation target.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequences of API calls where each call returns a slightly escalated privilege or information disclosure, building toward critical access. Example: enumerate objects → bypass auth → read sensitive field → exfiltrate. Look for request chains with increasing severity indicators (initially denied, then partial success, then full access).

suggestion.title: API Reconnaissance and Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article describes pentesting methodology as 'recon, probe, observe, reason, escalate, validate.' Reconnaissance phase explicitly discussed as foundational attack step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect systematic enumeration of API endpoints and object IDs: repeated requests to /api/{resource}/{id} with incrementing or pseudo-random IDs, OPTIONS/HEAD probes on API paths, or schema enumeration attempts (request errors revealing field names). Baseline benign API crawler patterns first.

suggestion.title: Autonomous Continuous Attack Probing
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Autonomous attackers are already probing application surfaces continuously at machine speed' and identifies this as ongoing threat requiring detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect high-frequency, non-interactive API probing: >10 requests/second to endpoints, probes with bot-like User-Agent strings, requests that do not include user interaction telemetry (mouse, keyboard), or request patterns that match no known legitimate client behavior (e.g., every endpoint enumerated in numeric sequence).

suggestion.title: Authentication Bypass Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 'authentication bypasses' as explicit vulnerability class. Phrase: 'BOLA or IDOR, cross-tenant data leakage, authentication bypasses, and especially chained vulnerabilities.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect patterns suggesting authentication bypass: requests to /admin with no session token followed by successful response, credential submission to endpoints that normally skip auth, or access to protected resources using expired/malformed tokens that succeed.

suggestion.title: Phishing email impersonating IT support with callback requests
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'SRG actors send phishing emails to urge employees to call the SRG actor posing as IT support' and describes attackers who 'register domains to impersonate IT helpdesk or support portals.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag emails with sender addresses mimicking internal IT support (help-desk, IT-support, servicedesk typos) requesting callback to 'verify system access' or grant remote sessions. Correlate with newly registered or typosquatted domains and monitor for distinctive urgency language triggering immediate employee action.

suggestion.title: Unsolicited callback phishing from threat actor posing as IT
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'SRG actors either directly call or send phishing emails to urge employees to call the SRG actor posing as IT support' and 'While on the phone, the SRG actor directs the employee to grant access to a remote desktop session.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate employee-reported unsolicited calls claiming to originate from IT support with subsequent phishing emails in overlapping timeframes. Flag spike patterns where multiple employees within days report similar calls requesting remote-access grants, credential verification, or system permissions.

suggestion.title: Suspicious remote access tool activation post-phishing
suggestion.rationale: Article states threat actor 'directs the employee to grant access to a remote desktop session' and exfiltrates data 'through legitimate remote access tools' when initial compromise succeeds.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on initiation of RDP, TeamViewer, AnyDesk, or equivalent remote-access software immediately following phishing email interaction or within hours of employee-reported suspicious callback. Flag unusual process spawning, command-line parameters, or outbound network destinations from these tools.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized external storage device insertion and bulk data exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'SRG sends a threat actor to the victim's location to gain access to insert a storage device into the victim's computer' and exfiltration occurs 'by connecting USB drives or external hard drives to the victim's computer.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected external USB or hard-drive connections to corporate machines, especially off-hours. Correlate device insertion with bulk file operations (copy, robocopy, 7-Zip) to newly mounted storage, particularly involving sensitive document types or large file counts.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized physical access by individuals claiming IT support role
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 'the presence of unidentified or unauthorized individuals claiming to be IT support and attempting to access computers' as a possible SRG attack indicator and describes in-person intrusion to 'gain access to insert a storage device into the victim's computer.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference physical access logs (badge swipes, visitor sign-ins) with IT help-desk ticketing systems. Flag individuals claiming IT support but with no corresponding work order, no badge history for that role, or no roster entry in IT department. Correlate with employee reports of unexpected personnel requesting workstation access.

suggestion.title: Domain typosquatting targeting organizational IT helpdesk infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article states SRG 'register domains to impersonate IT helpdesk or support portals for major U.S. law firms and financial services firms, using typosquatted patterns.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DNS queries and web clicks to domains with common typosquatting variants of internal IT helpdesk domain names (off-by-one characters, homoglyphs, missing hyphens). Alert on newly registered domains matching organizational IT support naming patterns; gather WHOIS metadata to identify attacker infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Bulk Phishing Domain Registration Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states '300+ fake domains'—pipeline extracted zero IOCs or infrastructure detections despite this clear domain registration campaign indicator
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for rapid domain registrations using FIFA, World Cup, sporting event, or ticketing keywords. Flag batches of 10+ domains registered from single registrar within 24-hour windows. Cross-reference with phishing report feeds and domain similarity analysis.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email Delivery with Sporting Event Lures
suggestion.rationale: Article describes campaign 'targets FIFA World Cup fans'—primary attack vector is phishing emails but pipeline generated no email-based detection logic
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound emails with FIFA, World Cup, ticket, or sports-betting content linking to newly registered suspicious domains. Flag requests for credential submission or payment information. Correlate sender reputation with domain registration date anomalies.

suggestion.title: User Click-Through and Access to Phishing Domains
suggestion.rationale: Campaign uses fake domains to deceive users—missing detection for actual user interaction with malicious infrastructure despite this being the attack objective
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on user DNS queries and HTTP/HTTPS requests to newly registered domains containing sporting event keywords. Flag POST requests to these domains (credential submission). Correlate with email headers and URL click telemetry from phishing reports.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting Form Submission Detection
suggestion.rationale: Fake domains designed to 'harvest' credentials from fans—no detection for fraudulent login pages or payment forms despite this being core attack mechanism
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST requests to newly registered domains for credential or payment card data submission. Detect login forms on domains impersonating FIFA.com, official ticketing platforms, or sports betting services. Flag successful data exfiltration patterns.

suggestion.title: Yamcs API authentication with ChangeMissionDatabase privilege + algorithm PATCH
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'An authenticated user with the ChangeMissionDatabase privilege' can exploit this. Should detect privilege escalation or lateral privilege grant before exploitation attempt: 'algorithm text without enforcing a secure sandbox'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for accounts gaining ChangeMissionDatabase privilege in Yamcs access logs or directory service logs immediately before PATCH requests to algorithm endpoints. Baseline normal privilege grant patterns and flag anomalies or out-of-hours grants.

suggestion.title: Java process spawning interpreter without parent shell initiator
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'dynamically compiles and evaluates user-controlled algorithm text'—Janino compilation artifacts should appear in child processes. UC_28_4 detects shell spawning but misses the intermediate compilation step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Java or yamcsd process spawning javac, jshell, or other JVM compilation tools followed immediately by interpreter execution (bash, sh, python). Legitimate algorithm updates should not require compilation of arbitrary code.

suggestion.title: Algorithm PATCH request with Java method/class syntax in request body
suggestion.rationale: Article shows exploitation requires 'user-controlled algorithm text'—PATCH body should contain Java syntax (import, class, public, static). Look for HTTP request bodies containing Java/Janino keywords in `/api/mdb/*/algorithms/*` endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect PATCH request bodies to `/api/mdb/*/algorithms/*` for Java keywords (public, static, class, import, Runtime.exec, ProcessBuilder) that would be suspicious in algorithm expressions. Alert on requests containing process execution APIs.

suggestion.title: Failed Janino compilation errors in application logs
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability exists because code 'dynamically compiles and evaluates'—failed exploit attempts (malformed Java) will generate compilation errors. These are weak indicators of attack attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Yamcs application logs for Janino compilation errors (codehaus.janino.CompileException) following PATCH requests to algorithm endpoints. Cluster by source IP and timestamp to identify reconnaissance or fuzzing attempts.

suggestion.title: Yamcs algorithm endpoint reconnaissance scan
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exploitation requires API access to `/api/mdb/*/algorithms/*`—attackers must first enumerate or discover this endpoint. Look for HTTP GET/OPTIONS requests probing the endpoint structure before PATCH.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequences of GET or OPTIONS requests to `/api/mdb/*` endpoints (algorithm listing) followed within 5–30 minutes by PATCH requests from the same source IP. This two-step pattern (discovery → exploitation) is characteristic of API-based attacks.

suggestion.title: LiquidJS filter chain RCE gadget detection in template source
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly demonstrates exploitation using `{%assign r=1|valueOf%}` followed by `{{r|inspect}}`. Pipeline should detect characteristic filter chaining that accesses context/prototype objects. The `|valueOf` and `|inspect` filters piped sequentially are the core exploitation technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for template source containing `|valueOf` or `|inspect` filters applied to variables, especially chained operations that pipe filter output through reflection filters. Look for pattern `assign VAR=<value>|<gadget_filter>` followed by template variable expansion.

suggestion.title: Prototype pollution via __proto__ assignment in LiquidJS templates
