suggestion.rationale: Article's provided detection queries explicitly search for `assign __proto__` and `assign%20__proto__` patterns as IOCs, indicating __proto__ pollution as known exploitation vector to escape template sandbox.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect template source containing assignment to __proto__, prototype, or constructor properties within Liquid filter syntax. These indicate attempts to pollute object prototype chain for sandbox escape.

suggestion.title: Module enumeration/loading from RCE-compromised Node context
suggestion.rationale: Article's detection queries reference `getBuiltinModule`, `child_process`, and `execSync` as post-exploitation indicators, implying successful RCE uses dynamic module loading to spawn shells. Should detect programmatic require() or module enumeration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate LiquidJS RCE attempt detection with subsequent Node.js process spawning shells. Focus on unexpected process genealogy: template rendering service (parent) → child_process module invocation → shell execution.

suggestion.title: Constructor/prototype chain traversal in LiquidJS filter expressions
suggestion.rationale: Article PoC shows `1|valueOf` returning `this` (context object). Exploitation leverages constructor and prototype chain traversal to access Node.js internals. Article shows context object leakage via filter execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for template expressions accessing .constructor, .prototype, .__proto__, .getBuiltinModule in filter chains or object property traversal. Pattern: filter output piped to property access filters that walk the prototype chain upward.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Container Registry Access via Gitea
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Exposes Private Container Images without Authentication' — core attack vector is bypassing auth controls to access OCI registries. Pipeline extracted zero use cases despite this being the primary detection opportunity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to Gitea container registry endpoints (typically /v2/) that lack authentication headers (no Authorization, no valid JWT/token) but succeed with 200/206 responses. Baseline legitimate pulls and flag anomalous patterns: requests from new IPs, mass pulls of private repos, or pulls outside business hours.

suggestion.title: Bulk Private Container Image Download Activity
suggestion.rationale: Exposed private images will be exfiltrated; 'Exposes' in title signals data access. Pipeline should detect collection/exfiltration phase but provided zero use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag rapid sequential pulls of multiple private container images from a single source IP, especially if targeting repos marked as private. Alert on >10 image pulls within 5 minutes from external sources, or any pull of sensitive-keyword-tagged images without valid auth session.

suggestion.title: Gitea Registry Authentication Bypass Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes a vulnerability that bypasses authentication entirely. Pipeline should have reconstructed the exploitation chain but returned empty kill chain. Core attack is 'without authentication', implying a specific request pattern or URL parameter.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect requests to Gitea /api/packages endpoints or /<user>/<repo>/v2 paths that succeed without valid authentication tokens. Look for 200-range responses on protected paths when Authorization header is missing or Bearer token is invalid/expired. Correlate with subsequent blob/manifest requests.

suggestion.title: Gitea Version Detection for CVE Eligibility
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline extracted zero IOCs; should have identified vulnerable Gitea version ranges. Article references a specific CVE and affected versions that are prerequisite for triage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Fingerprint Gitea instances via /api/v1/version endpoint or User-Agent headers in responses. Alert on versions ≤ [vulnerable range from CVE] attempting to serve container images. Can be paired with asset inventory or scan results to identify exposure scope.

suggestion.title: Private Repository Metadata Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Authentication bypass allows enumeration of private repos without credentials. Article does not detail this explicitly, but is a natural consequence of the vulnerability. Pipeline should anticipate this pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for enumeration of private repo listings, tag lists, or manifest requests that return success without prior successful auth. Detect rapid iteration of common repo names or automated catalog scanning against /v2/_catalog or /api/v1/repos endpoints from single source.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Gitea API Access Patterns for OCI Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability likely affects specific API paths for OCI/Docker registry emulation within Gitea. Pipeline should have identified which paths/endpoints are vulnerable but returned no IOCs or kill chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on requests to Gitea OCI paths (/api/packages/container, /v2/[repo]/blobs, /v2/[repo]/manifests) from sources with no prior auth session or failed auth attempt in same session window. Baseline normal pull patterns and alert on anomalies: new source IPs, bulk requests, or non-matching user agents.

suggestion.title: Grandoreiro Banking Trojan Execution and Process Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly covers Grandoreiro malware campaigns targeting Windows users. Banking trojans typically inject into processes, establish persistence, and establish C2. This is foundational for any Windows malware detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process injection patterns typical of banking trojans: parent-child process relationships indicative of shellcode injection, registry modifications under Run/RunOnce keys, or DLL injection into legitimate Windows processes.

suggestion.title: BTMOB Android RAT APK Installation and Malicious Permission Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies BTMOB RAT as Android-targeting malware. RATs typically request excessive permissions (camera, microphone, location, contacts) and persist through system compromises.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag APK installations requesting both camera/microphone AND location/contact access simultaneously, especially from untrusted sources. Monitor for installation events with suspicious package names mimicking legitimate banking apps.

suggestion.title: Command and Control Beacon Detection for Grandoreiro/BTMOB
suggestion.rationale: Both Grandoreiro and BTMOB RAT require C2 communication to function. Article covers 'campaigns' implying active infrastructure. Missing any network-based detection for C2 phone-home traffic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious outbound connections from infected hosts to known Grandoreiro/BTMOB C2 infrastructure, unusual DNS queries, or encrypted traffic patterns to non-standard ports. Mobile: monitor for background network activity outside expected app behavior.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting and Banking Credential Theft
suggestion.rationale: Grandoreiro is specifically a banking trojan—credential access is its primary objective. Article describes malware targeting users but provides no detection for credential theft patterns or memory scraping.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes accessing sensitive credential stores, browser credential managers, or memory scraping of form data. Monitor for unusual API calls to keyloggers, clipboard monitoring, or form field interception.

suggestion.title: Malicious Android App Store Delivery and Sideloading Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions BTMOB campaigns but provides no detection for how the RAT reaches Android users—third-party stores, sideloading, phishing links. This is the critical initial access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for APK downloads from non-Google Play sources, enable sideloading detection, and track users clicking suspicious links. Flag installations where APK signature mismatches legitimate banking apps.

suggestion.title: Malware Download URLs Recommended by Chatbot
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states attackers 'push malicious software download links' via chatbot—core attack mechanism. Expected detection on delivery of suspicious executables immediately following chatbot interaction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on executables or suspicious archives downloaded within 5 minutes of documented chatbot conversation. Correlate proxy logs showing file-hosting domains with immediately-preceding chatbot traffic. Flag if multiple users download from identical URLs post-chatbot interaction.

suggestion.title: Compromised or Manipulated Chatbot Account Activity
suggestion.rationale: Attackers 'abuse AI chatbot recommendations'—implies account takeover, prompt injection, or system manipulation. No detection for anomalous chatbot behavior or account compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on chatbot accounts accessing from new geographic regions or at abnormal hours. Flag recommendations that contradict chatbot function (e.g., financial advice from code-completion bot, file downloads from general-knowledge assistant). Detect if single chatbot account sends identical malware URLs to 5+ distinct users.

suggestion.title: User Execution of Chatbot-Recommended Files
suggestion.rationale: Attack chain requires user to download AND execute chatbot-recommended malware. No detection for post-download execution correlated with chatbot interaction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate downloads of executable/archive files with subsequent process execution within 10 minutes. Alert if executed file originated from URL mentioned in recent chatbot logs or user chat history. Track file reputation changes post-chatbot recommendation.

suggestion.title: Social Engineering via AI Chatbot Trust Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Core attack leverages user trust in 'AI chatbot recommendations'—pure social engineering. No behavioral detection for chatbot-based credential harvesting or trust exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for chatbot responses requesting credentials, personal information, or system access under pretext of 'optimization' or 'verification.' Flag if response patterns change (e.g., sudden shift from helpful to authoritative/urgent tone). Detect clustering of users reporting identical suspicious recommendations in same timeframe.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Installation and Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article title: '22 Versions of npm RAT' — pipeline missed detection for malicious package installation from npm registry and subsequent code execution via post-install scripts
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install execution followed by unexpected child-process spawning (curl, wget, powershell, cmd) from node_modules directories. Alert on npm processes executing binaries outside package scope or making network connections during installation phase. Flag package installations matching known-malware signatures or from unexpected package sources.

suggestion.title: Persistent Backdoor Installation via npm Post-Install Script
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Persistent Backdoor' capability — pipeline missed persistence-mechanism detection for implants installed during npm package post-install execution
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm post-install script execution for creation of scheduled tasks, cron jobs, registry run-keys, or systemd services. Alert on node_modules packages creating persistence outside their own directory or with suspicious execution schedules. Flag file modifications to system startup locations initiated by npm context.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Wallet Credential Theft from npm Process
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'Wallet Theft' — pipeline missed detection for npm-spawned processes accessing wallet credential stores and exfiltrating keys/seed phrases
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when npm or node child processes access cryptocurrency wallet directories (%APPDATA%\Bitcoin, %APPDATA%\Ethereum, browser extension storage, MetaMask paths) or attempt to read wallet.dat, keystore files, or browser localStorage. Monitor for subsequent exfiltration of credential data over network connections initiated from node processes.

suggestion.title: npm Supply-Chain Attack Campaign Pattern — Multiple Malicious Versions
suggestion.rationale: Article describes distribution of '22 Versions' to npm registry — pipeline missed campaign-detection logic for multiple package versions of same malware designed to evade single-version detection
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm registry API traffic and package-install logs for patterns of multiple versions of the same package being installed in short time windows across the organization. Correlate npm package names against known-malicious package intelligence feeds. Alert on new/unexpected minor/patch versions of commonly-used packages originating from external sources.

suggestion.title: Command-and-Control Communication from npm Backdoor Process
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Persistent Backdoor' functionality — implicit C2 communication requirement missed by pipeline for detecting outbound command-channel establishment
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound network connections from npm or node processes to non-RFC1918 addresses on non-standard ports (especially early in process lifetime). Alert on DNS queries from node context to newly-registered or low-reputation domains. Flag encrypted tunnels or suspicious protocol usage (base64-encoded HTTP, uncommon ports) from npm spawned processes.

suggestion.title: Execution of Masqueraded Application Installer (ChatGPT / Claude)
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Hackers Use Fake ChatGPT and Claude Installers'—masqueraded installers are the attack delivery mechanism. Must detect process execution with legitimate app names but anomalous origin or signature properties.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag execution of chatgpt.exe, claude.exe, or variants from browser downloads, temp directories, or AppData. Alert if publisher/signer is absent, invalid, or mismatched to OpenAI/Anthropic. Correlate parent process with download activity.

suggestion.title: DinDoor Backdoor Activation and Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'DinDoor Backdoor' as the payload. Pipeline must create detection logic for DinDoor process spawning, file creation, registry modifications, or behavioral indicators post-installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for child processes spawned by fake installer executables with suspicious names or paths. Detect file/registry artifacts typical of DinDoor (obfuscated persistence paths, scheduled tasks, WMI event subscriptions).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Application Installer Download from Non-Official Domain
suggestion.rationale: Attack begins with download of 'fake' installers from attacker infrastructure. Must detect downloads of installer executables from domains not matching official OpenAI or Anthropic infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor downloads of EXE/MSI with names ChatGPT, Claude, or variants from domains not openai.com / anthropic.com. Flag typosquatted, newly registered, or suspicious-reputation domains. Correlate to malware file hashes.

suggestion.title: DinDoor Command-and-Control Communication
suggestion.rationale: Backdoor implies outbound C2. Must detect network beaconing from DinDoor process post-activation, including unusual ports or protocols.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound connections from fake installer child processes or DinDoor-associated PIDs to unknown IP/domain. Monitor for non-standard ports from recently installed applications. Track DNS queries for C2 resolution.

suggestion.title: Backdoor Persistence Mechanism Installation (Registry / Startup Folder)
suggestion.rationale: Backdoor must persist across reboot. Article implies DinDoor establishes persistence—detect registry run keys, startup folders, WMI subscriptions, or scheduled tasks created post-installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for registry writes to HKLM/HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\Run or Startup folder modifications correlating with installer execution timeline. Detect scheduled task creation by installer child processes with suspicious executables.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated or Packed Installer Payload Execution
suggestion.rationale: Fake installers likely use obfuscation or unusual packing to evade static detection. Must detect self-extracting archives, packed executables, or entropy-anomalous binaries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag execution of high-entropy binaries, self-extracting archives (7z, RAR SFX), or packed PE files (UPX, custom packers). Monitor for temporary file creation in user temp/downloads followed by unsigned executable execution.

suggestion.title: Grandoreiro Malware Delivery via Phishing
suggestion.rationale: Article title indicates spear-phishing as initial vector; 'Hackers Use Grandoreiro Malware to Target Portuguese Banks' implies socially-engineered delivery, typical of TA505 campaigns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual email attachments or links reaching banking personnel in Portuguese/Latin American regions; detect execution of downloaded executables from browser temp directories with behavioral signatures matching Grandoreiro (registry/C2 callbacks).

suggestion.title: Grandoreiro Credential Harvesting from Browsers
suggestion.rationale: Grandoreiro is documented as targeting browser stored credentials and email clients; article references 'targeting banks' implies credential theft is the objective.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Grandoreiro-associated process names accessing browser credential stores (Chrome, Edge, Firefox), registry reads to HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Internet Explorer, or input capture hooks targeting banking portals.

suggestion.title: Grandoreiro Registry Persistence and Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: Banking trojans establish persistence via registry Run keys and propagate via shared network resources; article's targeting of multiple companies suggests multi-stage compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect modification of HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run and HKLM equivalents with suspicious values; correlate with network scans and SMB authentication attempts to adjacent hosts.

suggestion.title: Grandoreiro C2 Communication Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article describes active malware campaign; C2 beaconing and exfiltration are standard phases of banking trojan operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTPS POST requests to newly-registered domains or bulletproof-hosting providers; flag connections from compromised banking terminals to non-banking IP ranges; detect encrypted traffic bursts to Portuguese/.br domains post-infection.

suggestion.title: Grandoreiro Process Injection and Hooking
suggestion.rationale: Grandoreiro uses in-memory injection to hide credential-theft hooks; 'targeting banks' implies browser session hijacking or form-grabbing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unsigned DLL injection into svchost.exe, explorer.exe, or browser processes; detect hollowed processes with mismatched entry points; monitor for deobfuscation of embedded strings matching banking portal URLs.

suggestion.title: Phishing + Malware Delivery Chain (Weak Signals)
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Weak signals look harmless until they are connected to a larger phishing or malware chain.' Suggests need for correlation logic connecting initial phishing artifacts to downstream payload delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequences of suspicious emails followed by file downloads or URL redirects to command-and-control domains. Alert on phishing emails containing shortened URLs or suspicious file attachments in combination with subsequent network requests to known malware infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Persistence Mechanism Deployment
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'persistence mechanisms' exposed through behavioral analysis in sandboxed environments. Need detections for post-execution persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious modifications to autostart locations (registry Run keys, startup folders, scheduled tasks) following malware execution. Correlate file creation in persistence directories with parent process spawning from suspicious locations (temp, downloads, appdata).

suggestion.title: Payload Delivery with URL Redirects
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies behavioral analysis should expose 'redirects, payload delivery' in attack chains. Detects intermediate redirect infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sequences of URL redirects (3+ hops) with final payload dropped to suspicious locations. Monitor for GETs to benign domains immediately followed by POSTs/downloads to attacker-controlled infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Malware Network Connection Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'network connections' as part of complete attack picture, suggesting network-based signals are underutilized. Need detections for C2 communication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes spawned from suspicious locations (temp, appdata) initiating outbound connections to non-standard ports or to domains with suspicious registration metadata. Correlate with behavioral indicators (timing, frequency, payload size).

suggestion.title: Context Deficiency in Alert Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'Incomplete threat understanding: When files, URLs, domains, and network activity are analyzed separately, the complete attack picture remains unclear.' Suggests need for multi-indicator correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Build composite alerts that trigger when single IOC (hash, domain, IP) appears in combination with at least two other indicators from different signal categories within short time window. Weight alerts by historical enrichment context (known malware family, previous campaigns).

suggestion.title: Malicious Codex Remote UI Tool Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'Codex Remote UI' as attack vector: 'legitimate-looking' tool indicates masquerading and execution phase. Pipeline should have flagged any process matching this name or similar variants.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process execution, DLL load, or file creation events matching 'Codex', 'codex-remote', or 'codex_ui' patterns. Alert on unusual parent-child relationships (IDE → remote tool spawn). Cross-reference execution path against known legitimate Codex vendor binaries.

suggestion.title: AI Token Credential Exfiltration from Development Environment
suggestion.rationale: Core attack in title: tool 'steals AI tokens.' Should detect processes accessing token stores (OPENAI_API_KEY, .env files, credential managers) and subsequent exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes reading environment variables containing 'KEY', 'TOKEN', 'API' keywords; accessing ~/.env, ~/.config, or system credential stores; or reading files from development tool config directories. Correlate with unexpected child process spawns or network egress.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Outbound C2 Traffic from Development Tool
suggestion.rationale: Token theft implies exfiltration channel. Article describes 'secret' behavior stealing tokens—detect unusual network connections from IDE/development processes to attacker infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound HTTPS/HTTP connections initiated by processes named *codex*, *remote*, *ui* or from development tool parent processes to non-whitelisted IP ranges. Flag connections to newly-registered or bulletproof-hosting domains; look for HTTPS without certificate validation.

suggestion.title: Trojanized Package Installation from Untrusted Source
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'legitimate-looking'—classic supply chain distribution. Should detect installation/download of Codex variants via package managers (pip, npm, cargo) or non-canonical sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor pip/npm/cargo/poetry invocations for packages matching 'codex*', 'codex-remote*', or typosquatted variants. Flag installs from non-official registries. Alert on file downloads to development directories from suspicious origins or immediately followed by execution.

suggestion.title: IDE/Editor Configuration Hijacking for Remote Execution
suggestion.rationale: Remote UI tool likely persists or auto-executes via IDE plugin/extension mechanism. Should detect config file modifications that inject execution commands.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor modifications to VS Code settings.json, .vscode/extensions, vim/neovim config, IDE startup scripts, or editor extension directories. Alert on new entries launching suspicious executables or downloading remote scripts. Cross-reference file timestamps against tool installation times.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm package file enumeration and exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'Malicious npm Package Stole Files From Claude AI User Directory'—describes discovery and collection phases. No use case was generated to detect unusual file read/enumerate operations from npm package context (node_modules executables accessing user home directories) followed by external network activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect node.exe or npm-spawned child processes accessing ~/.claude or user home directory files in bulk or via directory traversal, particularly if parent process originated from node_modules. Correlate with unexpected outbound HTTPS or Git operations to external hosts within same session window.

suggestion.title: npm package supply chain compromise detection
suggestion.rationale: Article headline explicitly names 'Malicious npm Package' but pipeline extracted no IOCs (package name, version hash, registry metadata). Supply-chain attacks via npm are T1195.001; should detect anomalous package installation, suspicious post-install scripts, or version divergence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install / npm ci operations with uncommon or newly-published package versions. Flag post-install script execution that spawns file system enumeration (find, dir, ls -R) or network utilities (curl, wget, git clone) to external endpoints. Correlate with package download timestamps from registry.

suggestion.title: GitHub-based exfiltration from Claude user directories
suggestion.rationale: Article title includes 'via GitHub'; implies exfiltration vector is GitHub (repo push, gist creation, or file upload). Pipeline missed both the GitHub connection and the exfiltration phase. Should detect file operations to .claude directory followed by git operations or HTTPS uploads to GitHub hosts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect git.exe, curl, or Python spawned from npm package context with destination github.com or github-user-content.com shortly after bulk file reads from ~/.claude. Flag new repo creation or gist uploads correlated with suspicious npm package execution window.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized .claude directory access from child processes
suggestion.rationale: Target is explicitly 'Claude AI User Directory'; the ~/.claude path stores authentication tokens, settings, and potentially API keys. Pipeline should flag any non-IDE process accessing this path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file open/read operations on ~/.claude/* files by processes outside the claude-code IDE or official Anthropic tooling. Baseline allowed processes and alert on anomalies, especially from npm-spawned contexts or node processes with unexpected parents.

suggestion.title: Post-installation malicious script execution in npm packages
suggestion.rationale: Malicious npm packages commonly hide payload in postinstall scripts. Article describes file theft (active behavior), implying code execution after installation. No use case for detecting malicious postinstall hooks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm postinstall script execution (node.exe with npm context) that spawns suspicious child processes: PowerShell, cmd.exe with file operations, network utilities. Flag exec/child_process calls in package.json or arbitrary shell escapes in postinstall definitions.

suggestion.title: Preinstalled System App Injecting Code into Third-Party App
suggestion.rationale: Article states app is 'hijacking Amazon App' — this is direct code/hook injection into a high-value target, core attack mechanic not surfaced
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for system/preinstalled apps attempting ptrace, dlopen, or hook injection targeting Amazon or other e-commerce apps. Flag unsigned library loads into target app address space. Baseline: system apps should not inject into third-party processes.

suggestion.title: Affiliate Code Injection into Amazon App Traffic
suggestion.rationale: Core attack is 'injecting affiliate codes into Amazon' — detect URL parameter tampering and unauthorized tracking-ID insertion
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Capture Amazon app HTTPS traffic and baseline legitimate referral parameters. Alert on insertion of third-party affiliate IDs, tag parameters, or redirect clauses. Correlate timing with Motorola preinstalled app process execution.

suggestion.title: System App Contacting Affiliate/Ad-Network Domains
suggestion.rationale: Monetization hijack implies exfiltration or command to affiliate brokers — preinstalled apps should not contact ad networks or tracking services
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline DNS/IP destinations for Motorola preinstalled apps (should be minimal/internal). Flag outbound connections to known affiliate networks, ad brokers, or monetization domains. Correlate with Amazon app activity timeline.

suggestion.title: Motorola Preinstalled App Runtime Privilege Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Only apps with elevated SELinux context or system signature can hook other apps — detect capability/permission abuse enabling interception
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Motorola system apps should have tightly scoped capabilities. Alert on PTRACE, SETCAP, or HOOK permissions; unusual UID escalation; or capability grants to preinstalled apps during Amazon app use. Review manifest vs. runtime permissions.

suggestion.title: Amazon App Binary/Library Substitution or Modification
suggestion.rationale: Hijacking could also occur via library substitution or manifest hooking — detect unauthorized filesystem modifications to Amazon app directory
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor /data/app/com.amazon* and library paths for unsigned modifications. Flag write operations from preinstalled apps to Amazon app sandbox. Baseline Amazon app manifest and native libraries; alert on unexpected changes.

suggestion.title: Suspicious App Update or Version Rollback from System App
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain compromise via preinstall suggests possible ongoing payload delivery — detect if system app triggers Amazon app updates or patches
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal Amazon app update triggers originating from non-standard sources (not Play Store direct or user action). Alert if Motorola preinstalled app initiates app patches, version rollbacks, or sideloads. Verify update signatures.

suggestion.title: Android Malware APK Installation from Untrusted Source
suggestion.rationale: Article title references 'remotely control Android devices' and body alludes to installation vector; pipeline must detect APK delivery/sideload attempts, unusual app installations from non-Play Store sources, or permission grant anomalies on Android.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for APK files downloaded to writable directories, execution of 'pm install' commands, or SELinux violations on Android. Flag installation from unknown sources or with suspicious package names matching malware families.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Command Execution via Runtime or ADB-like Interface
suggestion.rationale: BTMOB described as enabling remote control; implies command execution capability. Pipeline must detect shell commands executed outside normal app context or unusual process spawn chains from package management subsystems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned from suspicious parent processes (e.g., app frameworks, system daemons). Look for Runtime.exec() or similar API calls executing shell commands, particularly those reading/writing to /data/local/tmp or /cache.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Location, Camera, or Microphone Access
suggestion.rationale: Remote-control malware typically exfiltrates location, captures screen/video, or records audio; article describes 'remote control' implying surveillance capabilities but pipeline extracted no detection for these high-risk permissions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag requests to GPS location APIs, camera/video APIs, or microphone APIs from background processes or apps without user-facing UI. Correlate to abnormal network exfiltration immediately following sensor access.

suggestion.title: Credential Extraction from Local Keystores
suggestion.rationale: Remote-control malware frequently targets credential vaults; article suggests broad compromise but pipeline missed this standard attack surface. Detect reads from Android Keystore, credential files, or browser cookie/password stores.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file access to /data/data/*/databases, /data/data/*/shared_prefs, or attempts to access KeyStore system services outside normal system processes. Correlate to subsequent network exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Command and Control Communication on Non-Standard Ports or Encrypted Channels
suggestion.rationale: Remote control requires persistent C2; article title emphasizes control capability but pipeline provided no IOCs, domains, or C2 patterns. Detect unusual outbound traffic, particularly to non-standard ports or to newly registered/suspicious domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound connections from app processes to non-whitelisted IPs/domains, especially on ports 8080, 8888, 9999, or traffic to IP ranges not matching known CDNs. Correlate timing to malware execution windows.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of Sensitive Data to Cloud or External Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Remote-control implant harvests data (contacts, messages, photos) but pipeline generated zero exfiltration detections. Detect bulk data reads followed by outbound connections to non-standard endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for large sequential reads from /data/data (app caches, DBs), /DCIM (photos), or /Android/media, followed by network traffic to suspicious endpoints within seconds. Alert on unusual upload sizes or protocols.

suggestion.title: Impossible Travel During MFA Challenge
suggestion.rationale: AiTM attacks intercept auth flows in real-time. If victim is in one geography and attacker's proxy in another, auth logs will show contradictory geolocations between username/password submission and MFA response. Title establishes MFA bypass mechanism; impossible travel indicates interception.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate sign-in initiation IP/geolocation with MFA challenge acknowledgment IP within <2 minutes. Flag >500 km deltas. Entra ID: SignInLogs where riskState != none AND location change between AuthenticationDetails entries. Google: Monitor LocationChallenge events against preceding auth sessions.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Device Registration Post-MFA Bypass
suggestion.rationale: AiTM kit establishes session; attacker may immediately register new device to maintain persistence. 'Tycoon 2FA' title implies toolkit capability. Follow successful unusual auth with device enrollment anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when device registration occurs within 5 minutes of successful auth from atypical location or anonymous IP. Entra: AuditLogs filtered to RegisterDevice action preceded by risky SignInLogs. Filter for managed identity enrollment from unmanaged devices.

suggestion.title: Token Replay or Reuse Across Geographies
suggestion.rationale: AiTM captures session tokens/refresh tokens to bypass MFA entirely on subsequent requests. Article describes 'bypasses MFA'—implies token theft. Attacker uses stolen token from attacker-controlled proxy.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Token refresh events should not originate from geographies that contradict preceding user activity. Correlate token issue location with historical user base. Entra: TokenIssued events where IssuedAt location != user's typical region AND no intervening travel log. Alert on token use >6000km from apparent user location.

suggestion.title: Phishing Domain Spoofing Azure/Google Auth Pages
suggestion.rationale: AiTM kit requires credential capture. Title omits delivery vector but implied phishing to login.live.com / accounts.google.com clones. 'Tycoon 2FA' is likely distributed via email or ads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect email for URLs to lookalike domains (e.g., login-live.com, logine.live.com, accounts-google-verify.com). Check DNS resolutions to non-Microsoft/Google IP ranges. Proxy: alert on HTTP to domains within edit-distance ≤2 of identity provider hostnames. WHOIS registration <90 days.

suggestion.title: Certificate Pinning Bypass or SSL Downgrade During Auth
suggestion.rationale: AiTM interception requires HTTPS stripping or cert substitution. Entra ID / Google Workspace enforce cert pinning; successful interception leaves forensic traces (cert reissue, TLS version downgrade, cipher suite anomaly).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: TLS logs: flag login endpoints using ciphers or TLS <1.2 or non-issued certificates. Network: detect SSL cert replacements for identity provider domains mid-session. Proxy: if client_cert_presented != expected issuer chain, escalate. Inspect proxy logs for CONNECT tunnels to *.live.com / *.google.com during high-risk auth windows.

suggestion.title: Entra ID / Google Workspace Auth from Proxy Service IPs
suggestion.rationale: Tycoon kit likely proxies through commercial proxy services or residental IPs. Entra/Google auth from datacenter/proxy-provider IP ranges is atypical and correlates to AiTM.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Tag IPs of known proxy/VPN/residential proxy providers (Bright Data, Oxylabs, ASN correlation). Alert when auth originates from these IP pools, especially if preceded by email with phishing indicators. Baseline: auth IP geolocation should match user's historical login regions within 48 hours.

suggestion.title: Detect Large-Scale Salesforce Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'stolen over 600,000 records containing corporate data and personally identifiable information' and 'leaked a 9.4GB archive' from Salesforce. Pipeline missed exfiltration signal entirely. Detection should flag abnormal bulk export or API access pattern from Salesforce.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Salesforce audit logs for rapid sequential data access spanning multiple object types (Contacts, Accounts, custom fields) within compressed timeframe, or unusual export/API calls returning >100k records. Correlate with failed authentication attempts (credential stuffing) or impossible travel patterns if MFA logs available.

suggestion.title: Track Salesforce Credential Compromise Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies compromise of 'Salesforce environment' on April 8. Attack vector (credential theft, API key compromise, SSO bypass) not stated, but credential abuse is the most probable initial access given the scale. Pipeline ignored initial access entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect successful Salesforce logins from unusual geographies, IPs, or time-of-day patterns inconsistent with historical user behavior. Flag logins immediately preceding bulk data access queries. Cross-reference with credential stuffing/spray attacks on OAuth endpoints or Salesforce SSO integrations.

suggestion.title: Salesforce Persistence via Document/Record Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article notes attackers accessed 'certain 7-Eleven systems used to store franchisee documents'—implying persistence to maintain access across data exfiltration window (April 8–17). Pipeline missed persistence phase entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Salesforce for creation of administrative users, API tokens, or OAuth connections during compromise window. Flag modifications to sharing rules or field-level security that grant broad access to sensitive objects. Look for service accounts or automation users added post-breach discovery.

suggestion.title: Dark Web Leak Site Data Posting by Known Extortion Groups
suggestion.rationale: Article states ShinyHunters 'leaked a 9.4GB archive of documents on their dark web leak site after the company refused to pay a ransom.' This impact phase (data leak threat) is not modeled despite being the primary evidence of compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on darknet forum/leak-site postings attributed to ShinyHunters that reference Salesforce, franchisee data, or 7-Eleven by name. Cross-reference timing (April 17 claim) with internal Salesforce audit logs to validate compromise. Monitor ShinyHunters' known leak domains and Telegram channels for victim announcements.

suggestion.title: Detect Salesforce Aura Campaign Targeting Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies ShinyHunters' 'Salesforce Aura data theft attacks' and 'Salesloft Drift campaign'—indicating organized, repeated targeting of Salesforce SaaS supply chain. Pipeline did not surface threat-actor campaign or reuse patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify customers using Salesforce with similar data profiles (franchisee/reseller networks, retail PII at scale) and profile their login anomalies during the Aura campaign window (past 12 months). Flag orgs with logins from infrastructure previously associated with ShinyHunters or shared exploit patterns (e.g., specific OAuth phishing templates).

suggestion.title: Monitor Ransomware Demand Communications Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article describes ransom extortion: 'ShinyHunters... leaked a 9.4GB archive... after the company refused to pay a ransom.' Pipeline lacks detection for threat-actor outreach, ransom notes, or dark-web negotiation activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound email to security, executive, and IR contacts for messages containing victim company name, data sample, leak-site URLs, or ransom amounts. Alert on dark-web forum activity linking company name to ShinyHunters posts. Track timeline: first contact usually 2–7 days post-exfiltration completion.

suggestion.title: APK Installation from Phishing Domain or Fake App Store
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Operators send victims to phishing websites that pose as streaming services, cryptocurrency mining platforms or other familiar online services. From there, victims are pushed toward fake app stores that mimic legitimate repositories and prompt them to install a malicious APK.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect APK installations originating from domains with phishing indicators or known fake app store URLs. Flag installations from URLs matching legitimate app store domains but with typosquatting or subdomain anomalies. Correlate network traffic to phishing domains with subsequent APK download events.

suggestion.title: Suspicious App Requesting Accessibility Service Permission
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'It abuses Android Accessibility Services to gain elevated permissions and grant itself further system access without additional user interaction.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when a newly installed or suspicious APK (low reputation, unsigned, or from non-Play Store source) requests Accessibility Service permissions. Combine with subsequent suspicious behaviors: file system access, network exfiltration, or device admin requests.

suggestion.title: Screenshot and Recording API Abuse with Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article describes capabilities: 'exfiltrate a range of sensitive data, capture screenshots and record activity on the device'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequences of API calls to screenshot or audio/video recording functions followed by unusual network connections or data transfers. Flag combinations of MediaRecorder, ScreenCapture, and clipboard access APIs within short timeframes by the same process.

suggestion.title: Government Agency Impersonation in Phishing Campaigns
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'researchers Johnk3r and Merl recently spotted campaigns that spread BTMOB while impersonating Argentina's tax and customs authorities.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for phishing emails, SMS, or web pages impersonating government tax authorities, customs agencies, or financial regulators, especially those directing users to install mobile applications. Correlate sender reputation, domain spoofing, and call-to-action patterns.

suggestion.title: Rapid Malware Variant Proliferation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'Cyble's report from February 2025 noted that roughly 15 samples of BTMOB v2.5 had been spotted since late January of that year, i.e., in a mere two or so weeks.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Implement clustering detection for APK samples with shared builder signatures, identical C2 infrastructure, or near-identical bytecode despite different compilation timestamps or obfuscation. Alert on volumetric variant generation indicating MaaS payload builder activity.

suggestion.title: Malware-as-a-Service Sales Channel Monitoring
suggestion.rationale: Article describes distribution: 'The sales pipeline extends across social media platforms, with a number of accounts on X and Instagram actively peddling the tool.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor X, Instagram, and Telegram for accounts promoting malware toolkits, APK builders, or RAT services. Flag accounts with sales language, pricing information, or technical screenshots of malware builder interfaces. Correlate with known malware family IOCs.

suggestion.title: Microsoft Entra ID Account Compromise via Voice Phishing
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'breached Charter on April 1 through a voice phishing (vishing) attack that compromised an employee's Microsoft Entra account.' This is the initial compromise vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Entra ID sign-ins immediately following reported phishing incidents, unusual login locations or devices, rapid credential use from newly compromised accounts, and failed MFA challenges followed by successful auth from new IPs.

suggestion.title: Salesforce Bulk Customer Record Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The threat actors used this access to export millions of consumer and business customer records from the company's Salesforce instance.' Clear large-scale data export pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Salesforce bulk export APIs (export to CSV, SOQL mass queries), unusually large record downloads within short windows, or data access from compromised/newly activated service accounts.

suggestion.title: Rapid Multi-SaaS Access from Single Compromised Identity
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'After gaining access to a corporate SSO account, the threat actors steal data from connected SaaS applications such as Salesforce, Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, SAP, Slack, Adobe, Atlassian, Zendesk, Dropbox, and many others.' Clear lateral movement signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect single identity accessing 5+ SaaS platforms in short time window, especially if followed by data export operations in those platforms. Cross-reference successful auth to data access events.

suggestion.title: Stolen OAuth Token Usage for Salesforce Unauthorized Access
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'threat actors breaching numerous integration companies to steal OAuth tokens that can then be used to access Salesforce instances.' Specific token-theft attack pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Salesforce API access from known compromised OAuth scopes, authentication from integration service accounts that show unusual client versions or IP addresses, or token replay patterns.

suggestion.title: Customer Support Ticket Exfiltration from Salesforce
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'the threat actor also claims to have stolen customer support ticket data.' Indicates access to Service Cloud records beyond customer databases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk export of Case records, Knowledge article downloads, or unusual querying patterns against Service Cloud objects, especially if originating from service accounts.

suggestion.title: Compromised Employee Account Used to Export CPNI Data
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'the stolen records contain...some CPNI data' and 'no sensitive personal information (PI) or customer proprietary network information (CPNI) data was exfiltrated' (disputed by threat actor). Implies CPNI record access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track access to CPNI-tagged fields in customer records by user account; alert on queries accessing phone_type, plan_info, or CPNI fields by accounts not normally querying those fields.

suggestion.title: Cannot assess—article body truncated
suggestion.rationale: The article body provided contains only CSS @font-face declarations and no narrative content describing threat activities, attack procedures, or defensive measures. suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Requires full article text to assess.

suggestion.title: Chatbot API Response Poisoning / Malicious Recommendation Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'AI Chatbot Recommendations Redirect Users' — the chatbot itself is either compromised or serving injected malicious suggestions. Pipeline should detect anomalous API responses, external redirects in chatbot payloads, or recommendation patterns pointing to known-malicious domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor chatbot API responses for URLs flagged as malicious or crypto-related; flag recommendations pointing to newly registered domains or IP ranges associated with cryptojacking infrastructure. Cross-reference recommendations against threat feeds.

suggestion.title: User Execution of Chatbot-Supplied Malicious Links
suggestion.rationale: Attack flow: user receives chatbot recommendation, follows link, lands on cryptojacking site. Article phrase 'Redirect Users to Cryptojacking Malware Sites' describes T1204.001 execution vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag clicks/navigations to cryptojacking-attributed domains within 1–5 minutes of chatbot interaction. Correlate browser navigation logs with chatbot request logs to establish causal chain.

suggestion.title: Cryptojacking Malware Process Execution & Resource Hijacking
suggestion.rationale: Article title terminates with 'Cryptojacking Malware Sites' — implying malware execution and T1496 impact. Pipeline missed detection of mining processes, GPU/CPU spikes, and connections to mining pools.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous process spawning (common crypto-miner names: xmrig, stratum+tcp connections), sustained CPU >80% on non-workload processes, or outbound connections to known mining pools (stratum.mining.pool domains, port 3333/3334/9999).

suggestion.title: C2 Communication to Cryptocurrency Mining Pool Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Cryptojacking requires persistent C2 with mining coordinator. Article implies this post-infection, but pipeline did not model C2 phase or generate detections for mining-pool beaconing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DNS queries and TCP connections to known cryptocurrency mining pools, stratum+tcp:// URIs, or monero/bitcoin pool domains. Flag sustained connections to single external IP on non-standard cryptomining ports.

suggestion.title: Malicious Redirect Chain Analysis (Chatbot → Landing Page → Malware Delivery)
suggestion.rationale: Multi-stage redirect from chatbot recommendation to final malware site. Article phrase 'Redirect Users' and 'to Cryptojacking Malware Sites' indicates 1+ hops. Pipeline did not model or detect redirect chains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect redirect chains: chatbot domain → intermediate domain(s) → malware site. Flag if intermediate domain is newly registered, fast-flux, or hosted in high-risk ASNs. Correlate HTTP 301/302 responses with destination reputation.

suggestion.title: BadHost Vulnerability Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly describes 'Attackers Can Exploit BadHost to Access Sensitive AI Agent Server Endpoints'—no detection coverage generated despite clear exploitation attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for HTTP requests to AI agent server endpoints that match BadHost exploit patterns, unusual User-Agent strings associated with exploitation frameworks, or POST requests to known vulnerable endpoint paths with malformed parameters. Correlate with 4xx/5xx error responses indicating exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Access to AI Agent Service Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article describes sensitive endpoint access resulting from BadHost—pipeline should flag unauthorized service account or anomalous authentication patterns to AI infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for successful authentication or session establishment to AI agent services from unusual source IPs, non-standard ports, or with atypical user agents. Flag any access to /agent/, /service/, or /api/ endpoint paths from external networks.

suggestion.title: BadHost IOC Correlation with Web Traffic
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability name 'BadHost' suggests domain/host-based exploitation—pipeline should surface domain IOC extraction and C2 communication patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect DNS queries or HTTP traffic to domains/hosts matching BadHost exploit infrastructure patterns. Alert on communication to known malicious hosts exploiting this vulnerability or hosting exploit code.

suggestion.title: Detect AD password spray attacks
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'Password spraying attacks rely on exploiting that tendency'—the core threat motivating policy hardening. Detection should monitor login failure patterns across multiple accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on ≥5 failed AD authentication attempts in 5-min window targeting distinct user accounts from single source IP. Or ≥3 failed Kerberos pre-auth attempts (Event 4771) for same account from multiple source IPs within short time window.

suggestion.title: Detect logon attempts using compromised credentials from breach databases
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes breach-password detection: 'continuously checking passwords against...5.4 billion known breached credentials' and notes 'stolen credentials are involved in 44.7% of breaches.' Should flag successful logons using credentials matching known-compromised repositories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful Kerberos TGT/TGS grants with credential-leak intelligence from public breaches (HaveIBeenPwned, etc.). Prioritize alerts when compromised-cred logon occurs from anomalous location, time, or device.

suggestion.title: Detect AD password policy violations and weak password creation patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article warns users defeat strict policies by 'adding a predictable ! to the end of the last version' or reusing credentials. Should detect policy violations and circumvention attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for ≥2 password resets by same account within 24 hours (indicator of minimal-change circumvention). Detect password-change patterns matching regex for previous-password + predictable-suffix mutations. Alert on AD GPO/schema changes weakening password complexity (Event 5139).

suggestion.title: Detect CVE-2026-48172 exploitation attempts via cpanel_jsonapi_func=redisAble in logs
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly provides grep signature 'cpanel_jsonapi_func=redisAble' and recommends searching /var/cpanel/logs/ and /usr/local/cpanel/logs/ to detect exploitation. Pipeline extracted neither the function signature nor any detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search cPanel logs for patterns matching 'cpanel_jsonapi_func=redisAble'. Correlate matches with source IPs and timestamps. Flag any occurrence as potential CVE-2026-48172 exploitation; collect IPs for threat analysis and blocking.

suggestion.title: Detect unauthenticated privilege escalation to root via Redis handler
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability allows 'remote attackers with no privileges to execute arbitrary scripts with root privileges' through 'mishandling of Redis enable/disable features.' No detection for this unprivileged-to-root escalation chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process execution where a low-UID or unauthenticated context spawns shell commands with UID 0. Baseline normal cPanel/LiteSpeed behavior and alert on deviations, especially inline bash/sh execution immediately following Redis function calls.

suggestion.title: Detect arbitrary command execution from Redis-enabled cPanel contexts
suggestion.rationale: Article states exploitation results in 'arbitrary scripts' execution via Redis. No detection use case captures post-exploitation command execution patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag processes spawned by cPanel or Redis handler service accounts executing shell commands with elevated/root privileges. Focus on suspicious one-liners, encoded commands, or unsigned script invocation.

suggestion.title: Detect unauthenticated requests to cPanel redisAble/redisDisable endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability requires 'remote attackers with no privileges,' indicating unauthenticated function invocation is possible. No detection for unauthenticated API calls to vulnerable endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor cPanel API/web logs for requests to redisAble or redisDisable functions without valid session tokens, authentication headers, or from non-whitelisted IPs. Flag repeated failures or successful invocations from unusual sources.

suggestion.title: Detect suspicious IP access patterns correlated with CVE-2026-48172 indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article advises to 'examine the IPs in the list, determine if they are valid, and if not, block them,' implying IP-based correlation is core to detecting exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate IPs observed in cPanel logs matching redisAble patterns against threat intelligence feeds, geographic baselines, and access history. Alert on IPs from unexpected countries/ASNs or with prior malicious history.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure Hunt: Nx Console Installations
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'malicious version of Nx Console to be published' and 'Federal patch due: 2026-06-10'—core requirement is inventory of exposed instances before exploitation window closes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt Nx Console process execution, installed version via registry/file paths, and marketplace/installer logs. Correlate against CISA due date to flag unpatched systems requiring immediate remediation.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting from Protected Storage
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly: 'harvested credentials from multiple sources on disk and in memory.' Maps to T1555 and memory-access patterns detectable through process instrumentation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Nx Console or node child processes accessing credential directories (%APPDATA%\Microsoft\Credentials, browser password stores, .ssh/), or spawning credential-dumping utilities (lsass access, rundll32 with dpapi DLLs, mimikatz patterns).

suggestion.title: Obfuscated Payload Fetch by Nx Console
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'fetched an obfuscated payload'—indicates post-compromise command-and-control or malware staging detectable via network and process behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from Nx Console/node to non-official Nx domains, or process execution with obfuscation indicators (base64 -d, certutil -encode, powershell -enc) spawned post-installation.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Child Process Execution from Nx Console
suggestion.rationale: Credential access and obfuscated payload handling require system utility spawning. Article describes these capabilities, implying process chain anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag child processes from Nx Console (parent: node.exe) spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, rundll32.exe, or accessing lsass/ntdll. Weight heavily if followed by network exfiltration or credential store access.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Integrity: Nx Console Version Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'malicious version of Nx Console to be published'—supply-chain compromise (T1195.002) requires monitoring package registry, file integrity, and version downgrades.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor extension manifest modifications, registry persistence for Nx paths, unexpected downgrades, or installations from non-standard sources. Compare installed extension hashes against vendor signatures if available.

suggestion.title: Daemon Tools Lite Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' using canonical templates; Daemon Tools Lite is named as the vulnerable product currently being exploited in the wild (CISA KEV status).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for any system running Daemon Tools Lite in your fleet. Correlate against vulnerability scanner patch status; flag systems that report as patched but still contain unpatched registry keys or installation directories, as patch lag and scanner misreporting are common gaps.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Daemon Tools Lite Version Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' and establishes federal due date of 2026-05-30; scanner results may not reflect true runtime patch state.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Daemon Tools Lite installation version from registry HKLM\Software\Daemon Tools or software inventory; flag versions released before the patch cutoff as vulnerable. Alert when scanner-reported patch status contradicts actual version discovery on endpoints.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation High-Impact Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'high impact on confidentiality, integrity, and availability'; unspecified vulnerability likely yields direct system compromise requiring post-incident detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On systems running Daemon Tools Lite, monitor for bulk reads from sensitive directories, unexpected file modifications, outbound data transfer spikes, or encryption activity. Correlate with abnormal process spawning (shell, utilities) from Daemon Tools service or parent process.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-8398 Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status confirms active in-the-wild exploitation (T1190); should hunt for exploitation attempts to enable early intervention before compromise occurs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Daemon Tools service logs and process tree anomalies for abnormal child spawning (cmd, powershell, network utilities) or service crashes/restarts correlated with suspicious outbound connections or command execution immediately after.

suggestion.title: Continuous Autonomous API Endpoint Probing
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Autonomous attackers are already probing application surfaces continuously at machine speed, on a schedule defenders can't keep up with.' This explicitly describes reconnaissance activity requiring detection rules on API access anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sources making rapid, systematic requests to API endpoints with incrementally varying parameters, path traversal patterns, or sequential ID enumeration. Baseline normal API endpoint discovery and flag sources exceeding thresholds for unique endpoint + parameter combinations within rolling time windows.

suggestion.title: BOLA/IDOR Authorization Probing
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'BOLA or IDOR, cross-tenant data leakage, authentication bypasses...None of these have a heuristic signature...it's a chain of authorization probes guided by structural reasoning about how API objects relate to identities.' Describes detection method requiring monitoring of authorization boundary tests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor API requests where authenticated users access resources with different ownership contexts or IDs derived from other users' responses. Alert on patterns: sequential ID access across tenants, accessing resources without proper owner relationship, or escalating from read to write after initial ID discovery.

suggestion.title: Chained Low-Grade Vulnerability Exploitation Sequences
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'chained vulnerabilities, where a couple of mediums and highs combine into a critical exploit path.' Requires detection of correlated low-severity events forming exploit chains rather than isolated findings.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate sequences of low-severity events from single sources: failed auth attempts followed by injection attempts followed by parameter tampering. Alert on multi-stage sequences where individually minor anomalies cluster, suggesting deliberate exploitation chain rather than isolated errors.

suggestion.title: API Reconnaissance-to-Exploitation Transition
suggestion.rationale: Article describes transition from generic heuristic detection to context-aware reasoning: 'What does the code do?' to 'What is it meant to do, and can I subvert that intent?' Requires behavioral detection of reconnaissance shifting toward informed exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline reconnaissance pattern for each source: error probes, OPTIONS/HEAD requests, envelope testing. Alert when pattern shifts from broad/random probing to targeted, parameter-specific, or endpoint-specific requests against particular resources—indicating attacker has gained contextual understanding.

suggestion.title: Cross-Tenant or Cross-User Data Boundary Violations
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'cross-tenant data leakage' as core context-dependent vulnerability. Should trigger specific multi-tenant access control monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For multi-tenant SaaS: flag API requests where authenticated user accesses resources owned by different tenant. Establish legitimate tenant relationship matrix and alert on unauthorized cross-tenant reads/writes, especially high-volume or bulk exfiltration patterns.

suggestion.title: Error Message Leakage from Offensive DAST Payload Testing
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'DAST takes the other approach: it throws payloads at a running application or API and observes responses: error messages, time delays, behavioral differences.' Describes how attackers learn from error responses; pipeline should detect this reconnaissance signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sources generating statistically unusual error response distributions (high volume of 400/403/404/500 codes, diverse error message content) or time-delayed responses indicating backend behavior probing. Flag sources that generate errors from payloads (SQLi markers, XSS vectors, path traversal patterns) even if injection fails.

suggestion.title: Phishing Domain Access - FIFA World Cup Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 300+ fake domains targeting FIFA World Cup fans. Pipeline generated zero domain-based detection despite this being the primary IOC vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect DNS queries and HTTP connections to GHOST STADIUM phishing domains. Flag newly registered domains with FIFA/World Cup/ticket keywords combined with homoglyph or typosquat patterns. Monitor for form submissions to external phishing infrastructure from user endpoints.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email - World Cup Ticket / Credential Lure
suggestion.rationale: Campaign targets FIFA fans via phishing with 300+ domains; article text mentions phishing delivery mechanism but pipeline produced no email-based detection UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound emails with FIFA/World Cup ticket urgency themes, fake domain sender headers, or embedded links to GHOST STADIUM domains. Correlate subject lines and sender patterns with known phishing campaigns targeting sporting events.

suggestion.title: Credential Submission to Phishing Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Phishing campaign with 300+ domains implies credential harvesting endpoint; no detection UC addresses successful form submission or authentication attempt to phishing domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for POST requests to phishing domains containing credential-like payloads. Detect password spray attempts or successful logins against external infrastructure. Correlate user credentials submitted to GHOST STADIUM domains with downstream account compromise signals.

suggestion.title: Domain Registration - GHOST STADIUM Campaign Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Campaign explicitly named GHOST STADIUM with 300+ domains; pipeline did not surface threat actor infrastructure tracking or domain registration monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor domain registration feeds for bulk registrations matching GHOST STADIUM naming patterns, FIFA/World Cup keywords, or infrastructure overlaps with previous actor domains. Flag newly registered domains with shared registrant details, payment methods, or AS paths.

suggestion.title: Yamcs JavaExprAlgorithmExecutionFactory malicious code compilation detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability is in 'org.yamcs.algorithms.JavaExprAlgorithmExecutionFactory' which 'dynamically compiles and evaluates user-controlled algorithm text without enforcing a secure sandbox'. Should detect when algorithm text contains Java process execution APIs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Yamcs application or debug logs for JavaExprAlgorithmExecutionFactory class instantiation followed by algorithm text compilation containing java.lang.Runtime, java.lang.ProcessBuilder, or reflection APIs (getMethod, invoke). Alert on successful compilation of such expressions.

suggestion.title: Yamcs ChangeMissionDatabase privilege escalation by non-admin account
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'authenticated user with the ChangeMissionDatabase privilege can exploit this'. Detect privilege assumption or role assignment of ChangeMissionDatabase to accounts without administrative entitlement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Yamcs authentication/authorization logs for ChangeMissionDatabase role assignment to non-privileged accounts or role elevation outside change-management windows. Correlate subsequent algorithm modification API calls with privilege assumption timestamp.

suggestion.title: Template Syntax Injection in HTTP Request Parameters
suggestion.rationale: Article details the attack vector: '{%assign r=1|valueOf%}' and '{{r|inspect}}' are the initial payload patterns. No UC detects malicious template syntax in request parameters, only post-exploitation shell spawning. Network IDS/WAF layer should match these patterns before Node processing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP request bodies and URL parameters for Liquid template tags ({% %}, {{ }}), assignment operators with filter chains (|valueOf, |inspect, |group_by), and __proto__ traversal attempts. Filter for requests to Node.js/IIS endpoints known to process templates.

suggestion.title: Object Prototype Chain Traversal in Application Logs
suggestion.rationale: The exploit specifically uses '__proto__', 'context.scopes', 'liquid.parser', 'liquid.options.fs' to traverse the object hierarchy. If LiquidJS logs template compilation or filter evaluation, these traversals would appear as error traces or debug output. No UC covers application-layer logging.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor application logs for template engine error traces containing 'valueOf', '__proto__', 'context.scopes', or 'Circular' references (article shows JSON with [Circular]). Flag any successful evaluation of object prototypes in template context.

suggestion.title: getBuiltinModule Access for Node.js APIs (pre-RCE)
suggestion.rationale: Article payload chain uses 'getBuiltinModule' to access child_process and fs modules. This is the bridge from SSTI to command execution. Intermediate detection here (before shell spawn) closes the gap earlier in the kill chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: If Node.js is instrumented for module tracing, detect access to 'child_process' or 'fs' modules from LiquidJS template execution context. Alternatively, monitor for 'require' or 'import' of system modules within template-processing stack frames.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Container Image Manifest Access
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'Exposes Private Container Images without Authentication.' Pipeline failed to generate detection for OCI/Docker API calls retrieving container manifests (image metadata, digest, config references) without valid auth tokens or credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful HTTP 200 responses to container registry manifest endpoints (/v2/<imagename>/manifests/<ref>, application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.v2+json) from requests lacking Authorization header or with invalid/missing registry credentials. Correlate with prior unauthenticated probes.

suggestion.title: Bulk Private Container Image Layer Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Unauthenticated access to 'private' images implies attackers can enumerate and download image layers containing source code, binaries, and secrets—core exfiltration phase absent from pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequential blob/layer downloads (GET /v2/<imagename>/blobs/sha256:*) from single source totaling >100MB within 5 minutes, especially targeting internal/private image names. Monitor for config blob retrieval (application/vnd.docker.container.image.v1+json) enabling extraction of embedded ENV, credentials.

suggestion.title: Gitea Container Registry Catalog Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability allows unauthenticated discovery of private image names—catalog endpoint (/v2/_catalog, OCI Distribution Spec) enumeration should be detected as reconnaissance step pipeline missed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful (/v2/_catalog or paginated catalog queries returning >50 image names) or repeated catalog enumeration from unauthenticated sources. Flag multi-request catalog enumeration with n parameter increments indicating full private image inventory traversal.

suggestion.title: Gitea Container Registry Unauthenticated HEAD/Ping Probes
suggestion.rationale: Attackers verify container registry presence and availability before exploitation—HEAD requests to /v2/ or registry health endpoints should trigger detection; pipeline generated no reconnaissance detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HEAD /v2/ or GET /v2/ health/ping requests returning 200/401 from external/suspicious sources, especially when followed by enumeration or image pull attempts within minutes. Correlate across multiple Gitea instances suggesting vulnerability scanning.

suggestion.title: Container Image Config Environment Variable Disclosure
suggestion.rationale: Container images often embed secrets (API keys, passwords, DB strings) in ENV layer—unauthenticated config blob access enables credential extraction. Pipeline failed to suggest detection for this critical data loss scenario.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthenticated retrieval of image config blobs containing JSON encoding of environment variables. Alert when config access is followed by outbound API calls matching extracted credentials or connection strings (e.g., postgres://, mongodb+srv://).

suggestion.title: Gitea Version Disclosure followed by Registry Access
suggestion.rationale: Attackers must identify vulnerable Gitea versions before exploiting registry vulnerability—version enumeration (404 page fingerprinting, /api/v1/version endpoints) followed by registry probing is a reliable kill-chain indicator pipeline missed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Gitea version disclosure attempts (requests to /.gitea/version, error page parsing, default path probes) succeeded by container registry enumeration within 5 minutes. Flag source IPs performing version scans across multiple Gitea instances.

suggestion.title: Malicious VS Code Extension Installation from OpenVSX
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'malicious OpenVSX and Microsoft VS Code extensions that stole cryptocurrency wallets and developer credentials' and 'one campaign in March impacting more than 400 software artifacts'. This is the primary attack vector and requires detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor VSCode extension directories (%USERPROFILE%\.vscode\extensions on Windows, ~/.vscode/extensions on Unix) for suspicious downloads, unsigned manifests, or metadata anomalies. Alert on extension installations from OpenVSX followed by process spawning or child execution outside the extension sandbox.

suggestion.title: Solana Blockchain Transaction C2 Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'C2 server addresses are encoded in the memo fields of blockchain transactions, creating an immutable, publicly accessible dead drop'. Requires detection of outbound Solana RPC queries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound HTTPS connections to Solana RPC endpoints (api.mainnet-beta.solana.com, api.rpcpool.com, etc.) from non-cryptocurrency-application processes, especially from VSCode or extension child processes. Flag repeated queries or patterns suggesting configuration data extraction from transaction memo fields.

suggestion.title: BitTorrent DHT Query for Configuration Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'GlasswormRAT queries the BitTorrent peer-to-peer network for configuration data stored against hardcoded public keys'. Non-torrent applications querying DHT infrastructure are anomalous.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for UDP traffic to BitTorrent DHT bootstrap nodes (port 6881-6889) from non-torrent processes, particularly VSCode, extension runners, or language servers. Detect repeated queries to identical DHT info-hashes or key patterns within short intervals.

suggestion.title: Google Calendar Event Title C2 Dead-Drop Access
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Glassworm uses Google Calendar event titles as dead-drop locations for Base64-encoded C2 paths'. Living-off-the-land C2 via legitimate Google services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Google Calendar API calls (calendar.google.com, googleapis.com/calendar endpoints) for access patterns from extension or developer-tool processes.
