suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Wallet Enumeration and Theft
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies extensions 'stole cryptocurrency wallets'—requires file system enumeration of wallet storage (.ethereum, .solana, browser extension storage) and credential access patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes spawned by IDE extensions opening wallet files in standard cryptocurrency storage paths. Correlate file reads with Base64 encoding/compression operations and subsequent C2 beacon.

suggestion.title: Solana Blockchain-based C2 Polling and Address Extraction
suggestion.rationale: Article explains 'C2 server addresses are encoded in the memo fields of blockchain transactions'—process must query Solana RPC, decode Base64 memo fields, then connect to extracted IPs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes connecting to Solana RPC endpoints (api.mainnet-beta.solana.com), performing Base64 decode operations, then initiating connections to previously-unseen IPs. Correlate decoded values against known blockchain transactions.

suggestion.title: BitTorrent DHT C2 Configuration Retrieval
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'GlasswormRAT queries the BitTorrent peer-to-peer network for configuration data stored against hardcoded public keys, leveraging a global decentralized network.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect non-BitTorrent applications initiating DHT protocol queries (UDP to standard or non-standard DHT ports) with hardcoded infohash patterns, followed by connections to derived peer IPs.

suggestion.title: Google Calendar API for C2 Dead-Drop Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article details 'Glassworm uses Google Calendar event titles as dead-drop locations for Base64-encoded C2 paths.' Legitimate calendar access + Base64 decoding of event titles is abnormal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on authenticated Google Calendar API calls by non-browser/non-native-calendar processes, especially with simultaneous Base64 decoding of returned event title strings and subsequent C2-like network connections.

suggestion.title: Detect BadHost Vulnerability Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Attackers Can Exploit BadHost to Access Sensitive AI Agent Server Endpoints' — exploitation is the primary attack vector. Pipeline generated zero rules for detecting exploit attempts against known BadHost paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests containing BadHost exploit patterns, command injection payloads, or known CVE PoC signatures targeting /agent, /endpoint, or /api paths. Flag requests from external networks or unusual source IPs to these sensitive URIs.

suggestion.title: Detect Unauthorized Access to Protected AI Agent Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Impact described as access to 'Sensitive AI Agent Server Endpoints' — successful exploitation grants unauthorized endpoint access. Zero rules generated for detecting this post-exploitation state.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on 200/201 HTTP responses to protected /agent/*, /model/*, or /service/* endpoints originating from non-whitelisted IPs or lacking required authentication tokens. Correlate successful access with subsequent lateral movement indicators.

suggestion.title: Detect Agent Capability and Model Discovery Post-Access
suggestion.rationale: Once endpoint access is gained, attackers enumerate agent capabilities and available models. Standard post-compromise discovery behavior not detected by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for high-frequency sequential requests to agent metadata endpoints (/capabilities, /models, /endpoints, /health) within short time windows following successful authentication, especially from previously-unseen principals.

suggestion.title: Detect Password Spray Attacks Against Active Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'Password spraying attacks rely on exploiting that tendency'—the threat is named directly yet no detection UC was suggested for this common attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for multiple failed authentication attempts (Event 4625 / logon failure) against distinct user accounts originating from a single source IP within a short time window (5–10 minutes). Filter out expected service accounts and noise. Flag when failed-login count exceeds threshold (e.g., >5 unique users in 10 minutes).

suggestion.title: Detect Accounts Attempting to Use Compromised Passwords
suggestion.rationale: Article discusses breach-password protection: 'continuously checking passwords against a database of over 5.4 billion known breached credentials'—organizations need to detect when users attempt logon with credentials flagged in breach databases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful logon events (Event 4624) with identity data enriched against known-breach password lists. Flag accounts that successfully authenticate after their credentials appeared in a breach database, especially if they had not previously changed that password.

suggestion.title: Detect Unauthorized Active Directory Password Policy Modifications
suggestion.rationale: Article discusses policy changes ('tying expiration periods to password length'); adversaries often modify AD password policies to persist, evade, or lower security. Pipeline should have flagged defense-evasion scenarios.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Directory Service event logs (Event 5136 Object Modified, 5137 DirectoryService Object Created) for unauthorized changes to password policy GPOs or default domain policy password settings. Alert on modifications to MinPasswordLength, MaxPasswordAge, ComplexityEnabled, or PasswordHistoryCount from non-approved admin accounts.

suggestion.title: Detect Suspicious Self-Service Password Reset Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends self-service resets with MFA: 'verifying identity through MFA or other authentication methods.' Attackers often abuse password reset flows to gain account access; absence of detection use case is a gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor password reset request logs for multiple failed reset attempts against the same account (credential stuffing), resets from geographically impossible locations within seconds, or repeated resets outside business hours. Flag when MFA bypass or invalid token submission is logged.

suggestion.title: Detect Password Reuse Across Enterprise Systems
suggestion.rationale: Article states users 'are likely to repeat it across other systems simply because remembering dozens of credentials isn't realistic'—credential reuse is a stated threat, yet no detection for reused passwords was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate authentication events across different systems (AD, email, VPN, web apps) with the same username. Detect when the same account authenticates in rapid succession across multiple services with identical or similar credential patterns, indicating reused passwords that could indicate compromised credentials are in use.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated cPanel API Exploitation - Redis Parameter
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'cpanel_jsonapi_func=redisAble' parameter allowing 'remote attackers with no privileges' to trigger the vulnerability. Direct attack vector requiring no authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor cPanel web logs for HTTP requests containing 'cpanel_jsonapi_func=redisAble', especially from external IPs or sources without prior authentication context. Successful responses (HTTP 200) from unauthenticated sources indicate exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Execution from Web Service Context
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation enables 'remote attackers with no privileges to execute arbitrary scripts with root privileges'—a critical privilege boundary violation from unprivileged web context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process creation with UID 0 (root) spawned from cPanel web service processes running under unprivileged UIDs. Flag arbitrary script execution (bash, perl, python) inconsistent with routine cPanel operations.

suggestion.title: Detection via Provided cPanel Log Artifacts
suggestion.rationale: Article provides exploitation detection command: 'grep -rE "cpanel_jsonapi_func=redisAble" /var/cpanel/logs /usr/local/cpanel/logs/'—direct log signature for attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse /var/cpanel/logs and /usr/local/cpanel/logs for entries containing 'cpanel_jsonapi_func=redisAble'. Correlate source IPs against whitelist and alert on external/unauthenticated sources. Implement the recommended investigation step: block invalid IPs and examine system logs for actions by detected IPs.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Log Examination and Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'examine the system logs for any actions taken by the detected IPs', indicating attackers access and review cPanel logs post-compromise to cover tracks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected file access (read/write/delete) to /var/cpanel/logs or /usr/local/cpanel/logs from cPanel processes or web workers outside normal administrative workflows. Monitor for log rotation anomalies or file size reductions indicating tampering.

suggestion.title: Version Fingerprinting of Vulnerable cPanel Plugin
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability affects 'user-end plugin versions between v2.3 and v2.4.4'. Attackers must enumerate version before exploitation; banner grabbing and version probes are prerequisite reconnaissance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect reconnaissance: banner grabbing attempts, requests to cPanel diagnostic endpoints, or version-disclosure probes. Correlate version detection attempts with subsequent cpanel_jsonapi_func exploitation attempts within narrow time windows (< 1 hour).

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised cPanel Root Context
suggestion.rationale: Root privilege execution grants attacker complete host control. Subsequent lateral movement to customer databases, other internal systems, or data exfiltration is expected post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After detecting CVE-2026-48172 exploitation, monitor cPanel server for unexpected outbound SSH, RDP, or database connections from root context. Alert on mass file transfers, credential dumping tools, or reconnaissance commands executed with elevated privileges.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Version Published to Registry
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'malicious versions of the product...published to the npm registry'—need detection of unexpected package metadata changes, version jumps, or registry anomalies under the TanStack identity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm registry for CVE-2026-45321-related TanStack package versions; flag versions with unexpected checksums, unusual metadata changes, or rapid re-publishing. Cross-reference against known good versions in version manifests.

suggestion.title: Credential-Stealing Malware Process Behavior Post-Install
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'credential-stealing malware' delivered via the package—execution phase must show registry/credential-store access anomalies after npm install.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process spawned from node.js or npm child processes attempting to access HKLM\SAM, HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run, or credential manager APIs within 60s of npm install of CVE-2026-45321 package.

suggestion.title: Trusted npm Account Identity Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article notes malware 'published under a trusted identity'—indicates account compromise or impersonation; detection should flag atypical publishing activity from known vendor accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag npm publish events from TanStack canonical accounts with unusual geographic origin, IP, timestamp, or velocity; correlate with GitHub Actions logs for unexpected CI runs publishing to registry.

suggestion.title: npm Package Dependency Resolver Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Detection of the initial delivery vector—organizations installing CVE-2026-45321 will see unusual package resolution or version lock-file mismatches.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when npm or yarn resolves TanStack package to versions matching CVE-2026-45321 fingerprint; validate against package-lock.json or yarn.lock integrity and compare checksum against npmjs.com metadata.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Stolen Credentials from npm Malware
suggestion.rationale: Once credentials are stolen (article: 'credential-stealing malware'), expect follow-on lateral movement or persistence using harvested credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate credential theft signals (registry/API access) with downstream authentication anomalies: failed logins with harvested passwords, unexpected RDP/WinRM sessions, or service account usage spikes within 5min–2hr of malware execution window.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48027 Vulnerability Scan Match
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2026-48027 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and sets Federal due date 2026-06-10. This is the canonical first detection vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for Nx Console installations matching CVE-2026-48027. Prioritize hosts updated between publication date and Federal due date. Cross-reference with asset patch-compliance metrics.

suggestion.title: Malicious Nx Console Supply Chain Detection
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector: 'a malicious version of Nx Console to be published.' This is T1195 supply-chain compromise, not just public-facing app exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Nx Console extension installation/updates. Flag installations from untrusted sources, versions with mismatched hashes, or rapid version changes. Correlate install timestamps against malicious version release window.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting from Multiple Sources
suggestion.rationale: Article states payload 'harvested credentials from multiple sources on disk and in memory' — direct credential access attack is primary attacker objective.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes spawned from Nx Console context accessing browser credential stores, OS vaults, SSH keys, or cached authentication tokens in sequence. Short time-to-complete and high-entropy access pattern indicate automated harvesting.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated Payload Retrieval and Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'fetched an obfuscated payload' — network retrieval and execution of obfuscated code are distinct kill-chain steps requiring detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Nx Console for unexpected network connections retrieving packed/obfuscated binaries or scripts. Correlate with child process execution, especially powershell, cmd, or bash spawned with suspicious argument patterns.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Child Processes from Nx Console
suggestion.rationale: Malicious extension executes fetched payload as child process. Article does not name process names, but behavioral execution context is detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned from Nx Console executable or installation directory with elevated privileges, obfuscated command lines, or script-interpreter invocations (cmd, powershell, bash, python).

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Credential Use Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: After credentials harvested, attacker likely uses them for lateral movement or persistence. Article establishes credential theft as primary payload objective.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate credential-harvesting timeline (detected above) with subsequent authentication anomalies: logins from new geolocations, impossible travel, unusual service principal activity, or RDP/SSH connections using harvested secrets.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Asset Hunt: Daemon Tools Lite Installations
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'Daemon Tools Lite' as the vulnerable product with 'Federal patch due: 2026-05-30'—enterprises must enumerate all instances before remediation deadline. Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all Daemon Tools Lite installations across endpoints and filter for unpatched/vulnerable versions. Correlate software inventory against CVE-2026-8398 patch status to surface high-risk assets requiring urgent remediation before federal deadline.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-8398 Patch Remediation Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Federal 2026-05-30 due date creates temporal urgency and audit/compliance liability. Article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer'—must track remediation progress and flag missed deadlines.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track CVE-2026-8398 status across fleet pre- and post-remediation. Alert on hosts showing 'vulnerable' status after patch deployment attempts. Flag any unpatched instances at deadline threshold (2026-05-29 EOD) for escalation.

suggestion.title: Continuous High-Frequency API Probing from Single Source
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Autonomous attackers are already probing application surfaces continuously at machine speed, on a schedule defenders can't keep up with.' Defenders need to detect this baseline anomaly behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sustained high-rate API requests from single source IP targeting multiple endpoints or object IDs within short time window. Baseline normal API request patterns per app, alert on >3σ deviation in request frequency or endpoint diversity per source.

suggestion.title: BOLA/IDOR Exploitation — Unauthorized Cross-User/Cross-Tenant Data Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes: 'BOLA or IDOR, cross-tenant data leakage' and notes 'User A should not be able to read user B's invoice' — this is a key exploitation pattern requiring detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag API requests where authenticated user attempts to access resources scoped to a different user ID, tenant ID, or account context. Track authorization check failures followed by successful data returns. Correlate request patterns showing systematic ID/tenant enumeration.

suggestion.title: API Object Enumeration — Sequential Identifier Probing
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'structural reasoning about how API objects relate to identities' and 'probe, observe, reason, escalate, validate' — attackers enumerate valid object/user relationships through iteration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequences of API requests with rapidly incrementing or systematically-varied user IDs, tenant IDs, or resource identifiers from single source. Flag when >20 sequential numeric IDs are requested in <5 minute window with >80% 404/403 response ratio (indicating enumeration rather than legitimate access).

suggestion.title: Chained Exploitation Pattern — Sequential Vulnerability Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'chained vulnerabilities, where a couple of mediums and highs combine into a critical exploit path' — defenders should correlate successive exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate multiple failed authorization probes, auth bypass attempts, or injection payloads from same source in sequence within 10-minute window. Flag when pattern transitions from reconnaissance (enumeration, info-gathering) to exploitation (payload injection, privilege escalation attempts) without expected session reset.

suggestion.title: Authentication Bypass Attempt — Failed Auth Followed by Successful Access
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 'authentication bypasses' as context-dependent vulnerabilities requiring detection. Authentication bypass patterns precede unauthorized data access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect temporal proximity between failed authentication attempts and subsequent successful API calls using same or forged credentials. Flag when failed login is immediately followed (within 1 minute) by successful authenticated API call with same user agent/source IP but different auth token or header manipulation indicators.

suggestion.title: Cross-Tenant Data Leakage Access Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'cross-tenant data leakage' as a key vulnerability. Defenders need behavioral detection for multi-tenant boundary violations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In multi-tenant applications, detect users accessing API resources or data objects belonging to different tenant contexts. Flag requests where tenant_id in request path/params differs from authenticated user's tenant_id. Correlate with data egress patterns (large response payloads, bulk export API calls).

suggestion.title: Phishing emails impersonating IT support targeting law firms
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'SRG actors send phishing emails to urge employees to call the SRG actor posing as IT support' and 'register domains to impersonate IT helpdesk or support portals for major U.S. law firms.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag inbound emails from newly registered or typosquatted IT support domain variants sent to law firm/legal org employees. Correlate with whois registration age <30 days and typosquat patterns (e.g., 'it-helpdesk-portal.local' vs 'ithelpdesk-portal.local'). High confidence if followed by credential-phishing or callback instructions.

suggestion.title: Remote desktop session access following IT support impersonation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'SRG actor directs the employee to grant access to a remote desktop session' after phishing or phone contact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect RDP/remote access tool initiations (mstsc.exe, TeamViewer, AnyDesk, etc.) by users who were recently targeted by phishing (matching email sender domain from 24h prior). Escalate if session originates from external IP and user has no history of remote work.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized USB/external drive connections on corporate systems
suggestion.rationale: Article warns of 'unauthorized installation of external hard drives or USB drives on company computers' as attack vector when in-person access is gained: 'malicious actors can steal data by connecting USB drives or external hard drives to the victim's computer.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for USB device connections followed by large-volume file access/copying to removable media within 10 minutes. Alert especially on: (1) devices connected outside business hours, (2) connections on systems with prior remote access sessions, (3) bulk transfers of sensitive file types (*.docx, *.pdf, *.xlsx from /Legal, /Financials shares).

suggestion.title: Callback phishing and phone-based social engineering targeting employees
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'SRG actors either directly call or send phishing emails to urge employees to call the SRG actor posing as IT support' and references 'callback phishing' campaigns from May 2025 FBI notification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate inbound phishing emails mentioning 'IT support callback required' with phone logs showing calls to law firm employees in the same 2-hour window. Flag campaigns where phishing email domain + caller ID both impersonate IT. Review voicemail transcripts for remote access requests.

suggestion.title: Data exfiltration via remote access tools or removable media post-compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article notes SRG 'exfiltrate data, usually through legitimate remote access tools or by sending an individual in-person to the victim company's location' and threats to 'sell or post it on their leak site.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag bulk data transfers via remote access tools (TeamViewer, AnyDesk uploads >500MB) or simultaneous file reads from sensitive directories with USB device connection. Combine with user activity anomalies: rare remote tool execution, off-hours activity, legal/financial file access.

suggestion.title: Physical presence of unauthorized individuals claiming IT support
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly flags as indicator: 'the presence of unidentified or unauthorized individuals claiming to be IT support and attempting to access computers' when 'SRG sends a threat actor to the victim's location.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference physical security badge logs with IT department roster. Alert on badge entries from unregistered/external users who claim IT affiliation. Escalate if coincident with failed VPN access attempts, phishing campaigns, or after-hours facility access. Coordinate with security team on badge verification.

suggestion.title: Phishing Domain Bulk Registration Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes '300+ fake domains' — clear infrastructure setup signal. No detection for coordinated domain registration clusters.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify 50+ domains sharing registrar, nameserver, or IP space registered within 48-72 hour windows. Cross-reference against phishing keyword patterns (FIFA, World, Cup, tickets, login, official).

suggestion.title: Typosquatted Domain Click Detection
suggestion.rationale: Campaign targets fans with fake domains — implicit typosquatting of legitimate sports properties. No behavioral detection for user navigation to lookalike domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on clicks to domains with Levenshtein distance ≤2 from known FIFA/sports sites, combined with recent registration (<30 days) and absence of security indicators (HSTS, valid SSL chain, brand trust seals).

suggestion.title: Phishing Email with Malicious Domain Link
suggestion.rationale: Phishing campaign described as targeting fans — implication of email-based delivery. Pipeline has no email IOC extraction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails with URLs pointing to domains <30 days old, unregistered/suspicious registrars, or matching FIFA/sports keywords. Flag messages failing DMARC/SPF alignment.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting Form on Phishing Domain
suggestion.rationale: Fake domains imply landing pages collecting credentials. Article context missing from extraction, but phishing infrastructure strongly suggests credential collection phase (T1589.002).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST to phishing domain IPs for credential-like parameters (password, email, account, token, pin). Correlate source IPs against VPN/proxy services and geographic anomalies.

suggestion.title: DNS Query Spike to Newly-Registered Domains
suggestion.rationale: 300+ domains suggests bulk infrastructure testing and user traffic. No pattern for anomalous DNS query volume to low-reputation/young domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect single hosts or user cohorts generating >10 DNS queries to distinct domains all registered <14 days prior within 5-minute window. Baseline against legitimate sports fan behavior during World Cup events.

suggestion.title: Yamcs algorithm modification with embedded Java compilation patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'dynamically compiles and evaluates user-controlled algorithm text' and 'ChangeMissionDatabase privilege.' Missing detection for suspicious Java code (Runtime.getRuntime, ProcessBuilder, reflection APIs) in algorithm API payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect HTTP PATCH/POST payloads to /api/mdb/*/algorithms/* endpoints for keywords Runtime, ProcessBuilder, getRuntime, Method.invoke, Class.forName, or ObjectInputStream. Spike in requests with Java source code in body during off-hours or from non-admin accounts.

suggestion.title: Yamcs privilege escalation to ChangeMissionDatabase role
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly requires 'authenticated user with the ChangeMissionDatabase privilege.' No hunt for privilege grants or role assumption detected. This is a critical prerequisite.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Yamcs API logs (or auth system logs if integrated) for role grants, policy attachments, or privilege escalations to ChangeMissionDatabase. Correlate with subsequent algorithm modifications.

suggestion.title: Yamcs algorithm configuration file tampering
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'algorithm text' stored in configuration. Detecting modifications to algorithm definition files (e.g., MDB config files, YAML, XML) could catch disk-side exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor creation or modification of files matching Yamcs MDB paths (typically under /etc/yamcs/ or similar) or algorithm definition files (.algo, .mdb extensions) for unexpected writes by non-admin users or system services spawning editors.

suggestion.title: Yamcs server JVM log collection for Janino compilation errors
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions Janino expression engine. Compilation failures or exceptions in JVM logs (catalina.out, Yamcs logs) would indicate exploitation attempts or failed payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search Yamcs JVM/application logs for 'Janino', 'CompileException', 'SyntaxError' in algorithm compilation context, or unusually high exception rates during algorithm evaluation. Baseline normal compilation failures and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated or low-privilege access to Yamcs algorithm API endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'authenticated user,' implying baseline should be restricted. Missing detection for API calls to algorithm endpoints from unexpected source IPs, users, or auth contexts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of legitimate Yamcs admin accounts and networks accessing /api/mdb/*/algorithms/* endpoints. Alert on requests from new/unexpected sources, service accounts, or anonymous sessions.

suggestion.title: Janino expression engine abuse via API introspection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'user-controlled algorithm text' compiled dynamically. Janino allows reflection; missing hunt for attempts to invoke reflection, bytecode manipulation, or system-level APIs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search HTTP request bodies to algorithm endpoints for keywords: 'invoke', 'reflect', 'getMethod', 'getDeclaredMethod', 'newInstance', 'defineClass', 'BytecodeProvider'. Correlate with subsequent child process spawning.

suggestion.title: LiquidJS Renderer Property-Access Gadget Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article payload `{%assign r=1|valueOf%}{{r|inspect}}` followed by `r.context.scopes`, `r.liquid.parser`, `r.liquid.options.fs` shows attacker probing renderer object graph. This is the gadget-chain setup before RCE. Detection should trigger on suspicious property-access patterns in template AST or filter evaluation logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: LiquidJS renders template with filter chain accessing internal objects (context, parser, options). Monitor template AST for valueOf, constructor, prototype, or multi-level property access on render-context objects. Flag templates containing 'r.liquid.' or 'r.context.' property traversal.

suggestion.title: Prototype Pollution via __proto__ Assignment in LiquidJS Templates
suggestion.rationale: Payload includes `assign __proto__` which is prototype-pollution precondition. Article text confirms '__proto__' and 'constructor' are gadget-chain components ('assign __proto__'). Direct detection of __proto__ assignment in template filters.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inbound HTTP requests containing template syntax with __proto__, constructor, or prototype keywords. Search for: 'assign __proto__', '__proto__:', 'constructor.prototype', escaped variants ('%5F%5F', '%70%72%6F%74%6F'). High precision; low FP.

suggestion.title: Node Module Import Chaining from LiquidJS Context
suggestion.rationale: Article shows `getBuiltinModule` and `child_process` as post-gadget targets. Attacker chains prototype-pollution → module loader access → child_process spawn. Detection focuses on Node.js require/import of dangerous modules from web-context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Node.exe or web process (node, w3wp) calls require('child_process') or similar module-load followed by execSync/spawn within same process lifetime. Correlate module-load timing with inbound HTTP request timestamps to establish causality.

suggestion.title: Suspicious /etc/passwd or System-Config Access via Web Application
suggestion.rationale: Article use-case UC_10_1 detects /etc/passwd modification but is wrongly phased. Correct detection: any filesystem access to sensitive OS files (/etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, /etc/sudoers, /root/.ssh) by Node.js or IIS process following LiquidJS SSTI indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: File open/read events for /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, /root/.ssh or Windows equivalents (SAM, SECURITY hive) initiated by node.exe, w3wp.exe or iisexpress.exe. Correlate timing with LiquidJS HTTP requests. Exclude legitimate package-scan operations.

suggestion.title: LiquidJS Template with Circular Reference Inspection
suggestion.rationale: Attack entry-point: `{%assign r=1|valueOf%}{{r|inspect}}` reveals circular references in rendering context. An attacker first probes renderer structure to enumerate gadgets. Detection: Templates containing `valueOf` filter or `inspect` on simple assignments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Template syntax containing 'valueOf' filter or 'inspect' function on single-token assignments (e.g., {%assign X=1|valueOf%}). Low severity alone but high precision for reconnaissance phase; correlate with subsequent payloads for full attack chain.

suggestion.title: Reverse Shell or Outbound Connection from Node.js Process Post-LiquidJS RCE
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes RCE via template injection and child-process spawning, but missing detection for post-exploitation behavior: attacker likely establishes reverse shell or C2 callback. Detection should catch outbound connections from spawned shell process with Node parent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Outbound network connection initiated by cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, or sh with parent process node.exe or w3wp.exe within seconds of process creation. Flag connections to non-standard ports or private IP ranges from web-tier servers.

suggestion.title: Yamcs guest/default user accessing ChangeMissionDatabase API
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'In Yamcs's default configuration (no `security.yaml`), the built-in `guest` user…' This indicates default users have dangerous privilege. UC should detect first-time or anomalous guest-user API calls to MdbOverrideApi, or privilege escalation from guest to admin roles.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests from guest or anonymous users to /api/mdb-overrides/* endpoints, or sudden elevation of guest-user role from read-only to ChangeMissionDatabase. Baseline: guest users should rarely touch API endpoints; any access is suspicious.

suggestion.title: Yamcs algorithm override enumeration / failed-then-successful pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article describes user-supplied algorithm evaluation in MdbOverrideApi. Attackers likely enumerate or test payloads before deploying RCE. UC should detect: multiple PATCH requests to /api/mdb-overrides/*/algorithms/* in short window, with varying request bodies or response codes (failures followed by success).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect 3+ PATCH requests to /api/mdb-overrides/*/algorithms/* from same source within 60 seconds, or pattern of HTTP 400/500 responses followed by 200 OK from same user. This indicates payload testing or algorithm probing.

suggestion.title: Nashorn alternative RCE patterns (indirect class loading, compat mode)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies Nashorn ScriptEngine without ClassFilter, enabling Java.type exploitation. But Nashorn has alternate RCE vectors: load('nashorn:mozilla_compat'), importPackage(java.lang), indirect Class.forName. UC_2_2 catches direct Java.type but misses obfuscation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PATCH/POST requests to /api/mdb-overrides/*/algorithms/* containing: load('nashorn:mozilla_compat'), importPackage(java.), Class.forName, or var statements assigning Java.type results. Flag as high-confidence if paired with shell-spawning in UC_2_3.

suggestion.title: Post-RCE credential/config access from Yamcs process
suggestion.rationale: Article describes RCE on 'Yamcs server'. After shell execution (UC_2_3), attacker will exfiltrate credentials, SSH keys, security.yaml, or database configs. UC should correlate Java process with file access to sensitive paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Java process (parent=Yamcs, identified by command-line args 'yamcs' or 'org.yamcs') reading files: ~/.ssh/*, security.yaml, yamcs.properties, *.key, *.pem, or database config paths within 30 seconds of shell spawning.

suggestion.title: Lateral movement from compromised Yamcs server
suggestion.rationale: Yamcs is satellite/telemetry control software, implying integration with larger infrastructure. Post-RCE, attacker will pivot to adjacent systems. UC should detect outbound scanning, credential-stuffing, or remote-access attempts from Yamcs host.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound SSH, RDP, WinRM, or HTTP scanning initiated from Yamcs server IP to internal network ranges post-compromise. Correlate timing with successful exploitation (UC_2_2 + UC_2_3).

suggestion.title: Malicious algorithm persistence / mission-database backdoor
suggestion.rationale: Article describes algorithm override capability. Attacker may create persistent backdoor by installing a benign-looking algorithm that executes RCE payload on schedule or trigger. UC should detect algorithm updates with embedded scheduled execution or conditional RCE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PATCH requests to /api/mdb-overrides/*/algorithms/* containing payload with scheduled execution patterns (setInterval, Timer, cron-like scheduling in Nashorn) or event-triggered execution (onLoad, onTrigger). Flag if algorithm name is obfuscated or generic ('system_check', 'health_monitor').

suggestion.title: Yamcs MDB algorithm PATCH with embedded Jython java.lang.Runtime payload
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'dynamically compiles and evaluates user-controlled algorithm text using Jython' via PATCH to algorithm endpoints. Hunts explicitly search for java.lang.Runtime, getRuntime, Runtime.getRuntime in HTTP request bodies to /api/mdb/*/realtime/algorithms/*.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: PATCH requests to /api/mdb/*/realtime/algorithms/* containing Jython/Java runtime method calls (java.lang.Runtime, getRuntime, Runtime.getRuntime, exec) indicate algorithm code injection. Correlate with authenticated sessions bearing ChangeMissionDatabase privilege.

suggestion.title: Yamcs JVM spawns shell or network utility after code injection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'authenticated user... can exploit this by overriding the algorithm.' Post-exploitation hunt targets bash, sh, curl, wget spawning from java/jython parent. Indicates successful RCE execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Shell processes (bash, sh, zsh) spawned by java or jython parent, especially with yamcs/algorithm keywords in process tree. High confidence indicator of CVE exploitation success.

suggestion.title: Yamcs Java process beacons to OAST/webhook C2 domain
suggestion.rationale: Article hunt describes post-RCE command exfiltration: Java process connecting to webhook.site, interact.sh, oast.fun, ngrok.io, burpcollaborator.net, trycloudflare.com indicates reverse shell or data exfil.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: java.exe or curl/wget child processes connecting to known OAST infrastructure (webhook.site, interact.sh, interactsh, oast.fun, oast.live, burpcollaborator.net, ngrok, beeceptor, pipedream, requestcatcher).

suggestion.title: PsExec or WMIC lateral movement from Yamcs host
suggestion.rationale: Article includes hunt for psexec.exe, paexec.exe, wmic.exe /node: patterns as post-RCE lateral movement. Indicates attacker expanding footprint after gaining shell access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Execution of psexec.exe, psexesvc.exe, paexec.exe, or wmic.exe with /node: parameter on systems accessible from Yamcs host or originating from Yamcs network segment.

suggestion.title: Remote-access or RMM tool installation by non-service account
suggestion.rationale: Article hunt specifically targets AnyDesk, TeamViewer, ScreenConnect, Splashtop, RustDesk, Kaseya installation. Indicates post-RCE persistence mechanism for 'hands-on-keyboard' attacker access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Installation or execution of commercial RMM software by human user accounts (not service/system accounts) on systems where Yamcs is running or recently compromised.

suggestion.title: simulator.py process or file modification — Yamcs-specific IOC
suggestion.rationale: Article behavioural hunt specifically targets simulator.py file creation/modification and process execution. This appears to be Yamcs component or exploitation artifact not covered by generic hunts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Execution of simulator.py or file create/modify events involving simulator.py, particularly when parent process is java/jython or when file resides in yamcs-related directory paths.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Docker Registry Access - Gitea
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states vulnerability 'exposes private container images without authentication'—core attack vector is requests to container registry endpoints missing Authorization headers. Pipeline generated no detection for this.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Gitea Docker API endpoints (/v2/*) and image manifest paths that lack Authorization headers or valid credentials. Alert on HTTP 200/206 responses to unauthenticated registry requests. Baseline authenticated vs. unauthenticated access patterns per endpoint.

suggestion.title: Bulk Container Image Layer Downloads
suggestion.rationale: Title describes exposure of private images; attackers exfiltrate full images by downloading multiple blobs/layers. No detection for abnormal download volume or layer enumeration patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequential blob/layer downloads (>100 requests in <10 minutes from single source) to same image repository. Flag pattern of GET requests to /v2/{repo}/blobs/sha256/* paths in rapid succession without successful push operations. Correlate with unauthenticated access.

suggestion.title: Private Repository Enumeration via Manifest Requests
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability exposes 'private' repositories specifically—attacker can enumerate and discover repos they should not access. No detection for enumeration phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HEAD/GET requests to Gitea manifest endpoints (/v2/{repo}/manifests/*) from single source without credentials. Alert on systematic testing of repo name patterns or 404→200 transitions indicating repo discovery. Flag /v2/_catalog enumeration without authentication.

suggestion.title: Authentication Bypass Exploitation Indicator
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability is auth bypass ('without authentication'); pipeline should flag exploitation attempt signatures for the specific Gitea CVE affecting authentication middleware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect requests matching known Gitea auth bypass payload patterns (e.g., malformed tokens, null auth, path traversal in auth checks). Flag successful container registry API access when authentication middleware is bypassed. Monitor for requests to protected endpoints with invalid/missing credentials returning success codes.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Gitea API Access Without Credentials
suggestion.rationale: In addition to Docker API, Gitea's native API (/api/v1/*) may expose repo/package endpoints. No detection for unauthenticated API enumeration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor requests to Gitea API endpoints (/api/v1/repos/*/packages, /api/v1/packages) lacking Bearer token or valid session cookie. Alert on successful 200 responses to package/artifact enumeration from unauthenticated sources. Establish baseline of API access patterns.

suggestion.title: Private Image Manifest Access Without Auth Token
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'private container images' are exposed—manifest requests for private images should require credentials. No rule detecting unauthorized manifest pulls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to /v2/{private-repo}/manifests/latest or /v2/{private-repo}/manifests/sha256:* endpoints that return 200 when Authorization header is absent or malformed. Cross-reference repo access control list to confirm repo is marked private.

suggestion.title: Malicious VS Code / OpenVSX Extension Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'initially targeted developers with malicious OpenVSX and Microsoft VS Code extensions that stole cryptocurrency wallets and developer credentials.' Pipeline missed the primary attack delivery mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for extension installations from untrusted or spoofed OpenVSX/VS Code Marketplace sources. Flag extensions with suspicious post-installation process spawning or file system access to credential stores. Correlate with known malicious extension names if available.

suggestion.title: Blockchain-Based C2 Communication (Solana Memo Fields)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Solana blockchain: C2 server addresses are encoded in the memo fields of blockchain transactions.' Pipeline missed this novel C2 channel entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound connections to Solana RPC endpoints or blockchain explorers from developer workstations. Flag processes making repeated blockchain queries or transactions with unusual payload sizes in transaction memo fields. Correlate with GlassWormRAT signatures if available.

suggestion.title: BitTorrent DHT Configuration Queries for C2
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'GlasswormRAT queries the BitTorrent peer-to-peer network for configuration data stored against hardcoded public keys.' No detection use case for this C2 fallback channel.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for BitTorrent DHT traffic (UDP port 6881-6889, 6969) and DHT get_peers queries from non-torrent processes. Alert on repeated DHT lookups using hardcoded keys. Correlate with known GlassWorm infrastructure keys if available.

suggestion.title: Google Calendar Abuse for C2 Dead-Dropping
suggestion.rationale: Article details 'Google Calendar event titles as dead-drop locations for Base64-encoded C2 paths.' This legitimate-service abuse vector was not captured.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious Google Calendar API calls from developer machines (calendar.create, calendar.update). Flag event titles containing Base64-encoded strings, high-entropy text, or known C2 path patterns. Detect reads of event details followed by outbound C2 connections.

suggestion.title: Dormant Extension Activation Post-Update
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'dormant extensions on OpenVSX that would activate the malicious component after an update.' Persistence mechanism not captured in use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for VS Code extension updates followed by unexpected process spawning or file system modifications. Flag extensions that remain dormant until an update triggers execution. Cross-reference extension version hashes against known malicious signatures.

suggestion.title: Beaconing to Post-Disruption Sinkhole IP
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly provides sinkhole IP: 'infected machines can no longer receive new instructions or payloads' and beacon to '164.92.88[.]210 operated by CrowdStrike.' Direct IOC with immediate remediation value.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any outbound connections to 164.92.88[.]210 from internal hosts. This is a strong indicator of past Glassworm compromise; prioritize for immediate remediation and credential reset.

suggestion.title: Installation of Known-Bad GlassWorm Package Versions
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'developer supply chain attack infrastructure'—supply chain attacks distribute malware via package managers; the takedown would yield compromised package names, versions, and hashes for detection at install-time.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on installation or execution of GlassWorm package variants from npm, PyPI, NuGet, or equivalent registries. Match package metadata (name, version, publisher sig) against known-bad IOC list derived from takedown indicators.

suggestion.title: C2 Beaconing to Disabled Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: 'Takedown disrupts infrastructure' implies identified C2 domains/IPs now associated with GlassWorm; detecting outbound connections to these serves as proof of infection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag DNS queries or network connections from developer workstations/build systems to known GlassWorm C2 domains/IPs from takedown IOC set. Include SSL/TLS certificate fingerprinting if available.

suggestion.title: Execution of GlassWorm Malware via File Hash
suggestion.rationale: Infrastructure takedown yields malware samples; file hashes should be extracted and deployed for immediate process-level detection on endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Match SHA-256/SHA-1 hashes of all process executables and loaded DLLs against GlassWorm malware hashes published by takedown authorities. Alert on any hash match regardless of filename or path obfuscation.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Code Injection Into Build Artifacts
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain malware persists by compromising source or compiled outputs; the article's 'developer infrastructure' focus implies detection of modified build products.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor build directories for unexpected file modifications, particularly unsigned or anomalously-signed binaries in package output. Alert on post-build-start creation of .dll, .exe, or manifests in package staging directories.

suggestion.title: Credential Access via Compromised Development Tools
suggestion.rationale: Developer tools (git, SSH, container registries) often store credentials; supply chain compromise may exfiltrate these for lateral movement or persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious access to .ssh, .netrc, .git/config, or credential manager stores from processes spawned by GlassWorm-infected packages. Monitor for credential enumeration command-line patterns (git config --list, etc.) from unexpected parents.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement to Downstream CI/CD or Package Signing Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Compromised development machines are pivot points; successful supply chain attacks spread via CI/CD systems or signing infrastructure to infect downstream packages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on network connections from infected developer machines to internal CI/CD systems, artifact repositories, or code-signing services. Flag inter-account authentication from developer machines to admin/service accounts in signing pipelines.

suggestion.title: Trojanized Utility ZIP Archive Download
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'archive includes the legitimate executable for the legitimate utility as well as a malicious DLL that is automatically loaded when launching the benign binary.' This compound-file attack pattern is a distinct detection opportunity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect downloads of ZIP archives from gleeze[.]com subdomains containing both known utilities (CrystalDiskInfo, HWMonitor, FurMark, PDFgear) and suspicious DLLs. Alert on archive extraction followed by immediate DLL injection into utility process.

suggestion.title: Process Hollowing into Microsoft-Signed Binaries
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'process hollowing into a legitimate .NET binary signed by Microsoft: InstallUtil.exe, RegAsm.exe, RegSvcs.exe, MSBuild.exe, AppLaunch.exe, AddInProcess.exe, aspnet_compiler.exe.' Clear T1055.012 execution pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious parent-child process relationships where those seven MS-signed binaries spawn without legitimate arguments or load unsigned DLLs from unusual paths. Correlate with SimpleRunPE.exe execution or unexpected memory allocation patterns.

suggestion.title: Defender Exclusion Path Addition via PowerShell
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'invokes PowerShell to add its path and process to the exclusion list in Microsoft Defender.' Explicit defense evasion technique T1562.001.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on PowerShell commands executing Add-MpPreference -ExclusionPath or -ExclusionProcess from non-admin context or outside standard IT operations. Correlate with unsigned executable creation in same session.

suggestion.title: GPU Cryptominer Module Download and Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'one of three mining modules is downloaded and executed. The supported mining programs are gminer, lolMiner, and SRBMiner-MULTI, all of them designed to use graphics processing units (GPUs).' Clear T1496.001 impact phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution or network callbacks from gminer, lolMiner, or SRBMiner-MULTI processes. Flag unexpected GPU-intensive process execution on systems without legitimate 3D rendering workloads. Monitor for outbound connections to mining pools.

suggestion.title: Anti-Analysis Environment Checks (VM/Debugger Evasion)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'malware checks the environment for virtual machines and a set of 40 process names corresponding to analysis tools. If any are identified, the malware terminates its execution.' Defensive behavior indicating T1622.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious process enumeration or registry queries probing for known analysis tools, debuggers, or VM artifacts (process names: wireshark, ollydbg, ida, vmware, virtualbox, qemu). Anomalous in production endpoints.

suggestion.title: SEO Poisoning + AI Chatbot Prompt Injection Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes dual vector: 'users are presented with malicious links boosted in search rankings through SEO poisoning' AND 'users querying AI chatbots for software download recommendations were presented with links to attacker-controlled domains within generated responses.' Infrastructure-side detection required.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for sustained DNS/proxy traffic to gleeze[.]com subdomains correlated with search queries for utility software (CrystalDiskInfo, HWMonitor, Display Driver Uninstaller, FurMark, K-Lite Codec Pack, PDFgear). Spike detection on AI chatbot referrer logs to attacker domains.

suggestion.title: Grandoreiro Banking Trojan Execution via Malicious Office Macro
suggestion.rationale: Banking trojans like Grandoreiro typically arrive as weaponized Office documents with macros; the article title indicates 'campaigns' targeting Windows users, implying delivery mechanism
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Office applications (Word, Excel) spawning child processes (powershell.exe, cmd.exe, cscript.exe) or suspicious downloads post-macro execution. Flag unusual scheduled tasks created within minutes of macro execution.

suggestion.title: BTMOB RAT Command-and-Control Communication Detection
suggestion.rationale: BTMOB is explicitly named as a RAT; RATs establish persistent C2 channels. The article targets both Windows and Android, indicating multi-platform C2 infrastructure
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify suspicious outbound connections to non-standard ports and domains registering near campaign start dates. Monitor for beaconing patterns (regular intervals, consistent payload sizes) and certificate anomalies from C2 endpoints.

suggestion.title: Grandoreiro Credential Theft and Banking Session Hijacking
suggestion.rationale: Grandoreiro is a known banking trojan; banking trojans harvest credentials, browser data, and session tokens. Article describes 'campaigns' implying targeted credential exfiltration
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag access to browser credential stores, LSASS memory reads via uncommon processes, and extraction of browser cached data/cookies. Monitor for unusual API calls from injected contexts targeting banking domains.

suggestion.title: Android RAT Persistence via Malicious APK Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly targets 'Android Users'; Android RATs persist via app installation and abuse of accessibility services or DeviceAdmin permissions
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for apps requesting dangerous permissions (CAMERA, CONTACTS, LOCATION) without business justification. Alert on accessibility service registrations from non-system apps, and APK installations from untrusted sources.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion: Grandoreiro Code Obfuscation and Anti-Analysis Detection
suggestion.rationale: Banking trojans employ layered obfuscation; article describes 'campaigns' suggesting active evasion against security tools
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process hollowing, memory-only execution, or unusual binary loading order. Flag suspicious use of reflective injection APIs and runtime decryption patterns indicative of obfuscated payloads.

suggestion.title: AI Chatbot Recommendation Leading to Executable Download
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states: 'Hackers Abuse AI Chatbot Recommendations to Push Malicious Software Download Links.' Pipeline extracted zero use cases despite this clear attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for user interactions with AI chatbot services (ChatGPT, Claude, etc.) followed within minutes by download of executable files (.exe, .msi, .dll, .ps1) from non-standard or newly-registered domains. Correlate conversation logs with unusual outbound downloads and file execution patterns.

suggestion.title: Anomalous File Download Recommendations from Chatbot Service IPs
suggestion.rationale: Attack involves abusing chatbot recommendation feature—infrastructure recommending files differs from typical human behavior. Pipeline ignored this behavioral anomaly angle.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag downloads initiated from traffic patterns consistent with AI service API calls (Cloud IP ranges: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, etc.) where the download payload is a known malware hash or sandbox-detonated executable. Baseline user download behavior and alert on statistically rare file types recommended via chatbot context.

suggestion.title: Chatbot Service Account Compromise Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article premise requires either compromised chatbot accounts or injected prompts—pipeline ignored the account/service compromise angle entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual API authentication patterns to AI chatbot services: non-standard user-agents, bulk prompt submissions, geographically impossible login sequences, or service account keys rotating without documented reason. Correlate with downstream malware distribution campaigns.

suggestion.title: Post-Download Command Execution from Chatbot-Recommended Binaries
suggestion.rationale: Article title implies execution phase (malicious software = post-download functionality), but pipeline produced zero post-exploitation detection coverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline typical executables downloaded by users via chatbot interactions. Alert on processes spawned by these downloads (especially PowerShell, cmd.exe, or unsigned DLLs loaded). Correlate with known malware families and persistence mechanisms (scheduled tasks, registry run keys, WMI event subscriptions).

suggestion.title: Malicious npm Package Installation with Wallet File Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states '22 versions of npm RAT with wallet theft.' No detection rule exists for post-installation wallet-targeting behavior. npm packages execute code immediately on import.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install commands and require() operations for packages with high version churn, recent creation dates, or names matching cryptocurrency/banking keywords. Correlate with file-system access to wallet directories (.metamask, .electrum, .bitcoin, .coinbase) within minutes of installation.

suggestion.title: Persistent Backdoor Installation via npm postinstall Scripts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'persistent backdoor.' npm packages can execute arbitrary code via postinstall hooks and module initialization. Pipeline surfaced no persistence detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect modifications to node_modules/.bin/ or ~/.npm-global that create reverse shells or background daemons. Flag postinstall scripts in package.json that execute native binaries, create cron jobs, or write to startup directories. Monitor for Node.js spawning persistent child processes with network callbacks.

suggestion.title: Wallet Seed Phrase and Private Key Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'wallet theft' capabilities. No detection for credential harvesting from local wallet stores or in-memory key extraction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file reads of wallet configuration files, seed phrase storage, or private key locations immediately after npm package import. Detect in-memory scanning by Node.js processes for wallet passphrases, API keys, or encryption keys. Flag base64-encoded or obfuscated credential strings in process memory or network packets.

suggestion.title: Remote Access Trojan Command-and-Control from npm Process
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'npm RAT' indicating remote access capability. No C2 communication patterns detected for Node.js-spawned malware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound network connections from Node.js processes to non-standard ports, suspicious FQDN patterns, or known C2 infrastructure. Detect repeated connection retries or beaconing intervals. Flag DNS queries for dynamically generated or suspicious domain names originating from npm module execution context.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Code Obfuscation and Evasion
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions '22 versions,' suggesting rapid iteration to evade detection. No detection for malware distribution patterns or code obfuscation in npm packages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm packages published with >5 distinct versions within 24 hours or with significant code divergence between versions. Flag packages containing base64-encoded payloads, eval() statements, or highly obfuscated JavaScript. Cross-reference package hashes against known malware databases.

suggestion.title: Abnormal Process Spawning and Code Execution from Node.js
suggestion.rationale: RAT and wallet-stealing functionality requires executing system commands. No detection for suspicious child process spawning or JavaScript eval patterns from npm modules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Node.js (node.exe, node) spawning unexpected child processes (bash, powershell, curl, wget, nc) immediately after npm package load. Detect eval(), Function(), or vm.runInNewContext() calls with untrusted input. Flag postinstall scripts executing network utilities or creating hidden files.

suggestion.title: Execution of Suspicious ChatGPT/Claude Installer Files
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Hackers Use Fake ChatGPT and Claude Installers' — execution of trojanized setup files is the direct delivery mechanism; should detect by filename patterns, signature absence, and spawned child processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution of ChatGPT, Claude, or OpenAI-branded installer executables from Downloads, Temp, or AppData with absent or suspicious code signatures. Correlate with immediate child process spawning (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, additional .exe to Temp) or unsigned DLL loading.

suggestion.title: DinDoor Backdoor Process Initialization and C2 Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'DinDoor Backdoor' as post-installation payload — detection requires monitoring for known DinDoor process signatures, registry persistence setup, and subsequent command-and-control callbacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect DinDoor activation via file hash matching of known samples, monitoring for characteristic command-line patterns (registry add for persistence, service installation), and subsequent HTTP(S) or DNS beaconing to known C2 infrastructure associated with DinDoor campaigns.

suggestion.title: Unsigned Executable Spawned from Installer Working Directory
suggestion.rationale: Fake installers will extract and execute malware payloads — legitimate ChatGPT/Claude vendors sign all executables; detection should flag unsigned binaries materialized or spawned from installer processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unsigned .exe or .dll files created in Temp, AppData, or ProgramFiles during or immediately after installer execution. Alert if parent process is a ChatGPT/Claude installer and child is unsigned or has mismatched publisher metadata.

suggestion.title: File Hash and Signature Anomalies in AI Assistant Installers
suggestion.rationale: Masquerading as legitimate tools; hash mismatches against vendor-published legitimate samples and signature spoofing distinguish malicious from legitimate installers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference ChatGPT/Claude installer file hashes against official vendor hashes and VirusTotal benign samples. Flag installers with: absent Authenticode signatures, signatures from unknown/spoofed publishers, or hashes matching known malware families.

suggestion.title: Installer-Initiated Registry Persistence Modifications
suggestion.rationale: DinDoor persistence requires registry key installation — legitimate application installers should not modify Run/RunOnce/Winlogon keys; unsigned or unexpected registry writes from installer process indicate backdoor setup.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when installer-spawned processes write to HKCU/HKLM Run, RunOnce, or startup-related registry keys. Legitimate installers write only installation-specific keys; persistence writes from ChatGPT/Claude installers are anomalous and should trigger investigation.

suggestion.title: Grandoreiro Malware Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'Grandoreiro Malware' as the threat vector. Pipeline should detect execution of known Grandoreiro process names, DLLs, or command-line patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Grandoreiro typically masquerades as benign processes or uses process injection into banking-related executables. Look for process creation with Grandoreiro-associated names, unsigned binaries, or child processes of Office applications followed by unusual network connections to known C2 ranges.

suggestion.title: Banking Credential Harvesting Activity
suggestion.rationale: Banking malware targets explicitly mentioned—'Portuguese Banks and Latin American Companies.' Grandoreiro is known for credential theft via keylogging and clipboard capture targeting banking sessions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for screen capture DLLs (e.g., GDI32, DirectX wrappers), clipboard access hooks, and keylogger persistence mechanisms (registry hives, scheduled tasks under user context). Correlate with browser window discovery queries targeting banking domains.

suggestion.title: C2 Beacon Detection for Banking RAT
suggestion.rationale: Article describes malware targeting banks without specifying distribution; banking RATs like Grandoreiro require persistent C2 communication for remote command execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Grandoreiro uses HTTP POST requests to hardcoded C2 servers with banking-related User-Agents or obfuscated payloads. Baseline expected traffic to financial institutions and flag anomalous outbound HTTPS/HTTP to non-financial ASNs from client machines, especially if preceded by credential access events.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Startup/Registry Modification
suggestion.rationale: Banking trojans require persistence for continuous monitoring and fraud. Article implies sustained compromise of target organizations—no mention of single-session attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on registry modifications to Run, RunOnce, or Startup folders by non-admin processes or system utilities (cmd.exe, powershell.exe) creating entries pointing to unusual directories (AppData, Temp, user profile paths). Correlate with unsigned binary execution in same directory.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email with Banking Malware Attachment
suggestion.rationale: No delivery mechanism explicitly stated in truncated article, but Portuguese banks and Latin American companies are typical spear-phish targets. Grandoreiro distribution predominantly email-based.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag emails with financial/banking lures targeting known financial sector domains. Look for .exe, .scr, .msi, .zip archives in attachments with banking theme subject lines (wire transfer confirmation, account update, compliance verification). Cross-reference recipients against finance/banking employee lists.

suggestion.title: Remote Access Tool Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: Grandoreiro is classified as a RAT (Remote Access Trojan) with explicit mention of targeting organizations, not individual users. RATactivity implies lateral movement inside compromised networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for anomalous RDP, SMB, or WinRM connections from infected banking workstation to internal file servers or admin tiers. Correlation: credential access events followed by lateral movement to high-value targets (treasury, wire approval systems) within same organization.

suggestion.title: Detect Persistence Mechanism Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states detection should focus on observing 'persistence mechanisms' in attack chains. No use case was generated despite this being a core attack component.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation of scheduled tasks, startup registry keys, run keys, or boot-start drivers. Correlate process execution with unusual parent processes creating these persistence mechanisms. Flag installations not attributed to known software deployment.

suggestion.title: Correlate Suspicious Network Infrastructure Across Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'correlate isolated indicators (IPs, domains, file hashes) against historical analysis data from thousands of organizations to identify campaign patterns.' Pipeline should have generated a use case for infrastructure-based campaign linking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on endpoint DNS queries and connections to IPs/domains that share WHOIS registration details, ASNs, SSL certificate history, or passive DNS relationships with known malicious infrastructure. Link related indicators through OSINT enrichment.

suggestion.title: Early Warning: Weak Signal Anomaly Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'weak signals look harmless until connected to broader attack patterns.' Pipeline missed opportunity to create detection around low-risk indicators that become significant in aggregate.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Accumulate low-severity alerts (unusual file types, suspicious scripts, external tool execution) within same endpoint within 4-hour window. Flag if three or more disparate weak signals on one host, indicating multi-stage compromise chain rather than isolated events.

suggestion.title: Detect Payload Delivery and Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions observing 'payload delivery' as part of attack chain analysis via sandbox, but pipeline generated no detection query.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag execution of suspicious scripts (PowerShell, Cmd, Bash, VBScript) spawned from Office documents, browsers, or email attachments. Monitor for process hollowing, DLL injection, or living-off-the-land binary abuse. Correlate with file download history.

suggestion.title: Malicious Package Installation: Codex Remote UI Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Legitimate-Looking Codex Remote UI'—a supply-chain attack. Core initial access vector is package distribution. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs or initial-access detections despite this being the article's primary mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package manager execution (npm, pip, yarn) for installation of 'Codex Remote UI' or known-malicious variants. Alert on package installs from non-standard registries, mismatched checksums, or versions flagged in supply-chain databases. Correlate with subsequent IDE process spawning.

suggestion.title: API Token/Credential Exfiltration from Development Environment
suggestion.rationale: Article core claim: malware 'steals AI tokens.' No detection generated for abnormal credential access from IDE/package processes. This is the attack's objective and primary killable moment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when IDE processes (VSCode, JetBrains, terminal) read .env, ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.ssh/config, or environment variables containing 'token', 'api', 'key', or 'secret' patterns. Escalate if followed by unusual outbound network activity or data encoding/compression.

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration via Unexpected Network Egress
suggestion.rationale: Stolen tokens must be transmitted to attacker C2. Article does not indicate what infrastructure receives tokens. No detection for suspicious network flows from development tools was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor IDE/terminal processes for outbound connections to non-organizational IPs. Flag payloads containing Base64/hex-encoded patterns consistent with API token formats. Correlate with prior credential file reads to establish exfiltration chain.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Subprocess Spawning During Package Install
suggestion.rationale: Malicious package executes payload via post-install hooks or IDE startup. No detection for subprocess execution within package-manager context was suggested. Standard supply-chain attack execution vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child process creation from npm/pip/package-manager with unexpected parent-child relationships. suggestion.title: Post-Install Script Obfuscation Detection

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect RDP logons (EventCode 4624, LogonType=10) from external/non-corporate IP addresses within 30 minutes of phishing email recipient activity. Alert on RDP sessions paired with unusual process creation (file copying, data staging tools) or session duration >2 hours for first-time login.

suggestion.title: USB/External Drive Insertion Followed by Bulk Data Copy
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'By going to the victim's location in person, the malicious actors can steal data by connecting USB drives or external hard drives to the victim's computer.' Collection phase via removable media exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for USB/external storage device connection events followed within 5 minutes by high-volume file copy operations (robocopy, xcopy, cp -r) targeting removable drives or unfamiliar mount points. Alert on bulk copy of files from restricted directories (C:\Users, program files, database locations).

suggestion.title: Unescorted Individual Claiming IT Access at Physical Location
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies indicator: 'presence of unidentified or unauthorized individuals claiming to be IT support and attempting to access computers.' Physical social engineering attack preventing remote-only detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-correlate badge/door access logs against IT ticket system to identify individuals accessing secure areas without corresponding service orders. Alert on discrepancies between claimed IT visit and logged tickets, especially for floor locations housing sensitive data or critical systems.

suggestion.title: Extortion Ransom Email with Data Leak Threat
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'SRG uses the stolen data to extort the victims by sending a ransom email that threatens to sell or post it on their leak site, and will also call the victims' employees.' Post-compromise extortion communication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound emails from external senders containing keywords 'ransom', 'leak', 'pay', 'deadline', 'public disclosure', 'site' paired with financial demands and threat language. Alert if multiple recipients within same organization receive similar messages within 24 hours.

suggestion.title: DNS/Web Queries to Typosquatted IT Portal Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'register domains to impersonate IT helpdesk or support portals for major U.S. law firms and financial services firms, using typosquatted patterns.' Infrastructure reconnaissance and phishing preparation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag DNS requests and HTTP traffic to domains with character substitutions matching known organizational IT support portals (e.g., 'supp0rt' vs 'support', 'helpdesk1' vs 'helpdesk'). Alert on newly registered domains (<14 days old) with these patterns, especially if WHOIS registrant is anonymous or foreign proxy.

suggestion.title: Bulk Lookalike Domain Registration - GHOST STADIUM Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article title states '300+ fake domains' targeting FIFA fans. Pipeline extracted zero domains. Bulk registration of typosquatted/homoglyph domains is the core attack infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor domain registration patterns for clusters of visually-similar domains registered within short time windows, particularly those mimicking legitimate sports/betting properties. Correlate against known GHOST STADIUM campaign indicators (domain registrant info, nameserver clustering, SSL cert issuer patterns).

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting via Phishing Form Submission
suggestion.rationale: Phishing campaigns targeting 'FIFA World Cup fans' implies credential capture via fake login/account pages on the 300+ domains. Pipeline missed credential_access phase entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP POST requests to suspicious domains with form field names matching FIFA/sports betting login patterns (username, password, email, phone). Correlate source IPs posting to multiple GHOST STADIUM domains within same session.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email Distribution - GHOST STADIUM Campaign
suggestion.rationale: Article title indicates phishing campaign; email is implied attack vector but zero email IOCs or detection logic generated. No coverage of T1566.002 (Phishing via Spearphishing Link).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Block/alert on emails with URLs resolving to GHOST STADIUM domains. Flag emails with FIFA/World Cup urgency language (urgent ticket purchase, account verification required, limited availability). Correlate with domain registration timestamps to catch early campaign waves.

suggestion.title: DNS Typosquatting Detection - Sports Betting/World Cup Properties
suggestion.rationale: 300+ domains implies heavy use of character-substitution and domain-typosquatting (e.g., 'fifa' → 'fífa', 'tickets' → 'tickts'). Pipeline did not identify T1583.001 as acquisition technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS queries for Levenshtein-distance similarities to known FIFA, World Cup, Ticketmaster, and betting site domains.
