suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'execute arbitrary code remotely as the Gogs server process user via pull requests' that trigger rebase. Git rebase should spawn bounded set of children (git objects, possibly gpg); spawning cmd/powershell/python/perl indicates exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor git-rebase or git-merge processes spawned by Gogs service account. Alert on any child process that is NOT git-related (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, python, perl, etc.) or unexpected binaries. Baseline expected child processes per Gogs version to reduce FP.

suggestion.title: Credential Dumping from Gogs Data Directories After RCE
suggestion.rationale: Article warns attackers can 'dump credentials (password hashes, API tokens, SSH keys, 2FA secrets)' and 'read every repository on the instance (including other users' private repos).' Post-exploitation file access to config, database, or SSH key directories is a clear impact signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After successful code execution on Gogs server, monitor for file reads/copies of: .ssh/ directories, credential config files, Gogs database files, and private repository contents. Flag bulk file enumeration or exfiltration of plaintext secrets from Gogs install directory.

suggestion.title: Pull Request with Malformed or Suspicious Branch Name Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires 'pull requests that use a malicious branch name to inject' the --exec flag. Branch names with unusual escaping, backticks, semicolons, or double-dash sequences are anomalous in typical Git workflows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect pull requests where source or target branch names contain injection-suspicious patterns: backticks, $(...), &&, ||, ;, --, =, or base64-encoded strings. Cross-reference with Gogs version to determine if instance is vulnerable (0.14.2, 0.15.0+dev).

suggestion.title: Gogs Instance Detection and Vulnerability Assessment
suggestion.rationale: Article cites ShadowServer tracking 2,400+ Gogs servers and Shodan finding 1,000+ IPs with Gogs fingerprint. Detection should identify all Gogs instances and flag versions 0.14.2 and 0.15.0+dev as vulnerable, particularly those with open registration enabled.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Gogs instances via HTTP headers, /api/v1/version endpoint, or distinctive URL patterns (/repo/create, /user/register). Cross-reference version against 0.14.2, 0.15.0+dev. Flag instances with DISABLE_REGISTRATION=false or MAX_CREATION_LIMIT=-1 in accessible config or inferred behavior.

suggestion.title: DLL Side-Loading via Legitimate Installer + Malicious Sibling
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes: 'The archive contained a legitimate executable, HLS Installer.874.exe, alongside a malicious DLL. Launching the EXE triggered a DLL side-loading mechanism.' This is a direct detection gap—no use case covers paired legitimate exe + suspicious adjacent DLL.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect archive extractions where a legitimate, signed executable (e.g., HLS Installer.exe) and an unsigned or suspicious DLL exist in the same directory, followed by the executable's launch. Monitor for discrepancies between DLL signer and EXE signer; legitimate installer DLLs typically match the publisher.

suggestion.title: Fake Browser/Player Plugin Update Lure to Archive Download
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'the player displayed a message saying the plugin version was outdated and asking to install an update to continue. Clicking the link downloaded a ZIP archive.' No use case covers this social-engineering pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for users on known pirated streaming domains (.ru, .top TLDs) receiving fake update dialogs, followed by suspicious archive downloads. Correlate browser/player process with unexpected Archive Manager or 7-Zip launches within 30 seconds.

suggestion.title: SilentCryptoMiner + RAT Hybrid Payload Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'the miner based on SilentCryptoMiner gained a RAT module' and 'The library contained the logic for deploying the miner and establishing persistence on the device.' No use case addresses hybrid miner+RAT or persistence establishment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect DLL module deployed by legitimate process establishing registry run keys, scheduled tasks, or WMI event subscriptions for miner execution. Look for XMRig or cryptominer process spawned hours/days after initial infection, paired with outbound C2 traffic to urush1bar4[.]online or similar.

suggestion.title: Multi-Part Archive Download from Evasion Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'the archive was downloaded in parts from the domain file[.]ipfs[.]us[.]69[.]mu' switching to 'urush1bar4[.]online.' No use case detects multi-part exfiltration or domain rotation patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for sequential HTTP requests to unusual/newly-registered domains (.online, .top, bulletproof hosters) downloading parts/chunks of archives over short timespan. Correlate with user presence on pirated media sites and follow with process execution of extracted executables.

suggestion.title: Process Injection into Legitimate Service via DLL Sideload
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'injecting the malicious module into a legitimate program process and executing code within its context.' No detection mapped for the injection mechanism itself.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect parent-child process relationships where a recently-extracted or temporary-directory executable (HLS Installer.exe) spawns and injects into a benign system process (svchost, explorer, winlogon). Look for unsigned DLL load events from suspicious paths immediately prior.

suggestion.title: Watchdog Agent Deployment and Scheduled Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions: 'Watchdog RAT agent' and 'DLL analysis... Watchdog' as a component. This suggests a monitoring/persistence component with no corresponding detection use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Windows Task Scheduler entries or registry run keys spawning unsigned executables from temp/appdata directories at regular intervals (watchdog pattern). Correlate with parent process being rundll32 or regsvcs—common sideload carriers.

suggestion.title: Go-compiled ransomware process execution with entropy anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically identifies malware as 'Go encryptor' — Go binaries have distinct entropy signatures and import patterns. Pipeline should detect Go.exe or go-compiled executables with encryption/syscall patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for uncommon process execution of Go-compiled binaries (identifiable by import tables or section names like .gopclntab) with subsequent access to sensitive file extensions or NTFS alternate data streams. Correlate with parent process and command-line arguments.

suggestion.title: Privilege escalation exploitation preceding encryption
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly discusses 'Elevation of privilege' as a keyword. Pipeline missed detection for UAC bypass, token impersonation, or service exploitation that precedes ransomware execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process creation with elevation flags (token manipulation, registry modification of privilege-related keys, or service binary replacement) followed within seconds by file encryption or network propagation attempts.

suggestion.title: Network-based self-propagation via SMB/lateral movement
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'self-propagating' and keywords include 'Lateral movement'. Pipeline should detect SMB enumeration, admin share access, or worm-like propagation payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process enumerating network resources (Net.exe, nbtstat, Get-ADComputer) or accessing remote shares, followed by lateral spawning of child processes and file writes to UNC paths. Look for repeating patterns indicating worm replication.

suggestion.title: File encryption activity with Windows Volume Shadow Copy destruction
suggestion.rationale: Ransomware impact phase mentioned as 'Extortion' — article discusses encryption as core mechanism. Pipeline should detect encryption syscalls, VSS deletion, and recovery file destruction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk file access followed by vssadmin/wmic calls to delete shadows, combined with file extensions being added to known-clean files in rapid succession across multiple directories. Correlate with process entropy and signing status.

suggestion.title: Ransomware-as-a-service (RaaS) command infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article keywords include 'Ransomware as a service'. Pipeline must detect C2 beaconing, decryption-key retrieval, or attacker command channels.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP/HTTPS POST requests to attacker-controlled domains with ransom negotiation or decryption-key endpoints. Look for TLS certificate anomalies, JA3 fingerprints of known RaaS families, or encrypted payloads with specific entropy profiles.

suggestion.title: Defense evasion via binary obfuscation and UAC bypass chains
suggestion.rationale: Human-operated ransomware (per keywords) typically employs layered evasion. Pipeline should detect code caves, API hooking, or legitimate-tool abuse (living-off-the-land).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Go binaries spawning PowerShell or cmd.exe with suspicious argument obfuscation, WMI process creation, or DLL loading from non-standard paths. Correlate with absence of standard event log entries (indication of log tampering).

suggestion.title: FortiClient EMS Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'threat actors exploit critical FortiClient EMS flaw' — this is the initial access vector and should have a dedicated UC to detect exploitation traffic/payloads before stealer deployment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiClient EMS endpoints for unexpected HTTP POST/PUT requests to known vulnerable endpoints, abnormal process spawning from FortiClient service accounts, or unsigned binary execution in FortiClient installation directory.

suggestion.title: Credential Stealer Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'credential stealer' deployment — need detection for stealer binary execution, likely spawned by or running under compromised FortiClient context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious process creation from FortiClient service/parent processes, especially unsigned binaries or scripts; monitor for credential access libraries (mimikatz, lsass access patterns) spawned in FortiClient service context.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting Activity
suggestion.rationale: Core payload is credential stealer — must detect credential access patterns such as LSASS access, SAM/registry reads, or password storage enumeration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for LSASS.exe access from child processes, registry queries to HKLM\Security\SAM or HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\RunMRU, or suspicious credential manager access.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Stolen Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Credential stealer typically exfiltrates credentials for follow-on lateral movement — should detect usage of harvested credentials across network segments within short timeframe.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate credential harvesting events with unexpected logon attempts using stolen credentials from different source IPs/devices, especially across segment boundaries in short time window.

suggestion.title: FortiClient EMS Service Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates exploitation of FortiClient EMS — legitimate service behavior should be baselined and deviations (unexpected child processes, network connections, file modifications) flagged.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of FortiClient EMS process tree and network behavior; alert on deviation such as unexpected child processes (not fortisslvpn/update utilities), outbound HTTPS to non-Fortinet IPs, or modifications to EMS config/plugin directories.

suggestion.title: Credential Stealer C2 Communication
suggestion.rationale: Credential stealer must exfiltrate harvested data — should detect outbound C2 communication patterns (DNS tunneling, HTTPS beacons, or custom protocols) from FortiClient service context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DNS queries to suspicious domains from FortiClient service account, outbound HTTPS connections to non-Fortinet infrastructure, or encoded/obfuscated DNS TXT record queries.

suggestion.title: Google Password Manager Vault Decryption with Captured PIN
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes PIN-based vault unlock: 'steals entire Google Password Manager Vault with one captured PIN' — this is the core attack mechanism and requires detection of vault decryption/unlock attempts with non-standard authentication factors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Google Password Manager client executing vault unlock/decryption operations outside normal user patterns. Monitor for GPM process spawning cryptographic operations or direct vault file access with authentication bypass indicators. Alert on PIN validation events that bypass expected MFA challenges.

suggestion.title: Bulk Credential Export from Google Password Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article states attack 'steals entire vault' — exfiltration of all stored credentials at once represents a distinct detection opportunity compared to single-password access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusually large data transfers from Google Password Manager client or Google Passwords API endpoints. Monitor for bulk credential sync/export operations (distinguish from routine periodic syncs). Alert when GPM exfiltrates credential count inconsistent with user's typical access patterns.

suggestion.title: PIN Interception/Capture Preceding Password Manager Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Attack depends on 'one captured PIN' — detection should include upstream PIN acquisition via keylogging, screen capture, or shoulder surfing, not just downstream vault access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect keylogging or screen capture processes running concurrently with password manager client active. Monitor for clipboard exfiltration of PIN-like numeric patterns. Alert on user input monitoring tools (screenshot, OCR, keystroke recording) spawned immediately before GPM client unlock attempts.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Google Password Manager Client Behavior Post-PIN Compromise
suggestion.rationale: After PIN capture, attacker gains unauthorized vault access — should trigger detections for GPM client performing actions inconsistent with legitimate user (export format, destination, timing, device context).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GPM client exporting/syncing credentials to non-standard destinations (different device, cloud storage, email). Monitor for credential access from unexpected geographic location or device not previously associated with user's GPM account. Alert on rapid sequential access to disparate service credentials post-unlock.

suggestion.title: MDM Agent Termination or Service Disablement
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly frames 'what MDM can't protect'—implies adversary must disable or bypass MDM controls as attack prerequisite
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on termination, uninstall, or configuration tampering of common MDM agents (Jamf, Intune, Workspace ONE, Kandji). Monitor for service disablement commands (sc stop, launchctl unload) targeting MDM daemons on developer machines.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Developer Environment
suggestion.rationale: Article scope implies attacker must escalate beyond MDM-enforced user restrictions to achieve compromise of dev environment
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sudo abuse, UAC bypass, or process injection originating from developer tools (Xcode, VS Code, Docker). Flag elevation requests from non-admin dev users, especially clustered around build or package-manager execution.

suggestion.title: Developer Credential Material Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Developer machines hold unencrypted or weakly-protected secrets (SSH keys, cloud API tokens, git credentials) that MDM lacks visibility into
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file access patterns targeting credential stores: ~/.ssh/, ~/.aws/, ~/.config/, .git/config, keychain queries. Monitor for mass export or copy of private keys/tokens to temp locations or cloud storage.

suggestion.title: Malicious Code Execution Blended with Build Artifacts
suggestion.rationale: MDM inspects endpoint state but cannot distinguish attacker-injected code in build pipelines from legitimate compilation, a core 'can't protect' gap
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious child processes spawned by package managers (npm, cargo, pip) or build tools (make, gradle). Flag downloads and execution of unsigned binaries in build directories. Monitor for network I/O from build processes to non-standard infrastructure.

suggestion.title: AI Chatbot Malicious Recommendation Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'AI Chatbot Recommendations Redirect Users to Cryptojacking Malware Sites' — this is a primary attack vector (poisoned chatbot responses) that warrants detection of suspicious URLs/domains injected into chatbot outputs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor AI chatbot response logs and user-interaction flows for embedded URLs pointing to known malicious domains. Correlate chatbot recommendation timestamps with user click-through events and downstream network connections to cryptojacking infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Cryptojacking Malware Site Redirect Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'Cryptojacking Malware Sites' as the redirect target. Pipeline must correlate redirect chains and landing-page signatures to identify browser-based or JavaScript-injected miners.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect redirect chains from chatbot domains to malware hosting infrastructure. Look for JavaScript mining libraries (CoinHive, Monero miners) in HTTP responses, CPU spikes during browser sessions, and memory patterns consistent with in-browser cryptominers.

suggestion.title: Resource Hijacking via Compromised Chatbot Output
suggestion.rationale: Article describes users being directed to 'cryptojacking malware sites' — this is T1496 impact. Detection should focus on abnormal resource consumption (CPU, memory) post-chatbot interaction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal CPU and memory usage during chatbot interactions. Flag sustained CPU elevation (>70% for >5 min) on browser processes following chatbot recommendations, especially from new/unsigned JavaScript sources.

suggestion.title: Malicious Domain/IP IOC Correlation with Chatbot Logs
suggestion.rationale: Article context implies multiple malware-hosting domains ('Cryptojacking Malware Sites' plural). Pipeline should have extracted domain IOCs and correlated them against user network telemetry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference chatbot responses against threat feeds (known cryptojacking C2 domains, malware hosting IPs). Alert on user clicks from chatbot outputs to domains flagged in URLhaus, PhishTank, or abuse.ch Cryptojacking tracker.

suggestion.title: Browser Process Persistence of Malware Loader
suggestion.rationale: Cryptojacking malware typically persists via browser cache, cookies, or injected browser extensions. Article context suggests persistence mechanisms post-initial redirect.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor browser plugin/extension directories and cache locations for unsigned miners. Detect suspicious browser startup arguments injecting remote JavaScript miners. Correlate with known cryptojacking signatures.

suggestion.title: Detect AD Password Spraying Attacks
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'Password spraying attacks rely on exploiting that tendency' toward weak passwords. No use case generated despite clear attack vector discussed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for multiple failed authentication attempts across distinct AD user accounts from single source IP within 10-minute window. Alert threshold: >5 failed logons to different principals, indicating password spray.

suggestion.title: Detect Compromised Password Creation in Active Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes blocking compromised passwords: 'continuously checking passwords against a database of over 5.4 billion known breached credentials.' No detection logic generated for breach-password matching.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag password change/creation events where the new password hash or plaintext-derived signature matches public breach databases (HaveIBeenPwned, Specops 5.4B list). Correlate with user identity and timestamp.

suggestion.title: Monitor Excessive Password Reset Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'Password resets are one of the most common causes of helpdesk tickets in AD environments'—attributed to strict policies causing user friction and workarounds. Abnormal reset rates may indicate frustration-driven weak passwords or account compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish per-user password reset baseline. Alert on users resetting >3× baseline within 7 days, correlate with failed logon counts to identify either repeated lockouts or potential account takeover recovery attempts.

suggestion.title: Detect Predictable Password Manipulation Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article warns users avoid complexity by 'adding a predictable "!" to the end of the last version' and making 'minimal tweaks, changing a few characters.' Detectable via password history or hash comparison.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare successive password changes for low edit distance (Levenshtein < 3) or common suffix/prefix manipulation (!, @, #, year). Alert on users repeatedly applying predictable transformations rather than generating new passphrases.

suggestion.title: npm Package Integrity Mismatch Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'malicious versions of the product to be published to the npm registry'—detection must verify installed packages against known-good hashes or registry metadata.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package.lock or yarn.lock for hash mismatches against npm registry canonical values. Alert if installed package version differs from registry metadata or if package install timestamp precedes known-good signature time. Correlate against CISA KEV and vendor security advisories for CVE-2026-45321.

suggestion.title: Credential Access Post-npm Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'credential-stealing malware'—detection must identify credential access patterns immediately following TanStack or suspicious npm package installations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate process creation (child of node/npm) with subsequent credential-store access (LSASS dump, registry reads, ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, environment variable reads). Look for unusual API calls to credential managers or file opens on paths commonly containing API keys, SSH keys, or password stores within 5–60 seconds of malicious package execution.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized npm Account Activity / Registry Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'published under a trusted identity'—detection must identify compromised npm accounts or registry API abuse that enables package injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm audit logs for unexpected package publishes from known-good accounts, especially version bumps for mature packages or publishes outside normal development schedules. Alert on registry API calls from unfamiliar IP/user-agent. Cross-reference against employee access logs to flag publishes when developers are offline.

suggestion.title: Malicious npm Package Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'malicious versions' that execute on install—detection must catch post-installation code execution and suspicious behavior in Node.js runtime.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected child processes spawned from node.exe or npm.cmd (e.g., PowerShell, cmd.exe, curl, wget). Look for suspicious environment variable expansion or shell commands in npm lifecycle scripts (postinstall, preinstall). Alert if TanStack or unknown dependencies spawn network connections to non-standard domains.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-45321 Vulnerable TanStack Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies CVE-2026-45321 affecting TanStack with federal due date 2026-06-10—detection must inventory affected versions and flag non-remediated hosts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory and package managers for TanStack installations. Correlate with vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-45321. Flag any host where TanStack is installed and the version has not been updated after the federal due date (2026-06-10). Cross-reference build pipelines to ensure no frozen dependencies pin vulnerable TanStack versions.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Nx Console Installation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'CVE-2026-48027 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' explicitly recommended. This is the foundational detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset management or vulnerability scanning for Nx Console versions published before 2026-05-27 or lacking patches dated after CVE-2026-48027 disclosure. Federal remediation deadline is 2026-06-10.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Obfuscated Payload Fetch from Nx Extension
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'compromised extension fetched an obfuscated payload'—direct behavioral indicator. Extensions should not make unexpected network requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Nx Console process or node.exe child executing unexpected outbound connections outside documented IDE update domains. Flag high-entropy domain requests, unusual port usage, or binary downloads from non-Nx infrastructure post-Nx installation.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting: Nx Process Accessing Credential Stores
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'harvested credentials from multiple sources on disk and in memory'—explicit credential-access attack step not matched to any detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Nx Console or node processes for suspicious file/registry access to credential locations (.ssh, .aws, .git-credentials, browser password DBs, Windows credential vault). Process access to sensitive credential files at runtime should be baselined against known IDE behavior; deviations trigger alerts.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Integrity Violation: Malicious Nx Version Distribution
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'malicious version of Nx Console was published'—supply-chain compromise attack vector requiring version/signature validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Nx extension signature validation failures, unexpected version downgrades, or installations from non-official repositories. Cross-check installation timestamps near 2026-05-27 disclosure against known-compromised window.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Ransomware Precursor Behavior
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Known ransomware use: Known'—establishes secondary impact chain. Detection should flag credential theft followed by reconnaissance or lateral-movement indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After Nx compromise is identified, monitor for follow-on discovery/enumeration: network share scanning, local user enumeration, registry querying, privilege escalation attempts, or unusual authentication patterns—hallmarks of ransomware staging post-credential-theft.

suggestion.title: Autonomous API Reconnaissance at Machine Scale
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Autonomous attackers are already probing application surfaces continuously at machine speed, on a schedule defenders can't keep up with.' Pipeline missed entire reconnaissance phase and anomalous probing velocity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline typical API request patterns per client/source. Flag anomalous velocity of requests to discovery endpoints (user enumeration, object enumeration, capability probing). Autonomous scanning typically shows uniform request timing, rapid sequential ID/parameter iteration, and broad coverage of endpoint space—human behavior is bursty and targeted.

suggestion.title: BOLA/IDOR Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly calls out 'BOLA or IDOR, cross-tenant data leakage' as context-dependent vulnerabilities being exploited. Pipeline produced zero use cases for object-level authorization abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor API requests for sequential or randomized manipulation of object IDs (user_id, invoice_id, resource_id parameters). Flag requests for objects belonging to different tenant/account identifiers than the authenticated user. Baseline what objects a user should be able to access; unauthorized access patterns are lateral movement indicators.

suggestion.title: Authentication Bypass and Credential Validation Testing
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'authentication bypasses' as a key class of context-dependent vulnerabilities exploited. Pipeline missed detection scenarios around failed auth escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual authentication patterns: repeated failed auth attempts with valid credentials but invalid token/session structures; auth token replay or modification; requests bypassing expected auth checks (e.g. unauthenticated access to /admin endpoints). Look for systematic testing of auth boundaries rather than opportunistic access.

suggestion.title: Chained Vulnerability Exploitation (Multi-Step Escalation)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'chained vulnerabilities, where a couple of mediums and highs combine into a critical exploit path.' Pipeline failed to model multi-step exploitation chains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate sequences of low-impact anomalies (object enumeration → failed auth → cross-tenant access) within short time window from same source. Individual events may be benign; their combination signals systematic exploitation. Use correlation to detect escalation paths.

suggestion.title: Rapid Object/Resource Enumeration via API
suggestion.rationale: Article discusses vulnerability discovery via probing and reasoning about 'how API objects relate to identities.' Pipeline missed enumeration-driven reconnaissance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag systematic iteration through object namespaces (incrementing IDs, UUID patterns, enumerable resource paths). Baseline legitimate API usage; attackers show non-random ID selection patterns, wide coverage of namespace, and requests for resources unlikely to belong to the user.

suggestion.title: Callback Phishing Emails - IT Support Impersonation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'SRG actors either directly call or send phishing emails to urge employees to call the SRG actor posing as IT support.' This distinct callback-to-external-number attack pattern requires detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for external emails containing directives to 'call IT support immediately' or similar callback language without typical internal helpdesk contact info. Correlate email receipt timestamps with subsequent outbound employee phone calls to numbers not in corporate directory.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized USB/External Storage Device Connection
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'If that attempt fails, SRG sends a threat actor to the victim's location to gain access to insert a storage device into the victim's computer' and 'malicious actors can steal data by connecting USB drives or external hard drives.' FBI explicitly cited this as an indicator: 'unauthorized installation of external hard drives or USB drives on company computers.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on USB or external storage device insertion events, especially outside business hours or coinciding with visitor badge access logs or facility access to IT-sensitive areas. Baseline normal device types and alert on unfamiliar hardware.

suggestion.title: Remote Desktop Access Granted via Social Engineering
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'While on the phone, the SRG actor directs the employee to grant access to a remote desktop session.' RDP access is the primary data exfiltration vector before physical fallback occurs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect RDP sessions initiated from external IP ranges during or immediately after suspicious IT support contact attempts (phishing emails, callback-directed calls). Flag sessions showing bulk data transfer or file enumeration of sensitive shares.

suggestion.title: Typosquatted Domain Registration - IT Helpdesk Spoofing
suggestion.rationale: Article references attack infrastructure: 'attackers register domains to impersonate IT helpdesk or support portals for major U.S. law firms and financial services firms, using typosquatted patterns.' Domain registration is prerequisite for phishing and credential-theft infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for newly registered domains matching typosquatting patterns against legal and financial organization names (one-character typos, extra hyphens, homoglyph variations of 'support', 'helpdesk', 'itsupport' subdomains). Cross-reference with phishing email sender domains and callback numbers in social engineering attempts.

suggestion.title: Phone-Based Social Engineering - IT Support Impersonation Calls
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'SRG actors use a social engineering scheme to pose as an employee from the victim's IT department. SRG actors either directly call or send phishing emails to urge employees to call.' Direct phone calls are the social engineering vector. Article also states: 'will also call the victims' employees or clients to pressure them into beginning ransom negotiations.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PBX/phone logs for incoming calls claiming to represent IT support from external numbers, especially during off-hours. Implement employee reporting mechanism for suspicious IT support requests and correlate call patterns with contemporaneous phishing campaigns targeting same organization.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration to External Physical Media
suggestion.rationale: Article describes final exfiltration method: 'malicious actors can steal data by connecting USB drives or external hard drives to the victim's computer.' Large-scale data staging and transfer to external media follows initial access and credential compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk file copy operations to newly connected external storage devices, especially targeting legal documents, financial records, or other sensitive data repositories. Alert on high-volume data writes to USB/external drives following RDP session activity.

suggestion.title: Yamcs ChangeMissionDatabase privilege grant anomaly — unauthorized role elevation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'authenticated user with the ChangeMissionDatabase privilege' as the prerequisite. This is the gatekeeping privilege. Should detect new role assignments to this permission level outside normal provisioning workflows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal ChangeMissionDatabase privilege grants (should be rare). Alert on new assignments to non-admin accounts or service accounts, and on grants occurring outside business hours or outside IT-controlled provisioning requests. Correlate with subsequent algorithm modifications.

suggestion.title: Janino expression compilation errors or suspicious Java keywords in Yamcs algorithm payloads
suggestion.rationale: Article names org.yamcs.algorithms.JavaExprAlgorithmExecutionFactory and Janino as the vulnerable compilation engine. Attack vector is unsanitized algorithm text. Should hunt for Janino compiler exceptions, failed compilations, and suspicious Java code patterns in algorithm evaluation logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Yamcs application logs for Janino compilation errors and exceptions on algorithm evaluation. Flag algorithm text containing Runtime.getRuntime(), ProcessBuilder, exec(), or java.lang.reflect APIs. Correlate with shell-spawning activity on the JVM host.

suggestion.title: Yamcs MissionDatabase algorithm XML modification — schema drift or code injection payload signatures
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires modifying algorithm definitions stored in MissionDatabase. Article does not specify the mechanism (API vs. file-system), but algorithm payloads are the actual attack surface. Should detect suspicious modifications to algorithm code blocks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt HTTP PATCH/POST bodies to /api/mdb/*/algorithms/* for Java syntax keywords (new, import, Runtime, ProcessBuilder, exec). Baseline normal algorithm update patterns and alert on unexpected code patterns. Cross-reference with Yamcs process spawning events.

suggestion.title: Yamcs configuration file tampering — algorithm executor factory or plugin classpath modification
suggestion.rationale: Persistence or pre-exploitation could involve modifying Yamcs XML/YAML configs to alter algorithm execution policies or inject malicious JAR references. Article does not explicitly describe this but is possible vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Yamcs installation directory and config files for unauthorized modification. Flag changes to algorithm executor factory definitions, classpath entries, or Janino policy settings. Establish baseline of approved configuration changes and alert on deviations outside maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: Yamcs API authentication or session anomalies — privilege escalation or token replay on MDB endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Precondition for exploitation is authentication + ChangeMissionDatabase privilege. Could be initial access via credential theft, session hijacking, or auth bypass. Should monitor for suspicious authentication patterns before algorithm modifications occur.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal authentication patterns to Yamcs API. Alert on failed login attempts followed by successful authentication from same source, on API calls from unusual IP/user-agent combinations, and on rapid MDB endpoint access from a single session. Correlate with privilege grants and algorithm modifications.

suggestion.title: Yamcs process and child-process tree anomaly — Java spawning multiple interpreters or utilities
suggestion.rationale: Execution phase will likely manifest as Java process spawning shell interpreters (bash, sh, cmd.exe). Multiple child process spawning (chains of shells launching curl/wget/nc) is unusual and indicates active exploitation or post-exploitation activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Yamcs JVM process for spawning of shell interpreters and network utilities. Alert on suspicious process chains where java → bash → curl or java → cmd.exe → powershell occur in rapid succession. Baseline normal Yamcs process behavior and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: LiquidJS vulnerable version in application inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes LiquidJS as the vulnerable component; pipeline should flag affected applications. 'It is possible to execute arbitrary code with crafted templates' indicates version check needed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for `package.json` files containing LiquidJS dependency versions <4.0.3 (or version disclosed in CVE-2026-45618 advisory). Correlate against inbound HTTP requests to applications that parse user input as LiquidJS templates. Flag if vulnerable version exists in internet-facing web root.

suggestion.title: valueOf filter chain exploitation in template context
suggestion.rationale: Article POC shows `{%assign r=1|valueOf%}` directly accessing context object. This is the gadget chain entry point. Pipeline should hunt for this specific filter usage or similar reflection chains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for HTTP POST/GET requests with LiquidJS template syntax including `valueOf`, `constructor`, `prototype`, or `__proto__` in URL-decoded query parameters or request body. Correlate with requests to endpoints known to process Liquid templates (e.g., `/render`, `/template`, `/mail`).

suggestion.title: Child process module imports in Node.js context after SSTI
suggestion.rationale: Article payload uses `child_process` module to spawn shell commands. Article shows 'getBuiltinModule' and 'child_process' gadgets. This is the execution mechanism post-template-injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In Node.js processes (node.exe, w3wp.exe with iisnode), detect dynamic module loading or `require('child_process')` calls preceded within 1 minute by inbound HTTP requests matching SSTI patterns. Flag as execution phase of LiquidJS RCE chain.

suggestion.title: Prototype pollution chain detection in Node.js memory
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions `__proto__` and `assign __proto__` in payload variants. This is a second-stage gadget chain for privilege escalation or sandbox escape within the Node process.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for Node.js processes with command-line or environment variables containing `__proto__`, `prototype`, or `constructor` manipulation. Correlate with prior LiquidJS SSTI inbound requests. Escalates detection confidence if found in w3wp.exe (IIS) or authenticated service context.

suggestion.title: LiquidJS render() calls with untrusted template source
suggestion.rationale: Article does not name the vulnerable function directly, but implies templates are 'crafted' and user-controlled. Detection should focus on entry points where user input reaches template rendering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Static analysis: flag any `liquidjs.render()` or `LiquidEngine.parse()` calls where the template string originates from HTTP request parameters, headers, database fields marked as user-controlled, or file uploads. Dynamic: instrument Node.js to log template source on render calls; alert if source is not hardcoded string literal.

suggestion.title: HTTP response time anomaly from Node.js template rendering
suggestion.rationale: SSTI exploitation involves reflection and gadget chain traversal, which is CPU-intensive. Article payload involves context introspection and module loading—detectable as response latency spike.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP response times for requests to LiquidJS template endpoints. Alert on single requests with >5s response time (indicating payload evaluation delay), especially if preceded by URL parameters containing filter syntax or special characters. Correlate with request size and process CPU usage spike on node.exe parent.

suggestion.title: Teams Account Impersonation - IT Staff Naming Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title directly states 'Impersonate IT Helpdesk Staff'—attackers create fake accounts mimicking IT support. Pipeline should detect Azure AD accounts with IT-support naming patterns created outside normal provisioning windows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Azure AD for user creation where DisplayName or UserPrincipalName contains IT-support keywords (helpdesk, itsupport, support, techsupport, admin) created outside business hours or from unusual geolocation, with rapid addition to multiple Teams channels or security groups.

suggestion.title: Bulk Teams Messages with Phishing and Credential-Harvesting Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article phrase 'exploit Teams collaboration features' implies broad-target phishing. Helpdesk impersonation requires bulk messaging with credential-harvesting payloads to multiple users.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Teams users sending identical or near-identical messages to 5+ users within 30 minutes, especially containing: URL shorteners, 'verify account'/'confirm identity'/'update password' language, suspicious domains, or typosquatted domains matching corporate auth infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Teams Phishing Links - Credential Harvesting and Fake Authentication Pages
suggestion.rationale: IT helpdesk impersonation attacks require fake login pages to harvest credentials. Detection must identify malicious authentication URLs shared in Teams messages to catch the credential-access phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Teams messages (via audit logs or DLP) for URLs matching known phishing infrastructure (evilginx, OAuth-phishing providers), suspicious shortener domains, or domains with high character similarity to legitimate Microsoft/corporate auth endpoints. Correlate with Azure AD failed MFA within 15 minutes.

suggestion.title: Teams File Share - Malware and Info-Stealer Distribution from Impersonated Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Helpdesk impersonators distribute malware as 'patches' or configuration files via Teams. Article phrase 'exploit collaboration features' includes file-sharing execution vectors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Teams file uploads from newly-created or IT-named accounts, especially: .exe, .msi, .scr, .zip containing executables, and macro-enabled Office documents (.xlsm, .docm). Cross-reference file hashes against VirusTotal and internal malware repos. Flag from accounts with <7 day tenure.

suggestion.title: Post-Phishing Login Spike - Brute Force After Teams Message Delivery
suggestion.rationale: After phishing credentials via Teams, attackers attempt account takeover using harvested credentials. Article describes credential-theft attacks; detection should flag subsequent login compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate suspicious Teams messages (phishing indicators, bulk distribution) with 5+ failed login attempts from the same IP within 60 minutes, followed by successful login from a new device/location within 10 minutes. Pattern indicates credential compromise post-phishing.

suggestion.title: Teams External App Authorization by Impersonated Service Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Compromised accounts impersonating IT staff can authorize malicious external apps for data exfiltration or command-and-control. Relates to 'exploit collaboration features' for maintaining attacker foothold.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor authorization of third-party apps/connectors by newly-created or IT-named accounts, especially those with message-read, data-access, or administrative permissions. Flag authorizations outside normal IT provisioning workflows or from unusual approval chains/geolocation.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Installation Matching Typosquat Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article title and meta explicitly state 'typosquatted npm packages' as attack vector. Pipeline extracted zero detections for package-name-similarity attacks despite this being the direct initial access mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install/npm ci invocations and cross-reference installed package names against Levenshtein distance similarity to legitimate packages. Flag packages with >80% name similarity but different publisher/signature, or packages created within 30 days of legitimate package creation.

suggestion.title: Node.js Child Process Spawning Credential Enumeration Commands
suggestion.rationale: Attack steals 'cloud and CI/CD credentials from developer environments'—requires postinstall script execution harvesting env vars (AWS_*, GitHub tokens). Pipeline missed credential-access detection despite explicit article narrative.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect node.js or npm processes spawning child processes executing env, printenv, cat against ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.docker/config.json, or piping 'env' output to secondary processes. Flag process chains initiated within 5 seconds of npm install completing.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of Environment Variables via HTTPS POST from npm Install Context
suggestion.rationale: Attack objective is credential theft; pipeline missed network-layer detection for credential exfiltration triggered by malicious package postinstall scripts to attacker C2.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound HTTPS POST requests from node.js processes within 10 seconds of npm install completion, especially to IP/domain with no prior organizational whitelist. Payload analysis: flag Base64-encoded credentials, AWS access keys (AKIA*), or GitHub PAT patterns in HTTP body.

suggestion.title: Malicious Package Execution in CI/CD Build Environment
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly targets 'CI/CD secrets' alongside developer credentials. Pipeline missed CI/CD-context detection for npm execution spawning credential access or exfiltration during build stage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In CI/CD logs, detect npm install followed immediately by process spawning env enumeration, curl/wget to external infrastructure, or credential file access (AWS, Azure, GitHub tokens) within the same build job. Flag packages executed in ephemeral runners with cloud credential environment variables populated.

suggestion.title: Postinstall Script Execution Accessing Credential Stores
suggestion.rationale: npm postinstall/preinstall scripts in malicious packages trigger credential harvesting. Pipeline missed execution-phase detection for script-based credential access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag npm packages whose postinstall script (parsed from package.json) contains patterns matching credential store access: references to ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, /root/.docker, KUBECONFIG env vars, or registry-credential files. Cross-check against known malicious package repository lists.

suggestion.title: Package Masquerading via Similar Namespace (Typosquat Detection)
suggestion.rationale: Core attack mechanic is masquerading via package-name similarity. Pipeline should surface dependency-analysis detection comparing installed vs. requested package names.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse package-lock.json / yarn.lock and compare resolved package names character-by-character against requested names in package.json. Highlight discrepancies: e.g., requested 'express-server' but resolved to 'expres-server'. Alert on first-seen packages with minimal version history (<10 versions) matching popular projects.

suggestion.title: VS Code Remote-SSH Extension RCE Execution
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'RCE' and 'Remote-SSH' but pipeline extracted zero execution-phase detections. Should detect command execution initiated through the vulnerable extension.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor VS Code (code.exe) for unexpected child processes or shell command execution spawned via the Remote-SSH extension. Alert on execution of arbitrary commands from SSH tunnel contexts or extension-spawned process chains.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement: SSH Key Exfiltration to Cloud Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Title describes 'Pivot From Developer Machines to Cloud Servers' but zero lateral-movement detections generated. Pivoting requires credential theft from developer machine.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect access to ~/.ssh directories (private keys, config, known_hosts) by VS Code or its child processes. Correlate with subsequent SSH connections from the developer machine to cloud infrastructure (AWS, Azure, GCP) using those credentials.

suggestion.title: Suspicious SSH Tunnel Establishment from VS Code Context
suggestion.rationale: RCE leading to cloud pivot requires SSH tunneling, but no command-and-control or lateral-movement network signatures captured.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for SSH connection establishment initiated from VS Code processes (typically non-SSH binaries). Flag SSH traffic to non-standard ports or to cloud provider IP ranges initiated outside normal development context.

suggestion.title: Malicious VS Code Remote-SSH Extension or Plugin Installation
suggestion.rationale: RCE likely delivered via extension mechanism; no supply-chain or execution-delivery detections present despite specific component (Remote-SSH extension) being named in title.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor VS Code extension directory ($HOME/.vscode/extensions) and the VS Code Marketplace API for unexpected remote-ssh extension downloads or versions. Detect .vsix file execution or unsigned extension installation.

suggestion.title: Phishing Emails Targeting World Cup Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article keywords explicitly include 'phishing' as primary attack vector; description states actors targeting critical infrastructure during major event
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for mass phishing campaigns targeting World Cup infrastructure operators, ticketing systems, and venue networks. Track URL redirects to lookalike domains and credential harvesting pages. Correlate with failed MFA attempts post-delivery.

suggestion.title: Malicious QR Code Distribution
suggestion.rationale: Article keywords explicitly mention 'QR Codes' as attack vector; common phishing delivery method for sporting events requiring rapid ticket/credential handling
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect QR codes embedded in promotional emails purporting to be from FIFA/venue operators. Monitor landing pages for credential capture forms. Track redirect chains from decoded QR destinations to C2 or data exfiltration sites.

suggestion.title: Typosquatting Domains Impersonating World Cup Entities
suggestion.rationale: Article keywords include 'typosquatting'; standard pre-breach reconnaissance for targeting infrastructure operators and legitimate ticket distribution partners
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS queries and SSL/TLS certificates for registered domains homoglyphic to 'fifa.com', 'worldcup2026.com', venue domains, and ticketing partners. Flag newly registered domains with World Cup keywords. Correlate with phishing email campaigns.

suggestion.title: Wiper Malware Deployment Against Event Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article keywords explicitly include 'wiper'; ransomware/state-actor groups use wipers for disruptive impact against high-visibility targets like major sporting events
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for mass deletion patterns, disk erasure utilities (cipher.exe, sdelete), MBR modification, and sudden process termination across infrastructure OT/IT systems. Track suspicious administrative tool execution and lateral movement preceding wiper deployment.

suggestion.title: State-Aligned Actor Reconnaissance of World Cup Critical Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Description states 'state-aligned actors' are targeting critical infrastructure; actor names Fighting Ursa and Razing Ursa suggest nation-state groups conducting strategic reconnaissance
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect scanning activity against World Cup venue networks, credential enumeration attempts via OAuth/LDAP, and OSINT collection targeting venue operators. Monitor for spear-phishing campaigns with legitimate business context (venue partnerships, broadcast logistics).

suggestion.title: Ransomware Group Initial Access Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'ransomware groups' as threat; phishing + QR codes + typosquatting are standard attack chain for ransomware deployment on high-value targets
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate phishing delivery with subsequent execution of Office macros, script interpreters, or archive extraction. Track lateral movement post-execution to domain controllers and backup infrastructure. Monitor for ransom note creation and encryption activity.

suggestion.title: npm Package Installation with Embedded Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Exposes Threat Actor's Private GitHub Token' — pipeline should detect packages containing hardcoded secrets in distributed code, package.json, or init scripts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm package installations where source code or artifacts contain patterns matching GitHub token formats (ghp_*, gho_*, ghu_*, ghs_*), SSH private keys, or API credentials. Cross-reference with public compromises.

suggestion.title: Malicious npm Package Installation from Unexpected Registry
suggestion.rationale: Article centers on AI-generated npm malware indicating supply-chain compromise; initial access occurs via dependency injection or typosquatting to unexpected registry sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm install commands targeting non-standard registries, package-lock.json entries with registry domain drift, or packages fetched from repositories not in org-approved list. Correlate with package signature mismatches.

suggestion.title: Node.js Process Exfiltrating Data via GitHub API with Stolen Token
suggestion.rationale: Exposed GitHub token is an actionable indicator for lateral movement and data exfiltration; malware could use stolen token to access/modify repositories or exfiltrate via GitHub.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for node.js or child processes issuing HTTPS requests to api.github.com or github.com carrying authorization headers with GitHub tokens. Alert on token usage from unexpected geographies, IP blocks, or contexts.

suggestion.title: AI-Generated Code Obfuscation Patterns in npm Package Source
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically identifies 'AI-Generated' malware — LLM-generated code exhibits entropy, function naming, and control-flow patterns distinct from human-written or traditional obfuscators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan npm package source for LLM signatures: high lexical redundancy, unnatural identifier patterns, obfuscated payloads with atypical logic flow, excessive comments, or suspicious string concatenation sequences typical of LLM output.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized GitHub Account Activity Using Exposed Token
suggestion.rationale: Threat actor's exposed GitHub token is a persistence and reconnaissance mechanism; unusual API calls, repository access, or webhook creation using compromised token indicates ongoing exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate GitHub audit logs for token usage anomalies: API calls from new IP ranges, bulk repository access, secret exfiltration, webhook/deploy key creation, or team-permission modifications using the compromised token.

suggestion.title: npm Package Post-Install Script Executing Unauthorized Network Calls
suggestion.rationale: npm supply-chain attacks frequently use install-time hooks (postinstall scripts) to execute malware before visibility; article context suggests malware payload triggered at install.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on postinstall script execution spawning network calls to non-standard destinations, credential exfiltration attempts, or spawning child processes with unusual arguments. Baseline npm install scripts and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Detection of Accessibility Service Abuse for Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states BTMOB 'abuses Android Accessibility Services to obtain elevated permissions and additional system access without further user interaction.' This is a direct privilege escalation attack step with minimal defender visibility.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Accessibility Service permission grants immediately following APK installation from non-Play Store sources. Flag if the requesting app is newly installed (first seen <30 min) or lacks legitimate accessibility use case (e.g., keyboard app, screen reader). Correlate with permission changes to system settings or storage access.

suggestion.title: Phishing Redirect to Fake Google Play Portal
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'potential victims are redirected to portals mimicking Google Play and prompted to download the fake apps.' This is the initial access vector for BTMOB distribution in the described campaign.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify DNS/TLS mismatches where domains resolve to non-Google infrastructure but mimic play.google.com (homoglyph variants, subdomain tricks). Flag APK downloads from non-canonical Google Play domains. Alert on User-Agent spoofing of legitimate Play Store clients originating from suspicious IPs.

suggestion.title: Evasive APK Installation with Icon Hiding and Google Play Disabling
suggestion.rationale: Article describes builder features including 'hide its icon to make it more difficult to remove from the device, or prevent sleep mode' and 'disable Google Play.' These are post-installation evasion tactics specific to the malware customization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for apps that disable the PackageManager (Google Play) or delete launcher shortcuts immediately after installation. Detect system property modifications (ro.debuggable, persist.sys settings) and app visibility flag changes. Correlate with absence of user interaction logs in the accessibility framework.

suggestion.title: Financial Transaction Interception and Screenshot Collection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies malware 'intercepting financial transactions, capturing screenshots' as core capabilities. This collection phase requires monitor-level access to banking app interactions and clipboard/framebuffer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag suspicious processes capturing screenshots or accessing input events during banking app foreground (com.intra.banking.* patterns). Detect clipboard access by non-keyboard apps. Monitor for unusual network exfiltration patterns (small, frequent, image-sized packets) after banking app activity. Correlate Accessibility Service grants with financial app use.

suggestion.title: Rapid APK Polymorphism Evasion via Builder-Generated Variants
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'rapid generation of new payloads can undermine the effectiveness of single-layered defenses' and describes the builder's payload customization. This requires behavioral/yara clustering rather than hash-based detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cluster APK samples by behavioral signature (permissions requested, C2 domains contacted, file access patterns) rather than hash. Flag high-velocity clusters (>5 unique hashes, same behavior, 24h window) as polymorphic malware variants. Use dynamic analysis telemetry (ANYRUN/ESET) to correlate builder-generated payloads with observed family markers (SpySolr ancestry, Accessibility Service abuse timing).

suggestion.title: Localized Phishing Campaign with Government Agency Impersonation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'BTMOB campaigns that used an Argentinian government agency as a lure.' This is a campaign-specific social engineering tactic enabling targeted phishing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag phishing campaigns using government entity branding (Argentine ministry domains, official seals, .gov.ar spoofs). Detect lure content referencing government services (tax filing, licenses) with urgency themes. Monitor for infrastructure registrations mimicking official gov sites, particularly with recently active C2 infrastructure overlaps.

suggestion.title: Employee Account Compromise - Anomalous Login Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'An unauthorized actor used social engineering to deceive an employee to gain access' on April 10, compromised account active until blocked April 14. Zero detection rule generated for flagging logins from non-standard geography, time, or IP inconsistent with employee baseline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag employee account logins from geographies/IPs inconsistent with historical baseline, outside business hours, or involving rapid authentication failures followed by success. Require manual review if correlated with failed MFA challenges.

suggestion.title: Bulk Data Exfiltration - Volume Baseline Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'bad actor illegally copied personal information' and 'stolen documents containing over 8.7 million records with personally identifiable information and terabytes of internal corporate data.' No detection rule for file access volume spike or database export anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when single user account accesses >50 files in 1-hour window or >2GB file volume in 4-hour window, especially if accessing data outside their departmental scope (e.g., call-center employee querying loyalty program database). Correlate with non-standard login location/time.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Database Access - Mariner Society Loyalty Program
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The data contained fields indicating it related to the Mariner Society loyalty program run by Holland America' and included 5.9M customer records with names, DOBs, email, loyalty status. Detection gap: no rule for unauthorized access to customer database or loyalty program export.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline which employee roles should query Mariner Society database. Alert on queries from employees outside customer-service or loyalty teams, or queries returning >10K records at once. Flag any bulk export of customer PII fields.

suggestion.title: ShinyHunters - Threat Actor IOC Correlation & Leak Site Monitoring
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'ShinyHunters extortion gang claimed responsibility'; 'ShinyHunters has been targeting Salesforce customers' with documented campaigns (Salesloft Drift, Aura). Article confirms breach but pipeline captures zero threat-actor context or correlation with prior incidents.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Consume threat intelligence on ShinyHunters infrastructure (leak site URLs, C2 endpoints, associated ASNs). Flag any outbound traffic to known ShinyHunters domains or CDNs. Alert if employee browses to leak site or GitHub accounts tied to group.

suggestion.title: Carnival Recidivism Pattern - Fourth Breach in Six Years
suggestion.rationale: Article: Breaches disclosed in 'March 2020 and June 2021' plus 'August 2020 and December 2020.' Four prior breaches + this April 2026 breach = endemic control failures. Pipeline generated zero correlation rule for repeat-offender organization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag organization as 'high-recidivism breach target.' Lower alerting thresholds for any employee phishing, credential reuse, shared password patterns, or guest/contractor access. Assume attacker has reconnaissance data from prior 2020–2021 breaches; monitor for re-exploitation of known weak departments.

suggestion.title: Salesforce Environment - High-Risk ShinyHunters Targeting Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article contextualizes ShinyHunters' known focus: 'Over the past year, ShinyHunters has been targeting Salesforce customers and has breached hundreds of companies worldwide, claiming to have stolen billions of records.' Carnival likely runs Salesforce for sales/CRM; no use case for Salesforce-specific anomalies.

Alert on authentication from suspicious geographies or failed MFA followed by success. Correlate with any email phishing campaigns targeting Salesforce admin users.

suggestion.title: Gogs Post-Auth RCE: Child Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Any Authenticated User Execute Arbitrary Code' — explicit code execution post-login; no detections generated for shell process spawning from git-daemon or Gogs service.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes (bash, cmd.exe, powershell, sh) created by Gogs or git-daemon parent processes within 60 seconds of successful API authentication. Prioritize uncommon command-line arguments (curl, wget, nc, reverse shells, base64-encoded payloads).

suggestion.title: Gogs API: Authentication + Anomalous Endpoint Access
suggestion.rationale: RCE exploited post-login; pipeline missed correlation of successful auth events with unusual API endpoints (hooks, file ops, raw content access).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline per-user Gogs API call patterns. Flag sequences of: successful authentication → rapid calls to admin/hook endpoints or unusual git operations → execution indicators.

suggestion.title: Gogs Version Identification and Vulnerability Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline failed to extract any IOCs or version identifiers for vulnerable Gogs instances; essential for asset detection and risk scoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Extract Gogs version from HTTP Server headers, git-daemon banners, and process command-lines. Cross-reference with CVE advisory to identify vulnerable instances; trigger patch advisories or network isolation.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Git Push/Clone with Embedded Payloads
suggestion.rationale: RCE typically triggered via malicious git push or specially-crafted repository clones; no git operation anomalies detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor git push/clone for suspicious patterns: shell metacharacters in branch/tag names, symlinks in payloads, path traversal sequences, or abnormal object sizes. Correlate with post-auth code execution.

suggestion.title: Typosquatted FIFA Domain Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes threat actors using 'minor spelling changes' like 'fiffa[.]com' and alternative TLDs (.org, .xyz, .live, .sale). These are highly detectable patterns in DNS queries, web proxy logs, and email links.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DNS resolutions and HTTP requests to domains that closely match 'fifa.com' using edit distance or regex patterns (fiffa, fifa-*, *fifa*, etc.). Alert on alternative TLD registrations (.xyz, .live, .sale) combined with FIFA-related keywords. Cross-reference against known typosquatting patterns tracked in phishing feeds.

suggestion.title: Fraudulent FIFA Employment Portal Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes fake employment sites 'jobs-fifa[.]com' and 'fifa-hiring[.]com' used for credential harvesting. These portal patterns are enumerable and correlate with typosquatted domain infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on domain registrations containing patterns like 'jobs-*', '*-hiring', '*-careers' combined with FIFA brand keywords. Correlate with WHOIS data for recent registrations and hosting on free/bulletproof providers. Monitor for employment portal landing pages serving credential-capture forms.

suggestion.title: World Cup Malvertising Campaign Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies campaigns promoted via 'Google Search, Facebook ads, Telegram, and WhatsApp' with World Cup branding. These platform-specific malvertising vectors are detectable through email link inspection, web proxy inspection, and social media API monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for click-throughs on ads referencing '2026 World Cup', 'FIFA tickets', 'FIFA hospitality', 'World Cup merchandise' from untrusted ad platforms or spoofed Google/Facebook ad landing pages. Flag URLs with World Cup keywords pointing to newly registered or typosquatted domains. Alert on suspicious referrer chains from social platforms (Telegram, WhatsApp) to phishing infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Fake Ticket / Hospitality Premium Fraud Portal
suggestion.rationale: Article documents 'Ghost Stadium' operating '300+ phishing sites, clones of the real FIFA portal, for premium ticket fraud' and Bitdefender observing fake merchandise/collectibles/streaming services. Portal cloning + payment processing is a distinct attack vector warranting its own detection.

Alert on domains hosting payment forms requesting credit card data in contexts inconsistent with official FIFA ticketing.

suggestion.title: Personal Data Exfiltration Form Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states fraudulent websites 'collect from visitors various types of data, including names, physical and email addresses, phone numbers, banking/payment details'. Form fields requesting these data combinations in phishing contexts are detectable via web sandbox analysis or form inspection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag web forms that request multi-field credential/PII combinations (name + email + phone + payment details) on suspicious or newly registered domains. Correlate form fields with FIFA-related keywords or job application framing. Monitor for exfiltration of captured form data via DNS tunneling or HTTPS to non-FIFA endpoints.

suggestion.title: AI-Generated Phishing Lure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states GreyVibe 'used multiple AI tools, including ChatGPT, Ideogram AI, and Google Gemini, to generate detailed and realistic content' for phishing lures, establishing systematic LLM-assisted social engineering as primary vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for phishing emails with image attachments exhibiting LLM artifact patterns—unusual text consistency, identical formatting across language variants, structural markers of synthetic content. Correlate image metadata and visual artifacts with known GreyVibe themes (Ukrainian government, military, emergency services).

suggestion.title: Fake CAPTCHA/ClickFix Command Execution Redirect
suggestion.rationale: PhantomClick campaign 'fake CAPTCHA/ClickFix pages disguised as Zoom and LAPAS sites trick victims into running self-infecting commands through fake Cloudflare verification prompts.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on redirects to fake Cloudflare/CAPTCHA verification pages followed by command-line execution (cmd.exe, powershell.exe) or rundll32 invocation within seconds. Flag domains spoofing Cloudflare, Zoom, or LAPAS with HTTPS interception patterns.

suggestion.title: PowerShell RAT Behavior – File Theft, Screenshot, Credential Access, RDP Setup
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'PowerShell-based remote access trojan named LegionRelay' supporting 'file theft, screenshot capturing, browser credential theft, Telegram and WhatsApp data exfiltration, and RDP access setup,' establishing discrete post-compromise signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for PowerShell processes with dynamic script loading, followed by browser credential store access (DPAPI/vault queries), screenshot capture API calls, and netsh RDP port forwarding commands. Obfuscated variable names suggest LOOKVALPS/LOOKVALJS obfuscators.

suggestion.title: Malware Archive via Google Drive & 4sync Phishing
suggestion.rationale: PhantomMail delivers 'malicious ZIP/RAR archives via Google Drive and 4sync links, using decoy PDFs or fake errors while deploying malware.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor emails with hyperlinks to Google Drive or 4sync with archive downloads (ZIP/RAR). Flag archives containing executables paired with decoy PDFs, or archives designed for auto-extraction. Correlate with Ukrainian government/telecom/energy organization imagery in decoy documents.

suggestion.title: FallSpy Android Spyware via Fake Dating Websites & WebRTC Audio/Video Capture
suggestion.rationale: PrincessClub campaign uses 'Fake Ukrainian adult/dating websites delivering FallSpy Android spyware' and 'fake female Telegram personas and later added WebRTC-based live calls that could capture the victim's audio/video.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Android APK installations from domains mimicking Ukrainian dating/charity organizations with permissions for contacts, call logs, location, media. Detect WebRTC streams and audio capture initiated from fake Telegram accounts matching known female persona naming patterns.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Miner Deployment Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'cryptocurrency miner was deployed on some victim machines,' indicating resource hijacking as secondary post-compromise objective.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution of known crypto miner binaries (xmrig, monero variants, stratum pool connectors). Detect sustained elevated CPU usage anomalies correlated with connections to mining pools. Hunt for parent-child process chains attempting to inject miners into legitimate system processes.

suggestion.title: Marimo Application RCE Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names Marimo RCE as entry point ('Move From Marimo RCE'). No detection UC generated for this primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Marimo process for unexpected code execution or shell spawning. Alert on suspicious POST payloads to Marimo endpoints. Track process lineage from Marimo worker to child processes (bash, powershell, python).

suggestion.title: Multi-Hop Lateral Movement Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes four pivots: 'Move From Marimo RCE to Internal Database in Four Pivots'. No detection for multi-stage lateral movement chain despite explicit kill-chain description.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect chains of remote sessions (RDP, SSH, WinRM) initiated from single compromised host within hours. Flag reuse of service account credentials across multiple remote-access events. Alert on pivots to systems not previously accessed.

suggestion.title: Internal Database Access Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Attack objective explicitly stated as 'Internal Database'. No detection for database enumeration, suspicious credentials, or large data reads following lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on database connections from atypical source IPs following lateral movement. Detect unusually large SELECT queries on sensitive tables. Flag connections using non-standard credentials or service accounts to databases.

suggestion.title: LLM Agent-Driven Automated Exploitation Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article highlights LLM agent orchestrating attack steps—central TTPs. Pipeline did not extract technique for autonomous agent execution or command chaining.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect LLM library imports (LangChain, AutoGen, Claude SDK) from suspicious contexts. Monitor for rapid sequential command execution mimicking agentic loops (scan → parse → execute → next). Flag subprocess chains from single parent with short inter-command timing.

suggestion.title: Network Service Discovery from Compromised Host
suggestion.rationale: Four-pivot attack requires reconnaissance of internal targets. Article structure implies enumeration phase. No discovery UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect port scans or net view / Get-ADComputer enumeration from Marimo process context. Alert on LDAP queries or SMB probes from application server. Flag discovery tools spawned from web-tier processes.

suggestion.title: Fake Recruiter Email with macOS Payload Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'Fake Recruiter Lures' targeting cryptocurrency firms. Pipeline should detect phishing emails impersonating HR/recruitment with macOS malware attachments or credential-harvesting links.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Emails impersonating recruiters or HR professionals with PKG/DMG attachments, or links to fake job applications and credential forms. Target domain: cryptocurrency exchange or trading firms. Flag if sender uses lookalike recruiter domain or free email with job title references.

suggestion.title: Unsigned macOS Binary Execution from Download/Temp
suggestion.rationale: Article payload is 'macOS Malware'—pipeline must detect execution of unsigned or suspicious binaries following recruiter email interaction, indicating successful delivery and user execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Process execution originating from ~/Downloads, /tmp, or Caches directories on macOS systems within cryptocurrency-sector targets.
