Detect unsigned code or code signing bypass (T1553.001). Monitor bash/zsh spawning suspicious curl/wget for secondary payloads or reverse shells.

suggestion.title: macOS Command-and-Control Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Malware implies C2 infrastructure. Pipeline should detect outbound callbacks from compromised macOS systems to attacker-controlled infrastructure, establishing command channel.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Periodic outbound HTTPS or DNS queries from macOS systems to suspicious/newly-registered domains with no business justification. Look for beaconing patterns (fixed intervals), especially from cryptography/exchange employee machines post-recruiter contact.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Wallet or Exchange Credential Theft
suggestion.rationale: Targeting cryptocurrency firms implies financial payload: detection of credential exfiltration, keylogging, or unauthorized wallet/exchange access following malware execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Exfiltration of files matching crypto wallet patterns (seed phrases, private keys, exchange API credentials) from infected macOS devices. Monitor for unusual login locations or API key usage on exchange accounts belonging to employees at targeted firms post-compromise.

suggestion.title: Recruiter OSINT and Targeting Campaign
suggestion.rationale: Social engineering vector implies reconnaissance: pipeline should detect indicators of JINX-0164 researching and profiling cryptocurrency employees prior to lure delivery (article phrase: 'Fake Recruiter Lures').
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Bulk reconnaissance of LinkedIn/GitHub profiles of crypto firm employees. Fake LinkedIn recruiter profiles with minimal history contacting multiple targets at same organization within short timeframe. Registration of lookalike job board or recruiter domain weeks before phishing campaign launch.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised macOS to Internal Crypto Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Successful macOS compromise may serve as beachhead for lateral movement to exchange infrastructure or wallet management systems, escalating impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Anomalous lateral connections from compromised employee macOS device to internal exchange wallets, hot wallets, or administrative systems. Monitor for SSH/RDP attempts, internal scanning, or credential reuse from macOS systems to Linux/Windows infrastructure.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Workflow Credential Exfiltration (Megalodon Campaign)
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'The campaign relies on GitHub Actions workflows containing a payload designed to steal credentials, keys, tokens, and other secrets. The workflows were injected through over 5,700 malicious commits.' This is a direct credential-access attack via supply-chain workflow injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub repositories for workflow file (.github/workflows/*.yml) modifications on 2026-05-18 or bulk commit batches. Alert on workflows containing curl/wget commands exfiltrating environment variables, Base64-encoded payloads with C2 URLs, or credential scanning disables. Correlate with downstream outbound HTTP POST from affected repo runners.

suggestion.title: Domain-Fronting Abuse for Brand Hijacking (Underminr)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes: 'The Underminr domain-fronting attack allows threat actors to modify web requests and leverage trusted websites to cloak malicious activity.' Requires detection of SNI/Host header divergence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect TLS connections where SNI hostname differs from HTTP Host header or certificate CN. Flag requests routing through CDNs (CloudFlare, Akamai, Fastly) where backend target domain is unexpected or unrelated to SNI. Alert on repeated mismatches from single internal IP over short duration.

suggestion.title: DICOM File Format Heap Overflow Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'heap overflow vulnerability through the exploitation of the DICOM file format' with vulnerabilities in MediaInfoLib, GDCM, and Orthanc. PACS systems 'automatically ingest files received over the network.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DICOM ingestion on PACS systems for abnormal file uploads followed by process crashes or unhandled exceptions in MediaInfoLib/GDCM parsers. Alert on heap-related exceptions (access violations, segfaults) correlating with DICOM processing. Flag outdated versions of vulnerable libraries.

suggestion.title: Cloud Credentials Published to Public Git Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'contractor intentionally published AWS GovCloud keys and a vast trove of other agency secrets on a public GitHub account.' Clear credential exposure requiring detection and response.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan committed files for AWS credential patterns (AKIA*, AWS secret key format) in public repos. Correlate exposed credentials with CloudTrail login attempts. Alert on bulk data exfiltration from affected AWS accounts post-exposure. Monitor GovCloud environments for lateral movement using compromised credentials.

suggestion.title: Bulk Repository Supply-Chain Commit Injection
suggestion.rationale: Megalodon: 'malicious commits pushed to the impacted repositories on May 18' across 5,700+ repos. Represents coordinated persistence attack requiring temporal correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect commits from service accounts or newly-created bot identities pushing to human-owned repos on 2026-05-18. Alert on bulk workflow file additions across repositories within 1-hour window. Flag commits with suspicious authorship metadata and generic messages. Cross-reference commit hash patterns for reuse.

suggestion.title: Russian-Hosted Infrastructure for Cyber Operations and Sanctions Evasion
suggestion.rationale: Article reports: 'web hosting company established on Feb. 10, 2022, weeks before Russia invaded Ukraine. The infrastructure was allegedly used to support cyber attacks, disinformation campaigns, and sanctions evasion linked to Russia.' State-actor infrastructure targeting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify infrastructure registered Feb 2022 or later by Russian registrars; correlate with sinkholed C2 domains. Alert on traffic to seized hosting provider ASNs/IP ranges. Monitor for resurrected infrastructure under new domains post-seizure. Track WHOIS/RDAP changes for re-registrations.

suggestion.title: GitHub Security-Policy Account Suspension Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'GitHub Researcher Account Removal' as a key event. Pipeline missed opportunity to detect platform enforcement actions (account suspension, repository takedown) that appear as audit events in GitHub logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when GitHub researcher accounts are suspended or terminated in proximity to public vulnerability disclosure activity. Monitor for rapid state transitions (active to suspended) with audit log entries indicating policy violations.

suggestion.title: Bulk Repository Deletion or Code Removal
suggestion.rationale: GitHub account removal context implies repository deletion or purge. Pipeline missed detection of mass repository state changes, deletions, or access-control modifications following platform policy enforcement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk repository deletions, commit history redaction, or sudden access-permission revocation on suspended researcher accounts. Correlate timing with disclosure incidents to identify enforcement actions.

suggestion.title: Gogs 0-Day Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly describes 'remote code execution' via '0-day vulnerability.' Article body states attackers 'run malicious code on the server remotely'—this is the attack vector. Pipeline identified zero exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP traffic to Gogs instances for requests to known-vulnerable endpoints with suspicious payloads, encoded command syntax, or git-config injection patterns. Baseline normal Gogs API calls and alert on anomalies in request structure or parameter encoding.

suggestion.title: Post-RCE Process Execution on Gogs Service Account
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'run malicious code on the server'—once vulnerability is exploited, attacker executes arbitrary processes. Pipeline missed the execution phase entirely despite this being the impact statement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor child processes spawned from Gogs service accounts (gogs, git, www-data). Alert on shell execution (bash, sh, powershell, cmd.exe), reverse shells, curl/wget downloads, or compression utilities. Baseline normal operations and detect deviation.

suggestion.title: Gogs Repository Integrity Compromise Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: RCE on Gogs enables repo data exfiltration, poisoning, or deletion. Article body unreadable but RCE on Git hosting platform implies repository tampering risk. Pipeline generated no impact-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file modification events on Gogs repositories and hooks directories for non-scheduled changes outside normal deployment windows. Alert on modifications to git hooks, config files, or repository contents by unexpected process/user combinations.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Gogs API Requests with Code Execution Payloads
suggestion.rationale: Title references '0-day' suggesting the vulnerability likely exists in Gogs API handlers. Article body corrupted, but HTTP request inspection is fundamental to catching exploit attempts before execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Gogs API endpoints (/api/v1/*) for requests containing shell metacharacters, template injection syntax, or git command sequences in body/query parameters. Correlate HTTP 4xx/5xx spikes during exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Gogs Malicious Branch Name Injection Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers 'inject the "--exec" flag into git rebase during the "Rebase before merging" merge operation' via 'malicious branch name' in pull requests. This is the core RCE mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Gogs application logs for branch names containing command injection metacharacters (--exec, --, backticks, $(), ||, &&) being created in pull requests. Alert when such branches are merged using rebase merge operations.

suggestion.title: Gogs Account Creation to Repository Exploitation Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'an unauthenticated attacker can simply create an account and repository on any default-configured instance' due to DISABLE_REGISTRATION=false default. Exploitation begins with account creation and immediately proceeds to repository creation and merge operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect account creation followed within minutes by repository creation and pull request merge operations from newly created, low-privilege accounts. Flag if rebase merge is configured immediately after repository creation.

suggestion.title: Gogs Unauthorized Private Repository Access by New Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers can 'read every repository on the instance (including other users' private repos)' after compromising the server.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for newly created Gogs accounts accessing multiple private repositories they were not added to as collaborators. Alert on rapid repository enumeration or cross-project data access by low-privilege accounts.

suggestion.title: Gogs Dangerous Default Configuration Audit
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes prerequisite vulnerability: 'Gogs ships with open registration enabled by default (DISABLE_REGISTRATION = false) and no limit on repository creation (MAX_CREATION_LIMIT = -1)' enabling unauthenticated exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit Gogs instances via configuration inspection for DISABLE_REGISTRATION=false or MAX_CREATION_LIMIT=-1. These settings are prerequisites for the described attack and should trigger remediation alerts.

suggestion.title: Gogs Credential Dumping from Repository Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states compromised servers allow attackers to 'dump credentials (password hashes, API tokens, SSH keys, 2FA secrets)' from accessed repositories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk data extraction operations on repositories after suspicious account access. Alert on accounts reading credential files (.ssh, .env, config.yml) or exporting repository contents in high volume.

suggestion.title: Gogs Repository Code Tampering Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers can 'modify any hosted repository's code' after server compromise, representing repository integrity violation and potential supply chain impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on code commits or merges to critical repositories by newly created accounts or accounts with RCE indicators. Flag commits with unusual authorship, timing, or code patterns deviating from legitimate developer behavior.

suggestion.title: DLL Side-Loading via Trojanized Media Player Installer
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attack execution: 'Launching the EXE triggered a DLL side-loading mechanism, injecting the malicious module into a legitimate program process' with HLS Installer.874.exe as delivery vehicle.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for execution of legitimate media player installers from temp directories immediately followed by DLL loading from mismatched versions or suspicious paths. Flag when process injects code into trusted executable context with timestamps indicating DLL creation post-executable launch.

suggestion.title: SilentCryptoMiner with Embedded RAT Module Multi-Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'the miner based on SilentCryptoMiner gained a RAT module' and describes both components deployed from single infection vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when XMRig or SilentCryptoMiner process (high CPU/GPU utilization, stratum pool connections) co-executes with outbound connections to non-standard ports or suspicious C2 domains within same session. Monitor for registry persistence creation alongside miner service instantiation.

suggestion.title: Fake Media Player Update Lure Injection on Piracy Sites
suggestion.rationale: Attack initiates when 'player displayed a message saying the plugin version was outdated and asking to install an update to continue.' Targets users of illegal streaming/book sites via social engineering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag browser-triggered downloads of ZIP archives from non-standard domains containing paired legitimate executables + unsigned DLLs. Alert on fake update dialogs originating from video playback contexts on piracy domains; monitor for 'HLS Installer' archive downloads with embedded suspicious payloads.

suggestion.title: Malware Distribution via urush1bar4[.]online and IPFS Gateway Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'urush1bar4[.]online' as active distribution domain and 'file[.]ipfs[.]us[.]69[.]mu' as previous source for trojanized ZIP archives containing legitimate + malicious DLL pairs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Block downloads from urush1bar4[.]online and IPFS-gateway domains. Detect ZIP archive downloads where archive structure contains both signed executable and unsigned/suspicious companion DLL. Alert on archive extractions to user temp directories followed by immediate parent executable launch.

suggestion.title: Malicious Persistence Registry Modification via Side-Loaded DLL
suggestion.rationale: Injected DLL 'contained the logic for deploying the miner and establishing persistence on the device' through registry-based auto-start mechanisms triggered from legitimate process context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious registry modifications to Run, RunOnce, or Startup folders when initiated by legitimate media player processes that were recently side-loaded with malicious DLLs. Detect persistence pointing to unsigned binaries, temp paths, or NTFS alternate data streams.

suggestion.title: Piracy Site Malware Injection - Compromised Video Streaming Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'malware was being distributed via illegal movie and TV show streaming sites' targeting tens of millions of visitors on .ru and .top TLD piracy domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify piracy/streaming domains serving malicious update redirects or ZIP downloads. Monitor for users accessing known piracy sites followed by suspicious file downloads or process execution patterns. Alert on plugin exploitation attempts on .ru/.top piracy domains.

suggestion.title: FortiClient EMS Remote Code Execution / Exploit Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states exploit of 'Critical FortiClient EMS Flaw' — zero detection generated for the initial-access vector of the entire attack chain
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiClient EMS service for unexpected HTTP POST/PUT requests to vulnerable endpoints, malformed payloads, or process spawning anomalies following network requests to the EMS port. Correlate with failed authentication events and version fingerprinting attempts.

suggestion.title: Credential Stealer Payload Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes threat actors 'Deploy Credential Stealer' — no execution-phase detection for malware staging, dropped files, or child-process spawning
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected binaries or scripts executed with FortiClient EMS service privileges, suspicious file drops to temp directories (%TEMP%, ProgramData), unsigned DLL loads from non-system paths, or process injection into legitimate processes from the EMS service context.

suggestion.title: In-Memory Credential Harvesting Activity
suggestion.rationale: Attack explicitly delivers 'Credential Stealer' — no credential-access use case generated despite this being core to the attack objective
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on LSASS memory access or credential dumping tools (mimikatz patterns), DPAPI key queries by non-system processes, registry enumeration of credential stores (HKLM\SAM, HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SECURITY), or credential manager vault access post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration over Anomalous C2 Channel
suggestion.rationale: Credential stealer must exfiltrate stolen data — no detection for abnormal outbound connections, encrypted tunnels, or data staging
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for FortiClient EMS and affected client egress patterns. Alert on long-duration TCP connections to rare external IPs, DNS queries for newly registered domains, unusual port usage (non-HTTP/HTTPS), or TLS certificates with suspicious Subject ALN patterns during exfiltration window.

suggestion.title: PIN Input Capture or Social Engineering Preceding Vault Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attack prerequisite is 'One Captured PIN' — this is the initial compromise step before vault unlock. No UC covers detection of PIN extraction vectors (keystroke logging, forced authentication, phishing for PIN).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual input-capture processes (keyloggers, input hooks) executing before Password Manager processes. Detect anomalous authentication failures followed by vault unlock. Flag social engineering campaigns targeting password manager PINs via phishing/forced auth flows.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Password Manager Vault Access After Credential Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Once PIN is captured, attacker gains vault access. Article describes full vault exfiltration following single PIN compromise — need detection for unexpected vault initialization/unlock, especially cross-device.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Password Manager vault unlock attempts with correct credential material immediately after failed authentication sequences. Alert on vault file access from non-standard processes or unusual geolocation/device following PIN compromise.

suggestion.title: Bulk Credential Export or Vault Synchronization to Attacker-Controlled Account
suggestion.rationale: Attack outcome is 'Entire Google Password Manager Vault' stolen — requires wholesale exfiltration. Article provides no detail on exfil mechanism but volume/timing of credential data movement is detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormally large or rapid access to Password Manager credential stores. Detect sync operations to unknown Google accounts or unusual cloud credential uploads. Flag API calls exfiltrating vault metadata or credential counts within seconds of unlock.

suggestion.title: Local Vault Decryption or Memory Dumping for Secrets Extraction
suggestion.rationale: PIN alone does not guarantee plaintext vault; attack implies decryption at rest or memory-resident plaintext access. Article does not explain mechanism but memory-resident or local-file decryption is likely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process memory access to Password Manager by non-package processes. Monitor for suspicious local decryption library calls (crypto APIs). Alert on vault file path access outside normal application contexts.

suggestion.title: Google Chrome Process Abuse or Extension Hijacking for Password Manager Access
suggestion.rationale: Google Password Manager is Chrome-bound; attack may leverage browser extension, process impersonation, or session hijacking. Title does not indicate mechanism, but browser-level compromise is probable attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unsigned Chrome extensions installing or executing alongside Password Manager. Monitor for chrome.exe process spawning vault-access methods or hooking credential APIs. Flag session token theft targeting Google account auth.

suggestion.title: MDM Policy Circumvention via Local Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article title 'What MDM can't protect' directly implies attack vectors to escape MDM control; absence of kill-chain phases on privilege escalation despite topic suggests gap
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes spawning with elevated privileges on macOS/Linux dev machines not typically requiring escalation (npm, git, editor processes). Alert on sudo/doas usage by developer accounts outside expected hours or targeting unexpected binaries.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting from Development Tools
suggestion.rationale: Developer-focused article implies credential access vectors (API keys, git tokens, SSH keys); pipeline empty on credential_access phase
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag reads/exfils of ~/.ssh, ~/.git/config, ~/.aws/credentials, .env files or environment variable dumps targeting credential stores. Monitor for base64-encoded credential patterns in process command lines.

suggestion.title: Malicious Package Installation via Package Managers
suggestion.rationale: Developer machines run npm/pip/brew; article likely covers supply chain or installation vectors; pipeline missed execution-phase detection
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious npm/pip/brew installs not in organization's approved package registries. Alert on package installs with modified checksums, installs during off-hours, or execution of post-install scripts with network/file I/O.

suggestion.title: Evasion of MDM Monitoring via Process Hiding
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly frames MDM limitations; defense_evasion techniques to hide activity from MDM agents are core gap; pipeline never surfaced this
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for kernel modules, rootkits, or process injection frameworks loaded on dev machines. Alert on execution of ptrace, dyld hijacking, or DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES usage on macOS.

suggestion.title: Microsoft Entra Authentication Anomaly Post-Vishing
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'vishing attack that compromised an employee's Microsoft Entra account.' This is explicit initial access. Pipeline generated zero use cases for detecting compromised cloud identity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate employee reports of voice phishing with subsequent Entra authentication anomalies: new geography, new IP, new user-agent, or rapid failed-then-success pattern. Flag any cloud authentication from non-corporate ASN within 6 hours of reported call.

suggestion.title: Bulk Salesforce Record Export by Single Account
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'they used this access to steal 42 million records from the company's Salesforce instance, including consumer and business customer names, email addresses, physical addresses, phone numbers.' Pipeline missed this large-scale collection event.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on single user exporting >10k records in 24h, especially outside business hours or via unfamiliar API calls requesting PII fields in bulk. Correlate with Entra compromise timeline.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Employee Directory Bulk Export
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'A subset of approximately 85k records originating from an internal employee directory also included job titles.' Attackers accessed HR/personnel system; no detection suggested for employee roster theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor directory bulk queries or roster exports. Flag if single account queries >5k employee records in one hour or exports employee lists with timestamps clustering near Salesforce access window.

suggestion.title: Cloud Identity Pivot to SaaS Data Access
suggestion.rationale: Article describes compromise of Entra ID followed by Salesforce access. Pipeline missed lateral movement pattern: compromised identity system → CRM access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect authentication to Microsoft Entra from suspicious context (new country, VPN, proxy, off-hours), then within 1 hour Salesforce access with no historical baseline in 90 days. Correlate risk events across identity and SaaS logs.

suggestion.title: Single Account Multi-System Data Aggregation
suggestion.rationale: Article: one Entra account accessed Salesforce (42M records) + employee directory (85k records) + support ticket data. Pipeline missed account-as-aggregator pattern for mass exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag compromised account accessing 3+ distinct data sources (identity, CRM, HR, ticketing) within 48h with bulk export activity. Calculate data volume vs historical baseline; alert if >1000x typical user behavior.

suggestion.title: Threat Actor Breach Data Publication on Dark Web
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'the cybercrime group leaked the documents stolen from Charter's Salesforce instance on their dark web leak site.' Pipeline missed post-breach dark web publication event.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest threat intelligence feeds monitoring ShinyHunters leak site. Alert when organization's customer/employee emails appear in published dataset. Correlate timing: breach date (early April) to leak publication (late May) to establish exfiltration-to-publication timeline.

suggestion.title: Samba Process Crash or Unexpected Termination Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'Enables Remote Code Execution'—RCE exploits in Samba commonly cause smbd/nmbd daemon crashes (SIGSEGV, buffer overflow signals). Pipeline should have flagged this execution-phase artifact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected termination of smbd or nmbd processes with abnormal exit codes (SIGSEGV, SIGABRT) preceded by inbound SMB traffic spikes on ports 139/445 from external or suspicious sources.

suggestion.title: Exploitation-Pattern SMB Traffic Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates active RCE vulnerability—initial-access phase must involve network-based exploitation attempts. Pipeline should map SMB-based scanning and payload delivery indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag inbound SMB handshakes (ports 139, 445) exhibiting version negotiation mismatches, malformed packet structures, null-byte injection patterns, or buffer-overflow-like payload signatures targeting Samba code.

suggestion.title: Command Execution Under Samba Service Account
suggestion.rationale: RCE definition is arbitrary command execution under vulnerable service context. Pipeline should detect unexpected process spawning from smbd/nmbd with shell interpreters or network file descriptors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when smbd or nmbd spawns child processes invoking bash, sh, perl, or python interpreters, or when these daemons inherit socket file descriptors linked to network connections.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized File Access Post-RCE Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Following successful RCE, attackers enumerate and exfiltrate data via Samba shares. Pipeline should create collection-phase detections for abnormal file access patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal file read/write patterns in Samba-exported directories following process crashes or restarts, particularly reads of sensitive files (/etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, SSH keys, Samba config).

suggestion.title: Samba Binary and Configuration Tampering Detection
suggestion.rationale: Critical vulnerabilities are weaponized with persistence mechanisms. Pipeline should flag unexpected modifications to Samba binaries, configs, and loaded libraries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected file modifications to /etc/samba/smb.conf, smbd/nmbd binaries, or shared objects in /usr/lib/samba/, especially when correlated with exploitation timeframes or process anomalies.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Adobe Document Cloud Domain Access
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'Fake Adobe Document Cloud Pages' — this is the phishing vector. No detection use case exists for users visiting lookalike Adobe domains or downloading from them. Article implies credential harvesting and malware staging.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS queries and HTTP requests to domains with high string-similarity to 'adobe.com' or 'documentcloud.adobe.com'. Alert on file downloads from these suspicious domains, especially if followed by executable creation or process execution.

suggestion.title: ScreenConnect Remote Access Tool Abuse Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names ScreenConnect malware as the payload ('Deliver ScreenConnect Malware'). No use case was generated despite ScreenConnect being a known-abused legitimate RAT tool with distinctive network and process signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on ScreenConnect.Service.exe creation, registry modifications for persistence, or network beacons to known ScreenConnect relay servers. Flag ScreenConnect spawned from unexpected parents (browsers, Office apps, temp directories) as abuse indicator.

suggestion.title: Phishing Delivery Chain: Email to Fake Portal to Malware
suggestion.rationale: Article describes fake pages used to deliver malware — describes complete initial_access → execution chain but pipeline did not reconstruct this kill chain or generate corresponding detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate suspicious domain access (phishing page) with subsequent executable downloads and process spawning. Look for time-window correlation (within minutes) and parent-child process anomalies (explorer.exe or chrome.exe spawning ScreenConnect).

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting Via Fake Adobe Login Portal
suggestion.rationale: Fake Adobe pages imply credential harvesting endpoint. Article establishes credential_access phase as attack objective but no detection use case was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for authentication attempts to legitimate Adobe services immediately following visits to lookalike domains. Flag if source IP or user-agent differs between phishing portal access and subsequent authentic Adobe login.

suggestion.title: HTTPSpy Malware Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article headline states 'Deploys HTTPSpy'—implies active malware execution. Zero detection rules generated despite clear tool name.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTPSpy process creation, DLL injection into HTTP client libraries, and anomalous HTTP proxy traffic patterns. Correlate with Kimsuky C2 infrastructure to confirm malicious execution.

suggestion.title: HelloDoor Backdoor Deployment
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Expands Arsenal with HelloDoor'—named tool explicitly mentioned as new capability. Zero use cases despite clear indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HelloDoor process instantiation, file creation patterns matching known HelloDoor staging, and registry modifications associated with persistence. Correlate with known Kimsuky drop zones.

suggestion.title: VS Code Tunnel Abuse for Command and Control
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'VS Code Tunnels' integration—indicates legitimate tool abuse for C2. No corresponding detection despite clear architectural shift to tunnel-based C2.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual VS Code (code.exe, code-server) process creation with SSH or tunnel-related command-line arguments; monitor for ssh-agent or port-forwarding child processes spawned from VS Code; flag tunnel traffic to external IP ranges from engineering workstations.

suggestion.title: Kimsuky Phishing Campaign Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Kimsuky historically initiates via spear-phishing. Article discusses active campaign deployment. No initial-access use cases despite typical attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for emails matching Kimsuky phishing patterns (spear-phishing URLs, lookalike domains targeting defense/policy verticals). Correlate with payload delivery infrastructure tied to HTTPSpy or HelloDoor staging.

suggestion.title: Kimsuky Tool Ingress and C2 Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Article describes deployment of HTTPSpy and HelloDoor as new toolkit. No ingress-tool or C2-communication detection rules. Critical gap in asset tracking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound connections from compromised endpoints to known Kimsuky C2 domains; monitor for HTTP or HTTPS beaconing patterns from malware families; flag use of non-standard ports for encrypted tunneling.

suggestion.title: Detect Stolen OpenAI Codex Authentication Token Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly describes theft of 'OpenAI Codex Authentication Tokens.' Pipeline produced zero detection use cases for token leakage despite this being the core impact. Must detect credential submission to non-OpenAI endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST requests containing OpenAI API token patterns (sk-*) sent to non-openai.com domains. Correlate with credential-entry forms on non-official domains claiming Codex branding. Flag HTTPS POST to attacker infrastructure immediately post-compromise.

suggestion.title: Detect Legitimate-Looking Phishing UI Serving Fake Codex Login
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'Legitimate-Looking Codex Remote UI' used for credential harvesting. No detection for lookalike Codex login infrastructure was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect domains with Codex branding (codex-*, *codex-*, remote-ui-*) hosted on non-OpenAI infrastructure. Alert on HTTPS certificates issued to suspicious entities claiming Codex UI/remote access. Monitor for high-volume redirects from legitimate links to phishing domains.

suggestion.title: Detect Anomalous API Usage Post-Token Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Stolen Codex tokens would be abused for API calls. No detection for unusual Codex API activity patterns post-compromise was included in pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Codex API authentication logs for tokens accessing from unexpected geographies, unusual timestamps, or spike rates. Flag tokens used across multiple IPs in short windows or making API calls inconsistent with historical user behavior.

suggestion.title: Detect Credential Input on Non-Official Codex Domains
suggestion.rationale: Attack surface is credential harvesting via fake UI. Pipeline generated no detection coverage for form-based credential capture on non-OpenAI domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTPS traffic to non-openai.com domains serving HTML forms requesting OpenAI credentials. Cross-reference against known legitimate Codex UI endpoints. Alert on successful POST submission containing token/credential patterns to attacker-controlled infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Detect Download and Execution of Fake Codex Remote UI Application
suggestion.rationale: 'Remote UI' may be packaged as executable application delivery. Pipeline produced no detection for suspicious application installation related to Codex.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for downloads and execution of applications branded as Codex Remote UI or similar from non-OpenAI sources. Flag unsigned/suspicious-signed executables claiming to be OpenAI tools. Alert on process creation patterns consistent with credential-stealing malware.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Code-Signed Executable with Revoked or Malicious Sectigo Certificate
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states abuse of Sectigo certificate to bypass SmartScreen—code-signing evasion is the primary attack vector. Phrase: 'Abuses Sectigo Certificate to Bypass SmartScreen Warnings'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect executables signed with Sectigo certificates flagged in threat intel as malicious or revoked. Alert on file execution where certificate subject CN matches known-bad thumbprints or is associated with trojanized software. Correlate with file hash reputation.

suggestion.title: RVTools Installer Execution from Untrusted Source or Suspicious Parent
suggestion.rationale: Malicious RVTools installer is the delivery/initial access mechanism. Should detect RVTools execution where parent process, download location, or execution context is anomalous. Phrase: 'Malicious RVTools Installer'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect RVTools installer (e.g., RVTools*.exe, setup.exe) execution from browser temp directory, email attachment folder, or with suspicious parent process (explorer.exe, cmd.exe). Correlate with known-malicious download URLs or domains.

suggestion.title: SmartScreen Bypass or Suppression Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Core evasion: attacker specifically targets SmartScreen bypass using code-signing legitimacy. Should detect registry disablement, warning suppression, or SmartScreen policy changes. Phrase: 'Bypass SmartScreen Warnings'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HKCU or HKLM registry modifications disabling SmartScreen (e.g., SmartScreenEnabled DWORD set to 0). Alert on process execution with SmartScreen bypass CLI flags or suppressions. Baseline expected modifications per application deployment.

suggestion.title: Distribution of Malware Signed with Legitimate Certificate Authority
suggestion.rationale: Threat centers on abuse of Sectigo's legitimate CA to sign malware, trusting users into accepting it. Should detect when Sectigo-signed binaries appear in threat feeds or correlate with C2 beaconing. Phrase: 'Abuses Sectigo Certificate to Bypass SmartScreen Warnings'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest threat intel feeds tagged with 'Sectigo-signed malware' and correlate certificate thumbprint/serial against processes and image loads. Alert on execution of Sectigo-signed binaries that match known-malicious file hashes or trigger multiple AV engines.

suggestion.title: Malicious NuGet Package Download and Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Malicious Sicoob NuGet Steals Banking Credentials' — NuGet packages execute arbitrary code on install; should alert on source reputation, package name alignment with banking software, and child process spawning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor NuGet package downloads and installations from non-default feeds or publishers with low historical downloads. Alert on packages with names mimicking legitimate banking software (Sicoob, bank*, credential*, secret*) and any process spawning immediately post-install with network egress.

suggestion.title: Malicious npm Package Installation with Credential Theft
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'npm Packages Target Cloud Secrets' — npm post-install scripts run with full environment variable access in CI/dev contexts where cloud credentials and API keys are exposed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm installs from non-standard registries or with suspicious post-install script activity. Alert on child processes of npm that enumerate environment variables, access ~/.aws, ~/.azure, ~/gcp directories, or construct JSON/base64 payloads from credential patterns.

suggestion.title: Credential Access via Package Post-Install Environment Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article states packages 'steal banking credentials' and 'target cloud secrets' — npm and NuGet post-install execution contexts have direct access to environment variables and credential files; enumerate and exfiltrate pattern is primary mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor processes spawned by nuget.exe or npm for enumeration of environment (env, printenv, Get-ChildItem Env:), access to credential directories (%APPDATA%\Microsoft\Credentials, .ssh, .aws, .azure), or reads of cloud CLI config files (credentials, config, token).

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of Banking and Cloud Credentials from Development Environments
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates malicious packages steal credentials destined for export; packages execute in build/CI with network access and must beacon C2 with stolen secrets (banking creds, cloud tokens, API keys).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound HTTPS/HTTP from build agents, development machines, or package-manager processes to non-whitelisted external domains, especially with base64-encoded, JSON-serialized, or credential-pattern matching in request payloads (AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, password=, token=).

suggestion.title: Typosquatting or Impersonation of Sicoob Banking Libraries
suggestion.rationale: Article title specifically references 'Sicoob' — a Brazilian bank — indicating malicious packages likely impersonate legitimate Sicoob SDKs, libraries, or closely-named variants to evade detection and social engineer developers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference downloaded NuGet/npm packages against known legitimate banking software and SDKs. Flag new or low-reputation publishers releasing packages with names containing or phonetically similar to 'sicoob', 'banking', 'credential', or legitimate bank SDK names; inspect version history for zero or very low download counts.

suggestion.title: Browser Credential Store Access via Malicious Package
suggestion.rationale: 'Banking credentials' in article title suggests targets include stored browser credentials; malicious packages may access browser password databases, cookies, or autofill data from development machines.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor processes spawned by package managers for access to browser credential stores (Chrome/Edge user data directories, Firefox profiles, Safari keychain). Alert on SQLite queries or direct reads of Login Data, Key*.db, or keychain files.

suggestion.title: HuggingFace API Abuse for Data Exfiltration Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'uses HuggingFace Datasets for stealthy data exfiltration' — the most obvious attack indicator. Pipeline failed to generate any detection logic for this attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTPS POST/PUT requests to huggingface.co/datasets or huggingface.co/api endpoints originating from non-browser, non-SDK processes. Correlate with preceding bulk data reads or unusual credential access. Flag if source process is unsigned or has suspicious attributes.

suggestion.title: MicrosoftSystem64 Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Malware family name 'MicrosoftSystem64' is in the title — pipeline should create process-level detection for execution of this family or variant names.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process creation containing 'MicrosoftSystem64' or obfuscated variants ('System32' impersonation, 'Microsoft*' naming schemes). Alert on parent-child process chains typical of malware injection or dropper patterns.

suggestion.title: Bulk Sensitive Data Access Before Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article describes coordinated 'data exfiltration' implying systematic collection. Pipeline missed the collection phase ('T1005') entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes performing sequential reads of sensitive file categories (PII patterns, credential files, config files) within a short window, followed by network activity to external cloud services. Flag if process SID/token lacks legitimate business context.

suggestion.title: Credential Access for HuggingFace Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Stealthy uploads to HuggingFace require either compromised credentials or stolen API tokens. Article implies coordinated campaign, not random abuse. Pipeline missed credential-access phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DPAPI decryption, LSA secret queries, or browser password store access followed by HuggingFace authentication attempts. Flag attempts using extracted or default credentials.

suggestion.title: Typosquatted npm Package Installation Detected
suggestion.rationale: Article title and description explicitly focus on 'typosquatted npm packages'—the supply-chain entry point. No detection UC generated despite this being the core threat vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install operations for package names with high edit-distance similarity to popular packages (single-character substitutions, transpositions, vowel swaps). Alert on installation of typosquatted variants in CI/CD or development environments, especially from less-trusted sources or with recently-created package metadata.

suggestion.title: npm Post-install Script Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Article describes theft of 'cloud and CI/CD credentials' from developer environments. npm post-install scripts are standard vector for this. No UC covering credential access from package execution context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm-spawned child processes accessing credential stores (~/.aws/credentials, ~/.ssh/id_rsa, .docker/config, .kube/config) or reading credential environment variables (AWS_*, GITHUB_TOKEN, GITLAB_*, GCP_*) during post-install phase.

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration from npm Process Context
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly targets 'steal cloud and CI/CD secrets'—implies exfiltration. Pipeline missed outbound data transfer from malicious npm packages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound HTTPS/DNS traffic from npm processes to domains inconsistent with Node.js registries, CDNs, or legitimate package sources. Flag unusual TLDs, newly-registered domains, or uncommon geography from npm process tree during install/build phases.

suggestion.title: npm Package with Obfuscated Post-install Script
suggestion.rationale: Malicious npm packages conceal credential-theft logic in post-install scripts. Article implies obfuscation in package payloads but pipeline generated no behavioral detection UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect npm post-install scripts for base64, hex, or gzip-encoded shell commands. Alert on high-entropy script content, multiple layers of indirection, or execution of dynamically-fetched shell commands (curl | sh pattern).

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Compromise: npm Registry Deviation
suggestion.rationale: Article fundamentally addresses supply-chain attack via npm typosquatting. No UC for detecting package installation from unofficial registries or registry metadata mismatches.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm install operations with registry fallback to non-official sources, or mismatches between package-lock.json hash and actual installed package. Monitor for private registry proxies serving packages with conflicting metadata.

suggestion.title: Malicious npm Dependency Injection
suggestion.rationale: Typosquatted packages are installed as implicit dependencies or devDependencies. Article context implies dependency confusion but no UC for detecting unexpected transitive dependencies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package.json modifications or npm install for unexpected dependencies matching known typosquat patterns. Alert on installation of packages with names one edit-distance from legitimate high-value packages, or with zero GitHub stars/activity.

suggestion.title: VS Code Process Spawns Unexpected Shell via Remote-SSH
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'VS Code Remote-SSH RCE' — RCE means arbitrary code execution. Pipeline missed detection for abnormal process hierarchy where VS Code (code.exe/code-server) spawns cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or bash outside normal IDE workflows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when VS Code or RemoteExtensionHost spawns interactive shell interpreters with command-line arguments suggesting user input execution, correlated with SSH extension activity.

suggestion.title: SSH Connection Spike from Developer Machine to Cloud IPs
suggestion.rationale: Subtitle: 'Pivot From Developer Machines to Cloud Servers' — describes lateral movement stage. Missing detection for abnormal SSH tunnel establishment from dev workstations to cloud infrastructure immediately post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect SSH connections from dev-class hostnames (dev-, laptop-, workstation-) to AWS/Azure/GCP CIDR blocks within minutes of VS Code RCE indicators on source host.

suggestion.title: SSH Config or Key File Modification by VS Code Process
suggestion.rationale: RCE-to-pivot chain requires persistence: attacker must add SSH keys or modify config. Article implies this attack chain but pipeline surfaced no persistence-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for writes to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys, ~/.ssh/config, or ~/.ssh/id_* outside change-control windows, triggered by execution context chain linking to VS Code RCE activity.

suggestion.title: Remote-SSH Extension Argument Injection in Process Command Line
suggestion.rationale: RCE vectors in SSH-based IDEs typically exploit shell metacharacter handling or argument injection in remote command construction; no detection generated for malicious SSH extension parameters.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan VS Code/ExtensionHost command lines for shell metacharacters ($(), backticks, pipes) in SSH connection arguments or suspicious ExtensionHost flags; compare against baseline Remote-SSH invocation signatures.

suggestion.title: Cloud CLI Tool Invocation Correlated with Dev Machine Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Post-pivot impact requires cloud API/CLI execution (aws-cli, Azure CLI, gcloud). Should detect cloud tooling spawned on compromised developer machine shortly after RCE indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate RCE/SSH indicators on developer host with subsequent aws-cli, az, or gcloud process creation, especially with env-var credential passing or non-standard user execution context.

suggestion.title: Plaintext Credentials in Docker RUN Commands and Environment Variables
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly discusses 'Passing passwords via command arguments' and 'Use of default passwords'—credentials can be extracted from image layers, container metadata, and parent process environment at runtime.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Dockerfile RUN directives and docker run commands for password flags (-p, --password, --secret). Alert on environment variables matching credential patterns (PASSWORD, API_KEY, SECRET, TOKEN, PASSWORD_HASH). Cross-reference image layer metadata against credential regex patterns.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Misconfigured Sudo in Containers
suggestion.rationale: Article section 'Attacks on sudo' and 'Insecure file permissions' highlight sudo NOPASSWD rules and overprivileged capabilities as container-to-host escape primitives.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sudo executions within containers with NOPASSWD sudoers entries. Alert on containers running with CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_SYS_MODULE, or CAP_NET_ADMIN. Monitor for non-root child processes calling getuid(2) repeatedly—sign of privilege boundary testing.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Compromise via Vulnerable or Unsigned Base Images
suggestion.rationale: Article warns 'Software vulnerabilities and compromise of update sources'—base images from Docker Hub often persist outdated libraries and unsigned layers, enabling supply-chain backdoors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate container images by SHA256 and cross-reference against CVE feeds and image signature validation. Flag images pulled from non-approved registries. Alert on image promotion to production without OCI image signature or Docker Content Trust verification.

suggestion.title: Default Credentials Used in Containerized Services
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'Use of default passwords'—containerized databases, SSH services, and web consoles often retain factory credentials, exploitable at scale.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline successful authentication events for containerized services (postgres, mysql, redis, SSH). Alert on logins using common default accounts (admin, root, postgres, mongodb) from external networks. Correlate with container startup events to catch ephemeral instances.

suggestion.title: Lack of Container Layer Integrity Verification at Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article section 'Lack of integrity checks' notes containers frequently run without signature or hash attestation, enabling layer substitution and trojanization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Generate cryptographic baseline of approved container layers. Alert when container startup occurs with layer digest mismatch or missing signature. Monitor for image pull events where Docker Content Trust is disabled or skipped.

suggestion.title: World Cup Phishing Campaign Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article keywords explicitly mention 'phishing' as a threat vector targeting World Cup infrastructure. No phishing use cases were generated despite this being a primary attack method mentioned.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for spearphishing emails and URLs using World Cup lures, official tournament domains, or credential harvesting pages mimicking FIFA/venue ticketing systems. Flag emails with suspicious sender reputation, mismatched domains, or shortened/obfuscated URLs.

suggestion.title: Typosquatting Domain Registration for World Cup Impersonation
suggestion.rationale: Keywords explicitly list 'typosquatting' as a threat vector. No detection use case was created for monitoring typosquatting domains targeting World Cup infrastructure or FIFA entities.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on DNS queries and passive DNS registrations for World Cup typosquatting domains (FIFA variants, official venue domains with character swaps, ticket vendors). Flag registrations by known typosquatting actor infrastructure.

suggestion.title: QR Code-Based Malware Delivery Detection
suggestion.rationale: Keywords mention 'QR Codes' as an attack vector but pipeline generated no use cases for QR code exploitation. Should detect QR code usage in phishing and malware delivery campaigns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor email attachments and URLs containing QR code images or embedded QR data. Alert on QR codes pointing to known malware C2, credential harvesting pages, or suspicious shortened URLs. Cross-reference with World Cup-themed email subjects.

suggestion.title: Wiper Malware Execution Targeting World Cup Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Keywords include 'wiper' malware as a threat but no impact-phase detection use case was generated for wiper deployment or execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect wiper malware execution via suspicious process cmdlines using disk/partition wiping tools (cipher.exe, format, dd), registry modifications targeting boot sectors, or large sequential file deletions. Correlate with lateral movement or persistence indicators in tournament IT environments.

suggestion.title: Accessibility Service Abuse by Non-System Apps
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'it abuses Android Accessibility Services to obtain elevated permissions and additional system access without further user interaction.' This is a high-confidence detection anchor.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag when non-system APKs (especially those from non-Google Play sources) request and receive Accessibility Service permissions. Look for permission grants immediately following suspicious app installation. Cross-reference against known-malicious package names or hash signatures.

suggestion.title: Installation from Non-Official App Store Portals
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'potential victims are redirected to portals mimicking Google Play and prompted to download the fake apps.' This is the primary distribution vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP/HTTPS requests to domains that spoof Google Play (certificate mismatches, lookalike domains, redirects from phishing sites). Correlate with APK installations that follow within minutes. Flag if installation source is not play.google.com or official distributor domains.

suggestion.title: Suspicious APK Permission Combinations for Financial Theft
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'stealing specific data, intercepting financial transactions, capturing screenshots, and remote control capabilities' and customizable permission selection via builder. The combination of SMS/CALL + CAMERA + INTERNET is anomalous for most legitimate apps.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create a rule that flags APK manifests requesting unusual permission combinations: {READ_SMS OR READ_CALL_LOG} + CAMERA + RECORD_AUDIO + ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION + INTERNET. Priority increases if app claims to be a streaming service, crypto miner, or messaging app but requests financial-access permissions.

suggestion.title: Malware Builder Platform Activity (C2 Infrastructure)
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'The APK builder included in the offer provides easy customization' and 'sales are conducted in private Telegram channels' at $700/month. Detecting access to or use of the builder platform by enterprise users is a proxy detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTPS traffic to the BTMOB clearnet site (if domain is known) or Telegram bot interactions that match builder signature (APK customization requests, permission parameter exchange). Detect successful APK downloads followed by rapid re-upload/redistribution patterns.

suggestion.title: Phishing Lure Hosting Infrastructure (Fake Service Domains)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'distributed via phishing websites masquerading as streaming services and cryptocurrency mining platforms' and 'Argentinian government agency as a lure.' Domain registration and hosting patterns cluster.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for domain registrations that mimic legitimate streaming services or government portals using homograph variants or typosquatting. Cross-reference WHOIS changes, certificate issuer patterns, and temporal clustering (multiple registrations in same timeframe). Flag if domain serves APK binaries and has low ASN diversity.

suggestion.title: Financial Transaction Interception Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly notes: 'intercepting financial transactions' as a core capability. Detection requires monitoring for non-standard process injection or activity in banking/payment app sandboxes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for hooking/injection into banking and payment app processes (PayPal, Stripe, local banking apps). Detect if a child process spawns from an APK with Accessibility Services enabled and communicates over unexpected sockets. Look for process memory regions containing known banking APIs or transaction keywords.

suggestion.title: Employee Account Compromise via Social Engineering
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'An unauthorized actor used social engineering to deceive an employee to gain access to a limited portion of the Company's IT system.' Initial access vector is explicit and must trigger phishing/social engineering detection rules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on employee email accounts receiving phishing indicators followed by anomalous login within hours (atypical location, time, device). Correlate email security events with successful logons from the same account within 24-72 hours of social engineering attempt.

suggestion.title: Bulk Data Exfiltration from Compromised Identity
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'illegally copied personal information' and ShinyHunters 'stole documents containing over 8.7 million records with personally identifiable information and terabytes of internal corporate data.' Massive data volume movement should be anomalous.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag single-user accounts executing queries or exports returning >1M rows from customer/loyalty databases, or copying GB/TB-scale data from file shares in a single session. Baseline normal data access volumes per role.

suggestion.title: Mariner Society Loyalty Database Anomalous Access
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'data contained fields indicating it related to the Mariner Society loyalty program' with 'names, dates of birth, genders and data relating to status within the loyalty program.' Application-level detection on loyalty system.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Mariner Society database for unscheduled bulk SELECT operations on customer_pii or similar tables; alert if non-admin account executes queries returning entire customer sets or loyalty tiers in one transaction.

suggestion.title: Extended Dwell Time Indicator (4-Day Access Window)
suggestion.rationale: Article timeline: breach April 10, unauthorized activity detected April 14, determination of data theft April 22. 4-day undetected access suggests insufficient real-time monitoring of new account behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for account access patterns on day 1; trigger alerts within 6 hours if account suddenly accesses systems outside normal role scope. Reduce dwell-time detection SLA to <24 hours.

suggestion.title: ShinyHunters Salesforce Targeting Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'ShinyHunters has been targeting Salesforce customers and has breached hundreds of companies worldwide, claiming to have stolen billions of records in the Salesloft Drift campaign and the Salesforce Aura data theft attacks.' Carnival may use Salesforce; orgs should correlate with Aura breach tooling.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For Salesforce-using organizations: correlate Carnival breach April 10 timeline with known Aura/Drift-campaign email domains or phishing indicators. Monitor for accounts exhibiting Carnival-timeline-concurrent credential reuse or Salesforce API key exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized IT System Lateral Access from Employee Account
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'gained access to a limited portion of the Company's IT system' after social engineering. Access was not to email alone but to backend IT infrastructure, suggesting lateral movement from initial compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect compromised employee accounts accessing IT infrastructure (servers, backup systems, databases) outside normal job function. Flag RDP/SSH connections from employee workstations to data-center IPs, especially if preceded by phishing attempts.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Execution Following Gogs Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes 'authenticated user execute arbitrary code'—authentication is prerequisite for exploit trigger. Pipeline missed detection for execution phase post-login.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag child process spawns (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, sh) originating from Gogs process context (gogs, git-daemon, gitea-equiv binary) or user session within 5 minutes of Gogs authentication log entry. Execution from unexpected parent (web server proc) is high-confidence indicator.

suggestion.title: Code Execution via Git Hooks / Deploy Keys in Gogs
suggestion.rationale: Gogs is Git hosting platform; authenticated RCE likely routes through Git hooks, post-receive scripts, or SSH key abuse. Article doesn't detail mechanism but this is standard Gogs attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for .git/hooks/ file creation or modification within Gogs repository directories, followed by shell invocations. Detect SSH key injection (authorized_keys write) in git user home or Gogs data paths.

suggestion.title: Authenticated User Creates / Modifies Repository Hooks in Gogs
suggestion.rationale: Pre-exploitation indicator: authenticated user must add malicious hook. Article says 'any authenticated user'—this is the setup phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP POST/PUT to /api/v1/repos/{user}/{repo}/hooks or direct filesystem writes to .git/hooks/ subdirectories by non-repo-owner accounts or service accounts, especially with unusual Content-Type or payload size.

suggestion.title: Reverse Shell or Data Exfiltration Post-Gogs RCE
suggestion.rationale: Article title specifies 'execute arbitrary code' but provides no IOCs for post-exploitation C2. Detection should assume attacker opens reverse shell or exfils data after code execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After Gogs process or child execution detected, flag outbound network connections to non-whitelisted external IPs, especially ports 443, 4444, 8888, 9999 or ephemeral ranges. Combine with process lineage (parent=git/gogs daemon).

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation from Gogs Process to System Account
suggestion.rationale: Gogs service typically runs unprivileged; real-world attacks escalate. Article doesn't detail if RCE is unauthenticated-to-admin or privesc is separate, but missing from analysis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process token elevation, sudo invocation, or UAC bypass attempts originating from Gogs process tree. Flag setuid/setgid binary execution (e.g., gpasswd, pkexec) by Gogs user.

suggestion.title: Gogs Admin Account Creation or SSH Key Injection
suggestion.rationale: Authenticated RCE often persists via new admin user or SSH backdoor. Article doesn't mention persistence mechanism; this is critical detection gap for post-compromise hunting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Gogs user/org creation API calls (esp. with admin=true), SSH public key additions to non-user-initiated accounts, and direct database inserts into user tables. Correlate with RCE process execution timestamps.

suggestion.title: npm Supply Chain Malware Injection Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Lazarus...compromised axios lead maintainer's credentials to publish malicious versions...injected trojanized code into affected systems' (100M+ weekly downloads). Pipeline extracted zero supply-chain detection despite explicit exploitation of npm registry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm package installations from unusual sources, detect hash mismatches against published registry, monitor Node.js child process spawning for unexpected network connections, and alert on JavaScript execution loading non-bundled dependencies.

suggestion.title: Ivanti VPN Appliance Exploitation (PhiliKit/UNC5221 SPAWN)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'PhiliKit, new implant assessed part of UNC5221's SPAWN toolset targeting Ivanti VPN appliances.' Pipeline failed to surface any detection for this named vulnerability campaign with specific infrastructure target.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ivanti VPN administrative interfaces for authentication anomalies, unusual privilege escalations, and known CVE exploitation signatures. Detect beaconing to UNC5221 C2 infrastructure post-compromise.

suggestion.title: Bootkit-Style Wiper Deployment Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Rusty Boots and MoKhargosh...demonstrated destructive potential including deployment of bootkit-style wiper and retaining destructive tooling.' Pipeline completely omitted any wiper/bootkit detection rules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unsigned/suspicious driver loading, modifications to boot sector or bootloader registry hives, SYSTEM-context processes targeting disk structures, and attempts to disable recovery mechanisms.

suggestion.title: Rook Ransomware Lateral Propagation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Andariel...attempted to spread Rook ransomware within engineering company.' Pipeline extracted zero ransomware-specific detection despite named family and explicit propagation behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Rook-specific file extensions and encryption patterns, detect file encryption APIs in rapid-fire succession, alert on SMB lateral movement to adjacent systems, and identify ransom note creation and C2 callback patterns.

suggestion.title: TigerRAT Command & Control Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Andariel...deployed TigerRAT...within engineering company.' No detection use cases for TigerRAT beaconing, RAT capabilities (screen capture, exfiltration), or persistence mechanisms were generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on TigerRAT process creation patterns, detect C2 communication via HTTP/HTTPS beaconing, monitor for screen capture and file enumeration APIs, and identify persistence via scheduled tasks or registry run keys.

suggestion.title: North Korean Developer-Targeted Social Engineering
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Lazarus and DeceptiveDevelopment...invested in long-term relationship building...Kimsuky and Konni favored quicker...attacks' targeting 'developers and cryptocurrency ecosystem with social engineering schemes.' Pipeline failed to create detection for phishing/credential-harvesting targeting dev platforms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect phishing emails impersonating cryptocurrency platforms and developer recruitment, flag unusual authentication from compromised developer accounts, monitor GitHub/npm API activity anomalies, and alert on attacker-controlled URLs in developer communities.

suggestion.title: Typosquatted FIFA Domain Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'fake domains impersonate the official fifa.com, but rely on minor spelling changes that users are likely to miss, such as fiffa[.]com, and use alternative top-level domains (e.g., .org, .xyz, .live, .sale)'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS queries and HTTP traffic for domains matching FIFA typosquatting patterns (fiffa, fifa-*, *fifa) with non-standard TLDs (.xyz, .live, .sale, .org). Flag requests from inside the network, especially during World Cup period (June-July 2026).

suggestion.title: Suspicious FIFA Employment Portal Registration
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names: 'fake employment portals like "jobs-fifa[.]com" or "fifa-hiring[.]com"'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on newly registered domains matching jobs-fifa*, fifa-hiring*, or *fifa-careers patterns. Cross-reference WHOIS data for suspicious registrar or privacy proxies. Correlate with known phishing infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Malvertising Campaign Promotion Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'World Cup-related malvertising campaigns promoted through Google Search, Facebook ads, Telegram, and WhatsApp'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious World Cup 2026 ticket, merchandise, or hospitality ad campaigns across Google Ads, Facebook, Telegram, WhatsApp. Flag campaigns linking to non-FIFA domains or newly registered infrastructure. Correlate click-through data to phishing site visits.

suggestion.title: High-Volume Banking Data Form Submissions
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'collect from visitors various types of data, including names, physical and email addresses, phone numbers, banking/payment details, which could be used to create fraudulent accounts, commit identity theft, or run financial scams'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect form submissions collecting multiple PII fields (name, email, phone, address, banking details) on suspicious domains. Alert when legitimate users submit banking information to non-banking sites. Correlate with known phishing domains.

suggestion.title: Ghost Stadium Phishing Infrastructure Clustering
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'A major operation that Group-IB researchers attributed to a Chinese threat actor tracked as Ghost Stadium, uses more than 300 phishing sites, clones of the real FIFA portal'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify clusters of phishing domains using similar SSL certificates, hosting infrastructure, or registration patterns consistent with Ghost Stadium's 300+ site operation. Flag mass domain registrations within FIFA namespace. Cross-reference with Group-IB threat intel.

suggestion.title: Fake Ticket/Merchandise Purchase Funnel Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions: 'Starting in February, Bitdefender observed fraudulent activity...with fake merchandise, kits and collectibles, streaming services, and Panini sticker offers' with geographic targeting

Alert on unusual payment patterns or multiple failed transactions followed by credential changes.

suggestion.title: Recruiter-Impersonation Email Delivery

suggestion.title: macOS Malware Execution from Downloaded Attachment
suggestion.rationale: Article title specifies 'macOS Malware' as the payload, but no execution-phase detection for malware launched from email or browser was suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process spawning from ~/Downloads, /tmp, or /var/tmp within minutes of email attachment interaction. Flag unsigned or revoked code signatures. Monitor for archive extraction (DMG mount, PKG installer) followed by hidden script or binary execution.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency-Industry-Specific Phishing Targeting

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify phishing emails where recruiter lure content is hyper-specific to crypto/DeFi job titles, blockchain technical skills, or crypto compensation discussions. Cross-reference sender domain reputation against whitelisted crypto recruiter services.

suggestion.title: JINX-0164 Actor Infrastructure Tracking

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Workflow Injection — Credential & Secret Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Megalodon supply chain attack...GitHub Actions workflows containing a payload designed to steal credentials, keys, tokens, and other secrets. Workflows were injected through over 5,700 malicious commits pushed...on May 18.' Named campaign with explicit credential theft vector.

Correlate with commits pushed May 18+ timeframe and repo compromises with abnormal star/fork velocity. Alert on workflows reading .git/credentials or invoking curl/wget with output redirection.

suggestion.title: Cloud Credentials Exposed in Public Repository — AWS GovCloud
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'CISA contractor intentionally published AWS GovCloud keys and vast trove of agency secrets on public GitHub account.' Explicit credential exposure incident with AWS service scope.
