suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability specifically leverages ChatGPT's 'web summaries' feature — detection should monitor for abnormal summary request patterns, URL injection attempts, or summarization of phishing/malware domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect burst or sequential ChatGPT API calls to web summary endpoint with URLs pointing to known phishing or attacker-controlled domains. Correlate with downstream email delivery or social-engineering campaigns.

suggestion.title: ChatGPT Output Misuse for Phishing Kit Distribution
suggestion.rationale: If vulnerability generates phishing content or HTML, downstream detection should identify generated phishing kits being persisted or exfiltrated via file shares, pastebin, or email.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on exfiltration of generated phishing templates, HTML payloads, or summary-derived credential harvesting forms from endpoints where ChatGPT integrations are active. Baseline typical ChatGPT output sizes and flag anomalous mass downloads.

suggestion.title: Trusted Relationship Exploitation via ChatGPT
suggestion.rationale: ChatGPT's trusted brand used to bypass email filters or user skepticism — detection focus on ChatGPT-domain or integrations embedding phishing in legitimate-looking summary emails or summaries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify emails delivered with ChatGPT branding, headers, or generated content that route user clicks to attacker infrastructure. Monitor for summaries embedded with malicious links using URL shorteners or lookalike domains.

suggestion.title: Prompt Injection via OpenAI API Keys or OAuth Tokens
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation likely requires API access — detect unusual authentication patterns, token reuse, or lateral movement from compromised ChatGPT API credentials into malicious phishing workflows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for API authentication anomalies (geographic impossibility, rapid location changes, token rotation). Correlate API calls to summary endpoints with downstream phishing campaign telemetry.

suggestion.title: Detect Downloads from Domains Impersonating AI Platform Vendors
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'website at openew[.]app that impersonates OpenAI's desktop application download portal' — trivial IOC and behavioral marker; no detection generated despite clear masquerading intent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag network connections or file downloads from domains matching OpenAI/Claude/ChatGPT naming patterns but with suspicious TLDs or typosquats. Pair with cross-referencing against known-good OpenAI CDNs (cdn.openai.com). Alert on executable downloads from these domains with download behavior inconsistent with legitimate app distribution.

suggestion.title: Detect Executable Downloads Following ChatGPT Share Link Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states threat actors 'published it through a shared chatgpt.com/s/ link' and users downloaded malware after visiting. No detection proposed despite clear browser-to-execution pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequences: web access to chatgpt.com/s/* URLs (shared artifacts) followed within 5 minutes by executable downloads (EXE, MSI, DMG, PKG) with parent process chrome.exe, firefox.exe, or edge.exe. Elevated risk if executable is named with masquerading language (ChatGPT, OpenAI, Claude). Track file hash and raise alert on any execution.

suggestion.title: Detect VM/Sandbox Evasion via System Information Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'executes various commands to determine whether the device is a legitimate computer or a virtual machine' — direct MITRE T1082 execution pattern with no detection proposed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag child processes spawned from unsigned/recent executables (potential malware) that invoke VM/hypervisor detection commands: systeminfo, wmic path Win32_ComputerSystem, Get-WmiObject Win32_ComputerSystem, vboxcontrol, qemu-ga detection, or checks for common VM artifacts (/proc/cpuinfo for kvm, registry queries for vmware/virtualbox). Correlate process creation with recent suspicious download or document open.

suggestion.title: Detect Cloaked Malware URLs via URLScan/Platform Divergence
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'uses cloaking to display content only to targeted victims. When security platforms like URLScan visited the URL, they were shown a harmless AR/VR company website instead.' No detection for cloaking behavior or payload divergence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate URL click/access from employee device with security scanner submissions of the same URL. Flag URLs where scanner returns benign content (AR/VR, generic pages) but employee device downloads binary executable or shows post-compromise behavior (credential access, lateral movement). Cross-reference with Shodan/URLScan public history. Escalate if divergence signature matches known cloaking kits.

suggestion.title: Detect Google Ads Redirection to AI Platform Share Links
suggestion.rationale: Article states threat actors used 'Google ads to direct users searching for ChatGPT to a malicious shared ChatGPT page hosted on chatgpt.com' — attack vector requiring ad-click tracking and landing-page validation. No detection generated despite named attack method.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect network events where referrer is Google Ads domain (google.com/aclk or affiliate tracking) and final destination is legitimate AI platform (chatgpt.com, claude.ai) but URL path is /s/<uncommon-hash> or /s/<low-entropy-string>. Cross-reference artifact URL against known-safe shared prompts/conversations. Alert on artifact access immediately followed by out-of-band file download.

suggestion.title: Detect Infostealer Post-Execution Behavioral Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'earlier campaigns abusing AI platform sharing features have distributed infostealers' and references ClickFix payloads, but no behavioral detection proposed for credential/data harvesting post-execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After execution of unsigned binary from chatgpt/openai impersonation domain, detect infostealer indicators: child processes targeting browser credential stores (Chrome, Firefox, Edge), creation of temporary files in %APPDATA% or %TEMP% matching credential-staging patterns, network connections to non-standard ports (8080, 9090, 443 with non-SSL cert), base64-encoded data exfiltration, or rapid access to system files (SAM hive, LSASS).

suggestion.title: PAN-OS CVE-2026-0257 vulnerability scanner detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability 'allows attackers to bypass security restrictions'—scanner signatures must flag unpatched PAN-OS instances. This is the foundational detection for a CISA KEV entry with active wild exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag any PAN-OS instance unpatched for CVE-2026-0257 via vulnerability scanner or asset discovery. Escalate externally routable management interfaces. Cross-check with network exposure data to identify attack surface.

suggestion.title: PAN-OS authentication bypass on admin interface
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'allows attackers to bypass security restrictions.' Authentication logs should show bypass attempts or unauthenticated successful commands on admin channels.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PAN-OS admin/management logs for successful privilege operations without preceding valid authentication event, authentication state violations, or direct privilege escalation in audit trails.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized VPN session initiation post-exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'establish an unauthorized VPN connection' as the exploitation outcome. VPN logs must show anomalous session creation from unexpected sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on VPN session creation from IPs not in baseline allow-list, outside standard access windows, or from geographies inconsistent with organization. Flag sessions immediately following CVE-2026-0257 exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Failed-then-successful authentication pattern on PAN-OS
suggestion.rationale: Typical bypass exploitation signature: attacker triggers detectable auth failures while probing, then succeeds via exploit. Article mentions 'bypass security restrictions'—this pattern indicates exploitation success.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate 3+ failed authentication attempts on PAN-OS admin interface with successful session establishment from same source within 5-minute window. Flag as high-confidence exploitation indicator.

suggestion.title: PAN-OS management plane network exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article implies public-facing vulnerability. Detect inbound traffic to admin/management ports (SSH 22, HTTPS 443, API 10252) from untrusted network segments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on inbound connections to PAN-OS management interfaces from non-admin network ranges or from internet-routable sources. Baseline typical admin access paths; flag deviations correlating with CVE-2026-0257 scanning/exploitation.

suggestion.title: PAN-OS configuration drift post-exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Once VPN access is established via CVE-2026-0257, attacker will persist by modifying firewall rules, user accounts, or VPN settings. Detection must catch unauthorized config changes on vulnerable instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on firewall rule additions, VPN user account creation, or admin credential changes occurring outside maintenance windows on instances flagged as vulnerable or post-exploitation. Cross-correlate with authentication bypass detections.

suggestion.title: Residential Proxy Client Installation and Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'botnet consisted of at least 17 million infected devices' and 'platform offers corporate, residential, and mobile proxies.' Indicates unauthorized proxy client installation on victim endpoints without knowledge.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect installation of undocumented proxy client software establishing persistence via registry run keys, scheduled tasks, or system services. Monitor for suspicious child processes or DLL injection from proxy client executables. Flag processes with network signatures matching residential proxy client beaconing.

suggestion.title: Proxy Botnet Command and Control Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article: '200 servers used to host the infrastructure were located in the Netherlands' and 'seized several botnet servers from a hosting provider.' These servers directly controlled botnet endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify egress connections to seized server IP ranges in Netherlands hosting provider ASNs. Correlate against threat feeds listing seized infrastructure. Detect DNS lookups or HTTP requests to known Asocks C2 domains. Flag non-standard ports or protocol deviations in proxy client communication patterns.

suggestion.title: Hosting Provider Botnet Infrastructure Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'hosting provider took the botnet offline because it was being used for criminal activities.' Abuse of hosting infrastructure is persistence and operational enablement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor hosting provider ASN/IP ranges for mass C2 server patterns: multiple accounts provisioning servers with identical C2 traffic signatures, rapid iteration of IP addresses, correlation with abuse report clustering, and threat feed blacklisting of provider IP space.

suggestion.title: DDoS Attack Coordination from Distributed Proxy Botnet
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'botnets...used for illegal activities such as distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks.' Coordination of 17M endpoints for synchronized DDoS is measurable attack pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate incoming DDoS traffic with known residential proxy IP ranges and ASNs. Detect synchronized traffic spikes from distributed proxy addresses targeting single victim. Distinguish attack-pattern traffic from normal proxy load-balancing by examining request distribution and timing variance.

suggestion.title: Asocks Malicious Proxy Service IOC Identification
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'linked to a service called Asocks...advertises itself as a universal proxy service with 7 million IP addresses, 150 locations, and 100,000 clients.' Named malicious infrastructure with explicit operational scale.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Extract and blacklist Asocks infrastructure IOCs: known domains, C2 IP ranges, ASNs, client software hashes. Alert on download/execution of Asocks client binaries on non-proxy-designated systems. Cross-reference internal detections against public Asocks infrastructure lists and resold proxy IP feeds.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Mining Resource Hijacking via Proxy Botnet
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'botnets...used for illegal activities such as...cryptocurrency mining.' 17M-device botnet directed toward mining represents quantifiable compute resource hijacking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor proxy client hosts for anomalous sustained CPU/GPU load, memory pressure, and outbound traffic to mining pools. Detect execution of mining-specific processes (xmrig, xmr-stak) or monero pool communication (stratum protocol, port 3333). Flag child process creation anomalies under proxy client parent process.

suggestion.title: HTTP POST/PUT request body containing vm2 prototype pollution payload
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'By combining `Buffer.call.call({}.__lookupGetter__, Buffer, "__proto__")` ... allows the escape' — exploit is delivered via HTTP request body to vulnerable vm2 application.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound HTTP requests (POST/PUT to Node.js endpoints) for patterns indicating vm2 exploitation: Buffer prototype-chain access (__proto__, __lookupGetter__, __lookupSetter__) combined with Function/constructor references. Elevated confidence if payload appears after vm2 import detected in application code.

suggestion.title: Node.js process loading vm2/NodeVM followed by Object prototype pollution operations
suggestion.rationale: Article shows exploit requires vm2 library be loaded then chains `Buffer.call.call` operations — detect library import + suspicious prototype chain access at application instrumentation level.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Node.js process with (a) require('vm2') or NodeVM instantiation, then (b) subsequent __proto__/__lookupGetter__/__lookupSetter__ property access on Buffer or Object prototype within same process context. Time window: <5sec between require and access.

suggestion.title: TypeError constructor leak from sandbox context (ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE exploitation)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Node.js's ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE Error, the host's TypeError constructor can be obtained' — this is the critical escape moment and may leave detectable error traces.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for JavaScript error stack traces originating from vm2 sandbox context showing TypeError constructor resolution or ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE patterns combined with __proto__ chain access. Compare error context (sandboxed frame) against constructor origin (host frame).

suggestion.title: Process privilege/capability change after vm2 sandbox escape
suggestion.rationale: Article states exploit 'allows attackers to run arbitrary code' — successful escape would permit Node process to access host-level resources or spawn shells with elevated context not normally available to sandboxed code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Node.js process spawning child processes (shells, system utilities) with file-system or network access to paths/resources outside normal vm2 sandbox scope. Baseline legitimate vm2 app capabilities first; look for capability expansion after suspicious Error/prototype chain activity.

suggestion.title: vm2 module/NodeVM instantiation in public-facing HTTP endpoint handler
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exploit via 'Exploit Public-Facing Application' (T1190) — suggests vulnerable vm2 is reachable from external HTTP layer. Identify where vm2 is being instantiated in request handlers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Code-level detection: find vm2/NodeVM require() and new VM() calls within HTTP request handler chains (Express routes, API endpoints, middleware). High-risk: vm2 code instantiation in handler that accepts user input (request body, params, headers).

suggestion.title: vm2 package downgrade or version manipulation post-exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability in versions <=3.11.3. Attacker may downgrade to vulnerable version or tamper with package-lock.json/node_modules after gaining code execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected changes to vm2 version in package.json or package-lock.json (downgrade to <=3.11.3), or direct manipulation of node_modules/vm2 files. Correlate with Node process restart or npm install commands.

suggestion.title: Node.js spawning OS shell with reconnaissance commands
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes post-exploitation phase: 'Processes.parent_process_name="node.exe" OR Processes.parent_process_name="node"... FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe",...) ... Processes.process="*whoami*" OR Processes.process="*id*" ... OR Processes.process="*cat /etc*"'. This is the execution phase after sandbox escape succeeds.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect OS shell binaries (cmd.exe, powershell, bash, sh) spawned directly from node/node.exe parent. Cross-reference against enumeration command indicators (whoami, id, hostname, /etc/passwd). High-signal pattern for vm2 sandbox escape.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable vm2 package detection (<=3.11.3)
suggestion.rationale: Article hunt UC_5_3 establishes surface: 'Filesystem.file_path="*\\node_modules\\vm2\\package.json" OR ... "*/node_modules/vm2/lib/nodevm.js"'. Covers discovery/exposure assessment phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for vm2 package.json or nodevm.js file presence/modification in node_modules. Correlate against version metadata to identify unpatched installations. High false-positive rate in development environments; filter to production servers.

suggestion.title: vm2 NodeVM initialization with nesting:true and undefined require option
suggestion.rationale: Article core vulnerability: 'strict equality (options.require === false)... bypassed by omitting the require option... When require is not specified, options.require is undefined, not false.' Direct detection of the bypassed security check.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: If available: log or SIEM integration for vm2 NodeVM instantiation. Search for instances with nesting:true where require option is absent or undefined. Requires app-level instrumentation; this pattern is difficult to detect at OS level without behavioral signals.

suggestion.title: NodeVM process builtin access — denylist bypass exploitation attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'process and inspector/promises. Both can be used from sandboxed code to reach host-side execution primitives.' Pipeline should create dedicated detection for require('process') or getBuiltinModule('process') calls within NodeVM context, not just string matching in command line.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Node.js processes loading or referencing the 'process' builtin via require() or inspector/promises during execution. This represents the active exploitation step where sandboxed code attempts to break out of the NodeVM sandbox. Would require code/memory inspection or module loading telemetry if available.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable NodeVM dependency in application codebase — asset discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vm2/NodeVM as a library with a denylist bypass vulnerability. Organizations should inventory which applications and services have vm2 as a transitive or direct dependency. Article states vulnerability allows 'sandboxed code to bypass the intended builtin restrictions' implying vm2 is often embedded in larger applications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all systems and services where vm2 or NodeVM is installed as a package dependency, regardless of version. This establishes asset exposure baseline. Query package managers, SCA tools, and software inventory for vm2 presence. Prioritize public-facing applications and those accepting user-supplied code for sandboxing.

suggestion.title: Code execution via inspector/promises module — post-sandbox escape behavioral detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically names 'inspector/promises' as a denylist bypass vector distinct from 'process'. Inspector module is Node.js diagnostic tool. Article: 'the denylist misses...inspector/promises'. Should have dedicated detection for this specific module access pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Node.js processes instantiating or calling into the 'inspector' or 'inspector/promises' modules from within a NodeVM sandbox context. This represents the inspector-specific exploitation path. Can be detected via command-line inspection for require('inspector/promises') patterns or module loading telemetry if available via EDR.

suggestion.title: Code submission to vm2 service with Promise manipulation patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attackers to write code which can escape from VM2 sandbox'—no detection covers the INITIAL ATTACK VECTOR. Code with Promise.species, constructor chains, or Symbol introspection submitted via vm2.run() or sandbox entry point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor vm2 sandbox entry points (vm2.VM(), vm2.run() calls) for code containing: Promise subclass definitions, Symbol.species getters, constructor.constructor chains, Function.prototype manipulation, mainModule.require chains. High-fidelity when correlated with subsequent child_process spawn from node.exe (UC_6_2).

suggestion.title: Privilege escalation from node.exe post vm2 escape (integrity level jump)
suggestion.rationale: UC_6_2 detects child process spawn but not privilege escalation. Article implies 'arbitrary commands on host'—unprivileged Node.js should not spawn elevated shells. Missing: integrity-level and admin-context transitions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate node.exe parent→cmd.exe/powershell.exe child with integrity-level jump: initiating process (MEDIUM) spawning child (HIGH/SYSTEM). OR non-admin node.exe process suddenly writing to System32, registry HKLM, or accessing privileged resources post-escape.

suggestion.title: Failed resetPromiseSpecies sanitation bypass (Promise.species gadget chain)
suggestion.rationale: Article core technical detail: 'missing a call to resetPromiseSpecies to ensure that this has no special species.' No detection exists for the EXPLOITATION MECHANISM ITSELF—malicious code defining custom Promise.species inside vm2.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Promise prototype pollution inside vm2 VM context: Promise[Symbol.species] getter definitions, thenable object chains, Promise constructor callbacks that inspect 'this' without reset, or any code path that exploits deferred resetPromiseSpecies() call.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-47208 vulnerability present in software inventory (asset exposure)
suggestion.rationale: No detection for vulnerable package in deployment/CMDB. Article CVE is primary IOC but pipeline extracted zero IOCs. Need inventory-based detection mapping vm2 package version to vulnerability window.
log_sources: Software inventory (SCCM, ServiceNow, cloud asset inventory)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate endpoint software inventory records showing vm2 presence with vulnerability bulletin (version ≤3.11.3, patched 2025-06-15). Flag deployments that have not updated past patch version or lack deployment logs confirming patch application.

suggestion.title: Node.js with JSPI-enabling flags spawning shell — CVE-2026-47210 pre/post-exploit correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'when untrusted code is executed with async support on runtimes exposing WebAssembly JSPI.' Exploitation requires explicit runtime flag (--experimental-wasm-jspi) enabling the vulnerability; successful exploit immediately spawns shell.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Node.js spawned with --experimental-wasm-jspi or --expose-wasm flags that subsequently spawns shell/LOLBin within 3–5 seconds. Correlation of suspicious flag + immediate post-exploitation behavior is high-confidence indicator of active exploitation.

suggestion.title: vm2 module instantiation with anomalous Promise/async stack traces — CVE-2026-47210 exploitation signature
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Promise can reach Promise.prototype.finally() in a way that bypasses the expected Promise-species hardening.' Exploit path induces Promise-method interception or unusual Promise constructor chains; detectable via unhandled async exceptions or Promise-tampering in vm2 runtime logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: vm2 child process terminating with UnhandledPromiseRejection or showing Promise.prototype modifications in call stacks indicates exploitation attempt. Correlate anomalous async-call depth or recursive Promise construction with successful shell escape.

suggestion.title: vm2 module downgrade or forced pinning to vulnerable version — CVE-2026-47210 persistence/evasion
suggestion.rationale: Article provides patch (vm2 >3.11.3 safe). Post-exploitation or pre-attack setup may involve deliberate downgrade to re-enable vulnerability for persistence or lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm uninstall followed by npm install vm2@<3.11.3 or package.json edits pinning vm2 to vulnerable version. Suspicious if initiated by non-developer account or outside maintenance windows. Strong signal when preceded by vulnerability remediation.

suggestion.title: Adobe Document Cloud Impersonation Domain Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'fake Adobe Document Cloud pages' as delivery vector. Pipeline missed initial-access phishing entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to domains closely matching documentcloud.adobe.com or Adobe typosquats. Flag newly-registered domains (<30 days) with Adobe branding in SSL certificate or WHOIS. Alert on user clicks from email links pointing to these domains, especially with credential-entry forms.

suggestion.title: ScreenConnect Malware Process Execution from Suspicious Location
suggestion.rationale: Article describes ScreenConnect delivery but pipeline skipped execution-phase detection. ScreenConnect spawning from TEMP, Downloads, or email attachment paths is anomalous.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on ScreenConnect.exe, scrcpy.exe, or variants executing from non-program-files paths (TEMP, AppData\Local\Temp, Downloads). Cross-reference execution timestamp with recent user downloads or email attachment extraction. Flag if parent is browser, Office app, or script interpreter.

suggestion.title: ScreenConnect Outbound C2 Connection
suggestion.rationale: ScreenConnect is a commercial RMM tool repurposed as malware. Pipeline did not suggest detection for abnormal C2 beaconing or non-standard port usage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from ScreenConnect processes to unknown/high-risk IP blocks or C2 domains. Alert on ScreenConnect using ports 8080, 8443, or other non-standard HTTPS ports. Detect registry/scheduled-task persistence mechanisms for ScreenConnect process auto-start.

suggestion.title: Credential Entry on Fake Adobe Form
suggestion.rationale: Impersonation pages imply credential-harvesting objective. Pipeline did not suggest monitoring for suspicious credential submission on Adobe lookalike domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST requests from user to Adobe-like domains with high domain-name distance (Levenshtein/edit distance >2 from adobe.com). Monitor for credential-submission patterns (form-encoded username/password). Correlate with failed login attempts to internal systems hours after fake-site access.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email with Adobe Branding and Download Link
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates social-engineering campaign delivery mechanism. Pipeline skipped email-based phishing detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag emails impersonating adobe.com or Document Cloud support with sender-domain spoofing or lookalike addresses. Detect links to malicious domains in email body. Alert on newly-registered domains (<14 days) linked from phishing emails. Block attachments or URLs known to distribute ScreenConnect.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Video Player Update Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article core attack vector is 'Fake Video Player Updates'—the delivery mechanism for malware. Pipeline should have generated detection for impersonated update executables. No existing UC covers spotting fake updates or non-standard update mechanisms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for executables with video player update naming patterns (*update*.exe, *setup*.exe, *player*.exe) executed from download, temp, or AppData directories, or launched by browser/email. Alert on processes lacking valid code signatures or with mismatched file metadata. Flag parent-child chains where update executables spawn unknown children.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Miner Detection by Sustained Resource Consumption
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly deploys 'miner' malware. Pipeline should detect CPU-intensive processes from suspicious sources. No existing UC addresses resource-hijacking patterns typical of cryptominers—sustained CPU >50% with minimal user interaction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify processes consuming sustained high CPU (>50% for 10+ minutes) spawned from downloads/temp/update executables. Correlate with outbound network connections to pool domains, loading of mining libraries, or CUDA initialization.

suggestion.title: Remote Access Trojan C2 Beaconing Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article names RAT (Remote Access Trojan) as deployed payload. Pipeline generated zero detections for RAT command-and-control, beaconing, or lateral movement infrastructure. This is a critical gap for a RAT campaign.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound connections from suspicious processes to known RAT C2 infrastructure or anomalous destinations (non-standard ports, newly registered domains, low-reputation IPs). Correlate with parent process being fake update executable. Alert on repeated DNS queries or connection retries characteristic of beaconing.

suggestion.title: Malware Persistence via Scheduled Tasks or Registry
suggestion.rationale: Both miner and RAT require persistence across reboots. Article does not specify mechanism, but typical persistence leverages scheduled tasks (T1053.005) or registry run keys (T1547.001). Pipeline should have generated these even without explicit article mentions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for new scheduled tasks or HKLM/HKCU Run registry modifications created by or referencing files from download/temp directories. Flag tasks with obfuscated commands, unusual scheduling, or creation by non-admin processes. Correlate timestamps with malware execution.

suggestion.title: Impersonated Software Publisher Detection
suggestion.rationale: Attack impersonates legitimate video player vendors (VLC, WMP, etc.). Pipeline should have extracted vendor names and created detection for PE metadata mismatches, unsigned binaries claiming to be from legitimate publishers, or files from unauthorized domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify executables with version strings, copyright claims, or filenames impersonating known video player vendors, sourced from non-official domains or lacking valid digital signatures. Validate against known legitimate publisher hashes. Alert on downloads of impersonated software from email, messaging, or sharing platforms.

suggestion.title: LinkedIn Phishing → Malware Execution Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states LinkedIn social engineering vector to deploy custom macOS malware. No use case exists to detect pre-compromise reconnaissance on LinkedIn or post-click malware execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect phishing attempts originating from or impersonating LinkedIn profiles that deliver malware links. Monitor for rapid profile creation, LinkedIn post interaction patterns preceding malware delivery, or malicious links hosted on legitimate CDNs with LinkedIn-like referrers.

suggestion.title: macOS Malware Execution Post-Social Engineering Click
suggestion.rationale: Custom macOS malware deployment mentioned as delivery payload. Article lacks detection for the execution phase after user interaction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect macOS process creation from browser download directories (~/Downloads, ~/Desktop) executed immediately after user opens a phishing link. Look for parent process being browser with suspicious command-line arguments or script execution via /bin/bash, /usr/bin/python, osascript.

suggestion.title: macOS Malware Persistence via LaunchAgent or Cron
suggestion.rationale: Custom malware implies persistence mechanism. Article title does not specify persistence TTPs; pipeline should infer common macOS persistence patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ~/Library/LaunchAgents, ~/.launchd, /var/db/launchd.db, and crontab modifications for new entries created at time of malware execution. Cross-reference with process lineage from initial download or execution event.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Code Signing or Notarization Evasion (macOS)
suggestion.rationale: Custom macOS malware requires execution permission model bypass. Article suggests evasion; no detection for code-signing bypass or notarization spoofing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect macOS processes executed from unsigned binaries or with invalid/missing code signatures. Flag processes where spctl (System Policy Control) status check would fail. Monitor for attempts to bypass Gatekeeper via xattr or quarantine-flag removal.

suggestion.title: Custom macOS Malware Beaconing to C2
suggestion.rationale: Article implies custom malware; no use case captures C2 communication patterns specific to post-exploitation macOS behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious outbound HTTPS or DNS queries from malware process (identified via lineage from initial execution). Look for repeated connections to newly registered domains, high-entropy subdomains, or uncommon TLDs. Monitor for DNS queries to multiple subdomains under same parent domain in short timeframe.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Sudo or AuthorizationDB on macOS
suggestion.rationale: Custom malware often escalates privileges. Article lacks detection for macOS-specific priv-esc techniques following initial execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for sudo execution from malware process without prior user prompt, or modification to /etc/sudoers, /var/db/sudoers.d, or AuthorizationDB (security.plist). Flag attempts to add or modify entries granting passwordless execution.

suggestion.title: Kimsuky HTTPSpy C2 HTTPS Protocol Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'HTTPSpy' tool deployed by Kimsuky — protocol-level C2 beaconing signature absent. Should detect HTTPS C2 patterns specific to this tool.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTPS traffic to known Kimsuky HTTPSpy C2 domains with anomalous certificate issuer patterns or JA3/TLS fingerprints consistent with this malware family. Detect unexpected HTTPS sessions from non-browser processes to infrastructure not matching legitimate CDNs.

suggestion.title: HelloDoor Tunneling Tool Child Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'HelloDoor' tunneling tool expansion — no process execution detection for tunnel instantiation captured.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of HelloDoor samples or process parents spawning tunnel processes with command-line parameters indicative of proxy configuration (listening ports, backend server config). Monitor for abnormal parent-child process relationships (e.g., Office/browser spawning tunnel services).

suggestion.title: VS Code Remote Tunneling Abuse Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article headline specifies 'VS Code Tunnels' as new Kimsuky technique — no detection for legitimate tunneling tool abuse (T1021.005 Remote Access Software).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for VS Code tunnel daemon (code-server, tunnel service) spawned without user login context or running under SYSTEM/unexpected accounts. Detect tunnel sessions with atypical geographic origin, time-of-day anomalies, or tunneled connections to internal infrastructure from external origin IPs.

suggestion.title: Kimsuky Reconnaissance via System/File Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Kimsuky campaign context (article body truncated but title signals APT espionage) — no detection for post-compromise reconnaissance phase typical of this actor.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inline PowerShell/cmd discovery commands (systeminfo, ipconfig, dir, findstr, tasklist, net user) spawned from HTTPSpy or HelloDoor parent processes. Alert on batch enumeration of %APPDATA%, %PROGRAMFILES%, network shares within 5min window.

suggestion.title: Kimsuky Tooling Arsenal Install/Load Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'Expands Arsenal' with multiple tools — no behavioral detection for staged delivery or simultaneous tool orchestration (HelloDoor + HTTPSpy + VS Code) loading.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file creation/registry writes for multiple Kimsuky toolnames within single parent session or 10min window. Alert on obfuscated filenames (temp directories, fake extensions) containing 'httpspy', 'hellodoor', or vscode tunnel indicators. Monitor for staged download patterns from C2 followed by sequential tool launches.

suggestion.title: Kimsuky C2 Callback Chain Reconstruction
suggestion.rationale: Empty kill chain reconstruction in pipeline output — no multi-step C2 callback pattern detection across initial compromise to full toolkit staging.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate DNS queries + TLS handshake patterns + HTTP/HTTPS callbacks to identify complete C2 chain. First callback fetches HelloDoor + HTTPSpy. Detect sequential tool C2 phases: initial beacon (likely minimal footprint), tool download (HTTPS traffic spike), tool C2 (HTTPSpy protocol), tunnel setup (non-standard ports).

suggestion.title: Credential Access: Fake Codex UI Token Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'Legitimate-Looking Codex Remote UI Steals OpenAI Codex Authentication Tokens' — core attack is credential theft via UI spoofing. Pipeline missed entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process execution mimicking OpenAI Codex or VS Code Copilot. Look for suspicious outbound HTTPS connections to non-OpenAI domains immediately following authentication UI interaction. Alert on clipboard exfiltration or browser automation APIs in non-browser contexts.

suggestion.title: Credential Access: API Token Exfiltration to Attacker Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Stolen tokens must be transmitted to attacker. Article describes 'steals...tokens' implying C2 callback. No exfiltration signals generated by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline legitimate OpenAI Codex token usage patterns. Alert on token requests from unexpected geolocations, suspicious user agents, or to non-standard API endpoints. Monitor for tokens appearing in unauthorized HTTP headers or POST bodies.

suggestion.title: Initial Access: Distribution of Malicious Codex UI Clone
suggestion.rationale: Article title implies user is tricked into running 'Legitimate-Looking' malicious UI. Attack vector (phishing, malicious download, compromised package repo) not analyzed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify download/execution of Codex UI from untrusted sources (suspicious domains, GitHub forks with typo names, npm packages with version squatting). Look for suspicious GitHub raw URLs or self-signed certificate errors in TLS handshakes when connecting to fake Codex services.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion: UI Spoofing to Bypass User Authentication Skepticism
suggestion.rationale: Threat specifically named 'Legitimate-Looking' — the evasion IS the attack. Needs detection for UI that mimics OpenAI branding/layout.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for browser plugins or injected scripts that overlay legitimate OpenAI domain with fake login forms. Flag CSS/HTML modifications that clone OpenAI Codex UI on unexpected domains. Alert on self-signed certs presented with OpenAI branding.

suggestion.title: Suspicious NuGet Package Installation from Non-Standard Source
suggestion.rationale: Article describes malicious NuGet package spoofing legitimate Sicoob SDK; pipeline should detect installation of unsigned or suspicious packages. Title phrase: 'Malicious NuGet Package as Sicoob SDK'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for nuget.exe or dotnet.exe downloading packages from non-Microsoft repositories with typosquatting/spoofing of legitimate banking SDKs. Alert on installation of packages with low download counts from unknown publishers matching banking infrastructure names.

suggestion.title: Banking Credential Exfiltration from NuGet-Loaded Assembly
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Exfiltrates Banking Passwords'; should detect credential theft post-execution. Missing detection for in-memory credential access or registry keylogging tied to SDK execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes spawned by NuGet-installed assemblies attempting access to credential storage (DPAPI, LSA, browser password vaults). Monitor for keylogging or clipboard reads from banking applications linked to suspicious .NET assemblies.

suggestion.title: Command and Control Communication from NuGet SDK Process
suggestion.rationale: Credential exfiltration implies C2 callback; pipeline failed to reconstruct or detect exfiltration communication. Article describes password stealing with no stated delivery method for exfil.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound HTTPS/HTTP connections from processes loading the malicious NuGet DLL to unknown or newly-registered domains. Monitor for DNS queries to C2 infrastructure from development/build environments using the compromised SDK.

suggestion.title: Registry Persistence by NuGet-Sourced Assembly
suggestion.rationale: Banking trojans often establish persistence; no UC suggests detection of registry hooks, startup folders, or scheduled tasks installed by the SDK. Article mentions password exfiltration but not persistence mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for modifications to HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\Software\Microsoft\Windows\Run or credential provider registry hives by processes spawned during NuGet package load. Alert on scheduled task creation tied to NuGet cache directories.

suggestion.title: Execution of Obfuscated .NET Code from Package Cache
suggestion.rationale: Malicious SDK suggests obfuscated/reflective loading; no UC for detecting suspicious CLR/JIT behavior or unpacking. Title indicates code is disguised as legitimate SDK.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unsigned or suspicious .NET assemblies loaded from %USERPROFILE%\.nuget\packages or Visual Studio build caches. Monitor for CLR JIT compilation anomalies or reflection-based type instantiation from unknown assemblies.

suggestion.title: Malicious Package Installation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly references 'malicious Sicoob NuGet' and 'npm Packages' — supply-chain compromise is the primary attack vector. Pipeline extracted zero package indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor NuGet and npm package manager invocations (nuget.exe, npm.exe, dotnet package restore) for suspicious package downloads. Flag installations of packages with names matching typosquatting patterns (Sicoob-adjacent names) or from untrusted sources. Correlate with process execution of installation scripts.

suggestion.title: Banking Credential Access & Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'Steals Banking Credentials' — pipeline missed credential access phase entirely. Should detect enumeration of banking software and credential stores.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process execution of banking software (Sicoob applications, browser credential stores) by non-standard parents, memory reads against banking apps, or filesystem access to credential caches. Flag unusual registry queries for saved passwords or certificates.

suggestion.title: Cloud Credential Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Title mentions 'npm Packages Target Cloud Secrets' — exfiltration of cloud credentials (AWS, Azure, GCP keys) should be detected but pipeline returned no use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for reads of common cloud credential paths (~/.aws/credentials, AZURE_CREDENTIALS_FILE, GCP service account JSON) by package manager processes or their child processes. Detect network exfiltration to non-standard C2 domains immediately after credential access.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm/NuGet Script Execution
suggestion.rationale: Malicious packages typically execute scripts during installation (npm install hooks, NuGet .nupkg post-install). No execution-phase detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag execution of powershell.exe, cmd.exe, or bash spawned from npm.exe or nuget.exe context without user interaction. Monitor npm lifecycle scripts (preinstall, postinstall, prepare) for suspicious patterns (credential access, network calls, file exfiltration).

suggestion.title: Package Metadata Anomaly — Name Similarity to Known Brands
suggestion.rationale: Sicoob is a specific target (Brazilian cooperative bank). Pipeline should detect and alert on package names resembling legitimate financial software or banking libraries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package registries (NuGet, npm) for packages with names similar to banking software, Sicoob, or common financial tools. Alert on any installation of such packages. Use Levenshtein distance or regex to catch typosquatting variants.

suggestion.title: ChatGPT API Abuse for Phishing Payload Generation
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly describes 'Attackers Turn Web Pages Into Phishing Payloads' — pipeline should detect abnormal ChatGPT API or chat patterns generating credential-harvesting HTML, transformed web content, or phishing templates.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag ChatGPT conversations or API calls requesting HTML/CSS/JavaScript payloads for page cloning, credential forms, or social-engineering templates. Correlate with suspicious outbound deliveries of generated content.

suggestion.title: Phishing Link to Transformed Web Content
suggestion.rationale: Attack surface is 'Web Pages Into Phishing Payloads' — requires detection of emails or social channels distributing links to suspiciously-transformed web pages impersonating legitimate services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect phishing links pointing to newly-registered or newly-hosting domains that serve web pages resembling legitimate services. Cross-correlate with ChatGPT-rendered HTML fingerprints or CSS patterns indicative of AI-generated phishing content.

suggestion.title: Credential Form Harvesting via AI-Generated Phishing Page
suggestion.rationale: Phishing payloads described in article would target credential theft — detection must cover forms embedded in AI-transformed pages requesting authentication or sensitive identity information.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify embedded login forms or credential-collection fields on suspicious or newly-hosted web pages. Correlate with email gateways and external communication channels for distribution of these phishing links.

suggestion.title: Anomalous ChatGPT Session or Plugin Token Usage
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is ChatGPT-specific; requires monitoring of API tokens, authenticated sessions, or plugins exhibiting unusual behavior indicative of compromise or weaponization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag API tokens with unusual content-generation patterns (high volume, repeated phishing-payload requests, geographic anomalies, or unusual plugin activity). Alert on tokens used for mass delivery of transformed web pages.

suggestion.title: Web Page Cloning or CSS-Injection Attack Surface
suggestion.rationale: Article core attack is transforming 'Web Pages Into Phishing Payloads' — implies CSS manipulation and page rendering abuse. Detection should cover suspicious requests for web-rendering or CSS-transformation services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for requests to web-rendering APIs, CSS injection endpoints, or page-cloning services. Detect unusual CSS patterns or JavaScript injection attempts that could be used to transform legitimate pages for phishing.

suggestion.title: SYSTEM Scheduled Task Creation for Ransomware Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Ransomware Uses SYSTEM Scheduled Task'—this is the primary attack vector and pipeline missed it entirely. Scheduled task creation as SYSTEM is a signature escalation+persistence pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for schtasks.exe or PowerShell New-ScheduledTask execution with /ru SYSTEM or -User SYSTEM flags, especially when spawned from unexpected parent processes or user contexts (WebShell, SQL Server, Exchange). Look for tasks with suspicious binary paths or script blocks referencing file encryption libraries.

suggestion.title: File Encryption Spike with Elevated Process Context
suggestion.rationale: Title states ransomware 'Encrypt[s] Local Drives'—T1486 is the impact technique but pipeline omitted it. Elevated (SYSTEM) encryption is high-confidence indicator of ransomware vs. legitimate tools.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file create/write operations with SYSTEM context targeting multiple file extensions sequentially (*.doc, *.xls, *.pdf, etc.) within short time windows on mounted drives. Baseline should exclude system maintenance tasks; ransomware typically hits user shares first.

suggestion.title: Scheduled Task Execution of Unknown Binary with File Operations
suggestion.rationale: Article describes ransomware executing via scheduled task—this is execution + impact chaining. Pipeline did not reconstruct this sequence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate scheduled task creation (EventID 4698) followed within seconds/minutes by process creation from that task's binary path, combined with high-volume file modification events. Alert if the scheduled binary is not whitelisted and is not in System32 or Program Files.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation to SYSTEM via Task Scheduler Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly describes privilege elevation mechanism ('With Elevated Privileges'). Pipeline missed T1548 family techniques that enable this escalation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for schtasks.exe modifications to existing tasks or new task creation where /ru parameter specifies SYSTEM or LocalSystem, sourced from non-elevated parent process. Include detection for task creation by service accounts (SQL, Exchange) that do not normally create schedulable work.

suggestion.title: Ransomware File Extension Targeting Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article context indicates multi-file encryption of local drives. Pipeline should have suggested detection for ransomware-typical file-extension targeting behavior as secondary indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file rename or encryption (write to temp + rename pattern) involving multiple document/media extensions within short time window, especially on C:, D: drives or network shares. Combine with process execution from unusual location or with unusual parent process.

suggestion.title: Typosquatted npm Package Installation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Typosquatted npm Packages Steal Cloud and CI/CD Secrets' — installation of lookalike package names is the initial access vector; no UC covers dependency confusion or malicious package source detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm install operations for packages with edit-distance similarity to known legitimate libraries (lodash-utils vs lodash, request-api vs request-promise). Monitor registry source metadata mismatches and unexpected package author changes.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting from npm Post-Install Scripts
suggestion.rationale: Article states packages 'Steal Cloud and CI/CD Secrets From Developer Systems' — post-install hooks execute with developer environment access. No UC detects credential file reads or environment variable exfiltration within npm context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm post-install child processes reading ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.ssh/id_rsa, $GITHUB_TOKEN, $GITLAB_CI_JOB_TOKEN, $AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, or similar secret storage. Alert on environment variable enumeration (env, printenv) during package installation.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration from Compromised npm Process
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'Steal' — implies credential exfiltration to attacker infrastructure. No UC covers outbound C2 communication or credential transmission from npm/node.js processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP(S) POST/PUT from npm/node.js processes during install phase containing base64-encoded credentials, AWS key patterns, or token formats. Monitor DNS queries to non-standard domains from npm contexts.

suggestion.title: Secret Enumeration in CI/CD Environment Variables
suggestion.rationale: Article highlights 'CI/CD Secrets' as targets — malicious packages in CI agents inherit CI-specific credentials (GITHUB_TOKEN, CIRCLECI_TOKEN, AWS_ROLE_ARN). No UC detects reconnaissance of CI environment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect enumeration of CI-specific environment variables by npm/node processes; flag listing operations targeting .git, .ssh, .aws directories or commands like 'env | grep -i token'.

suggestion.title: Persistence via npm Package Sideloading
suggestion.rationale: Malicious npm packages may implant backdoors or credential-stealing payloads persisting beyond install. No UC covers file writes to startup locations (.bashrc, cron, launchd) during package installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file writes to ~/.bash_profile, ~/.bashrc, ~/.zshrc, ~/Library/LaunchAgents, /etc/cron.d during npm install; alert on writes to non-standard directories outside node_modules with executable bits set.

suggestion.title: npm Dependency Version Pinning Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Typosquatting exploits package resolution logic; article implies trojanized packages. No UC detects malicious version resolution or package.json integrity violations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm package.json and package-lock.json modifications; alert on version mismatches between declared and installed packages, or unexpected resolution of ambiguous dependency names to untrusted sources.

suggestion.title: npm Package Name Typosquatting Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'typosquatted npm packages'—pipeline must detect package installations with names that are homoglyphs or minor typos of legitimate dependencies, especially from new/unvetted publishers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install operations and package-lock.json for additions where package name matches legitimate names via typo patterns (single-char transposition, common misspellings, homoglyphs). Flag when installed from unfamiliar npm publisher and first-seen in environment.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Postinstall Script Execution
suggestion.rationale: Malicious npm packages execute via postinstall hooks—alert on npm spawning shells, curl, or network tools during package installation phases outside normal build tool behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm/node processes spawning /bin/sh, /bin/bash, curl, wget, or nc during package installation. Flag unexpected outbound HTTPS/HTTP from postinstall context. Baseline legitimate tool vendors (build frameworks, transpilers) to reduce false positives.

suggestion.title: Credential Access from Build Environment
suggestion.rationale: Article core threat: 'steal cloud and CI/CD secrets'—detection must surface file/env reads of AWS_* tokens, GitHub PAT, AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET, or ~/.aws/credentials by npm-spawned processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when npm/node child-processes read .aws/credentials, .ssh/id_rsa, .docker/config.json, or call env/printenv/Get-ChildItem in CI/CD runner context. Correlate suspicious file read + network exfil within short timeframe.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of Cloud Credentials via HTTPS
suggestion.rationale: Attack chain completes with stolen secrets sent to attacker infrastructure—detection for outbound POSTs from build agents with base64-encoded or JSON credential payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTPS POST/PUT from CI/CD agent IPs to non-approved external domains with payload containing base64 strings or key=value patterns matching AWS key format, GitHub token patterns, or Azure credential structure. Exclude known artifact repos (npm, artifactory).

suggestion.title: Process Lineage Anomaly: npm Spawning Network Tools
suggestion.rationale: Credential exfil requires network I/O; detect parent-child relationship of npm spawning curl, wget, or Invoke-WebRequest with unrecognized arguments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for npm/node parent spawning curl/wget with -d, -X POST, -H headers, or -o flags; or PowerShell parent spawning Invoke-WebRequest in build runner context. Alert on unusual external IP or domain targets.

suggestion.title: npm Registry Configuration Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attack may include npm config redirects to attacker-controlled registries—detect registry URL changes or .npmrc modifications in CI/CD configs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm config set registry commands or .npmrc file modifications pointing to non-standard registries. Correlate with unexpected package installs and unknown registry C2 IPs in subsequent network traffic.

suggestion.title: Plaintext Credential Exposure in Container Startup Arguments
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Passing passwords via command arguments' as vulnerability. Detectable via process argument inspection against keyword patterns (password=, token=, secret=, passwd=).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor docker run/exec and container process invocations for plaintext secrets in arguments. Match patterns like password=, token=, aws_secret_access_key= in command-line telemetry. Correlate with credential manager/vault logs to confirm exposure.

suggestion.title: Default Account Authentication to Container Services
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'Use of default passwords' as primary misconfiguration. Detect login attempts with hardcoded defaults (root/root, admin/admin, admin/password) against containerized services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful or repeated authentication attempts using known default credential pairs against container services. Prioritize external source IPs or unusual access times.

suggestion.title: Sudo Privilege Escalation Within Container Runtime
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly covers 'Attacks on sudo' and 'Privilege escalation in the container' as exploitation techniques. Detect sudo invocations with NOPASSWD config or unusual escalation chains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sudo execution with elevated privileges inside containers, especially NOPASSWD entries or privilege transitions from non-root to root. Flag repeated sudo failures followed by success.

suggestion.title: Insecure File Permissions Enable Local Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'Insecure file permissions' and 'Lack of integrity checks' as exploitable container misconfigurations. World-writable SUID binaries and setuid scripts enable escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan container image layers for world-writable SUID binaries, setuid scripts, and writable system directories. Alert on runtime modification of permissions on critical files or privilege-escalation vectors.

suggestion.title: Container Escape to Host Filesystem
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'escape the container, compromising the entire enterprise network' as end-state impact. Detect privileged syscalls, host volume mounts, or process manipulations attempting breakout.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for privileged syscalls (ptrace, mount, bpf, reboot_syscall) from container context, container-to-host volume mounts, or child processes spawned with host filesystem access from container runtime.

suggestion.title: Malicious or Vulnerable Container Image Deployment
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'compromise of update sources' and Docker Hub images containing 'outdated and vulnerable software versions.' Detect deployment of images with high-severity CVEs or untrusted registries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on container image pulls from untrusted registries, images with known critical CVEs (CVSS ≥8.0), unsigned images, or unexpected image sources. Correlate image digest against threat intel feeds for supply-chain IoCs.

suggestion.title: Phishing Campaign Against World Cup Infrastructure Targets
suggestion.rationale: Keywords explicitly reference 'phishing' in context of 2026 World Cup attack surface; article discusses threat actors targeting critical infrastructure surrounding major event.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails with World Cup-themed subject lines or sender addresses spoofing event organizers, particularly those containing malicious links or attachments. Correlate with phishing framework detections (Phish.ai, URLhaus) and look for credential theft indicators in subsequent access logs.

suggestion.title: Typosquatting Domain Registration and Hosting
suggestion.rationale: Keywords explicitly flag 'typosquatting' as attack vector; 2026 World Cup domains and FIFA-related sites are high-value targets for lookalike registration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for domain registrations with one-character swaps, homoglyph variants, or subdomain spoofs of official World Cup infrastructure (FIFA.org, tournament-specific domains). Flag SSL certificates issued for lookalike domains, and correlate DNS queries to these domains with credential submission patterns.

suggestion.title: QR Code-Based Malware Distribution
suggestion.rationale: Keywords specifically mention 'QR Codes' as attack method; commonly used in large-event scenarios (tickets, merchandise, venues) for initial infection vectors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of URLs decoded from QR codes that resolve to known malware hosting, phishing sites, or newly registered infrastructure. Monitor for scanning events followed by immediate browser navigation to suspicious domains, and alert on QR codes embedded in spoof merchandise or venue signage.

suggestion.title: Wiper Malware Deployment Against Event Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Keywords explicitly include 'wiper' as threat category; consistent with destructive attacks on high-profile events by state-aligned and hacktivist groups.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process execution of known wiper families (WhiskeyBravo, WhiskeyAlfa, etc.) or behavior patterns: rapid file deletion, MBR/partition table overwrites, system shutdown commands. Monitor for suspicious disk I/O patterns and correlate with preceding lateral movement or privilege escalation.

suggestion.title: Credential Access via Event-Themed Pretexting
suggestion.rationale: Article addresses 'Attack Surface' of World Cup; attackers use event ticketing, volunteer accounts, and venue access credentials as high-value targets for credential harvesting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect multiple failed login attempts on World Cup-affiliated accounts (volunteer portals, vendor systems, ticketing platforms) followed by successful authentication from new IP ranges. Flag account creation patterns associated with event roles (security, logistics, broadcasting) and monitor for credential modification by third parties.

suggestion.title: Multi-Stage Attack Chain: Threat Actor TTPs Across World Cup Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Four distinct threat actors mentioned (Fiddling Scorpius, Fighting Ursa, Muddled Libra, Razing Ursa); kill-chain analysis missing entirely despite multiple attack phases implied across phishing → execution → impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Construct kill-chain signatures for each named threat actor's observed infrastructure (C2 domains, ASNs, hosting providers). Alert on beaconing patterns to known/suspected actor infrastructure, especially from systems with World Cup-related data or roles. Cross-reference with WHOIS/passive DNS telemetry for infrastructure pivoting.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Accessibility Service Enablement by App
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'abuses Android Accessibility Services to obtain elevated permissions and additional system access without further user interaction'—core privilege escalation mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag when non-system applications request or enable AccessibilityService permission, especially those associated with phishing campaigns or installed from non-Play Store sources. Correlate with anomalous app-list changes or permissions suddenly granted after installation.

suggestion.title: APK Installation from Phishing-Mimicked Google Play Domain
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Malicious apps on fake Google Play sites' and 'potential victims are redirected to portals mimicking Google Play and prompted to download the fake apps'—initial access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect APK downloads from domains containing 'play.google' variations or look-alike registrations (typosquatting). Correlate with phishing lure campaigns (Argentinian government agency mentioned) and downstream Accessibility permission requests.

suggestion.title: Disabling Google Play Protect or Play Services
suggestion.rationale: Article notes customers 'can select... disable Google Play' as a configurable feature—direct defense evasion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on attempts to disable, uninstall, or modify Google Play Services or Play Protect via shell commands or app-level calls. Cross-reference with recently installed or sideloaded applications.

suggestion.title: Launcher Icon Hiding for Evasion
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'hide its icon to make it more difficult to remove from the device' as a configurable payload option.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect modifications to app manifest (android:visible=false) or removal of launcher shortcuts post-installation. Flag applications where package exists but no launcher entry found.

suggestion.title: Interception of Financial Transactions
suggestion.rationale: Malware 'intercepting financial transactions' is listed as core capability; requires detection of Man-in-the-Browser or certificate-pinning bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for SSL/TLS certificate pinning bypass attempts, redirection of banking app traffic, or hooking of financial app processes. Correlate with suspicious Accessibility Service use for credential harvesting.

suggestion.title: Bulk Screenshot Capture by Untrusted App
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 'capturing screenshots' as a primary data collection feature without user visibility.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag repeated screenshot API calls (Android ScreenCapture) by apps not in system allowlist, especially correlated with Accessibility Service enablement or credential entry moments.

suggestion.title: Gogs Process Child Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes RCE capability ('Execute Arbitrary Code'). Attackers exploiting this would spawn children from Gogs service process; no detection use case generated despite this being the most obvious execution artifact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes spawned by Gogs service account with unexpected parent-child relationships or command lines. Gogs running git-related child processes with shell interpreters (bash, sh, cmd.exe) outside normal git operations warrants investigation. Correlate with authentication logs to identify post-login RCE patterns.

suggestion.title: Authenticated User Followed by Privilege Escalation (Gogs)
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability requires valid authentication ('Any Authenticated User'). Detection should chain successful auth to subsequent execution with elevated privileges, but no such UC exists.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful Gogs logins (HTTP 200 on /user/login) with subsequent process execution running as root, NT_AUTHORITY\SYSTEM, or service-escalated accounts. Identify suspicious time deltas (< 5 seconds between auth and unexpected execution).

suggestion.title: Git Repository Code Injection via Gogs RCE
suggestion.rationale: Gogs is a Git service; RCE exploitation would likely manipulate repositories or hooks. Article does not detail this, but kill-chain should include repository tampering. No UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for git hook files (.git/hooks/*) or repository metadata modified immediately after Gogs RCE exploitation attempts. Detect pre-receive or post-receive hooks with embedded shell commands or suspicious interpreter invocation. Cross-reference with process execution logs for hook execution.

suggestion.title: Gogs HTTP Request Anomalies (RCE Payload Indicators)
suggestion.rationale: Article title indicates code execution, suggesting HTTP request payloads contain executable code. No web-application detection use case generated despite HTTP being Gogs's primary interface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect HTTP POST/PUT requests to Gogs endpoints (e.g., /repo/create, /wiki/*, /release/*) for embedded shell metacharacters (backticks, $(cmd), pipes, semicolons) or suspicious encoding sequences. Flag authenticated users sending requests with uncommon User-Agents or rapid request sequencing post-login.

suggestion.title: Outbound Connections from Gogs Process (C2 Exfiltration)
suggestion.rationale: RCE allows arbitrary code execution; attackers would establish reverse shells or C2. No network-based detection UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Gogs process (gogs or git service) initiating outbound TCP/UDP to non-standard ports (not git 22/9418 or HTTP 80/443) from the service account. Detect long-lived connections or connection attempts to known C2 domains/IPs post-RCE exploitation.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Credential Access from Developer Tool Processes
suggestion.rationale: Article title establishes 'secrets exfiltration' via 'trusted tooling'—attackers must first steal credentials. Must detect reads of .ssh, .netrc, ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.docker/config.json, IDE keystore files by developer tools.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on non-standard process access to credential files (.ssh/*, .netrc, maven settings, package manager auth tokens). Focus on developer tools (git, Maven, npm, gradle, curl, wget) or IDE child processes reading secrets. Add context: file copy, encoding, or upload to external service elevates severity.

suggestion.title: Repository Bulk Export or Archive Operations
suggestion.rationale: 'Source code exfiltration' requires detecting when attackers dump entire Git repositories or codebase archives. Pipeline must watch for git-archive, git-bundle, or recursive clone operations with unusual data volume.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Git command-line or IDE Git UI for git archive, git clone (especially with --mirror or --bare), or repository export. Detect when one user/service clones multiple internal repos in rapid succession. Correlate with large data transfers to external endpoints.

suggestion.title: Malicious IDE Plugin Installation from Untrusted Sources
suggestion.rationale: Abuse of 'trusted developer tooling' often begins with rogue IDE plugins (VS Code extensions, IntelliJ plugins). Must detect unsigned or unofficial plugin downloads/installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor IDE plugin installation directories for unsigned plugins or installations from non-official repos (not VSCode marketplace, not JetBrains official repo). Flag IDE processes fetching plugins over HTTP (not HTTPS) or from known malware C2 domains.

suggestion.title: CI/CD Pipeline Artifact Exfiltration to External Storage
suggestion.rationale: Developer 'tooling' includes CI/CD systems (Jenkins, GitHub Actions, GitLab CI). Attackers abuse these to export build artifacts, binaries, or logs to personal cloud buckets or C2.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect CI/CD job outputs (artifacts, logs, compiled binaries) uploaded to unauthorized cloud storage (personal S3/GCS/Azure, external FTP, Telegram/Discord webhooks, pastebin). Flag CI/CD systems making outbound connections to known C2 infrastructure or data exfiltration services.

suggestion.title: Developer Tool Process with Anomalous Network Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Compromised or malicious developer tools may establish persistent C2 communication. Must detect known-clean tools (git, Java, npm, curl) establishing outbound C2 connections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when developer tool processes (git, java, npm, maven, gradle, node) make outbound HTTPS/DNS connections to known C2 domains, suspicious IPs, or internal exfil services. Establish baseline of normal external endpoints these tools contact and flag outliers.

suggestion.title: LLM Agent Command Execution via Marimo Session
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Attackers Use LLM Agent for Post-Exploitation'—pipeline missed opportunity to detect when an LLM or automated agent invokes shell commands or system calls within a Marimo/Jupyter context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process execution spawned from Marimo or Jupyter Python environments with suspicious command patterns (curl, wget, base64 decoding, reverse shells). Correlate with unusual LLM library calls or imports of subprocess/os modules in notebook cells or runtime logs.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Automation Loop Detection
suggestion.rationale: LLM Agents typically execute in loops—article mentions post-exploitation use case but pipeline missed detection for repeated automated actions or self-modifying agent behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid sequences of commands or API calls initiated from a single compromised Marimo session, or evidence of the agent writing and executing new scripts. Look for iterative file creation, deletion, and re-execution patterns consistent with an agent's reasoning loop.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-39987 Marimo Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly names CVE-2026-39987 as the initial attack vector, but pipeline extracted no CVE IOC or detection rule for exploitation activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to Marimo endpoints with payloads matching known CVE-2026-39987 exploitation patterns (likely notebook deserialization, code injection, or configuration file tampering). Baseline expected Marimo operations and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: LLM Agent Token/Model Misuse Detection
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation via LLM Agent implies the attacker either controls an API endpoint, injected a prompt, or compromised model credentials—pipeline missed credential-access and privilege-escalation implications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor LLM API logs (OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.) for unusual model calls, excessive token consumption, or requests from unexpected source IPs. Correlate with Marimo session logs to identify if the notebook environment has been compromised to exfiltrate or misuse API credentials.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Python Library Imports in Marimo
suggestion.rationale: LLM agents commonly import libraries for system interaction (subprocess, os, socket, requests). Pipeline missed detection for behavioral indicators of agent-driven execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Python import statements and sys.modules within Marimo notebooks for known agent-driver libraries or sudden introduction of subprocess/socket/requests in previously clean sessions. Cross-correlate with process creation events.

suggestion.title: Vishing-Compromised Cloud Account: Anomalous Entra Login Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'breached the company's systems on April 1 in a voice phishing (vishing) attack that compromised an employee's Microsoft Entra account.' Must detect Entra logins from new geography, unusual time-of-day, or device post-phishing campaign.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Microsoft Entra logins from atypical geolocations or outside normal user hours, especially within 24–48 hours of internal vishing reports. Correlate user phishing-report timestamps with subsequent authentication anomalies.

suggestion.title: Salesforce Bulk Data Export by Compromised Cloud Account
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'used this access to steal 42 million records from the company's Salesforce instance.' Detect abnormal Salesforce API access, export requests, or data downloads by the compromised Entra identity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Salesforce data exports and API calls for abnormal volume/scope by a single identity, especially bulk queries returning customer PII, CPNI, or support ticket data. Flag accounts transitioning from normal use to export-heavy patterns within days of cloud account compromise.

suggestion.title: Cross-SaaS Lateral Movement After Entra Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article: attacker compromised Entra, then immediately pivoted to Salesforce. Detect rapid lateral movement from identity platform to high-value SaaS apps by one compromised account.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Entra anomalies with subsequent access to downstream SaaS systems. Flag same-user activities where authentication pattern shifts from normal to unusual, followed by privileged or bulk-data operations within hours.

suggestion.title: Ransomware Extortion Communication Channel Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'threat actors claimed... ShinyHunters extortion gang... demanded by ShinyHunters to have the stolen data returned.' Detect outbound communications to attacker-controlled channels or dark web sites.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound HTTPS/DNS to known ShinyHunters dark web leak site domains, ransom note delivery domains, or Tor gateway IPs. Flag emails from attacker-controlled addresses demanding ransom or threatening data release.

suggestion.title: Salesforce Permission Escalation Within Compromised Account
suggestion.rationale: Article: threat actors extracted 4.9M–42M records including CPNI. Likely required privilege escalation or role modification within Salesforce to access restricted customer/CPNI data.
