suggestion.rationale: Article: attackers 'used this access' (Entra account) to 'steal 42 million records from...Salesforce'—lateral movement from identity provider to SaaS application requires cross-platform correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Entra sign-ins from risky/impossible-travel locations immediately preceding Salesforce OAuth grants or API authentication. Flag when identity performs data access (record exports, API pagination) inconsistent with role or outside business hours.

suggestion.title: Large-scale data exfiltration over web service to attacker infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article: attackers 'leaked the documents stolen from Charter's Salesforce instance on their dark web leak site'—exfiltration of stolen enterprise data to attacker-controlled infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for encrypted tunnels or web connections from compromised identity with large byte transfers (multi-GB of data). Flag attempts to reach Tor exit nodes or anomalous HTTPS SNI patterns. Correlate with Salesforce data access patterns in preceding hours.

suggestion.title: Threat-actor leak site enumeration and attribution
suggestion.rationale: Article: ShinyHunters 'claimed responsibility' and posted data to 'their dark web leak site'—visibility into threat-actor operational patterns and victim data exposure requires proactive leak site monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Automated scanning of ShinyHunters leak site and associated channels for presence of Charter customer records. Alert on new leak posts containing customer PII (names, emails, phone numbers, addresses). Index leaked data schema and sample records against HIBP for victim notification prioritization.

suggestion.title: Ransomware/extortion group operational attribution via communication artifacts
suggestion.rationale: Article describes ShinyHunters 'told BleepingComputer that they breached' and demanded ransom—extortion communications contain threat-actor operational TTPs and signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse ransom notes, extortion emails, dark web leak-site posts for linguistic markers, ransom demand structures, and victim-specific metadata. Correlate with known ShinyHunters communication patterns (formatting, payment instructions, public disclosure timelines). Flag rapid progression from breach to extortion demand (<72h) as signature of this group.

suggestion.title: Phishing URL Injection into ChatGPT Web Summaries
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'ChatGPT Web Summaries Into a Phishing Surface'—clear indication of injection-based phishing delivery. No use cases were generated despite this explicit attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious URLs or HTML injection payloads embedded in ChatGPT API responses and web summary outputs. Monitor for user clicks on ChatGPT-originating links to known phishing/credential-harvest domains. Alert on obfuscated URLs within ChatGPT context.

suggestion.title: ChatGPT Web Summary Endpoint Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability-specific attack requires detection of malicious payloads targeting the web summary feature. No technical attack reconstruction or API-level indicators were extracted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify payloads in ChatGPT API requests attempting HTML/JavaScript/URL injection into summary endpoints. Alert on error responses indicative of exploitation probing. Detect API rate anomalies or repeated malformed requests to summary feature.

suggestion.title: Credential Capture Following ChatGPT Phishing Click
suggestion.rationale: Phishing attack chain logically progresses to credential harvesting; pipeline did not model downstream collection/impact phases or establish secondary indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate ChatGPT access with subsequent traffic to spoofed login pages or credential-capture infrastructure. Alert on failed login attempts or anomalous geographic logins post-phishing interaction. Monitor for browser credential-store access after ChatGPT context shift.

suggestion.title: Malicious Installer Download from Spoofed Portal Domain
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'offers both macOS and Windows downloads that install malware' from cloaked site 'impersonates OpenAI's desktop application download portal.' Delivery mechanism and file execution must be detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for .exe/.dmg executables downloaded from domains impersonating legitimate software vendors (openai, anthropic, etc.) that do not resolve to official infrastructure. Correlate with subsequent installer execution from %TEMP% or %DOWNLOADS%.

suggestion.title: VM Detection Execution from Recently Downloaded Executables
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'executes various commands to determine whether the device is a legitimate computer or a virtual machine.' Malware performs defense evasion checks post-execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious process execution patterns typical of VM detection (WMI queries for guest OS, registry reads for Hyper-V/VMware artifacts, CPUID execution, /proc/cpuinfo parsing) spawned from recently-downloaded installers or from %TEMP% directories.

suggestion.title: Cloaked Malware Distribution Site Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'site uses cloaking to display content only to targeted victims. When security platforms like URLScan visited the URL, they were shown a harmless AR/VR company website instead.' Differential content delivery based on User-Agent or context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound HTTPS requests to suspicious domains that serve executable payloads only to non-security User-Agents (not Googlebot, URLScan, curl, etc.). Use threat intelligence on openew[.]app and pattern-match similar domain registration (registered post-campaign date, domains impersonating SaaS vendors).

suggestion.title: Malicious Content Download from AI Platform Share Links
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector: 'malicious shared ChatGPT page hosted on chatgpt.com' and 'Claude Artifacts...to host ClickFix-style lures.' Users execute or download content from legitimate platform share URLs that host attacker payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file downloads initiated from chatgpt.com/s/* or claude.ai artifact share URLs (legitimate domains, but abused as hosting). Flag executable or script downloads from these links. Cross-reference with execution events on downloaded files.

suggestion.title: Google Ads Redirect to Malicious Share URL Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'uses Google ads to direct users searching for ChatGPT to a malicious shared ChatGPT page hosted on chatgpt.com.' Attacker leverages legitimate ad network to seed credential harvesting and malware distribution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for click chains: Google Ads domain → redirect via goog\.xxx → landing on chatgpt\.com/s/* with unusual query parameters or path indicators. Correlate with searches for 'ChatGPT download' or 'ChatGPT outage' and check for fake outage messaging in rendered page.

suggestion.title: Fake Software Outage Message Rendering Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: Attackers created 'fake outage notice...rendered through ChatGPT itself' claiming 'website is temporarily unavailable' to drive users to malicious download. Social engineering vector embedded in legitimate platform.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outage or service-status lures served from legitimate AI platform share URLs (chatgpt.com/s/, claude.ai/artifacts). Signature match on phrases like 'temporarily unavailable,' 'high traffic,' combined with 'download desktop app' CTA. Flag if subsequent network activity includes downloads from non-official domains.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized VPN Connection Establishment Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'establish an unauthorized VPN connection' as the attack outcome. Pipeline missed the lateral-movement/impact detection entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor VPN gateway logs for connection attempts immediately following failed or suspicious auth events on PAN-OS. Look for new or anomalous source IPs establishing VPN tunnels, particularly if correlated with CVE-2026-0257 scanner hits or auth-bypass signatures.

suggestion.title: Authentication Bypass Attempts Against PAN-OS
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability is 'authentication bypass' per article. No detection for malformed or unauthenticated requests attempting to establish admin/service sessions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PAN-OS authentication logs for failed login attempts followed by successful session establishment without credential submission, or HTTP 401/403 responses followed by successful requests to restricted endpoints. Flag if source IP is external or non-whitelisted.

suggestion.title: Unpatched PAN-OS Instance Inventory Check
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies federal due-date 2026-06-01 and emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer'. Asset-exposure hunt template is referenced but no specific UC for vulnerability scanning CVE-2026-0257.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference vulnerability scan results for CVE-2026-0257 against PAN-OS device inventory. Flag any instance running affected PAN-OS versions without documented patches applied before 2026-06-01 due date.

suggestion.title: PAN-OS External Exposure Discovery
suggestion.rationale: T1190 (Exploit Public-Facing Application) is the mapped technique; pipeline should surface detection for externally-reachable PAN-OS management interfaces or services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify PAN-OS management ports (443, 8081, 10.x admin interfaces) reachable from internet-facing network boundaries. Correlate with open-port scan results and threat-intel feeds. Priortize instances without WAF or VPN-gating.

suggestion.title: Botnet C2 Communication Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: '200 servers used to host the infrastructure' controlling '17 million infected devices to carry out cyberattacks.' No detection logic for outbound C2 patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag devices establishing persistent outbound connections to infrastructure IP sets with C2 behavioral traits: small set of destination IPs, non-standard ports, regular beacon intervals. Correlate residential/IoT device networks with known proxy infrastructure. Alert on mass connection initiation from single command vector.

suggestion.title: Default Credential Exploitation on Network Interfaces
suggestion.rationale: Article mitigation: 'ensure the default credentials have been changed to something unique and strong'—implying initial compromise vector was unchanged defaults on network devices.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor successful logins using known default credential pairs (admin/admin, root/123456, etc.) on routers, NAS, and IoT admin interfaces. Alert on rapid failed-then-succeeded attempts on non-standard admin ports. Cross-reference successful default-cred logins with subsequent suspicious process execution or network behavior.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Residential Proxy Egress Traffic
suggestion.rationale: Article: Asocks provides 'residential and mobile proxies'—botnet exploits consumer IP ranges for DDoS and malicious proxying. 'Companies, tablets, and smartphones' were commandeered for 'cyberattacks.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect consumer ISP-ranged IPs with unusual egress volume, connection velocity, or targeting patterns (same-second connections to 1000+ unique destinations, HTTP floods to known DDoS targets). Flag SOCKS5/HTTP CONNECT tunneling from residential devices. Alert on rapid IP rotation within proxy pools.

suggestion.title: Firmware Currency and Vulnerable Device Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'latest firmware update has been applied' is primary mitigation. Implies botnet prevalence on devices running outdated firmware with exploitable bugs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory all network-accessible devices and flag firmware versions older than 12 months or with published critical CVEs (cross-reference NVD). Trend firmware recency by device class and ISP. Correlate out-of-date devices with C2 communication or botnet indicators. Alert on firmware downgrades.

suggestion.title: Exposed Remote Administration Interfaces
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'remote administration panels are disabled when not needed.' Indicates devices exposed SSH/Telnet/HTTP admin endpoints to internet, allowing initial compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for and alert on inbound WAN connections to standard admin ports (22, 23, 80, 443, 8080, 3389, 5900) on consumer devices. Flag successful admin logins from external/residential IP sources. Detect port-scan patterns targeting admin ports across device clusters.

suggestion.title: Mass Worm/Botnet Propagation Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article: '17 million infected devices' and 'owners... did not knowingly participate.' Suggests rapid automated propagation, not consent-based.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect identical file hashes written to hundreds of devices within short time windows. Monitor for suspicious process spawning from network services (SMB, UPnP, HTTP). Alert on lateral movement initiation from compromised devices toward new targets. Flag rapid propagation vectors (SMB worm, peer-to-peer replication).

suggestion.title: AI-Generated Code with Known Vulnerable Dependency Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article states '65–70% of production code is now generated by AI, and nearly half of it contains exploitable vulnerabilities.' This describes code commits with predictable vulnerability signatures, detectable via dependency tree fingerprinting and known-bad SCA patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor repository commits for AI-generated code markers (copilot, Claude, etc.) coupled with dependency manifests matching known-vulnerable SCA profiles. Correlate commit timestamps with AI assistant activity logs to detect staged vulnerable code deployment.

suggestion.title: Autonomous Batch Dependency Upgrade Campaigns
suggestion.rationale: The Remediation Agent performs 'fully autonomous, intelligence-guided remediation at scale' with 'asynchronous Remediation Agent that runs without a developer prompt, against a backlog filter, that produces fully validated, mergeable PRs.' This describes programmatic, high-velocity PR generation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag PR creation patterns with abnormally high dependency upgrade velocity (>50 dependency updates per hour), automated author claims (agent/bot accounts), and cross-repo correlation suggesting a centrally-triggered remediation campaign. Baseline normal upgrade patterns by organization.

suggestion.title: Frontier Model Exploitation Chain Assembly
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Frontier models can chain together previously-ignorable, low-severity findings into working, novel zero-day exploits.' This describes AI-driven synthesis of multi-step attack primitives that were individually non-critical.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate low-severity vulnerability exploitation events (CVSS <5.0) occurring in temporal clusters, targeting the same asset/application within short windows. Model combination of CVE patterns to identify synthetic zero-day chains; correlate with AI-based code generation or fuzzing tool activity.

suggestion.title: Unvalidated Autonomous Remediation PR Merge
suggestion.rationale: Article discusses risk that 'autonomous workflows that were supposed to save time are now costing developers even more time as they babysit AI's every move,' and acknowledges fixes may 'compile but may not resolve the CVE.' Detects merges of remediation PRs lacking proper security validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify merged PRs authored by remediation automation that lack security review approvals, contain high diff entropy (>500 lines changed across multiple package manifests), or merge within <5 minutes of creation (suggests bypassed validation gates).

suggestion.title: AI Model Context Injection for Vulnerable Code Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article describes the Remediation Agent 'pairing the reasoning ability of frontier models with Snyk's security intelligence' and injecting 'the right context into your LLM.' This is a technique for teaching models about vulnerabilities; misconfiguration could propagate flawed understanding.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor LLM API calls and local model inference logs for prompts querying vulnerability contexts; flag patterns where instruction-injection attempts (e.g., adversarial prompts asking to 'bypass validation' or 'ignore security checks') precede code generation. Correlate with subsequent vulnerable commits.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable vm2 package dependency detection in application artifacts
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'NodeVM blocks several dangerous Node.js builtins' implying code-level dependency. The attack requires vm2 to be in use and vulnerable. Missing: hunt for package.json or package-lock.json containing vm2 with version matching vulnerable ranges (e.g., 3.x < 3.11.4). Phrase: 'sandboxed code can be used from sandboxed code' implies vm2 is deployed in the target application.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation or modification of package.json or package-lock.json files containing vm2 package dependency. Cross-reference against vulnerable version fingerprints. Correlate with deployment or application startup events to identify exposed assets.

suggestion.title: Node.js process inline script execution with require('process') or require('inspector')
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'the denylist misses `process` and `inspector/promises`'. The exploitation requires executing require() calls to bypass. Missing: detection of Node.js invocations with inline script arguments (-e flag) or file arguments containing these require patterns, distinct from post-escape shell spawning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for node.exe or node process execution where ProcessCommandLine contains -e, --eval, -c flags followed by patterns like require('process'), require("process"), or require('inspector/promises'). Catch sandbox escape attempts before shell spawning.

suggestion.title: Node.js listening on Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP) with external connections
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'inspector/promises' is the Node.js inspector module exposing Runtime.evaluate. This is accessed via CDP on port 9229 (default). Missing: detection of Node.js opening inspector/CDP ports and accepting connections, which enables the Runtime.evaluate exploit path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for node.exe with --inspect or --inspect-brk flags binding to localhost/0.0.0.0 on ports 9229-9500. Correlate with unexpected inbound connections or remote CDP protocol activity. Flag if inspector is exposed to non-localhost interfaces.

suggestion.title: vm2 Package Version Mismatch — Vulnerable <=3.11.3 via Package Lock Analysis
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability applies to '<=3.11.3', but UC_17_1 detects any vm2. Need positive confirmation of outdated version via package-lock.json or yarn.lock resolved versions rather than presence alone.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for package-lock.json or yarn.lock files containing resolved vm2 version field with value <3.11.4 OR git log showing recent package.json edits without corresponding lock file updates (indicating stale vulnerable version). Correlate against patch date 2026-05-29 for high-confidence 'known vulnerable installed post-awareness' signals.

suggestion.title: Promise.prototype[Symbol.species] Direct Manipulation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article root cause: 'missing a call to resetPromiseSpecies'—direct detection of Symbol.species assignment to Promise.prototype would catch exploitation technique itself, not just post-sandbox effects. Rare in legitimate code; high specificity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Node.js process command lines or in-memory patterns containing Promise.prototype[Symbol.species] = OR Object.defineProperty(Promise, Symbol.species, ...) OR direct Symbol.species assignment within Promise context. Distinguish weaponization from legitimate Promise subclassing by absence of formal class definition or prototype extension patterns.

suggestion.title: vm2 runInNewContext + Rejection Handler Chain Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exploitation via 'localPromise constructor changed to call this.then(undefined, eater)'. Direct pattern: vm2 context + unusual rejection handler chains (no-op eater functions) indicate exploitation vs. normal usage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for node.exe executing .js files importing vm2 AND containing Promise.then(undefined, <handler>) OR .catch(()=>{}) followed by Symbol species operations within same script scope. Baseline legitimate vm2 usage and flag deviations with rejection handler chaining patterns.

suggestion.title: Node.js Child Process Spawn Correlated with vm2 Module Context
suggestion.rationale: UC_17_2 spawns generic 'node.exe → cmd.exe' detection with high FP. Adding vm2 context requirement (require('vm2') or runInNewContext calls visible in parent cmdline or parent script) would significantly reduce FP and increase confidence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for node.exe processes with InitiatingProcessCommandLine containing vm2 indicators (require vm2, runInNewContext, vm2 module path) followed by child process spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or bash.exe within 5-second window. Reduces FP by requiring vm2 context confirmation.

suggestion.title: npm Module Persistence via vm2 Post-Installation Scripts
suggestion.rationale: Article doesn't detail delivery mechanism, but npm packages with postinstall scripts could install vulnerable vm2 and trigger exploitation on first require. Hunt for package.json postinstall scripts calling Node.js code that requires vm2.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for package.json files with postinstall script containing vm2 imports or execution, OR npm install activity preceded by suspicious package.json edits adding vm2 with postinstall hooks. Correlate with child process spawns within postinstall execution window.

suggestion.title: vm2 Sandbox Escape Success Indicator — Unexpected Process Elevation or Capability Gain
suggestion.rationale: UC_17_2 detects exploitation execution, but no hunt for 'success' signals: process integrity level changes, token privilege escalation, or filesystem ACL modifications post-child-process spawn from Node.js context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for node.exe spawning cmd.exe or powershell.exe with MEDIUM or HIGH integrity level on systems where parent node.exe was LOW or MEDIUM integrity, OR file system permission changes on sensitive directories immediately following node.exe → cmd.exe pattern. Indicates successful sandbox escape and privilege escalation.

suggestion.title: WebAssembly JSPI module instantiation from Node.js
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes exploitation via 'WebAssembly.promising / WebAssembly.Suspending' (JSPI) and 'JSPI-backed Promise' reaching Promise.finally(). Pipeline missed this vector entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Node.js processes for WebAssembly instantiation patterns involving JSPI (check V8 heap or process memory for 'WebAssembly.promising' calls or Promise.finally() hooks invoked from WASM contexts). Flag if spawned by untrusted/sandboxed contexts.

suggestion.title: Unexpected async/await with Promise species manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'bypasses the expected Promise-species hardening' — this is a Promise constructor override/interception technique that should be detectable at the vm2 boundary.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag code samples or script execution within vm2 contexts that override Promise.prototype or attempt to access Promise[Symbol.species]. Cross-reference with untrusted/user-supplied code execution.

suggestion.title: Privilege escalation from Node.js uid to parent/system uid
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'arbitrary code execution in the host process' — successful exploit grants host UID to code running under Node sandbox UID. Detect uid/privilege transitions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Node.js process (running as unprivileged user) spawns child with elevated or parent-process UID. Focus on transitions from Node→root or Node→admin context.

suggestion.title: vm2 module property inspection or internals access
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires reaching host Promise via JSPI-backed Promise and .finally() method — implies introspection of vm2 object internals. Article states 'exposes host-originated' Promise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect vm2 context attempting to access properties like 'constructor', 'prototype', or 'Symbol.species' on Promise or other globals. Use taint tracking on untrusted input passed to vm2.runInNewContext().

suggestion.title: PraisonAI `execute_code()` invoked with builtins/vars/import string patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes extraction of `__import__` via `vars()` and runtime string construction to bypass the sandbox. No UC captures detection of this exploitation technique in action. Phrase: 'extract `__import__` can be extracted via `vars()` and runtime string construction'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Python processes spawned from PraisonAI contexts executing code containing patterns like `vars(`, `__import__`, string concatenation with module/function names, or dynamic exec/eval in rapid succession. Look for subprocess/exec calls immediately following such patterns.

suggestion.title: Python process accessing __builtins__ or __self__ attribute outside stdlib contexts
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'print.__self__` to retrieve the real Python `builtins` module'. The __self__ descriptor and __builtins__ access are the core pivot point of the sandbox escape. Detection should flag access to these introspection attributes in application code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Python process command lines and created/modified .py files for patterns matching `__builtins__`, `__self__`, and `getattr(print`, which indicate attempts to access the real builtin namespace. Correlate with PraisonAI parent processes or library paths.

suggestion.title: Subprocess spawned from PraisonAI with unusual working directory or environment variable leakage
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'arbitrary OS command execution' as the impact. The hunts show detection of env var exfiltration (AWS_SECRET, OPENAI_API_KEY) but no standalone UC for unusual subprocess context. Phrase: 'arbitrary OS command execution on the host, completely defeating the sandbox'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag subprocess creation (sh, bash, cmd, powershell) where parent is Python with PraisonAI in the context, AND the subprocess accesses files in /proc/self, /etc/passwd, /var/run/secrets, or reads environment variables containing API keys or credentials.

suggestion.title: Flask app initialization with default-disabled authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article states the generated server ships with 'authentication disabled by default.' Detection should hunt for Flask initialization patterns like app.config["AUTH_ENABLED"]=False, absence of authentication middleware registration, or werkzeug.security imports followed by disabled checks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag file creation/modification of generated Flask app files (app.py, server.py, api.py) containing 'Authentication' / 'AUTH' / 'auth' in combination with False/disabled/skip keywords, or Python process execution of generate_api_server_code() function.

suggestion.title: PraisonAI package installation via package manager in deployment flow
suggestion.rationale: Article describes quickstart flow requiring praisonai installation. Lack of installation detection means missing the provisioning phase. Hunt for 'pip install praisonai' or 'conda install praisonai' sequences.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect pip or conda process execution with 'praisonai' argument, correlate with subsequent praisonai deploy commands on same endpoint to establish supply-chain/provisioning chain.

suggestion.title: Enumeration of PraisonAI endpoints by reconnaissance tooling
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions CVE-Detector scanner probing endpoints; any attacker would enumerate /agents, /chat, /config, /api/* paths. Detection should aggregate HTTP requests to common Flask/LLM-app paths from single source in short window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Aggregate HTTP GET/OPTIONS requests by source IP to port 8005 within 5-minute sliding windows. Flag sources attempting >5 distinct endpoint paths, especially with scanner user-agents or rapid 404/200 patterns.

suggestion.title: Execution of LLM-generated code via agent tool-use sandbox escape
suggestion.rationale: Article documents PraisonAI as an agent framework; if /chat endpoint accepts user-controlled prompts, attacker can coerce agent to generate and execute shell commands. Detection should hunt for exec() / subprocess / os.system() calls spawned from Flask request handlers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate parent=python (Flask app on 8005), grandparent=python/bash, with child processes spawned shortly after inbound HTTP request. Flag exec/eval patterns in Python source or compiled bytecode if available.

suggestion.title: API endpoint exploitation baseline (T1190 detection)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'cross-workspace IDOR' via `/api/v1/workspaces/{id}/` endpoints but no detection maps to T1190 (Exploit Public-Facing Application). Baseline API error-rate and probing patterns should be detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sustained or spiking rates of 4xx errors (401, 403, 404) to `/api/v1/workspaces/*` patterns from a single source/user within short time windows—indicates probing for IDOR exploitability before successful bypass.

suggestion.title: Cascading privilege escalation + data exfiltration chain
suggestion.rationale: Article describes role elevation followed by cross-workspace data access. UC_2_2 (member role mutation, T1098/T1548) and UC_2_3 (resource enumeration, T1213) are independent—missing detection that chains both in time sequence as single attack thread.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PATCH/POST to `/api/v1/workspaces/*/members` endpoint (privilege escalation attempt) followed within 90 seconds by GET/PATCH requests to nested resource endpoints (agents, issues, projects) from same source IP/user—indicates abuse-then-exfil chain.

suggestion.title: Authorization boundary bypass (failed workspace check → successful nested resource access)
suggestion.rationale: Article's core vulnerability: `require_workspace_member(workspace_id)` checks workspace boundary but nested resource handlers accept the context without re-validating. Should detect 401/403 to workspace root followed by 200 to nested resource in same workspace.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequence where user receives 401/403 on `/api/v1/workspaces/{X}` but receives 200-299 on `/api/v1/workspaces/{X}/agents/{Y}`, `/api/v1/workspaces/{X}/issues/{Z}`, etc.—signature of auth check bypass.

suggestion.title: Compromised/stolen account probing across workspaces (T1078 abuse pattern)
suggestion.rationale: T1078 (Valid Accounts) is listed but no detection for identifying when a legitimate account is abused to probe beyond its authorized workspace scope. UC_2_3 detects resource enumeration but not the workspace-scope deviation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline each user's regular workspace access pattern (histogram of workspace_ids they access). Flag when a user's API requests reference 4+ workspaces not in their historical baseline within 10 minutes—indicates credential compromise or insider enumeration.

suggestion.title: Structured resource ID enumeration (sequential/batch access patterns)
suggestion.rationale: Article implies resource access by 'primary ID'. UC_2_3 detects high-count enumeration; missing detection for request-pattern anomaly (sequential IDs, sub-second intervals, or predictable ID structures).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequences of requests to `/api/v1/workspaces/{W}/agents/{ID1}`, `/agents/{ID2}`, `/agents/{ID3}` where IDs show sequential increment (UUID byte-order patterns), numeric progression, or requests arrive at consistent sub-second intervals—automated enumeration signature.

suggestion.title: Hardcoded JWT secret materialization in config files or environment
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability is hardcoded literal string 'dev-secret-change-me' as default. No existing UC hunts for this string in config files, source code, or environment variable logs. This is the root-cause artifact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for literal string 'dev-secret-change-me' or pattern PLATFORM_JWT_SECRET.*dev in .env files, Python source (app.py, main.py, config.py), and environment variable dumps. Flag containers/VMs where this string is present without explicit override before startup.

suggestion.title: JWT token forgery exploitation via anomalous account assumption claims
suggestion.rationale: Article core threat: 'allowing token forgery for any user'. No UC detects actual forged-JWT usage. Authentication logs will show valid JWT signatures with payload claims (user ID, workspace ID, roles) that deviate from legitimate issuance patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of legitimate JWT payload claims (iat timestamps, jti values, user_id sequences) from /auth/register and /auth/login endpoints. Flag authentication events where valid JWT signatures contain user_id / role claims not issued by these baseline sources, or iat timestamps that predate legitimate token issuance by >30s.

suggestion.title: Production environment running with PLATFORM_ENV unset or explicitly set to 'dev'
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'safety check only fires when PLATFORM_ENV != dev; default value is dev; check is bypassed in any deployment where PLATFORM_ENV unset'. This misconfiguration is the vulnerability activator. No hunt for this anti-pattern in production infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all praisonai-platform deployments by process discovery (uvicorn with praisonai_platform in cmdline). For each, extract PLATFORM_ENV via /proc/PID/environ or container inspect. Flag any where PLATFORM_ENV is 'dev' or missing in hosts labeled production (hostname matches regex prod|prd, or IP in production subnet, or DNS SRV indicates production tier).

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Role Elevation in Request Body — Verify role parameter=owner in PATCH body
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'body.role' is passed to MemberService.update_role() but no detection verifies the actual role value in request payloads. The entire attack hinges on setting role='owner', which should be directly observable in HTTP request bodies or API gateway logs.
log_sources: Web proxy with request body logging
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for PATCH requests to /workspaces/*/members/* endpoints where request body contains role field set to 'owner' or elevated role values. Baseline against legitimate admin role assignments and alert on unauthorized sources (non-admin user IDs performing the PATCH on behalf of other users).

suggestion.title: Self-Promotion Detection — User ID matches target member ID in PATCH request
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'Any workspace member can promote themselves or others'. Distinguish self-promotion (malicious) from admin-mediated promotion (potentially legitimate). When Web.user matches the member_id in the URL path, flag as self-promotion attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when PATCH /workspaces/{id}/members/{user_id} request originates from a user where the user_id in the URL equals the authenticated user making the request, AND role is changed to 'owner'. This directly maps to unauthorized self-promotion.

suggestion.title: Post-Privilege-Escalation Administrative API Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: After role promotion succeeds, attacker will query administrative surfaces to understand their new scope. Article mentions agents, issues, projects access after escalation. Detect queries to /workspaces/*/roles, /workspaces/*/members (list), or admin configuration endpoints within 5 minutes of successful role change.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful role-change PATCH (200/204) to same source issuing subsequent GET requests to administrative list/query endpoints (members, roles, permissions, settings). Timeline constraint: discovery queries within 5 minutes of privilege escalation indicate reconnaissance post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: Workspace Owner Cardinality Spike — Sudden elevation of owner count
suggestion.rationale: The CVE allows arbitrary promotion to owner. A spike in workspace owner count, especially multiple promotions from a single source, is a strong signal of exploitation. Not explicitly in article but natural follow-up to detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline owner count per workspace. Alert when owner count increases by >1 in a 1-hour window, or when multiple users are elevated to owner role from a single source IP/account in short timespan. Correlate against change requests or bulk provisioning windows to reduce FP.

suggestion.title: Cross-Member Unauthorized Role Escalation — Non-Admin Promoting Other Users
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability allows any member to promote 'or others' to owner. Detection should flag when a non-admin/non-owner user successfully changes role for a different user. This is the lateral privilege model distinct from self-promotion.
log_sources: Web proxy logs with request/response metadata
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify PATCH requests where (authenticated_user != target_user_id) AND (authenticated_user_current_role != 'owner') AND (response status = 200/204). This is privilege escalation of another user by a non-privileged account.

suggestion.title: ScreenConnect Remote Access Software Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly delivers 'ScreenConnect Malware' (the RAT/RMM tool itself). Pipeline extracted no execution or C2 detection rules. Must detect installation, registry artifacts, and network callbacks typical of ScreenConnect post-installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: ScreenConnect installations are characteristically triggered from unusual download paths and create specific service names or registry keys. Monitor for process execution with ScreenConnect in the command line, service creation with known ScreenConnect identifiers, and outbound TLS/HTTPS connections to known ScreenConnect C2 ranges.

suggestion.title: Fake Adobe Document Cloud Phishing Landing Pages
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Fake Adobe Document Cloud Pages'—credential harvesting infrastructure. Pipeline missed detection for HTTP requests to typosquatted or lookalike Adobe domains, and form submissions to non-Adobe origins masquerading as Adobe login.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify HTTP requests to domains with high string similarity to 'adobe.com' or 'documentcloud.adobe.com', or requests containing 'adobe' in the host but resolving to non-Adobe IP space. Flag form submissions (POST requests) to these fake domains containing credential patterns (email + password fields).

suggestion.title: Phishing Email Delivery of ScreenConnect Installer
suggestion.rationale: Title implies phishing delivery mechanism ('Hackers Use Fake... Pages to Deliver'). Pipeline extracted no email-based initial access detections or IOCs (sender, subject, attachment hashes).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails containing .scr, .exe, .msi, or .zip attachments linking to or containing ScreenConnect installers. Flag emails with body text directing users to fake Adobe login pages. Correlate email delivery with subsequent DNS queries to known ScreenConnect C2 or fake-Adobe domains.

suggestion.title: Credential Submission to Non-Adobe Origins
suggestion.rationale: Fake Adobe pages are credential harvesters. Pipeline did not surface detections for successful credential exfiltration to attacker-controlled endpoints or POST requests with credential patterns to non-Adobe domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP POST requests containing email and password parameters sent to domains outside Adobe's legitimate IP space. Flag successful submissions (HTTP 200/302) that occur immediately after visiting lookalike Adobe domains.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Download of ScreenConnect Installer from Non-Official Sources
suggestion.rationale: ScreenConnect delivery implies download of the malware binary from attacker infrastructure or compromised sites. Pipeline has no file-download or hash-based IOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect downloads of .msi, .exe, or .scr files with names containing 'ScreenConnect', 'Support', 'Remote', or similar terms from domains not owned by ConnectWise (legitimate ScreenConnect vendor). Flag followed by execution from %TEMP% or %Downloads%.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Lateral Movement via ScreenConnect
suggestion.rationale: Once ScreenConnect is installed, it becomes a lateral movement and persistence tool. Pipeline missed detections for ScreenConnect being used to pivot to other hosts or establish secondary C2.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for ScreenConnect process spawning child processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe) or initiating network connections to internal IP ranges. Flag multiple simultaneous ScreenConnect connections from a single source to different internal hosts.

suggestion.title: Fake Software Update Delivery Detected
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attack using 'fake video player updates' as initial access. Pipeline failed to map supply chain/trojanized software technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect attempts to download or execute video player updates from non-official sources, unsigned update binaries, or update processes initiating from web-download artifacts rather than official application paths. Monitor for update executables launched from TEMP, Downloads, or AppData/Local directories.

suggestion.title: Cryptominer Process Execution Post-Software Update
suggestion.rationale: Article states miners are deployed; article body suggests execution follows update installation. No UC generated for post-installation payload activation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect resource-intensive processes (xmrig, monero miners, etc.) spawned within minutes of software update completion. Alert on child processes of legitimate-appearing update utilities with high CPU/memory consumption or cryptomining signatures in command line arguments.

suggestion.title: RAT Command and Control Communication Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions RAT (Remote Access Trojan) malware deployment, but no detection UC for C2 beaconing or lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect DNS queries or network connections from recently-updated applications to suspicious domains or IPs. Alert on RAT-associated ports, DGAs, or domains known to host RAT infrastructure. Focus on outbound connections from injected/child processes of update mechanisms.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Scheduled Tasks from Update Process
suggestion.rationale: Multi-stage attack pattern (update → miner + RAT) implies persistence mechanism not identified. Article describes ongoing deployment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation of scheduled tasks, registry autorun entries, or startup folder artifacts spawned by or in the seconds following software update executable completion. Cross-correlate task creation with update binary path and payload process execution.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Resource Consumption Post-Update Installation
suggestion.rationale: Miners cause sustained CPU/memory spike; RAT causes network anomalies. No behavioral detection UC generated despite clear malware impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when system CPU utilization spikes >75% for sustained periods (>10 min) immediately following software update completion, especially if process is not identifiable in official software vendor libraries. Cross-check against baseline for user's typical post-update behavior.

suggestion.title: LinkedIn Social Engineering Profile Engagement
suggestion.rationale: Article headline explicitly states 'Using LinkedIn Social Engineering'—pipeline extracted zero detection for initial access. Should detect profiles impersonating recruiters, suspicious job postings targeting specific orgs/roles, or unusual LinkedIn API activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for LinkedIn traffic spikes from unusual geographies, repeated profile visits to HR/infosec staff, or download of bulk employee contact lists. Flag accounts created within 30 days of first targeting contact.

suggestion.title: macOS Custom Malware Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article headline mentions 'Custom macOS Malware'—pipeline found no execution detection. Should detect suspicious binary launch, unsigned code, or staged malware delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on: (1) execution of unsigned binaries from Downloads or temp; (2) process spawning shell interpreters from unusual parents (Safari, Mail); (3) code signing validation failures on newly-downloaded files.

suggestion.title: macOS Persistence via Launch Agents or Boot Scripts
suggestion.rationale: Custom macOS malware typically establishes persistence—article does not specify mechanism, but pipeline should have flagged common patterns. Detection needed for .plist modifications, ~/Library/LaunchAgents writes, or cron/launchd abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for writes to ~/Library/LaunchAgents/, ~/Library/LaunchDaemons/, or /Library/LaunchDaemons/ by non-system processes. Alert if launchd spawns unexpected executables or scripts from non-standard paths.

suggestion.title: Suspicious macOS Application Bundle Delivery
suggestion.rationale: LinkedIn-delivered payloads often disguise malware as legitimate apps (.app bundles). Pipeline missing detection for unexpected bundle modifications, Info.plist tampering, or masqueraded applications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unsigned or re-signed .app bundles in non-standard locations (~/Downloads, /tmp). Flag if application bundle contains executables in unexpected paths or calls shell scripts during launch.

suggestion.title: Detect VS Code Tunnel Reverse Shell Activation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes abuse of VS Code Tunnels as expanded C2 arsenal. Should detect port tunneling via devtunnels.ms or local tunneling process. ('VS Code Tunnels' appears in title as attack vector.)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for code.exe or codeserver.exe spawning with --tunnel flag or child processes establishing outbound TLS connections to devtunnels.ms. Alert on persistent devtunnels tunnel sessions in user profiles. Correlate with unusual RDP or SSH lateral movement following tunnel activation.

suggestion.title: Detect HTTPSpy C2 Beacon Traffic
suggestion.rationale: HTTPSpy is explicitly named as deployed tool. Requires IOC extraction (domains, IPs, certificate fingerprints) and behavioral detection for HTTP(S) beacon patterns. Article confirms HTTPSpy is active Kimsuky tooling. Need network baseline for this C2 family.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify HTTPSpy beacon signatures via HTTP header anomalies, User-Agent patterns, and POST intervals. Cross-reference with known Kimsuky infrastructure. Alert on HTTPS traffic to low-reputation IPs with self-signed certs or certificate pinning bypasses.

suggestion.title: Detect HelloDoor Backdoor Installation and Persistence
suggestion.rationale: HelloDoor is explicitly named as expanded arsenal tool (article title). No existing IOCs provided. Pipeline should surface installation vectors (email, watering hole, supply chain) and persistence mechanisms (registry, scheduled task, startup folder).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HelloDoor binary execution (file name / hash TBD). Detect registry modifications under HKLM/HKCU indicating persistence (Run, RunOnce, scheduled task creation). Alert on suspicious service installations or WMI event subscription creation.

suggestion.title: Detect Kimsuky Credential Harvesting via Compromised Dev Tools
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates expansion into developer tools (VS Code) as C2 vectors; Kimsuky historically targets credentials. Pipeline missed connection between tool abuse and credential access kill-chain phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for credential-access patterns post-tunnel activation: browser credential dumping (LSASS access), clipboard monitoring, form filling tools. Correlate code.exe spawning with credential manager or browser profile access. Alert on exfiltration of .git credentials or SSH keys.

suggestion.title: Detect Kimsuky Initial Access via Spear Phishing and Watering Hole
suggestion.rationale: Article title mentions 'expands arsenal' implying continued initial access campaigns. Kimsuky signature includes targeted spear-phishing and watering holes. Pipeline should include pre-execution detection for phishing payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for emails with Korean-language social engineering or geopolitics lures to policy/research targets. Detect suspicious Office macro execution or LNK file execution tied to public shares. Alert on anomalous PowerShell/CMD spawning from Temp or Downloads folders.

suggestion.title: Detect VS Code Tunnel Lateral Movement and Persistence
suggestion.rationale: VS Code Tunnels enable remote code execution and persistence across networked systems. Article does not detail but standard TTPs would include using tunnel for lateral movement. Pipeline missed persistence mechanism entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for tunnel connections from unexpected source IPs or user accounts. Detect code.exe spawning in System or Service context (anomalous). Alert on tunnel port forwarding enabling SSH or RDP access to internal systems post-initial compromise.

suggestion.title: OpenAI Codex Authentication Token Theft via Spoofed UI
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly describes theft of 'OpenAI Codex Authentication Tokens' through a 'Legitimate-Looking' remote interface. This is the core attack vector and must be detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for token exfiltration targeting OpenAI API endpoints. Detect browser/process interactions with domains impersonating Codex (homograph variants, typosquatted subdomains). Alert when authentication tokens are accessed from unexpected processes or transmitted to non-OpenAI C2 infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Access to Codex Phishing Domain / Homograph Attack
suggestion.rationale: The 'Legitimate-Looking' UI is a phishing attack surface described in the title. Requires detection of spoofed Codex domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify access to domains with typosquatting or homograph variations of Codex, OpenAI, or legitimate code model platforms. Flag visits by developers or R&D staff to such domains, especially if credential entry or token access follows.

suggestion.title: Abnormal OpenAI API Token Usage / Abuse Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Once tokens are stolen, threat actors abuse them for code generation, data exfiltration, or resource consumption. Should detect anomalous token activity patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor OpenAI API audit logs for unusual token usage: geolocation anomalies, request volume spikes, non-standard endpoints, off-hours access, or requests from suspicious user agents. Correlate with credential exposure timeline.

suggestion.title: Developer Credential Phishing / Social Engineering Detection
suggestion.rationale: Attack depends on social engineering to direct developers to fake Codex UI. Should detect phishing campaigns targeting developer communities.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag emails or messages containing links to Codex lookalike domains, especially if sent to known developer/AI research communities. Correlate with phishing infrastructure (shared IPs, registrant data, SSL certs) and downstream token exfiltration events.

suggestion.title: Suspicious NuGet Package Installation with Credential Context
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states malicious NuGet package exfiltrates banking passwords. No detection use case was generated for NuGet-based initial delivery combined with credential access signals.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for NuGet package installation (nuget.exe, dotnet restore) where the originating package source is external or mismatched from organizational allowlists. Correlate with subsequent credential-access indicators (LSASS access, registry queries for credential stores, WMI queries for credentials). Anomalous package names impersonating legitimate SDKs (e.g., containing typosquatting patterns or unofficial version numbering) warrant immediate isolation.

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration from SDK/Package Initialization Code
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies passwords exfiltrated; pipeline detected zero credential-access phase or techniques. SDK/package loading provides execution context for malware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify processes spawned by NuGet/package managers (dotnet.exe, msbuild.exe) that subsequently access LSASS, SAM hive, or browser credential stores. Flag network connections from these processes to non-standard ports or external IPs. Monitor for in-memory credential dumping tools (mimikatz patterns) or credential enumeration via WMI/registry queries initiated from package load context.

suggestion.title: Build/Development Environment Beaconing to C2 Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates exfiltration; no detection for command-and-control communication was proposed. Banking credential theft typically involves data transfer to attacker infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor build and development workstations for outbound connections to IP ranges or domains not whitelisted for legitimate package repositories and CI/CD systems. Flag DNS queries from build agents to newly registered domains or known malware C2 infrastructure. Correlate with process trees originating from package installation to establish causality.

suggestion.title: Typosquatted or Impersonation NuGet Package Detection
suggestion.rationale: Headline explicitly names the attack as impersonating Sicoob SDK; no detection strategy was generated to catch lookalike package names in package manifests or restore operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Implement a baseline of legitimate package identifiers from organizational nuget.config and project files. Alert on installation of packages with names similar to known SDKs (Levenshtein distance or common typosquatting patterns: missing letters, numeric substitution, domain confusion). Cross-reference package source URLs against authorized package registries (internal Artifactory, official NuGet.org); flag pulls from untrusted sources.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Registry Access by Package Runtime for Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Banking password exfiltration implies registry enumeration (Windows credential manager, browser auto-fill stores). Pipeline did not map this access pattern to a detection use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes spawned from .NET/NuGet context querying HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Authentication or HKCU\Software\[Mozilla|Google|Microsoft]\[Firefox|Chrome|Edge]\Profiles for credential enumeration. Flag unusual registry access frequency or access to multiple credential stores in a short window. Cross-correlate with network exfiltration events.

suggestion.title: Malicious NuGet Package Installation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'Malicious Sicoob NuGet Steals Banking Credentials' — package manager installation is the entry vector. Pipeline generated zero use cases for NuGet or dotnet CLI package downloads despite this being the primary attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor NuGet.exe or dotnet CLI invocations with .nupkg source URIs or install commands, followed by child-process spawning outside expected build directories. Alert on connections to non-official NuGet repositories or packages with typosquatting indicators (Sicoob variants: sicoob-*, sicoob-client-*, etc.).

suggestion.title: npm Postinstall Script Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'npm Packages Target Cloud Secrets' — malicious postinstall/preinstall hooks steal credentials, yet zero use case detects npm spawn + credential file access pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate npm install or yarn add with child processes reading .env files, ~/.aws/*, ~/.azure/*, KUBECONFIG, or Registry paths (HKEY_CURRENT_USER\*\Credentials). Flag if access occurs within 5 seconds of package install completion.

suggestion.title: Banking Credential Theft from Package Initialization
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Steals Banking Credentials' — indicates malware execution during or after package install, but zero detection use case for process trees spawning credential-scraping tools.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect NuGet or npm parent process spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or curl with unusual command lines (credential store queries, registry dumps, password manager enumeration). Alert on child process network connections immediately following spawn.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of Stolen Credentials from Package Processes
suggestion.rationale: Banking credentials are stolen ('Steals Banking Credentials') implying command-and-control callback or data upload, but pipeline generated zero exfiltration detection use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP POST/PUT or DNS queries from NuGet/npm-spawned processes to suspicious domains (non-Microsoft, non-npm registry hosts). Correlate with preceding file reads of credential stores and validate domain reputation against known attacker infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Package Manifest vs. Content Integrity Mismatch
suggestion.rationale: Malicious NuGet and npm packages likely contain obfuscated or unsigned payloads. Pipeline should flag packages with file-count or hash discrepancies but generated zero artifact integrity use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Unpack .nupkg or .tgz archives and compare declared manifest (file list, sizes, hashes) against actual extracted contents. Alert on binary executables in packages declared as script-only, DLLs with no publisher signature, or size deviations > 5% from manifest.

suggestion.title: Phishing Emails Leveraging ChatGPT-Rendered Payloads
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'Turn Web Pages Into Phishing Payloads'—core attack vector is weaponized pages delivered via ChatGPT
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails containing links to attacker-controlled web pages or ChatGPT-generated rendering endpoints. Flag emails with suspicious ChatGPT conversation URLs or encoded payloads designed to render login forms.

suggestion.title: Malicious HTML/JavaScript Injection via ChatGPT Endpoint Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability enables attackers to weaponize ChatGPT itself to generate/deliver phishing pages; requires execution of attacker-supplied prompts
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ChatGPT API calls and web.archive-like endpoints for prompts requesting HTML/CSS/JavaScript generation targeting credential harvesting, form injection, or page cloning. Detect encoding of payloads to evade filtering.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting via Fake Login Forms Rendered by ChatGPT
suggestion.rationale: Attack converts web pages to phishing payloads; rendered pages likely contain fake login forms for credential capture
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify web pages served via ChatGPT or OpenAI-hosted infrastructure containing HTML form elements requesting credentials, 2FA codes, or API tokens. Monitor for exfiltration of submitted form data to non-OpenAI domains.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Developer Tool Process Execution with Unusual Arguments
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'attackers abuse trusted developer tooling'—suggests legitimate tools (git, npm, IDEs, build systems) executing with abnormal parameters or in unexpected contexts. No UC generated despite this being the central attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor trusted dev tools (git.exe, npm.cmd, maven, gradle, xcodebuild, dotnet) for execution with exfiltration-related flags (--branch, upload-pack, clone with unusual destinations), credential-passing arguments, or from non-developer user contexts.

suggestion.title: Bulk Source Code Repository Access and Staging
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'exfiltrate source code'—implies repository enumeration, cloning, or bulk file access. No detection logic captured despite being primary data-gathering phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect large-scale repository clones, bulk .git directory access, recursive source file reads, or staged data (>500MB of source code in temp directories). Baseline per-user repo access patterns.

suggestion.title: Credential and API Key Extraction from Developer Environments
suggestion.rationale: Article title includes 'exfiltrate...secrets'—strongly implies API keys, tokens, .ssh directories, or .env files accessed. No use case addresses secrets harvesting despite it being explicitly named in title.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor access to .ssh, .aws, .kube config directories, .env file reads, git credential helper invocations, and environment variable enumeration from non-standard processes. Flag staging of credential files to exfil paths.

suggestion.title: High-Volume Data Exfiltration from Development Workstations
suggestion.rationale: Article core claim is exfiltration via developer tools. No detection for abnormal outbound data volume, C2 communication, or compression/archiving of source repositories despite being the impact phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sustained egress (>100MB/hour) from dev workstations to non-whitelisted external IPs, especially paired with compression utilities (7z, tar, zip) or cloud upload tools (curl, rclone, aws s3). Flag C2 patterns: low-frequency beacons exfiling staged data.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised Developer Machine to Repositories or CI/CD
suggestion.rationale: Trusted developer tooling abuse suggests initial compromise of dev workstation, then lateral movement to central code repositories or CI/CD systems. Article does not detail this but is implicit in 'trusted tooling' supply-chain angle.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate compromised dev workstation (process anomalies, unusual tool execution) with subsequent git/VCS authentication from that host to central repositories. Monitor for SYSTEM or service-account git pushes originating from user workstations.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Modified Developer Tools or Build Artifacts
suggestion.rationale: If attackers 'abuse trusted developer tooling,' they may inject malicious code into build systems, git hooks, IDE plugins, or package repositories. No persistence mechanism modeled despite implicitly present in 'tooling abuse' narrative.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthorized modifications to .git/hooks, build pipeline configs (Jenkinsfile, .gitlab-ci.yml, GitHub Actions), IDE plugin directories, or npm/maven local cache. Detect unsigned or revoked-certificate tool updates.

suggestion.title: Marimo CVE-2026-39987 Remote Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly calls out 'Marimo CVE-2026-39987 Exploit' as attack vector. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs or initial-access detections. This is the beachhead.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST/GET requests to Marimo application instances with payloads targeting CVE-2026-39987 (likely code injection or unsafe deserialization in notebook execution path). Correlate with Marimo process spawning unexpected child interpreters or outbound network connections.

suggestion.title: LLM Agent Spawning and Execution Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'LLM Agent for Post-Exploitation'—this is the core attack mechanism after initial access. Pipeline generated zero use cases for LLM agent detection or behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of Python/Node.js interpreters or subprocess spawning from Marimo application context with LLM-related libraries (langchain, openai, anthropic SDKs) or unusual command-line arguments. Flag process execution containing prompt injection patterns or model provider API tokens.

suggestion.title: LLM Agent API Exfiltration and C2
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation LLM agents require external control or data transmission. Article describes attack beyond initial access but pipeline surfaced no C2 or API communication patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTPS API calls from Marimo or child processes to known LLM provider endpoints (api.openai.com, api.anthropic.com, etc.) with high frequency, large payloads, or anomalous authentication. Detect exfiltration of sensitive data through LLM API request bodies (credentials, database dumps embedded in prompts).

suggestion.title: Marimo Process Network Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Exploited application should exhibit unusual network behavior; pipeline did not suggest detection for outbound connections or data exfiltration from Marimo.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Marimo process initiating outbound connections to non-standard ports or high-entropy domains. Detect large data transfers from Marimo context to external IPs. Correlate Marimo network activity with file read operations on sensitive paths (config, credential, database directories).

suggestion.title: LLM Agent Privilege Escalation or Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation attacks typically establish persistence or move laterally. Article implies ongoing exploitation beyond RCE but pipeline extracted no persistence or privilege escalation detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Marimo child processes creating scheduled tasks, cron jobs, or Windows services with LLM-related names or payloads. Detect service creation from Marimo context targeting system-level execution. Flag file system modifications to startup directories or service binaries.

suggestion.title: File Access Patterns from Marimo Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Exploited Marimo instance will read sensitive files for exfiltration. Article describes post-exploitation phase but no data collection/staging detections were generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequential reads of sensitive files (config files, credential stores, database binaries) from Marimo process or spawned children. Alert on file compression or reading of multiple files in rapid succession from sensitive directories. Correlate file reads with outbound network activity.

suggestion.title: Voice Phishing Attack Targeting Employee Credential Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'they breached the company's systems on April 1 in a voice phishing (vishing) attack that compromised an employee's Microsoft Entra account.' Initial access vector is precisely documented but entirely missed by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate inbound voice calls to corporate numbers with Entra sign-in spikes, unusual Entra risky sign-ins, or MFA failures within 1–2 hours. Alert on credentials used from atypical geographies or devices immediately following vishing social-engineering indicators (caller ID spoofing, domain impersonation).

suggestion.title: Entra Service Account Compromise Leading to Salesforce Access
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'compromised an employee's Microsoft Entra account' → 'used this access to steal 42 million records from the company's Salesforce instance.' Credential compromise event and lateral movement chain not captured.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Entra user credentials accessing Salesforce OAuth/federated apps post-compromise. Flag impossible-travel sign-ins, sign-ins from new devices, repeated failed authentication followed by successful login. Monitor for changes to MFA enrollment or authentication method post-breach.

suggestion.title: Bulk Data Export from Salesforce CRM System
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'they used this access to steal 42 million records from the company's Salesforce instance, including consumer and business customer names, email addresses, physical addresses, phone numbers…' Massive exfiltration volume (42M records) is undetected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Salesforce API calls and reports for bulk record exports (>1K records in <5 minutes). Alert on CSV/Excel downloads from Contacts, Leads, or Accounts objects. Flag unusual query patterns (SELECT * queries) and Export calls from user/service accounts post-compromise.

suggestion.title: Employee Directory Dump and CPNI Data Collection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'A subset of approximately 85k records originating from an internal employee directory also included job titles' and 'support ticket data, and some CPNI data.' Targeted collection of sensitive internal data not modeled as detection use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk queries to internal employee directory tables or custom employee records in Salesforce. Flag access to CPNI-tagged fields (support ticket notes, network information) from non-telecom-operations accounts. Monitor for data exports immediately following account compromise detection.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Trusted SaaS Application Access
suggestion.rationale: Attacker compromised one Entra account but accessed a separate Salesforce instance—a classic trusted-relationship/federation-based lateral movement. Article describes movement from 'employee Entra account' to 'Salesforce instance' without re-authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for federation/SSO-based access to Salesforce from newly compromised Entra accounts. Alert when a low-privilege user account suddenly accesses admin-level Salesforce reports or system objects. Track OAuth token refresh patterns for anomalies.

suggestion.title: Dark Web Leak Site Data Publication Confirmation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'the cybercrime group leaked the documents stolen from Charter's Salesforce instance on their dark web leak site.' Exfiltration confirmation and threat publication event—required for post-breach threat intelligence correlation and exposure scope assessment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference breach timeline and stolen data indicators (4.9M email addresses, CPNI, employee directory) against dark web leak site databases and threat feeds. Alert when confirmed Charter data appears on known ShinyHunters leak sites or underground forums selling bulk PII/CPNI.

suggestion.title: ChatGPT Summary API Requests Containing Phishing URLs
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names ChatGPT web summaries as a phishing surface. Detection needed for requests to ChatGPT's summarize endpoints carrying phishing indicators (credential-harvest patterns, lookalike domains, typosquatting).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP/HTTPS requests to OpenAI ChatGPT API endpoints with payloads containing known phishing domains, newly registered domains, or URLs with credential-harvesting parameter patterns (password reset redirects, SSO spoofs). Alert on abnormal request frequency or source IPs.

suggestion.title: Malicious Website Content Optimized for AI Summarization
suggestion.rationale: ChatGPhish vulnerability implies attackers craft web content specifically to exploit ChatGPT parsing behavior, injecting phishing payload into summaries that appear legitimate. Detection for obfuscated/encoded HTML structures that evade traditional phishing filters but mislead AI text extraction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify web pages with encoded scripts, hidden text, or structural obfuscation designed to trigger phishing content extraction in AI summarizers while hiding from static filters. Correlate with responses from summarization services that yield credential-harvesting or brand-impersonation text.

suggestion.title: User Click-Through on URLs from ChatGPT Summaries to Phishing Sites
suggestion.rationale: ChatGPT summaries may legitimize or distribute phishing URLs to end users. Need detection correlating URLs extracted from ChatGPT outputs with subsequent HTTP requests to known or high-risk phishing domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate URLs present in ChatGPT summarization responses with user HTTP requests. Alert on users accessing phishing domains, newly registered lookalike domains, or credential-harvesting sites via URLs originating from ChatGPT summaries within short time windows.

suggestion.title: High-Volume Probing of ChatGPT Summarization Feature
suggestion.rationale: Attackers likely probe ChatGPT's summarization to refine phishing content, test which URL patterns bypass detection when summarized, or enumerate valid targets. Abnormal API request patterns indicate reconnaissance or payload tuning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequential or high-frequency requests to ChatGPT summarization endpoints from single IP/user/account with rotating phishing URLs, malformed payloads, or credential-harvesting parameters. Pattern suggests iterative refinement of phishing content.

suggestion.title: ChatGPT/Claude Share Link Phishing Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'fake outage notice is rendered through ChatGPT itself' via 'shared chatgpt.com/s/ link' — the core distribution vector. Pipeline missed the primary attack infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag clickthrough events where user arrives at chatgpt.com/s/* or claude.ai/artifacts/* links originating from Google Ads referrer or suspicious email, especially if landing page renders download prompt or outage message. Monitor for share links that render HTML outside normal chat context.

suggestion.title: Malware Download from Cloaked Impersonation Domain
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'site uses cloaking to display content only to targeted victims' with 'harmless AR/VR company website' shown to URLScan but malware download to others — requires detection of domain behavior misalignment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect downloads of .exe/.dmg files from openew[.]app or similar domains spoofing AI platform download portals. Cross-reference threat intel feeds for cloaking indicators. Flag user-agent or IP-based content variation from single domain.

suggestion.title: Suspicious VM/Sandbox Detection Commands Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'executes various commands to determine whether the device is a legitimate computer or a virtual machine' — clear post-execution discovery behavior that should trigger alerts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious command execution patterns post-malware install: registry queries for hypervisor/VM artifacts (e.g. HKLM\HARDWARE\ACPI, VirtualBox/VMware driver checks), WMI queries to Win32_ComputerSystemProduct, or commands like 'systeminfo' followed by hypervisor string parsing. High confidence indicator of malware-as-service behavior.

suggestion.title: Fake Outage Social Engineering Lure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'rendered outage notice' claiming 'website temporarily unavailable' urging download of desktop app — social engineering mechanism requiring behavioral detection on rendered content.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect when legitimate AI platform domains (chatgpt.com, claude.ai) serve unexpected content types (rendered HTML impersonating outage/status pages) or trigger suspicious desktop application downloads. Flag user workflow anomalies: visiting legitimate service → redirected to download page.

suggestion.title: Claude Artifacts ClickFix Command Injection Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article reports 'attacks abusing Claude Artifacts' to host 'ClickFix-style lures that tricked users into executing malicious commands' — specific secondary vector requiring detection rules for command execution post-artifact interaction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for command execution immediately following user click-through from claude.ai/artifacts/* links. Flag PowerShell/cmd.exe invocation with suspicious parameters post-artifact visit. Correlate artifact URL in browser history with command execution timeline (within 5min).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-0257 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs: 'CVE-2026-0257 — match against your vulnerability scanner'. This instruction produced no use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners for CVE-2026-0257 against PAN-OS fleet. Cross-reference with asset inventory and exposure scans to identify internet-facing instances. Flag any unpatched assets; federal due date is 2026-06-01.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized VPN Connection Establishment on PAN-OS
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack outcome: 'establish an unauthorized VPN connection'. This attack step warrants detection but generated no use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for unexpected VPN sessions on PAN-OS from anomalous IPs or outside maintenance windows. Correlate VPN auth logs with CVE-2026-0257 vulnerability status and authentication event gaps to detect exploitation.

suggestion.title: PAN-OS Authentication Bypass Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article core vulnerability is 'authentication bypass'. Pipeline should detect exploitation attempts or access patterns consistent with authentication validation being skipped.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor admin portal logs for authentication anomalies: successful privilege access without corresponding auth events, access from new/unexpected source IPs, or admin actions during non-maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: Botnet C2 Phone-Home Detection (17M+ Devices)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 200 coordinated servers controlling 17 million infected devices for DDoS and proxy abuse. Pipeline captured no kill-chain phase or C2 detection pattern despite explicit infrastructure numbers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect mass-convergence of outbound connections from multiple internal devices to a small set of external C2 servers. Botnet C2 typically shows high fanout (1000s devices → single server) and regular heartbeat intervals. Correlate DNS queries for proxy infrastructure (150 locations mentioned) against known residential proxy providers.

suggestion.title: Residential Proxy Traffic Abuse (Asocks Pattern)
