suggestion.rationale: Standard pre-encryption ransomware step in article scope but zero detection. vssadmin.exe or wmic shadowcopy delete commands should trigger alerts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor execution of vssadmin.exe (delete shadows), wmic.exe (shadowcopy delete), diskshadow.exe, or PowerShell (Remove-Item \\?\GLOBALROOT\Device\HarddiskVolumeShadowCopy*). Alert on execution from scheduled tasks, parent processes with no business justification, or SYSTEM context originating from user-initiated operations.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Child Process Spawning from Task Scheduler
suggestion.rationale: Ransomware delivery vector (scheduled task in title) requires detection of unusual process execution. Article establishes scheduled task as execution mechanism but no process-chain analysis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect children of svchost.exe (Task Scheduler host) or taskeng.exe launching obfuscated scripts (PowerShell with -enc, VBScript with //E:VBScript), compression utilities (7z, WinRAR), or encryption tools (OpenSSL, AES). Alert if command line contains UNC paths, base64, or unusual environment variables.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Scheduled Task Execution
suggestion.rationale: Title emphasizes 'Elevated Privileges' and SYSTEM context. Article indicates privilege escalation to SYSTEM for encryption but no detection for the escalation mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate task creation events with subsequent process execution at SYSTEM privilege level. Flag if task creator was non-SYSTEM account or if created task is first indicator of SYSTEM-level activity from that user context. Monitor for token impersonation or WMI-based task creation.

suggestion.title: Dependency Confusion: Public npm Package Resolution Bypassing Private Registry
suggestion.rationale: Article core topic: attackers publish higher-version malicious packages to public npm registry; systems resolve public versions before private/internal registries. Article phrase: 'abuse dependency confusion to profile developer environments.' No use case flags this resolution behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install/yarn install commands with process or network telemetry to detect unexpected package fetch from public registry when internal/private registry is configured. Flag when installed package version jumps significantly or newly-discovered package name appears in lock files after installation.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance Commands Executed from npm Package Installation Context
suggestion.rationale: Article states packages 'collect reconnaissance data from developer and build environments'; malicious install scripts execute system enumeration. Article phrase: 'profile developer environments.' No use case captures post-install execution of whoami, env, uname, hostname, git config, etc.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes spawned by npm/yarn with system reconnaissance signatures (env var enumeration, user enumeration, git configuration reads, network interface queries). Baseline legitimate npm post-install scripts and alert on anomalous syscalls or process chains from node_modules context.

suggestion.title: Environment Variable and Credential Exfiltration from Build Context
suggestion.rationale: Article: packages target 'build environments' where CI/CD secrets, API keys, and tokens are exposed. Article phrase: 'collect reconnaissance data from developer and build environments.' No detection use case covers credential leakage via HTTP/DNS from npm package code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound network connections initiated by npm/node processes, especially those containing base64-encoded strings, environment variable patterns (CI_*, BUILD_*, AWS_*, GITHUB_*, etc.), or API tokens in DNS queries or HTTP POST payloads. Flag npm package dependencies not in baseline or with unexpected external communication.

suggestion.title: npm Package Metadata Anomaly: Typosquat and Rapid Version Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Dependency confusion requires attackers to publish under legitimate-looking names with aggressive version bumping (e.g., 0.0.1 → 999.0.0). Article doesn't detail naming strategy in visible text, but 33 packages suggests systematic package abuse. This gap: no detection for unusual version climb or lookalike package names.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when package.json or lock files contain package versions with gap >10 minor versions between installed and previously-installed versions, or when newly-installed packages are not in historical baseline of dependencies. Cross-reference against public npm registry reputation feeds.

suggestion.title: Monorepo Private Registry Fallback Detection
suggestion.rationale: Dependency confusion specifically exploits resolution order (public registry checked before private). Article scenario implies monorepo or corporate npm setup with private registries. No UC detects when a package should resolve to private registry but resolved to public instead.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For organizations with private npm registries, monitor and baseline which packages are expected to resolve from private vs. public sources. Alert when a package known to exist in private registry suddenly resolves from public registry (registry audit logs + npm network telemetry), or when npm falls back to public after private registry failure.

suggestion.title: PAN-OS GlobalProtect Authentication Bypass Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-0257 described as 'authentication bypass' under active exploitation; article title signals this is the primary attack vector but pipeline extracted zero kill-chain phases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PAN-OS GlobalProtect gateway logs for unauthenticated session establishment, repeated failed authentication followed by successful entry without valid credentials, or CVE-2026-0257 vulnerability signatures in HTTP/SSL traffic destined to VPN portal. Alert on 401→200 sequences without credential submission or anomalous UserAgent strings targeting GlobalProtect URIs.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploit PAN-OS Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates 'active exploitation' but pipeline reconstructed no post-compromise phases. Auth bypass to active exploitation implies lateral movement or data exfil occurs downstream.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect lateral movement from PAN-OS gateway to internal resources post-auth-bypass. Look for unexpected east-west traffic initiated from GlobalProtect tunnel IPs, RDP/SSH egress from gateway VLAN, or data staging patterns (large file transfers to external IP) originating inside VPN after successful exploitation.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-0257 Exploit Signature Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'under active exploitation' but pipeline extracted zero IOCs and zero exploitation signatures. Should include HTTP request pattern, exploit payload markers, or vulnerable endpoint access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP/HTTPS requests to GlobalProtect endpoints with crafted parameters that trigger CVE-2026-0257 (e.g., malformed session-token, auth-bypass parameter fuzzing, or known PoC request signatures). Alert on 200-OK responses to /sslvpn/api/ URIs lacking prior authentication handshake or with invalid auth headers.

suggestion.title: Suspicious PAN-OS Admin Activity Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Auth bypass implies potential admin-panel access; article describes active exploitation but no use case for post-auth privilege escalation or configuration tampering was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PAN-OS admin CLI/WebUI logs for unauthorized configuration changes, new user creation, firewall rule modifications, or remote backup downloads occurring within seconds of suspicious GlobalProtect session spawning. Alert on any admin action from session originating from external IP via compromised VPN tunnel.

suggestion.title: GlobalProtect Gateway Resource Exhaustion / DoS Indicator
suggestion.rationale: Auth bypass often precedes resource-depletion attacks or tunnel flooding. Article signals active exploitation but pipeline missed operational impact indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PAN-OS system metrics for connection pool exhaustion, session table overflow, or CPU/memory spikes coinciding with bulk CVE-2026-0257 exploitation attempts. Flag abnormal gateway load (>N concurrent VPN sessions from single source, repeated tunnel resets, or sustained high-bandwidth tunnels from attacker IP).

suggestion.title: Package Metadata / Manifest Tampering — Unexpected Dependency or Build Hook Injection
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'Attackers Abuse Trusted Developer Tooling' — implies compromised package definitions, malicious post-install hooks, or transitive dependency injection. Pipeline missed execution-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package manager (npm, pip, NuGet, Cargo) manifests and lock files for unexpected dependency additions, post-install script changes, or references to unfamiliar registries. Alert on process spawning from package unpacking directories or executing scripts bundled in packages.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of Plaintext Secrets and Source Archives from Dev Machine
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states exfiltration of 'source code and secrets' — yet zero collection/exfiltration detections generated. This is the primary impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal egress for dev environments (sanctioned package repos, corporate git, cloud artifact stores). Alert on: bulk tar/zip of .git or entire repos, mass access to .env / secret-manager files, or high-volume data exfil to non-approved IPs/domains.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting from Developer Config Files and Secret Stores
suggestion.rationale: Exfiltration of 'secrets' implies T1552 credential-access. Pipeline identified zero use cases for SSH keys, API tokens, or password-manager vaults accessed from compromised tooling.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for batch or automated access to sensitive credential locations (.ssh, .aws, .kube, .netrc, browser storage, IDE config) by unexpected processes or service accounts. Flag correlations with remote network activity.

suggestion.title: Unvetted Upstream Package Update / Namespace Confusion Attack
suggestion.rationale: Trusted tooling abuse likely involves dependency confusion or malicious package push. Pipeline surfaced zero supply-chain or package-registry IOCs or detection UCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package manager logs and artifact repositories for: installations of unexpectedly-high-version packages, private namespace packages replaced by public-registry versions, or packages signed by new or dormant maintainers. Cross-reference with outbound C2 indicators.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Outbound Network from Build / Development Processes
suggestion.rationale: Exfiltration implies C2 or data-upload channel. Pipeline generated no network-based C2, DNS, or proxy IOCs despite clear exfil requirement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish allowlist of expected egress endpoints for dev tooling (package registries, corporate VCS, cloud storage). Alert on outbound connections from build agents, IDEs, or package managers to non-sanctioned external IPs, newly-registered domains, or suspicious TLDs during normal build windows.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Child Process Spawning from Marimo Notebook
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Attackers Use LLM Agent for Post-Exploitation'—LLM agents executing arbitrary commands via Marimo (Python reactive notebook) must spawn or inject into child processes; no detection rule captured this.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Python or Marimo parent processes (marimo.py, jupyter, ipython) spawning suspicious children (cmd.exe, powershell, sh, curl, wget) or executing dynamic code via subprocess/os.system. Flag parent-child pairs with short time deltas and command strings containing encoded payloads or tool indicators.

suggestion.title: LLM API Calls for Command Execution
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly mentions 'LLM Agent for Post-Exploitation'—agent must communicate with LLM backend (OpenAI, Claude, custom) to receive and execute commands; no network-level detection rule exists.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Python/Marimo processes making HTTPS requests to known LLM API endpoints (api.openai.com, anthropic.com, etc.) or suspicious custom domains. Alert on request payloads containing instruction patterns (e.g., 'execute', 'run command', 'bash', 'powershell') or JSON structures with code/command fields.

suggestion.title: Credential Access via Marimo Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation phase typically includes credential harvesting; article context suggests attackers gain persistent access, implying OS/app credential theft not captured in use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Marimo/Python processes reading sensitive registry hives (SAM, SECURITY), accessing credential manager APIs, or executing credential-dumping tools (mimikatz, Get-Credential, credential_dumper). Alert on file reads from ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, browser profile directories, or password manager DBs.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-39987 Marimo Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly references CVE-2026-39987 but no IOC or pattern for detecting exploitation attempts was extracted; pipeline should surface payload signatures or HTTP request patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify HTTP requests triggering CVE-2026-39987 in Marimo by monitoring for request paths/methods exploiting known Marimo weaknesses (e.g., deserialization, unsafe cell execution). Correlate with 500 errors, timeouts, or successful shell spawns in application logs immediately following HTTP requests.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration via LLM Agent
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation attack chain includes data theft; no detection rule for sensitive data being read and exfiltrated through LLM agent channels.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Marimo/Python processes reading large volumes of files (especially .doc, .xls, .db, .json, .pem, .key) followed within seconds by HTTPS requests to external LLM APIs or C2 domains. Flag if file reads precede API calls with data patterns matching file content (base64, hex, chunked encoding).

suggestion.title: Voice Phishing with Entra Account Compromise Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers executed 'voice phishing (vishing) attack that compromised an employee's Microsoft Entra account' on April 1. No detection proposed for post-vishing account takeover anomalies or impossible-travel sign-ins.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Entra accounts with successful sign-in from new device + geolocation within 6 hours of vishing report. Alert on sign-in from Tor/proxy IPs followed by Salesforce API calls. Detect multiple failed MFA rejections then successful non-MFA fallback.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Bulk Export from Salesforce by Compromised Identity
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attackers 'stole 42 million records from the company's Salesforce instance, including consumer and business customer names, email addresses, physical addresses, phone numbers.' Pipeline ignored the collection phase entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on single Salesforce API session exporting >10k customer records in bulk (CSV/JSON export or batch API calls). Flag if export contains both CPNI and PII fields. Baseline normal export volumes per service account and alert on 100x+ deviation.

suggestion.title: Entra Credential Compromise Followed by SaaS Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: Article shows attacker pivoted from Entra compromise 'to steal' from Salesforce in same attack sequence. Federated identity abuse patterns not addressed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Entra sign-in anomalies (new device/location) with immediate downstream SaaS API activity (Salesforce data access). Alert when single user account accesses 3+ SaaS platforms within 1 hour after compromise indicator.

suggestion.title: Large-Scale Customer PII/CPNI Exfiltration from Telecom Provider
suggestion.rationale: Article documents 'exposed 4.9M unique email addresses along with names, phone numbers and physical addresses' plus 'subset of approximately 85k records originating from an internal employee directory.' No detection for telecom-scale data theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound transfer of structured data (CSV, JSON) containing 1M+ customer records. Alert if Salesforce export process connects to non-whitelisted egress IPs or known anonymization/dark-web infrastructure. Flag CPNI fields transiting unencrypted.

suggestion.title: Dark Web Monitoring for Organizational Data Dumps
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'threat actors claimed they used this access to steal...The group later published the data' on a dark web leak site. No detection for incident confirmation or secondary extortion threats.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor dark web paste sites and ShinyHunters-tracked leak sites for mentions of company name, Salesforce breaches, or customer record dumps. Cross-reference leaked field counts (4.9M emails) with internal data volumes to confirm authenticity.

suggestion.title: ChatGPT Web Summary URL Injection Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'turns ChatGPT Web Summaries into a phishing surface' — pipeline must detect when summaries contain injected or attacker-controlled URLs that deviate from source legitimacy and correlation patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ChatGPT API calls to web-summary endpoints; flag when returned summary content embeds URLs with newly-registered domains, known phishing TLDs, or typosquatting patterns. Correlate with downstream credential access attempts.

suggestion.title: Malicious Prompt Injection for Phishing Content Generation
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability presupposes attacker ability to craft ChatGPT prompts that generate phishing payloads — detect API payloads combining social-engineering keywords with content-generation requests (email, URL, HTML output).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify ChatGPT API requests containing both (a) urgency/authority keywords ('verify identity', 'confirm credentials', 'urgent action') and (b) explicit requests to generate phishing artifacts (shortened URLs, HTML forms, email templates).

suggestion.title: AI-Sourced Phishing Content Forwarded to External Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article implies attackers forward ChatGPT-generated summaries containing phishing content to targets — detect when summaries are exfiltrated to attacker-controlled infrastructure or used as social-engineering lures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag ChatGPT-generated summary content being forwarded to domains registered within 7 days, on DGA blocklists, or with lexical similarity to legitimate targets. Correlate with phishing click-through detection.

suggestion.title: Enumeration of ChatGPT Web Summary Feature Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Attack requires attacker to understand and exploit ChatGPT's specific summarization API — detect reconnaissance patterns: repeated API calls with edge-case URLs, parameter fuzzing, or domain variation to craft exploitable summaries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for burst activity against ChatGPT summarization endpoints with rapidly changing target URLs, parameter mutations, or attempts to summarize attacker-controlled test domains. Flag high-frequency summary requests from single source.

suggestion.title: Google Ads Directing to Malicious AI Shared Links
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'The LLMShare campaign...uses Google ads to direct users searching for ChatGPT to a malicious shared ChatGPT page.' Google Ads abuse is the initial access vector and warrants network/log detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect user clicks on Google Ads followed by navigation to legitimate-domain shared content (e.g., chatgpt.com/s/, claude.ai/artifacts) from suspicious referrers. Monitor for rapid transitions from ad networks to sharing URLs.

suggestion.title: Fake Service Outage Pages Rendered via AI Platforms
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'fake outage notice is rendered through ChatGPT itself' and 'custom HTML page using ChatGPT's rendering capabilities.' This abuse of AI rendering for social engineering is a novel vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag shared AI conversation links (chatgpt.com/s/, claude.ai/artifacts) that render fake system notifications or warnings to download applications. Alert on 'Show code' or 'Remix' controls in rendered pages.

suggestion.title: Content Cloaking: Harmless Content to Security Tools, Malware to Users
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'site uses cloaking to display content only to targeted victims. When security platforms like URLScan visited the URL, they were shown a harmless AR/VR company website.' Detection via evasion fingerprinting required.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify domains serving different content based on User-Agent, referer, or known security tool signatures. Monitor for divergence between sandbox/tool-initiated requests and organic user traffic from same domain.

suggestion.title: VM Detection in Downloaded Malware
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'test of the Windows version...found that it executes various commands to determine whether the device is a legitimate computer or a virtual machine.' VM evasion is behavioral indicator of infostealer/malware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of WMI queries (Get-WmiObject Win32_ComputerSystem, systeminfo, wmic), Hyper-V checks, or virtualization interrogation commands shortly after application execution. Alert on typical VM detection commands from non-IT processes.

suggestion.title: Desktop Application Impersonation via Legitimate Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'website at openew[.]app that impersonates OpenAI's desktop application download portal' and malware 'disguised as the ChatGPT desktop application.' Domain and binary masquerading.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for executables claiming OpenAI/ChatGPT origin (via file metadata, signatures, or naming) downloaded from non-official domains. Alert on ChatGPT-named binaries with anomalous creation paths or unsigned/invalid signatures.

suggestion.title: Claude Artifacts Abused for ClickFix Command Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'researchers...observed attacks abusing Claude Artifacts...to host ClickFix-style lures that tricked users into executing malicious commands.' Artifact sharing abuse for command injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Claude Artifacts links (claude.ai/artifacts) in user click logs and referrer chains. Alert on subsequent execution of shell commands (cmd.exe, powershell.exe) with system administration flags (whoami, icacls, Get-Acl) within minutes of artifact access.

suggestion.title: Exploit attempt against PAN-OS management interface (CVE-2026-0257)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes authentication bypass in PAN-OS; should detect HTTP(S) requests to management endpoints (API, XML-API, or admin UI) with patterns indicative of bypass attempts. Article phrase: 'Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS contains an authentication bypass vulnerability'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PAN-OS management ports (443, 8443) for HTTP requests with suspicious payloads (e.g., XML-API, /api/* endpoints) or response patterns (401/403 followed by 200). Flag requests lacking corresponding successful pre-authentication logs or originating from unexpected source IPs.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized VPN session establishment post-authentication bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers 'establish an unauthorized VPN connection' after authentication bypass. Should detect successful VPN logins without corresponding pre-authentication events or from non-provisioned users.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful VPN authentication (login_success, auth accepted) events that lack corresponding failed authentication attempts immediately prior, or originate from unexpected geographic regions, times, or unprovisioned user accounts.

suggestion.title: Anomalous resource access to PAN-OS protected endpoints without valid session
suggestion.rationale: Article phrase 'bypass security restrictions'—indicates authentication controls can be circumvented. Should detect access to admin/API resources returning 200 OK despite missing or invalid session credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PAN-OS access logs for requests to restricted paths (/api/*, /admin/*, /login*) that receive 200 OK or 302 responses despite missing, expired, or malformed session tokens/cookies in request headers.

suggestion.title: Botnet C2 Beaconing to Seized Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article states '200 servers used to host the infrastructure' were seized and controlled compromised devices. Pipeline should detect outbound connections to known botnet C2 ranges.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on repeated or sustained outbound connections from residential/non-ISP networks to seized server IP ranges. Narrow for non-standard ports (>10000) and low inter-packet variance (C2 heartbeat pattern). Correlate with known Asocks hosting provider ranges if available.

suggestion.title: Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) Attack Coordination
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states botnet was 'used for...distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks.' Pipeline missed detection for coordinated outbound attack traffic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect synchronized outbound traffic spikes from multiple IPs in the residential proxy range to single destination IP/domain within short window. Flag for unusual packet size/rate ratios and repeated SYN floods or HTTP floods.

suggestion.title: Residential Proxy Abuse and Traffic Tunneling
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'malicious traffic proxying' and '7 million IP addresses' for proxy service. Missing detection for suspicious tunnel/proxy pattern establishment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on inbound SOCKS5/HTTP proxy connections from suspicious sources, particularly from ISPs/ranges known to host Asocks clients. Flag high-volume, low-latency proxy relay chains. Look for proxy client software installation without admin/user consent.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Mining Process and Pool Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article states botnet used for 'cryptocurrency mining.' Pipeline entirely missed impact-phase resource hijacking detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect high-CPU processes spawning without user context, communicating to known mining pool domains/IPs (stratum, getwork protocols on ports 3333, 8332, 9999, 14433). Correlate with unusual memory/GPU utilization and parent process mismatches (svchost.exe, rundll32.exe).

suggestion.title: Default Credential Exploitation on Networked Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article's remediation guidance ('ensure default credentials have been changed') signals weak-password initial compromise vector. No detection for brute force or default credential attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on repeated login attempts using known-default credentials (admin/admin, root/root, admin/password) against SSH, Telnet, HTTP admin panels on IoT/networking devices. Flag successful logins from unusual geolocations or ASNs associated with proxy infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Firmware/Software Update Bypass or Outdated Device Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends 'latest firmware update has been applied' as mitigation, implying initial compromise exploited unpatched firmware. Pipeline missed vulnerability-exploitation detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect devices running firmware versions with known critical CVEs targeted by botnet (e.g., router, IoT device firmware <6 months old from CVE disclosure). Alert on exploitation signatures (e.g., unusual system calls post-firmware load, web shell upload attempts to admin interfaces).

suggestion.title: Prototype-chain method access in Node.js script execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attack: 'Buffer.call.call({}.__lookupGetter__, Buffer, "__proto__")' and '__lookupSetter__' calls. These specific methods (__lookupGetter__, __lookupSetter__) are non-standard destructive patterns in legitimate Node code but are hallmarks of this sandbox-escape technique. Zero existing UC detects this attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Node.js processes executing code that contains __lookupGetter__ or __lookupSetter__ method calls on Object prototypes, especially when combined with Buffer manipulation. Look for ProcessCommandLine or process environment containing these keywords, or Node debug/error logs showing TypeError constructor access from within vm2 context.

suggestion.title: Node.js ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE error preceding shell process spawn
suggestion.rationale: Article mechanism relies on 'Node.js's ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE Error' to trigger TypeError constructor leak. Detectable as: (1) Node.exe process generates error-type event, (2) immediately followed by unexpected child shell process. Temporal correlation would catch exploitation attempt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Node.js process that logs or throws ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE error within <100ms of spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or bash. Requires event-log correlation; look for timestamps within same second and parent-child process relationship.

suggestion.title: vm2 or NodeVM module instantiation followed by shell spawning
suggestion.rationale: Article targets vm2 library explicitly. Detection should look for evidence of vm2 import/instantiation (e.g., 'new VM()' or 'require("vm2")' in command line or script) followed by unexpected shell or system call. No existing UC detects this module-level trigger.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Node.js process with InitiatingProcessCommandLine or ProcessCommandLine containing 'vm2' or 'NodeVM' or 'new VM(' or 'require("vm2")' that subsequently spawns shell or creates suspicious files. Restrictive to vm2-specific context to avoid generic Node.js FPs.

suggestion.title: Buffer constructor and __proto__ access anomaly in vm2 sandbox context
suggestion.rationale: Core attack is accessing Buffer's __proto__ to escape sandbox isolation. If JavaScript engine logging or script analysis is available, this specific pattern (Buffer + __proto__ + constructor chain walk) is extremely rare in legitimate code.
log_sources: DeviceProcessEvents (if running Node with debug flags)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Suspicious pattern: sequence of calls attempting to access or modify Buffer object's prototype chain, especially calls to __lookupGetter__ or __lookupSetter__ on Buffer or related objects. Would require process argument inspection (--inspect, --expose-internals flags) or script static analysis.

suggestion.title: Node.js spawning OS shell with enumeration commands — vm2 sandbox escape
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes "nesting:true without explicit require still allows full RCE" and kill-chain ends at OS shell enumeration (whoami, id, etc). Article already shows this UC (UC_23_2) but pipeline failed to extract/generate it.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect when node.exe or node process spawns cmd.exe, powershell.exe, sh, bash with enumeration commands (whoami, id, uname, ipconfig, /etc/passwd). This is post-exploitation activity following vm2 RCE escape.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable vm2 package (≤3.11.3) present on host
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies vulnerable vm2 versions. UC_23_3 was listed in recommendations but pipeline failed to extract it. This is the weapon/delivery phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for presence of vm2 package.json or nodevm.js in node_modules across all hosts. Combined with application inventory, identify which hosts run vulnerable versions ≤3.11.3 and lack patches.

suggestion.title: Node.js application using vm2 with nesting:true but no require option
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability is the strict equality bypass: `options.require === false` check fails when `require` is undefined. Article states: 'The check uses strict equality (options.require === false), which is trivially bypassed by omitting the require option entirely.' Pipeline should detect actual code patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Static analysis or runtime inspection of Node app code: detect vm2 script execution with {nesting: true} in options but no require field present, or require field set to undefined/true. This is the specific bypass mechanism.

suggestion.title: JavaScript execution within vm2 HostVM invoking child_process module
suggestion.rationale: Article lists `child_process` and `execSync` in hunt patterns (UC_23_2 payload). JavaScript inside the sandbox escaping to OS requires child_process invocation. Pipeline should correlate this to T1059.007.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for JavaScript code within vm2 VM context attempting to require() or access child_process module. Correlate with subsequent shell process spawning by parent Node process.

suggestion.title: Node.js require('process').getBuiltinModule() sandbox escape in vm2 contexts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'denylist misses process and inspector/promises. Both can be used from sandboxed code to reach host-side execution primitives' and describes require('process').getBuiltinModule as the primary exploitation method. UC_21_4 hunts command-line strings but misses eval'd code patterns and file-based payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Node.js processes for code patterns calling require('process').getBuiltinModule() or accessing process.moduleLoadList outside legitimate npm contexts. Flag if found in eval/exec contexts or dynamically loaded files outside node_modules/.

suggestion.title: Node.js inspector module access and promise-based API abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'inspector/promises' as explicit denylist bypass vector used to reach 'host-side execution primitives.' Current UCs miss direct inspector module access patterns that precede exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Node.js process loading require('inspector') or require('inspector/promises'), particularly followed by open(), connect(), or Session.post() calls. Correlate with subsequent child process spawning or file creation.

suggestion.title: Denylist bypass via module metadata and prototype chain manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability as 'denylist bypass' attempting to access specifically-blocked modules (module, worker_threads, cluster, vm, repl). Detection should focus on evasion techniques attempting indirect access to denied APIs, not just post-escape execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Node.js code patterns attempting to bypass blocklist via getBuiltinModule(), accessing process.bindings(), prototype pollution, or indirect require() paths that resolve to blocked modules. Look for multiple require() attempts on the specific denied modules list.

suggestion.title: Malicious JavaScript file delivery to Node.js execution contexts
suggestion.rationale: Article describes sandboxed code executing exploit; PoC would arrive as JavaScript file. Article lists T1204.002 (User Execution: Malicious File) as technique. Need detection for suspicious .js/.mjs files with embedded PoC indicators created by or in proximity to Node.js processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for .js/.mjs file creation in temp directories, process working directories, or unexpected locations by non-npm processes. If file content inspection available, flag files containing getBuiltinModule, inspector/promises, or Runtime.evaluate strings.

suggestion.title: vm2 module initialization in suspicious runtime contexts
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability allows 'attackers to write code which can escape from the VM2 sandbox.' Missing hunt for the initialization/import phase where vm2 is loaded in suspicious contexts. Article narrative: 'allows attackers to write code'—this implies the attack requires vm2 to be instantiated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for node.exe/nodejs.exe process execution of scripts that require/import vm2 module in combination with dynamic code evaluation or script.run() calls. Correlate with new .js file writes to non-standard directories or temp paths.

suggestion.title: Promise.prototype or Symbol.species mutation in active JavaScript execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability is caused by missing `resetPromiseSpecies` call and `localPromise` constructor mishandling. This is the core technical exploit mechanism: 'localPromise constructor was changed to call this.then(undefined, eater).' Direct detection of Promise prototype modification is missing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for JavaScript code patterns that assign to Promise.prototype, manipulate Symbol.species, or modify the Promise constructor behavior. Particularly sensitive when these patterns appear in scripts loaded from untrusted sources or execute with elevated privileges in node contexts.

suggestion.title: vm2 module absence in production environments with sandbox dependencies
suggestion.rationale: Inverse hunt: organizations that depend on vm2 for security-critical sandboxing (e.g., code evaluation services) should have inventory of all endpoints running vm2. Article vulnerability affects all <=3.11.3 versions. Detecting where vm2 is *missing* (presumed patched to 3.11.4+) validates remediation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Regular asset inventory sweep for endpoints that *historically* had vm2 installed (from baseline or previous scans) but no longer show it in current inventory scan, or show version >3.11.3. Generates positive coverage metric for remediation tracking.

suggestion.title: Unpatched vm2 instances in JavaScript execution contexts across enterprise
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerable range <=3.11.3. UC_24_1 attempts this but incorrectly. Need enterprise-wide software discovery correlating package manifests, npm audit output, and vulnerability databases to identify all vulnerable vm2 installations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse package management manifests and lock files across all endpoints for vm2 presence, extract precise version numbers, correlate against CVE database to identify systems running <=3.11.3. Generate inventory report grouped by department/team for patch prioritization.

suggestion.title: Exploitation attempt signatures: thisPromise.then + resetPromiseSpecies absence pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article details the exact vulnerability: 'localPromise constructor was changed to call this.then(undefined, eater)' without subsequent 'resetPromiseSpecies' call. No UC directly hunts for this technical pattern in active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for .js files or runtime bytecode containing the pattern: Promise instance receives .then() call without preceding resetPromiseSpecies() or Promise.setPrototypeOf() reset. Can be detected via AST analysis of downloaded scripts or memory scanning if vm2 runtime is instrumented.

suggestion.title: JSPI WebAssembly module load + Promise.finally() call sequence — vm2 escape attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article describes JSPI-backed Promise reaching `.finally()` as the core exploit mechanism: 'JSPI-backed Promise can reach Promise.prototype.finally()...bypasses expected Promise-species hardening.' No UC detects WebAssembly module instantiation paired with Promise manipulation from Node process.
log_sources: DeviceProcessEvents (with module load callback telemetry if exposed)
Custom ETW / DTrace / strace output from Node process
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Node.js process loads WebAssembly.Suspending or WebAssembly.promising module (JSPI) followed by execution of Promise.prototype.finally() call graph within same transaction. This is a post-exploit signal: if JSPI is loaded synchronously within a vm2 context, the exploit has likely executed. Pair with Promise.prototype.finally override detection if DLL/module-level hooks available.

suggestion.title: vm2 module version downgrade or replacement — CVE-2026-47210 bypass attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability fixed in vm2 > 3.11.3. Attacker may attempt to downgrade installed version or replace vm2 with backdoored copy. Current UC_22_3 detects presence but not version changes over time.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm/yarn commands uninstalling or downgrading vm2 module version (parent_process = npm/yarn, arguments contain 'uninstall vm2' or 'install vm2@<3.11.4'). Alert on file modification timestamps of vm2 package.json or index.js after initial baseline with content hash mismatch. Correlate with lack of prior npm audit/update logs.

suggestion.title: Node.js async runtime feature enumeration — JSPI availability probe
suggestion.rationale: Exploit requires WebAssembly JSPI support ('runtimes exposing WebAssembly JSPI'). Attacker must probe for JSPI availability before triggering exploit. Detection of `WebAssembly.Suspending` or `WebAssembly.promising` property access in untrusted script context is missing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: vm2 script execution followed by JavaScript attempting to access `globalThis.WebAssembly.Suspending`, `globalThis.WebAssembly.promising`, or checking `typeof WebAssembly.Suspending !== 'undefined'`. This is a capability probe before exploit. Pair with process command-line containing --experimental-wasm-jspi or similar Node flags.

suggestion.title: vm2 Host object reference escape — Promise constructor override
suggestion.rationale: Article alludes to 'host-originate' object exposure through species bypass. Core exploitation step is overriding Promise constructor or Promise.prototype to access host realm. No UC detects Promise prototype manipulation or constructor override within vm2 sandboxed context.
log_sources: Script execution logs with Promise constructor call stacks
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Untrusted code executing within vm2 context modifies Promise.prototype.finally, Promise.prototype.then, or Promise[Symbol.species] descriptor. This is a direct attempt to hijack Promise contract. Pair detection with spawning of shell/LOLBin (UC_22_2) to indicate successful escape: Promise prototype mod + shell spawn = confirmed exploit.

suggestion.title: PraisonAI execute_code() called with `__self__` accessor in payload
suggestion.rationale: Article states exploit uses `print.__self__` to retrieve builtins module. UC_11_6 detects the signature in command-line, but misses detection at network/API request layer if PraisonAI service logs incoming payloads. Suggested: 'Python code submitted to PraisonAI execute_code() endpoint containing string literals like `__self__`, `vars()`, `__import__` in suspicious combination.'
log_sources: HTTP request logs from PraisonAI service
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor API logs or application stdout for user-submitted Python code payloads to execute_code() that contain `__self__` or `vars(print`. Correlate with successful subprocess spawn. This detects the *attempt* before OS execution.

suggestion.title: Python process reading /proc/self or builtins introspection post-execute_code
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'retrieve the real Python builtins module, from which __import__ can be extracted via vars()'. This describes introspection of the Python runtime itself. Detection should key on file access patterns or bytecode signatures post-sandbox entry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In child processes spawned from Python interpreters tagged to PraisonAI, detect reads of /proc/self/environ, /proc/self/fd, or imports of `builtins`, `inspect`, `sys._getframe`. These are necessary precursors to sandbox escape.

suggestion.title: PraisonAI version advisory lookup + behavioral correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article notes vulnerability is in v1.6.37 and earlier. UC_11_4 detects package version, but no UC combines version + observed behavior (e.g., subprocess spawning with discovery commands). Article: 'defeating the sandbox' implies absence of expected isolation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert if PraisonAI ≤1.6.39 is detected AND within 1 hour child processes spawn from the Python interpreter with shell commands (sh/bash). Absence of sandbox markers + vulnerable version + shell spawn = high-confidence breach attempt.

suggestion.title: PraisonAI Flask server config inspection — authentication disabled flag detected
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'authentication disabled by default' but no UC examines configuration file contents or runtime parameters. Detecting deployment configs with auth=false or authentication disabled is a direct artifact hunt. Article: 'emits a Flask API server with authentication disabled by default.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file creation/modification of PraisonAI YAML or JSON configs, and command-line arguments to praisonai deploy, for flags or values disabling authentication (e.g., 'auth: false', '--no-auth', 'authentication: off'). Correlate with UC_12_3 to link deployment commands to insecure configs.

suggestion.title: External network scanning of port 8005 — LLM service enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article describes public-facing surface (0.0.0.0 bind) but no UC detects reconnaissance probes to the port. Attackers discover exposed services via port scans or vulnerability scanners. Missing reconnaissance-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound SYN scans, connection probes, or connection-refused attempts to TCP/8005 from external sources. Threshold: more than 2 failed connection attempts from a single external IP in a 5-minute window. Correlate with CVE-Detector, Shodan, or masscan user agents if available.

suggestion.title: PraisonAI package version monitoring — vulnerable release detection
suggestion.rationale: Article references two CVEs but no UC detects installation/upgrade of vulnerable PraisonAI versions. Package manager logs and pip output are available sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor pip install/upgrade commands targeting praisonai package; extract version from command-line or stdout/stderr. Flag installations of versions matching CVE-2026-47393 and CVE-2026-44338 affected ranges. Correlate with UC_12_3 (deploy execution) to confirm vulnerable version was deployed.

suggestion.title: Known CVE scanners probing PraisonAI endpoints — active vulnerability assessment
suggestion.rationale: UC_12_5 filters for CVE-Detector user agent but buries this signal. Detecting active vulnerability scanning of the endpoints warrants its own hunt, as it indicates external reconnaissance by automated tools.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to /chat or /agents endpoints with user agents matching known scanners: CVE-Detector, CVE-Searcher, Shodan, Censys, masscan, nikto, nmap, nessus. Even unauthenticated probes count as evidence of external reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: Sensitive data in LLM responses — context exfiltration via /chat endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article describes /chat and /agents endpoints as exposed but no UC detects abnormal response patterns. Attackers with endpoint access can craft prompts to exfiltrate secrets, environment variables, or training data from the model context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP response bodies from /chat endpoint for high-entropy payloads, environment variable patterns (AWS_SECRET, DATABASE_URL), file paths (/etc, /home), or credential-like patterns (base64 blobs, JWT headers). Detect via DLP or response-size anomalies (LLM chat responses >50KB may indicate exfiltration).

suggestion.title: PraisonAI Platform: failed cross-workspace resource access probe
suggestion.rationale: Article describes IDOR in nested resources (agents, issues, projects under `/api/v1/workspaces/{id}/...`). Attacker would probe with 403/401 responses before successful exploitation. Missing detection for enumeration/scanning phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate 403/401 responses on workspace resource endpoints from single user/src across multiple distinct resource IDs or workspace IDs within short time window (5–10 min). High 403 volume followed by 200 success suggests transition from reconnaissance to exploitation.

suggestion.title: PraisonAI Platform: self-service privilege escalation (member → owner role)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'member-role privilege escalation.' UC_9_2 detects modifications to other users' roles; this detects self-promotion pattern (user modifying their own role via member endpoint without admin approval).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when a user issues PATCH/POST to `/api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/members/{same_user_id}` with role field mutated from member/contributor to owner/admin. Requires parsing request body (role update) and matching user from auth context to target ID.

suggestion.title: PraisonAI Platform: new account rapid workspace resource enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article describes privilege escalation; UC_9_4 covers registration + action. This detects new account immediately probing workspace/resource boundaries (automation/scripted attack pattern) as distinct from legitimate onboarding.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate account creation (POST `/api/v1/auth/register`, 200-299) with ≥10 distinct GET requests to workspace or resource endpoints within 60 seconds from same IP/user agent. Legitimate users onboard gradually; attackers enumerate fast.

suggestion.title: PraisonAI Platform: resource access without workspace membership
suggestion.rationale: Core IDOR: 'The dependency only checks that the caller is a member of the workspace_id in the URL prefix,' but does not validate the caller owns/can access the nested resource. Missing detection for accessing resources where caller has no explicit membership grant.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline: for each user, maintain whitelist of workspace_ids they are explicitly members of (infer from successful member list queries or admin audit logs). Alert on GET/PATCH to resource under workspace_id not in user's membership list. High precision if membership truth is available in logs.

suggestion.title: PraisonAI Platform: cross-workspace bulk data access
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'Data from Information Repositories' (T1213) and 'Data from Cloud Storage' (T1530) as outcomes. Attackers exploiting IDOR for bulk exfil would show: many sequential GETs on resources across multiple workspaces in high volume.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Within 30-min window, detect single user/src issuing ≥50 GET requests to resource endpoints (agents, issues, projects, dependencies, labels) spanning ≥3 distinct workspaces. Filter out legitimate batch-export patterns (known admin accounts, scheduled jobs) via whitelist.

suggestion.title: JWT Token Forgery via Hardcoded Secret
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers can forge tokens for 'any user' using the known default secret 'dev-secret-change-change-me'; no hunt provided for attempted token validation with this literal secret string or signature bypass indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for JWT tokens signed with the hardcoded key 'dev-secret-change-me' or requests presenting tokens for workspaces/users not matching the authenticated account. Track auth failures followed by successful access to /auth/me or /workspaces/* endpoints within same session.

suggestion.title: PLATFORM_ENV=dev Configuration Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'the default value of PLATFORM_ENV is dev, so the check is silently bypassed.' No hunt detects processes/containers running with unset or explicitly dev-mode PLATFORM_ENV without corresponding PLATFORM_JWT_SECRET override.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify praisonai-platform processes with PLATFORM_ENV unset or set to 'dev' AND PLATFORM_JWT_SECRET either absent from environment or set to non-secret default. Correlate with listening HTTP ports.

suggestion.title: Cross-Workspace Lateral Movement via Forged Auth
suggestion.rationale: Article describes UC_8_3 attack but without detailed behavioral patterns: 'cross-tenant workspace operations from single source IP.' Need hunt for single source accessing 3+ distinct workspace IDs via /workspaces/* with destructive methods (DELETE/PATCH/POST) that violate workspace isolation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests from single source accessing multiple workspace IDs (regex /workspaces/[0-9a-f-]{8,}) with DELETE/PATCH/POST methods within short window; especially if authenticated user differs from workspace owner or workspace_id is enumerated sequentially.

suggestion.title: Non-owner member successfully escalates own role to owner in single PATCH
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The require_workspace_member(workspace_id) defaults to min_role=member and is never overridden.' Direct self-escalation by any member is the core exploit. Detect a user with member role modifying their own role to owner.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on PATCH /workspaces/{id}/members/{user_id} where user_id matches the authenticated user, request body contains role=owner, and the user's pre-request role was member. Correlate with identity store to confirm privilege elevation occurred.

suggestion.title: Workspace owner removal cascade: attacker demotes all existing admins post-escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article use case UC_7_3 explicitly describes 'legitimate-owner demotion chain.' After escalating to owner, attacker removes competing owners to prevent detection/reversal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline legitimate owner count. Alert when a user recently promoted to owner (within 30 min) executes >=2 PATCH requests demoting or downgrading other owners in same workspace. Threshold: 2 demotions correlates well with defensive attack behavior vs. admin maintenance.

suggestion.title: API endpoint authorization bypass: non-owner issuing workspace-level writes post-member promotion
suggestion.rationale: After privilege escalation, attacker has write access to workspace resources (agents, projects, etc.). Article mentions T1136.003 (create cloud account), T1098 (account manipulation). Detect new member accounts created immediately after role escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful PATCH member role->owner with subsequent POST requests to /workspaces/{id}/members (create new members) within 5 minutes from the same source. Alert on attacker creating new high-privilege accounts to establish persistent backdoor access.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized AI Assistant Tool Usage Detected
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions shadow AI risk: 'Providing sanctioned tools also helps reduce shadow AI by discouraging developers from turning to unmanaged consumer services.' Pipeline should surface detection for unapproved AI APIs (Claude, OpenAI direct calls, ChatGPT, etc.) in CI/CD logs or local environments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor developer workstations and CI runners for API calls to non-sanctioned AI services (claude.ai, openai.com, etc.) that bypass the GitHub Copilot license infrastructure. Look for environment variables containing API keys for competing tools or curl/Python requests to unapproved AI endpoints.

suggestion.title: Pre-commit Hook Disabled or Modified
suggestion.rationale: Article describes custom pre-commit hooks as critical: 'Building on Snyk's built-in secure-at-inception hooks, Esaie extended the capability with custom pre-commit hooks.' Pipeline should detect tampering with or removal of security hooks before code commits.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on modifications to .git/hooks/ directory or deletion of pre-commit/commit-msg hook files. Flag execution of git commands with --no-verify flag or environment variable overrides (GIT_TRACE_PERFORMANCE, SKIP_HOOKS). Correlate with Snyk/security scan bypass patterns.

suggestion.title: Security Scanning Tool Bypassed or Output Ignored
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'Before this even makes it to the PR, I want it to scan and catch everything.' Pipeline should detect attempts to suppress, ignore, or skip embedded security scans before commit/push.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for patterns indicating Snyk/security scan suppression: '--severity-threshold 0', 'snyk test --json | jq .ignore', environment variable GIT_AUTHOR_DATE manipulation, or git amend/rebase operations immediately after failed security checks. Look for rapid push-to-PR cycles that skip local scanning.

suggestion.title: LinkedIn Spearphishing Link Click Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes JINX-0164 using LinkedIn social engineering as attack vector. No UC generated for detecting abnormal LinkedIn message patterns or unusual link-clicks from social platforms, which is the entry vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect users clicking links from LinkedIn messages that lead to credential-harvesting or malware-staging domains. Correlate LinkedIn web traffic with subsequent downloads of suspicious binaries or ZIP archives on macOS systems, especially from non-standard TLDs or recently registered domains.

suggestion.title: macOS Malware Execution from Downloads
suggestion.rationale: Article describes deployment of 'custom macOS malware' but pipeline generated no detection for malware execution post-delivery. Typical attack flow: LinkedIn → phishing link → malware binary download → execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for parent-child process spawning from /Users/*/Downloads or /tmp directories on macOS. Detect execution of unsigned or recently-signed binaries that communicate outbound shortly after launch, especially if the binary was downloaded in same session as malicious link-click from social platform.

suggestion.title: macOS Persistence via LaunchAgent or Cron Job
suggestion.rationale: Article implies ongoing compromise (custom malware suggests C2 capability). Pipeline missed persistence mechanisms typical of macOS malware: LaunchAgent plist creation or cron persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation or modification of ~/Library/LaunchAgents/*.plist files with suspicious commands (especially those referencing recently-downloaded binaries). Detect cron job modifications in /var/at/jobs or .zprofile/.bash_profile additions that execute remote commands or staged malware.

suggestion.title: Unsigned Executable Spawning Network Connection
suggestion.rationale: Custom macOS malware likely communicates with attacker C2. No UC for detecting unsigned/self-signed processes initiating outbound connections, a hallmark of post-delivery behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unsigned or code-signed-by-untrusted-cert macOS processes opening TCP/UDP connections to non-RFC1918 IPs, especially on non-standard ports (8080, 8888, 443 with invalid cert chains). Correlate process spawn time with network initiation to identify C2 callbacks within minutes of malware execution.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated Shell Command Execution on macOS
suggestion.rationale: Custom malware likely uses shell scripts or base64-encoded commands for execution/persistence. Article describes malware deployment but no UC for detecting obfuscated bash/zsh commands.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for /bin/bash or /bin/zsh spawning with arguments containing base64-encoded strings, hex-encoded payloads, or pipe chains to eval/osascript. Flag execution of shell commands with unusual entropy or containing PowerShell-style obfuscation techniques ported to macOS.

suggestion.title: HTTPSpy Proxy Tool Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly names HTTPSpy as deployed by Kimsuky; no mention in pipeline IOCs or UCs despite being a marquee indicator. This is a new or updated tool in Kimsuky's arsenal requiring immediate detection coverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTPSpy process execution, network connections to known HTTPSpy C2 IPs/domains, and characteristic HTTP proxy command patterns. Correlate with Kimsuky-attributed infrastructure if available. Look for parent processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, rundll32.exe) launching proxy tools.

suggestion.title: HelloDoor Tool Activity and Remote Access
suggestion.rationale: Article title lists HelloDoor as expansion of Kimsuky's arsenal; no IOC, no use case generated despite being a named malware/tool.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HelloDoor process names, file hashes, registry modifications, and associated network beacon traffic. Cross-reference with Kimsuky C2 infrastructure. Expect non-standard port usage and potential use of legitimate services for transport.

suggestion.title: Abuse of VS Code Remote Tunnels for C2 / Remote Access
suggestion.rationale: Article title specifically mentions VS Code Tunnels as part of Kimsuky's expanded toolkit. Abuse of legitimate development tools for C2 is a critical defense-evasion pattern that the pipeline missed entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect VS Code / codespace-related processes initiating unexpected network connections. Monitor for vsls-agent.exe or tunnel processes from non-development contexts, particularly from suspicious parent processes. Alert on connections to Kimsuky-attributed C2 domains via VS Code tunnel infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Kimsuky Tool Deployment via Malware Distribution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes expansion of Kimsuky arsenal (HTTPSpy, HelloDoor); implies delivery mechanism not captured by pipeline. Missing IOCs on how these tools are dropped/executed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious attachment downloads or email macros that trigger secondary tool deployment. Look for Kimsuky's known phishing/spear-phishing patterns and post-compromise execution chains that deploy HTTPSpy/HelloDoor.

suggestion.title: Network Signature Detection for HTTPSpy / HelloDoor C2 Traffic
suggestion.rationale: No network IOCs (IPs, domains, FQDNs) extracted by pipeline despite article title indicating malware deployment. C2 communications are fundamental to detecting these tools.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify C2 domains, IP ranges, and beacon patterns associated with HTTPSpy and HelloDoor. Monitor DNS queries, TLS handshakes, and HTTP/HTTPS traffic metadata for known and suspected Kimsuky infrastructure. Use domain frequency and ASN analysis to surface new C2 nodes.

suggestion.title: Suspicious NuGet/npm Package Download from Unusual Source
suggestion.rationale: Article describes malicious packages distributed via package managers (NuGet and npm). Need detection for package install from untrusted registries or with mismatched publisher metadata (T1195 supply chain compromise signature).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for package manager invocations (nuget.exe, npm.exe, dotnet.exe) downloading from non-standard package sources or URLs. Flag discrepancies between package name and publisher metadata, or installations of packages newly registered to untrusted accounts.

suggestion.title: Credential Dumping / Banking Credential Exfiltration Post-Package Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states packages steal 'banking credentials'. Need detection for process access to credential stores, registry queries to Local Security Authority (LSA), or suspicious LSASS memory reads after malicious package execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child processes spawned by package manager or .NET runtime attempting mimikatz-like credential dumping (OpenProcess on LSASS, registry reads of SAM/SECURITY hive, or SecretManagementModule queries). Correlate with package installation timestamps.

suggestion.title: Cloud Secret / Environment Variable Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article headline mentions 'Cloud Secrets' as attack target. Need detection for processes reading environment variables (AWS_ACCESS_KEY, AZURE_*, GCP_*), config files, or cloud credential files (.aws/credentials, ~/.kube/config).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for non-cloud-agent processes reading cloud credential environment variables or accessing credential files. Flag unexpected child processes of package manager reading .aws, .azure, .gcp, or .kube directories, or environment variable enumeration followed by outbound HTTPS to uncommon destinations.

suggestion.title: Malicious Package Obfuscation / Code Reflection Evasion
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain malware typically uses reflection, dynamic loading, or string obfuscation to evade static analysis. Article does not detail obfuscation but it is a standard TTPs in package attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect .NET runtime (CLR) executing code via System.Reflection.Assembly.LoadFrom, Emit, or Process.Start with heavily obfuscated/base64-encoded payloads. Look for parent-child relationships between managed processes and suspicious system binaries (cmd.exe, powershell.exe) spawned with no command-line arguments visible.

suggestion.title: NuGet / npm Package Persistence via Project File Injection
suggestion.rationale: Malicious packages can inject themselves into .csproj, package.json, or .nuspec files to persist across rebuilds and developer machine reinstalls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected modifications to .csproj, .nuspec, package.json, or packages.config files by package manager processes or post-package scripts. Flag additions of non-standard dependencies or post-install scripts that invoke curl, wget, or PowerShell to fetch remote payloads.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Shared Development Credentials in VCS
suggestion.rationale: Stolen banking and cloud credentials are often committed to Git repositories as build secrets or hardcoded in CI/CD pipelines. Attackers may use these to pivot.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect exfiltrated credentials being used to authenticate to non-local Git repositories, cloud consoles, or VPN endpoints from machines that did not previously have those credentials. Cross-correlate stolen credentials (from package malware) against authentication logs in CI/CD systems, AWS/Azure console logins, and Kubernetes cluster access.

suggestion.title: Detect GREYVIBE Malware Execution via Suspicious Process Chains
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'AI-Powered Cyberattacks' but zero execution-phase use cases generated. Standard detection for any attributed threat actor campaign.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor process creation chains from Ukraine-targeted initial access vectors. Alert on anomalous parent-child relationships, living-off-the-land execution (PowerShell, WMI), and injection patterns consistent with AI-assisted payload obfuscation.

suggestion.title: Detect GREYVIBE Command-and-Control Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: AI-powered attacks require attacker control infrastructure; title contains no IOCs and pipeline generated zero C2 use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Once IOCs are extracted, alert on network connections from Ukrainian networks to GREYVIBE-attributed C2 infrastructure. Establish behavioral baselines for encrypted/obfuscated C2 traffic patterns.

suggestion.title: Detect GREYVIBE Credential Harvesting via Phishing
suggestion.rationale: Russia-linked group targeting Ukraine typically leverages spearphishing; pipeline produced zero credential-access detections despite clear threat actor designation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on malicious attachments or URLs in email campaigns targeting Ukrainian government, energy, defense sectors. Correlate with suspicious login attempts (failed + successful) from recipients within 48 hours of campaign delivery.

suggestion.title: SYSTEM Scheduled Task Creation for Ransomware Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Ransomware Uses SYSTEM Scheduled Task to Encrypt Local Drives With Elevated Privileges' — the core attack vector (T1053.005 + execution context) entirely absent from pipeline output
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for schtasks.exe or Task Scheduler API calls creating tasks with Principal set to SYSTEM or NETWORK SERVICE. Correlate task creation (Event 4698) with executable references outside System32, temp dirs, or admin-approved paths. Alert on task actions containing obfuscated commands or indirect execution (e.g., cmd.exe /c).

suggestion.title: Elevated Privilege Ransomware Task Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly emphasizes 'elevated privileges' and SYSTEM-level context as enabling mechanism — privilege-escalation detection use case required to flag when low-privilege user triggers high-privilege encryption via scheduled task
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect scheduled task execution (Event 4698 + task runtime correlation) where parent is System/svchost, child process runs as SYSTEM, but task was created or triggered by non-admin user. Flag RunLevel=Highest in task definition when creator is unprivileged.

suggestion.title: Bulk File Encryption from Task Scheduler Child Process
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Encrypt Local Drives' — the encryption impact phase (T1486) requires secondary detection tying file activity back to scheduled task lineage
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process spawned by Task Scheduler (parent svchost.exe with SYSTEM token) executing rapid file modifications across multiple drives/volumes. Flag high write counts to diverse file extensions (.doc, .xls, .pdf, .jpg, .zip, etc.) within short timeframe, plus creation of ransom notes or .key/.encrypted files.

suggestion.title: Ransomware Persistence via RunOnce or Scheduled Task at System Startup
suggestion.rationale: Article does not explicitly describe persistence mechanism, but SYSTEM-privilege scheduled task is a persistence vector warranting detection (T1547.005 or T1053.005 configured for logon/startup)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect scheduled task creation with triggers set to system startup, user logon, or idle time, especially if action runs as SYSTEM and executable is in user-writable path or renamed/obfuscated binary.

suggestion.title: LLM API Request Abuse - Malware/Payload Generation Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes GREYVIBE 'leverage ChatGPT and Google Gemini to fuel cyberattacks' — direct evidence of adversary using public LLM APIs for attack content generation. No UCs generated to detect this vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound HTTPS traffic to known LLM endpoints (api.openai.com, gemini.google.com, etc.) from systems consistent with attacker infrastructure (rapid API calls, token reuse patterns, requests for code/obfuscation/shellcode generation). Profile API key patterns and session anomalies.

suggestion.title: Threat Actor Infrastructure Registration — GREYVIBE TTPs
suggestion.rationale: Actor name GREYVIBE mentioned but no reconnaissance UC for OSINT-based detection of associated domains, cloud buckets, or code repos. Title alone insufficient to generate C-level IOCs; pipeline should have flagged the need for manual IOC discovery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline GREYVIBE IOCs via threat intel feeds and passive DNS. Monitor for inbound communications (phishing, credential phishing emails) originating from newly registered domains or infrastructure overlapping known GREYVIBE TLDs, mail servers, and ASNs.

suggestion.title: LLM-Generated Phishing Content Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates LLMs fueling attacks; attack chain likely includes social engineering or phishing with AI-crafted content. Pipeline failed to hypothesize detection for grammatical/stylistic signatures of LLM-generated email bodies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Score inbound email for LLM-generation artifacts (excessive formality, unusual phrasing patterns, markdown rendering, repetitive clause structure). Correlate with URLs shorteners or tracked C2 infrastructure. Flag emails with high confidence LLM tokens and credential-harvesting links.

suggestion.title: npm Package Installation from Dependency Confusion Source
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 33 packages exploit 'dependency confusion'—attackers register lookalike package names to public npm to hijack resolution. Detection should flag installations from unexpected public sources when private scopes are misconfigured.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install/ci execution with parent process context. Alert when npm fetches packages matching known internal naming conventions from public registry instead of private proxy, or when registry URL bypasses normal enterprise artifact manager.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Environment Variable Collection from Build Processes
suggestion.rationale: Campaign goal was 'profile developer environments'—article implicitly indicates env var exfiltration (API keys, credentials, workspace paths). Detection should catch child processes spawned during npm package installation attempting to read or transmit environment state.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes spawned as children of npm/node with command-line arguments or syscalls reading common env vars (AWS_*, AZURE_*, GH_TOKEN, NPM_TOKEN) or calling uname/systeminfo/whoami immediately after module load without legitimate use case.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration via HTTP from npm Node.js Child Processes
suggestion.rationale: Profiling campaign requires exfiltration channel. Malicious npm packages would spawn HTTPS or DNS-based C2 callbacks from node child processes with stolen environment/system metadata.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound HTTPS/HTTP from node.exe or npm.exe processes to non-whitelisted external IPs, especially with POST payloads containing encoded environment variable dumps, hostname, or metadata signatures (base64 blobs >200 bytes with low entropy randomness).

suggestion.title: npm preinstall/postinstall Script Execution Without Explicit Declaration
suggestion.rationale: npm lifecycle scripts (preinstall, postinstall, prepare) are blindly executed on install. Malicious packages abuse this to run reconnaissance without package.json visibility. Detection should catch undeclared script invocation or obfuscated script paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install parent-child relationships. Alert when bash/cmd spawn from npm.exe with arguments containing encoded/obfuscated commands, or when child processes load from node_modules/.bin/ without corresponding entry in top-level package.json scripts or lifecycle hooks.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance Data Staging in npm Cache or Temporary Directories
suggestion.rationale: Before exfiltration, the campaign must collect and stage environment profiles. npm cache directories (/npm or C:\Users\*\AppData\Roaming\npm-cache) and temp folders are natural staging points for stolen data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect writes to npm cache or temp directories of JSON/text files containing env var dumps, system metadata (hostname, whoami, uname output), or package.json manifests during package installation. Monitor for files with entropy patterns matching base64-encoded system information.

suggestion.title: npm Registry Request Anomalies Indicating Dependency Confusion Probing
suggestion.rationale: Before deploying malicious packages, attackers must probe target environment naming conventions. Repeated npm registry requests for package names matching internal/private naming patterns (e.g., '@company-internal/*') from same build machine indicate reconnaissance of target infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS/HTTPS to registry.npmjs.org and mirror registries. Correlate requests for non-existent packages matching private scope patterns with subsequent installation of lookalike packages from public registry. Flag build agents querying >10 non-existent scoped packages in single session.

suggestion.title: GlobalProtect Forged Authentication Cookie Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacks used 'forged authentication override cookies that targeted the local administrator account.' Core attack vector but no detection UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for rapid successful authentication to GlobalProtect using override cookies where decryption succeeds but signature validation should fail (if implemented correctly). Alert on any admin-account authentication via override cookie where the preceding 24 hours show no legitimate override-cookie usage patterns from that source IP.

suggestion.title: Public Certificate Extraction from GlobalProtect HTTPS Service
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'attackers can obtain the corresponding public key via the HTTPS session and then use it to create forged cookies.' Technique precedes cookie forgery but no detection for reconnaissance step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on certificate extraction from GlobalProtect portal/gateway HTTPS service followed within 1 hour by authentication override attempts from the same source IP. Flag repeated certificate lookups from external IPs.

suggestion.title: VPN Authentication Success with Failed Session Establishment
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'in many incidents, even though the appliance accepted the forged cookie, they were unable to establish a full VPN session.' Unusual pattern distinguishes exploitation attempts from normal auth failures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect authentication success (cookie accepted) immediately followed by session establishment failure within 5 seconds. Normal users typically fail at auth stage or successfully establish sessions. Rapid auth-success + session-fail within same source IP indicates forged-cookie exploitation attempt.

suggestion.title: GlobalProtect Attacks from Vultr and Dromatics Systems Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies attack sources: 'infrastructure hosted by Vultr' (May 18) and 'Dromatics Systems' (May 21). Named malicious infrastructure should generate detections but none appear.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Block or alert on any GlobalProtect connection attempt from Vultr ASN ranges and Dromatics Systems known IP space. Flag any authentication activity (override cookie or standard) from these sources with severity high, noting CISA KEV listing as of May 29.

suggestion.title: Rapid Successive Authentication Override Cookie Validation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes large-scale testing: 'Rapid7 MDR identified successful exploitation across numerous customers.' Suggests widespread scanning/exploitation attempts not captured by single-instance detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on more than 3 authentication override cookie attempts in 10 minutes from single source IP, or more than 1 successful override cookie auth in 24 hours from any external source. Track per-device for org-wide trending.

suggestion.title: Certificate Reuse Between HTTPS and Authentication Override Services
