suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for successful access to host-context Promise constructors, global objects, or prototype chains from within vm2 contexts. Detect attempts to call host methods (e.g., require() or process object manipulation) after Promise manipulation.

suggestion.title: Software inventory — vm2 module presence and version enumeration (CVE-2026-47210)
suggestion.rationale: UC_24_3 covers filesystem path detection. Extend with software inventory queries (TVM, SCCM, EDR native API) for programmatic asset exposure scoring against CVE-2026-47210. Article emphasizes version < 3.11.3 is vulnerable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query software inventory databases (TVM, SCCM, npm audit) for installed vm2 versions <= 3.11.3. Correlate with Node.js process executions accepting untrusted code input to identify exploitable assets.

suggestion.title: [LLM] Unauthenticated JSON-RPC POST to PraisonAI /a2a endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly provides this as UC_12_2 with labeled detection. Core delivery mechanism: 'An unauthenticated network client can send a JSON-RPC request to the /a2a endpoint'. Network-based exploit indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: POST requests to /*a2a* endpoints on ports 8000/80/443/8080 with HTTP 200 response from external (non-RFC1918) sources. Filter on successful responses to identify exploitation attempts, not probing.

suggestion.title: [LLM] Suspicious child process spawned by PraisonAI uvicorn/python A2A server
suggestion.rationale: Article provides UC_12_3 exploit-phase hunt. Root cause: 'The example registers a calculate(expression) tool implemented with Python eval(expression)' — this hunt detects RCE post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Shell executables (sh/bash/cmd.exe/powershell/zsh) or command utilities (whoami/id/curl/wget/nc) or Python patterns (os.system/subprocess) spawned by parent python/uvicorn with 'a2a-server.py' or 'praisonai' in parent command line.

suggestion.title: [LLM] PraisonAI A2A server started with vulnerable 0.0.0.0 binding
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies root cause: 'The example exposes an A2A server without configuring auth_token' and 'binds the server to 0.0.0.0'. UC_12_4 is the install/config-stage detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Python/uvicorn processes executing with 'a2a-server.py', 'praisonaiagents', or 'A2A' serving keyword where command contains 0.0.0.0 or --host 0.0.0.0 binding. Medium confidence due to dev/test environments.

suggestion.title: [LLM] Credential exfiltration via eval() RCE — LLM API key exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article describes impact: successful eval() RCE provides arbitrary Python execution. Detection hunts explicitly search for 'OPENAI_API_KEY', 'ANTHROPIC_API_KEY', 'GEMINI_API_KEY' accessed post-exploitation — this is the credential-access phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Subprocess execution (env, printenv, cat) under compromised uvicorn/python process accessing ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.ssh/id_*, /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, or environment variables matching *_API_KEY, *_TOKEN patterns.

suggestion.title: Asset inventory — systems running vulnerable PraisonAI with exposed /a2a endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article provides asset-exposure template. Organizations must identify which endpoints expose PraisonAI /a2a handlers reachable from untrusted networks (external IP space, internet-routable).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference installed PraisonAI packages (via dependency/SCA tools) with network scans showing /a2a endpoints accessible from external IPs on high-numbered ports. Match CVE-2026-47391 to unpatched versions.

suggestion.title: [LLM] Python attribute introspection to builtins escape: `__self__` + `vars()` pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'retrieve the real Python `builtins` module, from which `__import__` can be extracted via `vars()`'. Detection must catch getattr/attribute access chains targeting `__self__` on callable objects like print.
log_sources: FileWrite (suspicious .py file creation with introspection patterns)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Python processes executing code containing attribute access patterns (`.__self__`, `getattr(obj, '__self__')`) combined with `vars()` or `__dict__` access, particularly in context of `print`, `input`, or other builtins. Elevated suspicion if parent process is PraisonAI or execute_code-related.

suggestion.title: [LLM] Dynamic `__import__` construction via string concatenation in Python
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'extract `__import__` via `vars()` and runtime string construction'. Attackers construct the string '__import__' dynamically to bypass static detection and access os.system, subprocess, etc.
log_sources: DeviceFileEvents (suspicious Python files written by execute_code)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Python processes with string concatenation or format operations constructing `__import__`, `__builtins__`, `subprocess`, or `os` dynamically. Look for patterns like `'__' + 'import__'`, `format()` with dunder names, or char-code/ord() reconstructions in subprocess/execute_code contexts.

suggestion.title: [LLM] Shell subprocess spawning from Python interpreter with privilege context metadata
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'achieves arbitrary OS command execution on the host, completely defeating the sandbox'. After escaping, attacker spawns sh/bash/cmd to execute discovery (id, whoami, env, /etc/shadow reads). UC_13_5 partially covers this but lacks the privilege context (e.g., running as service account, escalated UID).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Subprocess creation (sh/bash/cmd/powershell) initiated by Python parent (python*.exe/python3*), where Python's process tree includes execute_code or praisonai in cmdline or module path, combined with discovery/credential-reading commands (id, whoami, uname, printenv, /proc/self/environ, /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, AWS_* env reads, /run/secrets).

suggestion.title: [LLM] PraisonAI execute_code sandbox detection: subprocess mode activation + restricted builtin mutation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes subprocess sandbox mode as the target. Detection of activation of sandboxed execute_code with subsequent observed bypasses.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Python processes spawning child Python subprocesses (subprocess.Popen, os.system calling python -c) with code containing builtins-disabling patterns (replacing __builtins__, removing keys from __dict__), followed within seconds by shell spawning or credential access syscalls.

suggestion.title: [LLM] Credential exfiltration post-sandbox-escape: env var + secrets directory reads
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions defeating sandbox; post-exploitation phase includes reading environment variables and credential files (AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, /run/secrets, /var/run/secrets). This is discovery + credential access.
log_sources: Sysmon Event 10 (ProcessAccess) for env var reads
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Shell processes spawned from Python subprocesses (UC_13_5 covers this) executing printenv, env, cat /etc/passwd, cat /proc/self/environ, kubectl, or direct reads of /run/secrets, /var/run/secrets, ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.ssh within 5s of sandbox-escape indicators.

suggestion.title: PraisonAI Flask server binding to 0.0.0.0:8005 — unrestricted network listener creation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'binds to `0.0.0.0` per the recommended sample YAML' and 'users who follow the documented quickstart...get a server that binds to 0.0.0.0'. UC_14_4 detects inbound connections to this socket, but not the initial binding event itself, which is the root cause of exposure and occurs before external scanning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Python processes (python, python3, pythonw) creating listening sockets bound to 0.0.0.0 on port 8005 or high-numbered ports immediately following praisonai deploy command execution. A socket bind to 0.0.0.0 with no host-based firewall rule represents direct external exposure.

suggestion.title: CVE-Detector vulnerability scanner probing PraisonAI API endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: '(incl. CVE-Detector scanner)' in UC_14_5, indicating a known public scanner actively targeting this CVE. This specialized reconnaissance behavior warrants a dedicated hunt beyond generic POST counting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify HTTP(S) requests from known CVE-Detector scanner IPs/user-agents to /chat or /agents endpoints on port 8005. Baseline legitimate traffic first. Multiple sequential probes to both endpoints within short time window (e.g., <5 min apart) from single source indicates active vulnerability scanning.

suggestion.title: Generated api_server.py code artifact — dynamic Flask server code generation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'code-generator (`praisonai.deploy.api.generate_api_server_code`)' which dynamically emits Flask server code. The generated file artifact (api_server.py, generated_api.py, etc.) is a key execution indicator not directly covered by process-only UCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file creation or modification of api_server.py, generated_api.py, or similar artifacts in temp/project directories concurrent with or immediately following praisonai deploy command. Hash and extract generated file contents; confirm presence of Flask imports (flask, flask_restful) and binding patterns (app.run(host='0.0.0.0')) to confirm generation by praisonai.deploy.api.generate_api_server_code.

suggestion.title: PraisonAI member-role escalation via workspace members endpoint mutation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'member-role privilege escalation' as the core attack. Phrase: 'The dependency only checks that the caller is a member of the workspace_id in the URL prefix' then allows mutation of member roles via PATCH/POST/DELETE. Pipeline generated no detection for T1098 member manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP PATCH, POST, DELETE to /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/members* endpoints. Alert on successful mutations (200-299 status) especially from accounts <24h old. Correlate with account creation events to detect create-then-escalate pattern.

suggestion.title: Cross-workspace IDOR enumeration: nested-resource access anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability: 'route handlers then look up the inner resource (agent_id, issue_id, project_id, label_id, comment_id, dependency_id) by primary key only' — bypasses workspace membership. Pipeline missed T1190 exploitation pattern and T1213 data enumeration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect users accessing 15+ distinct resource IDs (agents|issues|projects|labels|dependencies) across ≤2 workspaces in <10min. IDOR allows blind enumeration of valid inner IDs. Flag if user has no explicit membership in target workspace.

suggestion.title: Account creation + workspace API privilege escalation sequence
suggestion.rationale: Article lists both T1136 (Create Account) and T1098 (Account Manipulation). The vulnerability permits newly created accounts to immediately escalate within workspaces via IDOR. Pipeline failed to correlate this sequence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate /api/v1/auth/register POST (200-299) with subsequent workspace member/agent/project mutations by same account within 600s. Flag if new account modifies resources in workspaces it did not create.

suggestion.title: PraisonAI POC tool indicators: named process/file artifacts
suggestion.rationale: Article body explicitly names three POC artifacts in Defender KQL: start_server.sh, run_poc_video.sh, poc_cross_workspace_idor.py. These are direct IOCs for exploitation attempts. Pipeline extracted zero file/process IOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any process execution or file creation matching {start_server.sh, run_poc_video.sh, poc_cross_workspace_idor.py}. High-fidelity POC deployment indicator. Check both file and process datamodels.

suggestion.title: Workspace membership bypass: unauthenticated access to /api/v1/workspaces/*/agents|issues|projects|labels|dependencies
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability: FastAPI dependency validates workspace_id membership but nested resource lookup skips inner-resource authorization. Article: 'require_workspace_member(workspace_id) dependency'. This suggests non-member access attempts should be detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline per-user workspace endpoint access. Alert when user requests /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/[agents|issues|projects|labels|dependencies]/* where user is NOT an explicit member. Elevated alert if requestor is <24h old account.

suggestion.title: JWT Token Forgery via Hardcoded Secret Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'allowing token forgery for any user' but no detection exists for the actual exploit—JWT token creation/signing using the known hardcoded string 'dev-secret-change-me'. This is the core attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to */auth/* endpoints that succeed with tokens signed using the hardcoded secret, or application logs showing token generation with default keys. Detect unusual auth success patterns shortly after vulnerable deployment startup.

suggestion.title: Missing PLATFORM_JWT_SECRET Environment Variable at Process Start
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'when PLATFORM_JWT_SECRET is unset' and 'safety check... only fires when PLATFORM_ENV != dev; the default value of PLATFORM_ENV is dev'. Need direct detection of this unsafe configuration state.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag uvicorn/praisonai process launches where PLATFORM_JWT_SECRET environment variable is absent and either PLATFORM_ENV is unset or equals 'dev'. Requires environment variable visibility from process telemetry or container instrumentation.

suggestion.title: Hardcoded JWT Secret String Detection in Configuration
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies the literal hardcoded value 'dev-secret-change-me'. Configuration files, logs, or memory dumps containing this exact string signal vulnerability without successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search file-create/modify events and application logs for the exact string 'dev-secret-change-me' in contexts related to praisonai (config dirs, .env files, process environment dumps). Presence of this string outside of source code repositories or vendor documentation indicates misconfiguration.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized User Elevation via Forged JWT Token
suggestion.rationale: Article describes token forgery enabling 'access any user'. No detection for the behavioral outcome: low-privilege or anonymous sessions suddenly accessing high-privilege workspaces/APIs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to privileged endpoints (*/workspaces/*, */auth/admin*, */users/*) where the originating JWT claims (extracted from Authorization header) show unexpected privilege escalation (e.g., claims for admin role from a session that was never elevated, or claims for multiple workspace IDs that don't match user history).

suggestion.title: praisonai-platform Deployment with Default PLATFORM_ENV Value
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'default value of PLATFORM_ENV is dev, so the check is silently bypassed'. Direct check for absence of explicit prod/staging environment override.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect praisonai-platform uvicorn processes where PLATFORM_ENV is not explicitly set to production/staging/hardened value. Absence of an explicit non-dev environment setting indicates vulnerable default configuration.

suggestion.title: Workspace role-change API request without corresponding audit log entry
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'require_workspace_member(workspace_id)' authorization check defaults to min_role='member' and is never overridden, implying possible audit logging bypass. Article does not confirm audit trail is generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PATCH requests to /workspaces/*/members/* endpoints that succeed (HTTP 200/204) but have no corresponding entry in application audit logs within 5 minutes. Cross-correlate Web events against audit log presence to identify authorization checks that do not trigger audit events.

suggestion.title: Cascading workspace member role promotions by same user within short timeframe
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attacker can 'promote themselves or others' — phrasing suggests multi-user elevation attacks. Attacker promoting self then promoting confederates in rapid succession is distinctive.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect single user_id issuing multiple PATCH /workspaces/*/members/* requests that succeed (200/204) against different target user_ids within 10 minutes. Correlate srcIP/User-Agent to identify if attacker is also the initiator. Alert if pattern matches: self-promote → promote confederate → demote legitimate owner.

suggestion.title: PATCH request to workspace member endpoint with role field in body not previously seen for that endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'MemberService.update_role(workspace_id, user_id, body.role)' — implies role parameter in request body. No detection rule validates body payload mutation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for PATCH requests to /workspaces/*/members/* where request body contains role parameter set to 'owner' or 'admin'. If WAF or application logging exposes request bodies, flag those with role in payload where prior baseline for this endpoint does not show role mutations. Anomaly-score if baseline has never seen role field mutated for that endpoint.

suggestion.title: LinkedIn Spearphishing URL Click to macOS Malware Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly: 'LinkedIn Social Engineering to Deploy Custom macOS Malware'—detect the initial click-through on malicious LinkedIn links
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for employee clicks on LinkedIn URLs that redirect outside LinkedIn's domain or to attacker infrastructure. Correlate successful clicks with subsequent unsigned macOS binary downloads or execution within 30 minutes. Flag targeting of high-value roles (exec, engineering, finance) during off-business hours.

suggestion.title: Unsigned macOS Binary Execution from User Downloads
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'custom macOS Malware'—detect unsigned Mach-O execution, the standard delivery and execution pattern for this class of malware
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution of Mach-O binaries lacking valid Apple code-signing certificates, especially when spawned from ~/Downloads or /tmp. Correlate with recent suspicious process parents (bash, curl, Archive Utility) and timestamp proximity to LinkedIn interaction.

suggestion.title: macOS Shell Script Download and Execute Chain
suggestion.rationale: macOS malware commonly uses shell scripts for post-exploitation—'custom macOS Malware' implies capabilities requiring scripted execution and persistence
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bash/zsh commands that download binaries via curl/wget, decode payloads (base64/xxd), or launch unsigned binaries. Monitor for shell execution spawned from recently-opened unsigned binaries or user-accessible directories immediately post-LinkedIn access.

suggestion.title: Anomalous DNS and HTTPS C2 from macOS Hosts
suggestion.rationale: Custom malware requires command-and-control communication—while not explicitly detailed, essential post-execution behavior for establishing attacker control
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of legitimate macOS outbound destinations (Apple CDNs, software repos, iCloud). Alert on HTTPS traffic to unrecognized domains with high-entropy SNI values or invalid certificate chains from macOS hosts after malware execution window.

suggestion.title: LinkedIn Profile Reconnaissance Targeting Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Social engineering via LinkedIn presupposes target selection and profiling—'Using LinkedIn Social Engineering' implies reconnaissance phase precedes phishing delivery
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous LinkedIn profile browsing—rapid sequential views of executive/tech staff profiles, clustering by department, or off-hours reconnaissance activity. Cross-reference with subsequent spearphishing attempts or malware delivery to the profiled employee population.

suggestion.title: macOS LaunchAgent or Daemon Persistence Installation
suggestion.rationale: Custom macOS malware typically establishes persistence for long-term access—expected post-execution behavior for trojanized samples, standard macOS persistence vector
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation/modification of .plist files in ~/Library/LaunchAgents, /Library/LaunchDaemons, or system startup directories post-malware execution. Alert on unsigned binaries referenced in Launch Agent configurations or LaunchServices spawning with suspicious parents.

suggestion.title: HTTPSpy Malware Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names HTTPSpy as newly deployed Kimsuky tool. Pipeline extracted no IOCs or detections despite this being a primary malware artifact and executable indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process creation matching HTTPSpy naming variants, HTTP/HTTPS socket operations by suspicious parents, and DLL injection attempts. Alert on execution following macro-enabled document opening or from %TEMP% directories. Cross-reference with known Kimsuky C2 domains if available.

suggestion.title: HelloDoor Backdoor Persistence Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly cites HelloDoor as component of expanded Kimsuky arsenal. Pipeline produced zero persistence-layer detections despite this being a backdoor used for remote access establishment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: HelloDoor typically installs via registry (Run keys, Winlogon) or scheduled tasks. Monitor for suspicious registry modifications in persistence locations post-execution, task scheduler entries creating unexpected binaries, or files written to startup folders with timestamps matching malware execution.

suggestion.title: VS Code Remote Tunnels Abuse for C2
suggestion.rationale: Title directly identifies VS Code Tunnels as part of toolkit. This represents abuse of legitimate remote development tools for command-and-control, a defense-evasion technique. Pipeline generated no C2-layer detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for code-server or vscode-server processes running on unusual accounts (service, SYSTEM, non-developers). Alert on outbound HTTPS to known tunnel relay endpoints (e.g., tunnels.dev domains) from VS Code processes. Flag registry entries enabling remote tunnels or tunnel CLI arguments in process command lines.

suggestion.title: Kimsuky Spear-Phishing Initial Access Chain
suggestion.rationale: Kimsuky is known spear-phishing operator (article context: targets govt, think tanks, academia). Initial delivery of HTTPSpy and HelloDoor occurs via social engineering. Pipeline mapped no initial-access phase or phishing-specific detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for email attachments with Korean-language metadata or targeting sectors historically attacked by Kimsuky. Alert on macro-enabled Office documents from untrusted senders, OLE embedded objects, and immediate child process spawning (PowerShell, cmd) from macro execution.

suggestion.title: Multi-stage Malware Deployment Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'expands arsenal with' three tools, implying staged deployment. Pipeline generated no detection correlating download→extract→execute chain typical of Kimsuky campaigns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate parent process chains: delivery vehicle (Office macro, LNK dropper) → command-line tools (certutil, powershell, bitsadmin) → remote file fetch → execution from %TEMP% or %APPDATA%. Flag suspicious cmd.exe/powershell spawning from non-standard parents or with base64-encoded content.

suggestion.title: Kimsuky Infrastructure IOC Callback Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article implies C2 communication channels for three tools but pipeline extracted zero domains, IPs, or callback indicators. Pipeline should correlate malware execution with known Kimsuky C2 infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP/HTTPS callbacks from HTTPSpy or HelloDoor to Kimsuky-attributed C2 domains (if available). Alert on unusual outbound connections from compromised hosts to rare/new domains, especially POST requests with encoded payloads, or tunnel relay connections from residential IPs.

suggestion.title: Malicious NuGet Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article headline explicitly states 'Malicious Sicoob NuGet Steals Banking Credentials'—pipeline should detect NuGet package installation events, especially for packages with financial/credential-related names or from unfamiliar publishers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for dotnet.exe/nuget.exe spawning unusual child processes (PowerShell, cmd) during package restore. Alert on NuGet package names containing typosquats of banking/credential libraries being installed in build pipelines.

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration from Build Environment
suggestion.rationale: Title states packages 'Steal Banking Credentials' and 'Target Cloud Secrets'—pipeline should surface detections for credential access and exfiltration from development/CI environment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate NuGet package installation events with child process access to credential stores (Windows Credential Manager, .aws directories, SSH keys, environment variables). Flag unexpected outbound HTTPS/DNS from build agents immediately post-installation.

suggestion.title: npm Package Post-Install Script Execution
suggestion.rationale: Title mentions 'npm Packages Target Cloud Secrets'—pipeline should detect npm post-install hooks that spawn credential-stealing processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm.exe process trees for spawned PowerShell/cmd during package install. Flag processes that read from credential locations or make network calls during post-install script execution window.

suggestion.title: Outbound C2 Connections from Build Agents
suggestion.rationale: Credential theft implies exfiltration—pipeline should detect unusual network activity from development/CI machines to attacker infrastructure following malicious package installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on new/unresolved domains contacted by npm.exe or dotnet.exe child processes within minutes of package installation. Prioritize encrypted connections (HTTPS/TLS) with small payloads characteristic of credential exfil.

suggestion.title: Supply-Chain Repository Typosquatting Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article centers on malicious packages in public registries—pipeline should detect NuGet/npm packages with names mimicking legitimate financial/credential libraries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag newly-published NuGet and npm packages with names containing 'sicoob', 'banking', 'credential', 'secret' or similar financial/auth keywords. Alert on version bumps in dormant packages or those from new/spoofed maintainer accounts.

suggestion.title: AI-Powered Malware Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article headline explicitly states 'AI-Powered Cyberattacks'—no use case was generated to detect anomalous process behavior, unusual library loads, or execution chains typical of AI/ML frameworks (TensorFlow, PyTorch, scikit-learn) being weaponized. This is the core attack differentiator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual Python/compiled ML framework execution in memory (esp. runtime model loading, TensorFlow DLL loads, PyTorch C++ bindings), combined with suspicious parent-child process chains or signed-executable living-off-the-land patterns. Flag if ML inference is launched from non-standard directories or with obfuscated command lines.

suggestion.title: GREYVIBE Infrastructure Callback Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title identifies GREYVIBE as Russia-linked actor; no C2 callback or network-based detection was created. Russian-attributed APTs typically use distinct ASN, geolocation, or bulletproof-hoster patterns in their C2 infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound HTTPS/DNS to Russian ASNs (AS12389, AS43456, etc.) or bulletproof hosting providers, especially from Ukrainian government/defense sector systems. Correlate with process execution of unusual scripting engines or network tools (curl, wget, certutil) in the same 5-minute window.

suggestion.title: Ukraine-Sector Targeting by Eastern European Actor
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly targets Ukraine; no geo-behavioral or victim-profile detection was generated. Russian-attributed campaigns targeting Ukraine show distinct email lures (Cyrillic language, Ukraine-specific entities), document macros, or watering-hole patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on phishing emails or drive-by-download attempts where sender/domains are spoofing Ukrainian government, military, or critical infrastructure entities. Correlate with file downloads of Office documents or executables in Ukrainian language or with Ukraine-related metadata.

suggestion.title: Machine-Learning-Based Evasion Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title states AI-powered attacks but provides no behavioral detection for adversaries using AI to evade detection (polymorphic obfuscation, dynamically generated payloads). This is the most novel threat vector and must have detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for rapid mutation of child-process command lines, repeated re-obfuscation of the same malware sample across multiple hosts within hours, or encoding patterns inconsistent with known packers (suggesting dynamic generation). Baseline command-line entropy and alert on anomalous spikes.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration via ML Training Data Staging
suggestion.rationale: APT using AI likely collects large datasets (for model training or espionage); no detection for bulk data staging or compression typical of pre-exfiltration activities.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation of large .tar, .zip, or .7z archives in %TEMP% or non-standard staging directories on Ukrainian government/defense networks, especially if preceded by discovery activity (dir /s, find, net share commands) or correlated with suspicious network connections.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via AI-Generated Credential Spraying
suggestion.rationale: Russian APTs targeting Ukraine typically pivot across enterprise networks; no detection for credential stuffing or password-spray patterns that may be AI-optimized (using ML-predicted weak passwords or contextual lures).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on failed logon spikes followed by successful logon to different accounts or systems within the same source IP, especially across domain-joined hosts. Cross-reference with failed RDP/SSH attempts to detect spray patterns, flagging sources that cycle through username lists at rates > 5 attempts/min.

suggestion.title: SYSTEM Context Scheduled Task Creation
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'Ransomware Uses SYSTEM Scheduled Task'—this is the persistence/execution mechanism and should generate a detection for privileged task creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation of scheduled tasks running under SYSTEM context, especially those calling executable files from user-writable directories or with suspicious command-line patterns. Monitor Task Scheduler event logs (Event ID 106 task registration, 140 task updated) for tasks created outside known administrative tooling.

suggestion.title: High-Volume File Encryption Operations from Scheduled Task
suggestion.rationale: Article states ransomware 'encrypts local drives'—detection should trigger on encryption-pattern file activity spawned from scheduled task execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate scheduled task execution with rapid file write operations to local drives, especially .exe to .encrypted or .locked rename patterns. Baseline legitimate file operations and alert on anomalous volume or entropy changes from task-spawned processes.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via SYSTEM Scheduled Task Execution
suggestion.rationale: Title emphasizes 'elevated privileges' and SYSTEM context—use case needed to detect the privilege-escalation path from user context to SYSTEM before encryption begins.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process creation where a user-context process spawns a scheduled task that executes with SYSTEM privilege. Monitor for Task Scheduler spawning child processes and track the context transition from initiating user to SYSTEM.

suggestion.title: Ransomware Task Scheduler Persistence Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Core attack pattern described in title—scheduled tasks are persistence mechanism for ransomware to survive reboot and re-execute encryption.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag scheduled tasks with uncommon triggers (e.g., logon, startup), referencing recently-created or dropped binaries, or with obfuscated command lines. Correlate task creation timing with file-system anomalies and encryption artifacts.

suggestion.title: Anomalous LLM Service API Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article title states attackers leverage ChatGPT and Google Gemini; no detections for authentication anomalies to these services. Title phrase: 'Leverage ChatGPT and Google Gemini'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for sign-ins to LLM services (OpenAI, Google) from unusual geographies, IPs, or with impossible-travel patterns. Flag bulk authentication failures followed by success. Alert on access from VPN/proxy networks uncommon to the organization.

suggestion.title: LLM Prompt Injection or Jailbreak Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Attackers 'leverage' LLM services to 'fuel cyberattacks' implies prompt manipulation or instruction-injection attacks. No detection for malicious prompt patterns. Title phrase: 'to Fuel Cyberattacks'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect and alert on common jailbreak/injection keywords in LLM API requests (e.g., 'ignore previous instructions', 'system prompt', 'DAN mode', 'ignore safety guidelines'). Flag requests asking LLM to generate malware, phishing content, or exploit code.

suggestion.title: LLM API Quota Exhaustion or Bulk Generation Activity
suggestion.rationale: Attackers may abuse API quotas to generate at scale (phishing emails, malware variants, social-engineering content). No consumption or rate-based detection suggested. Title implies large-scale abuse: 'Fuel Cyberattacks' (plural).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for spike in LLM API request volume from a single user/service principal relative to baseline. Alert on rapid-fire completions (high token consumption in short window) that exceed organizational norms, especially if payloads contain phishing or malware-generation indicators.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Tool Installation or Script-Execution via LLM Output
suggestion.rationale: LLM outputs (generated code, scripts, commands) may be executed locally or deployed to targets. No detection for scripts/binaries sourced from or validated against LLM-generated content. Title: 'to Fuel Cyberattacks' suggests downstream execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate suspicious process execution (unsigned, obfuscated, or known-malicious script patterns) with recent LLM API calls from the same user. Flag execution of scripts/binaries that match signatures of LLM-generated payloads (e.g., base64-encoded, unusual variable naming, common LLM patterns).

suggestion.title: Email Campaign with LLM-Generated Phishing Content
suggestion.rationale: LLM services are ideal for generating convincing phishing emails and social-engineering content at scale. Title directly mentions ChatGPT/Gemini abuse. No detection for phishing campaigns with LLM-like linguistic patterns or high variability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk email campaigns with unusual linguistic consistency (suggests template-based generation) or suspicious variability (signature of LLM paraphrasing). Flag emails with high-entropy subjects or bodies generated in rapid succession. Correlate with known LLM prompting patterns in user's search/chat history if available.

suggestion.title: GREYVIBE Actor Identified in Threat Intelligence
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names GREYVIBE as the threat actor. Pipeline must extract and correlate actor names from article titles and body. Missing: zero actor tagging in output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline indicators of compromise (IOCs, infrastructure, tactics) for GREYVIBE from threat intelligence feeds. Correlate on network/endpoint logs for signs of compromise, C2 communication, or known attack infrastructure associated with this actor.

suggestion.title: Malicious npm Package Installation via Dependency Confusion
suggestion.rationale: Article states '33 malicious npm packages abuse dependency confusion'—core attack vector. No UC generated despite this being the attack entry point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install processes for attempts to resolve package versions from non-standard registries or typosquatted package names. Alert on installation of packages with names similar to internal/private registry entries. Track package metadata inconsistencies (version mismatch, unexpected publisher).

suggestion.title: Environment Variable and Credential Exfiltration from npm Package Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes campaign to 'collect reconnaissance data from developer and build environments'—implies env var/credential harvesting at execution time. Zero detections for collection phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm package post-install scripts reading and exfiltrating environment variables (AWS_ACCESS_KEY, CI_TOKEN, SSH_KEY, USER_HOME paths). Alert on child processes spawned by npm install that make outbound HTTPS connections to non-standard domains during execution.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Network Egress from Build/Dev Environment During npm Operations
suggestion.rationale: Campaign profiles 'developer and build environments'—implies data exfiltration. No C2 or exfiltration detection suggested despite reconnaissance payload explicitly harvesting this context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate npm install process trees with outbound DNS queries and HTTPS connections. Flag resolves to newly-registered or high-entropy domains. Alert on Base64/JSON-encoded POST bodies containing environment variable values, CI/CD configuration secrets, or system metadata from npm child processes.

suggestion.title: Typosquatted and Confusable npm Package Name Registration
suggestion.rationale: Dependency confusion attack relies on attackers registering similar package names. Article does not detail specific package names, but this is the threat model. Pipeline missed defense-evasion/initial-access signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm registry for newly-published packages with names that closely resemble private/internal package names in your dependency trees (Levenshtein distance < 3, vowel/consonant swaps). Cross-reference against organization's known private packages. Alert on version bumps for packages with 0 prior versions or inconsistent author metadata.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Script Execution During npm Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Malicious packages execute reconnaissance code via install scripts. Article describes 'profile developer environments'—direct reference to post-install script behavior. No execution-phase detections suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when npm/yarn post-install scripts spawn child processes with names inconsistent with the package purpose (e.g. curl, powershell, bash in packages claiming to be UI libraries). Flag execution of scripts that read /etc/passwd, ~/.ssh, CI environment files, or call whoami/env/id during package initialization.

suggestion.title: GlobalProtect Admin Authentication Without Credential Submission
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack technique: 'Rapid7 developed a proof-of-concept exploit that demonstrates how an attacker can retrieve the public certificates exposed by a GlobalProtect portal or gateway, generate a forged authentication override cookie for an arbitrary user, and authenticate without knowing valid credentials.' Detectable via authentication acceptance bypassing normal credential validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful GlobalProtect authentication to admin account where authentication override cookie was used but no prior credential exchange (username/password submission or MFA challenge) occurred in the same session. Correlate auth override token validation against expected pre-auth handshake patterns.

suggestion.title: Suspicious VPN Connection Following Failed Auth Override Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'In some cases, attackers were able to connect to the device via VPN using forged cookies, granting them access to internal networks. However, Rapid7 says that in many incidents, even though the appliance accepted the forged cookie, they were unable to establish a full VPN session.' VPN session establishment post-exploitation is a clear lateral movement indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate timestamp of auth override cookie validation with subsequent VPN tunnel establishment on same gateway. Alert on VPN sessions initiated by local admin account from external/untrusted source IPs, especially during May 17-29, 2026 timeframe or when correlated with CVE-2026-0257 exploitation signatures.

suggestion.title: Public Certificate Extraction via HTTPS Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article root cause: 'If the same certificate is reused for both HTTPS services and authentication override cookies, attackers can obtain the corresponding public key via the HTTPS session.' Attack chain begins with certificate discovery via standard HTTPS handshake.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for anomalous certificate queries to GlobalProtect portal HTTPS endpoints, particularly bulk or high-frequency certificate requests. Alert on HTTPS TLS handshake patterns that deviate from standard browser clients or legitimate VPN clients, especially if followed by auth override cookie manipulation within same session.

suggestion.title: Certificate Configuration Audit – Shared HTTPS and Auth Override Cert
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies root vulnerability condition: 'PAN-OS's validation of authentication override cookies...A GlobalProtect VPN device decrypts these types of cookies using a configured private key and then trusts the decrypted contents without performing any signature verification. If the same certificate is reused for both HTTPS services and authentication override cookies, attackers can obtain the corresponding public key.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory all GlobalProtect gateway certificate configurations. Flag devices where HTTPS service certificate matches authentication override cookie certificate. Alert on new instances of shared certificate assignment or recently modified certificate bindings on production gateways using vulnerable configuration.

suggestion.title: Vultr and Dromatics Systems Source IP Attack Attribution
suggestion.rationale: Article provides explicit infrastructure attribution with dates: 'The company first observed exploitation on May 18 from infrastructure hosted by Vultr, with a second wave of attacks detected on May 21 originating from Dromatics Systems.' This enables network-based detection and threat intelligence correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate GlobalProtect authentication attempts from Vultr ASN space on/after May 18 and Dromatics Systems ASN space on/after May 21. Alert on any successful or failed authentication from these infrastructure providers to GlobalProtect endpoints, particularly to admin accounts. Cross-reference source IPs against known malicious Vultr/Dromatics infrastructure blocklists.

suggestion.title: Authentication Override Feature Enabled Configuration Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Rapid7's investigation into affected customers found that the impacted devices had GlobalProtect authentication override cookies enabled.' Also notes mitigation strategy: 'turning off the authentication override feature.' Identifying vulnerable configuration state is prerequisite for scope and risk assessment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan all GlobalProtect gateway configurations for authentication override cookie feature enabled status. Alert on recent enablement of auth override on production gateways, especially those also using shared certificates. Create inventory of all devices with auth override enabled and prioritize patching and/or mitigation per CISA KEV directive (federal agencies by June 1, 2026).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-0257 GlobalProtect Authentication Bypass Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article headline explicitly states 'PAN-OS GlobalProtect Authentication Bypass ... Under Active Exploitation'; this is the core attack vector and pipeline generated zero use cases for it
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PAN-OS GlobalProtect authentication and web interface logs for requests matching CVE-2026-0257 exploitation patterns. Alert on authentication successes from sources previously observed in exploitation attempts, null-byte sequences in request parameters, or malformed authentication packets characteristic of bypass techniques.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from GlobalProtect VPN Session
suggestion.rationale: Successful authentication bypass grants attacker internal network access; pipeline missed detection for post-exploitation lateral movement originating from compromised VPN sessions
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate GlobalProtect session initiation with immediate internal network reconnaissance or lateral movement activity. Flag sessions showing abnormal port scanning, SMB/RDP connection attempts, or data exfiltration patterns within minutes of authentication.

suggestion.title: Abnormal Data Transfer Over GlobalProtect Tunnel
suggestion.rationale: Article describes active exploitation; attackers would exfiltrate data post-breach but pipeline surfaced no command-and-control or exfiltration use cases
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GlobalProtect tunnel traffic for abnormal data volumes, encrypted tunnels within tunnels, or data flow patterns inconsistent with typical remote-work usage. Alert on sessions transferring structured data (database dumps, config files) or large archive files.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting from Compromised Internal Network
suggestion.rationale: Once inside via auth bypass, attacker typically escalates privileges and harvests credentials; pipeline missed this credential_access phase entirely
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor internal systems for LSASS access, token impersonation, SAM dumps, or credential-dumping tools (mimikatz, secretsdump) triggered by processes or users originating from GlobalProtect tunnel sessions.

suggestion.title: PAN-OS GlobalProtect Privilege Escalation Post-Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Authentication bypass alone grants VPN access; article context suggests attacker then escalates to administrative access but no privilege_escalation detection generated
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for privilege escalation attempts (sudoers addition, UAC bypasses, token elevation) originating from GlobalProtect-authenticated sessions, particularly targeting PAN-OS management plane access or internal administrative systems.

suggestion.title: Trusted Developer Tool Credential Abuse for Mass Code Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'Attackers Abuse Trusted Developer Tooling to Exfiltrate Source Code and Secrets'—core attack vector yielded zero detections. Developer tools (git, npm, pip, CI/CD systems) provide legitimate cover for unauthorized code exfil.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for anomalous repository clones/exports, unusual package manager uploads to external registries, and bulk data transfers initiated by developer tool processes. Baseline per-user git/package-manager activity volumes and alert on deviations consistent with code or secrets exfil.

suggestion.title: Credential Exposure via Developer Configuration Files
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'Secrets' exfiltration; developer workflows frequently expose credentials in .env, .git/config, docker configs, npm tokens, and kubeconfig files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for developer processes accessing credential storage locations (.env, .netrc, .aws, .kube, .docker/config.json) outside their normal workflow context. Alert on credential material appearing in process command lines or being read by unexpected process parents.

suggestion.title: Repository-Scale Enumeration and Rapid Access Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Title implies 'Source Code' plural exfiltration; attackers abuse trusted tooling to enumerate and mass-clone/export multiple repositories in compressed timeframes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track git clone, git archive, and repository API operations per user. Alert on rapid sequential clones of multiple sensitive repos, full-org repo enumeration, or archive exports followed by exfil-sized data transfers.

suggestion.title: Build/CI System Credential Harvesting and Lateral Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Trusted CI/CD, build systems, and package managers store high-value credentials for downstream systems; compromise enables pivot to exfil infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor CI/CD job logs and build system credential usage for unexpected service principal/token activations, credential reads from vault systems by unfamiliar processes, and subsequent network connections to non-org-approved endpoints.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-39987 Marimo Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'Marimo CVE-2026-39987 Exploit' as attack vector. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs and no initial-access kill-chain phase despite clear vulnerability identifier and product name in title.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Marimo web endpoints and associated Python processes for exploitation patterns. Detect HTTP requests with malformed serialization payloads, code-injection attempts in Marimo cell execution, or subprocess spawning from Marimo worker processes correlated with inbound exploit traffic.

suggestion.title: LLM Agent Subprocess Execution from Marimo
suggestion.rationale: Core attack premise: 'attackers use LLM agent for post-exploitation.' Pipeline failed to generate any execution-phase UC despite explicit agent deployment mention.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect spawning of LLM inference engines (Ollama, vLLM, LlamaCPP, transformers) as child processes under Marimo workers or in Marimo execution context. Flag unexpected Python subprocess calls to model inference endpoints, unusual library imports (torch, transformers), and GPU/memory spikes from Marimo processes.

suggestion.title: Marimo Process Beaconing to LLM/C2 Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation phase requires command channel for attacker control of LLM agent. Pipeline generated no C2 or lateral-movement use case despite implicit attacker persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from Marimo processes to known LLM API endpoints, containerized inference services, or C2 infrastructure. Detect repeated beacon patterns, DNS queries for dynamic LLM hosting, and unusual egress over non-standard ports.

suggestion.title: Persistence Mechanism via LLM Agent Scheduler
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation attack implies persistent agent deployment. Article indicates attacker maintains foothold post-CVE; pipeline missed persistence kill-chain phase entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation of scheduled tasks, cron entries, or systemd services executing LLM agents or Marimo callbacks. Monitor for modifications to Marimo config files, unauthorized pip installs in Marimo environment, and placement of agent bootstrap scripts in autostart paths.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Processing via LLM Agent Prompts
suggestion.rationale: LLM agent in post-compromise context enables adversary to query and exfiltrate system data. Pipeline generated no collection or exfiltration UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate file-read operations from Marimo process (e.g., /etc/passwd, env vars, config files) with LLM API calls or inference prompts. Detect large data volumes passed as token context to LLM, followed by encrypted or obfuscated outbound network traffic.

suggestion.title: Vishing Campaign Targeting Employee Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'breached the company's systems on April 1 in a voice phishing (vishing) attack that compromised an employee's Microsoft Entra account.' This is the entry vector; pipeline must detect inbound voice phishing attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag inbound voice calls requesting credential verification, password resets, or urgent authentication confirmation. Correlate with subsequent anomalous cloud authentication attempts (new geography, device, time-of-day) within 30 minutes of the call timestamp.

suggestion.title: Compromised Microsoft Entra Identity - Post-Vishing Activation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'compromised an employee's Microsoft Entra account'—this account then accessed Salesforce. Detect abnormal Entra activity post-compromise (new IP, impossible travel, MFA bypass, token manipulation).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful Entra login from non-corporate IP immediately following vishing timeframe, repeated MFA challenges followed by successful bypass, or token issuance to unexpected OAuth clients. Prioritize logons from geolocations impossible to reach from employee's known location.

suggestion.title: Salesforce Bulk Data Exfiltration via Compromised Identity
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'used this access to steal 42 million records from the company's Salesforce instance, including consumer and business customer names, email addresses, physical addresses, phone numbers, phone types, plan information, support ticket data, and some CPNI data.' Massive export from single compromised account.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Salesforce export jobs, bulk API queries, or data download operations retrieving >50k records by a single user. Flag unusual export-to-external-destination patterns, queries to all customer tables in single session, or off-hours bulk access from the compromised Entra identity.

suggestion.title: Ransom Threat and Extortion Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'the ShinyHunters extortion gang...told BleepingComputer that they breached...After the company refused to pay the ransom demanded by ShinyHunters...the cybercrime group leaked the documents.' Monitor for active extortion contact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on inbound extortion demands via email, contact form, or third-party notification to security/executive mailboxes. Monitor dark web forums, paste sites, and ShinyHunters' known leak domains for publication of victim company names and leaked sample data with matching schema to internal systems.

suggestion.title: CPNI Exfiltration from Telecommunications Provider
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'ShinyHunters...stole...some CPNI data' and later 'threat actors also stole additional CPNI data.' As telecom provider, CPNI (Customer Proprietary Network Information) access is tightly regulated; detect bulk access/export of subscriber records.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag bulk queries to customer tables joining phone numbers, service plans, call logs, or address records. Detect exports of CPNI data to non-approved infrastructure, staging of compressed archives containing customer records, or network exfiltration of structured data matching telecom customer schema.

suggestion.title: Multi-Victim SaaS Targeting Pattern - ShinyHunters Salesforce Campaign
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'ShinyHunters has been targeting Salesforce customers over the past year, breaching hundreds of companies worldwide.' This is a known, ongoing threat targeting SaaS instances; correlate with similar compromise patterns across customer base.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-correlate Salesforce bulk export events across multiple customers within 7-day windows. Identify clusters of Salesforce data exfiltration by compromised cloud identities; these may indicate coordinated ShinyHunters campaign activity targeting SaaS ecosystem.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email Linking to ChatGPT Web Summary Feature
suggestion.rationale: Article describes ChatGPhish as 'turns ChatGPT web summaries into a phishing surface'—attack vector is clearly phishing emails/messages leveraging ChatGPT's summary feature as a credential-harvesting redirect. Pipeline missed initial-access detection entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails containing links to ChatGPT web summary features (e.g., chat.openai.com/g/..., openai.com/blog/chatgpt-can-now-see-hear-and-speak) paired with urgency language ('verify account', 'confirm identity'). Correlate with user clicks on suspicious summary-derived links followed by login-page form submissions.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting via Fake ChatGPT Summary-Derived Phishing Page
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability leverages ChatGPT summaries to deliver users to phishing pages; article explicitly states summaries become 'a phishing surface'. Detection should capture the post-click credential capture phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for form submissions to domains mimicking OpenAI/ChatGPT infrastructure (openai-verify, chatgpt-auth, summary-confirm variants) following click-through from ChatGPT web summaries. Flag high-volume form-fill activity from different users on same spoofed domain within short window.

suggestion.title: Abuse of ChatGPT Summary Feature in Automated Phishing Campaign
suggestion.rationale: Article title specifies the vulnerability 'turns ChatGPT web summaries into a phishing surface'—implies programmatic abuse or misconfiguration. Pipeline should detect attacker-crafted queries designed to trigger summaries containing malicious links.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect ChatGPT API calls or prompt-crafting patterns that consistently generate phishing-URL-bearing summaries in responses (e.g., repeated queries to common phishing domains, URL shorteners, or redirect services). Cross-reference API caller identity with mass-email patterns.

suggestion.title: ChatGPT Web Summary Redirect to Credential Harvesting Domain
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability exploits ChatGPT's web summary rendering to inject redirects; article body truncation prevents detail, but title clearly indicates summary feature is the attack vector. Detection should identify the redirect chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track redirect chains originating from openai.com/*/summary endpoints (or similar ChatGPT summary URLs) to attacker-controlled credential-harvesting domains. Flag if redirect destination uses homograph domains (e.g., 0penai.com, chatgpt.co), IP ranges, or newly registered domains.

suggestion.title: PAN-OS CVE-2026-0257 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2026-0257 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and 'patch lag is the silent killer'; scanner hits are the first-line detection for known-exploited vulnerabilities
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when vulnerability scanners identify CVE-2026-0257 on any PAN-OS appliance, particularly those exposed on the internet. Cross-reference against patch-tracking inventory to confirm unpatched state. Due date 2026-06-01 shifts this to critical urgency post-date.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized VPN Connection via Authentication Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'allows attackers to...establish an unauthorized VPN connection'; VPN connection logs are evidence of successful exploitation
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag VPN connections initiated from non-corporate ASNs, geolocations inconsistent with known user location, or authentication bypass indicators (e.g., successful connection without RADIUS/MFA challenge). Correlate with failed auth attempts on PAN-OS management interface.

suggestion.title: Exposed PAN-OS Management Interface Port Scan Success
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV observation of active exploitation 'against exposed assets'; internet-accessible management interfaces on 443/tcp are direct targets
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect internet-routable packets reaching PAN-OS management port (443/tcp) from untrusted networks, followed by HTTP 200 responses from login page. Correlate with authentication bypass attempts. Consider asset inventory as baseline for 'exposed' flag.

suggestion.title: PAN-OS Authentication Bypass Exploitation Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article describes bypass of 'security restrictions'; multiple failed auth attempts followed by successful access without credential submission indicates bypass exploitation
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify sequences of failed password attempts on PAN-OS web interface (HTTP 403) immediately followed by successful session establishment (HTTP 200 GET to authenticated endpoint) without credential submission in request. This anomaly indicates bypass exploitation.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise VPN Reconnaissance Activity
suggestion.rationale: Successful VPN access enables internal reconnaissance; unusual VPN tunnel activity post-exploitation indicates attacker movement
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After unauthorized VPN connection, detect DNS lookups for internal assets (subnets, hostnames) or port scans across corporate ranges originating from the VPN tunnel. Unusual data volumes or protocol distributions (scanning tools) post-VPN-connect flag recon phase.

suggestion.title: PAN-OS Patch Compliance Post Due-Date
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Federal patch due: 2026-06-01' and emphasizes organizations will 'be asked about by auditors / regulators'; post-due-date unpatched instances indicate noncompliance
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On or after 2026-06-01, flag any PAN-OS instance not patched for CVE-2026-0257 as non-compliant. Generate executive report for regulatory response. Track remediation timeline separately from active exploitation timeline.

suggestion.title: vm2 module import + child process spawn correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers achieve arbitrary code execution post-escape, with PoC implying child process spawning. Article phrase: 'allows the escape from the sandbox...allows attackers to run arbitrary code.' Should detect vm2 require() followed by child_process.exec/spawn/fork within same Node process.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Node.exe processes that loaded vm2 module (via parentheses patterns or module inspection) followed immediately by spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, sh. Correlate process command-line arguments and parent context. PoC includes 'echo pwned' and 'execSync' as execution markers.

suggestion.title: Prototype chain constructor access via Buffer manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Article PoC specifically states: 'By combining Buffer.call.call({}.__lookupGetter__, Buffer, __proto__) ... the host's TypeError constructor can be obtained'. This is the direct privilege escalation mechanism. Should flag __lookupGetter__/__lookupSetter__ invocations on Buffer objects in Node sandboxed contexts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Node.js process arguments and loaded code for regex patterns /__lookupGetter__|__lookupSetter__|\.__proto__|Buffer\.call\.call/ combined with presence of vm2 module in parent context. Flag constructor access attempts on Buffer, Error, or TypeError objects.

suggestion.title: ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE abuse for sandbox context escaping
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically calls out 'Node.js's ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE Error' as part of exploitation chain. This error code is intentionally triggered to obtain host's TypeError constructor. Should detect ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE in logs/errors correlated with vm2 execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Index Node.js application error logs for ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE when parent process is running vm2 or new VM(). Flag when error originates from sandboxed code context followed by process property access or require() calls.

suggestion.title: vm2 NodeVM instantiation with untrusted code input source
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attackers leveraging vm2 to escape sandbox—implies vm2 is being used to execute untrusted code. Should detect NodeVM/VM class instantiation where code argument originates from HTTP request, user input, or file upload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Node.js process spawning with 'new VM(' or 'new NodeVM(' in command-line arguments, combined with preceding HTTP request/user input. Flag if code parameter contains __proto__, constructor, or Buffer manipulation patterns.

suggestion.title: Suspicious mainModule.require escalation post-vm2 execution
suggestion.rationale: Article body's Splunk detection explicitly flags 'mainModule.require' as indicator. This is how post-escape code gains access to real require(). Should detect mainModule property access or require() invocation in code context known to be sandboxed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag when Node.js processes attempt to access process.mainModule.require, module.constructor.prototype.require, or global.require within vm2 execution context. Track return value use (e.g., .require('child_process').exec()).

suggestion.title: vm2 package version regression in deployment/CI logs
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes CVE-2026-47131 affects vm2 ≤3.11.3. Should detect deployments, container builds, or CI jobs that introduce or fail to upgrade past vulnerable version. Complements inventory hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install, yarn add, package-lock.json updates, and Docker builds for vm2 version pinning to ≤3.11.3 or version ranges that include vulnerable versions. Flag in CI/CD pipelines, dependency upgrades, and container build stages.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable vm2 application — package version ≤3.11.3 enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names affected versions 'vm2 package (<=3.11.3)' and describes version-pinning as the remediation vector. Pipeline ignored straightforward asset detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate Endpoint.Filesystem for node_modules/vm2/package.json or package-lock.json containing version string <=3.11.3. Cross-correlate with running Node.js processes to identify at-risk applications.

suggestion.title: Node.js sandbox escape — shell spawning after vm2 execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes post-exploitation via 'child_process' and 'execSync' spawning shells to run enumeration (whoami, id, hostname). Pipeline created UC_25_2 structurally but algorithm failed to extract it.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Node.js process spawning unexpected child shell (cmd.exe, bash, sh, powershell) within 5 seconds, especially if command contains reconnaissance keywords (whoami, id, uname, /etc/passwd, ipconfig). Correlate parent command line for vm2 or user-supplied script input.

suggestion.title: Source code pattern — nesting:true without explicit require in vm2 config
suggestion.rationale: Article root cause: 'nesting: true without explicit require still allows full RCE' — the vulnerability hinges on missing require option in application code. Pipeline did not generate code-pattern detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Static analysis: in JavaScript application code, detect vm2 instantiation with nesting:true and missing or undefined require option (e.g., `new NodeVM({nesting: true})` without require key). Flag as misconfiguration requiring developer notification.

suggestion.title: JavaScript process execution flow — require() to OS command execution chain
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names exploitation methods 'child_process' and 'execSync' as the RCE vector. Pipeline missed correlation between JavaScript require patterns and subsequent OS execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Node.js process loading child_process module (via require logs if available) followed by shell process spawning, especially if the JavaScript source originates from untrusted input or is a web-facing application receiving external code.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable npm package introduction — vm2 ≤3.11.3 in new deployments
suggestion.rationale: Article describes this as a supply-chain exposure surface. Pipeline should alert on new package.json commits or npm installs pinning vm2 to vulnerable versions after 2026-05-29 publication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for package.json modifications or npm install/update events that add or retain vm2 ≤3.11.3 post-advisory date. Flag as supply-chain risk requiring immediate remediation or version pinning audit.

suggestion.title: Behavioral hunt — Node.js enumeration sequence post-application execution
suggestion.rationale: Article states exploitation yields RCE allowing OS command execution. Pattern: application accepts JavaScript input → vm2 processes it → shell commands issued in sequence (whoami, hostname, ifconfig). Pipeline template was weak (looking for process names like exploit.js, which is unrealistic).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequence of shell commands issued within 30s from single Node.js parent process: reconnaissance (whoami, id, hostname, uname), network enumeration (ifconfig, ipconfig), and file system access (/etc/passwd). Presence of 3+ indicates likely sandbox escape exploitation.

suggestion.title: NodeVM sandbox escape via process module — getBuiltinModule call detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states "denylist misses process" and bypass exploits require `process.getBuiltinModule()` calls to access host functions. No UC detects this abuse pattern directly. Phrase: "Both can be used from sandboxed code to reach host-side execution primitives."
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Node.js process executing code containing getBuiltinModule pattern or require('process') followed by privileged module access. Monitor for require statements attempting to load process builtin in JavaScript payloads or process command-line arguments containing inspector/promises or process module references.

suggestion.title: NodeVM sandbox escape via inspector/promises module — esoteric module import detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states inspector/promises as bypass vector ("denylist misses... inspector/promises") but no hunt detects inspector module access. Phrase: "Both can be used from sandboxed code."
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file operations or process events related to loading inspector/promises module from Node.js sandbox context. Unusual: inspector module imports from application-provided sandbox code or dynamic require() of inspector submodules.

suggestion.title: Host-level code execution post-vm2 escape — elevated privilege or file write from Node.js
suggestion.rationale: Article describes sandbox escaping to "execute code in the host process." No hunt specifically detects file modifications, registry changes, or privilege escalation originating from Node.js post-exploit. Phrase: "execute code in the host process."
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file creation/modification in sensitive directories (System32, Program Files, user startup folders) or registry modification with Node.js as parent process or initiating process. Monitor for host-level execution (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, C++ runtime execution) triggered by Node.js interpreter with non-standard privilege elevation.

suggestion.title: NodeVM vulnerability exploitation chain — process escape + shell spawn correlation
suggestion.rationale: Kill chain described in article but marked "none detected." Exploit flow is: bypass denylist → use process/inspector modules → spawn host shell. No correlation hunt between privilege escalation and subsequent shell execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Node.js process lifetime with immediate spawning of system shells (cmd.exe, powershell.exe). Look for Node.js executing within seconds before child shell creation, particularly when Node.js is running untrusted code (npm package, web server, etc.) or has unusual parent process (web server, email, document converter).

suggestion.title: vm2/NodeVM package version detection on vulnerable versions 3.0–3.11.3
suggestion.rationale: Article/KQL implies vulnerable range but UC_23_2 detects presence only. No separate hunt for direct package.json or require graph analysis to find vm2 use in codebase. Phrase: "Vulnerabilities.severity, vulnerable versions implied by version pattern."
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan package.json, package-lock.json, yarn.lock, npm shrinkwrap for vm2 dependency within vulnerable version range (>= 3.0.0, <= 3.11.3). Scan source code for direct vm2.NodeVM imports or require('vm2') calls. Flag repositories, container images, and deployments containing vulnerable versions.

suggestion.title: Promise.prototype or Promise.then manipulation in Node.js execution contexts
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'localPromise constructor was changed to call `this.then(undefined, eater)` to ensure a rejected promise' — core exploit exploits Promise.then() behavior. No hunt covers detection of Promise prototype/method modification patterns, which are indicative of sandbox escape attempts pre-code-execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for evidence of Promise.prototype.then or Promise.prototype.constructor being reassigned or Symbol.species being accessed on Promise objects within Node.js process address space. Can manifest as unusual .then() chains or constructor property access in command-line arguments or injected code strings.

suggestion.title: vm2.VM() invocations containing child_process require() or import statements
suggestion.rationale: Article describes sandbox escape enabling 'arbitrary commands on the host system' — this happens via child_process module. Detection should catch the dangerous pattern of code being sandboxed AND having access to process spawning, indicating likely malicious setup.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Node.js code patterns where vm2.VM() is instantiated and the code string being sandboxed contains require('child_process'), require('child_process').exec, or similar process spawning calls. High signal-to-noise if targeting unusual npm packages or dynamic code.

suggestion.title: Correlation: vm2 npm installation or module load followed by child process spawning from node.exe
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 'Vulnerable vm2 package (<=3.11.3)' as exposure point — suggests two-step attack: acquire vm2 (via npm install, package.json modification, or node_modules sync), then exploit. Detection should flag temporal cluster of vm2 acquisition + suspicious child processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate npm install / package.json modify events involving vm2 with subsequent spawning of cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or curl.exe from node.exe within 5-60 second window on same host/user. Filter out CI/CD contexts and legitimate build pipelines.

suggestion.title: PraisonAI generate_api_server_code execution detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'code-generator (`praisonai.deploy.api.generate_api_server_code`)' as the root cause—this specific function call is the vulnerability trigger and precedes Flask startup. Should be hunted independently from the broader deploy command wrapper.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Python process execution with command-line arguments or module invocation referencing 'generate_api_server_code'. This function call represents the actual generation of vulnerable code before server startup and is more specific than UC_14_3's deploy wrapper detection.

suggestion.title: Flask server public-bind detection (0.0.0.0 on TCP/8005)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'binds to `0.0.0.0` per the recommended sample YAML'—this is the network exposure precondition. UC_14_4 detects inbound traffic, but this UC detects the bind itself (defense-evasion via misconfiguration).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Python/Flask process arguments containing 'host=0.0.0.0', 'bind=0.0.0.0', or network bind syscalls from python.exe/python3 to wildcard addresses on port 8005. Alert on Flask initialization logs showing public binding.

suggestion.title: YAML PraisonAI deployment configuration staging
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'recommended sample YAML' that triggers the vulnerable deploy. Detection of config file creation/modification precedes command execution and represents the persistence/configuration step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for YAML file creation/modification in user home directories, /tmp, or app-specific paths with names matching PraisonAI patterns (deploy.yaml, config.yaml, praisonai*.yaml, api_config.yaml) that temporally precede praisonai deploy command execution.

suggestion.title: PraisonAI Platform sequential/enumeration-pattern resource ID discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability allows access via primary-key lookup of resource IDs (agent_id, issue_id, project_id, etc.). Detection should identify attackers enumerating valid UUIDs by observing patterns of 404 → 200 responses on nested-resource endpoints, not just hit-count thresholds.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/{resource_kind}/{inner_id} endpoints. Flag anomalous sequences of 404 (invalid ID) followed by 200 (hit) responses, or sustained high rate of HTTP 404s on sequential/similar UUID patterns, indicating systematic probing for valid resource IDs.

suggestion.title: PraisonAI Platform access to unauthorized workspace resources
suggestion.rationale: Article describes IDOR that bypasses workspace authorization checks. Attacker accesses resources in workspaces they are not members of. Detection needs to correlate Web access logs against workspace membership roster.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate user's API requests to /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/... against authoritative workspace membership records. Flag accesses where user is not in the member list of the workspace_id, or accesses specific nested resources (agents, issues, projects) where user lacks role-based permission.

suggestion.title: PraisonAI Platform self-role escalation via member PATCH endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'member-role privilege escalation.' Attackers exploit the IDOR to modify their own member record and escalate from user → admin. Detection should identify PATCH requests where caller elevates their own role field.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PATCH requests to /api/v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/members/{member_id}.
