Flag if: (1) authenticated user's ID matches {member_id} in the request, (2) role field in request body changes to 'admin' or 'owner' (escalation), (3) HTTP 200 response indicates modification succeeded.

suggestion.title: Hardcoded JWT Secret In-Use — Absence of PLATFORM_JWT_SECRET Override
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The JWT signing secret defaults to the hardcoded literal "dev-secret-change-me"'. Pipeline must detect when this hardcoded default is actively in use—indicated by praisonai_platform processes launched without any PLATFORM_JWT_SECRET environment variable set.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify praisonai_platform uvicorn instances where PLATFORM_JWT_SECRET is not present in the process environment or command line. Enumerate process environment on suspected hosts to confirm absence. Cross-reference against patched/properly-configured baseline deployments.

suggestion.title: Safety Check Bypass — PLATFORM_ENV Default Remains 'dev' in Production
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'A safety check exists but only fires when PLATFORM_ENV != "dev"; the default value of PLATFORM_ENV is "dev", so the check is silently bypassed in any deployment that does [not override it]'. The root cause is the default environment remaining unset or set to 'dev'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag praisonai_platform deployments where PLATFORM_ENV is absent or equals 'dev' in prod/staging network segments or cloud accounts. Compare against secure baseline configurations where PLATFORM_ENV is explicitly set to 'production' or 'staging'.

suggestion.title: JWT Token Forgery Behavioral Indicator — Rapid Multi-User Authentication from Single Source
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'allowing token forgery for any user'. Token forgery would enable rapid impersonation across user identities. Detect behavioral anomaly of single source authenticating as many different users in short window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for single source IP/session establishing valid authenticated sessions with 5+ distinct user accounts in <5 minute window. Correlate with workspace access (UC_10_3) to identify lateral movement via forged credentials.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable praisonai-platform Version Enumeration and Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline must identify praisonai-platform deployments to scope asset exposure. Article does not specify vulnerable version range, creating a dependency gap for version-based hunting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all praisonai-platform installations across infrastructure via process monitoring (uvicorn + praisonai_platform pattern), pip list enumeration, and container manifest scanning. Cross-reference against CVE database for affected versions once vendor specifies ranges.

suggestion.title: Configuration File / Environment Variable Audit — Hardcoded Secret String Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'hardcoded literal "dev-secret-change-me"'. This default string may persist in config files, git history, or uncleared environment snapshots, serving as a traceable indicator of vulnerable or misconfigured deployments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search environment variable dumps, config files, and startup logs for the literal string 'dev-secret-change-me'. Presence indicates either vulnerability in-use or recent/incomplete remediation. Hunt in backup/snapshot data to identify drift from secure configuration baseline.

suggestion.title: LinkedIn Social Engineering Profile Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'LinkedIn Social Engineering to Deploy Custom macOS Malware.' Pipeline has zero IOCs or initial-access detections. Should capture newly-created LinkedIn profiles or suspicious outreach to employees, particularly those with macOS/developer personas.

suggestion.title: Malware Execution from Downloaded Archive on macOS

suggestion.title: Suspicious Archive Extraction and Execution Chain on macOS
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'custom macOS Malware' delivery—typical chain involves archive download → extraction → execution. Pipeline kill-chain reconstruction is empty despite this clear execution sequence.

Flag execution of .app bundles or LaunchAgent plists created within same session as archive operations. Alert on obfuscated file names or mismatched extensions.

suggestion.title: Command and Control Communication Post-Malware Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'custom macOS Malware' implies post-exploitation C2 or callbacks. Pipeline kill-chain shows zero phases; should include command-and-control detection for typical macOS C2 patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect beaconing or DNS queries to unknown domains from macOS hosts post-infection. Flag high-frequency HTTPS connections to non-standard ports, proxy tunneling via legitimate services, or DNS over HTTPS to unconfigured resolvers. Baseline against org known SaaS.

suggestion.title: Persistence via macOS Launch Agents or Scheduled Tasks

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ~/Library/LaunchAgents and /Library/LaunchDaemons for new plist creation with suspicious executable paths or hidden binaries. Flag modification timestamps clustering with malware execution events. Alert on plist files with unusual permissions or obfuscated binary references.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration via Custom macOS Malware
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Deploy Custom macOS Malware'—custom payloads often include exfiltration. No exfiltration-phase detections in empty kill-chain reconstruction. Should detect unusual data flows post-infection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk data transfer to external IPs or cloud storage from macOS hosts post-infection. Flag archiving of sensitive files (.zip, .tar, .gz) in temp directories followed by exfiltration. Monitor for data staging in non-standard directories before network transmission.

suggestion.title: HTTPSpy Tool Execution Detection

suggestion.title: HelloDoor Remote Access Tool Installation

suggestion.title: VS Code Remote Tunnels Abuse for C2

suggestion.title: Kimsuky Phishing Email with Tool Deployment

suggestion.title: Kimsuky C2 Infrastructure Communication

suggestion.title: Malicious NuGet Package Installation Detected

suggestion.title: Credential Extraction from Running Processes Post-Package Installation

suggestion.title: Cloud Credential Enumeration or Exfiltration from Package Processes

suggestion.title: Outbound C2 Communication from Package-Spawned Processes

suggestion.title: Typosquat Package Name Matching in Package Manager Logs

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Execution Following Phishing Artifact

suggestion.title: SYSTEM Context Process Loading Encryption Libraries

suggestion.title: Scheduled Task Executing Suspicious Binary from Non-Standard Path
suggestion.rationale: Ransomware delivery via task implies malware payload; should detect task actions pointing to temporary, obfuscated, or unsigned executables.

Alert if creator is non-admin or execution context is SYSTEM from low-privilege source.

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for registry HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run modifications. Detect creation of .lnk files in Startup folders. Alert on scheduled task creation with suspicious payloads or execution from temp directories.

suggestion.title: Post-Takedown Sinkhole Traffic - Botnet Remediation Indicator
suggestion.rationale: Dutch authorities dismantled botnet—detection should capture the transition from live C&C to law enforcement sinkhole to measure remediation progress and identify stubborn infections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-takedown, monitor for continued DNS resolution of botnet C&C domains that now resolve to sinkhole IPs. Flag endpoints still attempting C&C callback to sinkhole infrastructure as candidates for remediation. Trend decline in sinkhole connections to validate botnet cleanup effectiveness.

suggestion.title: Botnet Malware Family Identification - Hash/Signature Matching
suggestion.rationale: Article references specific botnet dismantled by authorities but pipeline extracted zero file hashes or malware signatures—should surface malware samples and detection signatures for this botnet family.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Match discovered botnet samples against known malware hash databases and YARA signatures. Deploy file-integrity monitoring for known botnet binary locations. Alert on execution of botnet family samples observed in wild or recovered during law enforcement operations.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Installation with Reconnaissance Commands
suggestion.rationale: Article describes malicious packages executing 'postinstall scripts' to 'collect reconnaissance data from developer and build environments'—this is execution + discovery in the npm lifecycle. No UC captured this.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes spawned during npm install/update with parents npm/node executing whoami, uname, env, id, or network enumeration commands. Correlate with package installation events and unusual postinstall script execution timeframes.

suggestion.title: Dependency Confusion Attack Pattern—Version Resolution Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article's central attack vector is 'dependency confusion' exploitation. No UC covered abnormal version resolution, package source switching, or package metadata inconsistencies. Should detect when npm resolves from public registry instead of private after initial private fetch failure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm package resolution decisions and version selection logic. Alert when a package that previously resolved from private registry (organization scoped) suddenly resolves from public npm registry, or when version numbers spike unexpectedly in resolution chains.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration During npm Install via HTTP Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article states packages collected reconnaissance data and profiled environments—this data must be exfiltrated. No UC covers outbound network activity initiated from npm postinstall scripts or unexpected C2 connections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests from npm processes during package installation, especially to non-standard domains or IPs without prior DNS history. Flag encoded/compressed payloads in POST bodies during postinstall execution.

suggestion.title: npm postinstall Script Execution with Elevated Scope
suggestion.rationale: Packages execute reconnaissance in 'developer and build environments'—implies execution in CI/CD or privileged build contexts. No UC specifically alerts on postinstall scripts running with elevated privs or in automated environments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm postinstall scripts executed in CI/CD runners (GitHub Actions, Azure Pipelines) or elevated process contexts (SYSTEM, root). Baseline normal postinstall activity and flag anomalies in script runtime, arguments, or spawned children.

suggestion.title: npm Package Metadata Tampering—Suspicious Version Deltas
suggestion.rationale: 33 packages were malicious—suggests rapid publication or version spoofing. No UC covers abnormal package versioning patterns, sudden major version jumps, or packages with identical postinstall scripts across versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm package publication metadata for anomalies: multiple packages published to same author within short timeframe, versions with identical postinstall checksums, packages with no legitimate commit history, or rapid version succession without changelog.

suggestion.title: Forged GlobalProtect Authentication Cookie Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attackers were able to connect to the device via VPN using forged cookies... generate a forged authentication override cookie for an arbitrary user.' Core attack technique; detectable via cookie cryptographic anomalies and auth validation patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on authentication override cookie usage where decrypted payload passes validation but signature verification is absent or bypassed. Correlate successful auth via override cookies with absence of corresponding credential validation events in upstream systems.

suggestion.title: Public Certificate Extraction from GlobalProtect Portal
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'retrieve the public certificates exposed by a GlobalProtect portal or gateway... obtain the corresponding public key via the HTTPS session.' Attackers enumerate certs to forge cookies; certificate requests to GlobalProtect portals should be monitored.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTPS requests to GlobalProtect gateways that query, parse, or export certificate metadata. Flag certificate enumeration followed within hours by authentication attempts from same source IP.

suggestion.title: VPN Authentication Success Without Session Establishment
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'even though the appliance accepted the forged cookie, they were unable to establish a full VPN session.' Partial success indicates exploitation; incomplete tunnel setup combined with successful auth is anomalous.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on VPN gateway logs showing Phase 1/2 authentication completion followed by tunnel negotiation failure. Baseline normal auth:session-established ratio; flag sources exceeding failed-session thresholds.

suggestion.title: Administrator Account VPN Access from IaaS Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'targeted the local administrator account... earliest date for observed exploitation was May 17, 2026 from infrastructure hosted by Vultr, with a second wave... May 21 originating from Dromatics Systems.' Admin VPN from Vultr/AWS/Azure ranges is abnormal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag successful VPN authentications for administrative accounts originating from IaaS provider IP space (Vultr, AWS, Azure, GCP). Baseline legitimate admin VPN sources; alert on first-seen IaaS + admin combination.

suggestion.title: Multiple Failed Auth Attempts Preceding Override Cookie Success
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attacks began with hackers authenticating... two waves of attacks detected.' Attackers likely tested payloads; pattern of failed standard auth followed by override-cookie auth is suspicious.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sources with 5+ failed standard auth attempts to GlobalProtect in 1-hour window followed by successful auth override cookie usage. Flag as credential-stuffing-turned-exploit pattern.

suggestion.title: Auth Override Cookies Enabled Alongside Certificate Reuse
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'If the same certificate is reused for both HTTPS services and authentication override cookies, attackers can obtain the corresponding public key via the HTTPS session and then use it to create forged cookies.' Configuration audit identifies vulnerable setups enabling the attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit PAN-OS device configurations for: (1) auth override cookies enabled, (2) certificate used for both HTTPS and override cookies, (3) lack of signature verification on override cookies. Flag as critical misconfig; requires immediate certificate separation or override-cookie disable.

suggestion.title: GlobalProtect Unauthenticated API Access Post-Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'authentication bypass' in GlobalProtect — this allows attackers to invoke API endpoints normally protected by credential validation. Pipeline should detect requests to admin or sensitive endpoints (/api/session, /api/config) that succeed despite missing or invalid auth tokens.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP 200 responses to /api/* or /ssl-vpn/transaction paths when requests lack valid SAML assertions, JWT tokens, or session cookies. Correlate with source IPs probing multiple endpoints in short timeframes or using known exploit user-agents.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Portal Admin Privilege Escalation Post-Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Authentication bypass admits attacker to portal; article's focus on 'active exploitation' implies post-compromise actions. Pipeline should surface detection for elevation to admin roles or credential creation immediately following auth-bypass attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation of admin-group users, SAML/LDAP policy changes, or role assignments occurring within 5 minutes of unauthenticated API access attempts. Flag if new accounts are created from non-standard administrative interfaces or with properties matching known Metasploit/public exploit defaults.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-0257 Signature-Based Exploit Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article names CVE-2026-0257 explicitly under 'active exploitation' — pipeline must surface IOC for the vulnerability identifier and craft detection rules for known attack patterns (malformed SAML, parameter injection, token crafting).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Generate signatures for HTTP requests with CVE-2026-0257 exploitation patterns: malformed or oversized SAML assertions, URL-encoded bypass attempts, null-byte injection in auth headers, or JWT claims without signature validation. Cross-reference against public PoC repositories and vulnerable version identifiers (e.g., <=PAN-OS 10.1.x).

suggestion.title: VPN Lateral Movement via Compromised GlobalProtect Session
suggestion.rationale: Successful auth bypass grants attacker trusted VPN session — article's 'active exploitation' phase implies threat actor pivots to internal resources. Pipeline should detect post-breach lateral movement from newly-established GlobalProtect sessions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful GlobalProtect authentication-bypass events with unusual RDP/SSH login attempts from the same source IP within 10 minutes. Alert if a single VPN session IP attempts password spray across 5+ internal hosts or logs into high-privilege accounts without corresponding successful authentication to the VPN portal.

suggestion.title: GlobalProtect Configuration Tampering for Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation typically involves backdoor installation or configuration hardening by attacker — pipeline should detect unauthorized changes to auth policies, certificate pinning, or account creation in PAN-OS config.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for edits to /config/devices/entry/*/deviceconfig/system/authentication parameters, including SAML IdP endpoints, certificate stores, or user-group mappings. Flag changes committed from non-administrative consoles or from IPs lacking baseline admin access patterns.

suggestion.title: Botnet C2 Communications (High Volume)
suggestion.rationale: 17 million infected devices implies large-scale outbound command-and-control traffic; article explicitly references 'botnet,' establishing C2 as core attack phase. No detection rule provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound connections from large cohorts of internal hosts to previously identified C2 domains/IPs on non-standard ports or via DNS tunneling. Botnet takedown articles typically disclose C2 WHOIS registrations, sinkhole domains, or ASN blocks that can be used as anchors for backscatter detection.

suggestion.title: Malware Execution—Mass Infection Pattern
suggestion.rationale: 17-million-device scale indicates coordinated infection campaign; article does not specify infection vector (drive-by, email, supply-chain) but detection hypothesis must cover process execution post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious script interpreter invocations (powershell.exe -enc, cmd.exe /c), unusual DLL loads from temp directories, or process trees with mismatched parent-child relationships. Botnet malware often uses obfuscated loaders before dropping persistence mechanism.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Registry/Scheduled Tasks (Botnet)
suggestion.rationale: Botnet maintaining 17M infections requires persistence mechanism; article title implies successful long-term compromise. No persistence detection rule surfaced.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\Run or HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run modifications by non-admin processes, or rare scheduled task creation with binary paths pointing to %temp% or %appdata% locations.

suggestion.title: Dutch Authority Sinkhole/Takedown IOC Ingestion
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Dutch Authorities Dismantle Botnet'—takedown action implies law enforcement has published C2 domains, malware hashes, or registrar data. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs despite high-confidence disclosure likelihood.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Automated IOC feed should have scraped official Dutch NCSC/MIVD statements or coordinated takedown reports. Flag any historical DNS queries, passive DNS hits, or certificate transparency logs matching published sinkhole domains.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Detection (Botnet Replication)
suggestion.rationale: Botnet reaching 17M devices suggests active worm-like propagation or lateral movement capabilities; no detection rule addresses how the malware spreads within networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for SMB file transfers to multiple internal hosts from a single source, RDP/SSH login storms from newly compromised machines to other subnets, or Windows share enumeration (net view, arp scans) followed by lateral movement attempts.

suggestion.title: Botnet Initial Access Vector Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article does not specify infection method (email phishing, malvertising, exploit kit, software vulnerability, supply-chain), but 17M scale suggests coordinated delivery—likely exploit or social engineering. No initial-access detection rule generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate mass email campaigns with executable/macro attachments or malicious URLs to spike in new process creation, file downloads, or web requests from internal hosts. If exploit kit: monitor for suspicious DNS resolution patterns or browser process crashes before malware execution.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated AJAX Access to WP Maps Pro with check_temp Parameter
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'AJAX endpoint used for this feature was accessible to unauthenticated users' and 'request is made with a check_temp parameter set to false, the function creates a new WordPress user.' Initial access vector undetected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for POST/GET requests to /wp-content/plugins/wp-maps-pro/* endpoints with check_temp=false parameter from non-authenticated sources. Correlate with WordPress version metadata to identify vulnerable installations.

suggestion.title: WordPress Admin Account Creation via wp_insert_user() Function
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'function creates a new WordPress user via wp_insert_user() with the hardcoded role of administrator, a randomly generated username, and the hardcoded email address support@flippercode.com.' Direct privilege escalation signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on new wp_users table entries with role='administrator' created without prior authentication session, or with email support@flippercode.com. Flag wp_insert_user() calls in plugin hooks unrelated to legitimate user registration flows.

suggestion.title: Passwordless Magic Login URL Authentication to Admin Account
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'generates a "magic login URL" using generate_login_link(), stores it as user meta, and returns it in the response body. Once the attacker visits this URL, they are automatically authenticated.' Token-based admin bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect successful WordPress admin logins from newly created user accounts with zero prior login attempts, no password change events, and immediate admin-level actions within minutes of account creation.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Web Shell and Backdoor Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Having admin-level access on the site means attackers can inject persistent backdoors, modify content...deploy web shells, install malicious plugins.' Persistence indicators following admin account creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor wp-content/uploads/ and wp-content/plugins/ for suspicious .php or executable file writes within 5 minutes of suspicious admin account creation. Flag files with obfuscated/base64 code, eval() calls, or reverse-shell indicators.

suggestion.title: Malicious WordPress Plugin Installation by Rogue Admin
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'install malicious plugins' as explicit post-compromise action. Plugin installation audit trail should correlate with rogue admin creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on plugin installations triggered by newly created admin accounts or accounts with creation timestamps matching AJAX exploitation attempts. Flag installs from non-official WordPress plugin repositories.

suggestion.title: WP Maps Pro Version 6.1.0 and Older Present in Environment
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'impacts WP Maps Pro versions 6.1.0 and older' with fix in 'WP Maps Pro 6.1.1 was released with a fix on May 20.' Asset inventory failure for vulnerable plugin detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan all WordPress installations for WP Maps Pro plugin via plugin headers, readme.txt version strings, or HTTP footprinting. Alert on any version ≤ 6.1.0 remaining in production >7 days post-advisory date (2026-05-20).

suggestion.title: ChatGPT API Abuse for Malware Development
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes GREYVIBE 'leverage[s] ChatGPT' to 'fuel cyberattacks.' No use case generated despite this being a primary attack vector—APT actors requesting code generation, malware obfuscation, or evasion techniques via LLM APIs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Python/PowerShell processes spawning curl/wget requests to ChatGPT API endpoints (api.openai.com) or Google Gemini APIs with suspicious Content-Type application/json payloads. Flag accounts making requests for malware-development keywords: 'obfuscate code', 'reverse shell', 'bypass antivirus'.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email Crafting via LLM API
suggestion.rationale: Article title 'Leverage ChatGPT and Google Gemini' strongly implies AI-generated phishing content for social engineering. No detection rule for identifying AI-crafted phishing emails despite this being a core attack mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag emails with linguistic patterns consistent with LLM generation (unusual formality, template-like structure, generic salutations + specific payload). Cross-reference sender IP against ChatGPT API proxy/endpoint access logs. Monitor for bulk email sends preceded by LLM API queries.

suggestion.title: Google Gemini C2 Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'Google Gemini' as a tool GREYVIBE leverages, yet no detection for using Gemini API as a command-and-control channel or data exfiltration tunnel. LLM APIs provide high-entropy C2 camouflage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes sending API requests to gemini.google.com or generativelanguage.googleapis.com with suspiciously large payload or response sizes. Flag requests from non-browser processes or from systems with known malware execution history.

suggestion.title: LLM-Assisted Reconnaissance & Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Use of ChatGPT/Gemini for attack planning implies reconnaissance automation and social-engineering payload generation. No detection for bulk LLM queries requesting victim information, employee lists, or credential-harvesting templates.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect ChatGPT API requests containing queries like 'find employees', 'linkedin scraping', 'email enumeration', or 'harvest credentials'. Flag API accounts with geolocation/network anomalies or requests from VPN/proxy infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Malware Code Generation via Public LLM APIs
suggestion.rationale: Title implies GREYVIBE directly uses public LLM models (ChatGPT, Gemini) for attack tooling. Pipeline should detect development toolchains requesting generated malware families, payload templates, or evasion code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate ChatGPT API activity with local code compilation/execution. Monitor for file writes to temp directories immediately after LLM API queries. Flag requests for 'RAT code', 'privilege escalation exploit', 'AV evasion technique'.

suggestion.title: GREYVIBE Infrastructure & Credential Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article names GREYVIBE explicitly but pipeline extracted zero IOCs—no known C2 domains, email patterns, API keys, or infrastructure associations for this actor. Should contain fingerprint baseline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Once GREYVIBE infrastructure is identified (awaiting full article), create rules for domain/IP lookups, email sender domain registration patterns, and ASN/geolocation clustering. Flag any endpoint connecting to confirmed GREYVIBE C2 infrastructure.

suggestion.title: npm package install from unexpected registry source
suggestion.rationale: Article core mechanic is 'abuse dependency confusion' — attackers register package names on public npm registry that match private org dependencies, exploiting npm's resolution order. Detection must catch install of public packages where private scopes expected. 'Malicious npm packages abuse dependency confusion'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install operations; alert when package version resolved from registry.npmjs.org instead of configured private registry for @scoped packages; flag package installs where version differs significantly from previous baseline in build environment.

suggestion.title: Environment profiling commands from npm post-install hooks
suggestion.rationale: Attack objective to 'profile developer and build environments' — malicious postinstall scripts enumerate system state. Article: 'collect reconnaissance data from developer and build environments.' Expect systeminfo, uname, whoami, env, npm list, git config, docker/k8s queries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child processes spawned by node.js/npm (svchost.exe, conhost.exe) executing reconnaissance commands. Flag npm processes reading environment variables en-masse, querying system registry for tool installations, or executing docker/git configuration reads during package install.

suggestion.title: Data exfiltration via npm postinstall network callback
suggestion.rationale: Reconnaissance data must be exfiltrated. Article describes 'collect' implying data staging and transmission. Postinstall hooks are vector for out-of-band communication. 'Collect reconnaissance data' → exfiltration to attacker infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound HTTP(S) connections from npm/node.js processes during package installation; flag connections to non-CDN destinations; detect POST requests with environment data (base64-encoded JSON serializing hostname, OS, user, installed software); flag compression/staging of data in node_modules/.bin before transmission.

suggestion.title: Code obfuscation in npm package post-install scripts
suggestion.rationale: Malicious packages hide payloads in postinstall hooks. Article mentions 'observed tradecraft' — offensive packaging techniques. Payloads obfuscated via base64, eval, require() from temporary decrypted sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan installed package.json and node_modules/*/package.json for postinstall/preinstall scripts containing eval, Function(), Buffer.from().toString(), or base64 patterns; monitor for node.js execution with obfuscated code arguments; flag dynamic require() from /tmp or %TEMP%.

suggestion.title: CI/CD credential and pipeline enumeration from npm context
suggestion.rationale: Attack targets 'build environments' specifically. Attackers enumerate CI/CD tooling, credentials, and deployment secrets. Article: 'profile developer and build environments' — includes stealing secrets for lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect reads of CI/CD environment variables (GITHUB_TOKEN, GITLAB_CI, JENKINS_HOME, CIRCLECI, BUILDKITE, TRAVIS, BUILD_TOKEN, etc.) from npm/node.js processes; monitor for SSH key enumeration in ~/.ssh or CI credential stores; flag git credential-helper queries and .netrc access.

suggestion.title: Lateral movement via build artifact compromise
suggestion.rationale: Reconnaissance of build systems likely enables follow-on compromise. Malicious npm install in CI/CD pipeline can inject backdoors into build artifacts, Docker images, or deployment packages. Article describes 'build environments' as target — implies downstream damage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect modifications to build output directories (dist/, build/, .dist/) during npm install phase; monitor for artifact signing key access or Docker layer modifications; flag unexpected commits to CI artifact repositories or image pushes from build nodes with new digests during package install window.

suggestion.title: GlobalProtect Admin Authentication via Override Cookie
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'authenticating to GlobalProtect gateways using forged authentication override cookies that targeted the local administrator account'—must detect unauthorized admin VPN auth
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on GlobalProtect authentication attempts to local admin accounts using authentication override cookies. Establish baseline for override-cookie auth patterns and flag deviations, especially successful admin auth followed by immediate VPN session establishment or geographic anomalies.

suggestion.title: VPN Connection Attempts from Vultr and Dromatics Systems Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article documents: 'first observed exploitation on May 18 from infrastructure hosted by Vultr' and 'second wave of attacks detected on May 21 originating from Dromatics Systems'—track infrastructure-based threat indicators
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Block or alert on VPN connection attempts originating from Vultr and Dromatics Systems ASN ranges. Correlate VPN auth attempts with known malicious hosting infrastructure and flag authentication override usage from these sources.

suggestion.title: Authentication Override Cookie Acceptance Without Signature Verification
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'decrypts these types of cookies using a configured private key and then trusts the decrypted contents without performing any signature verification'—detect the validation gap being exploited
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for GlobalProtect authentication override cookie processing that accepts decrypted cookies without cryptographic signature validation. Alert on cookie acceptance to privileged accounts (local admin) when device is configured with authentication override enabled.

suggestion.title: Certificate Misuse: HTTPS Public Key Extraction for Cookie Forgery
suggestion.rationale: Article explains: 'If the same certificate is reused for both HTTPS services and authentication override cookies, attackers can obtain the corresponding public key via the HTTPS session and then use it to create forged cookies'—detect certificate reuse misconfiguration
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit GlobalProtect device configurations to flag when HTTPS service certificates and authentication override cookie signing certificates are identical. Monitor for unusual certificate enumeration attempts against GlobalProtect HTTPS endpoints that precede authentication attempts.

suggestion.title: VPN Session Establishment Failure Despite Valid Override Cookie
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'even though the appliance accepted the forged cookie, they were unable to establish a full VPN session'—flag the auth-accepted-but-session-failed indicator of exploitation
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequences where GlobalProtect accepts authentication via override cookie but subsequent VPN session establishment fails (handshake failure, config mismatch, protocol error). Multiple such failures from same source or targeting same user within minutes indicate cookie forgery attempts.

suggestion.title: Rapid7 MDR-Level Pattern: High Auth Override Success Rate, Low Session Completion
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Rapid7 MDR identified successful exploitation across numerous customers, however we did not observe any indication of successful lateral movement'—detect auth vs. session ratio anomalies that indicate exploitation attempts
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Build aggregate detection for GlobalProtect gateways showing unusually high ratio of successful authentication-override authentications relative to completed VPN sessions. Baseline per device and alert when override-cookie auth success rate exceeds VPN session establishment rate by threshold (e.g. 10:1).

suggestion.title: GlobalProtect Portal Unauthenticated Access Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Authentication Bypass' and 'Active Exploitation.' The vulnerability itself is the bypass—must detect exploitation patterns against the portal login interface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to GlobalProtect portal (/ssl-vpn/auth.html or similar) that return 200 status without preceding valid SAML/RADIUS authentication handshake. Flag requests from IPs with no prior VPN session history. Correlate CVE-2026-0257 exploitation payloads in User-Agent or request parameters.

suggestion.title: GlobalProtect Session Establishment from Unlikely Geolocation
suggestion.rationale: Bypass enables attackers to initiate VPN sessions. Article context ('Under Active Exploitation') implies bulk session attempts. Must detect laterally inconsistent VPN logins post-bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag GlobalProtect session establishment from geolocations not in user baseline (if known) or from datacenter/proxy IP ranges. Detect multiple session initiations from same source IP within short window. Alert if session from anomalous location established hours after normal user shutdown.

suggestion.title: Internal Reconnaissance from GlobalProtect VPN Session
suggestion.rationale: Post-bypass lateral movement is immediate concern. Attacker with VPN access will perform network discovery. Article severity HIGH indicates threat of data exfiltration or lateral spread.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor VPN-sourced traffic for port scanning (multiple connection attempts to different ports on single/multiple internal IPs). Detect DNS queries from VPN sessions to internal domain names not previously queried by that user. Flag SMB, RDP, or SSH connection attempts from newly-established VPN sessions to sensitive servers.

suggestion.title: PAN-OS GlobalProtect Vulnerability Exploit Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article describes specific vulnerability (CVE-2026-0257). Exploit chains for auth bypasses typically involve specific request structures or payload patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on requests matching known CVE-2026-0257 exploitation patterns (specific parameter tampering, path traversal, or request structure). Monitor for abnormal request sizes or encoding in GlobalProtect portal requests. Detect requests with null bytes or double-encoding targeting authentication endpoints.

suggestion.title: Botnet C&C Communication via Suspicious Protocol Tunneling
suggestion.rationale: Article title references botnet dismantling implying C&C infrastructure was operational and detectable. Phrase 'botnet linked to 17 million infected devices' establishes ongoing command-and-control traffic as core attack mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound connections to known C&C domains/IPs with characteristic beacon timing (regular intervals, entropy-low payloads). Flag parent processes spawning network connections typical of botnet agents (encoded/obfuscated cmdline, system-impersonating names).

suggestion.title: Mass Malware Propagation via Infected Device Network
suggestion.rationale: With 17 million infected devices, the article implies lateral propagation and continuous replication. 'Infected devices' phrase indicates widespread malware distribution mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process spawning or file writes indicative of self-propagating malware: multiple child processes from single parent, rapid file creation/modification in system paths, unsigned executables in temp directories, or network shares being scanned/infected.

suggestion.title: Sinkhole Traffic Post-Takedown Infrastructure Redirect
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'Dutch Authorities Dismantle' indicates law enforcement seizure/sinkhole redirect of C&C. Detectable when infected devices continue beacon attempts to now-redirected addresses.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for DNS queries or HTTP/HTTPS requests to known C&C domains that return sinkhole infrastructure IP addresses (CISA/law enforcement controlled). Correlate source IPs against known botnet victim ranges.

suggestion.title: Botnet Fallback Channel Activation Post-Primary C&C Disruption
suggestion.rationale: Sophisticated botnets maintain multiple command channels. After primary takedown, fallback mechanisms activate—detectable as secondary C&C contact patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for rapid DNS resolution failures to primary C&C domains followed by successful connections to secondary domains (encoded names, DGA variants, bulletproof hosting). Correlate with geographic/ASN diversity of resolvers.

suggestion.title: Malware Automatic Update / Command Execution Post-Takedown
suggestion.rationale: Botnets push updates or stand-alone payloads after infrastructure is threatened. Article title implies ongoing operational botnet—updates/commands were being distributed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious process executions following network beaconing: cmd.exe/powershell spawned from unsigned services, base64-encoded scripts, or WMI process creation. Correlate parent process with C&C beacon timing.

suggestion.title: Botnet Agent Configuration Exfiltration or Dead Drop Collection
suggestion.rationale: Botnets store C&C config in protected registry/files. 'Dismantled botnet' suggests investigators recovered configs/infrastructure. Behavioral detection: agents may attempt to refresh/backup configs pre-takedown.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for processes accessing HKLM\Software (malware configs), reading files from %AppData%\Local\Temp, or opening network sockets immediately after. Flag entropy-high registry values and base64-encoded file contents.

suggestion.title: WP Maps Pro Unauthenticated AJAX Admin Account Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'AJAX endpoint used for this feature was accessible to unauthenticated users' and describes attackers 'sending a specially crafted request that triggers code to create a new WordPress user'. Pipeline failed to generate the primary exploitation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to /wp-admin/admin-ajax.php from unauthenticated contexts with WP Maps Pro parameters and check_temp=false. Alert on requests triggering wp_insert_user() with administrator role. Correlate request timing with admin account creation events within 1 second.

suggestion.title: Rogue Admin Creation with Hardcoded Support Email
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies the vulnerability 'creates a new WordPress user via wp_insert_user() with the hardcoded role of administrator' and 'hardcoded email address support@flippercode.com'. This unique IOC and account creation pattern was completely missed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for WordPress user accounts with email support@flippercode.com or randomly-generated usernames paired with this email. Flag admin account creation events lacking corresponding registration emails or admin invitations. Correlate with WP Maps Pro AJAX logs.

suggestion.title: Passwordless Magic Login URL Generation and Use
suggestion.rationale: Article states the attack 'generates a "magic login URL" using generate_login_link()' allowing the 'attacker visits this URL, they are automatically authenticated to the newly created administrator account, with no password'. No detection for this authentication bypass mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect generate_login_link() function calls storing passwordless tokens in user_meta. Alert on successful admin authentication events with no prior password reset, password challenge, or MFA interaction. Flag login attempts using login-link parameters in URL.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-8732 Exploitation Attempt Signature
suggestion.rationale: Article documents active exploitation with '3,600 attempts over the past 24 hours' blocked by Wordfence. Pipeline provided no CVE-based detection signature despite clear, measurable attack volume.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Generate detection for CVE-2026-8732 pattern: requests to WP Maps Pro admin-ajax.php endpoints from external IPs with parameters triggering user creation. Baseline against legitimate plugin usage. Alert on exploitation attempts to WP Maps Pro ≤6.1.0 installations.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable WP Maps Pro Plugin Inventory Flag
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies affected versions are '6.1.0 and older' with patch released in 'WP Maps Pro 6.1.1 on May 20'. Pipeline should flag vulnerable installations as immediate remediation targets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan WordPress installations for WP Maps Pro presence and version. Alert on any installation with version ≤6.1.0. Escalate sites running vulnerable versions >14 days post-patch. Cross-reference with WAF/proxy logs for exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Admin Account Creation Following WP Maps Pro AJAX Trigger
suggestion.rationale: Article describes the attack sequence: AJAX request → 'code to create a new WordPress user' → 'assign it the administrator role' → 'generate a passwordless login URL'. Pipeline missed correlation detection across this sequence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate WP Maps Pro AJAX POST requests (admin-ajax.php from unauthenticated source) with WordPress user creation events (wp_insert_user) within 5 seconds. Flag admin accounts created immediately after suspicious AJAX activity to WP Maps Pro endpoints.

suggestion.title: LLM API Call Anomalies for Malware Generation
suggestion.rationale: Article states GREYVIBE 'leverage ChatGPT and Google Gemini to fuel cyberattacks'—suggesting the threat actor uses LLM APIs to generate malicious payloads, code, or social-engineering templates. No detection use case was produced despite this being the primary attack vector described.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process execution (PowerShell, cmd, Python) immediately following uncommon HTTP/HTTPS calls to OpenAI or Google API endpoints from non-developer accounts. Correlate with file creation of suspicious scripts or executables within 60 seconds of API calls.

suggestion.title: ChatGPT/Gemini API Credential Abuse
suggestion.rationale: If GREYVIBE uses ChatGPT/Gemini APIs, they must have obtained or compromised API keys or user accounts. Article does not describe credential acquisition, but pipeline should have surfaced monitoring for API key exfiltration or stolen account usage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect impossible-travel sign-ins to OpenAI/Google accounts (API key usage from multiple geolocations within minutes). Flag bulk API calls from free-tier accounts or anomalous token consumption spikes.

suggestion.title: Suspicious LLM Output Staging and Delivery
suggestion.rationale: GREYVIBE uses LLMs to 'fuel cyberattacks'—implying generated payloads/prompts are downloaded, staged, and deployed to victims. Pipeline lacks detection for exfiltration of LLM-generated content to external C2 or staging servers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for files created minutes after ChatGPT/Gemini API calls being renamed, compressed, or moved to staged exfiltration directories. Alert on encrypted uploads to unknown cloud storage or C2 domains.

suggestion.title: Phishing Content Generation via LLM
suggestion.rationale: GREYVIBE likely uses ChatGPT/Gemini to craft convincing phishing emails, payloads, or social-engineering scripts. Article does not detail phishing mechanics, but this is a known LLM abuse pattern absent from pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate inbound emails with unusual linguistic fingerprints (e.g., formal tone, repeated rare phrases, perfect grammar from traditionally-sloppy actor) to LLM API timestamps. Flag click-through of URLs in those emails within minutes of LLM API activity on attacker infrastructure.

suggestion.title: npm Package Installation from Public Registry Overriding Private Scope
suggestion.rationale: Article title centers on 'dependency confusion'—the core attack vector where public packages resolve ahead of private ones. Article phrase: 'abuse dependency confusion.' Detection gap: no UC for flagging unexpected public registry installations when private registry is configured.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm/yarn/pnpm pulling packages from registry.npmjs.org when corresponding @scoped packages exist in private registry configuration, or when installation occurs on developer workstation with non-empty .npmrc pointing to private registry.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Environment and File System Enumeration During Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes packages that 'profile developer environments'—implying active reconnaissance. Article phrase: 'collect reconnaissance data from developer and build environments.' Detection gap: no UC for detecting environment variable reads, .ssh/.aws enumeration, or credential file access within postinstall hooks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag npm postinstall scripts or spawned subprocesses that enumerate PATH, NODE_ENV, CI/CD variables (GITHUB_TOKEN, GITLAB_CI, JENKINS_HOME), or access credential directories (.ssh, .aws, .docker, .kube, .npmrc with tokens, .netrc).

suggestion.title: Unexpected Outbound Network Connections from npm Package Installation Process
suggestion.rationale: Profiling-focused attack implies exfiltration of gathered data. Article phrase: 'profile developer environments' suggests data collection and transmission. Detection gap: no UC for detecting C2 callbacks from postinstall execution contexts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound HTTPS/HTTP connections initiated by npm package installation processes (node, npm, sh, bash, powershell spawned from npm) to non-canonical registries or non-CDN destinations; particularly suspicious if connections occur 5-30 seconds post-extraction with small data payloads.

suggestion.title: npm Postinstall Hook Code Execution with Elevated or Unusual Privileges
suggestion.rationale: Dependency confusion attacks universally leverage postinstall/postuninstall hooks for code execution. No UC generated despite this being core tradecraft. Article phrase: 'malicious npm packages' implies active code execution during install.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm postinstall script execution that spawns PowerShell, bash, sh, or curl/wget; accesses /etc/passwd or HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE registry; or runs with sudo/elevated token when npm install was invoked without elevation.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Configuration or Registry URL Modification
suggestion.rationale: Dependency confusion or MITM attacks require registry redirection. No UC for detecting .npmrc tampering or npm config CLI changes. Article phrase: 'malicious npm packages' could involve registry substitution attack variant.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file modifications to ~/.npmrc, /etc/npmrc, or project .npmrc files within 24 hours before unexpected package installations; npm config commands that alter registry= URLs; or DNS A/AAAA record changes for known npm registries.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Child Process Execution Spawned from npm Package Manager
suggestion.rationale: Package postinstall scripts execute arbitrary code; reconnaissance implies spawning discovery tools. No UC for detecting cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, or curl spawned directly from npm context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag when npm package manager (npm.exe, node.exe, yarn, pnpm) spawns cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, or curl without user interactive context; detect parent-child relationships showing node.exe → powershell.exe → whoami/systeminfo/net commands.

suggestion.title: Forged Authentication Override Cookie Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes core exploit mechanism: 'attackers can obtain the corresponding public key via the HTTPS session and then use it to create forged cookies that the device will accept as legitimate.' Pipeline failed to generate detection for this technical attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GlobalProtect authentication override cookie validation failures or successful admin authentications absent corresponding credential submissions. Alert on authentication events for local administrator accounts from external/non-corporate IP ranges, particularly known attacker infrastructure (Vultr AS20473, Dromatics Systems).

suggestion.title: Unauthorized GlobalProtect VPN Connections
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'attackers were able to connect to the device via VPN using forged cookies, granting them access to internal networks.' No VPN anomaly detection use case was generated despite this being explicit attack outcome.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful GlobalProtect VPN session establishment from external IPs without documented valid authentication event or MFA completion. Correlate with IP reputation databases to identify Vultr (first wave, May 18) and Dromatics Systems (second wave, May 21) infrastructure ASN ranges.

suggestion.title: Public Key Certificate Extraction from GlobalProtect Portal
suggestion.rationale: Article details exploit prerequisite: attackers 'can retrieve the public certificates exposed by a GlobalProtect portal or gateway.' No reconnaissance detection generated for this preliminary attack step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for repeated certificate-endpoint requests to GlobalProtect portals from external sources. Alert when certificate retrieval attempts precede authentication attempts from the same source IP within minutes, indicating preparation for cookie forgery.

suggestion.title: Privileged Account Authentication Bypass via Forged Cookies
suggestion.rationale: Rapid7 investigation explicitly noted: 'attackers authenticating to GlobalProtect gateways using forged authentication override cookies that targeted the local administrator account.' No detection generated for privileged-account targeting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful local administrator account authentications from external/non-standard locations without MFA evidence. Flag any such authentication immediately preceding or concurrent with GlobalProtect VPN session establishment events.

suggestion.title: Exploitable Configuration: Shared Certificates for HTTPS and Auth Override
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability root cause: 'If the same certificate is reused for both HTTPS services and authentication override cookies, attackers can obtain the corresponding public key via the HTTPS session.' No configuration-vulnerability detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit PAN-OS configurations for overlapping certificate usage (HTTPS service certificate == auth override cookie signing certificate). Flag misconfigurations and implement elevated monitoring on those devices for external authentication attempts and traffic from Vultr/Dromatics Systems infrastructure ranges.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Post-VPN Bypass Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates successful compromises led to 'access to internal networks' following VPN connection establishment. Pipeline generated no detection for post-compromise lateral movement despite clear attack progression.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate GlobalProtect unauthorized VPN session timestamps with subsequent RDP/SSH connection attempts to internal systems. Alert on enumeration or scanning activity originating from VPN-connected endpoints shortly after compromise.

suggestion.title: GlobalProtect Authentication Bypass Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly flags 'CVE-2026-0257...Under Active Exploitation.' Pipeline must detect attempts to exploit the bypass—malicious actors sending crafted requests to bypass authentication mechanisms. Cite: '[HIGH]...Under Active Exploitation.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GlobalProtect gateways for HTTP/HTTPS POST requests to `/ssl-vpn/auth.cgi` or similar authentication endpoints with missing or malformed session tokens, absence of expected TLS certificate validation, or responses indicating authentication success without credential submission. Correlate with vulnerable PAN-OS versions (see IOC recommendations).

suggestion.title: Successful GlobalProtect Authentication Without Credential Submission
suggestion.rationale: Authentication bypass vulnerability implies adversaries can establish valid sessions without proper credentials. Detection must identify legitimate-appearing GlobalProtect sessions initiated without credential exchange logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag GlobalProtect gateway logs showing session establishment (auth success events) without corresponding credential validation events in the authentication pipeline. Baseline against normal VPN onboarding patterns to reduce false positives.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from GlobalProtect-Compromised Sessions
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation scenario: once attacker bypasses GlobalProtect authentication, they gain network access and can pivot. Article describes active exploitation but pipeline omits detection for command execution or lateral movement following successful bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual outbound network connections (RDP, SSH, WinRM) originating from VPN-assigned IP ranges shortly after GlobalProtect session establishment, or process execution (cmd.exe, PowerShell) from VPN session context.

suggestion.title: PAN-OS Vulnerable Version Inventory - CVE-2026-0257
suggestion.rationale: High-severity active-exploitation vulnerability requires immediate inventory of affected PAN-OS versions. Pipeline extracted no version information despite article likely specifying vulnerable release range.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory and PAN-OS management logs for instances running vulnerable versions of PAN-OS GlobalProtect. Generate incident list for patching priority. Use PAN-OS 'show system info' or Panorama inventory APIs.

suggestion.title: Botnet C2 Domain Beaconing Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly references 'botnet'—these require C2 communication. Pipeline should have extracted known C2 domains or IP ranges from the dismantling details and generated detection for outbound DNS/HTTP to those infrastructure assets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DNS queries or HTTP/HTTPS traffic to known botnet C2 domains identified in law-enforcement takedown. Alert on periodic beaconing patterns or long-duration connections from devices attempting to reach dead infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Malware Persistence Registry/Task Scheduler Modifications
suggestion.rationale: Botnet infection of '17 million devices' requires persistence across reboots. Common mechanisms (Run keys, scheduled tasks, WMI subscriptions) should have been surfaced from botnet family description if article contained technical details.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag creation or modification of HKLM/HKCU Run/RunOnce registry keys, creation of scheduled tasks with suspicious command lines, or WMI permanent event subscriptions matching known botnet persistence indicators.

suggestion.title: Botnet Malware Process Execution and Injection
suggestion.rationale: No attack techniques mapped despite botnet inherently involving code execution. Botnets typically inject into legitimate processes or spawn suspicious child processes—these execution patterns should have been identified.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious process injection into svchost, explorer, or other high-privilege processes, or execution of unsigned/low-reputation binaries followed by outbound network initiation.

suggestion.title: Suspicious WordPress Admin Account Creation via Plugin Exploit
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'function creates a new WordPress user via wp_insert_user() with the hardcoded role of administrator, a randomly generated username, and the hardcoded email address support@flippercode.com'—direct IOC and behavioral signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on wp_insert_user() calls creating administrator-role accounts with randomly-generated usernames. Flag accounts created with email support@flippercode.com immediately. Correlate with authentication logs showing first login from that account within seconds of creation, no password reset history.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to WP Maps Pro AJAX Endpoint with check_temp Parameter
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies the vulnerability: 'AJAX endpoint used for this feature was accessible to unauthenticated users' with parameter check_temp=false triggering the exploit code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST requests to wp-admin/admin-ajax.php containing WP Maps Pro parameters (action=wp_maps_pro_*) with check_temp=false from unauthenticated sessions. Baseline legitimate traffic; flag spike patterns matching the 3,600 blocked-attempt profile cited in article.

suggestion.title: Public Nonce Exposure in Plugin Frontend JavaScript
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'relied solely on a publicly exposed nonce check in frontend JavaScript, rendering the protection ineffective'—client-side credential validation failure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan WP Maps Pro plugin JavaScript files for hardcoded nonce values or wp_nonce_field() outputs visible in page source. Monitor requests to plugin AJAX endpoints using expired/replayed nonces or omitting nonce entirely. Cross-correlate with known plugin version ≤6.1.0 fingerprints.

suggestion.title: Magic Login URL Generation and Passwordless Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The function then generates a "magic login URL" using generate_login_link()...Once the attacker visits this URL, they are automatically authenticated to the newly created administrator account, with no password or any other verification required.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt WordPress usermeta for login_link entries. Correlate with successful password-reset-free logins (no wp_password change event prior). Alert on magic URLs used from IP addresses without prior site access. Cross-reference login timestamps against admin account creation timestamps.

suggestion.title: Persistent Backdoor/Plugin Installation by Exploit-Created Admin Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Having admin-level access on the site means attackers can inject persistent backdoors...install malicious plugins'—post-exploitation persistence mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor wp-content/plugins/ for plugin installation within 5 minutes of admin account creation with randomized username or support@flippercode.com email. Flag plugin .php files created or modified by newly-promoted admin accounts. Cross-check plugin hashes against known backdoor signatures (e.g., eval, base64_decode, create_function).

suggestion.title: Hardcoded Support Email IOC Tracking Across WordPress Site
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies 'the hardcoded email address support@flippercode.com' as the email assigned to all exploit-created admin accounts—a direct, repeatable IOC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query WordPress wp_users table for accounts with email=support@flippercode.com. Alert on any login activity from this account. Monitor SMTP logs for password-reset emails sent to this address. Flag account metadata containing login_link entries. Correlate with exploitation timeline (May 31, 2026 onwards).

suggestion.title: AI-Assisted Phishing Prompt Injection Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states GREYVIBE 'leverage[s] ChatGPT and Google Gemini to fuel cyberattacks'—implies crafting malicious payloads or social engineering templates via LLM. No use case captured this attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious API calls to ChatGPT or Gemini APIs from non-standard user agents or high-velocity requests. Correlate with subsequent spear-phishing campaigns or malware delivery. Flag prompts requesting code obfuscation, evasion techniques, or social-engineering copy.

suggestion.title: Anomalous LLM API Token Usage
suggestion.rationale: GREYVIBE's use of ChatGPT and Google Gemini implies API authentication and potentially API-key abuse or token compromise. Pipeline missed cloud-API instrumentation angle.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk ChatGPT/Gemini API calls from service accounts or non-standard origins. Detect unusual query patterns (e.g., requests for malware source, exploit code, credential formats). Cross-reference with suspicious browser automation or headless-client user agents.

suggestion.title: Threat-Actor Infrastructure: GREYVIBE Attribution Pivot
suggestion.rationale: Article headline names GREYVIBE as active threat group; pipeline extracted zero actor intelligence. Attribution data (C2 domains, email patterns, campaign timestamps) should be indexed for correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Build lookup table of GREYVIBE indicators: known sender domains, phishing landing pages, C2 infrastructure. Alert on email campaigns matching historical group patterns or using identical LLM-generated social engineering templates.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Install with Environment Profiling
suggestion.rationale: Article states campaign 'collect[ed] reconnaissance data from developer and build environments'—need detection for npm install/execution that immediately queries system properties (OS, architecture, installed tools).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag npm package execution that spawns child processes querying system info (uname, systeminfo, node --version) immediately post-install, or outbound connections to exfiltration domains within seconds of npm install completion.

suggestion.title: Dependency Confusion Attack Detection via Package Resolution
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector: 'dependency confusion to profile developer environments'—need detection at package manager level when private package resolved from public registry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install activity where a package name matches naming patterns of internal/private packages (e.g., @company-scope) is resolved from public npm registry instead of private feed. Flag if versions are higher than internal versions or from unexpected maintainers.

suggestion.title: npm Package Post-Install Script Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Article implies automated reconnaissance in malicious packages—standard npm attack vector. Need detection for post-install scripts executing system enumeration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm package installation where postinstall/preinstall hooks spawn commands like whoami, id, env, ls -la $HOME/.ssh, git config, docker ps, or kubectl queries in developer environment contexts.

suggestion.title: Build Environment Credential Exposure via Package Code
suggestion.rationale: Article targets 'build environments'—attackers exfiltrate CI/CD credentials, tokens, and SSH keys. Need detection for packages reading sensitive paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag npm package processes reading or accessing paths like ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.git-credentials, /etc/ssh, environment variables containing TOKEN/KEY/SECRET, or .env files during installation phase.

suggestion.title: Malicious npm Package Egress to Command Server
suggestion.rationale: Profiling data must be exfiltrated—article describes 'profile developer environments' implying data collection and transmission. Need network-based detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for npm package process (node.js) making outbound connections to low-reputation or newly-registered domains immediately after install, especially if transmitting structured data (JSON-encoded system info, encoded credential material).

suggestion.title: GlobalProtect Gateway: Forged Authentication Cookie Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'attackers authenticating to GlobalProtect gateways using forged authentication override cookies that targeted the local administrator account' and explains attackers extract public keys from HTTPS to forge valid-looking cookies. This is the core attack vector and should trigger on cookie signature validation failures or timing anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GlobalProtect gateway authentication logs for successful logins to local admin account from non-standard authentication paths, or for decryption failures on authentication override cookies. Baseline legitimate cookie rotation and alert on outliers, especially from IP ranges associated with Vultr or Dromatics Systems hosting.

suggestion.title: GlobalProtect VPN: Multiple Failed Session Establishment
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'even though the appliance accepted the forged cookie, they were unable to establish a full VPN session' in many cases. Failed VPN sessions following successful authentication are indicative of exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sequences where GlobalProtect gateway accepts authentication override cookies (successful auth) but subsequent VPN session establishment fails within 30 seconds. Correlate multiple failures from same source IP or cookie issuer across a time window.

suggestion.title: GlobalProtect: Certificate Reuse Between HTTPS and Auth Override
suggestion.rationale: Article explains vulnerability root cause: 'If the same certificate is reused for both HTTPS services and authentication override cookies, attackers can obtain the corresponding public key via the HTTPS session and then use it to create forged cookies.' This requires config audit rather than log detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory GlobalProtect gateway certificates used for HTTPS termination and authentication override cookies. Flag any device where the same certificate thumbprint appears in both roles. Compare against baseline of devices using segregated certificates per Palo Alto hardening guidance.

suggestion.title: VPN Access from Vultr/Dromatics Systems IP Space During May 17-29 Window
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'attacks began with' infrastructure from 'Vultr' (May 18 onwards) and 'Dromatics Systems' (May 21 onwards). This is a direct IOC source tied to active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Block or alert on all VPN connection attempts (successful or failed) from Vultr IP ranges and Dromatics Systems IP ranges between 2026-05-17 and 2026-05-31. Prioritize any that reached local admin account or internal network segments.

suggestion.title: GlobalProtect Authentication Override Feature: Disabled Baseline Enforcement
suggestion.rationale: Article advises mitigation via 'turning off the authentication override feature' and notes exploitation only works 'if devices configured with authentication override cookies enabled.' Devices still running this feature should be flagged.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query all GlobalProtect gateway configurations for the `override-cookie-authentication` setting. Alert on any device where this is enabled after 2026-05-30 (post-public-disclosure). Cross-reference against CISA deadline of 2026-06-01 for federal asset compliance.

suggestion.title: Rapid7 MDR Observation: Successful Lateral Movement Post-VPN Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states Rapid7 'did not observe any indication of successful lateral movement from the devices,' but this is a critical negative indicator. If lateral movement detection is absent, attacks may pivot undetected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For any host that accepted a forged GlobalProtect authentication cookie and established a VPN session, monitor for lateral movement indicators (SMB, RDP, Kerberos traffic to other internal assets, process execution from unfamiliar network paths). The lack of observed lateral movement in Rapid7's data suggests either rapid patching or insufficient monitoring depth.

suggestion.title: PAN-OS GlobalProtect Authentication Bypass Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Authentication Bypass' in CVE-2026-0257. Pipeline failed to generate any detection logic despite this being the headline attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GlobalProtect gateway logs for abnormal authentication sequences, failed-then-successful login patterns, or HTTP 401→200 transitions without valid credential submission. Correlate with known CVE-2026-0257 exploitation signatures (URI patterns, header anomalies).

suggestion.title: Unauthorized PAN-OS Admin Access Post-Authentication Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation of authentication bypass typically leads to privilege escalation or lateral admin access. No lateral movement/privilege escalation detection use cases generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on administrative API calls or config changes originating from IPs that previously failed GlobalProtect authentication. Track XML-API or WebUI access tokens issued without corresponding successful SAML/LDAP validation.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Traffic to PAN-OS GlobalProtect Portal
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Under Active Exploitation'—should detect active exploitation attempts, not just post-breach behavior. No inbound exploit traffic use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP POST/GET requests to /ssl-vpn/* or GlobalProtect authentication endpoints with payloads matching known CVE-2026-0257 exploitation patterns (oversized headers, XML injection, XXE vectors).

suggestion.title: Botnet C2 Traffic Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title directly references botnet dismantlement; command-and-control communication is the core attack pattern. Pipeline generated zero C2 detection cases despite this being foundational to botnet operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify outbound connections to known botnet C2 servers, anomalous port usage, DNS requests to newly-registered or malicious domains, and encrypted tunneling traffic characteristic of botnet command channels.

suggestion.title: Malware Persistence via Registry and Scheduled Tasks
suggestion.rationale: Scale of 17 million infected devices implies persistent establishment across diverse endpoints. No persistence-phase detections generated despite this being mandatory for sustained botnet control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor suspicious modifications to HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\Run, registry startup folders, scheduled task creation tied to unsigned binaries, and task scheduler execution of suspicious scripts.

suggestion.title: Process Injection and Code Execution Obfuscation
suggestion.rationale: Large-scale botnet delivery requires evasion techniques to bypass endpoint detection. No execution-phase defense-evasion cases generated despite injection being standard in modern malware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process hollowing via CreateRemoteThread patterns, mismatched parent-child process trees (svchost spawning cmd.exe), unusual memory allocation/write sequences, and code execution from non-standard paths.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Network Enumeration and Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Botnet scale to 17M devices implies worm-like propagation via network enumeration and exploitation of vulnerable systems. No lateral-movement detections suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag execution of ipconfig, arp, net view, nmap, or similar enumeration tools from suspicious parent processes; detect scanning patterns across internal subnets; identify exploitation attempts against SMB, RDP, or HTTP services.

suggestion.title: Initial Access via Phishing or Public-Facing Service Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: 17M device compromise requires documented initial-access vector (phishing, exploit, brute force). Article title does not specify mechanism; pipeline generated zero initial-access use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect mass phishing campaigns with macro-enabled attachments, exploitation of known vulnerabilities in public-facing services (RDP, SMB), unusual authentication spikes, or exploitation payloads in HTTP logs.

suggestion.title: DNS-Based Botnet Domain Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Botnet C2 coordination typically uses DNS for command delivery or domain fluxing. Article references botnet but pipeline extracted zero IOCs including no C2 domains or DNS patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify DNS requests to newly registered domains, domains with poor reputation, domains exhibiting DGA characteristics, or domains previously associated with known botnet infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated AJAX Endpoint Exploitation (WP Maps Pro CVE-2026-8732)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'AJAX endpoint used for this feature was accessible to unauthenticated users' and describes the check_temp=false parameter as the attack vector. No detection UC was generated despite this being the initial exploitation step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to WP Maps Pro AJAX endpoints (e.g., wp-admin/admin-ajax.php) with check_temp=false parameter from unauthenticated or external sources. Alert if requests originate from non-admin IPs or lack valid WordPress session cookies. Correlate with Wordfence/threat-intel feeds for CVE-2026-8732 exploitation patterns.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Admin User Creation Without Admin Panel Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states the exploit 'creates a new WordPress user via wp_insert_user() with the hardcoded role of administrator' via AJAX, not through normal admin UI. No UC was generated for detecting privilege escalation via programmatic account creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when WordPress user accounts with admin role are created from non-admin HTTP requests (AJAX, REST API) or lack corresponding entries in wp-admin UI logs. Baseline legitimate admin creation patterns and flag deviations. Correlate timing of user creation with web access anomalies.

suggestion.title: Known-Malicious Email Address in User Creation (support@flippercode.com)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names the hardcoded email 'support@flippercode.com' inserted into every exploited site's admin account. This is a precise IOC for detecting successful exploitation, yet was not extracted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert immediately on any user account creation with email address support@flippercode.com in WordPress user tables. This email is hardcoded and unique to exploitation; any occurrence indicates successful CVE-2026-8732 compromise. Check for multiple instances across customer environment.

suggestion.title: Passwordless Magic Login URL Generation and Usage
