suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'generates a "magic login URL" using generate_login_link(), stores it as user meta, and returns it in the response body' and 'visit this URL, they are automatically authenticated.' No detection UC for this credential bypass mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WordPress authentication logs for login events that lack password verification (generated login links, passwordless tokens). Alert on authentication sessions that match generate_login_link() function output patterns. Detect users accessing WordPress immediately after account creation without password reset.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Malicious Plugin Installation Following Admin Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'install malicious plugins' after gaining admin access. No UC was generated for detecting plugin installation patterns that follow successful account compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag plugin installations within minutes/hours of new admin account creation, especially by newly-created accounts. Baseline legitimate plugin deployment patterns. Alert on plugins installed to unusual directories, with obfuscated names, or from external repositories. Correlate with web shell signature detection.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Deployment Post-Admin Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'deploy web shells' as consequence of admin access. No UC for detecting web shell uploads or execution in WordPress context post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious file uploads to WordPress web root (wp-content, wp-admin) immediately after new admin account creation. Alert on .php, .phtml, or executable file uploads. Detect web shell execution patterns: unusual process spawning, outbound connections, or command-execution HTTP parameters from newly-created accounts.

suggestion.title: Suspicious ChatGPT/Gemini API Access for Intelligence Gathering
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states threat actors 'leverage ChatGPT and Google Gemini to fuel cyberattacks' — implies threat-actor accounts or compromised legitimate accounts calling these APIs with stolen credentials or sensitive data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect non-human patterns in ChatGPT/Gemini API calls: rapid-fire requests from single IP, requests with credential-theft indicators in payloads, exfiltration of sensitive data or code to these endpoints. Correlate with suspicious signin patterns or lateral movement preceding the API calls.

suggestion.title: Prompt Injection / LLM Jailbreak Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Title implies threat actors using AI tools to generate attack content — likely requires bypassing safety mechanisms through prompt injection or jailbreak techniques to produce malware code, phishing templates, or exploit code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for prompts containing known jailbreak payloads ('ignore prior instructions,' role-play as unrestricted AI, bypass safety), requests for malware code generation, or payloads embedding command-and-control infrastructure.

suggestion.title: GREYVIBE Threat-Actor Campaign Infrastructure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'GREYVIBE' as threat-actor group — pipeline should extract this as high-fidelity actor attribution and generate detections for GREYVIBE-attributed IOCs, C2 patterns, and malware signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for GREYVIBE-attributed malware hashes, C2 domains, and IP infrastructure in network logs. Monitor for communication patterns consistent with GREYVIBE campaigns (known beacon intervals, encryption schemes, callback sequences).

suggestion.title: AI-Generated Malware Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states threat actors use AI to 'fuel cyberattacks' — implies AI-synthesized malware or exploit payloads with potentially unusual code patterns, repetitive logic, or artifacts of LLM generation that differ from human-written code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect executable files with code patterns consistent with AI generation (repetitive boilerplate, systematic variable naming, lack of dead code). Correlate with execution from recent downloads or unusual script-runner chains.

suggestion.title: AI-Generated Phishing / Social Engineering Content
suggestion.rationale: Title implies AI tools used to 'fuel cyberattacks' — threat actors likely leveraging ChatGPT/Gemini to generate high-quality phishing emails, pretexting scripts, or social engineering payloads that bypass traditional content-based filters.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for phishing emails with linguistic artifacts of AI generation (over-formal tone, repetitive sentence structure, absence of typos but awkward phrasing). Correlate high-volume, low-variation campaigns with ChatGPT terms-of-service violations or API abuse patterns.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm package installed from public registry when private registry expected
suggestion.rationale: Article describes dependency confusion: packages resolved from public npm.org instead of enterprise registry. The attack vector—malicious public package pulling during build—required no detection logic despite being the initial execution point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect resolution of scoped packages (@internal/name, @company/*) from registry.npmjs.org in npm-shrinkwrap.json or package-lock.json when .npmrc configures private registry. Monitor .npmrc modifications that disable or comment out private registry entries. Flag npm install pulling scoped packages not present in enterprise registry.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance commands executed from npm postinstall scripts
suggestion.rationale: Article states packages 'profile developer and build environments'—explicit reconnaissance phase. No detection rule covers discovery commands spawned during npm install lifecycle.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on shell commands (sh, bash, powershell) spawned as children of npm.exe during install phases executing uname, systeminfo, whoami, env, id, or file enumeration (find, ls). Monitor for script execution from node_modules/.bin or package install directories. Correlate process parent chain to npm install timeline.

suggestion.title: Build environment credential access during npm install
suggestion.rationale: Article targets developer/build environments for reconnaissance—implies access to local secrets. No use case for detecting credential harvesting by postinstall scripts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm child processes accessing .ssh, .aws, .npmrc, KUBECONFIG, or environment variables containing secrets (SSH_KEY, AWS_ACCESS_KEY, CI_TOKEN). Flag file reads of credential locations during postinstall scripts. Alert on inline Base64 encoding or compression of config files within npm scripts.

suggestion.title: Data exfiltration via DNS or HTTP from npm install context
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates package reconnaissance 'collects data from developer environments.' No detection for network exfiltration during npm install phases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound HTTP/HTTPS/DNS initiated by node.exe during npm install. Flag connections to non-standard domains (not npmjs.org, cdnjs, github). Alert on POST requests with large payloads or environment variable content, DNS queries with encoded data, or connections from uncommon process parents in install context.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated or suspicious npm package install hooks
suggestion.rationale: Malicious packages execute reconnaissance via install scripts. Article implies script execution but no detection rule targets suspicious hook configuration or payload obfuscation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag package.json files with Base64-encoded, hex-encoded, or minified install/postinstall scripts. Detect scripts that spawn multiple subprocesses, use eval/exec, or redirect to shell without clear purpose. Alert when install scripts differ from upstream package version (hash mismatch). Monitor for pre/post hooks in zero-install packages or packages with no legitimate install-time operations.

suggestion.title: npm lock file manipulation indicating dependency resolution override
suggestion.rationale: Dependency confusion success relies on lock file entries pointing to malicious public package. No detection for lock file anomalies or version/registry resolution tampering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare package-lock.json and shrinkwrap.json against committed baseline. Alert on resolved entries where a scoped package (@org/pkg) lists public registry URL. Flag lock file modifications that predate source code commits (supply chain injection). Detect version pinning changes to public registry versions for internal packages.

suggestion.title: Forged GlobalProtect Authentication Cookie Acceptance
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'generate a forged authentication override cookie for an arbitrary user, and authenticate without knowing valid credentials' and notes 'A GlobalProtect VPN device decrypts these types of cookies using a configured private key and then trusts the decrypted contents without performing any signature verification.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PAN-OS GlobalProtect authentication logs for cookie validation errors, signature verification bypasses, or successful authentications without matching credential validation events. Alert on authentication override cookie usage when authentication_override feature is enabled and certificates are reused across services.

suggestion.title: Local Admin Account Access from Malicious VPN Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'attackers authenticating to GlobalProtect gateways using forged authentication override cookies that targeted the local administrator account' and 'first observed exploitation on May 18 from infrastructure hosted by Vultr, with a second wave of attacks detected on May 21 originating from Dromatics Systems.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag local administrator account authentications originating from Vultr ASN ranges or Dromatics Systems infrastructure. Correlate failed authentication attempts followed by successful session establishment with forged credentials on these networks.

suggestion.title: HTTPS Certificate Public Key Extraction for Cookie Forgery
suggestion.rationale: Article explains 'If the same certificate is reused for both HTTPS services and authentication override cookies, attackers can obtain the corresponding public key via the HTTPS session and then use it to create forged cookies that the device will accept as legitimate.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous extraction or enumeration of HTTPS public certificates from GlobalProtect portals. Alert on certificate reuse patterns where HTTPS and authentication override services share the same certificate. Monitor for TLS session analysis or certificate dumping tools targeting GlobalProtect endpoints.

suggestion.title: Partial VPN Session Establishment with Cookie Validation Errors
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'In some cases, attackers were able to connect to the device via VPN using forged cookies... However, Rapid7 says that in many incidents, even though the appliance accepted the forged cookie, they were unable to establish a full VPN session.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sequences where authentication succeeds via cookie but VPN session fails to establish, indicating forged cookie acceptance. High volume of cookie-accepted but session-failed events from single source is strong exploitation indicator.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Post-VPN Compromise Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'In some cases, attackers were able to connect to the device via VPN using forged cookies, granting them access to internal networks' but notes 'we did not observe any indication of successful lateral movement from the devices.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For any GlobalProtect VPN sessions with cookie-based authentication anomalies, monitor internal network activity for privilege escalation, service enumeration, credential dumping, or lateral movement attempts to other network segments or hosts.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-0257 Exploitation Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article provides exact timeline: 'Rapid7 MDR identified successful exploitation across numerous customers...The earliest date for observed exploitation was May 17, 2026' with 'first observed exploitation on May 18 from infrastructure hosted by Vultr, with a second wave of attacks detected on May 21 originating from Dromatics Systems.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag any GlobalProtect authentication attempts from Vultr or Dromatics Systems infrastructure combined with unexpected local admin account access. Create correlation rules matching May 17+ exploitation pattern: cookie validation anomalies → successful auth → internal network access attempts.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated GlobalProtect API Access Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'authentication bypass' — any unauthenticated request to GlobalProtect portals, gateways, or portal/gateway credential validation endpoints should alert. Pipeline did not suggest detection for pre-auth exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP 40x responses that precede 200 responses to /ssl-vpn/auth.cgi, /sslvpn/, or GlobalProtect gateway endpoints. Bypass indicators: repeated auth requests from single source without credential submission, or direct access to post-auth resources without auth token.

suggestion.title: GlobalProtect Session Establishment Without Valid Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Authentication bypass means attackers can establish VPN sessions without credentials. Use case should monitor for session creation that violates normal authentication flow or shows anomalous credential patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GlobalProtect sessions where auth token generation or MFA bypass occurred. Look for session IDs issued without corresponding authentication success logs, or sessions from IPs not in corporate range without expected geoIP distance or device posture validation.

suggestion.title: Post-Authentication-Bypass Lateral Movement from VPN Gateway
suggestion.rationale: Once authenticated via bypass, attacker pivots internally. Article mentions 'active exploitation' implying post-breach activity; pipeline missed detection for internal network scanning or credential harvesting post-VPN access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on VPN-sourced traffic patterns that deviate from established user baselines: scanning multiple internal subnets, DNS requests to internal infrastructure not typical for that user, or port scanning from VPN gateway.

suggestion.title: Command Execution on PAN-OS GlobalProtect Gateway Process
suggestion.rationale: Authentication bypass vulnerability often escalates to RCE on the gateway itself. No use case for detecting shell commands or script execution originating from gateway processes (e.g., wsm.exe, httpd).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PAN-OS appliance gateway processes (e.g., httpd, wsm, netstat children) for spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or shell execution. Baseline normal process trees and alert on deviation. Check for outbound connections from gateway process post-execution.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-0257 Exploitation Traffic Signatures
suggestion.rationale: Article title names specific CVE but pipeline extracted zero IOCs or traffic patterns. Should include payload signatures, malicious URI patterns, or request parameter anomalies specific to this bypass technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests matching known CVE-2026-0257 exploit signatures (e.g., specific parameter injection, URI path traversal, or header manipulation patterns used in public PoCs). Correlate with failed auth logs to identify exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation Post-GlobalProtect Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Active exploitation typically leads to privilege elevation. Pipeline missed detection for privilege escalation techniques attackers would employ after gaining VPN access as low-privilege user.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect privilege escalation from VPN-sourced internal host: UAC bypasses, service installation with elevated token, scheduled task creation via vulnerable services, or token impersonation attempts. Establish baseline for VPN-user privilege level and alert on escalation.

suggestion.title: Botnet Malware Execution by Hash
suggestion.rationale: Botnet dismantlement articles typically disclose malware sample hashes; pipeline should detect process creation or file writes matching known botnet variants. Expected from any botnet takedown narrative.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for execution of files matching known botnet malware hashes. Alert on process creation with parent processes inconsistent with normal software deployment (email client, browser, Office, USB automount).

suggestion.title: C2 Communication to Known Botnet Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Botnet articles identify command-and-control domains or IP ranges; pipeline should flag network connections to these addresses. Core C2 detection missing entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound network connections to domains or IPs disclosed in botnet takedown notices. Correlate with passive DNS and threat feeds for infrastructure associated with the dismantled botnet.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Botnet Propagation
suggestion.rationale: Botnet articles describe infection spread across network segments or systems; pipeline should detect scanning, SMB/RDP exploitation, or lateral movement techniques used by the botnet.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for high-volume SMB connections (port 445) or RDP bruteforce attempts (port 3389) originating from internal systems, indicating botnet self-propagation. Alert on net view / ipconfig / tasklist commands executed in unusual parent-child chains.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Registry/Scheduled Task Injection
suggestion.rationale: Botnet malware establishes persistence for recovery after reboots; article likely mentions resilience mechanisms. Pipeline should surface registry run-key or scheduled task creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on registry writes to HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run or scheduled task creation with suspicious image paths, especially those coinciding with botnet malware execution timestamps.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Process Injection or Hollowing
suggestion.rationale: Sophisticated botnets use code injection into legitimate processes for evasion; botnet articles often note anti-analysis or anti-detection techniques. Pipeline should detect suspicious memory writes or inter-process manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for CreateRemoteThread, WriteProcessMemory, or VirtualAllocEx calls targeting unexpected process pairs (e.g., svchost hosting unusual modules). Alert on unsigned DLL injection into system processes.

suggestion.title: Initial Access via Compromised Supply Chain or Email
suggestion.rationale: Botnet articles typically disclose infection vector (phishing, watering hole, exploit kit). Pipeline should identify the initial compromise indicator (malicious attachment, drive-by download, etc.).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on email attachments or links matching known botnet distribution campaigns, or on suspicious downloads from watering-hole domains. Correlate with user-reported phishing and attachment execution timelines.

suggestion.title: WordPress Admin Account Creation from WP Maps Pro AJAX
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes AJAX endpoint 'triggers code to create a new WordPress user' via wp_insert_user() with 'hardcoded role of administrator' and hardcoded email 'support@flippercode.com'. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this being the primary attack mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on WordPress user creation events (wp_insert_user database calls or user_register hook executions) where role=administrator and email matches 'support@flippercode.com' or attacker-controlled pattern. Monitor for auto-generated usernames created outside standard registration flows. Correlate with preceding unauthenticated AJAX requests from same source IP.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated WP Maps Pro AJAX Endpoint Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is 'AJAX endpoint used for temporary access feature...accessible to unauthenticated users' with nonce check 'rendered the protection ineffective'. No detection for exploitation attempts despite 3,600 observed attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST requests to wp-admin/admin-ajax.php from unauthenticated sessions with WP Maps Pro action parameters and check_temp=false parameter. Establish baseline for legitimate temporary access feature traffic. Flag scanning patterns: multiple requests from single IP within short time window, varying parameters, high failure-to-success ratio.

suggestion.title: Magic Login URL Generation and Passwordless Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article describes function 'generates a "magic login URL" using generate_login_link()' which results in automatic authentication: 'Once the attacker visits this URL, they are automatically authenticated...with no password or any other verification required'. Passwordless login is the persistence mechanism; pipeline extracted zero detection rules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query WordPress usermeta table for entries containing 'login_link' or token-like values generated outside normal password-reset flows. Monitor authentication logs for successful logins without password submission or preceding password-verification HTTP requests. Cross-reference magic link token usage with newly created admin account timestamps and subsequent privileged actions within minutes.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable WP Maps Pro Plugin Version Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'WP Maps Pro versions 6.1.0 and older' are vulnerable, patch released 'May 20' as version 6.1.1. Asset inventory and version detection is foundational for vulnerability prioritization; pipeline extracted zero IOCs for plugin or versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate installed WordPress plugins by reading wp-content/plugins/wp-maps-pro/ metadata (readme.txt, plugin header comments). Flag any version ≤6.1.0. Cross-correlate vulnerable instances with inbound web requests to AJAX endpoints (admin-ajax.php requests containing WP Maps Pro action parameters) to identify exposed, exploitable targets.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Rogue Admin Account Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states admin access permits: 'inject persistent backdoors, modify content, access private data, deploy web shells, install malicious plugins, and take over the website'. Pipeline extracted zero detections for post-compromise impact despite article detailing these high-risk behaviors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor newly created admin accounts (created within minutes of suspicious AJAX activity) for: plugin uploads/installations, file writes to wp-content/uploads or wp-content/themes, modification of wp-config.php or .htaccess, suspicious SQL queries (SELECT * FROM wp_users, exfiltration queries), and web shell patterns (eval(), system(), exec() in uploaded files).

suggestion.title: Attacker Email IOC Hunting: support@flippercode.com
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies hardcoded attacker email 'support@flippercode.com' is embedded in all rogue admin accounts: 'hardcoded email address support@flippercode.com'. This IOC is present in every compromised WordPress instance and enables cross-site victim identification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search WordPress user database (wp_users and wp_usermeta tables) for email address 'support@flippercode.com'. Alert on any matches. Monitor email gateway logs for inbound/outbound mail to this address. Query DNS logs for flippercode.com domain resolution from WordPress server IPs. Check for callback traffic to flippercode.com C2 infrastructure from compromised hosts.

suggestion.title: npm Dependency Confusion: Non-Standard Registry Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article states attack 'leveraged 33 malicious npm packages' via 'dependency confusion' to abuse resolution order. Pipeline produced zero use cases. Detection should flag package installation attempts from non-whitelisted registries or typo-squatted names resolved before official npm.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install/require operations (especially from CI/build agents) that resolve package names to public registries before internal mirrors, or that pull from unfamiliar registry URLs. Correlate with package names containing common typos or obfuscations of legitimate libraries.

suggestion.title: Build System Reconnaissance: Environment Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article describes campaign 'to collect reconnaissance data from developer and build environments.' Pipeline extracted no discovery/collection use cases. Should detect common profiling commands (env, printenv, whoami, id, systeminfo, uname, cat /proc) execution within package install hooks or post-install scripts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process execution of reconnaissance tools (env, printenv, whoami, uname, cat, id, systeminfo, net user) spawned as child processes of npm/node or package managers, particularly in build/CI contexts. Look for shell commands enumerating system state, user accounts, or installed software.

suggestion.title: Malicious Package Post-Install Hook Execution
suggestion.rationale: Dependency confusion attacks typically execute code via postinstall scripts. Article mentions 'attack chain' and package installation but pipeline generated no execution-phase detection. Should monitor for suspicious script execution during npm package installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag process trees where npm/node spawn unusual child processes (curl, wget, powershell, bash) with suspicious arguments (exfiltration of env vars, API calls to external IPs, credential harvesting). Correlate with package.json postinstall/preinstall hooks containing obfuscated or network-based payloads.

suggestion.title: Build Agent Data Exfiltration via HTTP/DNS
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates campaign 'to collect reconnaissance data' from build environments and profile developers. Pipeline has no exfiltration/C2 use cases. Should detect build agents establishing unusual outbound connections to attacker infrastructure with stolen environment/system data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound HTTPS/HTTP requests initiated from CI/build environments (Jenkins, GitHub Actions, GitLab CI agents) to newly registered or low-reputation domains carrying encoded or base64-encoded payloads in query strings or POST bodies. Correlate with process trees spawned by npm/node.

suggestion.title: Typosquatted npm Package Name Installation
suggestion.rationale: Dependency confusion exploits typos and naming tricks to shadow legitimate packages. Article title mentions 'abuse dependency confusion'; no IOC-based detection rule was generated for specific malicious package names despite '33 malicious npm packages' being the article's core finding.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference npm package installation logs (from package-lock.json, yarn.lock, or npm audit output) against known typosquatting patterns and attacker-controlled package registries. Flag package names that are one or two edits away from legitimate popular libraries (lodash→loadsh, express→expres, etc.).

suggestion.title: Forged Authentication Override Cookie Usage
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'attackers were able to connect to the device via VPN using forged cookies' and 'forged authentication override cookie for an arbitrary user'—this is the core attack technique and essential detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GlobalProtect authentication logs for override-cookie auth events where the cookie signature or decryption validates but the credential source is anomalous (no matching interactive login, HTTPS certificate handshake, or password change prior). Flag admin-account authentications via override cookie as high priority.

suggestion.title: Public Certificate Retrieval from GlobalProtect Portal
suggestion.rationale: Article explains 'attackers can obtain the corresponding public key via the HTTPS session'—adversaries must retrieve the cert before forging cookies. Detecting this early indicators disrupts the attack chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unusual or repeated TLS certificate retrieval requests to GlobalProtect portal endpoints (e.g., cert download URIs, public-key exposure in portal responses, or certificate inspection tools like openssl connecting to the gateway). Correlate with subsequent suspicious auth events.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Local Admin Account VPN Session via Override Cookie
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'forged authentication override cookies that targeted the local administrator account'—targeting privileged accounts for remote access is high-confidence malicious.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on VPN session establishment where (user=admin OR user=root) AND auth_method=override_cookie AND no corresponding interactive logon event or password reset precedes the session. Baseline expected admin VPN logins and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: GlobalProtect Authentication Override Feature Enabled or Misconfigured
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'devices had GlobalProtect authentication override cookies enabled and were configured in a way that allowed attackers to forge valid authentication cookies'—presence of this misconfiguration is a prerequisite and should trigger remediation alerts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan GlobalProtect gateway configs for auth_override_cookies=enabled. Flag instances where the same certificate is used for both HTTPS services and override-cookie signing (cross-service cert reuse). Generate alerts for config changes enabling or modifying this setting.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Infrastructure Hosting Exploitation (Vultr, Dromatics Systems)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'hackers authenticating to GlobalProtect gateways' with 'earliest date for observed exploitation was May 17 from infrastructure hosted by Vultr, with a second wave...originating from Dromatics Systems'—allow-list these IPs/ASNs for threat feeds.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate VPN authentication attempts (especially via override cookie) with source IPs belonging to Vultr and Dromatics Systems ASNs. Flag connections from these providers to GlobalProtect gateways as elevated-risk and correlate with device access logs post-authentication.

suggestion.title: Failed vs. Successful VPN Session Establishment Post-Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'in many incidents, even though the appliance accepted the forged cookie, they were unable to establish a full VPN session'—distinguishing accepted-but-failed auth from full breach is important for severity and response.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for VPN authentication successes (override-cookie or otherwise) that do NOT result in a subsequent successful tunnel establishment within 30 seconds. This indicates an attack probe. Separately track authentication events → successful session → network activity for lateral movement baseline.

suggestion.title: GlobalProtect Authentication Bypass - Unauthenticated Portal Access
suggestion.rationale: Article title indicates authentication bypass vulnerability; pipeline failed to model initial access. Exploit of GlobalProtect portal is the attacker's entry point. Should detect successful authentication or portal resource access without legitimate credential submission.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful GlobalProtect authentications preceded by failed credential attempts, or portal access anomalies that bypass standard authentication flows. Monitor for requests to protected portal resources returning success without auth headers or with malformed credentials.

suggestion.title: Post-GlobalProtect Lateral Movement from VPN Entry Point
suggestion.rationale: Active exploitation of auth-bypass followed by internal network access; pipeline missed lateral movement detection. Attacker gains authenticated foothold and pivots internally.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect RDP, SMB, WinRM, or admin-share access originating from GlobalProtect-authenticated VPN source IPs within 10 minutes of session establishment, especially to high-value targets (DCs, servers, admin workstations).

suggestion.title: Arbitrary Code Execution via GlobalProtect RCE
suggestion.rationale: PAN-OS GlobalProtect vulnerability exploited in active attacks implies remote code execution capability post-authentication. Pipeline did not model execution phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or arbitrary binary execution spawned from or immediately following GlobalProtect session initiation. Flag process trees with unusual parents (network services, gateway components) or suspicious command lines in early session window.

suggestion.title: Credential Dumping Post-GlobalProtect Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation typically followed by credential harvesting to enable lateral movement; pipeline did not generate use case for post-compromise credential access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect failed authentication attempts (Event 4625) or LSASS memory access (Sysmon 10) originating from authenticated GlobalProtect user sessions. Monitor for SecurityLogon or Credential Manager API access shortly after portal authentication.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration via Compromised VPN Session
suggestion.rationale: Terminal phase of exploitation; attacker with authenticated VPN access and internal foothold typically exfiltrates data. Pipeline omitted exfiltration detection entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on anomalously high outbound data volume (bytes/connections) from authenticated GlobalProtect sessions to external IPs, especially non-standard ports or to known C2 infrastructure. Flag data transfers to cloud storage or FTP during off-hours.

suggestion.title: Domain Controller Netlogon RPC Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'unauthenticated remote attackers' exploiting Netlogon service on domain controllers via 'specially crafted' RPC calls. No detection for malformed RPC traffic or Netlogon service abuse was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for RPC connections to domain controllers on ports 135, 445, or 389 originating from external/unexpected sources with signs of exploitation payloads (malformed PDUs, encoded shellcode in RPC calls, or abnormal call sequences to lsass.exe). Alert on Netlogon service (lsass) spawning child processes or accessing unusual resources post-connection.

suggestion.title: SYSTEM Privilege Escalation on Domain Controller Post-RPC
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states exploitation grants 'SYSTEM-level privileges.' No use case for detecting privilege escalation from vulnerable service account to SYSTEM.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect SYSTEM-level process spawning or token impersonation from lsass.exe or Netlogon service context after RPC activity. Look for unexpected privileged process execution, WinRM/PSRemoting initiation, or lateral movement tools launched with SYSTEM context.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Domain Controller RPC Port Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions exploitation via RPC but no network-based detection for anomalous connection patterns to DC RPC services. 'Active exploitation in the wild' demands immediate network visibility.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag connections to domain controller RPC ports (135, 445, 389) from non-standard sources (non-corp networks, residential IPs, TOR exits). Baseline normal DC RPC chatter and alert on connection attempts with zero successful authentications or anomalously short session durations.

suggestion.title: Netlogon Service Crash or Restart Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Specially crafted RPC payloads often cause service instability. Article implies active exploitation campaigns; service restarts are forensic indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Netlogon service (lsass.exe, svchost netlogon) unexpected termination or rapid restart cycles on domain controllers. Correlate with preceding RPC connection spikes. Lsass crashes are high-fidelity exploitation signals.

suggestion.title: Domain Controller Command/Scriptlet Execution Post-RPC
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'arbitrary code execution' but no hunt for post-exploitation command execution. RCE implies subsequent execution; detection should cover cmd.exe, PowerShell, or WMI spawned from DC vulnerable context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect cmd.exe, PowerShell, cscript.exe, or wmic.exe execution on domain controllers with parent process lsass.exe, svchost.exe (netlogon), or lpremote.exe. Flag execution with encoded payloads, obfuscated parameters, or network callbacks in the command line.

suggestion.title: Botnet C2 Command Execution Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Botnet dismantling articles establish C2 infrastructure used to command infected hosts; this UC captures beaconing and task execution characteristic of active botnet membership.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound connections to known botnet C2 domains or IPs with periodic beaconing patterns. Monitor for DNS queries to C2 infrastructure or large-scale lateral command propagation across infected hosts.

suggestion.title: Botnet Propagation & Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: Large-scale botnets (17M devices) require propagation mechanisms; article context implies mass infection via vulnerability exploitation or malware distribution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect mass file drops or process spawning consistent with worm-like propagation. Monitor for SMB or RDP-based lateral movement attempts across subnets post-initial compromise.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Botnet Agent Installation
suggestion.rationale: Botnets persist via injected agents or scheduled tasks; detection of installer/loader execution is critical to identifying compromised machines.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious scheduled task creation or registry persistence mechanisms (startup folders, run keys) correlating with known botnet loader execution patterns.

suggestion.title: Initial Infection via Known Vulnerability
suggestion.rationale: Botnet articles typically detail the initial infection vector (e.g., CVE-based exploitation); this UC captures exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for exploitation attempts or downloads of known botnet malware families. Detect anomalous child processes spawned from web browsers or email clients.

suggestion.title: Botnet Malware Heuristic Detection
suggestion.rationale: Botnets are distributed as executable payloads; missing hashes, file paths, or behavioral signatures is a critical analytical gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of unsigned binaries or DLLs with characteristics matching documented botnet agents (e.g., process hollowing, API hooking, or cryptographic key material in-memory).

suggestion.title: Mass Device Infection Spike Detection
suggestion.rationale: A 17M-device botnet implies coordinated mass infection events; this UC detects sudden infection rate anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate sudden spikes in malware detections, process creation failures, or network outbound connections across large device populations within short time windows.

suggestion.title: WordPress Admin Account Creation via Plugin AJAX
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'the function creates a new WordPress user via wp_insert_user() with the hardcoded role of administrator.' No detection rule was generated for this direct admin instantiation mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on wp_insert_user() calls executed via admin-ajax.php from unauthenticated sessions that assign 'administrator' role. Flag user creation events with randomly-generated usernames and admin privileges spawned by plugin AJAX handlers rather than authenticated admin accounts.

suggestion.title: Exploitation of Unauthenticated Plugin AJAX Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'the AJAX endpoint used for this feature was accessible to unauthenticated users and relied solely on a publicly exposed nonce check in frontend JavaScript, rendering the protection ineffective.' No detection for AJAX abuse or nonce bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect requests to wp-admin/admin-ajax.php with check_temp=false parameter from non-authenticated sources. Flag nonce values extracted from frontend JavaScript being reused across multiple requests or high-velocity exploitation attempts against vendor support endpoints.

suggestion.title: Passwordless Magic Login URL Generation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'generates a 'magic login URL' using generate_login_link(), stores it as user meta, and returns it in the response body.' No detection for passwordless authentication mechanism or suspicious user metadata writes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor usermeta table modifications for login_link, temporary_access, or passwordless_token entries. Flag AJAX responses containing login URLs or authentication tokens. Correlate generate_login_link() function execution with concurrent user creation events.

suggestion.title: Attacker-Controlled Email in Rogue Admin Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'hardcoded email address support@flippercode.com.' This hardcoded indicator is planted in every exploited account and is a definitive compromise signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any WordPress user created with email support@flippercode.com or flippercode.com domain. Correlate with requests to WP Maps Pro temporary access endpoints. Block domains and emails matching vendor support forgery patterns.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-8732 WP Maps Pro Exploitation Signature
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'threat actors are trying to exploit the vulnerability, and blocked more than 3,600 attempts over the past 24 hours.' No signature-based or CVE-specific detection rules were generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create CVE-2026-8732 signatures: requests containing check_temp parameter in wp-admin/admin-ajax.php action handlers from unauthenticated sources. Alert on WP Maps Pro version ≤6.1.0 installations receiving such payloads. Low false-positive: this endpoint has no legitimate unauthenticated use.

suggestion.title: Frontend Nonce Extracted and Reused for CSRF Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'relied solely on a publicly exposed nonce check in frontend JavaScript.' No detection for nonce extraction, reuse across sessions, or CSRF token exhaustion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect the same nonce value used in multiple requests from different IP addresses or user agents within short time windows. Flag high-volume requests using nonces extracted from static JavaScript assets. Correlate with geography/ASN anomalies.

suggestion.title: Multiple Password Reset Requests on High-Value Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'forwarding password reset codes' (plural). Threat actors bypass verification through repeated requests; >2 resets per account within 1 hour is anomalous and should trigger alerts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on multiple password reset initiations targeting same user within short timeframe, prioritizing high-value accounts. Successful reset following multiple failed attempts indicates exploitation of recovery-tool bypass.

suggestion.title: Account Recovery Chatbot Rapid-Fire Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'trick the chatbot'—implies programmatic or rapid interaction patterns. Detect high-velocity reset-code requests or suspicious query sequences in chatbot sessions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor account recovery chatbot for sessions with >5 reset-code requests, unusual patterns consistent with prompt injection, or queries from suspicious user agents. Correlate with downstream account takeover indicators.

suggestion.title: Account Login Following Password Reset Event
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates attackers 'hijack high-value accounts' post-recovery. Detect access from anomalous locations within hours of successful account recovery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful account recovery with login from new geographies, new devices, or high-risk IPs within 2-hour window. Flag password change + unusual login pattern as probable compromise.

suggestion.title: Missing Verification Checkpoints in Account Recovery
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability: 'no verification required' for password reset code issuance. Detect recovery flows where security challenge steps are skipped or verification logs show gaps.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag account recovery transactions where expected verification steps (security questions, email confirmation, OTP) are missing from audit trail, or reset codes issued without matching IP/device baseline.

suggestion.title: Netlogon RPC Exploitation — Malformed Packets to Domain Controller
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated remote attackers...sending specially crafted [packets]'. Pipeline missed the exploitation attempt phase despite active exploitation being central to threat.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor domain controllers for lsass.exe spawning unexpected child processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, rundll32.exe) with SYSTEM integrity post-network spike. Correlate inbound RPC calls (ports 135, 445) with Event ID 4625 (failed logon) or 7022 (service failure) on the same DC within 2-minute window.

suggestion.title: Domain Controller SYSTEM-Context Code Execution Post-RCE
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'arbitrary code execution with SYSTEM-level privileges'. Pipeline did not model post-exploitation detection for unexpected SYSTEM-spawned processes from lsass.exe or svchost.exe.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation with ParentProcessId=lsass.exe or svchost.exe spawning command shells, network utilities (net.exe, wmic.exe), or remote-access tools with LogonType=0 (SYSTEM) on domain controllers. Severity HIGH if parent is Netlogon-related svchost.

suggestion.title: Domain Controller Reconnaissance — Netlogon Fingerprinting Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article: vulnerability 'affects Windows servers configured as domain controllers'. Attackers must enumerate DC before exploitation; pipeline omitted reconnaissance detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect external hosts performing RPC endpoint enumeration (port 135 followed by repeated SMB 445 attempts), LDAP queries for DC discovery (port 389), or NetBIOS NBSTAT queries (port 137) from untrusted subnets. Flag sequences suggesting scanning-then-exploitation pattern.

suggestion.title: Netlogon Service Instability or Restart Cycles on Domain Controller
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation or failed exploitation attempts likely cause Netlogon service instability. Article describes active exploitation; failed attempts will leave observable service artifacts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Event ID 7022 (service failed to start), 7034 (service crashed without user action), or rapid lsass.exe restart cycles on domain controllers. Correlate with preceding network anomalies or failed authentication spikes (Event ID 4625) to identify exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Credential Harvesting from Compromised Domain Controller
suggestion.rationale: 0-click RCE to SYSTEM on a DC is high-value for credential theft. Article implies active exploitation; threat actors will follow up with credential access. Pipeline missed post-exploitation phases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect lsass.exe memory access from unexpected parents (rundll32.exe, comsvcs.dll invocations for procdump), Invoke-Mimikatz patterns, or credential dumping utilities post-RCE. Monitor for suspicious Kerberos ticket requests (Event ID 4769 spikes) or DCSync activity (Event ID 4662 — privileged attribute reads) from SYSTEM context.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised Domain Controller
suggestion.rationale: DC compromise with SYSTEM privileges enables rapid domain escalation. Pipeline's empty kill chain omitted post-exploitation lateral-movement phase critical to modeling attacker impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-RCE, detect unusual outbound SMB (445), WinRM (5985/5986), or RDP (3389) from compromised DC to member servers or other DCs. Flag remote execution (Event ID 4688 with cmdline showing WMI, PSRemoting, or service creation) originating from SYSTEM context post-exploitation window.

suggestion.title: Botnet C2 Communication Detected
suggestion.rationale: Article describes botnet linked to 17M devices; implies active C2 infrastructure and periodic beacon/callback traffic that should trigger network detection before takedown occurs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify anomalous outbound traffic to known botnet C2 infrastructure (once IOCs are properly extracted). Look for beaconing patterns, unusual DNS queries, or encrypted tunnels matching known botnet family signatures. Alert on suspicious process spawning network connections to attacker-controlled domains.

suggestion.title: Mass Malware Distribution via Botnet Network
suggestion.rationale: 17M infected devices implies initial compromise vector; botnet likely distributed malware at scale. Pipeline should capture propagation IOCs and distribution methods.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect malware delivery mechanisms targeting the infection vector (email, watering hole, supply chain, or vulnerable service exposure). Monitor for suspicious download activity, email with malicious attachments matching botnet payloads, or exploitation attempts against known vulnerable services.

suggestion.title: Botnet Malware Persistence Mechanism
suggestion.rationale: Sustaining 17M infections requires robust persistence; article should specify registry keys, scheduled tasks, service installation, or other mechanisms for surviving reboots.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious registry modifications in Run/RunOnce keys, scheduled task creation by unknown processes, service installation with random names or spoofed binary paths, or startup folder modifications. Cross-reference against known botnet persistence IOCs.

suggestion.title: Malware Obfuscation / Anti-Analysis Behavior
suggestion.rationale: Large botnets employ obfuscation, packing, or polymorphic techniques to evade detection. Article should reference obfuscation methods or anti-reverse-engineering tactics.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process hollowing, code injection into legitimate processes, or execution of heavily obfuscated/packed binaries. Monitor for entropy anomalies in PE headers, suspicious memory allocations followed by code execution, or process spawning with unusual parent-child relationships.

suggestion.title: Botnet Lateral Movement / Worm Behavior
suggestion.rationale: Botnets often propagate via lateral movement (SMB, RDP, USB). Article should detail propagation methods across the 17M-device footprint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect brute-force RDP/SMB attempts, unusual lateral movement patterns via compromised accounts, or mass file propagation over network shares. Alert on suspicious LSASS access, credential theft attempts, or propagation via USB/removable media.

suggestion.title: Dutch Authority Botnet Takedown Infrastructure Artifacts
suggestion.rationale: Dutch authorities taking down botnet infrastructure may seize servers, sinkhole C2, or modify DNS records. Article should reference sink-holed domains, law-enforcement ISPs, or shared hosting artifacts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-takedown, identify orphaned/sinkholed C2 domains responding to law-enforcement IP ranges or previously-active botnet domains now resolving to null/takedown pages. Correlate with historical botnet IOCs to validate disruption and measure remediation success.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated WP Maps Pro AJAX Endpoint Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'the AJAX endpoint used for this feature was accessible to unauthenticated users' — this is the attack surface. Pipeline failed to suggest detection of unauthorized endpoint access or suspicious AJAX parameter patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to /wp-admin/admin-ajax.php with WP Maps Pro action parameters from sources lacking valid WordPress session cookies. Alert on check_temp parameter variations or admin creation payloads from unauthenticated clients.

suggestion.title: Admin User Creation with Hardcoded Email support@flippercode.com
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'creates a new WordPress user via wp_insert_user() with the hardcoded role of administrator...the hardcoded email address support@flippercode.com' — direct IOC for detection that pipeline entirely missed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert immediately on any WordPress user creation with email 'support@flippercode.com' or admin role assignment via wp_insert_user() from non-authenticated sessions. Monitor for randomized username patterns in conjunction with admin role assignment.

suggestion.title: Passwordless Login URL Generation and Magic Link Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'generates a "magic login URL" using generate_login_link()...Once the attacker visits this URL, they are automatically authenticated to the newly created administrator account, with no password or any other verification required' — passwordless auth bypass detection completely absent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WordPress authentication endpoints for login completions bypassing password verification. Alert on token-based login URL usage or generate_login_link() execution. Correlate magic-link generation with prior AJAX endpoint exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-8732 Exploitation Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article documents active exploitation: 'Researchers at WordPress security company Defiant observed that threat actors are trying to exploit the vulnerability, and blocked more than 3,600 attempts over the past 24 hours' — pipeline failed to extract CVE or suggest attack pattern signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for request sequences to WP Maps Pro AJAX endpoints targeting the temporary access feature, followed by wp_insert_user() database operations or admin account creation events. Alert on failed and successful exploitation attempts within same session.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Deployment and Plugin Installation via Rogue Admin
suggestion.rationale: Article warns: 'Having admin-level access on the site means attackers can inject persistent backdoors...deploy web shells, install malicious plugins' — post-compromise persistence mechanisms not detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file uploads or plugin installations by admin accounts created immediately after CVE-2026-8732 exploitation. Alert on suspicious .php, .phtml, or shell-like files in wp-content/plugins or wp-content/uploads directories from non-standard admin users.

suggestion.title: Client-Side Nonce Validation Bypass Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies root cause: 'relied solely on a publicly exposed nonce check in frontend JavaScript, rendering the protection ineffective' — weak nonce implementation and bypasses should trigger detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor AJAX requests lacking server-side nonce validation or using client-source nonces. Alert on nonce reuse across multiple requests from different sources or IPs. Flag requests with nonce values visible in frontend source code or HTML.

suggestion.title: Multiple Password Reset Requests for High-Value Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'trick the chatbot into forwarding password reset codes with no verification required.' Detection gap: rapid or repeated password reset requests on the same account, especially high-value targets, signal possible exploitation of the chatbot reset flow.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on 3+ password reset code requests for the same user account within 60 minutes. Escalate when the target account has privileged roles, public figure status, or high follower count. Correlate with failed authentication attempts preceding the resets.

suggestion.title: Account Configuration Changes Post-Password-Reset
suggestion.rationale: Article describes the threat outcome as account hijacking. Post-compromise, attackers typically change recovery email, phone, or MFA settings to lock out the legitimate owner.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag account modifications (recovery email change, phone number swap, MFA reset, password change) occurring within 15 minutes of a password reset event or from a new device. High-fidelity indicator if the legitimate user's device is offline during the change window.

suggestion.title: Login From New Device After Password Reset
suggestion.rationale: Attackers obtaining reset codes implies subsequent account access. Article implies immediate account takeover. Detection opportunity: first-ever login from a new device immediately after password reset event.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect successful authentication from a previously unseen device fingerprint within 30 minutes of a password reset. Combine with anomalies in IP geolocation, user-agent, or enrollment status (e.g., device not enrolled in MDM).

suggestion.title: Chatbot Reset Code Request Abuse Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies the attack vector as exploiting the AI chatbot itself ('tricking the chatbot'). This implies chatbot logs will record unusual reset-request patterns before account compromise occurs—the critical early-warning signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor chatbot interaction logs for rapid successive password reset requests or requests for multiple distinct accounts from the same IP/session. Flag if the same prompt or phrasing is repeated (behavioral matching on 'trick' patterns). Alert on reset requests originating from known Tor exit nodes or datacenter IPs.

suggestion.title: Netlogon Service Child Process Execution with SYSTEM Context
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states code executes 'with SYSTEM-level privileges' via Netlogon RCE. Pipeline generated no detection for abnormal process spawning from Netlogon service despite this being a direct execution indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation where parent is Netlogon service (svchost.exe or lsass.exe subtree) spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or arbitrary executables with SYSTEM privileges in non-maintenance windows. Baseline normal DC activity and correlate against patch status.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated RPC Inbound to Domain Controller Netlogon Ports
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'unauthenticated remote attackers' sending 'specially crafted' requests to Netlogon RPC (ports 445/139). Pipeline did not suggest detection for exploitation payloads or anomalous RPC traffic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound RPC traffic to DCs for malformed/truncated requests, exploitation signatures matching CVE-2026-41089, or payloads from external/untrusted networks. Correlate with IDS/IPS alerts.

suggestion.title: Domain Controller Service Anomalies or Unexpected Restarts
suggestion.rationale: RCE exploitation often manifests as service crashes, kernel exceptions, or unplanned reboots. Article notes 'active exploitation' but pipeline suggested no post-exploitation detection for impact indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Netlogon service unexpected crashes or DC reboot sequences in short timeframe, especially if preceded by inbound RPC anomalies from external sources. Correlate against patch applicability.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Domain Controller Asset Exposure — CVE-2026-41089
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline summary states 'one use case(s) fired' but generated use cases output is empty. The recommended asset-exposure hunt should have materialized as a detection use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate domain controllers and cross-reference against CVE-2026-41089 patch status using OS build numbers and KB entries. Flag unpatched systems for immediate isolation or compensating control deployment.

suggestion.title: Botnet C&C Beaconing and Protocol Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'botnet'—C&C communication is the defining characteristic of botnets. Pipeline generated zero detection logic despite this explicit mention.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect infected hosts establishing outbound connections to known-malicious or anomalous C&C infrastructure via HTTP/HTTPS or raw sockets. Pivot on rare external IPs from internal IP space, repeated connection attempts to dynamic/high-ASN IP blocks, or beacon-like regularized traffic patterns on non-standard ports.

suggestion.title: Persistence Mechanisms and Autostart Execution
suggestion.rationale: Botnets typically persist via registry/task scheduler/launchd modifications; article states 17M infected devices likely sustained long-term implants. Pipeline missed persistence detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process execution of legitimate OS binaries (rundll32, regsvcs, schtasks) with suspicious arguments targeting HKLM/HKCU Run keys, or on scheduled task creation from unusual parent processes. Cross-reference against known benign auto-start entries.

suggestion.title: Malware Execution and Process Spawning Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Botnet injection, UAC bypass, or in-memory execution are typical infection mechanics; no process execution rules detected despite 'infected devices' language in article.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for execution of unsigned binaries in temp directories, DLL injection (unusual LoadImage calls), or process hollowing (mismatched parent-child pairs). Flag powershell/cmd.exe spawned by non-shell parents or with obfuscated arguments.

suggestion.title: WordPress admin user creation with hardcoded external email
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'creates a new WordPress user via wp_insert_user() with... the hardcoded email address support@flippercode.com.' This is a direct IOC and highest-confidence detection signal for CVE-2026-8732 exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WordPress user creation events (wp_insert_user, user_register hooks) for admin role assignment paired with email address support@flippercode.com, regardless of username. Also monitor user_meta creation for magic login links (generate_login_link output). This email should never legitimately appear in enterprise WordPress environments.

suggestion.title: AJAX endpoint exploitation attempts targeting WP Maps Pro temporary access feature
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'the AJAX endpoint used for this feature was accessible to unauthenticated users and relied solely on a publicly exposed nonce check in frontend JavaScript.' The check_temp parameter with false value triggers admin creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP POST requests to AJAX endpoints in WP Maps Pro (typically /wp-admin/admin-ajax.php) containing 'check_temp=false' parameter or the map-related action parameters associated with the plugin, especially from unauthenticated sessions. Defiant blocked 3,600+ attempts in 24 hours, suggesting a recognizable pattern.

suggestion.title: Passwordless admin login URL generation and usage
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'generates a "magic login URL" using generate_login_link(), stores it as user meta, and returns it in the response body.' Attackers receive a URL that auto-authenticates them with the rogue admin account.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for metadata creation on newly-created WordPress users (particularly those with random usernames and external emails) where the metadata key indicates a login token or magic link. Correlate with immediate admin login attempts from suspicious IP ranges within seconds of account creation.

suggestion.title: Successful authentication immediately following WordPress admin account creation
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation sequence: attacker creates admin account via AJAX, receives magic login URL in response, visits URL, and is 'automatically authenticated to the newly created administrator account, with no password or any other verification required.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect patterns where a new WordPress user with admin role is created and then immediately logs in from a different IP or user agent within a tight time window (seconds), especially if the account creation originated from an AJAX endpoint and the authentication bypassed password verification.

suggestion.title: Multiple failed AJAX requests with nonce variation (CVE-2026-8732 brute attempts)
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability relies on 'publicly exposed nonce check in frontend JavaScript, rendering the protection ineffective.' Attackers can extract and replay nonces, enabling brute force of the AJAX endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for repeated requests to WordPress AJAX endpoints (wp-admin/admin-ajax.php) with the WP Maps Pro action parameters, using different nonce values or no nonce, originating from the same IP or user agent across a short time period. Volume threshold: Defiant observed 3,600+ attempts in 24 hours.

suggestion.title: Backdoor installation on WordPress site post-admin account takeover
suggestion.rationale: Article warns of post-exploitation impact: 'Having admin-level access on the site means attackers can inject persistent backdoors, modify content, access private data, deploy web shells, install malicious plugins, and take over the website.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-compromise, monitor newly-created WordPress admin accounts for installation of suspicious plugins, creation of PHP files in web-accessible directories, or injection of code into themes/plugins. Correlate with the creation timeline of the rogue admin account from the AJAX exploitation.

suggestion.title: WP Maps Pro Unauthenticated Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'Critical WP Maps Pro Flaw Actively Exploited'; no detection rule generated for exploitation attempts against the vulnerable plugin endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to WP Maps Pro plugin endpoints (wp-content/plugins/wp-maps-pro/) for known exploitation patterns. Detect POST requests with unusual payloads, directory traversal attempts, or unauthenticated access to admin-level functionality. Flag requests that precede sudden user creation events.

suggestion.title: Suspicious WordPress Admin Account Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article core attack is 'Create Admin Accounts' via vulnerability; pipeline generated no detection for this privilege-escalation endpoint, the attacker's objective.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WordPress user creation events (wp_users table INSERT, REST API /wp-json/wp/v2/users POST) for new administrator accounts. Flag if creation originates from unauthenticated or web-facing contexts, occurs outside business hours, or is preceded by HTTP 404s or plugin-related errors.

suggestion.title: Admin Account Created by Non-Admin User
suggestion.rationale: The vulnerability allows unprivileged or unauthenticated access to escalate to admin; detection should flag admin creation by non-admin principals.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate WordPress user role assignment (wp_usermeta meta_key='wp_capabilities', meta_value containing 'administrator') with the calling user context. Alert if a non-admin or guest session grants admin role, or if admin role assignment follows immediately after plugin error conditions.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Hidden Admin Account Detection
suggestion.rationale: Attackers often create backdoor admin accounts with obfuscated names; article implies admin accounts are created for persistence, yet no rule covers detection of anomalous account characteristics.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify WordPress admin accounts created post-exploit by anomaly scoring: new accounts with display_name matching common backdoor patterns (e.g., single characters, numbered names, 'admin2', 'support'), no profile data, zero published posts, or user_registered timestamp clustering near known exploit dates.

suggestion.title: Package Installation from Malicious Packagist Repository
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes malware 'hiding inside a legitimate PHP package available through Packagist.' Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this obvious detection opportunity. Developers installing `roberts/leads` package should trigger detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect composer install or require statements pulling from packagist.org/packages/roberts/leads or github.com/roberts/leads. Monitor for package manager activity fetching these specific package names. Alert on composer lockfile changes referencing the compromised package.

suggestion.title: Configuration File Execution from PHP Package
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware is 'disguising a dangerous payload as a routine configuration file.' This indicates execution via config file, not detected by pipeline. Detection should monitor for PHP/composer configuration files being executed or sourced.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for execution of configuration files (composer.json, config.php) or sourcing of configuration files via php -r or require statements. Detect unusual execution patterns from package vendor directories where configs are typically read-only.

suggestion.title: Abnormal Child Process from Composer/PHP Package Manager
suggestion.rationale: Attack 'blends in easily with normal development workflows' — implies malware executes within context of legitimate composer/php process. Detection should monitor for process lineage anomalies after composer install.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual child processes spawned by composer.phar or php processes, especially network connections, privilege escalation, or command execution that deviate from normal package installation behavior.

suggestion.title: GitHub Package Source Retrieval Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates `github.com/roberts/leads` as source for malicious package. Detection should monitor for unusual GitHub API calls or git clone operations from suspicious repositories during development workflows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for git clone, git pull, or GitHub API calls to github.com/roberts/leads from development machines. Alert on composer.json entries requiring packages from non-standard GitHub sources.

suggestion.title: Developer Workstation PHP Process Network Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'application layer protocol' use (T1071) for C2. After malware executes from package config, detection should monitor for unusual outbound connections from PHP processes on developer machines.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for network connections initiated by php.exe or composer.phar processes to non-standard destinations. Alert on unusual DNS queries or HTTP requests from PHP child processes spawned during or after package installation.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated PHP Code in Package Vendor Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'obfuscated files or information' (T1027). Should detect obfuscated PHP code being written to vendor directories, which is anomalous for legitimate packages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation of obfuscated or encoded PHP files in vendor/ directories. Flag files with unusual entropy, base64 encoding, or hexadecimal patterns in .php files that deviate from typical library code.

suggestion.title: Chatbot-Mediated Account Recovery Without Standard Verification
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers 'trick[ed] the chatbot into forwarding password reset codes with no verification required' — this is a direct attack pattern where the AI system bypasses intended security controls. No UC was generated despite this being the attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor account recovery requests routed through AI chatbot or automated recovery flows that succeed without completing all expected verification steps (e.g., email confirmation, OTP validation). Flag cases where password reset codes are issued and consumed from different geographic locations or IP ranges within short time windows, or where recovery succeeds despite incomplete user challenge responses.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Pattern of Account Recovery Requests Targeting High-Value Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article notes threat actors 'hijack high-value accounts' — suggesting reconnaissance or targeting behavior. Pipeline missed reconnaissance/targeting phase entirely. Phrase: 'hijack high-value accounts' implies selective targeting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect clusters of failed or successful account recovery attempts against known VIP/high-value user accounts (e.g., verified influencers, organizational accounts) within compressed time windows or from coordinated IP/device sources. Baseline typical recovery request patterns and alert on deviation.

suggestion.title: Successful Account Access Immediately Following Password Reset Completion
suggestion.rationale: Hijacking attack succeeds when password is reset via the vulnerable chatbot, then attacker uses new credentials. Article: 'allowed attackers to hijack high-value accounts' — the impact phase involves login with reset credentials. No impact/lateral-movement detection was proposed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful password reset events (especially those initiated through automated/chatbot-driven recovery) with subsequent login attempts from anomalous geographies, devices, or user agents within minutes. Flag if legitimate account owner's subsequent login attempt is blocked or differs significantly from the attacker's initial post-reset access.

suggestion.title: Chatbot Instruction Injection / Security Control Bypass via Natural Language
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability is that 'attackers' trick the 'chatbot' into mishandling security gates. This suggests prompt injection or instruction override. Phrase: 'tricking the chatbot' indicates adversarial manipulation of the AI model's behavior outside intended guardrails.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor chatbot conversation logs for patterns of user inputs that attempt to override or bypass security instructions (e.g., repeated requests to 'skip verification', 'just send the code', requests in multiple languages if the bot is susceptible to language-switching attacks). Detect when chatbot outputs deviate from expected security-control enforcement (e.g., forwarding codes without confirmation).

suggestion.title: Netlogon RPC Anomalies to Domain Controllers
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'specially crafted' network traffic targeting Netlogon protocol on domain controllers. Pipeline must detect malformed or unusual RPC requests to the Netlogon service (RPC interface) from external IPs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor domain controller RPC traffic (TCP 445, UDP 135/139) for connection attempts followed by anomalous packet patterns indicative of exploit payloads. Baseline normal Netlogon RPC traffic and alert on deviations in packet structure, timing, or source legitimacy.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access Attempts to Domain Controller Services
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated remote attackers' can trigger RCE. Detect authentication-bypass attempts or null-auth sessions to normally-authenticated DC services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on failed or null authentication sequences to domain controller RPC endpoints, especially Netlogon. Correlate with network connection events showing external IP to DC port 445/135. Look for repeated or high-volume auth failures in short timeframes.

suggestion.title: SYSTEM-Level Process Creation Triggered by Network Exploit
suggestion.rationale: Article states successful exploitation achieves 'arbitrary code execution with SYSTEM-level privileges.' Detect process creation from parent processes associated with network services (svchost, RPC) that result in SYSTEM processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for SYSTEM-level process creation (especially cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or services.exe children) spawned by RPC service hosts (svchost.exe, lsass.exe) without legitimate scheduled task or service install events preceding them. Correlate with network connection logs showing external source.

suggestion.title: Domain Controller Netlogon Service Restart or Crash
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation attempts against Netlogon RPC interface often destabilize or crash the service before successful code execution. Monitor for service state changes on DCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected restarts or crashes of the Netlogon service (lsass.exe child or netlogon-specific service) on domain controllers, especially within minutes of unusual network traffic or auth failures.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Domain Controller Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: After achieving SYSTEM-level code execution on a DC, adversaries typically dump credentials, modify policies, or move to additional DCs. Article notes active exploitation but doesn't detail secondary actions—assume standard DC-compromise behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-exploitation telemetry: credential dumping tools (mimikatz, comsvcs.dll IAT hooks), DCSync activity, SMB lateral movement from the compromised DC to peer DCs, or elevated privilege use on other systems. Correlate DC compromise timestamps with subsequent lateral movement.

suggestion.title: Netlogon Port Scanning or Service Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Attackers reconnaissance before exploit delivery often scan for Netlogon service availability. Article mentions 'actively exploited in the wild,' implying reconnaissance precedes attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect port scans or repeated connection attempts to TCP 445 (SMB/Netlogon RPC) and UDP 135/139 on domain controllers from external or suspicious internal IPs, especially if followed by exploit-pattern network traffic.

suggestion.title: Botnet C2 Outbound Connection Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article describes dismantled botnet infrastructure linked to 17M infected devices; would have detailed C2 domains/IPs. This detection is foundational and absent.
