suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish whitelist of legitimate C2 domains from article, then alert on outbound TCP/UDP traffic to known botnet C2 servers. Monitor DNS queries for sinkhole/takedown domains that may indicate legacy bot callbacks.

suggestion.title: Botnet Malware Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Botnet dismantlement articles typically specify malware binary names, file paths, and execution patterns; none extracted despite 'linked to' phrasing suggesting infection vector details.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution of known botnet malware samples (by hash or name if disclosed). Monitor for parent-child process relationships typical of botnet dropper payloads.

suggestion.title: Botnet Persistence Mechanism Installation
suggestion.rationale: A 17M-device botnet requires persistence across reboots; article likely describes registry modifications, scheduled tasks, or service installation. No detection use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious auto-start registry writes (HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run) or service creation pointing to unusual paths or containing obfuscated names typical of botnet persistence.

suggestion.title: Mass Device Compromise Pattern (Botnet Infection Wave)
suggestion.rationale: 17M device infection implies coordinated distribution; article would describe infection campaigns or exploit chains. Detection focus on mass outbound C2 or lateral movement patterns missing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect statistical anomalies in outbound connections from multiple devices to same C2 endpoint within time window. Alert on correlated anti-virus detections across asset population matching botnet malware signatures.

suggestion.title: Botnet Loader/Dropper Activity
suggestion.rationale: Botnet deployment typically uses loader component; phrase 'infected devices' suggests distribution chain (downloader → malware). No loader detection use case present.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unsigned or low-reputation executables making outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests followed by child process execution. Alert on file drop activity to %Temp%, %AppData%, or other staging directories followed by immediate execution.

suggestion.title: Post-Takedown Sinkhole Domain Callback Detection
suggestion.rationale: Dutch authorities dismantled infrastructure (not just arrest); sinkhole domains would be set up. Detecting bots still attempting callbacks to seized/redirected C2 is a critical post-incident detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any DNS resolution or connection attempt to announced sinkhole/takedown domains attributed to this botnet by law enforcement. Indicates devices still actively compromised and attempting callbacks post-dismantlement.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated WordPress AJAX Endpoint Nonce Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article states AJAX endpoint 'was accessible to unauthenticated users and relied solely on a publicly exposed nonce check in frontend JavaScript, rendering the protection ineffective.' No detection for unauthenticated POST to admin-ajax.php with nonce validation failure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP POST requests to /wp-admin/admin-ajax.php from sources lacking valid WordPress authentication cookies or session tokens. Spike in volume or repeated attempts with check_temp parameter is exploitation signature.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized WordPress Administrator Account Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker triggers 'code to create a new WordPress user via wp_insert_user() with the hardcoded role of administrator.' Pipeline missed privilege escalation to admin role.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for wp_insert_user() calls with role parameter set to 'administrator' outside normal admin workflows. Flag accounts with hardcoded email support@flippercode.com or randomly-generated usernames created without corresponding registration or password reset events.

suggestion.title: Passwordless Magic Login Link Authentication to Admin Account
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attacker receives 'magic login URL' via generate_login_link() and 'visits this URL, they are automatically authenticated to the newly created administrator account, with no password or any other verification required.' Persistent authentication mechanism not detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect successful WordPress admin logins lacking preceding password submission or credential entry in same session. Correlate successful admin authentication with recent user creation events for the same account. Alert on generate_login_link() function calls or unusual temporary token storage in wp_usermeta table.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Admin Activity Following User Elevation
suggestion.rationale: Article warns compromised accounts enable 'inject persistent backdoors, modify content, access private data, deploy web shells, install malicious plugins.' Pipeline generated no detections for post-exploitation indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect installation or activation of new plugins within 10 minutes of new admin account creation. Monitor wp_options table for changes to active plugins from newly-created accounts. Flag PHP file uploads to wp-content/plugins or wp-content/uploads correlated with recent account elevation.

suggestion.title: WP Maps Pro Plugin Version Reconnaissance and Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies vulnerable plugin by name (WP Maps Pro) and version (6.1.0 and older). Pipeline missed plugin fingerprinting opportunity and version-specific exploitation patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline HTTP requests to WP Maps Pro AJAX endpoints. Alert on requests containing plugin-specific parameters (e.g., check_temp=false, wp_insert_user patterns) or unusual parameter combinations. Cross-reference with WordPress plugin version detection to identify v6.1.0 or older installations still vulnerable.

suggestion.title: Suspicious User Metadata Modification for Credential Storage
suggestion.rationale: Article states function 'stores it [magic login link] as user meta, and returns it in the response body.' Pipeline failed to detect unusual usermeta entries used as credential storage or authentication bypass mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query wp_usermeta table for suspicious meta_key entries containing 'token', 'login_link', 'temp', or 'magic'. Flag entries created on newly-registered admin accounts outside normal user workflows. Cross-reference metadata values against expected formats (random strings, URLs) for authentication bypass tokens.

suggestion.title: Docker/Kubernetes Image Repository Poisoning
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'TeamPCP compromised Checkmarx KICS across multiple attack chains...poisoning a Docker Hub repository to later steal Kubernetes secrets.' Supply-chain poisoning is foundational to the entire attack scenario and requires upstream detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unauthorized manifest changes, tag rewrites, or layer substitutions in Docker Hub or private registries. Alert on image pulls followed by unexpected behavioral changes or process execution diverging from baseline scanning tools.

suggestion.title: Privileged Container Escape Capabilities Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article details container escape via: 'CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_SYS_MODULE, CAP_SYS_PTRACE, CAP_NET_ADMIN.' These capabilities are high-risk and necessary alert trigger points.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on container launch with dangerous capabilities. Escalate if container process subsequently calls ptrace(), attempts module loading (/proc/sys/kernel), or accesses /proc/<pid>/mem to manipulate host processes.

suggestion.title: Kubernetes ServiceAccount Secret Access and Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'steal Kubernetes secrets and other sensitive data.' Compromised container processes reading mounted ServiceAccount tokens or etcd-accessible credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file access to /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token and ConfigMap/Secret API access from non-system namespaces. Flag unusual API queries or token usage from unexpected source IPs or service accounts.

suggestion.title: Malicious Stealer Payload Execution in Build/Scan Context
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'tainted images distributed a stealer that was loaded during the KICS scanning process.' Detection of unexpected code execution during trusted tool invocation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child processes spawned by scanning tools (kics, trivy, etc.) or build pipelines. Alert if unsigned libraries are loaded or unexpected network connections originate from these processes.

suggestion.title: Container-to-Host Kernel Exploit Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Container escape followed by host compromise' exploiting 'host system vulnerabilities.' Detect kernel-level breakout indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect container processes accessing /sys/kernel/debug, /proc/sys/kernel/*, or /proc/<pid>/mem. Alert if container spawns process with UID 0 after such accesses or triggers kernel warnings/panics from within namespace context.

suggestion.title: Kubernetes API Reconnaissance and Abuse from Pod Context
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Exploiting misconfigurations and the insecure use of...orchestration APIs.' Abuse of Kubernetes API via compromised pods for cluster enumeration or manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Kubernetes API calls (get/list secrets, describe nodes, etc.) from service accounts making requests outside their declared RBAC roles. Flag bulk API queries from container runtimes.

suggestion.title: WP Maps Pro Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Critical WP Maps Pro Flaw Actively Exploited'—pipeline produced no use case to detect attempts against this named vulnerability. Needs detection of requests to vulnerable plugin endpoints, malformed parameters, or known CVE-specific payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests targeting WP Maps Pro plugin paths (/wp-content/plugins/wp-maps-pro/) with indicators of exploitation: unusual query parameters, shell metacharacters in POST bodies, or known malicious payloads. Alert on 4xx errors (failed exploits) and subsequent 2xx with admin-creation patterns.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized WordPress Admin Account Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly documents impact as 'Create Admin Accounts'—pipeline generated no persistence detection. This is the post-exploitation success criterion and should be monitored across WordPress logs and database activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on wp_users table INSERT/UPDATE operations creating users with role='administrator' that don't match deployment windows or approved user lists. Correlate with WP Maps Pro exploitation events within 10 minutes. Look for accounts created outside business hours or from non-administrative IP ranges.

suggestion.title: WordPress Plugin File Write/Execution Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Active exploitation of WP Maps Pro likely involves file system modification (upload, shell write, or code injection). Pipeline missed detection of file operations within plugin directory that precede admin account creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file system events (write, modify, execute) in /wp-content/plugins/wp-maps-pro/ or /wp-content/uploads/ directories, especially .php files or suspicious archives. Correlate temporal clustering of file writes + HTTP requests + database admin inserts as high-confidence exploitation chain.

suggestion.title: WordPress User Enumeration / Reconnaissance via WP Maps Pro
suggestion.rationale: Pre-exploitation reconnaissance often involves enumerating plugin existence, version, and endpoint discovery. Pipeline missed detection of probing activity that precedes successful account creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect repeated 404s or 403s for /wp-content/plugins/wp-maps-pro/* endpoints, followed by successful requests to a specific endpoint 5-20 times, then POST requests with malicious payloads. Baseline: normal usage should not probe plugin directory structure repeatedly.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Activity: Newly Created Admin Account Usage
suggestion.rationale: Admin account creation is persistence; follow-on activity (login, privilege use, content modification) indicates confirmed compromise. Pipeline missed post-success detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on first login from a newly created admin account within 30 minutes of account creation, especially if the login originates from an IP address different from the exploitation source IP. Flag any WordPress configuration or plugin changes made by accounts created outside standard provisioning.

suggestion.title: SQL Injection in WP Maps Pro Parameters
suggestion.rationale: Unnamed WP plugin flaws often exploit parameter validation. Article hints at SQL-level exploitation ('create admin accounts' implies database modification). Pipeline generated no injection detection use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect SQL syntax in HTTP request parameters targeting WP Maps Pro endpoints (e.g., map_id, location, user_input fields). Monitor database logs for unexpected INSERT/UPDATE to wp_users from non-admin connection IPs. Flag queries containing UNION, OR '1'='1', or prepared statement bypass patterns.

suggestion.title: Malicious Package Installation via Composer/PHP Package Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'hiding malware inside a legitimate PHP package available through Packagist.' No UC detects unexpected composer install commands, suspicious dependency additions, or installation of the 'roberts/leads' package family.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect composer install/update/require commands pulling packages from non-standard repositories or newly-created package sources. Alert on installations of 'roberts/*' packages or unusual version pins to pre-release/dev versions from Packagist. Monitor for rapid package version updates to the same package within short time windows.

suggestion.title: PHP Config File Execution from Vendor/Package Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article describes payload 'disguising a dangerous payload as a routine configuration file.' No UC detects PHP interpreter executing config-like files (.conf, .config, .php) from vendor/ or package installation directories with suspicious parameters.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on php.exe or php CLI executing files with config-like extensions from composer vendor directories. Monitor for php -c <path>, php -r, or similar config/runtime flags pointing to recently-installed package paths. Correlate with recent composer activity on the same host.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Package Repository Account Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack using 'legitimate PHP package' indicating repo account takeover or maintainer compromise. No UC hunts for suspicious GitHub/Packagist account activity, permission changes, or new collaborators added to trusted packages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub audit logs for: password resets on package maintainer accounts, new SSH/OAuth keys added, collaborators added to trusted repositories, or rapid release of versions (especially to 'stable' tag after dormancy). Flag email address changes or account recovery attempts on packages with >100k downloads.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Composer Dependency Graph Changes
suggestion.rationale: Attack 'blends in easily with normal development workflows' through malicious dependency injection. No UC detects unusual changes to composer.json: new repositories, version downgrades to malicious releases, or lock file inconsistencies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect modifications to composer.json that introduce new repository sources outside packagist.org or downgrade package versions below latest stable. Compare installed versions in composer.lock against known-good hashes published in Packagist metadata. Alert on lock file changes that don't correspond to manual composer commands.

suggestion.title: Chollima Developer-Targeting Activity Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly attributes attack to 'Chollima Hackers' and states attack 'targets PHP developers.' Pipeline failed to attribute Chollima/Lazarus and missed UC for detecting targeting of developer toolchains and IDEs by this actor.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference internal developer machines (git/IDE activity) against external IP geolocation and C2 beacon patterns known to be associated with Lazarus/Chollima (DPRK infrastructure). Alert on social engineering or phishing attempts directed at developer communities on GitHub, Stack Overflow, or PHP forums mentioning 'roberts/leads' package.

suggestion.title: Password Reset Code Distribution via Chatbot Social Engineering
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers trick the chatbot into 'forwarding password reset codes with no verification required'—a detectable pattern of abnormal account recovery issuance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for multiple password reset code requests for the same account within a short window, or reset codes issued followed by immediate login from anomalous IP/device. Flag chatbot interaction logs for patterns of repeated account recovery queries against distinct accounts from the same session.

suggestion.title: Account Access Immediately Following Forced Password Reset
suggestion.rationale: Article describes hijacking of 'high-value accounts' after obtaining reset codes—legitimate password resets are typically initiated by the owner, not followed by immediate remote login.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate password reset events (AADAuditLogs, action='Reset user password') with successful login within 5 minutes from a different IP/user agent. Flag where the reset was not initiated by the account owner (check RequestInitiator field).

suggestion.title: Chatbot-Mediated Credential Exfiltration Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article describes the vulnerability as existing in 'AI-powered account recovery tool'—attackers are using conversational manipulation against a security control, detectable as anomalous dialogue patterns requesting sensitive recovery data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Log all chatbot interactions requesting account recovery or password reset. Detect prompts that explicitly ask for reset codes, repeated requests for same account, or attempts to bypass security questions (e.g., 'ignore verification and send code directly').

suggestion.title: Geographic Mismatch: Account Recovery Initiated vs. Successful Use
suggestion.rationale: Article implies attacker-initiated account hijacking, which would manifest as password reset requested from one country/IP and account accessed from another within minutes—a classic post-compromise anomaly.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlation hunt: where password reset is initiated from IP#1 in geography#1 and a successful login occurs within 10 minutes from IP#2 in geography#2. Raise confidence if the account's historical login pattern contradicts geography#2.

suggestion.title: SSPR Reset Attempts Using Unverified Directory Contact Methods Post-Policy
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly: 'removing reliance on directory-stored contact information that has not been formally verified.' Pipeline should flag this closed attack surface and recommend hunting for attackers still attempting bypass via unverified phone/email fields after policy deployment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SSPR password reset requests that attempt to use unverified directory contact information (auto-populated phone or email) rather than explicitly registered authentication methods. Post-policy, legitimate users cannot use this path; any such attempts indicate attack or misconfiguration.

suggestion.title: Spike in SSPR Authentication Failures After Policy Enforcement
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'stricter authentication requirements designed to reduce identity-based attacks' and 'mandates use of explicitly registered authentication methods.' Pipeline should baseline pre-policy SSPR behavior and flag anomalous post-policy authentication failure patterns as potential attackers adapting to new controls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of normal SSPR authentication failures before policy deployment. Flag sustained elevation in failed SSPR reset attempts post-deployment, particularly concentrated on specific user populations, as likely attack retries against new authentication requirements.

suggestion.title: Policy Enforcement Validation: SSPR Resets Without Registered Auth Method Verification
suggestion.rationale: Article mandates 'explicitly registered authentication methods' as sole acceptable SSPR path. Pipeline should recommend compliance hunt to verify policy actually rejects unregistered methods—any successful resets bypassing registered-auth enforcement indicates implementation gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query for successful SSPR password resets where authentication method used does NOT match organization's registered-methods allowlist. Any hits indicate policy not enforced, misconfiguration, or account compromise enabling policy bypass.

suggestion.title: Website Compromise → Malware Redirect Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'compromising thousands of legitimate websites to push malware' — this is the initial vector — but no hunt addresses detection of compromised-site redirects. Gap in initial access visibility.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web servers for unusual outbound HTTP redirects to attacker-controlled domains, especially rare TLDs (.icu, .cfd, .bond). Correlate 4xx/5xx spike patterns on legitimate sites with downstream phishing/malware delivery to external IPs from the IOC list.

suggestion.title: Fake Browser Update Masquerading
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'fake browser update pages' used as infection vector, but uc_phish_link and uc_fakecaptcha only catch post-click behavior. Need pre-click detection of update impersonation in HTML content.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTML pages masquerading as Chrome/Firefox/Edge update prompts: look for update-themed language, version-bump UI patterns, false 'Update Required' overlays, and download buttons pointing to attacker domains or IP infrastructure (91.92.240.127, 46.226.166.57 etc).

suggestion.title: Clipboard Manipulation → Command Execution Sequence
suggestion.rationale: uc_fakecaptcha detects spawned PowerShell from explorer.exe but misses the clipboard-injection vector that T1204.004 describes. Need to detect clipboard writes preceding execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Sequence detection: browser or web UI process → clipboard write → system utility (explorer, RuntimeBroker, ctfmon) → spawns (powershell, cmd, mshta) with network/code-exec payload within 5 seconds. This isolates malicious copy-paste from legitimate clipboard use.

suggestion.title: Installation of Malicious npm Package codexui-android
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'codexui-android npm Supply Chain Attack' — pipeline must flag installation of this package and variants across development environments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm install, npm ci, or yarn add execution for package 'codexui-android' or registry entries referencing this name. Correlate with timeline of environment variable access and outbound connections to attacker infrastructure during/immediately after install.

suggestion.title: OpenAI Token Exfiltration via npm Postinstall Hooks
suggestion.rationale: Article states tokens were stolen post-supply-chain compromise — this indicates malicious postinstall scripts or dependencies enumerating/exfiltrating OPENAI_API_KEY and related credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child processes spawned by npm/node that enumerate environment variables, read credential files (~/.openai, ~/.config/openai, OPENAI_* env vars), or perform base64-encoded outbound connections during package installation. Flag postinstall scripts with obfuscated code or subprocess spawning.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Package Metadata Changes on npm Registry
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attack implies package was poisoned or hijacked on npm registry — detection should flag codexui-android versions with unexpected maintainer changes, new dependencies, or rapid version escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on version publishes of 'codexui-android' by new or unexpected maintainers, packages with unexpected transitive dependency injections, or version bumps with significant code changes within 24h of publication. Cross-correlate with npm-audit vulnerability disclosures.

suggestion.title: Outbound Network Connections from npm Package Code
suggestion.rationale: Token exfiltration requires attacker-controlled destination — detection should capture suspicious outbound connections initiated by node.js during package postinstall or runtime, especially to non-standard or suspicious domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag network connections from node.js child processes to external domains during npm install. Alert on connections using curl, wget, or native HTTP clients from postinstall scripts. Correlate IP addresses against threat-intel feeds for known exfiltration infrastructure.

suggestion.title: CodeX/OpenAI Token Usage from Unexpected Sources Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Stolen tokens will be used by attacker — detection should identify unusual API consumption patterns or token auth from IPs/geographic locations inconsistent with organization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor OpenAI API logs for Codex-model requests or token usage from IPs/geographic zones outside the organization's known footprint. Alert on request volume spikes post-npm-install. Correlate authentication failures followed by successful token reuse, or token usage in non-development APIs (e.g., production vs. dev-only services).

suggestion.title: Netlogon RPC Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is triggered via 'specially crafted' network packets; detection must identify malformed or anomalous Netlogon RPC protocol traffic to domain controllers from untrusted sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for RPC calls to Netlogon service (port 445, RPC endpoint mapper) from non-domain-controller sources with suspicious packet structures, large payloads, or repeated failed/error responses that match known CVE-2026-41089 exploitation signatures.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Process Spawning from Netlogon Service Context (lsass.exe)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'execute arbitrary code with SYSTEM-level privileges'; attacker will spawn shells, scripts, or backdoors as children of lsass/netlogon processes to maintain execution context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag process creation with parent=lsass.exe (netlogon context) spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, wmic.exe, or other command interpreters, particularly with suspicious command-line arguments or network connections. Legitimate netlogon operations do not spawn user shells.

suggestion.title: Domain Controller Lateral Movement Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Compromised domain controller becomes a pivot point for attacker to move laterally across the domain; article states vulnerability 'now actively exploited in the wild' and affects domain controllers, implying attacker persistence and movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect new outbound RDP (port 3389) or WinRM (port 5985/5986) sessions originating from domain controllers to unusual targets, especially to non-server systems or outside the datacenter. Establish baseline of normal DC-to-system communication and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Domain Controller Service Instability During Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation attempts may destabilize or crash the Netlogon service; detection should flag abnormal service lifecycle events on domain controllers to catch exploitation attempts or failed attacks in progress.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Netlogon service (lsass.exe or netlogon-related processes) crashes, emergency restarts, or resource spikes on domain controllers, especially when paired with network anomalies or suspicious process creation from system services.

suggestion.title: Detect Botnet C2 Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Article describes botnet affecting 17 million devices—requires active command-and-control communication to coordinate and command infected hosts. Pipeline extracted zero detections for C2 callbacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound connections from internal endpoints to known/suspected C2 infrastructure using suspicious timing (periodic beaconing), non-standard ports, or encrypted channels. Correlate frequency and destination patterns to identify hosts exhibiting command-and-control behaviors inconsistent with legitimate applications.

suggestion.title: Detect Botnet Malware Execution
suggestion.rationale: 17 million infections imply widespread code execution; article title signals active malware deployment. Pipeline failed to suggest execution-phase detections for suspicious process spawning or script injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify process execution chains where system utilities spawn unsigned or untrusted child processes, script interpreters (PowerShell, cmd.exe, wscript) invoke obfuscated payloads, or parent processes are network-accessible. Flag execution from temporary or user-writable directories.

suggestion.title: Detect Botnet Persistence via Registry and Autostart
suggestion.rationale: Botnets persist across reboots via Run keys, startup folders, or scheduled tasks. Article title implies sustained compromise of 17 million devices; pipeline generated zero persistence-layer detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor modifications to HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run[Once] and HKCU equivalents, Windows\Start Menu\Startup folders, and scheduled task creation. Flag registry entries pointing to Temp/AppData, new tasks with random names, and modifications by non-admin or service accounts during off-hours.

suggestion.title: Detect WP Maps Pro AJAX Exploitation via check_temp Parameter
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'When the request is made with a check_temp parameter set to false, the function creates a new WordPress user.' This is the direct exploit trigger and is detectable via HTTP request inspection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to WP Maps Pro AJAX endpoints containing check_temp=false. Alert on requests from unauthenticated contexts or without valid session tokens. Correlate against known vendor IP ranges to exclude legitimate support access.

suggestion.title: Detect Admin User Creation with Hardcoded support@flippercode.com Email
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'hardcoded email address support@flippercode.com' is assigned when wp_insert_user() creates the admin account. This email is a direct, high-confidence persistence indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any wordpress user_register hook or wp_insert_user() call assigning administrator role with email domain 'flippercode.com' or exact match 'support@flippercode.com'. This is a strong attacker signature.

suggestion.title: Detect Unauthorized Administrator Account Creation Without Admin Action
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'randomly generated username' with 'administrator role' created by the AJAX function. The combination of auto-generated username + admin role + missing authentication context is anomalous.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal admin account creation patterns. Alert on new administrator-role users created with non-human-generated usernames without preceding admin user interaction logs (no user invitations, no admin panel submissions, no credential provisioning requests).

suggestion.title: Detect Magic Passwordless Login URL Generation and Usage
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'generates a magic login URL using generate_login_link(), stores it as user meta, and returns it in the response body.' Then 'Once the attacker visits this URL, they are automatically authenticated.' These login events are detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for WordPress login events that bypass normal password validation (e.g., direct session creation, token-based auth outside normal flow). Correlate with usermeta containing generate_login_link() output patterns or magic-link tokens.

suggestion.title: Detect WP Maps Pro Vulnerability (CVE-2026-8732) via Plugin Version Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'impacts WP Maps Pro versions 6.1.0 and older' with fix in '6.1.1'. Vulnerable versions are directly detectable and should trigger prioritized investigation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate WordPress plugin versions via wp-content/plugins directory or database queries. Flag any WP Maps Pro version ≤6.1.0 as CVE-2026-8732 vulnerable. Cross-correlate with AJAX endpoint access logs to identify exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Detect Frontend-Only Nonce Validation Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies vulnerability: 'nonce check in frontend JavaScript, rendering the protection ineffective.' Requests bypassing or repeating nonces, or missing nonce parameters, are evasion indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor AJAX requests to WP Maps Pro endpoints for missing, invalid, or reused nonce parameters. Detect POST requests that omit wp_nonce fields entirely. Flag repeat nonce values across multiple distinct requests as potential nonce exhaustion or bypass attempts.

suggestion.title: Docker Hub Poisoned Image Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'poisoning a Docker Hub repository to later steal Kubernetes secrets' and 'tainted images distributed a stealer that was loaded during the KICS scanning process.' No use case captures malicious container image distribution vectors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor container image pulls from public registries (Docker Hub) followed by immediate process execution of known scanning tools (KICS, others). Correlate image pull events with unexpected child processes spawned by container runtime. Alert on image digests not matching trusted sigstore signatures.

suggestion.title: Linux Capability Exploitation in Privileged Container
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_SYS_MODULE, CAP_SYS_PTRACE, CAP_NET_ADMIN as vectors and states these enable 'container escape followed by host compromise.' No use case detects capability-based privilege escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on container processes calling prctl(PR_SET_NAME), loading kernel modules (requires CAP_SYS_MODULE), or ptrace operations (CAP_SYS_PTRACE). Monitor seccomp violations and capabilities not filtered by pod security policy. Detect /proc/sys writes from container processes.

suggestion.title: Kubernetes Secrets Exfiltration via Orchestration API
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'steal Kubernetes secrets and other sensitive data' and 'orchestration API abuse' as primary vectors. No detection use case covers abnormal API access to secrets store.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for list/get/watch requests to secrets API from service accounts outside expected namespaces. Alert when non-privileged service accounts request secret objects. Track unusual patterns: repeated secret queries from containers, exfiltration of multiple secret resources in short window, or secret access from compromised pod.

suggestion.title: Privileged Container Creation and Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article discusses 'privileged containers' and CAP_* capabilities as escape vectors. No use case detects privileged container instantiation in non-allowlisted scenarios.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on pod creation with securityContext.privileged=true or any capability in the 'add' field not matching organization security baseline. Monitor docker run/podman run with --privileged or --cap-add flags outside change-control windows. Baseline normal privileged container use and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Container Escape to Host: Abnormal Host Access from Container
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'container escape followed by host compromise' as primary vector. Requires detection of escape attempts such as mounting host filesystem or accessing host devices.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect attempts to mount host filesystem paths (/etc, /proc, /sys, /) inside container. Monitor for open/read syscalls on /dev/* from within container. Alert on processes spawned from container's init process that show host-level PIDs or access host cgroup files. Track successful namespace escape detection.

suggestion.title: Stealer Malware in Container Build/Runtime
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'stealer that was loaded during the KICS scanning process' as malware distribution via compromised supply chain. No use case detects credential-stealing behavior in container context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In container context, alert on execution of unknown binaries during image build phases, especially after image pull. Monitor for file reads of known secret locations (/.dockercfg, /run/secrets, /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io) or environment variable enumeration. Detect exfiltration of kubeconfig or auth tokens outside normal container egress.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Admin Account Creation via WP Maps Pro Plugin
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'actively exploited to create admin accounts' — this is the direct impact and persistence mechanism. Must detect account creation originating from plugin endpoints without valid admin session. Article phrase: 'Critical WP Maps Pro Flaw Actively Exploited to Create Admin Accounts'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WordPress wp_users table INSERT or REST API POST to /wp-json/wp/v2/users where: source lacks valid admin Authorization header, request originates from unauthenticated context, and payload includes role='administrator'. Correlate with POST requests to WP Maps Pro plugin paths lacking session authentication.

suggestion.title: Exploitation of Unauthenticated WP Maps Pro Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability requires attack surface — unauthenticated endpoint in plugin that permits privilege escalation. Must detect exploitation attempts at entry point. Article phrase: 'actively exploited'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to /wp-content/plugins/wp-maps-pro/* endpoints or REST API routes exposed by plugin. Flag requests from non-authenticated sources that trigger database writes to wp_users or wp_usermeta tables, or requests with payloads containing user creation/role elevation parameters.

suggestion.title: Suspicious WordPress User Role Elevation to Administrator
suggestion.rationale: Privilege escalation occurs when user role is set to admin via vulnerability. Need detection independent of account creation method to catch role elevation attempts. Represents T1548 (Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect wp_usermeta UPDATE/INSERT operations setting user capability 'administrator' to true or wp_users table role elevation, sourced from unauthenticated HTTP requests or non-admin plugin operations. Alert on multiple user role elevations within short window (batch privilege escalation).

suggestion.title: Newly Created Admin Account First Login from Suspicious Source
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation validation — attacker will test newly-created admin account. Should correlate account creation event with immediate login attempt from same/different region or time-of-day anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate wp_users INSERT (new admin account) with subsequent wp-login.php POST requests using new admin username within 1-10 minutes. Flag if login source IP differs from exploitation source IP, is non-residential/VPN, or creates admin panel session immediately after account creation.

suggestion.title: WP Maps Pro Plugin File or Database Configuration Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Attacker may modify plugin files or options post-exploitation for persistence or lateral movement. Should detect plugin directory/database modifications correlated with exploitation pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file writes to /wp-content/plugins/wp-maps-pro/main files or wp_options table modifications for plugin settings occurring after exploitation attempts. Alert on unauthorized plugin code changes or addition of hooks/filters outside normal update windows.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Package Installation from Packagist Repository
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'malware inside a legitimate PHP package available through Packagist' and that the payload was 'disguised as a routine configuration file' — attackers compromised the package manager itself as the distribution vector. Detect installation of the known-bad package name or unusual Composer/PHP package manager activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Composer install/update commands and composer.lock modifications for the package name 'roberts/leads' or related suspicious namespaces. Alert on Packagist package installations with mismatched hash signatures, unexpected dependency additions, or package metadata anomalies. Correlate with developer environment baselines.

suggestion.title: Configuration File Execution via PHP Interpreter
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes malware 'disguising a dangerous payload as a routine configuration file' — the attack hides executable code in .conf, .config, or similar files to evade detection. Detect PHP interpreter execution of configuration files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on php.exe or php-cgi executing from or reading .conf, .config, .json, or vendor/ directory paths. Flag process creation when PHP interprets files in configuration directories. Monitor for unusual environment variables or arguments passed to PHP from package installation workflows.

suggestion.title: File Hash Detection — Chollima Malware SHA256
suggestion.rationale: Article provides two SHA256 hashes as technical indicators of the malicious payload. Implement hash-based detection to catch the specific malware variants.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation or execution matching hashes 522b28a2f78771715497ba53729d4ab9a50e982322c391379f3bddf7c8cb363f or 96afdba882046385242cbed46871e41147c8055c5d9eff7460847b2c01a77dc3. Flag any endpoint with these files present, executed, or loaded into memory. Correlate with recent Composer install activity on same host.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Package Dependency Anomaly Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack targeting 'PHP developers' via package distribution — the attack succeeds when legitimate package dependencies are compromised. Detect unusual Composer lock file changes, unexpected version pinning, or dependency downgrades.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for modifications to composer.lock or composer.json files containing suspicious package names, unexpected version changes, or new repository sources. Alert on Composer install/update executed immediately after lock file changes. Baseline against known development workflows to reduce false positives.

suggestion.title: GitHub Malicious Repository Account Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 'github.com/roberts/leads' as a source repository — the attacker-controlled GitHub account hosts or distributes the malicious package. Monitor for activity from compromised developer accounts or suspicious repository patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on clones, pulls, or Composer installs directly from suspicious GitHub accounts or repositories with minimal commit history, unusual naming patterns, or typosquatting indicators. Flag developers pulling from non-canonical repository sources for well-known packages.

suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Network connections to article IPs / domains' hunt with high confidence; provides 11 IPv4 addresses and 4 domains as attack infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound connections to the 11 provided IPv4 addresses (31.172.87.20, 212.83.61.213, 66.85.26.183, 195.20.17.129, 46.246.125.131, 146.70.233.83, 91.193.19.198, 89.36.231.56, 84.200.89.52, 46.30.190.173, 45.150.108.61) and 4 domains (nefeshhope.com, members.nefeshhope.com, feedback.nefeshhope.com, banujcobaar.com). suggestion.title: Malware execution - File hash detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match' hunt; provides 7 SHA256 hashes as confirmed destructive malware payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for execution or file creation matching the 7 provided SHA256 hashes (81a25357d027d0f04a43139377d5d58384b8e9b0770e699cdcc37e600641cf90, c8cc4225d1e21324ef419adbb1c10dd0578fb034b5f5d7b8000f0aae1871c061, and 5 others). These are obfuscated destructive malware payloads implemented via T1027.

suggestion.title: Backup system destruction - Inhibit System Recovery
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes primary attack objective: 'erasing backups, and dismantling recovery infrastructure' and 'left victims with little ability to restore their [systems]'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for deletion or disabling of backup infrastructure including VSS snapshots, shadow copy deletion, backup application process termination, and recovery partition access/modification. Attackers systematically destroy recovery capabilities as primary objective.

suggestion.title: System partition and data wipe operations
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'wiping IT systems' and 'leaving victims with little ability to restore' — indicates destructive impact operations not covered by C2 or hash templates.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of disk wipe utilities, large-scale file deletion operations, or low-level disk write commands. Correlate high-volume file deletion events across multiple systems and critical partitions, indicating coordinated destructive operations.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated malware behavioral analysis
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1027 (Obfuscated Files or Information) as confirmed technique; behavioral signatures required beyond hash-based detection to catch obfuscated variants and similar malware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Analyze the 7 provided SHA256 malware hashes for obfuscation patterns (packing, string encoding, control flow obfuscation). Establish behavioral detection rules distinct from hash-only matching to detect obfuscated variants and similar malware implementing backup/system destruction.

suggestion.title: Network connections to article domains (C2 IOCs)
suggestion.rationale: Article lists six C2 domains with geographic targeting across US, Israel, UAE. Pipeline missed all of them. Maps directly to command-and-control kill-chain phase and article's stated vector: 'Iranian hackers...deployed...to target organizations.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DNS queries and network connections to buisness-centeral-transportation.com, premierhealthadvisory.com, ramiltonsfinance.com, business-startup.org, docspace-y4cumb.onlyoffice.com, docspace-twpf0e.onlyoffice.com. Establish baseline for legitimate onlyoffice traffic; flag typosquatted business domains as high-priority. Correlate with process execution of known malware hashes.

suggestion.title: File hash IOCs — install-phase malware detection
suggestion.rationale: Thirteen SHA256 hashes provided for malware samples. Pipeline ignored all. Critical for endpoint blocking and forensic hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation or process execution matching any of the 13 provided SHA256 hashes. Prioritize creation in temp directories, AppData, or Windows System paths. Correlate file hash detections with suspicious child-process spawning, network connections to C2 domains, or AppDomain manipulations.

suggestion.title: AppDomainManager Hijacking Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly centers on 'sophisticated .NET hijacking technique' and 'AppDomainManager hijacking to evade EDR.' This is the novel technique that differentiates the campaign, yet pipeline generated zero execution-phase detection for it. From article: 'deployed a sophisticated .NET hijacking technique to slip past endpoint defenses.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect AppDomainManager initialization by monitoring CLR profiler environment variables (COR_PROFILER, COR_PROFILER_PATH), registry writes to HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\.NETFramework, and AppDomain.CreateDomain() calls with untrusted AppDomainManager classes. Flag legitimate .NET processes (csc.exe, msbuild.exe, powershell.exe) loading unsigned or obfuscated assemblies from non-standard paths.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion via .NET Runtime Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Article's core claim: technique 'to evade EDR detection.' Pipeline missed the behavioral evasion layer entirely. Must detect process injection and CLR hooking that bypasses security sensors. From article: 'evade endpoint defenses.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Reflection.Emit(), Assembly.Load() with byte arrays, or DynamicMethod invocation in unexpected process contexts. Alert on process injection into .NET hosts (notepad.exe, calc.exe) or modification of CLR internals via unsafe P/Invoke. Detect EDR sensor queries or hook bypasses (e.g., direct syscalls, kernel callbacks disabled).

suggestion.title: Obfuscated .NET Malware + Outbound Communications
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly invokes T1027 (Obfuscation) combined with targeted C2 communications. Pipeline assigned both techniques to IOC hunts but missed behavioral correlation. From article: 'Obfuscated Files or Information' feeding into the six campaign domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate detection of obfuscated .NET binaries (high entropy, reflective method invocation, IL obfuscation markers) with outbound connections to typosquatted or newly-registered domains. Prioritize cases where binary matches article IOC hashes. Establish baseline for legitimate obfuscated .NET (license checks, telemetry, legitimate vendor tools) to reduce FP.

suggestion.title: PowerShell Assembly Loading + MITRE Technique T1059.001 Missing
suggestion.rationale: AppDomainManager campaigns typically deliver via PowerShell cradle + Assembly.Load(). Pipeline lists T1059.001 nowhere despite no evidence it was excluded. From article: delivery mechanism unstated but implied spear-phishing to target 'organizations across...United States, Israel, and the United Arab Emirates' suggests scripted initial execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PowerShell execution (encoded or plaintext) that loads .NET assemblies via Assembly.Load(), Assembly.LoadFrom(), or LoadFile(). Flag base64-encoded commands with entropy > 6.5. Alert on suspicious registry queries for .NETFramework paths or APPDOMAIN creation within PowerShell context. Correlate with C2 IOC domains in command line.

suggestion.title: npm Package Installation from Suspicious Registry or Trojan Version
suggestion.rationale: Article describes packages with compromised versions available in registry; no detection for installation of redhat-cloud-services packages from non-official sources or installation of known-malicious versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm/yarn install operations for redhat-cloud-services packages. Alert on installation from registries other than registry.npmjs.org, installation of versions matching known IOC lists, or installs with package.json pointing to GitHub/GitLab repositories instead of registry.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Spawning from node_modules Directory
suggestion.rationale: Malicious npm packages execute arbitrary code during install-time or require-time; no detection for unexpected child processes created by node/npm with CWD or executable path containing node_modules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation where parent is node.exe/npm.cmd and child executable resides in node_modules/.[bin] or similar. Flag execution of curl, wget, python, bash, or powershell spawned from package directories outside of legitimate build scripts.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Network Egress from npm/Node Process to Non-CDN Domains
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain malware typically establishes C2 or exfiltrates data; no detection for outbound connections from Node.js processes to domains outside npm registry, known CDNs, and corporate whitelists.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate network connections initiated by node.exe/npm processes against whitelist (registry.npmjs.org, *.npmjs.com, known CDNs). Alert on connections to newly registered domains, IP addresses, or non-standard ports (8080, 9000, 4444). Escalate if correlated with suspicious process spawning.

suggestion.title: Package.json or Lockfile Modification Outside VCS
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks inject malicious dependencies or pin compromised versions; no detection for unexpected changes to package.json, package-lock.json, or yarn.lock files that don't match git history.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package.json and lockfile write operations outside of CI/CD pipelines. Alert on version downgrades to known-compromised versions, addition of new dependencies not in version control, or modification timestamps that precede the parent commit.

suggestion.title: Installation of Typosquatted or Masqueraded redhat-cloud-services Package
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain compromise often uses naming similarity to legitimate packages (e.g., redhat-cloud-service vs redhat-cloud-services); no detection for installation of look-alike packages or packages with suspicious metadata.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm installs for package names with Levenshtein distance < 2 from known legitimate packages or with suspicious maintainer metadata (brand-new accounts, no activity history). Flag installation of any redhat-* package not published by official Red Hat accounts.

suggestion.title: Malicious npm Package Installation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'codexui-android npm Supply Chain Attack' — pipeline must monitor for installation of known-malicious packages by hash, name pattern, or checksum deviation from registry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install/update operations and compare package checksums against threat intel feeds. Flag installations of 'codexui-android' or packages with abnormally recent first-seen dates, mismatched maintainer accounts, or zero historical GitHub stars. Cross-reference against known-good package manifests.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized OpenAI API Token Access from Non-Expected Contexts
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'OpenAI Codex Authentication Tokens Stolen' — pipeline must detect when API tokens stored in app memory/disk are accessed by unexpected processes, especially third-party libraries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on patterns where a process spawned by npm/Android runtime reads files or memory locations known to contain OpenAI API tokens, or where token strings appear in unexpected process arguments, environment variables, or network payloads.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of Authentication Tokens to Non-API Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Title 'tokens stolen' indicates exfiltration phase — pipeline must detect when credentials leave app context to unauthorized domains, not just legitimate OpenAI endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag network connections initiated by the codexui-android package (or any Android app process) to non-OpenAI IP ranges or domains transmitting strings matching OpenAI API token regex patterns. Baseline legitimate OpenAI API FQDN and alert on anomalies.

suggestion.title: Android App Dynamic Library Injection for Credential Hooking
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain compromises often inject code to intercept authentication calls — monitor for unusual library loading patterns in apps using codexui-android.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected native library loads (*.so, *.dll) into Android processes that reference OpenAI or authentication APIs. Compare app's declared libraries against runtime-loaded libraries; alert on discrepancies or LoadLibrary calls to unsigned/unsigned-by-declared-app resources.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Package Repository Tampering Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article is npm supply chain attack — look for indicators of repo compromise: abnormal version jumps, republished older versions, unexpected maintainer changes, or install-time hook modifications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference package.json lockfiles against npm registry for mismatches: version was X, but npm now shows Y. Monitor for install scripts, preinstall hooks, or postinstall hooks added in recent versions of popular packages. Alert on packages with duplicate/near-duplicate names (typosquatting).

suggestion.title: Bulk API Credential Usage Anomalies Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Once tokens are stolen, attacker will use them — detect abnormal API call patterns from stolen credentials: high request volume, unusual endpoints, IPs outside organization, concurrent usage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on OpenAI API access from IPs not in org's ASN, geographic regions not matching user location, unusual API endpoints (e.g., code-completion called 1000x in 1 min), or multiple stolen tokens used in parallel. Correlate with theft timestamp if known.

suggestion.title: XenoRAT file-hash detection — endpoint quarantine
suggestion.rationale: Nine SHA256 hashes provided in IOC section; pipeline extracted zero. Each hash should trigger automatic quarantine/alert. Phrase: '9 SHA256' IOCs listed in article.

suggestion.title: Spear-phishing campaign to Afghan finance ministry officials

suggestion.title: Persistence mechanism installation — scheduled tasks, registry run keys
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states XenoRAT provides 'persistent' access but no hunt for persistence methods provided. Phrase: 'persistent remote access tool called XenoRAT'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor creation of scheduled tasks or registry modifications under HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run by non-system processes. Alert on suspicious scheduled task creation with command-line arguments containing file hashes from IOC list or IP addresses from article.

suggestion.title: C2 beaconing to article-specified infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Three IPs (185.235.137.106, 103.132.98.224, 103.132.98.226) and domain abimj.edu.af listed as C2 but only generic IOC-substitution hunt referenced (template not shown). Custom behavioral detection needed for XenoRAT's known beacon patterns.

Monitor for XenoRAT-typical HTTP User-Agent strings or TLS certificate fingerprints if available. Correlate with process execution of files matching IOC hash list.

suggestion.title: Defense evasion — packed/obfuscated executable detection
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1027 (Obfuscated Files) but provides no detection logic. Hash IOCs suggest packed delivery mechanism needs entropy/packer signature detection.

Cross-reference file hashes against YARA rules for XenoRAT variants. Alert when packed executables are executed by non-admin users or from unusual locations.

suggestion.title: Post-compromise data collection and exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Finance ministry RAT deployment strongly implies secondary objectives (credential theft, financial data exfiltration) but not explicitly addressed in kill-chain. Operational context implies collection phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-XenoRAT deployment, hunt for child processes spawned by beaconing network service: LSASS access (credential dumping), bulk reads from %AppData%, Document folders, and finance-system directories (e.g., Oracle, SAP folders if present). Look for unusual archive creation or outbound data volumes shortly after XenoRAT process initialization.

suggestion.title: Botnet C2 Communication Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title indicates Dutch authorities dismantled a botnet; botnets by definition establish command-and-control channels. Pipeline extracted zero techniques related to C2. Expected phrases: 'command and control servers', 'C2 infrastructure', 'botnet communication'.

suggestion.title: Mass Botnet Lateral Propagation

suggestion.title: Botnet Persistence Installation
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline extracted zero persistence-phase techniques. Botnet persistence is core to 17M device compromise. Expected phrases: 'persistence mechanism', 'auto-start', 'registry modification', 'scheduled task'.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Data Exfiltration by Botnet

suggestion.title: Known Botnet Malware Execution

suggestion.title: Botnet Command Execution and Task Distribution

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated AJAX request to WP Maps Pro check_temp endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes vulnerability: 'AJAX endpoint used for this feature was accessible to unauthenticated users' relying on 'publicly exposed nonce check in frontend JavaScript'. Requests with check_temp=false should be detectable.

suggestion.title: Administrator user creation with hardcoded email support@flippercode.com

suggestion.title: Passwordless login link generation and redemption

suggestion.title: Multi-source exploitation attempts against WP Maps Pro plugin

suggestion.title: WP Maps Pro version 6.1.0 or older in production inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability in 'WP Maps Pro versions 6.1.0 and older' with patch released 'May 20' (version 6.1.1). Affected version identification is primary precursor control.

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect spear-phishing campaigns targeting Czech government and Taiwan critical infrastructure. Flag emails with suspicious attachments (Office macros, executables) and monitored credential submission to attacker-controlled forms.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Across Czech & Taiwan Networks
suggestion.rationale: Multi-country attacks (Czech Republic and Taiwan) imply intra-network propagation, but pipeline missed all lateral movement techniques and reconnaissance patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect living-off-the-land techniques (PsExec, WMI, PowerShell) used to move laterally. Monitor for enumeration of network shares, credential harvesting, and access to sensitive systems consistent with Chinese APT playbooks.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration from Czech & Taiwan Government/Critical Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: High-severity targeting of Czech Republic and Taiwan (geopolitically significant) implies espionage objectives, but pipeline extracted zero exfiltration channels or data staging indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual file transfers to external IP addresses, compression of large document sets, and encrypted exfiltration channels from Czech and Taiwan networks. Detect staging to cloud storage or web shells.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion - Living-off-the-Land and Code Signing Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Sophisticated Chinese APT groups employ defense evasion tactics; pipeline completely absent on this dimension despite article's high-severity classification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect abuse of Windows signed binaries (certutil, bitsadmin, mshta) and execution of unsigned/malformed-signature files. Monitor for parent-child process chains consistent with Dragon Weave's known execution patterns.

suggestion.title: Privileged Container Capabilities Detected
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly enumerates CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_SYS_MODULE, CAP_SYS_PTRACE, CAP_NET_ADMIN as 'exploitation vectors for container escape'; these are direct detection opportunities.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor container creation logs for dangerous Linux capability assignments (CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_SYS_MODULE, CAP_SYS_PTRACE, CAP_NET_ADMIN). Correlate with process namespace escape attempts or sysctl modifications targeting kernel modules.

suggestion.title: Supply-Chain Image Poisoning: Registry Integrity Violation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'poisoning a Docker Hub repository' to distribute stealer malware via Checkmarx KICS image. Detection needed for unauthorized image updates or manifest tampering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected changes to image tags, manifest digest mismatches vs. signed baseline, or pulls of images with abnormal layer history. Flag registry API authentication from non-CI/CD IPs or service accounts with excessive push permissions.

suggestion.title: Kubernetes Secrets Enumeration and Extraction
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'steal Kubernetes secrets' as core objective; requires detection of unauthorized Secret API access and environment variable exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Kubernetes audit logs for Secret list/get operations from service accounts without explicit secret read permissions, or from containers mounting secrets into env vars. Flag cross-namespace secret access.

suggestion.title: Container Escape via Host Kernel Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'container escape followed by host compromise' and 'exploiting host system vulnerabilities' as primary attack paths; requires syscall anomaly detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes spanning container→host namespace boundaries (parent cgroup=/docker/*, child cgroup=/), excessive ptrace syscalls from container processes, or uname/utsname modifications indicating namespace escape.

suggestion.title: Malware Execution During Image Scanning Pipeline
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies stealer malware 'loaded during the KICS scanning process'; supply-chain execution requires detection of unexpected child processes and exfiltration during image analysis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor KICS, Trivy, Snyk, and Grype processes for unexpected child spawning, outbound connections to suspicious IPs/domains during scan execution, or environment variable access patterns consistent with credential harvesting.

suggestion.title: Kubernetes API Abuse for Persistence and Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 'exploitation of orchestration APIs' as discrete attack vector; API abuse for rogue pod creation or RBAC escalation is detectable via audit logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Kubernetes API calls (create/patch pod, patch clusterrolebinding, create serviceaccount) from service accounts with abnormal scope, from IPs outside cluster CIDR, or with binding of admin roles to default accounts.

suggestion.title: WordPress Admin Account Creation via Plugin Vulnerability
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Actively Exploited to Create Admin Accounts'—core persistence indicator. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this being the primary impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WordPress user creation events in wp_users table (INSERT statements in database logs). Correlate with authentication logs showing no interactive login prior. Look for admin role assignment (wp_usermeta wp_capabilities meta_value containing 'administrator'). High-fidelity signal if creation timestamp within seconds of plugin exploitation attempt.

suggestion.title: WP Maps Pro Plugin Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article headline identifies WP Maps Pro as the attack vector—'critically' flawed, actively exploited. Kill chain should start here (T1190). Pipeline omitted entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to /wp-content/plugins/wp-maps-pro/ with suspicious path traversal, script injection, or unauthenticated API endpoints. Alert on POST/GET patterns to known vulnerable endpoints (e.g., /wp-maps-pro/ajax or version-specific paths). High confidence if request includes shell commands, base64 payloads, or ../ sequences.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution via Plugin
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline provided no kill-chain phases at all. Article describes 'actively exploited' scenario implying code execution before account creation—this is the exploitation phase, not derivative.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected process spawning from web server context (www-data, apache, nginx user). Detect writes to wp-content/plugins/wp-maps-pro/ and wp-content/uploads/ directories outside normal deployment windows. Look for PHP execution in upload directories or suspicious .htaccess modifications that enable script execution.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Upload or Backdoor Injection in WP Maps Pro
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation of plugin vulnerability must establish either transient RCE or persistent backdoor. Article does not exclude web shell as post-exploitation artifact. Pipeline generated zero detections for file system indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for new .php files created in wp-content/plugins/wp-maps-pro/, wp-content/, or wp-root with suspicious entropy or obfuscated function names. Baseline known plugin file hashes; alert on additions. Correlate file creation timestamp with HTTP request logs containing base64 or gzip payloads to plugin endpoints.

suggestion.title: Database Privilege Escalation to WordPress Admin
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Create Admin Accounts'—this requires INSERT into wp_users + UPDATE to wp_usermeta. Pipeline did not surface database-level detection. Article text describes high-confidence attack outcome.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SQL queries for INSERT statements against wp_users with admin role assignment in single transaction. Alert on INSERTs with hardcoded user_login, user_email, user_pass values (not from HTTP request params). Cross-reference with Web server logs—if INSERT timestamp aligns with unauthenticated HTTP request to plugin, confidence is high.

suggestion.title: Malicious Composer Package Installation - roberts/leads
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'malware inside a legitimate PHP package available through Packagist.' Package identifier roberts/leads is the attack vector but has zero dedicated hunt coverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for composer install/require/update commands targeting roberts/leads package. Alert on composer.lock or composer.json modifications adding this package. Detect process execution spawned from vendor/roberts/leads/ directory or execution of any file within that tree.

suggestion.title: Configuration File Disguise - Non-PHP Execution via PHP Interpreter
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'disguising a dangerous payload as a routine configuration file.' This obfuscation technique is not operationalized into any detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PHP process execution of files with config-like extensions (.json, .conf, .config, .env, .yaml) originating from vendor/ or node_modules/ directories. Monitor for php -r / php -f / require_once / include statements targeting non-.php files from package manager trees.

suggestion.title: Command & Control from Developer Environments Post-Package Install
suggestion.rationale: Article attributes to 'well-known North Korean threat actor' with implicit C2 capability; domain IOCs listed but no hunt explicitly targets post-compromise command exfiltration from affected developers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate composer/PHP package manager process execution with subsequent outbound network connections from the same user/host. Flag connections to non-standard ports or domains associated with attacker infrastructure. Alert on DNS queries from PHP processes or developer shells.

suggestion.title: Namespace-Based Package Supply Chain Hunt - roberts/* Scope
suggestion.rationale: Attacker uses 'roberts' namespace on both Packagist and GitHub. Hunting the full namespace surface could detect siblings or variants not yet identified.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web proxy logs and DNS for requests to packagist.org, github.com, raw.githubusercontent.com referencing roberts/* packages. Alert on installations of any package from roberts/ namespace not whitelisted by corporate policy. Flag git clone or composer require commands with roberts/ prefix.

suggestion.title: Obfuscation Patterns in PHP Package Payloads
suggestion.rationale: Article implies obfuscation (T1027 listed but not hunted). Configuration-file-as-payload suggests encoding/obfuscation. No detection exists for PHP deobfuscation techniques.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect base64_decode, gzinflate, gzuncompress, unserialize, eval, assert, create_function, or @exec patterns in PHP command lines or files from vendor directories. Monitor for non-printable/binary content in supposedly-text configuration files. Alert on shell metacharacters or encoded payloads in .json or .conf files.

suggestion.title: praisonai-platform: POST /workspaces/*/members with role=owner
suggestion.rationale: Core exploitation scenario. Article: 'The POST /workspaces/{workspace_id}/members endpoint is gated only by require_workspace_member(workspace_id)... and forwards the request body's user_id and role straight into MemberService.add(workspace_id, user_id, role), which has no caller-permission check.' — any workspace member can elevate arbitrary users to owner.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST requests to /workspaces/*/members returning 201 Created status, especially with role=owner in the request body. High-confidence indicator of exploitation by workspace members.

suggestion.title: praisonai-platform: owner-grant followed by login from granted account (identity-swap chain)
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation pattern. After successful privilege elevation via endpoint, attacker logs in using the newly-elevated account. Article's mention of member-injection implies this progression—granting access to attacker-controlled user, then immediately using that user.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate POST /workspaces/*/members (201 status, role=owner payload) with successful Authentication events from previously-unseen accounts to the same workspace within 60 minutes. Medium-confidence account takeover indicator.

suggestion.title: praisonai-platform: MemberService module execution and file modifications
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names the vulnerable component: 'MemberService.add(workspace_id, user_id, role)... has no caller-permission check.' Exploitation and post-compromise modifications leave process execution and file-write artifacts at the application layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for unexpected process execution or file create/modify events targeting member_service.py and related Python dependencies on systems running praisonai-platform. Legitimate changes to backend service modules are rare.

suggestion.title: Vitest UI Server Network Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability requires Vitest UI 'explicitly exposes the Vitest UI server to the network (using `--api.host` or api.host config option)'. Detection must hunt for this prerequisite.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Node.js/Vitest processes for --api.host flag or api.host config pointing to 0.0.0.0 or public-facing IP address. Cross-reference with network listening events showing Vitest UI ports (typically 5173, 51204) bound to non-loopback addresses.

suggestion.title: Vitest UI Path Traversal or File Scheme Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article core vulnerability: 'arbitrary file can be read'. Exploitation requires HTTP requests with path traversal (../) or file:// scheme injection to Vitest UI endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to Vitest UI listener ports containing directory traversal patterns (../, %2e%2e), file:// scheme, or absolute Windows paths (C:\, \\) in query parameters or request bodies.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary Process Execution via Vitest Web Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'arbitrary file can be read and executed'. This is the execution phase—spawning of shell or system commands through the exploited interface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process spawning (cmd.exe, PowerShell, sh) with parent=Node.js/Vitest, especially with parent initiating from listening port context. Flag batch/enumeration-style process chains spawned from a single HTTP session context.

suggestion.title: Sensitive File Access from Vitest Context
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes Windows-specific impact and 'arbitrary file can be read'. Attackers would exfiltrate system files (SAM, NTDS, application secrets, source code).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file read/open events initiated by Node.js/Vitest processes targeting system paths (\Windows\System32, \Windows\Temp, registry hives) or batch scanning of project directory structure indicative of reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: Vitest Installation or Configuration Changes on Windows
suggestion.rationale: Article notes Windows-specific vulnerability path. Detection should cover Vitest installation, config modification with api.host settings, or upgrade to patched version.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Windows package managers (npm, yarn), node_modules creation, or manual Vitest config file modifications (vitest.config.ts/.js). Flag presence of api.host config in non-dev/CI environments.

suggestion.title: Connections to attacker C2 infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article Recommended Hunts section explicitly calls for this detection. Lists 11 attacker IPs and 5 domains; narrative describes C2 orchestrating the destruction campaign.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound connections to attacker IPs (31.172.87.20, 212.83.61.213, 66.85.26.183, 195.20.17.129, 46.246.125.131, 146.70.233.83, 91.193.19.198, 89.36.231.56, 84.200.89.52, 46.30.190.173, 45.150.108.61) or domains (nefeshhope.com and subdomains, banujcobaar.com) from any internal system. Prioritize alerts from backup, admin, or disaster-recovery infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Destructive malware execution by file hash
suggestion.rationale: Article Recommended Hunts section explicitly calls for hash-based endpoint detection. Seven SHA256 values provided are the primary destructive payload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation, process execution, or hash matches for the 7 provided SHA256 hashes. Highest confidence when originating from elevated-privilege processes on systems holding backups, recovery tools, or infrastructure credentials.

suggestion.title: Volume Shadow Copy / backup deletion
suggestion.rationale: Article narrative: 'erasing backups and dismantling recovery infrastructure.' VSS deletion is required precursor to destructive wipe operations but not covered by provided techniques (T1071, T1027).
