suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect vssadmin delete shadows, wmic shadowcopy delete, or powershell Get-WmiObject Win32_ShadowCopy deletion. Alert on disablement of Windows Backup Service, MSSQL/Oracle backup jobs, or third-party backup agents. Correlate with subsequent mass file deletions.

suggestion.title: Disk wipe / partition destruction
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers are 'wiping IT systems.' Low-level destructive attack beyond file-deletion, requiring detection of disk-wipe tools and direct partition access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of cipher.exe /w, sdelete, Eraser, shred, or dd with /dev/zero. Alert on access to raw disk devices (\\.\\ or /dev/sd*) or partition tables. Monitor for SMART commands used to reset HPA (Host Protected Area).

suggestion.title: Disaster recovery system disablement
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'dismantling recovery infrastructure'—explicit T1490 behavior. Disabling recovery boot options, recovery partitions, and DR systems is critical attack step not covered by T1071/T1027.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect commands disabling System Restore, Recovery Environment, boot recovery options, or BIOS password reset. Monitor for deletion of EFI boot partitions, PXE/netboot removal, or firmware password changes.

suggestion.title: Coordinated mass file deletion across infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'sweeping campaign of digital destruction'—sustained, multi-system file deletion at organizational scale. Volume-based detection required for end-state impact assessment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect thresholds: >1000 file deletions per system per hour, >50% of disk space deleted in 24-hour window, recursive deletion of backup paths (Program Files\*Backup*, C:\backup*, /var/backups). Alert on same pattern across 3+ systems within 12-hour window.

suggestion.title: AppDomainManager Hijacking Detection via Registry and Process Loading
suggestion.rationale: Article's primary attack mechanism: 'sophisticated .NET hijacking technique' and 'AppDomainManager Hijacking to Evade EDR Detection.' Core technical detail wholly absent from pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor .NET processes (w3wp.exe, managed .exe, etc.) for loads of AppDomainManager classes from non-standard locations; flag HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\Software\Microsoft\.NETFramework registry modifications creating custom AppDomain managers; correlate suspicious assembly loads from %temp%, ProgramData, or external URIs with parent process context.

suggestion.title: C2 Communications to Iranian APT Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists six C2 domains ('buisness-centeral-transportation.com', 'premierhealthadvisory.com', etc.) with recommended hunt phase 'c2' and 'High' confidence. Pipeline extracted zero domains and generated zero network detection use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound DNS queries and TCP/443 connections to six identified domains from endpoints in target regions (US, Israel, UAE). Flag successful connections or repeated resolution attempts as beaconing; correlate with AppDomainManager process trees.

suggestion.title: Malware Hash Matching for Iranian APT AppDomainManager Samples
suggestion.rationale: Article provides 12 SHA256 hashes ('44f4f7aca7f1d9bfdaf7b3736934cbe19f851a707662f8f0b0c49b383e054250', etc.) labeled as high-fidelity IOCs. Pipeline extracted zero hashes and generated zero hash-matching use cases despite explicit template recommendation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process execution or file creation matching any of 12 provided SHA256 hashes. Prioritize alerts on .NET hosting processes (w3wp.exe, msiexec.exe, rundll32.exe) loading these samples; correlate with AppDomainManager registry modifications and C2 domain traffic.

suggestion.title: EDR Evasion via .NET Obfuscation and Reflection
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'evade EDR Detection' and lists T1027 (Obfuscated Files or Information). Pipeline did not surface defense-evasion detection for the obfuscation and reflection techniques inherent to AppDomain hijacking attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag .NET processes exhibiting obfuscation signatures: high entropy in module names, compressed PE sections, reflective LoadAssembly calls without prior disk staging, or dynamic method invocation via Type.GetMethod(). Cross-reference with CLR JIT compilation anomalies and DisableStackOverflowProbing registry modifications typical of EDR-bypass tooling.

suggestion.title: SSPR Abuse via Unverified Contact Methods
suggestion.rationale: Article states old behavior relied on 'directory-stored contact information that has not been formally verified.' This is the attack surface being patched. Detect SSPR resets triggered via unverified secondary contacts—a known credential-access pattern—especially on high-privilege accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate and alert on SSPR password changes initiated via unverified secondary contact methods (unconfirmed recovery email, phone). Spike detection on accounts with geographically inconsistent contact-to-reset patterns within 24 hours.

suggestion.title: SSPR Authentication Method Enumeration & Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Article mandates 'explicitly registered authentication methods' as sole SSPR path. Attackers may pre-stage registered methods on target accounts to bypass incoming controls. Detect enrollment of new authentication methods outside normal risk profile or batch method registrations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful enrollment of new SSPR authentication methods outside business hours, or multiple method-registration failures followed by success (bypass attempt). Flag cross-region auth method registration spikes indicating lateral abuse.

suggestion.title: npm Postinstall Script Spawning Command Shells
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Multiple Red Hat Cloud Services npm Packages Compromised'—attack delivers via package.json postinstall scripts. Pipeline generated zero Node.js/npm-execution detections despite postinstall being the payload vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm/Node.js processes spawning powershell.exe, cmd.exe, bash, or curl during package installation. Correlate parent process (npm, node, yarn) with child process launching shells. Focus on @redhat-cloud-services scope packages and postinstall script execution with network egress.

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration from Node.js Environment Variables
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'credential-stealing malware' and 'credential-stealing worm'—pipeline generated zero credential-access detections despite explicit credential-theft goal. Mini Shai-Hulud likely harvests npm tokens, AWS keys, API tokens from process environment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Node.js processes accessing /root/.ssh, ~/.npm-credentials, ~/.aws, or reading environment variables (process.env). Correlate with outbound DNS/HTTP to non-npm-registry destinations immediately after npm install. Flag exfiltration of credential-like strings in network traffic.

suggestion.title: Multi-Package Compromise from @redhat-cloud-services Scope
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'over 30 official packages under the @redhat-cloud-services npm scope'—supply-chain attack on single scope. Pipeline missed initial-access detection correlating multiple malicious packages from same namespace published in same window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm install operations targeting @redhat-cloud-services scope. Flag packages versions published 2026-06-01+. Correlate multiple packages from same scope installed on same host within short timeframe. Monitor package.json changes introducing this scope as new dependency.

suggestion.title: Mini Shai-Hulud Malware Family Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'Mini Shai-Hulud malware family' and campaign 'Miasma: The Spreading Blight.' Pipeline returned zero IOCs. Malware family names are primary intelligence indicators requiring Yara rules and behavioral signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Generate Yara/SIGMA rules for Mini Shai-Hulud binaries and behaviors. Detect unpacked payloads, credential enumeration loops, or registry/file access patterns consistent with worm propagation. Prioritize npm cache directories and node_modules for suspicious executables.

suggestion.title: C2 Communication from Compromised npm Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article: malware performs credential theft (implies exfiltration). Pipeline generated zero command-and-control or exfiltration detections. Mini Shai-Hulud requires C2 channel to transmit stolen credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Node.js/npm processes initiating outbound connections to non-CDN, non-registry IPs immediately post-installation. Flag DNS queries for suspicious domains during npm package execution. Correlate process creation events with egress traffic volume and destination reputation (newly-registered domains, bulletproof hosters).

suggestion.title: Installation of Compromised NPM Package Version
suggestion.rationale: Article describes compromised @redhat-cloud-services packages. Detection required for when developers/CI/CD install affected versions—this is the infection vector for npm supply-chain attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install/update commands and package-lock.json for specific compromised package identifiers and versions. Alert on installation of @redhat-cloud-services packages matching CVE advisory signatures or known-malicious version ranges.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Script Execution from Node Modules During Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: npm supply-chain compromises commonly inject malicious code via preinstall/postinstall hooks. Article describes code embedded in compromised packages, triggering execution on install.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on script execution (PowerShell, cmd.exe, node.js) originating from node_modules directory or spawned during npm install. Correlate with presence of unknown/unsigned binaries or suspicious CLI arguments.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized NPM Registry Authentication or Version Publish Events
suggestion.rationale: Compromised packages indicate account takeover or registry credential theft. Detection of unusual auth events identifies the initial access phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm registry logs for new auth tokens, unusual login locations, atypical package publish events, or version pushes outside normal release cadence. Baseline per-package and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Environment Variable and Credential Enumeration from Node Processes
suggestion.rationale: Malicious npm packages typically exfiltrate environment variables containing API keys, credentials, and build secrets—a stated attack vector in supply-chain incidents.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Node.js and npm processes for process.env enumeration, .env file reads, or spawned child processes accessing credential stores. Alert during package installation contexts.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Outbound Connections from Node.js / npm Processes
suggestion.rationale: Compromised packages establish C2 or exfiltration channels. Detection of anomalous network behavior from node_modules context is critical post-infection indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound connections from node.js/npm processes to non-standard ports, unusual geographies, or known malicious IPs/domains. Baseline legitimate npm registry traffic and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Version Anomaly: Unexpected or Orphaned Packages in Node Modules
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks may involve version bumps, downgrades, or installation of unexpected release numbers to evade detection against lock files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare installed node_modules against package-lock.json and package.json. Alert when versions deviate, packages are orphaned, or release dates are anomalous relative to organizational baseline.

suggestion.title: npm Supply Chain Package Compromise — Installation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'codexui-android npm Supply Chain Attack.' Pipeline missed core attack vector—npm package installation as initial access. No detection for known-malicious package installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm install / yarn add of packages matching supply-chain IOCs (codexui-android and variants). Monitor for package installation with mismatched checksums, typosquat names, or publish dates <30 days.

suggestion.title: OpenAI Token Exfiltration — Credential Theft Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'OpenAI Codex Authentication Tokens Stolen'—direct credential objective. Pipeline generated zero credential-access detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt outbound HTTPS from node processes post-npm-install for base64/hex-encoded strings matching OpenAI token patterns (sk-*, org-*). Flag POST bodies or custom headers exfiltrating credentials to non-Microsoft domains.

suggestion.title: Post-Install Script Malicious Execution
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain npm attacks exploit postinstall/preinstall hooks. Article describes token theft likely via embedded payload in package lifecycle scripts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install process tree for spawn of curl, wget, powershell, or bash from postinstall context. Alert on scripts reading environment variables or accessing ~/.openai or similar credential stores.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Package Metadata & Typosquatting
suggestion.rationale: Malicious npm packages often masquerade as legitimate via typosquatting or metadata obfuscation. Article does not exclude this—pipeline missed T1036 defense evasion indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect package.json and dist/ for edit-distance similarity to legitimate package names (codex-ui, codex-android). Flag minified/obfuscated JS, suspicious preinstall scripts, or metadata mismatches.

suggestion.title: Token Exfiltration Over Network — C2 Communication
suggestion.rationale: Stolen tokens must be transmitted to attacker. Article 'Stolen in ... Attack' implies exfiltration phase—pipeline mapped zero network-based detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate npm-install events with outbound connections to newly-registered or low-reputation domains. Inspect TLS SNI and HTTP Host headers for obfuscated exfil destinations. Hunt for base64-wrapped credential strings in POST payloads.

suggestion.title: npm Package Registry Anomalies — Recent Publish & Account Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Compromised packages show: recent first publish, rapid version updates, author-account anomalies. Article does not exclude these indicators—pipeline missed T1195.001 supply-chain staging phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference installed package versions against npm public API: flag packages with publish-date <30 days, author-account-created recently, sudden download spike, or rapid minor-version increments preceding disclosure.

suggestion.title: Spearphishing email targeting Afghan finance ministry officials
suggestion.rationale: Article states campaign 'targeted provincial finance officials across all 34 Afghan Mustoufiats.' Initial compromise mechanism almost certainly spear-phishing or watering hole to finance.gov.af or similar. Pipeline extracted zero initial-access phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag emails with executable attachments (.exe, .zip, .scr, .msi) or malicious links sent to @finance.gov.af, @treasury.gov.af, or provincial finance domains. Correlate with sandbox detonations or hash matches to the 9 SHA256 samples. Monitor for sender spoofing of .gov.af or .edu.af domains.

suggestion.title: XenoRAT persistence via registry, scheduled task, or service creation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'persistent remote access tool' deployment. Persistence mechanism undetected. Pipeline missed T1547, T1053, T1543 techniques entirely despite 'persistent' keyword in threat narrative.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services and HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run for entries with obfuscated names or paths to %APPDATA%\Temp\. Detect scheduled task creation under Windows\Tasks or service creation with display names mimicking legitimate Windows services. Correlate with execution of the 9 SHA256 samples.

suggestion.title: Process injection or code cave tactics by XenoRAT
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'Obfuscated Files or Information' (T1027) but pipeline failed to map to injection-specific techniques (T1055). Custom RATs typically hollow or inject into legitimate processes to evade detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag suspicious parent-child process pairs: svchost.exe, explorer.exe, rundll32.exe, or msiexec.exe spawning unusual children or from unusual working directories. Monitor for unsigned DLL loads into system processes. Detect CreateRemoteThread and VirtualAllocEx API calls from processes matching the 9 SHA256 hashes.

suggestion.title: Outbound C2 beaconing to SideCopy infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article provides 3 C2 IPs and 1 domain. Kill chain reconstruction returned empty phases. C2 communications phase is critical post-execution detection and was completely missed by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound connections from Afghanistan-based hosts to 185.235.137.106, 103.132.98.224, 103.132.98.226 on any port. Monitor DNS queries to abimj.edu.af. Correlate with process execution of the 9 SHA256 samples. Look for HTTPS/TLS beaconing patterns to these IPs.

suggestion.title: Credential dumping post-compromise
suggestion.rationale: Target is Ministry of Finance across 34 provincial directorates. Actors will exfiltrate banking credentials, revenue system access, and financial data. Attack objective strongly implies credential harvesting (T1003) but pipeline output zero discovery/credential-access detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of mimikatz, procdump, comsvcs.dll, or ntdsutil.exe from non-administrative paths. Monitor LSASS.exe access from suspicious parent processes. Flag registry queries to SAM hive or attempts to export HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SECURITY. Correlate with PowerShell -EncodedCommand patterns for obfuscated credential dumping.

suggestion.title: Lateral movement to revenue/banking systems post-initial-compromise
suggestion.rationale: Finance ministry attack implies lateral movement to core financial systems (revenue databases, EFT/banking interfaces). Pipeline generated zero lateral-movement or discovery-phase detections despite targeting context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect remote administration tools (RDP, PsExec, WMI lateral movement) initiated from initially-compromised finance ministry workstations to banking or revenue system servers. Monitor for anomalous Kerberos TGT requests from compromised accounts to financial systems. Flag lateral movement over SMB or WinRM from non-IT users.

suggestion.title: RAT C2 Beaconing to Known Attacker Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'remote access malware' and lists 4 C2 IPs, but no behavioral hunt captures RAT command-and-control callback patterns. Missing hunt for outbound connections from user processes (not system services) to the supplied infrastructure. Article phrase: 'quietly plant remote access malware on Windows computers.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After RAT installs, it establishes persistent C2 communication. Detect outbound connections from non-system processes to the IOC IPs/domains, especially over unusual ports or protocols; DNS queries from user-context processes to C2 domains; and connection patterns matching keepalive or command-polling behavior (repeated short connections with regular intervals).

suggestion.title: RAT Post-Exploitation Registry Persistence
suggestion.rationale: RAT malware typically installs persistence mechanisms (registry run keys or scheduled tasks) to survive reboot. Article does not surface detection for these post-exploitation behaviors. Article states 'quietly plant' suggesting evasive installation, not one-shot execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect registry writes to HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\Run, HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\Run, or scheduled task creation triggered within 10 seconds of PowerShell execution spawned from ClickFix attack. Flag when non-system processes modify registry keys with suspicious executable paths or UNC paths.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated/Encoded Script Download and Interpretation
suggestion.rationale: ClickFix specifically tricks users into running obfuscated scripts. T1027 (Obfuscated Files or Information) is listed but no hunt surfaces actual obfuscation patterns. Article states 'ClickFix scripts' with implicit encoding. Missing detection for base64 decoding, variable substitution, or character concatenation in command lines.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PowerShell processes with command lines containing base64 strings (match against regex [A-Za-z0-9+/]{50,}={0,2}), IEX aliases, $() substitution patterns, or string concatenation operators. Correlate to clipboard content injection or recent browser activity. High specificity if occurring within 60 seconds of phishing link click.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Operations in Temp/AppData/SysWOW64 from Script Context
suggestion.rationale: ClickFix attack chain downloads RAT binary and executes it. Article mentions 'plant' malware but no hunt for file-write operations preceding RAT execution. Missing detection for parent process (PowerShell) writing unsigned executables to volatile paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file creation/write operations in C:\Users\*\AppData\Local\Temp, C:\Windows\Temp, or C:\Users\*\AppData\Local\SysWOW64 followed by execution of the written file from the same path within 10 seconds. Alert if parent process is powershell.exe and child executable has zero prevalence or known-bad reputation.

suggestion.title: Memory-Resident Payload Execution Patterns (Fileless RAT)
suggestion.rationale: Modern RAT variants (including some that use ClickFix delivery) execute entirely in memory without touching disk. Article's four SHA256 hashes are insufficient if the RAT variant is fileless. Missing hunt for process memory injection, process hallowing, or in-memory code execution indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PowerShell processes spawning child processes with unusual parent-child relationships (e.g., legitimate utility like notepad.exe, lsass.exe, or svchost.exe spawned with command line parameters), or PowerShell injecting into other processes via CreateRemoteThread. Flag MZ headers or PE signatures found in process memory dump analysis.

suggestion.title: Accessibility Service Abuse — Suspicious Permission Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article title and body emphasize trojan 'Abuses Accessibility Service to Control Devices.' No detection generated for accessibility permission requests or grants to suspicious apps.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Android apps requesting BIND_ACCESSIBILITY_SERVICE permission or toggling accessibility services on. Cross-reference against app store legitimacy and known malware signatures. Flag rapid permission escalation patterns post-installation.

suggestion.title: Banking Trojan — Overlay/Phishing UI Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes trojan as banking-focused with credential theft risk; accessibility service enables overlay attacks on legitimate banking apps. No detection for suspicious overlay windows or UI manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect accessibility service events combined with screenshots or window capture activity. Flag non-system processes requesting screen capture permissions. Monitor for overlay window creation by non-whitelisted apps over banking/finance apps.

suggestion.title: C2 Communication — OverlayPhantom Beacon Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article lists C2 domain 'bitlrewards-app.com' and IP '199.217.99.122' but pipeline generated no network hunt for these known infrastructure indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on DNS queries or network connections to bitlrewards-app.com or 199.217.99.122 from Android devices. Correlate with APK hash execution events. Monitor for HTTPS beaconing patterns consistent with mobile C2.

suggestion.title: Malware Installation — OverlayPhantom APK Hash Matching
suggestion.rationale: Article provides three SHA256 hashes; pipeline output shows empty IOC field and zero hash-based hunts despite article recommending 'File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Match file hashes against 9ef37376bfaa18e193cc72218924ad8ebf56d2667d348f0eae5ae6ec45ab8775, f8b614a2918378063d6e6655b676ceb52ae65b1510e2cc08087fcac31acb7aeb, 8ddc1f2a75f3d5b5bd054a5367bd5015ebc90f3453d63c7cce438c12dc2ae86a. Alert on execution or persistence mechanisms.

suggestion.title: Initial Access — Malicious Link Click / APK Download
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states trojan 'spreads through malicious links disguised as downloads from trusted, well-known applications.' No detection for link-based delivery or suspicious APK staging.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for downloads from non-official app stores or spoofed app domains. Detect users clicking links from phishing messages that resolve to *.apk files. Flag unusual DNS resolutions to domains impersonating legitimate app vendors.

suggestion.title: Dragon Weave C2 Domain Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article title cites 'Dragon Weave' campaign against Czech Republic & Taiwan; no C2 communications detection was generated despite this being standard for APT tracking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound DNS queries and HTTP connections to known or suspected Dragon Weave C2 infrastructure. Flag anomalous beaconing patterns from systems to attacker-controlled domains, especially those hosted in bulletproof hosting providers or CDNs.

suggestion.title: Dragon Weave Phishing Email Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Chinese APT targeting government/critical infrastructure typically begins with spear phishing; no initial-access detection was created.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on emails containing Dragon Weave-associated malware payloads, obfuscated macros, or malicious URLs targeting Czech and Taiwanese government/defense entities.

suggestion.title: Dragon Weave Lateral Movement via PsExec/WMI
suggestion.rationale: Article describes campaign targeting regional entities but no lateral movement detection logic was surfaced. Chinese APTs commonly use native Windows tools post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious WMI process creation, PsExec/PSEXESVC service installation, and lateral movement via administrative shares (\\host\ADMIN$) from initially-compromised hosts.

suggestion.title: CVE-2024-21182 Vulnerability Scanner Alert
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states CISA KEV entries are 'currently exploited' and patch-due 2026-06-04. Scanners detecting this CVE are the most reliable early indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Vulnerability scanner reports positive detection for CVE-2024-21182 against Oracle WebLogic Server instances. Cross-reference against patch inventory and escalate any unpatched hosts by federal deadline.

suggestion.title: Exposed Oracle WebLogic T3/IIOP Service Identification
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker needs 'network access via T3, IIOP' — these are WebLogic-specific protocols. Exposure hunt for T3 (port 7001 default) and IIOP (port 7002) on internet-facing assets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Network scan or asset inventory reveals Oracle WebLogic Server listening on T3 (default 7001) or IIOP (default 7002) ports exposed to untrusted networks. Indicates CVE-2024-21182 attack surface.

suggestion.title: WebLogic Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated attacker' can 'compromise' server — this implies RCE or unrestricted data access without credentials. Look for T3/IIOP protocol fuzzing, exploit payload signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Suspicious T3 or IIOP protocol traffic patterns (malformed requests, known exploit signatures, binary payloads) to WebLogic servers, followed by successful connection or error responses consistent with CVE-2024-21182 exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Oracle WebLogic Unauthorized Data Access Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states successful attacks result in 'unauthorized access to critical data or complete access to all Oracle WebLogic Server accessible data.' Post-breach detection for exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After CVE-2024-21182 exploitation, detect anomalous bulk data queries, database dumps, or outbound transfers of WebLogic configuration or application data from compromised instances to external IPs.

suggestion.title: WebLogic Server Patch/Upgrade Activity Post-Deadline
suggestion.rationale: Federal patch-due date 2026-06-04 is binding for compliance. Detect patching activity after deadline as indicator of breach discovery or post-breach remediation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Urgent WebLogic patches or version upgrades applied after federal deadline on previously unpatched systems. Combined with earlier CVE-2024-21182 exposure, suggests post-exploitation discovery and cleanup.

suggestion.title: T3 Protocol Handshake Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: T3 is WebLogic's proprietary RMI protocol. Article names T3 as attack vector. Baseline normal T3 handshakes and flag protocol violations consistent with exploit delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Analyze T3 protocol traffic to WebLogic ports (7001). Flag incomplete handshakes, premature disconnects, binary blobs in protocol fields, or known malicious payloads embedded in T3 initial contact frames.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Docker Image Pull from Poisoned Registry
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'poisoning a Docker Hub repository to later steal Kubernetes secrets and other sensitive data' — requires detection of registry compromise indicators and subsequent image deployments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Docker image pulls with unexpected digest or manifest changes. Monitor for CI/CD systems or container runtimes pulling from registries with recent access anomalies. Correlate image SHA against known-good inventory.

suggestion.title: Malicious Payload Execution in Build/Scanning Tool
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'stealer that was loaded during the KICS scanning process' — payload execution within legitimate tooling requires detection of child process spawning and data exfiltration from scanning contexts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor KICS scanner and similar CI/CD tools for unexpected child processes, library loading from non-standard paths, or outbound connections. Flag processes spawned by scanners that interact with file systems containing secrets or credentials.

suggestion.title: Kubernetes Secrets Enumeration and Theft
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'steal Kubernetes secrets' as attack outcome — requires detection of secret object access and exfiltration via orchestration APIs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Kubernetes API audit logs for high-volume reads of Secret objects or enumeration of secrets across namespaces. Alert on ServiceAccount tokens used to access secrets from unexpected workloads. Correlate with pod network egress to external IPs.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Dangerous Linux Capabilities
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 'CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_SYS_MODULE, CAP_SYS_PTRACE, CAP_NET_ADMIN' as exploitation vectors — requires detection of containers with excessive capabilities or runtime capability injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on container creation with CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_SYS_MODULE, CAP_SYS_PTRACE, or CAP_NET_ADMIN capabilities unless explicitly whitelisted. Monitor for runtime setcap or capset syscalls within containers. Flag --privileged container launches.

suggestion.title: Container Escape via Host Kernel Exploit
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Container escape followed by host compromise' and 'Exploiting vulnerabilities in the host system and container runtime components' — requires detection of kernel exploit patterns from container processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for anomalous syscall sequences (ptrace abuse, namespace/cgroup manipulation) originating from container processes. Alert on processes escaping container namespaces or executing with host-level privileges. Track known container escape CVE exploitation signatures.

suggestion.title: Orchestration API Compromise and Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'Exploitation of orchestration APIs' and 'insecure use of containerization and orchestration APIs' — requires detection of unauthorized Kubernetes API access and privilege abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Kubernetes API logs for unauthenticated or token-based access to sensitive endpoints (pod creation, RBAC modification, secret reads). Alert on ServiceAccount tokens used from unexpected contexts or IPs. Flag resource enumeration by pods.

suggestion.title: Mirasvit Cache Warmer Plugin Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states unauthenticated vulnerability in named plugin enabling RCE with 'no login, configuration changes, or admin access required.' No detection guidance supplied despite this being the primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP POST/GET requests to vulnerable Mirasvit Cache Warmer endpoints (common paths: /var/log/cache-warmer or plugin-specific endpoints) with serialized PHP object payloads or base64-encoded object injection attempts. Alert on 4XX responses followed by successful PHP code execution artifacts (new process spawns, file writes to web root).

suggestion.title: PHP Object Injection Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies attack as 'PHP object injection flaw'—a specific exploitation primitive that should trigger signature-based detection. No payload detection recommended.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests containing serialized PHP objects (markers: O:<digits>:"<class>", pO:, or url-encoded equivalents %4F%3A) targeting Magento installation paths. High-fidelity signal when combined with known unsafe Magento endpoints or plugin admin panels.

suggestion.title: Web Shell or Malicious Artifact Deployment Post-RCE
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'remotely execute malicious code'—implies attacker achieves code execution and will likely deploy persistence mechanisms. No follow-up detection suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After successful exploitation, detect creation of suspicious .php files in Magento web-accessible directories (pub/, var/, app/code/), especially with timestamps matching exploitation timeframe. Monitor for hidden or obfuscated PHP shells typical of Magento-targeted malware.

suggestion.title: Mirasvit Cache Warmer Version Fingerprinting
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies vulnerability in specific plugin version(s). No asset-discovery hunt provided to locate vulnerable installations before exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for presence of Mirasvit Cache Warmer plugin via HTTP response headers, admin panel fingerprints, or static file paths. Extract plugin version from JS assets or XML config files when accessible, filter for versions matching CVE-2026-45247 scope.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Magento Admin-Like Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability requires 'no login' or 'admin access'—implying the vulnerable endpoint bypasses normal authentication. No authentication-bypass detection included.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for successful HTTP responses (200, 301, 302) to Mirasvit Cache Warmer admin endpoints (e.g., /admin/mirasvit_cache, /admin_*/cache) from users without prior successful authentication (no session cookie, no user-agent history in asset requests).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-45247 Exploit Scanner Activity
suggestion.rationale: Named CVE with public disclosure will be rapidly scanned by threat actors. No IDS/WAF signature or traffic-pattern detection recommended despite high recency and exploitation likelihood.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on rapid, sequential requests to Magento installations probing for Mirasvit Cache Warmer plugin presence or known vulnerable endpoints within short timeframe. Combine with known exploit PoC request signatures (specific parameter names, payload patterns) once disclosed.

suggestion.title: WP Maps Pro Plugin Exploitation - Admin Account Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Critical WP Maps Pro Flaw Actively Exploited to Create Admin Accounts' — this is the core attack narrative. Pipeline should have surfaced detection for (1) exploitation attempts targeting the plugin, (2) unexpected admin user creation post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WordPress user_meta and wp_users tables for programmatic admin account creation following HTTP requests to WP Maps Pro plugin endpoints. Correlate plugin error logs with user creation events. Flag any admin user creation with suspicious registration IP or timestamp clustering.

suggestion.title: WP Maps Pro Plugin Parameter Injection or Unsafe Deserialization
suggestion.rationale: Critical plugin flaw suggests input validation bypass. Article states 'actively exploited' but pipeline extracted no exploit mechanics — should have mapped this to injection or unsafe object handling patterns typical of WordPress plugin vulns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline WP Maps Pro plugin request patterns (legitimate parameter names, payload sizes, parameter counts). Alert on deviations: oversized parameters, unexpected URL-encoded payloads, serialized PHP objects, or requests to admin.php with plugin-specific parameter names.

suggestion.title: WordPress Admin Account Anomalies Post-Plugin Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Attack outcome is admin account creation. Pipeline did not generate a standalone UC for account creation detection, which is a fundamental persistence indicator in WordPress environments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor wp_users INSERT events for new admin-role accounts (user_level 10, caps include 'manage_options'). Correlate creation timestamp with web access logs to identify source IP. Flag if creation occurs after plugin-related HTTP errors or unusual access patterns.

suggestion.title: POST /workspaces/*/members with role=owner privilege escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes the attack: 'POST /workspaces/{workspace_id}/members' endpoint accepts role parameter and 'forwards the request body's user_id and role straight into MemberService.add()' with no permission check. This is the core exploit vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST requests to /workspaces/*/members endpoints with HTTP 201 (Created) response and role parameter set to 'owner'. Correlate on source IP, account, and user-agent. High-fidelity indicator of lateral privilege escalation within multi-tenant workspace platform.

suggestion.title: Workspace owner grant followed by immediate login from new identity
suggestion.rationale: Article implies multi-step attack: attacker (workspace member) grants owner role to external/attacker-controlled account, then that newly-granted account authenticates. 'identity-swap chain' in hunts section shows the behavioral pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate POST /workspaces/*/members with 201 response (grant event) against subsequent successful authentication events within 1 hour. Flag when the newly-granted account identity differs from the grantor and login occurs from any source IP. Baseline: establish expected grant->login delay distribution for the environment.

suggestion.title: Asset exposure detection: praisonai-platform instances with CVE-2026-47413 vulnerable version
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)' as a recon-phase hunt. Pipeline should have surfaced version detection for vulnerable praisonai-platform deployments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate web services exposing /workspaces/ endpoints or praisonai-platform HTTP headers. Cross-reference application version against CVE-2026-47413 affected versions to build asset-at-risk inventory. Prioritize for patching and behavioral monitoring.

suggestion.title: Non-member account attempts to POST to /workspaces/*/members (authorization bypass probe)
suggestion.rationale: Article states endpoint is 'gated only by require_workspace_member(workspace_id)' — attackers without workspace membership may probe the endpoint. Failed 403/401 attempts indicate reconnaissance or access-control testing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST to /workspaces/*/members returning 403 Forbidden or 401 Unauthorized. Baseline: enumerate legitimate users who should have member access per workspace. Flag external/unexpected source IPs or service accounts attempting the endpoint.

suggestion.title: HTTP Request Pattern Anomaly Detection to WebSphere
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'specially crafted HTTP requests' as direct attack vector. Pipeline failed to surface hunt for anomalous request structures, payloads, or header combinations targeting WebSphere endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP traffic to WebSphere ports (default 80, 443, 9080, 9443) for requests with malformed headers, oversized payloads, or unusual parameter combinations. Flag multi-encoded payloads or requests matching known plugin-exploitation patterns. Baseline normal WebSphere request structure and alert on deviation.

suggestion.title: WebSphere Plugin Component Endpoint Access Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically names 'optional Web Server Plug-ins component' as the vulnerable surface. No UC generated to detect reconnaissance or exploitation attempts against plugin paths/config endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect access attempts to WebSphere plugin-related paths, admin consoles, or configuration interfaces. Look for 404/403 responses followed by successful 200 responses (plugin path enumeration). Flag requests to known plugin endpoints (/plugin, /admin, /jaxws, /ibm_application_discovery) from external or untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: Code Execution from WebSphere Java Process
suggestion.rationale: Article outcome is 'arbitrary code execution' but no process-level detection suggested. Pipeline failed to map execution phase despite explicit statement of RCE capability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor child process spawning from WebSphere JVM processes (java.exe, wsappserver.exe, startServer.sh). Baseline normal WebSphere child processes and alert on suspicious spawns (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, nc, curl from app server context). Correlate with HTTP request logs to tie exploitation to process execution.

suggestion.title: AppDomainManager Environment Variable Hijacking
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes '.NET hijacking technique' and 'AppDomainManager Hijacking' as the attack method. This behavioral detection is critical but absent. Article: 'sophisticated .NET hijacking technique to slip past endpoint defenses.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation or modification of registry values APPDOMAIN_MANAGER_ASM or APPDOMAIN_MANAGER_TYPE under HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\.NETFramework. Track parent processes (MSBuild, CSC, PowerShell, Office). Pair with child process spawning unusual .NET utilities or loading non-standard assemblies.

suggestion.title: Suspicious .NET Assembly Load from Unusual Location
suggestion.rationale: AppDomainManager hijacking depends on loading attacker-controlled assemblies. Article describes hijacking for EDR evasion, implying custom assembly injection. Missing behavioral detection for execution phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect .NET processes loading assemblies from temporary directories, AppData, Downloads, or network shares. Flag LoadImage events for DLLs with mismatched signer or loaded via unusual APIs (LoadLibrary from within CLR). Establish baseline for each environment.

suggestion.title: Legitimate .NET Process with Abnormal Registry/Memory Access
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'evade EDR Detection' — attackers leverage trusted .NET processes (msbuild.exe, csc.exe, ngen.exe) to hide malicious activity. Detection must surface behavioral anomalies in these processes, not just hash/network IOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag .NET processes (msbuild.exe, csc.exe, ngen.exe) that access registry under SOFTWARE\Microsoft\.NETFramework, create threads in unrelated processes, or load unsigned DLLs. Add baseline context: typical .NET processes do not touch AppDomainManager registry keys.

suggestion.title: Iran-Linked APT Targeting US/Israel/UAE: Temporal Correlation to Feb 28, 2026 Conflict
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Campaign intensified following a regional conflict that began on February 28, 2026, attributed to an Iran-linked advanced persistent threat.' This temporal pivot and geo-targeting context should drive urgency scoring and alert routing. Missing from pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate network traffic to identified domains with organizational geo-tagging (US/Israel/UAE targets). Flag accounts or hosts with recent privilege changes, data-access patterns, or exfiltration activity around Feb 28 onwards. Use campaign start date as a temporal anchor for alerting urgency.

suggestion.title: OnlyOffice Subdomain Abuse for Payload Staging/C2
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 'docspace-y4cumb.onlyoffice.com' and 'docspace-twpf0e.onlyoffice.com' as IOCs. If legitimate OnlyOffice infrastructure, this indicates account compromise or typosquatting. Needs categorization and signature for C2 traffic patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For legitimate OnlyOffice subdomains: monitor for unusual volume, data exfiltration, or C2 beacon patterns (regular intervals, fixed payload sizes). For typosquat domains: verify DNS CNAME/A record targets; if not resolving to official OnlyOffice IPs, flag as infrastructure abuse.

suggestion.title: npm/node spawning shell processes during package install
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'compromised npm packages deployed credential-stealing malware'—npm post-install scripts are the execution trigger. Malware must spawn cmd/powershell to exfiltrate credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on node.exe or npm.exe spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, curl, wget, or Python during npm install (detect post-install phase via parent process and process timing). Baseline normal post-install scripts; most should not spawn shell interpreters.

suggestion.title: npm/node accessing credential stores during install
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'credential-stealing worm'—malware must read ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.npmrc, ~/.ssh, .env, or %USERPROFILE%/.aws. These reads are suspicious during routine npm install.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor node.exe/npm.exe file access to home-directory secret stores: ~/.aws/*, ~/.npmrc, ~/.ssh/id_*, .env, %USERPROFILE%/.aws. Flag reads during npm install phase; baseline legitimate package dependencies that access credentials.

suggestion.title: Outbound connections from node/npm to non-registry endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Credential-stealing malware must exfiltrate stolen credentials. Article describes active 'worm'—data exfiltration is implicit in credential theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP/HTTPS POST or DNS queries from node.exe/npm.exe during install to non-npm-registry endpoints. Flag base64-encoded payloads, suspicious User-Agents, or repeated connections to unfamiliar IPs/domains.

suggestion.title: Environment variable enumeration by npm post-install script
suggestion.rationale: Malware steals credentials. npm post-install scripts (JavaScript) can enumerate process.env to harvest AWS_*, GITHUB_*, NPM_*, SSH_*, DOCKER_* tokens. Article: 'credential-stealing'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm/node processes for repeated environment variable reads or process memory queries. Suspicious if followed by credential file access or network exfiltration. Baseline known packages that legitimately read env vars.

suggestion.title: Unusual script execution context in npm package.json
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 30+ compromised @redhat-cloud-services packages—malware injected into package.json scripts (preinstall/postinstall/prepare fields). These fields execute with npm privileges during install.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag npm packages with post-install, preinstall, or prepare scripts containing shell redirects (&&, |, >, >>) or obfuscated JavaScript (atob, eval, String.fromCharCode). Monitor for scripts spawning processes outside npm workspace.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Installation or Unexpected Version Update
suggestion.rationale: Article title establishes multiple npm packages were compromised; no detection UC exists for monitoring installation of known-malicious packages or unexpected version bumps. Phrase: 'Multiple redhat-cloud-services npm Packages compromised'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for npm install, yarn add, or pnpm add targeting redhat-cloud-services packages. Alert on version changes outside normal deployment windows or to versions not matching pinned ranges in package-lock.json. Cross-reference installed versions against known-bad hashes.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Child Processes or Network Activity from Node.js Process
suggestion.rationale: Compromised npm packages typically execute payload at require-time or during initialization. Article indicates malicious code in packages but no detection exists for post-installation behaviors. Phrase: implicit in 'packages compromised'—payload execution expected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor node.js and npm processes for unexpected child process spawns (powershell, cmd, curl, wget) or network connections to non-package-registry domains shortly after package installation or application startup.

suggestion.title: npm Registry Account Takeover or Unauthorized Package Publish
suggestion.rationale: Article title indicates packages were compromised—most likely via maintainer account compromise or direct registry breach. No detection UC exists for monitoring unusual npm publish behavior. Phrase: 'compromised' implies unauthorized code change.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm audit logs for unusual publishes from known package maintainers (new IP, unusual time, outside office hours). Alert on publish events lacking corresponding Git commits or code review approvals in upstream repository.

suggestion.title: Detection of Known-Malicious npm Package Hashes or Names
suggestion.rationale: Foundational detection: alert when any installed package matches indicators from this incident. Article provides package names and versions but pipeline extracted zero IOCs. Phrase: 'redhat-cloud-services npm Packages'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference package-lock.json, yarn.lock, and pnpm-lock.yaml against IOC feed of known-malicious redhat-cloud-services package versions and hashes. Alert if matched packages exist anywhere in the dependency tree.

suggestion.title: Malicious npm Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes supply chain attack via 'codexui-android npm' package—detection must catch installation of known-malicious or suspicious package versions
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install/update commands for packages matching known-malicious package names or versions. Alert when dev dependencies or transitive dependencies pull in unexpected versions from untrusted sources. Cross-reference package checksums against threat intel feeds.

suggestion.title: Authentication Token Exfiltration via Compromised Dependency
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'OpenAI Codex Authentication Tokens Stolen'—detection must capture token credential access and exfiltration
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes spawned by node_modules code that read environment variables containing AUTH_TOKEN, API_KEY, or similar sensitive patterns, or exfiltrate these to external domains. Monitor for unusual DNS queries or HTTP POSTs from package initialization code.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Post-Installation Script Execution
suggestion.rationale: npm packages often execute postinstall scripts—malicious ones can steal credentials or establish persistence. Article indicates token theft occurred during/after package installation
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag npm postinstall, preinstall, or prepare scripts that spawn child processes with network access or file system writes outside the package directory. Correlate with unexpected network beacons or DNS lookups during npm install.

suggestion.title: npm Registry Publishing by Compromised Account
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline should detect the attack vector: how malicious version was published to npm registry (account compromise implied)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm registry publish events for packages by accounts that typically do not publish, publish from unusual geographies/IPs, or publish versions that deviate from semantic versioning patterns. Alert on account login anomalies preceding publish events.

suggestion.title: Dependency Typosquatting or Namespace Injection
suggestion.rationale: Many npm supply chain attacks use package name similarity (typosquatting) or scope collision—article title implies 'codexui-android' may be a lookalike or legitimately compromised maintainer account
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference installed npm packages against known typosquatting/lookalike lists. Alert on packages with names similar to popular libraries (Levenshtein distance <2). Monitor for sudden popularity spikes or first-time publish of packages with similar names to existing projects.

suggestion.title: Token/Credential Disclosure in npm Package Metadata or Source
suggestion.rationale: Stolen 'OpenAI Codex Authentication Tokens' suggests tokens leaked in environment, code, or exfiltrated via network—detection should look for credential exposure patterns
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan npm package tarball contents (in CI/CD or at install time) for hardcoded API keys, bearer tokens, or environment variable patterns. Alert on packages that attempt to read .env files, process.env tokens, or AWS credential files during installation.

suggestion.title: XenoRAT Malware Detection via File Hash
suggestion.rationale: Article provides 9 SHA256 hashes ('194b912c242604d6f...', '3b4194bdfe40d94031...', etc.) for XenoRAT samples. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs. Hash-based detection is foundational malware identification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution or creation of files matching any of the nine provided XenoRAT SHA256 hashes. Cross-reference daily against endpoint telemetry.

suggestion.title: XenoRAT C2 Communication to Known Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article names three C2 IPs (185.235.137.106, 103.132.98.224, 103.132.98.226) and domain (abimj.edu.af). Article explicitly cites T1071 (Application Layer Protocol) for C2 masking. Pipeline generated zero network IOC hunts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound connections to the four C2 indicators. Monitor for DNS queries resolving abimj.edu.af. Inspect encrypted tunnel traffic (HTTPS, VPN-like beaconing) that could mask XenoRAT command channel.

suggestion.title: Persistent XenoRAT Installation — Autostart and Registry Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'persistent remote access tool' and 'persistent... deployment to all 34 Afghan Mustoufiats.' Persistence is a distinct kill-chain phase. Pipeline inferred zero persistence techniques.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for any of the nine XenoRAT hashes written to Windows persistence locations (Run registry hives, Startup folders, scheduled tasks, WMI event subscriptions). Alert on suspicious registry modifications establishing autostart mechanisms.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated XenoRAT Execution — Behavioral Evasion Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1027 (Obfuscated Files or Information) as explicit attack technique. Article describes XenoRAT as 'persistent' malware, implying sophisticated evasion. Pipeline generated zero defense-evasion detections despite T1027 being named.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unsigned or low-prevalence executables spawned from temporary directories (AppData\Local\Temp, %TEMP%). Alert on parent-child chains involving scripting engines (PowerShell, cmd.exe, wscript.exe) spawning binary execution—signature of deobfuscation or late-stage code injection.

suggestion.title: Targeted Initial Access to Afghan Finance Ministry Personnel
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies targeting of 'provincial finance officials across all 34 Afghan Mustoufiats,' indicating precision targeting. This suggests spear-phishing or credential-based initial compromise (T1566, T1598, or T1199). Pipeline detected no initial-access phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for suspicious email attachments or malicious URLs targeting Afghanistan finance ministry email domains. Correlate with anomalous logon patterns (failed then successful, external IP origin, off-hours) to finance-related user accounts within 24-72 hours of email receipt.

suggestion.title: Accessibility Service Abuse by Non-System Apps
suggestion.rationale: Article title and body emphasize 'Abuses Accessibility Service to Control Devices' as the defining evasion mechanism. This is the primary execution and privilege-escalation vector. No corresponding hunt generated despite being the malware's signature technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for non-system APKs binding ACCESSIBILITY_SERVICE permission. Alert when binding is paired with process injection capability, view hierarchy manipulation, or no declared accessibility-focused functionality. Correlate with hash IOCs.

suggestion.title: UI Overlay Keystroke/Credential Capture on Banking Apps
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly targets 'banking credentials, financial data, and cryptocurrency accounts.' Overlay-based credential theft is the mechanism but no detection rule covers banking app input interception or accessibility context around credential fields.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect accessibility service click/input capture when a non-banking app is in foreground with a banking app visible in window hierarchy. Flag apps simulating user input on banking app UI elements after permission grant.

suggestion.title: APK Hash Match: OverlayPhantom Malware Samples
suggestion.rationale: Three SHA256 hashes provided with high-fidelity designation. Article states spreading 'through malicious links' suggesting download-and-install flow. No hash-based hunt generated despite these being primary IOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag file downloads and APK installations matching any of the three provided SHA256 hashes. Correlate with non-Play Store installation paths and suspicious domains (bitlrewards-app.com). Monitor process execution originating from matched APKs.

suggestion.title: C2 Communication to OverlayPhantom Infrastructure (199.217.99.122, bitlrewards-app.com)
suggestion.rationale: Article provides infrastructure IOCs (IPv4 and domain) labeled 'high-fidelity.' Active since May 2025 (ongoing). No network-based detection hunt formalized despite being core C2 infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound connections from endpoints to 199.217.99.122 on any port. Alert on DNS resolution of bitlrewards-app.com. Correlate with APK process context (hash IOCs). Flag sustained or periodic callbacks indicating malware C2 beaconing.

suggestion.title: User Execution: Malicious App Download from Fake Trusted Sources
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'spreads through malicious links disguised as downloads from trusted, well-known applications.' No detection for the initial-access social engineering vector (malicious link click → APK download).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect clicks on URLs hosting APK downloads mimicking trusted app vendors. Flag downloads of APK files matching the three hash IOCs from malicious domains. Correlate with phishing/social engineering campaigns referencing 'rewards apps' or banking app updates.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of Banking and Cryptocurrency Account Data
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies targets as 'banking credentials, financial data, and cryptocurrency accounts at serious risk.' No hunt for data staging or exfiltration beyond what overlay captures. Missing collection and exfiltration phase coverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor read access to credential storage (keychain, SharedPreferences, wallet files) from non-finance apps post-infection. Detect bulk data staging in temporary directories. Flag encrypted outbound data to C2 infrastructure (bitlrewards-app.com, 199.217.99.122) from infected process context.

suggestion.title: Dragon Weave C2 Communication Detection
suggestion.rationale: Implied by multi-country targeted campaign with dwell time; state-sponsored actor managing multiple compromises requires persistent C2. Article title establishes actor name and geography but no detection use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on anomalous DNS queries to newly registered domains, HTTP requests with mismatched User-Agents to infrastructure associated with Chinese registrants, and outbound connections during off-hours to non-whitelisted IPs.

suggestion.title: Dragon Weave Multi-Stage Phishing or Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Multi-nation targeting requires initial access vector; targeting Czech Republic (NATO, sensitive tech) and Taiwan (strategic) implies either spearphishing campaigns or public-facing app exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect incoming emails with geopolitical or entity-specific lures targeting Czech/Taiwan government or critical infrastructure; monitor web server logs for exploitation signatures and unexpected web shell activity.

suggestion.title: Dragon Weave Lateral Movement via Living-Off-The-Land Binaries
suggestion.rationale: Multi-target, multi-country operations imply internal lateral movement across victim environments; no detection use case provided despite centrality to campaign success.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on lateral movement via WMI (wmic.exe), PsExec, or RDP/SMB from initially compromised systems to new internal hosts; flag successful credential use across multiple systems.

suggestion.title: Dragon Weave Persistence via Scheduled Tasks and Registry
suggestion.rationale: Campaign targeting suggests post-compromise persistence to maintain access; no persistence-phase detection use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation of scheduled tasks with obfuscated or random names, modification of startup registry keys (Run, RunOnce), and installation of Windows services pointing to unusual binary paths.

suggestion.title: Dragon Weave Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: State-sponsored multi-target campaign requires credential theft for lateral movement and persistence; no credential-access phase detection despite being essential to breach lifecycle.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unusual LSASS.exe access, failed login spikes from single source, keylogger injection into running processes, and suspicious registry queries for password storage locations.

suggestion.title: Dragon Weave Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Chinese state actor targeting Czech (NATO, sensitive sectors) and Taiwan (geopolitical value) implies high-value data exfiltration objective; no exfiltration-phase use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for large DNS query volumes to suspicious domains, bulk outbound connections during non-business hours, unusual access to sensitive file shares followed by external transfers, and encrypted tunneling traffic.

suggestion.title: CVE-2024-21182 Vulnerability Scanner Alert
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Anything in CISA KEV is *currently* being exploited' and recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' substituting CVE-2024-21182. Pipeline produced zero hunts despite this direct call-out.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vulnerability scanner detections for CVE-2024-21182 against Oracle WebLogic Server instances. Correlate with patch dates and federal due-date (2026-06-04) to identify unpatched assets under active exploitation.

suggestion.title: Unpatched WebLogic Server Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' and notes federal agencies must remediate by published due date. Requires inventory of WebLogic instances and patch compliance baseline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all Oracle WebLogic Server instances in the environment via CMDB/asset inventory. Cross-reference with patch level tracking to flag instances missing patches for CVE-2024-21182 as of federal due date.

suggestion.title: T3/IIOP Protocol Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies exploitation vector: 'unauthenticated attacker with network access via T3, IIOP.' Pipeline did not surface protocol-level detection for these proprietary Oracle protocols.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for inbound network traffic to Oracle WebLogic T3 (typically ports 7001, 7002) and IIOP (typically 7003, 7004) from untrusted sources. Correlate with failed authentication or unusual payload patterns indicative of exploit attempts.

suggestion.title: WebLogic Administration Interface Unauthorized Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states successful exploitation results in 'unauthorized access to critical data or complete access to all Oracle WebLogic Server accessible data.' Requires detection of auth bypass or unauthorized admin console access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Oracle WebLogic Server logs for unauthenticated or anomalous access to administration console, JNDI services, or data repositories. Flag login attempts from non-whitelisted IP ranges or patterns consistent with exploitation.

suggestion.title: Critical Data Access via WebLogic Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes impact: 'complete access to all Oracle WebLogic Server accessible data.' Detection should focus on data exfiltration indicators post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unusual or bulk data queries executed through compromised WebLogic data sources, particularly egressing sensitive tables or databases. Correlate timing with T3/IIOP exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Federal CISA KEV Patch Deadline Remediation Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Article sets explicit federal due date (2026-06-04) and notes 'Federal due-date dates also frequently match the timing your organisation will be asked about by auditors / regulators.' This is a compliance/timeline detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track remediation status of CVE-2024-21182 patches against the federal due date. Alert on any unpatched WebLogic instances remaining after 2026-06-04 to surface compliance violations.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Kernel Capability Assignments in Containers
suggestion.rationale: Article lists CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_SYS_MODULE, CAP_SYS_PTRACE, CAP_NET_ADMIN as escape vectors: 'Privileged containers CAP_SYS_ADMIN CAP_SYS_MODULE CAP_SYS_PTRACE CAP_NET_ADMIN'. No UC detects this container misconfiguration or runtime capability grants.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for containers launched with dangerous kernel capabilities (SYS_ADMIN, SYS_MODULE, SYS_PTRACE, NET_ADMIN) via docker inspect, kubelet logs, or orchestration API calls. These are direct precursors to container escape exploits and should trigger on any non-hardened deployment.

suggestion.title: Kubernetes Secrets Exfiltration via Supply Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'poisoning a Docker Hub repository to later steal Kubernetes secrets and other sensitive data' — a complete supply-chain-to-credential-theft chain. No UC models detection of secrets being accessed post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious access patterns to Kubernetes etcd, ConfigMap, or Secret API endpoints, especially from newly deployed containers or during image scanning operations. Correlate with recent Docker image pulls from untrusted registries.

suggestion.title: Malicious Payload Execution During Container Build/Scan
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'stealer that was loaded during the KICS scanning process' — payload execution triggered by security tooling itself. No UC detects this attack pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor security scanner processes (KICS, Trivy, Snyk, etc.) for unexpected child processes, network connections, or credential access. Alert on process execution originating from container image layers or build contexts outside known tooling.

suggestion.title: Docker Hub Repository Poisoning Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'compromised Checkmarx KICS across multiple attack chains for different vectors. This included poisoning a Docker Hub repository.' No UC for detecting repository or image integrity compromise signals.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unexpected changes to Docker Hub image manifests, layer counts, or scan results. Alert on pull-after-rescan disparities (image scanned clean, then rescanned with malicious layers). Monitor for images signed by untrusted signers or with modified digests.

suggestion.title: Container Escape via Host Kernel Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Container escape' and 'Exploiting host system vulnerabilities' as primary vectors. No UC detects kernel-level exploitation or namespace breakout attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for ptrace calls across namespace boundaries, /proc/sys access from container processes, mount syscalls with privileged flags, or cgroup escape patterns. Alert on container processes accessing host /proc/<PID>/ns/* or manipulating cgroup hierarchies.

suggestion.title: Orchestration API Abuse for Container Deployment
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 'Exploitation of orchestration APIs' as primary vector and 'Kubernetes secrets theft' outcome. No UC detects suspicious Kubernetes API calls for secret access or pod creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on service accounts or API tokens making unexpected get/list calls to secrets, configmaps, or serviceaccounts across namespaces. Flag pod creation with elevated permissions, host networking, or privileged containers from unusual source IPs or service accounts.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Web Application Vulnerability Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'no login, configuration changes, or admin access required' — requires detection of HTTP requests to Magento/Mirasvit cache endpoints without prior authentication session tokens, especially POST requests that may deliver serialized payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP POST/GET requests to Magento cache warmer paths (/mirasvit-cache/*, /cache/*) from untrusted sources that fail to include session cookies or Bearer tokens. Baseline legitimate cache-warming cron jobs and exclude. Flag rapid sequential requests as scanning behavior.

suggestion.title: PHP Object Injection Deserialization Attack
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly cites 'PHP object injection flaw' as the vulnerability mechanism — requires detection of serialized object patterns and unserialize() sink usage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP payloads containing PHP serialization markers (O:\d+: prefix, common gadget chains like Monolog\Handler) targeting plugin endpoints. Cross-reference with PHP error logs for unserialize() warnings. WAF should block known Magento gadget-chain payloads. High confidence if followed by process execution within 2-5 seconds.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Remote Code Execution Process Spawning
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability enables 'remotely execute malicious code' — successful exploitation surfaces as unexpected child processes spawned from web-server context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect parent process httpd/apache/php-fpm/nginx spawning suspicious children (cmd.exe, powershell, /bin/bash, /bin/sh) or executing from /tmp, /dev/shm, or Magento cache directories. High-confidence trigger: process creation timestamps within 5 seconds of HTTP POST to vulnerable Magento endpoint.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Creation in Magento Plugin Directories
suggestion.rationale: Successful RCE typically results in dropped webshells or backdoors in plugin cache paths; 'remotely execute' implies file-based persistence mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Magento plugin root (/app/code/Mirasvit/*, var/cache/*, var/www/html/app/*) for unexpected .php file creation by web-server UID. Alert on files containing suspicious functions (eval, system, passthru, base64_decode). Correlate creation timestamp with HTTP exploitation requests to vulnerable endpoints.

suggestion.title: Admin Account Creation from Web Application
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'exploit to create admin accounts'—privilege escalation and persistence mechanism. Pipeline missed the obvious privilege-elevation detection.
log_sources: Database audit logs for user creation
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for new local/domain admin account creation events correlated with recent web application deployment, plugin installation, or vulnerability exploitation timestamps. Flag accounts created by non-admin service principals or by web-application-owned service accounts.

suggestion.title: WP Maps Pro Plugin Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is in WP Maps Pro. Pipeline should detect attack vectors targeting this plugin—'WP Maps Pro' is the primary IOC and no exploitation detection UCs were generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to WordPress plugin directories containing 'wp-maps-pro' in path, or POST requests with parameters historically associated with plugin RCE/privilege escalation (e.g., unvalidated parameters, serialization patterns). Correlate with subsequent admin account creation or file upload events.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized User Registration or Privilege Escalation in WordPress
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation leads directly to admin account creation. Establish baseline of legitimate admin creation patterns and flag deviations. Article states 'actively exploited'—implies in-the-wild activity detectable via registration anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for user creation events with admin role assignment that deviate from normal provisioning workflow (e.g., no corresponding approval ticket, created from non-admin IP, created outside business hours). Flag bulk or rapid-succession account creation.

suggestion.title: Exploitation of Public-Facing WordPress Plugin
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector. Title establishes 'critical flaw' and 'actively exploited'—detection should cover parameter tampering, version-specific payloads, and post-exploitation behavioral indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to /wp-content/plugins/wp-maps-pro/ endpoints with known malicious parameter signatures, unusual encoding, or requests from IPs not in baseline web-service access patterns. Correlate with 4xx→2xx response transitions indicating bypass attempts.

suggestion.title: Multiple Failed Login Attempts from Geographically Distant Locations
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attempted logins from distant locations and unknown devices.' Pipeline missed the core brute-force signal—correlation of failed auths with geographic anomalies is table-stakes for credential-access defense.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on 5+ failed login attempts to a single user account from IP addresses in different geographic regions within 60 minutes. Correlate with account lockout events to confirm brute-force detection and severity.

suggestion.title: Device Registration Verification Emails Correlated with Failed Login Bursts
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The emails contained verification codes for legitimate account owners to register new devices' [following brute-force attempts]. This secondary auth flow is triggered by attack detection and serves as a detection signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate device verification email sends with immediately preceding failed login attempts. Flag accounts receiving 3+ verification emails within 24 hours from different geographic sources.

suggestion.title: Account Suspension Triggered by Brute-Force Threshold
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'suspension of those accounts as part of Dashlane's built-in security controls' following brute-force. Account lockout en masse is itself an indicator of active credential attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk account suspensions (10+ accounts within 1 hour) triggered by authentication anomaly rules. Cross-reference with external threat intel to assess whether attack is targeted, distributed, or opportunistic.

suggestion.title: Sequential Password Guessing: Same User, High Failure Rate
suggestion.rationale: Article defines attack as 'trying multiple passwords in succession until the correct one is found'—direct mapping to T1110.001 password-guessing tactic. Pipeline should have extracted this.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for 10+ failed login attempts to the same account from a single source IP within 5 minutes. Exclude legitimate retry patterns. Escalate if any attempt succeeds from same source IP immediately after brute-force sequence.

suggestion.title: Cross-Country Login Verification Chaining Against SaaS Password Managers
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'users...received notices of suspicious access requests from foreign countries.' Multiple verification events spanning distinct geographies is a fingerprint of distributed brute-forcing or credential-stuffing campaigns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag accounts with 3+ failed login attempts originating from 3+ different countries within 12 hours. Apply lower sensitivity threshold for password-manager SaaS platforms. Trigger mandatory secondary verification or account review.

suggestion.title: Brute-Force Targeting of Password-Manager User Base
suggestion.rationale: Article focuses attack surface as Dashlane users—password-manager accounts are high-value targets (compromise = lateral credential access). Pipeline should surface application-specific threat model.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For password-manager platforms: establish lower brute-force thresholds (3+ failures) compared to general SaaS. Correlate account vault size/credential count with attack targeting patterns to identify high-value compromise risk.
