suggestion.title: Unauthorized workspace member role enumeration and bulk privilege grant
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'forwards the request body's user_id and role straight into MemberService.add(workspace_id, user_id, role), which has no caller-permission check.' Attacker can enumerate valid workspace member IDs and grant arbitrary roles. Detection should correlate enumeration (repeated member lookups) followed by role-elevation POST.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequences of GET requests to /workspaces/{id}/members (enumeration) followed within minutes by POST to /workspaces/{id}/members with role elevation (owner, admin). Baseline per user; flag if a single actor sends >5 enumeration queries before privilege grant.

suggestion.title: Workspace member added to unrelated workspace
suggestion.rationale: CVE allows adding 'arbitrary user' with no cross-tenant boundary check apparent from description. Detection should flag when a user is added to a workspace they have no legitimate business accessing (requires workspace membership baseline or business-process intel).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track workspace membership changes. Flag when a new member is added to a workspace with no prior interaction history (no prior API calls, no login events from that identity in that workspace context).

suggestion.title: Workspace API authentication context mismatch — role grant from non-owner account
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'gated only by require_workspace_member(workspace_id) (default min_role="member")'. Means a low-privilege member can promote any user (including themselves) to owner. Should detect any POST /workspaces/{id}/members with role=owner originating from a non-owner account.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference POST /workspaces/{id}/members with the initiating user's role in that workspace (from authentication context or a membership table). Alert if a non-owner initiates owner-role grants. High precision if membership data is reliable.

suggestion.title: New workspace owner account created and used within minutes
suggestion.rationale: Follow-on impact after privilege escalation. Article describes arbitrary user can be added as owner; detection should catch the attacker escalating a freshly-created account they control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate user account creation events with workspace membership changes where the new user is immediately granted owner role (within 5 minutes), then performs authenticated actions in that workspace.

suggestion.title: Detect HTTP Requests Targeting WebSphere RCE Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attack vector as 'specially crafted HTTP requests' targeting WebSphere. No HTTP anomaly or request-pattern UC was generated despite this being the exploitation method.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to WebSphere Web Server Plug-ins endpoints with malformed or unusual payloads, particularly requests containing script/code markers or excessive URL encoding. Baseline against known WebSphere administrative endpoints.

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution via WebSphere Arbitrary Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article core impact is 'execute arbitrary code' but no code-execution or process-spawn detection was suggested. Missing execution-phase detection entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected child process spawning from WebSphere JVM processes (java.exe, wsadmin.sh) or unusual command-line arguments passed to WebSphere runtime. Look for System.Runtime.exec(), ProcessBuilder, or script-execution calls from WebSphere parent.

suggestion.title: WebSphere Patch Status / Vulnerability Assessment Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies CVE-2026-8633 and CVE-2026-8620 as affecting 'optional Web Server Plug-ins component'—a configuration-driven vulnerability. Hunt should enumerate WebSphere instances and confirm patch/configuration baseline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate WebSphere deployments via WMI, package managers, or registry heuristics. Cross-reference WebSphere Application Server version against CVE-2026-8633/CVE-2026-8620 affected versions. Flag unpatched or Web Server Plug-ins enabled instances.

suggestion.title: AppDomainManager Hijacking / SetAppDomainManager API Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article title and body center on 'AppDomainManager Hijacking to Evade EDR Detection' — this .NET-specific technique is the core attack vector but no detection rule targets it. Quote: 'sophisticated .NET hijacking technique to slip past endpoint defenses.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor .NET processes (w3wp.exe, dotnet.exe, csc.exe, msbuild.exe) for SetAppDomainManager API calls, AppDomain object instantiation, or System.Reflection.Emit use in memory contexts. Alert on CLR injection patterns and unusual assembly loading within AppDomain contexts.

suggestion.title: .NET Reflection-Based Execution and Runtime Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes .NET-based hijacking but provides no use case for detecting reflection abuse (System.Reflection.Assembly.Load, MethodInfo.Invoke) which is the delivery mechanism for AppDomainManager payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect .NET process memory anomalies: unusual System.Reflection namespace activity, dynamic assembly loading from non-standard paths, or suspicious Invoke/Emit patterns. Correlate with obfuscation indicators (strings entropy, packed assemblies).

suggestion.title: C2 Beaconing to OnlyOffice-Hosted Subdomains
suggestion.rationale: Article includes `docspace-y4cumb.onlyoffice.com` and `docspace-twpf0e.onlyoffice.com` — abuse of legitimate cloud services for C2 is high-fidelity when verified, but requires behavioral correlation to filter legitimate OnlyOffice users. Quote: network IOC hunt lists these but lacks execution-side filtering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect connections to listed OnlyOffice subdomains AND correlate with high-risk behavioral indicators: beaconing pattern (regular intervals), off-hours timing, unusual egress data volume, or non-standard user-agent. Exclude legitimate OnlyOffice syncing clients.

suggestion.title: Masquerading via Typosquat and Lookalike Domains
suggestion.rationale: Domains like `buisness-centeral-transportation.com` (note typo) and `ramiltonsfinance.com` masquerade as legitimate business entities. Article does not map T1036 (Masquerading) despite clear evidence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for DNS queries and resolutions to lookalike/typosquat domains; flag domains with common misspellings of Fortune 500 firms, financial institutions, or healthcare providers. Cross-reference with WHOIS for recent registration dates and registrar patterns associated with threat actors.

suggestion.title: File Hash Correlation with .NET Process Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article provides 12 SHA256 hashes without file type or metadata. Hunting these in isolation risks false negatives on variants; correlation with AppDomainManager/reflection abuse raises signal confidence. Pipeline should note detection requires behavioral pairing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Match the 12 provided SHA256 hashes AND require correlation with .NET process spawning, AppDomain creation, or memory injection events. Solitary hash hits are lower fidelity; behavioral context is critical.

suggestion.title: EDR Evasion Technique Detection — Memory Patching and Hook Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article's subtitle is 'Evade EDR Detection' but pipeline maps no use case for common EDR bypass techniques (kernel callback removal, AMSI bypass, Event Log tampering). Quote: technique is specifically designed to 'slip past endpoint defenses.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for AMSI.dll reflection/patching, WMI consumer suspension, Event Log channel deletion (wevtutil), or kernel callback tampering via SetWindowsHookEx/SetUnhandledExceptionFilter. Correlate with .NET process context to reduce FP.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Child Processes from npm/Node.js
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes a 'credential-stealing worm' deployed via npm packages. Worms typically spawn child processes to execute payloads or establish persistence — the article does not provide specific IOCs or process names, but this is a core attack pattern that must be detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child process spawning from node.exe or npm.exe with suspicious parents (npm install context). Look for cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or system utilities spawned with network connectivity patterns consistent with credential exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Credential Access from npm Package Execution Context
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'credential-stealing worm' — the pipeline missed detection rules for credential access APIs being invoked from npm-installed packages, which is the core payload behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect calls to credential APIs (DPAPI, vault access, browser credential stores, SSH key enumeration) originating from node.js processes or temporary npm module directories. Cross-correlate with network exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Package Registry Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article describes npm package compromise — pipeline should detect installation of packages from suspicious or typosquatted registry sources, unsigned packages, or packages with unexpected version jumps.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install/ci commands for registry URL anomalies, use of public registries when private expected, package version downgrades, or installation of packages not in lock files. Correlate with code signing failures.

suggestion.title: Worm Propagation via npm install Hooks
suggestion.rationale: Worms typically self-replicate; npm's preinstall/postinstall hooks are a known propagation vector. The article's 'worm' classification strongly suggests automated spread, but pipeline generated no detection for persistent npm hook modifications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation or modification of .npm, package.json, or lock file entries for postinstall/preinstall scripts containing obfuscated code, network calls, or spawning system processes. Flag unsigned or unexpected script additions.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of Credentials over C2 Channels
suggestion.rationale: Article title specifies credential stealing — pipeline missed detection for credential exfiltration patterns (bulk DNS queries, HTTPS POST to suspicious domains, memory access patterns consistent with credential dumping from running npm process).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate credential access signals with outbound network traffic from npm/node.js processes to non-standard ports or domains. Look for encrypted POST requests with large payloads, DNS exfiltration patterns, or HTTPS to IPs (not FQDN).

suggestion.title: File Write Activity in Node Modules and Sensitive Directories
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain malware must write persistence mechanisms or staged payloads to disk. Article does not specify, but worms typically stage second-stage payloads or modify application code. Pipeline missed file-based indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor writes to node_modules (outside package manager context), .npm directories, appdata/roaming paths, and startup folders originating from npm processes. Flag obfuscated script injection into package files.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Installation with Inline Credential Access
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly mentions 'npm Supply Chain Attack' and tokens stolen during install. Pipeline missed: 'codexui-android npm' package poisoning + credential theft vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm install/ci processes spawning child processes that access environment variables containing API keys, authentication tokens, or read .ssh directories. Flag processes exfiltrating credential-like strings over HTTP/HTTPS to non-package-registry hosts.

suggestion.title: OpenAI API Token Patterns in Build/CI Environments
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'OpenAI Codex Authentication Tokens' stolen — pipeline should detect token leakage patterns specific to OpenAI's sk-* prefix or org-* identifiers in logs/network traffic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for OpenAI token patterns (sk-[A-Za-z0-9]+ or org-[A-Za-z0-9]+) in process arguments, environment strings, or DNS/HTTP query strings. Correlate with npm install parent processes and non-production egress IPs.

suggestion.title: Malicious npm Package Registry Substitution or Typosquatting
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attack vector described in title: codexui-android poisoned. Pipeline should flag registry queries and package manifest downloads from untrusted sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm requests for 'codexui-android' or similar packages resolved to non-official npm registry CDNs or attacker-controlled domains. Flag package.json modifications that reference private/suspicious registries.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of Credentials via npm postinstall Scripts
suggestion.rationale: Typical npm supply-chain attack mechanism: postinstall hook exfiltrates tokens. Article indicates token theft but pipeline missed lifecycle hook execution detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm postinstall/preinstall/prepare script execution for child process spawning, environment variable access, or network calls. Cross-reference with known malicious package signatures or unexpected script content in node_modules.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized OpenAI API Calls from Compromised Build Systems
suggestion.rationale: Stolen tokens enable direct API abuse. Pipeline should detect anomalous API calls to api.openai.com or similar endpoints using leaked credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect API calls to openai.com/api/* endpoints from non-production CI/build networks or unusual request patterns (batch processing, quota exhaustion). Correlate with recent npm package installations and cross-reference token patterns in Authorization headers.

suggestion.title: Malicious npm Package Metadata or Version Pinning Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks often involve version confusion or dependency confusion. Article indicates 'codexui-android' was poisoned, but detection logic for identifying suspicious version metadata missing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm package.lock and yarn.lock files for unexpected version overrides, resolution to private registries, or packages with newer patch versions released in suspicious timeframes. Flag packages with mismatched author or sudden ownership changes.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated PowerShell execution with C2 beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly maps T1027 (Obfuscation) and T1071 (Application Layer Protocol) alongside RAT malware. UC_FAKECAPTCHA detects only execution initiation, not C2 phase. Gap phrase: 'remote access malware' with obfuscation strongly implies command-and-control communication not covered by existing detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PowerShell spawned from ClickFix execution context with command-line obfuscation patterns (base64 encoding, hex encoding, string reversal, double-encoded variables) initiating network connections to non-whitelisted destinations or IOC domains/IPs. High fidelity if combined with RAT C2 behavioral signatures (regular beaconing intervals, fixed ports, small request/response sizes).

suggestion.title: RAT malware persistence via registry and scheduled tasks
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'plant remote access malware' implying post-execution persistence mechanisms, but no detection covers registry modifications or scheduled task creation. Gap phrase: verb 'plant' indicates persistence (run keys, scheduled tasks, WMI subscriptions) is essential to the attack but undetected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious modifications to persistence-related registry hives (HKLM/HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\Run*, AppInit_DLLs, Shell Execute Hooks) or scheduled task creation issued by PowerShell/cmd.exe in the ClickFix execution context. Alert on rapid succession: script drop → execution → persistence write (delta < 10 seconds).

suggestion.title: Suspicious script file creation in temporary directories
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'ClickFix scripts' and 'malicious script' as the attack vector, but UC_FAKECAPTCHA detects only execution, not the file-drop phase. Gap phrase: 'malicious script' must be written to disk before execution — file creation in temp paths is a critical detection opportunity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect .ps1, .bat, .vbs, .js files being created in user-writable temp directories (%TEMP%, %APPDATA%\Local\Temp) by PowerShell, cmd.exe, or browser processes. Flag if followed within 1–5 seconds by execution (command line referencing the file) or permission modifications. Correlate with UC_FAKECAPTCHA to establish full ClickFix kill-chain.

suggestion.title: Android Accessibility Service Abuse – Device Control
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Abuses Accessibility Service to Control Devices.' This is the defining attack vector. Pipeline ignored the explicit technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for apps requesting accessibility service permissions, especially those installed from untrusted sources. Correlate permission grants with process behavior showing unintended device control (clicks, navigation, text input) without user interaction.

suggestion.title: Malicious Link – Banking App Masquerade Download
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'spreads through malicious links disguised as downloads from trusted, well-known applications.' Initial access via social engineering targeting financial apps.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect downloads of .apk files from external URLs to non-standard locations, especially those mimicking banking app names. Flag installation from non-Play Store sources following suspicious downloads.

suggestion.title: C2 – bitlrewards-app.com Domain Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists C2 domain. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs; this domain and IP 199.217.99.122 require immediate threat hunt deployment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on DNS queries and HTTP/HTTPS connections to bitlrewards-app.com from Android devices. Correlate with suspicious app installations and behavioral telemetry showing device control.

suggestion.title: Screen Overlay – Credential Interception
suggestion.rationale: Malware name 'OverlayPhantom' and threat description (targets banking credentials) indicate screen overlay attacks to intercept input or mimic legitimate banking UIs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for overlay windows created by non-banking apps positioned over known banking applications. Flag processes creating full-screen overlays with accessibility permissions.

suggestion.title: Malware Hash Matching – OverlayPhantom Variants
suggestion.rationale: Article provides 3 SHA256 hashes; pipeline extracted zero. File-based detection is foundational for banking trojans with multiple variants.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution or installation of files matching any of the three provided SHA256 hashes. Cross-reference with behavioral telemetry (accessibility service requests, network C2, credential access patterns).

suggestion.title: Dragon Weave C2 Beacon Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'Dragon Weave' conducting attacks; any APT campaign inherently requires command-and-control infrastructure which must be detectable via network telemetry
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound connections from Czech Republic and Taiwan network ranges to known malicious C2 infrastructure. Flag low-volume beaconing patterns with consistent timing intervals and small payload sizes characteristic of APT command channels.

suggestion.title: Web Application Exploitation and Shell Deployment
suggestion.rationale: Title references attacks hitting Czech Republic and Taiwan (likely government/critical infrastructure); initial access typically via web application exploitation followed by shell deployment for persistence
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual HTTP requests with SQL injection, command injection, or file traversal patterns to web applications. Flag subsequent file uploads to web-accessible directories and creation of executable files (aspx, jsp, php) in web roots.

suggestion.title: Process Execution from Web Server Process Context
suggestion.rationale: Web shell compromise leads to command execution; article describes active attack campaign implying execution phase activity post-exploitation
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on cmd.exe or powershell.exe spawned as child of w3wp.exe, apache2, nginx, or httpd with command-line arguments suggesting lateral movement or data exfiltration reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement to Critical Systems
suggestion.rationale: Targeting of nation-state entities (Czech Republic, Taiwan governments) implies post-compromise lateral movement to high-value assets within government networks
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for RDP connections, SMB file copies, and WinRM sessions between systems in different security zones or to systems with names matching government infrastructure patterns (parliament, ministry, defense).

suggestion.title: CVE-2024-21182 Exploitation via T3/IIOP Protocols
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated attacker with network access via T3, IIOP to compromise Oracle WebLogic Server'—explicit network attack vectors requiring network-layer monitoring and payload-level correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound connections to WebLogic T3 (port 7001) and IIOP (port 7002) from external sources. Detect T3 protocol malformation attempts, JNDI injection probes, or deserialization exploits. Correlate scan failures with successful connection within hours.

suggestion.title: Internet-Exposed WebLogic Server Asset Census
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Federal civilian agencies are required to remediate by published due date'—presupposes comprehensive asset enumeration; internet-facing instances are highest priority.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all WebLogic services on standard ports (7001, 7002, 7003). Cross-reference with asset database for exposure status, ownership, patch level. Flag internet-routable instances immediately; prioritize by compliance deadline.

suggestion.title: WebLogic Post-Compromise Data Access and Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Successful attacks result in unauthorized access to critical data or complete access to all Oracle WebLogic Server accessible data'—direct impact pathway from exploitation to data harvest.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk data retrieval queries in WebLogic audit logs post-exploitation window. Monitor for large-volume outbound connections from WebLogic hosts (netflow threshold). Correlate timing of successful T3 connections with subsequent data access spikes.

suggestion.title: WebLogic Network Reconnaissance (T3 Service Discovery)
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'network access' as exploitation prerequisite—attacker must discover WebLogic services before T1190 exploitation attempt; T1046 precedes T1190.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect external scans of WebLogic ports (7001–7003) from single source. Look for T3 banner-grab attempts, JNDI probes, or multi-port sequential scanning. Alert on two-phase signature: scan failures followed by successful connection within 24 hours.

suggestion.title: Docker Hub Supply Chain Poisoning - Compromised Image Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'poisoning a Docker Hub repository to later steal Kubernetes secrets' as TeamPCP's attack vector. No detection UC generated for supply chain image compromise despite this being the attack entry point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for pulls of Docker images from DockerHub with suspicious metadata, mismatched signatures, or unexpected digest changes. Flag images pulled from non-standard registries or with layer injection indicators. Correlate image pull timestamps with known compromise windows.

suggestion.title: Privileged Container Capability Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article enumerates CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_SYS_MODULE, CAP_SYS_PTRACE, CAP_NET_ADMIN as container escape vectors but pipeline generated no detection for these dangerous capabilities being granted to containers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on containers instantiated with CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_SYS_MODULE, CAP_SYS_PTRACE, or CAP_NET_ADMIN capabilities. Cross-reference against container image manifest policy. Flag privilege escalation syscalls (ptrace, module loading) from processes within privileged containers.

suggestion.title: Kubernetes Secrets Theft via API Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article highlights 'steal Kubernetes secrets and other sensitive data' as a core objective but no UC for detecting unauthorized Kubernetes secret enumeration or exfiltration patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Kubernetes API server logs for get/list operations against Secret and ConfigMap resources from unexpected service accounts or namespaces. Alert on bulk secret enumeration (>5 secrets listed in < 1 minute). Correlate with process-level credential access (environment variable reads).

suggestion.title: Malware Execution During Container Image Scanning
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'stealer that was loaded during the KICS scanning process' but no UC captures suspicious execution patterns triggered by image scanning tools.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected child processes spawned by image scanning tools (KICS, Trivy, Grype, etc.). Flag network connections initiated from scanning tool contexts. Alert on file writes to sensitive directories (/etc, /root, /var/lib) during or immediately after scanning operations.

suggestion.title: Orchestration API Abuse - Unauthorized Controller Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'orchestration API abuse' as a multi-stage attack vector but no UC generated for detecting unauthorized Kubernetes API access or token misuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Kubernetes API audit logs for token validation failures, unauthorized resource requests, and cross-namespace access from service accounts. Alert on API calls from container processes using escalated tokens or from unexpected source IPs.

suggestion.title: Container Runtime Vulnerability Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 'Exploiting vulnerabilities in the host system and container runtime components' but pipeline provided no detection for container runtime CVE exploitation patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious syscall patterns from container processes (unshare, prctl, clone with CLONE_NEWUSER/NEWNET). Alert on ptrace-family syscalls targeting host processes. Flag attempts to read /proc/sys or write to cgroup directories from containers.

suggestion.title: PHP Object Injection Attack Against Magento Cache Plugin
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated PHP object injection flaw'—a specific attack vector the pipeline completely missed despite clear keyword presence in narrative.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST/GET requests to Magento cache plugin endpoints for serialized PHP object payloads (base64-encoded PHP:// or phar:// streams, __wakeup/__destruct magic methods). Alert on requests lacking valid authentication tokens that contain suspicious object instantiation patterns.

suggestion.title: Asset Inventory: Magento Installations Running Vulnerable Mirasvit Cache Warmer
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'Mirasvit Cache Warmer, a full-page cache extension used by thousands'—specific product scope for asset discovery. Pipeline recommended this hunt in article text but failed to generate it.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset management databases, plugin registries, or web fingerprinting results for Magento instances running Mirasvit Cache Warmer. Cross-reference against CVE-2026-45247 scope to identify exposed targets before exploitation.

suggestion.title: Post-RCE Process Execution Following PHP Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'remotely execute malicious code' after injection—describes execution phase. Pipeline failed to generate detection for post-exploitation process spawning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP requests with serialized PHP objects to Magento cache endpoints with immediate child process creation (bash, sh, cmd) under web server user context. Baseline normal process ancestry and flag anomalous spawning within 0-10 seconds of malicious request timestamp.

suggestion.title: Indirect Code Execution via PHP Gadget Chain Deserialization
suggestion.rationale: Article describes PHP object injection leading to RCE—a gadget-chain attack pattern explicitly missing from technique list (T1202 not extracted).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor application logs for PHP deserialization of untrusted input, instantiation of unexpected classes during object reconstruction, or gadget-chain signatures (e.g., ysoserial patterns, Composer library magic methods). Flag __wakeup, __destruct, or __call invocations on unexpected objects.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized WordPress Admin Account Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states exploitation results in 'Create Admin Accounts'—highest-impact persistence mechanism in WordPress, directly mentioned in attack outcome.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on wp_users table INSERT or UPDATE operations outside scheduled admin maintenance windows that assign administrator role to previously non-existent users. Correlate with web service (www-data, apache) process context and anomalous user_registered timestamps.

suggestion.title: WP Maps Pro Plugin Exploitation—RCE Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Named vulnerability vector in title ('WP Maps Pro Flaw')—exploitation to admin-account creation implies unauthenticated or low-privilege code execution capability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST/GET to /wp-content/plugins/wp-maps-pro/ or derivative paths with parameter injection, serialization gadgets, or file-inclusion patterns. Flag responses with 200 OK or 500 errors indicating successful code path traversal, before admin-account creation events occur.

suggestion.title: WordPress Plugin Directory Write during Web Service Execution
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation would require ability to write webshell or malicious code to plugin directory; unusual file writes in wp-content/plugins should be visible before persistence (admin account) is created.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file create or modify operations in /wp-content/plugins/wp-maps-pro/ by web service processes, especially PHP or shell files created outside standard plugin-update windows. Correlate file timestamp with subsequent wp_users table modifications.

suggestion.title: Anomalous WordPress Admin API Access Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Once unauthorized admin created, attacker gains ability to modify site configuration, deploy backdoor plugins, and enroll additional users—detect post-compromise persistence movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag mass plugin-installation, theme-upload, or user-enrollment API calls from newly created or rarely-used admin accounts within minutes of account creation. Monitor wp-admin dashboard access logs for bulk user modifications or backup downloads.

suggestion.title: CVE-Based Vulnerability Scanning Traffic for WP Maps Pro
suggestion.rationale: Active exploitation in the wild implies scanning campaigns; inbound probes to known vulnerability endpoints should be detectable as baseline-separable anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on repeated HTTP 404/403/500 responses to WP Maps Pro plugin paths from external sources, especially when payloads contain URL-encoded injection, traversal sequences, or WordPress admin path references. Group by source IP and time delta.

suggestion.title: Database Activity: wp_users Enrollment Outside Admin Console
suggestion.rationale: Direct account creation via SQL injection or plugin-database access would bypass normal WordPress user-registration workflows and leave detectable query patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor database audit logs for INSERT/UPDATE to wp_users bypassing wp_create_user() function. Detect direct user_login assignments with user_pass hashes inserted in single transaction, or UPDATE operations that escalate existing low-privilege users to administrator role without privilege-management audit trail.

suggestion.title: Brute Force: Multiple Failed Login Attempts Per Account
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'brute-force attacks that attempted logins from distant locations and unknown devices.' Fundamental detection for account takeover defense. No corresponding use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag accounts with >5 failed login attempts within 5 minutes from any source IP. Dashlane triggered lockout at this threshold; detection correlates failed-attempt volume to account and source, blocking credential enumeration.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Device Registration During Login Storm
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'emails contained verification codes for legitimate account owners to register new devices' sent during failed login waves. No detection for pairing brute-force attempts with device-onboarding events.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when device-registration verification emails spike in volume during concurrent multi-account login-failure storms. Indicates attacker pairing brute-force with automated device-enrollment to establish persistence.

suggestion.title: Geographic Anomaly: Login from Distant/Unexpected Country
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states users 'received notices of suspicious access requests from foreign countries' and logins 'from distant locations.' No geolocation-based anomaly rule generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag login attempts from countries absent in user's 90-day history, or detect impossible travel (login in USA at 2pm, then login in China 30min later). Brute-force attackers operate from infrastructure unrelated to legitimate user geography.

suggestion.title: Account Lockout Spike — Defensive Response to Mass Brute Force
suggestion.rationale: Article states accounts 'were suspended as part of Dashlane's built-in security controls' in response to brute force. No detection for sudden lockout volume indicating platform-wide attack detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for rapid increase in account-lockout events across user population within short window. Indicates security control activation against coordinated brute-force attack; correlate with failed-login spike to confirm attack context.

suggestion.title: Verification Email Storm: Multiple Device-Registration Requests Per Account
suggestion.rationale: Article describes impacted users receiving multiple 'verification codes...to register new devices' from attackers. No rate-based detection on legitimate account's device-enrollment email volume.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when single account receives >3 device-registration verification emails within 10 minutes, especially if paired with failed login attempts from multiple IPs. Indicates account is under active brute-force and attacker is attempting device hijack.

suggestion.title: Suspicious HTTP requests to WebSphere plug-in endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability triggered via 'specially crafted HTTP requests' to 'Web Server Plug-ins component.' Detectable via HTTP request pattern anomalies to known WebSphere ports (80, 443, 8080, 9080) with atypical payload signatures or request morphology.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP access logs to WebSphere endpoints for requests with unusual headers, content-length anomalies, or serialization payloads characteristic of Java deserialization attacks. Establish baseline of legitimate plug-in traffic and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Unexpected process execution from WebSphere service account
suggestion.rationale: Article describes RCE via crafted requests, implying code execution on the target server. Attackers would spawn child processes from the WebSphere process context to execute commands post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected process spawning from WebSphere service accounts (e.g., was*, db2*, websphere*), particularly cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, or reverse-shell patterns. Correlate with HTTP access logs to WebSphere ports within 1-2 seconds.

suggestion.title: Outbound network connections from WebSphere to external C2
suggestion.rationale: Post-RCE, attackers typically establish C2 channels. Article threat profile indicates 'critical' risk and 'enterprise deployments,' suggesting multi-stage attacks requiring persistent callback.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound connections from WebSphere server IPs to non-whitelisted external IPs or domains, especially on high ports (>10000). Correlate with process execution events from suspicious child processes to establish attack chain confidence.

suggestion.title: WebSphere privilege escalation or lateral movement via RCE
suggestion.rationale: Article vulnerability allows 'arbitrary code execution,' which enables attackers to escalate privileges or move laterally. Monitor for AD/LDAP enumeration, service account compromise, or filesystem access outside normal WebSphere scope.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on administrative tool execution (whoami, net user, runas) spawned from WebSphere child processes, or unexpected file access to system directories (Windows\System32, /etc) initiated by WebSphere context.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-8633 and CVE-2026-8620 asset exposure hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists two CVE identifiers affecting WebSphere. Standard vulnerability management requires identifying all internet-facing WebSphere instances matching affected versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query CMDB or vulnerability scanner results for WebSphere Application Server instances with versions matching CVE-2026-8633 or CVE-2026-8620 scope. Cross-reference with network exposure (ports 80, 443, 8080, 9080 reachable from internet). Prioritize instances running optional Web Server Plug-ins component per article.

suggestion.title: AppDomainManager Class Instantiation / Hijacking Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title and body emphasize 'sophisticated .NET hijacking technique' via AppDomainManager to 'slip past endpoint defenses'. This is the core attack vector. No execution-phase UC generated despite being explicitly described. AppDomainManager hijacking loads malicious .NET code at app startup, bypassing standard execution controls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual AppDomainManager class loads or instantiation. Flag .NET processes spawning from unexpected code paths (temp, user profile, network shares). Alert on environment variables APPDOMAIN_MANAGER_ASM or APPDOMAIN_MANAGER_TYPE being set by non-system processes. Cross-reference with AMSI telemetry for obfuscated .NET bytecode execution.

suggestion.title: C2 Network Beaconing to AppDomainManager Malware Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 6 domains as IOCs in high-confidence section (buisness-centeral-transportation.com, premierhealthadvisory.com, ramiltonsfinance.com, business-startup.org, docspace-y4cumb.onlyoffice.com, docspace-twpf0e.onlyoffice.com). These are explicitly tagged as C2-phase IOCs. Pipeline generated zero network-based hunts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound DNS requests or HTTP/S connections to the 6 known C2 domains. High confidence: newly-disclosed malware C2 infrastructure. Correlate connection timing with unexpected process execution or AppDomainManager loading. Monitor for both direct connections and DNS-over-HTTPS bypasses.

suggestion.title: Malware File Hash Matching (12 Known AppDomainManager Samples)
suggestion.rationale: Article provides 12 SHA256 hashes marked 'high-fidelity only'. Despite explicit IOC labeling, no hash-based file detection UC was generated. These are likely the .NET hijacking payloads or loaders.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create file-hash alerts for all 12 SHA256s. Prioritize matches in AppData, Temp, ProgramData, and user-writable directories. Correlate with .NET process execution (msiexec.exe, powershell.exe, rundll32.exe, or managed executables). Flag any write/execute sequence within 24 hours of initial detection.

suggestion.title: .NET Framework Registry Configuration Tampering
suggestion.rationale: AppDomainManager hijacking requires registry modifications (typically HKLM\Software\Microsoft\.NET Framework\*). Article emphasizes 'sophisticated' .NET technique and EDR evasion—registry abuse is the mechanism. No registry-tamper UC suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor writes to HKLM\Software\Microsoft\.NET Framework* and HKCU\Software\Microsoft\.NET Framework, especially APPDOMAIN_MANAGER_* value writes. Flag SecurityManager registry modifications or CLR config changes. Correlate with unexpected .NET application execution or child process spawning.

suggestion.title: Process Injection via .NET Runtime (In-Memory Assembly Loading)
suggestion.rationale: AppDomainManager hijacking typically loads malicious assemblies in-memory at .NET process startup. Article describes 'sophisticated' technique and provides 12 malware hashes (likely stages or final payload). No injection/in-memory execution UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on .NET runtimes (clr.dll, coreclr.dll, System.Reflection.Assembly) loading unsigned or anomalously-sourced .NET assemblies. Monitor for parent-child process relationships where a .NET app spawns unexpected children (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, net.exe). Cross-reference with file hashes: matches against the 12 known malware SHA256s.

suggestion.title: Spear-Phishing or Watering Hole to Regional Targets (US/Israel/UAE)
suggestion.rationale: Article states campaign 'intensified following a regional conflict that began on February 28, 2026' targeting 'United States, Israel, and the United Arab Emirates'. Domain names (premierhealthadvisory.com, ramiltonsfinance.com) suggest business impersonation. No initial-access UC despite clear regional targeting and phishing-domain pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for emails or URLs from IOC domains targeting users in US, Israel, UAE. Flag lookalike domains mimicking healthcare/financial services. Alert on .lnk, .exe, .msi, or Office macro downloads from C2 domains. Correlate with geolocation and regional targeting patterns post-Feb-28-2026.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Installation from Untrusted Registry
suggestion.rationale: Article headline indicates supply-chain attack on 'Red Hat npm Packages'—pipeline should have flagged installation of packages from non-canonical sources or unsigned packages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm or yarn install commands executed against external or suspicious registries, or installation of packages with mismatched publisher metadata. Alert when npm_config_registry environment variable points to non-standard hosts or when package-lock.json contains unpinned versions from compromised ranges.

suggestion.title: Worm-like Process Spawning from node_modules Binaries
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'credential-stealing worm'—implies self-propagating child processes. Pipeline should detect multiple process spawns originating from node_modules directories or npm-installed executables.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation chains where parent=node.exe or parent=npm.cmd and child processes spawn with high frequency or fan-out patterns. Flag execution of unsigned scripts in node_modules/.bin/ directories and detection of recursive child-process trees from package binaries.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting from Environment Variables and Shell Configuration
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly mentions 'credential-stealing'—pipeline must surface detection of processes reading .bashrc, .bash_profile, .zshrc, env vars, or credential stores from npm/node context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect node.exe, npm, or child processes reading environment variables (env, getenv calls in process memory), accessing credential files (~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.kube), or calling credential managers (aws sts, vault, kubectl get secret). Flag use of process-env modules or dotenv in untrusted packages.

suggestion.title: Egress Connections to C2 from npm Installer Processes
suggestion.rationale: Credential-stealing worm implies command-and-control exfiltration. Pipeline should detect network connections from npm, node, or package post-install scripts to attacker infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound HTTPS/DNS from npm.exe, node.exe, or child processes spawned during install/postinstall hooks. Flag DNS queries for suspicious domains or IP ranges, especially if query originates from node_modules or post-install scripts. Correlate with credential environment variables in process memory.

suggestion.title: Persistence via npm postinstall Scripts with Concealment
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain worm requires re-execution—pipeline should detect malicious postinstall scripts in package.json or .npmrc that install hidden tasks, cron jobs, or scheduled tasks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation or modification of package.json postinstall/postuninstall scripts that call external executables, download scripts, or invoke system commands. Alert on cron entries, Windows scheduled tasks, or registry Run keys created from npm post-install context. Flag obfuscated or base64-encoded scripts in package manifests.

suggestion.title: Package Manifest Tampering and Dependency Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article title specifies 'compromised packages'—pipeline should alert on modifications to package-lock.json, yarn.lock, or shrinkwrap files that differ from published checksums, or installation of typo-squatted or dependency-injected packages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected modifications to dependency lock files outside of developer activity, or installation of packages with names similar to legitimate Red Hat libraries. Flag npm module resolution that loads from local/relative paths instead of registry. Correlate with failed integrity checks or mismatched SRI (Subresource Integrity) hashes.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Preinstall Script Execution in npm Packages
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes payload delivery via preinstall hook: 'npm runs preinstall scripts automatically during npm install, before any of your own code executes'. This is the execution vector for credential harvesting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect 'npm install' (or 'npm ci') process spawning child processes (node.js) for scripts not in user-controlled package.json files, or preinstall scripts executing network calls, environment variable reads, or file access to credential stores. High-fidelity signal: node process spawned by npm with arguments including eval() or atypical file/registry access within milliseconds of install completion.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Package Republishing by Compromised Identity
suggestion.rationale: Article describes worm propagation: 'It queries the registry for other packages the compromised identity can publish and republishes them, carrying the same payload'. This is the lateral movement that amplifies the attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm registry access logs or GitHub Actions logs for republish operations on packages authored by a user, especially when republish frequency is abnormally high, new versions are pushed without code review approval, or publishing happens from CI/CD contexts (GitHub Actions) with OIDC tokens rather than static credentials.

suggestion.title: GitHub OIDC Token Requested by Unexpected Workflow
suggestion.rationale: Article describes root cause: 'Those commits added a minimal GitHub Actions workflow that: Triggered on push to any branch. Requested a GitHub OIDC identity token via id-token: write.' This is the trust chain abuse that enables authentic-looking malicious publishing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GitHub Actions workflows (especially newly added or on orphan commits) requesting id-token: write permission, especially if the workflow then makes calls to npm registry or git push operations. Correlate with repositories not in allow-list or branches without code review history.

suggestion.title: Cloud Identity Enumeration During Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article highlights new capability: 'The notable change in this variant is a pair of new collectors for GCP and Azure that enumerate every identity the infected host can assume'. This discovery phase activity is detectable via API audit logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid enumeration of cloud service principals, roles, permissions in GCP and Azure during or immediately after npm package installation. Look for enumerate-all-identities patterns (list service accounts, list role assignments, get account metadata) initiated from CI/CD or development host contexts with no prior pattern of such queries.

suggestion.title: Credentials Exfiltrated from Package Installation Context
suggestion.rationale: Article states payload 'Harvests secrets and credentials from the local environment and CI context: environment variables, ~/.npmrc tokens, SSH keys, GitHub tokens, and CI/CD secrets.' This collection phase requires network exfiltration detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect node.js or npm-spawned processes reading ~/.npmrc, ~/.ssh/, environment variable dumps, or CI secret files (${CI_TOKEN}, ${GITHUB_TOKEN}, AWS credential files) followed by network exfiltration. Particularly high-confidence if file reads occur in rapid succession across multiple credential types during preinstall execution.

suggestion.title: Commits Pushed Without Code Review to Sensitive Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Article describes bypass: 'pushed malicious orphan commits directly into two RedHatInsights repositories, bypassing code review.' This is the initial access + execution step that enables everything downstream.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect commits pushed to RedHat or other sensitive namespace repositories that lack code review approval or merge request, especially orphan commits or commits that introduce GitHub Actions workflows. Baseline expected push patterns for repository and flag deviations (unusual time, unusual author context, unusual commit size/scope).

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Download Spike
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attack distributes malicious npm package 'codexui-android' — pipeline missed initial distribution vector entirely. Title establishes: 'OpenAI Codex Authentication Tokens Stolen in codexui-android npm Supply Chain Attack'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect first-time or version-mismatched npm package downloads followed by unusual child process spawning or network egress to non-npm registries. Correlate package name against known-malicious npm feed.

suggestion.title: API Token Exfiltration via Malicious npm Module
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states tokens are stolen — attack vector is package installation triggering credential access. Pipeline recognized zero credential-access indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for installed npm modules reading environment variables containing 'OPENAI', 'API', or 'TOKEN' patterns. Detect process spawned by npm post-install scripts accessing ~/.netrc, ~/.ssh, or credentials from memory.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized API Token Usage Post-Infection
suggestion.rationale: Compromised OpenAI Codex tokens will be used by attacker; pipeline should flag token usage anomalies. No exfiltration-phase detection suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on OpenAI API calls from unexpected source IPs, geographic locations, or request patterns (bulk completion requests, model access outside normal developer workflow). Correlate token with package installation timeline.

suggestion.title: npm Package Manifest / Dependency Chain Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Malicious npm packages often introduce unexpected dependencies or post-install scripts. Title mentions package distribution but pipeline extracted no dependency-graph signals.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm packages with excessive or suspicious post-install scripts (curl, sh, env-var exports). Alert on version publish times inconsistent with package maintainer history or dependency bloat in minor/patch updates.

suggestion.title: Supply-Chain Attack Vector: npm Registry Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Compromised package implies either registry takeover or account compromise. Pipeline should flag re-publish anomalies. Article mentions 'npm Supply Chain Attack' but no registry-level detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected version republishes from new IP/account, package metadata edits (author, description), or rapid version increments. Cross-reference with compromised credential indicators.

suggestion.title: Developer Environment Token Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Stolen tokens originate from developer machines installing the malicious package. Pipeline should cover local token collection indicators absent from output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm post-install scripts accessing .bash_history, .zsh_history, environment variables, or credential files. Alert on spawned sub-processes (curl, wget) exfiltrating data to non-standard domains during package installation.

suggestion.title: Persistent XenoRAT Autostart Mechanism Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'persistent remote access tool called XenoRAT'—XenoRAT requires persistence mechanisms to survive reboot. Pipeline extracted zero kill-chain phases and entirely missed Persistence phase despite 'persistent' being explicit in threat description.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for XenoRAT SHA256 hashes creating registry autostart entries (HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run) or scheduled tasks. Monitor for XenoRAT process execution originating from %AppData%\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup paths.

suggestion.title: Spear Phishing Targeting Afghanistan Finance Ministry Officials
suggestion.rationale: Article states campaign 'targeted provincial finance officials across all 34 Afghan Mustoufiats'—this precision targeting indicates spear-phishing or credential-harvesting initial access vector. No T1566 or initial-access technique detected despite clear targeting of specific government finance personnel.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for emails to @finance.gov.af recipients with XenoRAT-matched SHA256 attachment hashes or emails linking to abimj.edu.af domain. Correlate email delivery timestamp with subsequent XenoRAT execution on recipient device.

suggestion.title: C2 Beaconing to XenoRAT Command Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies 3 C2 IP addresses (185.235.137.106, 103.132.98.224, 103.132.98.226) and domain abimj.edu.af as IOCs. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs, leaving C2 communication completely invisible to detection hunts despite being fundamental to monitoring persistent RAT operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for outbound DeviceNetworkEvents from systems with XenoRAT-matched hashes connecting to 185.235.137.106, 103.132.98.224, or 103.132.98.226. Flag DNS resolution of abimj.edu.af from finance.gov.af network endpoints; flag any non-HTTPS egress to Pakistani IP space.

suggestion.title: User Execution of XenoRAT from Phishing Attachment
suggestion.rationale: To successfully deliver XenoRAT to 'provincial finance officials,' attack requires user interaction—opening malicious attachment or executing file. T1204 bridges phishing delivery to malware execution but was not detected by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for XenoRAT SHA256 hashes executed from typical phishing-delivery directories (%TEMP%, %Downloads%, %AppData%\Local\Temp, email cache). Look for XenoRAT process launch immediately following user interaction with Office process (winword.exe, excel.exe, outlook.exe).

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration from Afghanistan Finance Ministry Systems Over C2
suggestion.rationale: XenoRAT is deployed specifically to 'Afghanistan's Ministry of Finance'—primary mission objective is exfiltration of financial records, budgets, and ledgers. T1041 (Exfiltration Over C2 Channel) is core to RAT operations but was not detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for abnormally large data transfers (>5MB) from finance.gov.af systems to C2 infrastructure (185.235.137.106, 103.132.98.224, 103.132.98.226, abimj.edu.af). Monitor XenoRAT process file access to finance databases (.mdb, .accdb, .xlsx, .csv containing budget/transaction records) followed by network egress.

suggestion.title: Newly Registered Domain Mimicking Legitimate Service + High Click-Through
suggestion.rationale: Article states victims are 'lured through fake verification pages'—a core ClickFix tactic. No detection rules address the hosting infrastructure (fake domain registration or suspicious whois age). Should flag clicks to domains registered <7 days ago that contain keywords like 'verify', 'authenticate', 'captcha', 'login', 'confirm' and spike in click volume.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate recent domain registration (whois age <7 days) with content keywords matching fake CAPTCHA/verification patterns to newly registered C2 hosting infrastructure. Flag if the domain appears in phishing emails or web proxy logs.

suggestion.title: RAT Installation Post-ClickFix Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'quietly planting remote access malware'—but no post-exploitation detection. Should detect common RAT behaviors: service creation with binary in temp/users folder, scheduled task with suspicious parent, or registry run keys pointing to unsigned executables launched from user writable locations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After clipboard-spawned PowerShell execution, hunt for service creation (sc.exe, New-Service) or schtasks with parent=powershell.exe. Correlate to binary writes in %temp%, %appdata%, or ProgramData with .exe/.vbs/.ps1 files, especially unsigned.

suggestion.title: RAT C2 Communication on Suspicious Ports/Protocols
suggestion.rationale: Article lists C2 infrastructure IPs but no behavioral detection for RAT communication. T1071 (Application Layer Protocol) is mapped but underspecified. Should detect non-browser processes making outbound HTTP/HTTPS/DNS to article IPs or domains, or unusual port usage from client machines.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound connections from non-browser processes (not chrome/edge/firefox) to IoCs (178.156.165.82, 178.156.173.194, 89.110.110.119, 185.163.47.217, hiddenplanetlab.top, silverharvestnetwork.com) or to non-standard HTTP ports (8080, 8443, 81, 8888). Correlate to processes spawned by powershell.

suggestion.title: Clipboard Monitoring & Injection Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: ClickFix specifically abuses Windows clipboard. Article mentions 'malicious copy and paste' (T1204.004) and 'clipboard-injected PowerShell' but no behavioral rule detects the clipboard operation itself. Should monitor clipboard access sequences: web browser copy → explorer/clipboard manager read → powershell spawn.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect clipboard.exe, clipbrd.exe, or WinClip.exe spawning unusual children, or monitor for rapid clipboard read operations followed by ProcessCreate with suspicious parent (explorer, RuntimeBroker). Flag if the process inheriting clipboard data is powershell/cmd/mshta.

suggestion.title: Masquerading Fake Verification Page Content Matching
suggestion.rationale: Victims are deceived by 'fake verification pages that trick them into running a malicious script'. No detection for the page content itself (T1036.005 masquerading). Should detect when inbound email contains URLs hosting pages with Microsoft/Google/Apple/AWS logos, captcha UI elements, or 'verify your account' templates served from newly registered or compromised domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: When email is delivered with URL, fetch & analyze landing page HTML for masquerading indicators: brand logos (verified_logo, microsoft_logo), fake form elements (password fields, MFA prompts), and social engineering text ('verify your account', 'confirm identity'). Flag domain reputation and WHOIS age in parallel.

suggestion.title: SmartApeSG Indicator Enrichment & Retalking
suggestion.rationale: Campaign name 'SmartApeSG' appears in title and threat profile but is not cross-referenced to prior intelligence, actor profiles, or related IOCs. Should maintain actor-indexed library of known SmartApeSG infrastructure from prior campaigns to increase hit rate on partial overlaps.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enrich the 6 new IOCs (4 IPs, 2 domains) against historical SmartApeSG campaign data. If 'SmartApeSG' has used similar domain patterns, registrars, ASNs, or IP ranges before, flag correlated infrastructure. Widen hunting scope to WHOIS email, NS servers, or SSL cert common names shared with prior campaigns.

suggestion.title: Android Accessibility Service Abuse for Device Control
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly: 'Abuses Accessibility Service to Control Devices'—core privilege escalation and persistence mechanism completely missed by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag apps requesting AccessibilityService permissions with unusual capability combinations (screen capture, input injection, device admin). Alert on accessibility-enabled apps interacting with banking/wallet app UI or attempting to capture credential input. Correlate with post-May 2025 installation dates.

suggestion.title: Malicious APK Installation via Deceptive Links
suggestion.rationale: Narrative: 'spreads through malicious links disguised as downloads from trusted, well-known applications.' Initial access / execution vector not modeled.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect browser APK downloads immediately followed by PackageManager installation. Flag downloads from domains masquerading as banking/reward apps (bitlrewards-app.com pattern). Alert on app installations with names matching legitimate banking/crypto apps but sourced outside Play Store.

suggestion.title: Banking App Overlay Attack via Accessibility Service
suggestion.rationale: Targets 'banking credentials, financial data, and cryptocurrency accounts'—overlay-based credential harvesting mechanism not detected despite being implicit in accessibility service abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate accessibility service activity with suspicious windows drawn over banking app UI. Monitor for accessibility-enabled apps reading view hierarchies of payment/credential fields. Alert on rapid window state transitions and touch input patterns captured during legitimate app credential entry.

suggestion.title: File Hash and C2 Domain Correlation
suggestion.rationale: IOCs provided (3 SHA256 hashes, bitlrewards-app.com, 199.217.99.122) but no hunt linking malware samples to network C2 communication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on devices matching any of the 3 file hashes establishing HTTP/HTTPS or DNS queries to bitlrewards-app.com or IP 199.217.99.122. Enrich with device context: banking app installations, crypto wallets, location history.

suggestion.title: Multi-Country Campaign Timeline and Geography Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'targeting users across ten countries' and 'active since May 2025'—campaign scope and temporal markers should drive geo-based and timeline detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference device locations, language settings, and financial app installations against 10 target countries. Correlate hash installations with campaign start (May 2025). Aggregate detections by region and timeline to identify outbreak waves and prioritize incident response.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Wallet Targeting via Banking Trojan
suggestion.rationale: Explicitly targets 'cryptocurrency accounts' yet no detection for malware accessing crypto wallet apps (MetaMask, Trust Wallet, Coinbase, etc.).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for post-May 2025 installations of banking + cryptocurrency wallet apps on same device. Alert on accessibility-enabled apps attempting to read or inject input into crypto wallet UIs. Flag simultaneous network connections from device to banking C2 and crypto exchange infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Exposure: Oracle WebLogic Server Internet-Accessible
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated attacker with network access' can exploit—establishes that WebLogic exposure is necessary precondition for attack. Asset inventory hunt is canonical first detection step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for WebLogic Server instances accessible from untrusted networks. Monitor inbound connections to ports 7001, 7002, 8001, 8002 from Internet. Cross-reference with vulnerability scanner output for CVE-2024-21182 presence to identify exploitation risk.

suggestion.title: Protocol: T3/IIOP Traffic to WebLogic Ports
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attack vector is 'network access via T3, IIOP'—these are Oracle-specific application-layer protocols that warrant dedicated protocol-level detection rules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor T3 (7001–7002) and IIOP (7001–7003) protocol traffic to WebLogic instances. Alert on: external-sourced T3/IIOP connections, failed handshakes indicating exploit attempts, volumetric spikes in protocol requests, T3/IIOP traffic to unregistered WebLogic assets.

suggestion.title: Patch: CVE-2024-21182 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2024-21182 is the explicit identifier. Article emphasizes federal patch-due date (2026-06-04) and notes patch lag is the 'silent killer'—scanner correlation is critical.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate CVE-2024-21182 scanner findings with asset inventory. Immediate escalation for unpatched Oracle WebLogic instances in production. Verify patch status and deployment timeline against federal due-date deadline.

suggestion.title: Impact: Anomalous Data Access via WebLogic
suggestion.rationale: Article describes impact as 'unauthorized access to critical data or complete access to all Oracle WebLogic Server accessible data'—post-exploitation data access patterns should trigger alerts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WebLogic application logs for anomalous queries, exports, or data retrieval from compromised session. Alert on: large bulk data exports, queries from non-service accounts, access to sensitive schemas outside normal business hours or source patterns, unusual administrative API calls.

suggestion.title: Docker Hub Repository Poisoning Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes TeamPCP 'poisoning a Docker Hub repository to later steal Kubernetes secrets' via Checkmarx KICS compromise. No supply-chain image detection UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag image pulls from public registries (Docker Hub) immediately preceding processes marked as stealer/credential-access tools. Correlate pulled image digests against known-poisoned hashes. Detect spawning of persistence or exfil processes from build tool child processes (gradle, npm, kics, checkmarx scans).

suggestion.title: Dangerous Kernel Capabilities Abuse for Container Escape
suggestion.rationale: Article lists CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_SYS_MODULE, CAP_SYS_PTRACE, CAP_NET_ADMIN as specific escape vectors but no detection for their abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert containers started with CAP_SYS_ADMIN or CAP_SYS_MODULE. Detect modprobe, insmod, ptrace calls, or raw socket operations from unprivileged container processes. Flag child processes spawned by container daemons or escape-tool execution.

suggestion.title: Kubernetes Secrets Theft from Container Runtime
suggestion.rationale: Article states attack 'steal Kubernetes secrets and other sensitive data' and lists 'Exploitation of orchestration APIs' as primary vector; no secrets-access detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file access to /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/ or KUBECONFIG env-var usage from non-api-server processes. Flag API calls to kube-apiserver secretslist/get endpoints from pod service accounts. Correlate with outbound network traffic to external hosts.

suggestion.title: Stealer Payload Execution from Build Tools
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'tainted images distributed a stealer that was loaded during the KICS scanning process.' No process-tree detection for malware spawned by scanning/build tools.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child processes of scanning tools (checkmarx, kics, sonarqube runners, gradle, npm) exhibiting credential enumeration, file exfiltration, or known stealer family signatures. Alert on unexpected dynamic library loading or process memory injection from build containers.

suggestion.title: Host System Vulnerability Exploitation from Container Context
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 'Exploiting vulnerabilities in the host system and container runtime components' as primary vector but no detection for CVE-based container-to-host exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for container processes invoking ioctl, sysfs writes, or syscall sequences consistent with known container-escape PoCs (e.g. overlayfs, cgroup-based, namespace confusion exploits). Correlate with host-level process creation or network access outside pod CIDR.

suggestion.title: Privileged Container Misuse Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article discusses 'Privileged containers' and '--privileged' flag exploitation but no UC for detecting privileged mode spawn or capability abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on containers launched with --privileged flag or ALL capabilities granted (especially non-system containers). Detect child processes accessing /dev/mem, /dev/kmem, or raw kernel interfaces. Flag persistence mechanisms written to host /etc or /lib paths from privileged containers.

suggestion.title: Mirasvit Cache Warmer—PHP serialization exploit (CVE-2026-45247)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'unauthenticated PHP object injection flaw' enabling RCE; pipeline generated zero execution-phase hunts despite 'remotely execute malicious code' establishing clear post-compromise activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to Magento cache warmer plugin endpoints (Mirasvit) containing PHP serialization markers (O:, C:, a: patterns) in POST body or query parameters. Flag base64-encoded or hex-encoded payloads in cache plugin GET parameters, especially from non-administrative sources.

suggestion.title: Mirasvit Cache Warmer—Unauthenticated endpoint access
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'no login, configuration changes, or admin access required' but pipeline missed detection for direct unauthenticated exploitation; gap in initial_access phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline authenticated vs. unauthenticated requests to Magento cache warmer paths. Flag HTTP requests to plugin endpoints (paths matching 'mirasvit' or 'cache.*warmer') originating from non-admin sessions or sources without valid Magento session tokens.

suggestion.title: Magento cache plugin—Post-RCE process execution anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article's 'remotely execute malicious code' directly implies process spawn post-exploitation; pipeline detected no execution artifacts beyond HTTP requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected child process spawning from php-fpm or Apache worker processes during/after requests to Mirasvit Cache Warmer endpoints. Flag execution of curl, wget, bash, reverse shells, or base64 decoders from web service accounts.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-45247—Sansec-documented exploit signature
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline produced zero IOC-driven hunts despite 'Security researchers at Sansec uncovered' establishing vendor-published technical advisory; IOC extraction failed entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest published CVE-2026-45247 exploit signatures from Sansec advisory. Detect HTTP requests matching known vulnerable Mirasvit Cache Warmer parameter combinations, vulnerable URLs, or payload patterns documented in Sansec's technical analysis.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized WordPress Admin Account Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is 'actively exploited to create admin accounts' — this is the primary impact and persistence mechanism; zero detection use cases were generated for this.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WordPress wp_users table for new accounts with administrator role or admin_user meta added within minutes of first plugin exploit attempt. Flag if user_registered timestamp clusters within exploitation window or if account lacks corresponding legitimate registration email/confirmation flow.

suggestion.title: WP Maps Pro Plugin Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies critical vulnerability in WP Maps Pro plugin with active exploitation; should detect requests to plugin endpoints. Phrase: 'critical WP Maps Pro flaw actively exploited.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST/GET requests to /wp-content/plugins/wp-maps-pro/ endpoints with suspicious payloads (SQL injection, directory traversal, code injection markers). Alert on non-standard HTTP methods or encoded payloads to plugin parameter handlers.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation to WordPress Admin
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation results in admin-level access; should detect elevation of user privileges or role changes post-exploitation. Missing any privilege_escalation detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WordPress database for wp_usermeta changes where meta_key='wp_capabilities' is modified to include 'administrator' role for low-privilege accounts. Correlate with preceding plugin requests or file modifications within /wp-content/plugins/wp-maps-pro/.

suggestion.title: WP Maps Pro Post-Exploitation File Modification
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation likely involves webshell upload or plugin modification for persistence; should detect suspicious filesystem changes under /wp-content/plugins/wp-maps-pro/.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag creation or modification of .php files in /wp-content/plugins/wp-maps-pro/ directory (especially hidden files like .htaccess or files with suspicious names) outside of documented plugin update/deployment windows.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Payload Signature Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates this is an active, in-the-wild exploit; should detect known exploitation patterns or POC usage. Missing any signature-based detections for the actual payload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect requests containing known WP Maps Pro exploitation signatures (SQL injection patterns in specific parameters, directory traversal sequences, or PHP code execution attempts) targeting vulnerable plugin versions documented as affected.

suggestion.title: Admin Account Activity Immediately Post-Creation
suggestion.rationale: Unauthorized admin account would immediately be used for lateral movement or exfiltration; should detect admin-level actions by newly created accounts within 5 min of account creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate new admin account creation with admin-panel logins, plugin installations, theme uploads, or config changes within 5 minutes. Flag if IP address of login differs from exploitation IP or if user agent is automated tool.

suggestion.title: Multiple Failed Logins from Foreign Geographic Locations
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers 'attempted logins from distant locations and unknown devices.' Pipeline should have surfaced detection for geographic anomalies in login attempts within short timeframes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect >= 5 failed login attempts to the same user account originating from >= 2 distinct countries within a 15-minute window. Baseline user's historical login geography and alert when attempts originate from countries outside their typical access pattern, particularly when coupled with new device identifiers.

suggestion.title: Device Verification Requests from New/Unknown Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article states users 'received notices of suspicious access requests' with 'verification codes for legitimate account owners to register new devices.' Pipeline missed detection for spike in verification-code requests or device registration from unknown device fingerprints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when a single user receives >= 3 device verification code requests within 1 hour, or when device registration attempts originate from IPs not previously associated with the user. Flag requests with mismatched user agent strings or device fingerprints.

suggestion.title: Account Lockout Due to Automated Security Response
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'suspension of those accounts as part of Dashlane's built-in security controls' and 'all affected accounts had been unsuspended.' Pipeline should detect automated account lockout patterns as an indicator of active brute-force attack on that account.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for rapid account lockout followed by unsuspend cycle on the same account(s). Correlate with preceding failed-login spike logs. Batch detection: identify if >= 10 user accounts are locked out within a 5-minute window (indicates coordinated campaign rather than isolated lockouts).

suggestion.title: Credential-Access Attempt via Password Guessing at Scale
suggestion.rationale: Article defines attack method: 'brute-force attacks, which seek to gain access to an account by trying multiple passwords in succession until the correct one is found.' Pipeline should have explicitly mapped T1110.001 and surface password-guessing detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect >= 10 failed authentication attempts for the same username within 5 minutes from any single source IP. Escalate if the same IP attempts brute-force against multiple usernames (T1110 horizontal scan). Correlate failed login volume against baseline for the Dashlane login endpoint.

suggestion.title: JavaScript Injection via t.js Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'a JavaScript injection following the t.js?site=<id> pattern, where <id> is a unique value assigned to each compromised website.' This is the primary infection vector across all 80+ compromised sites.
