suggestion.rationale: Nation-state intelligence-gathering campaign (implied by 'attacks' on Czech Republic & Taiwan); exfiltration phase absent from pipeline output. Article phrase: 'China-Aligned Groups Ramp Up Attacks'—targets are intelligence-valuable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk data transfers to non-whitelisted IP space, particularly ASNs linked to China-aligned infrastructure. Alert on archive creation and encryption followed by network egress on non-standard ports.

suggestion.title: Living-off-the-Land Execution by Dragon Weave
suggestion.rationale: APT groups targeting government networks typically employ LOLBins to evade detection; no execution or defense-evasion UC produced. Missing from pipeline entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal PowerShell or cmd.exe execution from non-admin users in government environments. Alert on suspicious .NET reflection, DLL side-loading, or rundll32 calls tied to attacker infrastructure.

suggestion.title: CVE-2024-21182 Vulnerability Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'CVE-2024-21182 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt'; this is the primary detection vector for the KEV.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt vulnerability scanner output for CVE-2024-21182 detections on Oracle WebLogic Server. Prioritize by asset criticality and network exposure. Federal patch due 2026-06-04 provides compliance deadline.

suggestion.title: T3/IIOP Protocol Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'unauthenticated attacker with network access via T3, IIOP'—exploit payloads transit these specific protocols; network signatures are viable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor T3 (ports 7001/7002) and IIOP (port 3700) inbound traffic to WebLogic instances. Establish baseline of legitimate traffic and alert on exploit signatures or anomalous patterns.

suggestion.title: WebLogic Server Network Exposure Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article warns 'patch lag is the silent killer' and recommends asset-exposure hunting; any internet-facing WebLogic Server is immediately exploitable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all Oracle WebLogic Server instances reachable from the network perimeter (external port scans on 7001/7002/3700). Cross-reference with patch-compliance status to identify unpatched systems.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Data Exfiltration from WebLogic
suggestion.rationale: Article states successful exploitation 'can result in unauthorized access to critical data or complete access to all Oracle WebLogic Server accessible data'—monitor for the impact phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WebLogic application logs for atypical bulk data queries, unusual user account access, and large data transfers. Correlate with network exfiltration signatures to detect data moving out of the application tier.

suggestion.title: Patch Compliance Deadline Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Federal patch due: 2026-06-04' (2 days from publication); narrow window; track deployment status operationally.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Automated scan: flag all WebLogic Server instances without CVE-2024-21182 patches applied by 2026-06-04. Report non-compliance to management and audit teams. Escalate unpatched critical systems.

suggestion.title: Kubernetes Secrets Accessed from Pod
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'poisoning a Docker Hub repository to later steal Kubernetes secrets and other sensitive data.' Pipeline missed detection of unauthorized secret extraction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Kubernetes API calls to list/get secrets from compromised pod service account. Correlate with unexpected outbound connections from pod namespace. Baseline service-account token usage per workload and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Container Escape via CAP_SYS_ADMIN Capability Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists 'CAP_SYS_ADMIN' as a vector in container-escape section. Pipeline ignored containerization-misconfig attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect containers launched with CAP_SYS_ADMIN or other privileged capabilities (CAP_SYS_MODULE, CAP_SYS_PTRACE, CAP_NET_ADMIN). Correlate with process execution involving kernel module loading, process injection, or namespace manipulation from container PID.

suggestion.title: Malicious Stealer Execution During Container Build/Scan
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'stealer that was loaded during the KICS scanning process.' Pipeline missed detection of supply-chain payload execution within trusted build tools.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected child processes spawned by known scanning tools (KICS, container registries) or build stages. Flag exfiltration-pattern outbound connections (DNS queries, HTTP POSTs to external IPs) from container runtime.

suggestion.title: Docker Hub Repository Poisoning via Image Manifest Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'poisoning a Docker Hub repository to later steal Kubernetes secrets.' Pipeline ignored supply-chain detection for registry manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect image pushes from unusual accounts/IPs to shared registries. Alert on container-image hash mismatches vs. signed digest. Flag pulls of images with known backdoor signatures or behavioral anomalies from static analysis.

suggestion.title: Kubernetes Orchestration API Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 'Exploitation of orchestration APIs' as primary vector but provides no coverage. Pipeline missed API-abuse detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unusual kubectl/Kubernetes API calls (create deployment, patch RBAC, exec into pod, get secrets) from service account tokens or user accounts. Correlate with changes to pod security policies or network policies.

suggestion.title: CAP_SYS_PTRACE Process Injection from Container
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'CAP_SYS_PTRACE' in container-escape section. Pipeline missed specific capability-based lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect containers with CAP_SYS_PTRACE capability spawning process-tracing syscalls (ptrace, process_vm_readv) targeting host PID namespace. Flag context switches to host namespace from container context.

suggestion.title: Asset exposure — Magento systems running vulnerable Mirasvit Cache Warmer
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'widely used' plugin affecting 'thousands of Magento' installations. Pipeline's own recommendations section explicitly names 'Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)' with template reference, yet zero use cases instantiated. This is the foundational recon-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Magento installations running Mirasvit Cache Warmer versions prior to security patch. Detection via vulnerability scanning data, plugin manifest inspection, file-system presence checks for vulnerable plugin directories, or version string analysis.

suggestion.title: PHP object injection exploitation attempt against cache warmer
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies the attack vector as 'unauthenticated PHP object injection flaw'. This is the direct exploitation mechanism and should generate detection for HTTP requests containing serialized PHP payloads targeting the plugin.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Mirasvit Cache Warmer endpoints for PHP serialization patterns (objects prefixed with O:, arrays with a:, or base64-encoded serialized data). Flag unauthenticated requests containing such patterns as exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated RCE abuse via cache plugin endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'no login, configuration changes, or admin access required' for exploitation. This access control bypass is the critical attack element and must be detected when code execution occurs without credential validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on requests to cache plugin endpoints (typical paths /mirasvit/*, /cache/*, /magento/cache/*) with code injection characteristics originating from unauthenticated sessions. Correlate repeated attempts from single IP as mass exploitation scanning.

suggestion.title: WordPress Admin Account Creation via Plugin Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article core claim: 'Actively Exploited to Create Admin Accounts.' This is the primary attack outcome; requires real-time detection of admin user creation outside normal administrative workflows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WordPress user creation/modification events for new administrator-role accounts. Correlate timing and source with WP Maps Pro plugin requests in web logs. Alert on admin capability grants from non-administrative or unauthenticated origins.

suggestion.title: WP Maps Pro Vulnerability Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Critical WP Maps Pro Flaw.' Pipeline must detect exploitation attempts at initial access phase before persistence is established.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify HTTP requests to WP Maps Pro plugin endpoints (/wp-content/plugins/wp-maps-pro/) with payloads indicative of code injection, parameter tampering, or unauthenticated function calls. Flag requests with suspicious query parameters or POST bodies.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable WP Maps Pro Version Inventory and Alerting
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies specific vulnerability in WP Maps Pro. Continuous inventory of plugin versions and detection of unpatched installations is foundational.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Periodically scan WordPress instances for WP Maps Pro plugin presence and version. Alert on vulnerable versions (specific version threshold to be determined from CVE). Track plugin update/activation events.

suggestion.title: Suspicious User Role or Capability Modification
suggestion.rationale: Adjacent to admin creation, attackers may escalate existing user privileges. Article emphasizes admin account persistence mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on WordPress role changes, capability additions, or user metadata modifications (set_user_role, add_user_cap hooks). Correlate with plugin vulnerability exploitation timeframe and non-standard admin sources.

suggestion.title: High-Volume Failed Logins: Brute-Force Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'brute-force attacks that attempted logins from distant locations' and 'trying multiple passwords in succession until the correct one is found.' This is explicit T1110.001.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when a single cloud account experiences 10+ failed login attempts within 15 minutes, or 25+ failures within 1 hour, especially from distinct source IPs. Dashlane should emit failed authentication events; correlate with upstream IdP logs (if any) to catch the full attack window before account lockout fires.

suggestion.title: Geographic Anomaly: Auth Attempts from Rare/Distant Countries
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'brute-force attacks...from distant locations and unknown devices' and 'received notices of suspicious access requests from foreign countries.' Establishes geographic outlier as primary signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain per-user baseline of known login countries (from device registration history or previous successful logins). Alert on login attempts from countries/regions absent from baseline, especially within 24 hours of account creation. Combine with IP geolocation enrichment and flag attempts from countries with high brute-force activity.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Device Registration Following Auth Failure Spike
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'emails contained verification codes for legitimate account owners to register new devices' and 'suspicious access requests' triggered verification flows. Device add events correlate with failed auth.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate failed-login events with new device/session registration or MFA enrollment on the same account. Alert when device registration attempt occurs within 30 minutes of 5+ failed logins, or when registration happens from an IP that was previously used for failed-login attempts.

suggestion.title: Verification Code Issuance Spike Correlated with Auth Failures
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'emails contained verification codes' during brute-force window. Verification-code issuance is a loggable event that spikes during credential-attack phases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when a single account triggers 4+ verification-code issuance events within 30 minutes, especially if temporally adjacent to failed-login attempts from multiple IPs or rare geolocations. This indicates either active brute-force or compromised account triggering legitimate MFA challenges.

suggestion.title: Account Lockout/Suspension Event Following Auth Spike
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'suspension of those accounts as part of Dashlane's built-in security controls' in response to brute-force. Lockout events are a defensive signal that correlates with prior attack window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create a composite alert that fires when account lockout/suspension event is preceded by 15+ failed login attempts in <30 min from multiple distinct IPs or geolocations. This confirms automated defense engaged in response to detected brute-force and creates a retrospective detection window for SIEM correlation.

suggestion.title: praisonai-platform: 401/403 member-addition failures — privilege-escalation probing
suggestion.rationale: Article states endpoint gated by require_workspace_member(workspace_id). Unauthorized callers receive rejection. Repeated 401/403 responses to POST /workspaces/*/members indicates systematic privilege-escalation probing before successful exploit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Aggregate failed POST /workspaces/*/members (HTTP 401, 403) by user/IP. Alert on ≥3 failures within 10 minutes from single source. Correlate with subsequent HTTP 200/201 success within 24h window—indicates reconnaissance-to-exploit sequence.

suggestion.title: praisonai-platform: Workspace/user enumeration preceding member exploit
suggestion.rationale: Attacker must discover workspace_id and valid user_ids to craft exploit. Article describes endpoint requires both. Enumeration via GET /workspaces/* and GET /users APIs is prerequisite reconnaissance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate high-volume GET requests to /workspaces/* or /users endpoints with subsequent POST /workspaces/*/members from same source. Alert on >5 enumerations followed by exploit attempt within 30 minutes.

suggestion.title: praisonai-platform: Audit-log access post-member-addition — cover-tracks
suggestion.rationale: After adding malicious owner, attacker may attempt to hide trail by exporting, querying, or deleting audit logs. Article describes workspace-member context, implying audit trail exists.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful POST /workspaces/*/members (HTTP 200/201) with subsequent GET/DELETE/EXPORT requests to audit/activity endpoints. Alert on audit access within 5 minutes of suspicious member addition from same user/IP.

suggestion.title: praisonai-platform: Bulk owner-role assignments in short window
suggestion.rationale: Attacker maximizes impact by adding multiple owners to same or different workspaces rapidly. Normal operations grant owner role sparingly, not in bulk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Aggregate POST /workspaces/*/members with role=owner by session/user/IP in 10-minute windows. Alert when single source successfully adds ≥2 owner-role members, especially across different workspace_ids.

suggestion.title: praisonai-platform: Member-addition requests from non-browser clients
suggestion.rationale: Legitimate workspace admins use web UI (browser User-Agent). Automated exploitation uses curl, wget, Python, JavaScript clients with distinct signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST /workspaces/*/members requests. Flag User-Agents matching curl|wget|python|nodejs|requests|httpx|java patterns. Baseline legitimate admin clients (Postman, web console) and exclude from alerts. Suppress if User-Agent consistent with known automation.

suggestion.title: [LLM] Vitest UI server launched with non-loopback --api.host / --host (CVE-2026-47429 exposure)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends this hunt (UC_18_2). Detects dangerous configuration of vulnerable Vitest UI server exposure to network—the prerequisite condition: 'explicitly exposes the Vitest UI server to the network'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for node.exe, npm.exe, yarn.exe, pnpm.exe, or npx.exe spawning vitest with --ui or --browser AND specifying non-loopback --api.host or --host argument. Flag any binding to public IPs or private ranges; baseline loopback (127.0.0.1, ::1, localhost) as benign.

suggestion.title: [LLM] Path-traversal exploit hitting Vitest /__vitest_attachment__ endpoint (CVE-2026-47429 PoC)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends this hunt (UC_18_3). Detects exploitation phase using path-traversal payloads against the vulnerable endpoint—the core attack vector for arbitrary file read/execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP(S) requests to Vitest endpoints (__vitest_attachment__, __vitest__) for encoded path-traversal sequences (%3F%5C, %3F/.., %3F\) or literal (\?\.., ?\..) directory-traversal attempts. Alert on requests from non-loopback sources.

suggestion.title: [LLM] Post-exploit shell spawned by Vitest node.exe via rerun / saveTestFile
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends this hunt (UC_18_4). Detects execution of command shells and system utilities spawned as children of vitest node.exe, indicating code execution achieved through the vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on cmd.exe, powershell.exe, pwsh.exe, wscript.exe, cscript.exe, rundll32.exe, certutil.exe, curl.exe, wget.exe, net.exe, whoami.exe, hostname.exe, systeminfo.exe spawned as children of node.exe running vitest. Filter out legitimate vitest worker process spawning.

suggestion.title: [LLM] Inbound TCP connection to Vitest UI port 51204 from non-loopback source
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends this hunt (UC_18_5). Detects network-level delivery and reconnaissance against the vulnerable Vitest UI server, enabling early detection of exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound TCP to port 51204 from non-loopback source IPs (exclude 127.0.0.1, ::1, 0.0.0.0, 127.0.0.0/8). Correlate with Vitest process spawning on target. Baseline known CI/CD and local development use cases.

suggestion.title: [LLM] File read/exfiltration via Vitest path-traversal (CVE-2026-47429)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'arbitrary file can be read on Windows when Vitest UI server is listening'. Pipeline missed file-access detection correlating successful path-traversal exploits with actual file reads/writes. Article UC_18_1 includes Filesystem datamodel for this.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful path-traversal HTTP requests to __vitest_attachment__ with subsequent file-read/write/create events on sensitive paths. Alert on file access originating from node.exe running vitest, especially reads of config, secrets, or system files outside project directory.

suggestion.title: FakeUpdate - Suspicious Executable Download Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes fake browser update attacks delivering 'Browser Update.exe' via ZIP archive—attack vector explicitly demonstrated but no detection case generated. Quote: 'fake Firefox update that downloaded a ZIP archive containing multiple DLLs and a malicious executable named Browser Update.exe'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for executables with spoofed OS/browser update names (e.g., 'Browser Update.exe', 'Firefox Update.exe', 'Chrome Update.exe') downloaded to user temp directories or Documents. Correlate with ZIP extraction events and subsequent process execution. Reduce false positives by excluding system update processes initiated from legitimate Windows/browser directories.

suggestion.title: ClickFix - PowerShell Execution from Browser Context
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline missed explicit PowerShell-based ClickFix attack vector. Quote: 'ClickFix attacks involve PowerShell commands. The researchers identified eight technical fingerprints linked to the campaign'—no detection generated for browser-to-PowerShell parent-child relationship.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when browser processes (chrome.exe, firefox.exe, msedge.exe) spawn PowerShell or cmd.exe children with command lines containing suspicious patterns (e.g., registry modification, script download, credential access, Invoke-Expression, DownloadString). Require script block logging to validate obfuscation and encoding.

suggestion.title: JavaScript Injection - t.js Fingerprint Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes a specific JavaScript injection pattern as a technical fingerprint but pipeline extracted no indicator. Quote: 'JavaScript injection following the t.js?site=<id> pattern, where <id> is a unique value assigned to each compromised website'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect HTTP responses for injected script tags referencing patterns like 't.js?site=' followed by numeric or alphanumeric identifiers. Flag when injected from unexpected or newly-registered domains. Correlate with unusual redirect chains from legitimate domain origins.

suggestion.title: Malicious Domain Infrastructure - Injection Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies '80+ malicious injection domains' and 'pre-weaponized domains' as infrastructure indicators—zero domain-based detection suggested. Quote: 'Through analysis, Silent Push discovered more than 80 malicious injection domains and a set of pre-weaponized domains that had not yet been used in attacks.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for newly-registered or freshly-weaponized domains matching zTDS infrastructure patterns (e.g., high volume of requests with profiling parameters, short time-to-deployment, registration clustering). Alert on DNS queries and HTTP requests to domains hosting t.js injection payload or TDS redirect infrastructure. Integrate domain reputation feeds.

suggestion.title: Clipboard Hijacking - macOS JavaScript Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline missed explicit macOS-specific attack vector combining clipboard manipulation with JavaScript. Quote: 'obfuscated JavaScript payload specifically designed to target macOS desktop systems, delivered via verification-themed ClickFix attacks that hijack the clipboard'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On macOS, monitor for JavaScript engines (Safari, Chrome, Firefox) or Electron-based processes accessing UIPasteboard or clipboard services. Alert on clipboard reads following suspicious web content execution or verification-themed pop-up dialogs. Correlate with obfuscated JavaScript detection and credential harvesting patterns.

suggestion.title: Fake Browser Update Prompt Spoofing - Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Article describes FakeUpdates targeting multiple browsers but no detection for prompt spoofing or the resulting social engineering interaction. Quote: 'FakeUpdates lures contain bogus update notices for Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari, Opera, Brave, Yandex, Vivaldi, Samsung Internet, and UC Browser'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious browser-update-like dialogs originating from non-system processes or web content contexts. Flag when update prompts direct users to download executables from unexpected domains. Correlation: update prompt display → executable download → suspicious process execution.

suggestion.title: HTTP Request Signature — Crafted Requests to WebSphere Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'specially crafted HTTP requests' are the attack vector. This is the initial access footprint and the pipeline generated zero detection logic for it. 'The vulnerability [allows] attackers to execute arbitrary code through specially crafted HTTP requests' must map to HTTP log analysis, WAF rules, or IDS signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP access logs for requests to WebSphere admin/plugin endpoints (e.g., /, /admin, /config, /plugin-config, /_ibm_security_logout) from external/untrusted sources. Flag payloads containing Java serialization markers (aced0005, content-type: application/x-java-serialized), expression language injection (${...}), or multi-stage encoding patterns typical of RCE post-exploitation frameworks.

suggestion.title: WebSphere Process — Anomalous Child Execution Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'arbitrary code execution' from the vulnerability. Pipeline did not generate detection for the execution phase. Successful RCE spawns child processes; alert when WebSphere JVM spawns cmd.exe, powershell, bash, or unexpected compiled binaries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned by java.exe (WebSphere JVM) or wsadmin processes with command-line arguments indicating code execution (cmd /c, powershell -noprofile, sh -c). Establish baseline of legitimate child processes per environment; any deviation to shell interpreters, script downloaders (curl, wget), or reverse-shell patterns indicates compromise. Correlate timestamp with HTTP anomalies.

suggestion.title: Web Server Plug-ins Component — File Integrity & Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies the vulnerability is in the 'optional Web Server Plug-ins component.' Pipeline did not generate detection for the exact compromised component. Detection must (a) inventory systems with this component enabled, (b) alert on modifications to plugin binaries and configuration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline the Web Server Plug-ins installation directory (C:\IBM\WebSphere\AppServer\plugins or /opt/IBM/WebSphere/plugins). Alert on unauthorized .dll/.so/.jar/.config file modifications, new binary creation, or unexpected version changes post-compromise. Alert on file access from unusual processes (non-wsadmin, non-ibm-managed). Cross-reference with process spawning alerts.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation — RCE Executing as System/Root
suggestion.rationale: Article does not specify if WebSphere runs as elevated user, but RCE granting arbitrary code execution in that context is a privilege escalation. Pipeline mapped only T1190, missing the subsequent privilege escalation impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when RCE from WebSphere results in process creation with elevated privileges (SYSTEM, root, or unexpected account). Monitor for token impersonation (SeImpersonate) abuse or privilege elevation APIs called from WebSphere context. Flag discrepancies between WebSphere's configured identity and the actual privilege of spawned child processes.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Network Beaconing & Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: Article targets 'enterprise deployments' where compromised WebSphere servers have network access to backends, databases, and other systems. Pipeline did not suggest detection for C2 or lateral-movement indicators following successful RCE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound network connections from compromised WebSphere process to unusual external IPs/domains (establish baseline for environment). Alert on SMB (445), RDP (3389), SSH (22), WinRM (5985/5986) outbound connections to internal targets not in baseline. Correlate with process spawning from WebSphere. Monitor DNS queries from the server for domains not in the organization's whitelist or with suspicious TLDs.

suggestion.title: AppDomainManager Hijacking via CLR Initialization
suggestion.rationale: Article title and body explicitly cite 'AppDomainManager hijacking' as the technique; pipeline mapped this to generic T1027 instead of the specific abuse. Article phrase: 'sophisticated .NET hijacking technique to slip past endpoint defenses.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation of CLR InitializeSecurityManager registry keys, APPDOMAINMANAGER environment variables, or unusual clrjit.dll/mscorwks.dll module loads in non-standard .NET runtimes. Track attempts to load untrusted AppDomain managers via config files or registry HKLM/HKCU paths.

suggestion.title: EDR Sensor Bypass via CLR Interception
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states the technique is used 'to slip past endpoint defenses'; EDR evasion is the primary goal. No defense_evasion phase was reconstructed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for .NET processes disabling or unloading EDR hooks via AppDomainManager initialization. Alert on env vars APPDOMAINMANAGER_ASM or APPDOMAINMANAGER_TYPE pointing to unsigned or unsigned-in-context assemblies. Track registry writes to HKLM\Software\Microsoft\.NETFramework\*PolicyLevel.

suggestion.title: .NET Assembly DLL Injection via Configuration
suggestion.rationale: AppDomainManager hijacking loads arbitrary .NET assemblies without direct code injection; article describes 'sophisticated .NET hijacking' implying config-driven persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation or modification of *.config files adjacent to .NET executables, specifically app.config or web.config entries containing <runtime><loadFromRemoteSources enabled='true'/></runtime> or custom assembly-binding redirects pointing to external/attacker-controlled paths.

suggestion.title: Suspicious .NET Process Execution with Environment Variable Tampering
suggestion.rationale: AppDomainManager abuse requires env var or registry setup before .NET process launch; no execution-layer detection was proposed despite SHA256 hashes indicating binary delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate .NET process launches (csc.exe, msbuild.exe, aspnet_compiler.exe) preceded by SetEnvironmentVariable calls for APPDOMAINMANAGER*, or preceded by registry writes to CLR InitializeSecurityManager paths within 5 seconds. Alert on legitimate .NET runtimes spawned with suspicious module-load order anomalies.

suggestion.title: Masquerading via Typosquatted Domain C2
suggestion.rationale: Domains like 'buisness-centeral-transportation.com' (typo: 'business', 'central') and 'ramiltonsfinance.com' (typo: 'Hamilton') suggest deliberate masquerading. Article does not explicitly name this technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag DNS queries and connections to known-typosquatted domains or newly registered domains with character-substitution similarity to legitimate business/finance/healthcare brands. Correlate with process parents (svchost, explorer, chrome) typical of credential-theft or lateral-move C2 callbacks.

suggestion.title: npm Package Execution with Suspicious Child Process Spawning
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates malicious npm packages are executing worms post-install. Article states credential-stealing behavior, implying scripted execution during dependency resolution or post-install hooks—likely spawning shells or credential-access processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm.exe or node.exe spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or curl/wget child processes during or immediately after package install. Flag processes in npm cache directories or node_modules with network I/O in argument blocks.

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration via npm/Node Process Network Egress
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'credential-stealing worm'—this implies the malware harvests and exfils credentials. Should alert on npm/Node processes making unexpected HTTP/S or DNS lookups to non-standard domains, or process arguments containing encoded credential material.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm/Node processes initiating outbound connections to domains not in NPM registry whitelist, or command-line arguments containing 'token', 'credential', 'auth', 'password' patterns combined with base64-encoded data or curl/wget invocations.

suggestion.title: npm Package with Embedded Post-Install or Preinstall Scripts
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain npm attacks typically abuse postinstall/preinstall hooks in package.json to execute arbitrary code before the package is even used. Pipeline should flag package.json manipulation or script invocation at install time.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install logs or process traces for invocation of 'npm run postinstall', 'npm run preinstall', or direct shell spawning from package.json. Cross-reference against known-good package versions using NPM registry API baseline.

suggestion.title: Red Hat/CentOS Repository Poisoning—Malicious npm Package Version
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Red Hat npm packages'—implies either official Red Hat npm registry, npmjs.org hosting, or vendored dependencies. Should generate IOC hunt rules for compromised package names, versions, and checksums once article details are extracted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query package manager logs for installation of npm packages flagged as compromised. Alert on mismatches between expected package hash (from signed manifest) and actual downloaded file. Monitor Red Hat/CentOS systems for npm package installs outside scheduled patching windows.

suggestion.title: Worm Propagation via Shared npm Caches or node_modules Symlink Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Title mentions 'worm'—indicates self-propagating behavior. npm attacks can spread via shared node_modules directories in CI/CD or development environments, or via symlink injection in cache hierarchies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm cache directories (~/.npm, /tmp/npm-*) and node_modules for unexpected symlink creation or modification. Flag processes that traverse multiple node_modules trees or attempt to write to npm cache from non-npm-daemon processes.

suggestion.title: npm preinstall Script Execution with Credential Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states preinstall hook 'runs an obfuscated payload the moment a package is installed' and 'Harvests secrets and credentials from the local environment and CI context'. No detection rule for install-time script execution correlated with credential file/env-var access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on node.js spawned as child of npm install process, followed by child process accessing ~/.npmrc, ~/.ssh/id_rsa, environment variable inspection, or CI secret paths within 5 seconds. High-fidelity signal for preinstall payload execution.

suggestion.title: Cloud Identity Enumeration via GCP/Azure CLI from Non-Cloud Context
suggestion.rationale: Article highlights new Miasma capability: 'pair of new collectors for GCP and Azure that enumerate every identity the infected host can assume, not just static secrets'. No detection for gcloud/az enumeration from development machines.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect gcloud auth list, gcloud iam service-accounts list, az account list, or az role assignment list commands executed from developer workstations or npm-based CI runners. Baseline: rare or absent. Flag all instances.

suggestion.title: Burst npm Package Republishing by Single Account
suggestion.rationale: Article describes worm propagation: 'It queries the registry for other packages the compromised identity can publish and republishes them, carrying the same payload'. Republishing existing versions is anomalous.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect ≥3 npm publish operations by a single account within 5 minutes, especially republishing existing package versions. Cross-reference with OIDC token issuance events within the same hour.

suggestion.title: GitHub OIDC Token Request from GitHub Actions on Non-Default Branches
suggestion.rationale: Article details root cause: 'Those commits added a minimal GitHub Actions workflow that... Triggered on push to any branch. Requested a GitHub OIDC identity token via id-token: write'. Workflow injection bypassed review.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag GitHub Actions workflows requesting id-token: write permissions on push triggers to orphan or non-protected branches. Alert if the same OIDC token is used for npm publish or registry queries within the workflow execution.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated JavaScript with eval() and ROT String Decoding in npm Payloads
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'heavily obfuscated JavaScript file. The author relied on eval() and ROT-based string decoding to hide the logic'. No detection for this specific defense-evasion pattern in install-time scripts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor node.js child processes for eval() statements on decoded string content (rot13, rot47, XOR patterns). Flag preinstall/postinstall scripts with >8 KB of minified/obfuscated JavaScript. High confidence signal for Miasma or similar worm variants.

suggestion.title: Compromised OIDC Token Used for Orphan Commit Push to Protected Repository
suggestion.rationale: Article explains bypass mechanism: 'orphan commits directly into two RedHatInsights repositories, bypassing code review' using legitimate OIDC token from 'Requested a GitHub OIDC identity token'. Detection gap for commit activity with valid but anomalous provenance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on commits to protected branches signed with GitHub OIDC tokens from GitHub Actions workflows, especially if workflow was added via push to an orphan/non-protected branch in the preceding 24 hours. Flag SLSA provenance validity alone as insufficient; require workflow review.

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration from Node.js Process Context
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'credential-stealing malware' deployed via npm packages. No UC captures the exfiltration phase. Node.js processes reading environment variables (AWS_ACCESS_KEY, AWS_SECRET_KEY, API_TOKENS, etc.) and making outbound connections to attacker infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Node.js or npm processes reading sensitive files (.aws/credentials, .kube/config, .env) or environment variables containing credentials, followed by outbound network connections to non-standard ports or unrecognized domains. Monitor for env variable enumeration (GetEnvironmentVariable, getenv calls) from npm-spawned child processes.

suggestion.title: Unusual npm Registry or Package Version Download
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'over 30 official packages' compromised but not typosquatting—suggests legitimate package names with malicious content injected. No UC detects abnormal npm registry calls, version pinning changes, or fallback registries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: npm install/update requests to registry.npmjs.org or internal npm mirrors for @redhat-cloud-services packages with unusual version tags, checksums mismatched against known golden hashes, or registry fallback to unexpected mirrors. Monitor for rapid repeated requests to same packages (automated infection).

suggestion.title: Suspicious postinstall/preinstall Script Execution
suggestion.rationale: npm supply chain attacks commonly hide malicious payloads in package.json lifecycle scripts (preinstall, postinstall, prepare). Article does not specify delivery mechanism but this is standard npm attack vector. No UC scans for script execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Shell (bash, powershell, cmd) or script interpreter (perl, python) spawned by npm.exe or node.exe with parent_command_line containing 'install' or 'update', executing obfuscated code, base64-decoded payloads, or curl/wget/bitsadmin commands fetching external scripts.

suggestion.title: TeamPCP Malware Artifact Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article attributes malware to 'Mini Shai-Hulud malware family' and 'TeamPCP' threat actor. No UC or IOC captures known TeamPCP signatures, file hashes, C2 beacons, or malware family indicators (YARA rules, behavioral patterns).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Network traffic from compromised systems matching known TeamPCP C2 infrastructure, DNS queries for malware-associated domains, or process memory/file hash matches against Mini Shai-Hulud/Miasma signatures (if available from threat intel feeds). Monitor for known beaconing patterns or JA3 TLS fingerprints linked to the family.

suggestion.title: Mass npm Package Installation Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 30+ packages compromised in single campaign. No UC detects unusual volume or scope of npm installs from single source—could indicate automated infrastructure compromise or CI/CD pipeline poisoning.
log_sources: CI/CD logs (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Single user, host, or service account installing >5 @redhat-cloud-services packages within short time window (15 min), or install patterns deviating from known CI/CD baseline. Correlate with package version changes, lock file mutations, and downstream process execution anomalies.

suggestion.title: AWS/Cloud Credential Harvesting from Node.js Context
suggestion.rationale: Red Hat Cloud Services strongly implies AWS/cloud integration. Article mentions credential-stealing but no specific UC targets harvesting of cloud IAM keys, service tokens, or kubeconfig files often present in containerized/cloud environments running Node.js.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Node.js process reading AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, KUBECONFIG, or cloud service config files; followed by either exfiltration (outbound network from npm context) or use of harvested creds in unexpected AWS/cloud API calls from unrecognized IP/user. Correlate with npm install events.

suggestion.title: npm Package Installation — Suspicious Registry Source or Post-Install Hook Execution
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly names 'codexui-android npm' as attack vector. Supply-chain npm attacks rely on post-install scripts (package.json scripts field) to execute arbitrary code during 'npm install'. Article states tokens were stolen, implying runtime code execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag npm install commands followed by unexpected child process spawning (curl, wget, python, node -e). Monitor postinstall script execution for obfuscated commands, environment variable access ('OPENAI', 'API', 'TOKEN'), or network outbound connections.

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration — OpenAI/API Tokens via Malicious Node Process
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'Authentication Tokens Stolen.' Malicious npm package executes during install or at runtime, reads environment or config files containing OpenAI API keys, exfiltrates via HTTP/HTTPS.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect node/npm child processes making unexpected outbound HTTPS connections immediately post-install. Correlate with process-level access to files matching patterns *.env, *credentials*, *token*, or env var reads containing 'KEY' or 'OPENAI'.

suggestion.title: npm Package Metadata Anomaly — Version Mismatch or Tampered Package Signature
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks often insert malicious versions alongside legitimate versions or compromise official registry entries. Pipeline should extract package name 'codexui-android' as IOC and flag installation of any version.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference npm package hashes (integrity field in package-lock.json) against npm registry. Alert if hash mismatch, version string contains dev/beta markers in production, or package is installed from non-official registry.

suggestion.title: Build/CI Environment Token Harvesting — npm Run Script Side-Channel
suggestion.rationale: OpenAI tokens are often injected as environment variables in CI/CD pipelines. Malicious postinstall script can enumerate and exfiltrate them during 'npm install' in build contexts (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, etc.).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In CI/CD logs, detect npm postinstall or preinstall hooks that execute shell commands with env keyword, child processes calling printenv/set, or commands that base64-encode or gzip environment output before transmitting.

suggestion.title: Package Dependency Tree Manipulation — Dependency Confusion / Version Squatting
suggestion.rationale: Title names 'codexui-android' specifically. Pipeline should surface whether this package is a typosquat (e.g., legitimate 'codexui' + '-android') or a direct registry hijack of a previously-benign package.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan npm install manifests for package names within edit distance 1 of known popular packages (typos, hyphenation variance). Alert if a package with <100 downloads appears in dependency tree of major projects or if package name mimics legitimate OpenAI tools.

suggestion.title: Phishing link click to endpoint execution correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'fake verification pages that trick them into running a malicious script'—phishing link immediately drives user execution. This delivery-to-execution correlation is the attack signature the pipeline missed entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect URL click from inbound email followed within 60 seconds by suspicious child process spawn (PowerShell, cmd, mshta, rundll32) from browser or email client parent. Join ClickTime to ProcessCreationTime; this correlation eliminates 99% of benign-click noise.

suggestion.title: Fake CAPTCHA with clipboard-injected PowerShell execution
suggestion.rationale: Core attack mechanism: ClickFix scripts exploit clipboard injection to execute code post-click. Article explicitly mentions clipboard-injected PowerShell—pipeline must detect PowerShell/MSHTA spawned from explorer.exe with Base64, iex, DownloadString, or URL keywords.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PowerShell or MSHTA spawned from explorer.exe or RuntimeBroker.exe where ProcessCommandLine contains Base64 encoding, iex, Invoke-Expression, FromBase64, DownloadString, or http(s) patterns. High signal when parent process is non-standard or initialization timestamp correlates to user clipboard activity.

suggestion.title: RAT C2 callback detection via network IOCs
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'plant remote access malware'—post-installation RAT implies C2 communication. Network connections to hiddenplanetlab.top, silverharvestnetwork.com, or IPs 178.156.165.82, 178.156.173.194, 89.110.110.119, 185.163.47.217 are high-confidence compromises.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound TCP/UDP connections to known C2 domain or IP IOCs from Windows endpoints. Correlate to unsigned/suspicious process initiator (non-system, non-browser), and cross-check for temporal correlation to prior PowerShell execution within same session.

suggestion.title: File hash matching for SmartApeSG RAT payloads
suggestion.rationale: Article provides 4 SHA256 hashes of known RAT binaries—any match is confirmed compromise. Hash-based detection is deterministic highest-confidence signal the pipeline completely missed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Trigger critical alert on any file created, accessed, or executed matching SHA256: 1514b1268e9dc6d2f37137aa38c756cb4bf8186ac9235d6863b78e7f8bbbe976, 469bac8e10f50263e8ff0806e6ba126bb4cc660799129a8653eab3f8ec7201e5, 9c7eda2c4d3aaa8746495741bef57a07de180f0409409faf0f91658e88ba33f5, 7ba5481c873bb3081442561f749f590badd72ef249fddfe993e30b28dc0c2112. Correlate to parent process (PowerShell, cmd) to confirm delivery chain.

suggestion.title: Brute-Force Authentication Spike Against SaaS Password Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Brute-Force Attack'—this is the primary attack technique. Pipeline missed fundamental credential-access detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on multiple failed authentication attempts against Dashlane user accounts from the same source IP or user agent within a 5-minute window, or velocity-based detection of login attempts exceeding typical baseline for a given user/account by >10x within 1-hour sliding window.

suggestion.title: Encrypted Vault Bulk Download Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'encrypted vaults of fewer than 20 users downloaded'—clear exfiltration event. No detection coverage suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect downloads of vault backups or container files (.dhlane, .zip, or proprietary archive formats) from Dashlane infrastructure, particularly bulk exports from a single user account or multiple accounts within short time window post-authentication.

suggestion.title: Compromised Credentials Used for Unauthorized SaaS Access
suggestion.rationale: Brute-force success implies credential compromise. Article confirms attackers obtained access to encrypted vaults, indicating successful credential use.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful login post-high-volume failed attempts on same account; alert on login success where 95th percentile of failed attempts preceded it within 24 hours. Include enrichment for IP geolocation mismatch, impossible travel scenarios.

suggestion.title: Lateral Reconnaissance: Credential Enumeration Against Password Manager
suggestion.rationale: Brute-force attacks typically begin with user enumeration or list acquisition. Article context suggests attackers had a target list of Dashlane users.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for patterns consistent with credential stuffing: requests testing multiple username/email variations against Dashlane's login endpoint, particularly when combined with common password lists or patterns (dictionary words, year sequences). Look for source IPs showing behavior consistent with automated tooling (regular inter-request timing, sequential attempts).

suggestion.title: Proxy/VPN Obfuscation of Attack Source
suggestion.rationale: High-volume brute-force attacks typically use proxy chains or compromised infrastructure to avoid blocking. Article silence on attacker location suggests obfuscation not analyzed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify brute-force source IPs originating from known proxy services, VPN providers, or residential IP ranges indicative of botnet activity. Cross-reference with threat intel on Datascraper-tool fingerprints (common headers, TLS metadata, request pacing patterns).

suggestion.title: Account Takeover: Vault Access by Non-Approved User Agents
suggestion.rationale: Successful brute-force allows attacker to log into compromised accounts. Detection should trigger on access patterns inconsistent with victim's normal behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag successful authentications to Dashlane accounts from user agents, OS versions, or browser fingerprints not previously associated with that account. Include geolocation mismatch (e.g., user in US but login from ASN in NE Asia within < 12 hours of previous legitimate login).

suggestion.title: Chatbot-Initiated Password Reset Without Prior MFA Challenge
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers bypassed 2FA by asking the bot to 'hand over access.' Detect resets approved by chatbot without human identity verification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on password reset completions where the approval workflow bypassed MFA or where the reset request originated from a chatbot interaction without secondary identity proof. Correlate reset timestamp with immediate non-standard-location authentication.

suggestion.title: Clustered High-Value Account Compromises Over Short Time Window
suggestion.rationale: Article reports 'over the weekend, high-value OG Instagram handles, dormant institutional accounts, and verified profiles were stolen in minutes.' This temporal clustering and account-type selectivity is anomalous.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect multiple successful credential compromises of verified or institutional accounts within a 60-minute window. Weight alerts higher when account names match known high-value patterns (OG handles, institutional domains).

suggestion.title: Password Reset Followed by Anomalous Access Geography
suggestion.rationale: Stolen accounts used for resale implies immediate access attempts from attacker infrastructure, not victim's known locations. Article notes 'stolen usernames listed for resale,' indicating immediate post-takeover activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After a password reset via chatbot, flag sign-ins from IP geographies outside the victim's historical baseline within 15 minutes. Cross-reference against known attacker ASNs if available.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Chatbot Action: Credential Handoff Request
suggestion.rationale: Core attack: 'simply asking the bot to hand over access.' Detect chatbot conversations requesting credential resets, password exports, or access tokens.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor chatbot conversation transcripts for requests containing keywords like 'reset password,' 'unlock account,' 'send me my password,' or 'give me access.' Alert on approvals that proceed without escalation to human support.

suggestion.title: Exploit Public-Facing Chatbot: Logic Flaw Enabling Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article describes a 'critical logic flaw in Meta's AI-powered Instagram support chatbot.' Detect repeated chatbot queries using flaw-exploitation patterns or unusual conversation sequences.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal chatbot conversation flows; alert on conversations that skip identity verification steps, request sensitive actions without escalation, or follow known exploit patterns reported by security researchers.

suggestion.title: Accessibility Service Abuse Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title and body explicitly state 'Abuses Accessibility Service to control devices' — the core distinctive capability. Pipeline generated zero detections for this attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual accessibility service permission requests/grants to non-system apps. Track accessibility event patterns consistent with input capture (TYPE_VIEW_TEXT_CHANGED fired from banking apps without corresponding user interaction). Flag accessibility permissions granted to apps posing as utilities.

suggestion.title: Malicious APK Download from Phishing Link
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'spreads through malicious links disguised as downloads from trusted, well-known applications' — clear initial access vector pipeline omitted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect network requests to C2 infrastructure (bitlrewards-app.com, 199.217.99.122) followed by APK file downloads. Monitor for DNS queries to lookalike domains mimicking legitimate app vendors. Alert on executable downloads (*.apk) from unexpected URLs.

suggestion.title: C2 Beaconing to OverlayPhantom Network IOCs
suggestion.rationale: Article lists network IOCs (199.217.99.122, bitlrewards-app.com) but pipeline output IOC field was empty and no C2 detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound connections from Android devices to 199.217.99.122 or domains resolving to bitlrewards-app.com. Correlate DNS queries with HTTP/HTTPS traffic. Flag periodic beaconing patterns consistent with C2 check-in intervals.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Overlay Window Creation & Input Capture
suggestion.rationale: Banking trojans leverage accessibility to create fake login overlays for credential theft; article states 'placing banking credentials...at serious risk' but pipeline missed the collection mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor accessibility event logs for input capture patterns (sustained TYPE_VIEW_TEXT_CHANGED events from non-input-field apps, TYPE_VIEW_CLICKED events indicating button presses). Flag overlay window creation by apps lacking display permissions. Detect input events in banking/finance app context without corresponding user gesture.

suggestion.title: Sideloaded Non-PlayStore APK Installation
suggestion.rationale: Malware delivery via links to non-Play Store APKs; article emphasizes phishing link distribution but pipeline produced no installation detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on APK installation via sideloading (install_from_unknown_source=true). Flag installations sourced from URLs matching C2 domains or phishing indicators. Baseline against device policy and alert if sideloading disabled-yet-installed occurs.

suggestion.title: OverlayPhantom File Hash Matching
suggestion.rationale: Article provides three SHA256 hashes but pipeline IOC output was empty; hash-based installation detection should be primary detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Match files/processes against hashes 9ef37376bfaa18e193cc72218924ad8ebf56d2667d348f0eae5ae6ec45ab8775, f8b614a2918378063d6e6655b676ceb52ae65b1510e2cc08087fcac31acb7aeb, 8ddc1f2a75f3d5b5bd054a5367bd5015ebc90f3453d63c7cce438c12dc2ae86a on endpoint install / process startup. Hash match = immediate high-fidelity indicator.

suggestion.title: Dragon Weave C2 Command and Control Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'Dragon Weave' as the active threat actor. China-aligned APT groups must establish persistent C2 channels; the pipeline failed to surface detection for this fundamental attack phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor endpoints in Czech Republic and Taiwan for anomalous outbound connections to suspicious IP ranges (especially China-geolocated), unusual DNS queries for newly registered or suspicious domains, and persistent beacon-like connection patterns with consistent intervals. Correlate with known Dragon Weave infrastructure indicators.

suggestion.title: Spear Phishing Initial Access for Dragon Weave Targeting Czech / Taiwan Government
suggestion.rationale: China-aligned APT campaigns targeting government entities in Czech Republic and Taiwan characteristically initiate via spear phishing with credential harvesters or malware attachments. No initial-access detection provided despite article's attack notification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound emails with suspicious attachments, embedded hyperlinks to typosquatted or newly-registered domains, and emails targeting known personnel in Czech and Taiwan government ministries. Alert on file execution of archived payloads and subsequent process spawning.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via SMB Enumeration and Service Deployment
suggestion.rationale: Post-compromise lateral movement across Czech and Taiwan networks is a critical attack step for a multi-target APT operation. No lateral-movement detection use cases generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious SMB traffic patterns, enumeration of shares across network segments, scheduled task creation via schtasks or PowerShell, and installation of services via sc.exe. Flag unusual process spawning from SYSTEM or NETWORK SERVICE contexts initiating remote process execution.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting and Persistence via Scheduled Tasks or Registry Modification
suggestion.rationale: Dragon Weave operations targeting government entities require credential theft and persistent access mechanisms. No credential-access or persistence detections generated despite high-severity threat notification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious registry modifications to authentication providers, keylogger or screen-capture process execution, and harvesting of LSASS memory. Monitor for creation of scheduled tasks executing system enumeration scripts, credential dumping tools, or remote access utilities.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration via Encrypted Tunnels and Web Shells
suggestion.rationale: Attack campaigns flagged as high-severity against Czech Republic and Taiwan government imply strategic intelligence objectives requiring exfiltration. No collection or exfiltration use cases provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify large outbound data transfers to non-whitelisted external IPs, especially those geolocated to China or known proxy infrastructure. Monitor for web shell file creation, suspicious HTTP POST/PUT operations with data payloads, and DNS tunneling for command exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Oracle WebLogic T3/IIOP Protocol Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated attacker with network access via T3, IIOP' can exploit the vulnerability. No detection UC generated despite explicit attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on network connections to WebLogic standard T3/IIOP ports (7001, 7002, 8001, 8002) from untrusted sources, especially with unexpected payload patterns, failed auth sequences, or rapid connection attempts. Filter for source IPs not in asset management DB as known clients.

suggestion.title: Unpatched WebLogic Server Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes federal patch due-date urgency and recommends asset-exposure hunt template. Pipeline failed to materialize exposure detection referencing CVE-2024-21182.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference network exposure scans identifying WebLogic instances listening on T3/IIOP against patch inventory. Flag instances without recent CVE-2024-21182 remediation OR unable to connect for patch verification within SLA window before 2026-06-04 due date.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Data Exfiltration from WebLogic
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies successful exploitation yields 'unauthorized access to critical data or complete access to all Oracle WebLogic Server accessible data.' No UC addresses post-exploitation data movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WebLogic JVM process for bulk file reads from DOMAIN_HOME/config (esp. datasource.xml), unexpected database connection strings in memory, or unusual SQL query volumes that deviate from baseline. Alert on zip/tar archive creation in WEBLOGIC_HOME by compromised process.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Docker image upload to public repository
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'poisoning a Docker Hub repository to later steal Kubernetes secrets'—registry tampering is a critical supply-chain vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for image manifest modifications, unusual image pushes to public registries by service accounts, or image layer additions post-build. Correlate with scanner/build tool invocation.

suggestion.title: Stealer execution within container build/scan process
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'stealer that was loaded during the KICS scanning process'—malicious payload injection into CI/CD pipelines.
log_sources: Network connection logs from build pod
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for unexpected child processes spawned by container scanners (KICS, trivy, etc.), DNS/IP connections from scanner pods to external hosts, or process memory indicators of stealer capabilities.

suggestion.title: Kubernetes API enumeration and credential exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'steal Kubernetes secrets and other sensitive data'—attacker pivots from compromised container to k8s control plane.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unauthorized GET/LIST requests to secrets API, service account token abuse, or secret contents transmitted outside cluster. Correlate container lateral movement with API access from pod.

suggestion.title: Container escape via privileged capability abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article enumerates CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_SYS_MODULE, CAP_SYS_PTRACE, CAP_NET_ADMIN as exploitation vectors: 'container escape followed by host compromise.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for containers running with dangerous capabilities (CAP_SYS_ADMIN without justification), syscall patterns consistent with namespace escape (clone, unshare), or kernel module loading from container.

suggestion.title: Orchestration API abuse from compromised pod
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 'exploitation of orchestration APIs' as a current attack vector; compromised container pivots to cluster management.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect container processes calling orchestration APIs directly (e.g., via mounted socket), unusual API object creation/modification, or attempts to create new privileged pods.

suggestion.title: Host system exploitation from container context
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'exploiting vulnerabilities in the host system and container runtime components' leads to 'host compromise.'
log_sources: Host audit logs (unusual syscalls from container)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for kernel exploitation attempts (CVE patterns in runtime logs), abnormal container syscall sequences targeting host isolation, or privilege escalation from container runtime daemon.

suggestion.title: Detect HTTP POST to Magento Cache Plugin Exploitation Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated PHP object injection flaw' and 'no login required'—indicates HTTP POST exploitation path to vulnerable endpoint. Pipeline generated zero hunting recommendations despite this clear initial-access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP POST requests to Mirasvit Cache Warmer directories with serialized PHP objects in request body. Look for POST to /mirasvit-cache or similar endpoints with payloads containing 'O:' (PHP serialization marker) or unserialize patterns. High-volume scanning attempts would indicate reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: Detect PHP Object Deserialization Attacks in Web Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'PHP object injection flaw'—deserialization of untrusted data is the exploitation mechanism. No detection UC covers this attack primitive.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on serialized PHP object patterns in HTTP request payloads, particularly to Magento/e-commerce platforms. Track 'O:' strings (object notation), 'R:' (reference notation), and common gadget chain signatures in POST data. Filter false positives from legitimate serialized session data.

suggestion.title: Detect Process Execution from PHP-FPM/Apache Context
suggestion.rationale: RCE via object injection results in code execution within web server process. Article states attackers achieve 'remote code execution'—need detection for spawned processes from web service context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual child processes spawned by php-fpm, apache2, or nginx (e.g., shell, curl, wget, nc). Baseline legitimate plugin activity and alert on deviations. Watch for process cmdlines with common payload indicators: shell metacharacters, base64 encoding, or known tool names in suspicious context.

suggestion.title: Detect Suspicious File Write to Web-Accessible Directories
suggestion.rationale: RCE typically followed by webshell persistence or file modification. Article context (caching plugin) suggests cache directory exploitation—need to detect malicious file persistence in web root or cache paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PHP files written to cache directories, temp paths, or web-accessible locations originating from php-fpm/apache. Alert on .php/.phtml files in /var/www/magento/cache, /tmp, or upload directories. Correlate file creation with suspicious web request patterns.

suggestion.title: Detect Outbound Network Connections from Web Server
suggestion.rationale: Post-RCE attacker behavior typically involves C2 communication. Article mentions 'remote code execution' but no detection for post-exploitation command channels.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected outbound connections (non-standard ports, non-whitelisted destinations) from php-fpm/apache processes. Baseline legitimate plugin behavior (CDN, update checks) and alert on deviations. Flag DNS queries for suspicious domains from web server context.

suggestion.title: WordPress Admin Account Creation via Plugin Exploit
suggestion.rationale: Article headline: 'actively exploited to create admin accounts.' Pipeline generated zero UCs despite this core attack objective.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WordPress wp_users table INSERT/UPDATE events and wp_usermeta for privilege escalation. Correlate with unauthenticated HTTP POST requests to wp-admin/user-new.php or plugin-specific endpoints. Alert on new user_role=administrator without corresponding admin user session.

suggestion.title: Exploitation of Unauthenticated Plugin Vulnerability
suggestion.rationale: Title implies public-facing flaw: 'actively exploited.' No execution/initial-access UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to /wp-content/plugins/wp-maps-pro/ endpoints with unusual parameter patterns, POST payloads, or file uploads. Monitor for 200 responses followed by user creation events within 60 seconds.

suggestion.title: WP Maps Pro Plugin Exploitation Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Plugin name mentioned in title but no IOC or specific exploitation signatures captured by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST requests to wp-maps-pro plugin endpoints missing authentication context; monitor for plugin version disclosure in HTTP responses; flag unexpected file writes under /wp-content/plugins/wp-maps-pro/ or sibling directories suggesting web shell injection.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via WordPress User Role Modification
suggestion.rationale: End goal is admin account creation (persistence via privilege escalation). No detection for role promotion events.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor wp_usermeta table for user_role or wp_user_roles changes, especially role=administrator assignments to newly created accounts. Correlate with web access logs showing unauthenticated requests in the 60 seconds prior.

suggestion.title: Web Shell or Backdoor Installation via Plugin Flaw
suggestion.rationale: Active exploitation implies post-exploitation artifacts. No detection for secondary payloads or persistence mechanisms suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected .php, .phtml, or .phar files written to web-accessible directories (wp-content/uploads, wp-content/plugins, wp-admin). Flag requests to newly created files with execution intent (eval, system, exec calls in response body).

suggestion.title: High-Volume Failed Login Attempts Against Single Account
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'brute-force attacks that attempted logins from distant locations'. Rapid-fire authentication failures are the signature of this attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when 5+ failed login attempts occur against the same account within a 15-minute window. Establish per-user legitimate failure baselines; escalate on anomalous spikes. Correlate with source IP diversity and geographic spread for confidence scoring.

suggestion.title: Login Attempts from Geographically Impossible or New Locations
suggestion.rationale: Article reports attacks 'from distant locations and unknown devices'. Impossible-travel and geographic anomalies are key brute-force indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect authentication attempts from countries or regions a user has never accessed from, especially within hours of previous successful logins from different geographies. New/unknown device involvement increases confidence.

suggestion.title: Unsolicited Device Registration Verification Codes
suggestion.rationale: Users 'received notices of suspicious access requests...emails contained verification codes for legitimate account owners to register new devices.' Attackers triggered MFA challenges without authorization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when device registration or MFA verification codes are sent without corresponding user-initiated requests. Elevated signal if multiple codes sent in rapid succession to the same account.

suggestion.title: Account Lockout Clustering Following Authentication Storms
suggestion.rationale: Dashlane triggered 'suspension of those accounts as part of Dashlane's built-in security controls'. Account lockouts clustering in time correlate with automated brute-force defenses.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate account lockout events with preceding failed authentication attempts. When lockout follows 5+ failed logins within 20 minutes, classify as defensive response to attack. Track scope to estimate campaign scale.

suggestion.title: Multi-Source Login Attempts Targeting Same Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'distant locations' without specifying single source, indicating distributed attack. Multiple source IPs against the same account(s) is a classic brute-force signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect when 3+ distinct source IPs attempt authentication for the same account(s) within 30 minutes. Escalate if sources span multiple ASNs or countries. Baseline organizational patterns to reduce false positives.

suggestion.title: JavaScript Injection Pattern Detection (t.js?site=<id>)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'JavaScript injection following the t.js?site=<id> pattern, where <id> is a unique value assigned to each compromised website.' This is a forensic signature of DriveSurge infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests matching pattern 't.js?site=' from any domain, or unexpected script includes from unfamiliar domains on legitimate websites. Correlate with DOM modifications on web servers and establish baselines for legitimate JavaScript sources.

suggestion.title: Fake Browser Update Executable Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Fake update for Firefox that downloaded a ZIP archive containing multiple DLLs and a malicious executable named Browser Update.exe.' Specific detectable artifact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on downloads of 'Browser Update.exe' or variant filenames from non-official browser domains. Monitor for ZIP extractions containing executables from domains impersonating Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari, Opera, Brave, Yandex, Vivaldi, Samsung Internet, or UC Browser.

suggestion.title: PowerShell Execution Following ClickFix Social Engineering
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'ClickFix attacks involve PowerShell commands.' Attackers socially engineer users into copying and executing malicious PowerShell via web redirects.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PowerShell invocation shortly after web browser activity, especially with obfuscated parameters or clipboard paste operations. Flag unusual process parents (browsers invoking shell) or suspicious command-line argument patterns.

suggestion.title: macOS Clipboard Hijacking via Verification-Themed ClickFix
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Obfuscated JavaScript payload specifically designed to target macOS desktop systems, delivered via verification-themed ClickFix attacks that hijack the clipboard.' Platform-specific gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor unauthorized clipboard read operations from Safari, Chrome, or Firefox on macOS. Alert on clipboard paste events into Terminal following suspicious authentication/verification prompts. Detect obfuscated JavaScript execution in browser context.

suggestion.title: Silent Website Redirection via zTDS Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Using zTDS, DriveSurge hijacks thousands of legitimate, high-reputation websites and silently redirects visitors to malware, unbeknownst to the sites' owners.' Describes traffic distribution compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web server logs for unexpected 302/303 redirects to unfamiliar destinations. Alert on visitor traffic patterns through known TDS infrastructure. Detect modifications to web server files or unexpected script injections into legitimate pages.

suggestion.title: DLL Execution Chain from Fake Update ZIP Archive
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Fake update for Firefox...downloaded a ZIP archive containing multiple DLLs and a malicious executable.' DLL staging and execution from user-controlled archives is detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on rundll32.exe execution with DLLs from Downloads or temp directories recently extracted from ZIP. Monitor DLL loading from suspicious paths following browser-initiated archive downloads. Correlate archive extraction with child process execution.

suggestion.title: WebSphere Malformed Request Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers 'execute arbitrary code through specially crafted HTTP requests' but pipeline generated no detection for the exploit delivery itself. Need to surface attempts to send exploit payloads to WebSphere endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WebSphere endpoints (port 80, 443, Web Server Plug-in communication ports) for HTTP requests with anomalous structure, oversized headers, or payload patterns consistent with CVE-2026-8633/8620 exploitation attempts. Correlation with known exploit signatures or request patterns deviating from baseline application traffic.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Code Execution from WebSphere Plugin Process
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'optional Web Server Plug-ins component' is the attack surface. No use case detects code execution spawning from the plugin/AppServer process post-exploitation. This is the consequence of successful RCE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect abnormal child processes spawned by WebSphere/plugin worker processes (wsadmin, plugin container, Java process) that don't match deployment baseline—particularly shells, script interpreters, or reverse shell utilities. Include behavior analytics on unexpected outbound connections or file writes from these process chains.

suggestion.title: WebSphere Server Post-Exploitation Network Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Successful RCE via CVE-2026-8633/8620 would enable attacker to establish persistence and C2. No hunt addresses detection of callback attempts or data exfiltration originating from compromised WebSphere hosts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound HTTPS/HTTP/DNS from WebSphere application servers to known attacker infrastructure, non-standard ports, or high-volume data transfers post-exploitation. Include detection of C2 checkins or DNS tunneling attempts from WebSphere process context.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-8633 / CVE-2026-8620 Vulnerability Scan Absence
suggestion.rationale: Article describes enterprise deployments as critical risk. Absence of scheduled vulnerability scanning for these CVEs in production WebSphere infrastructure is a coverage gap—detection should alert when scans do NOT detect these CVEs (indicating no scanning coverage).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for WebSphere Application Server instances (especially those with optional Web Server Plug-ins enabled) that have NOT been scanned for CVE-2026-8633 or CVE-2026-8620 within the last 30 days. Alert on missing or incomplete vulnerability assessment coverage.

suggestion.title: AppDomainManager Registry Hijacking Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'AppDomainManager hijacking' as the core attack vector. This requires registry writes to .NET CLR configuration keys, which should be detectable via registry events. No use case exists for this signature attack step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious registry writes to .NET Framework or CLR registry hives (HKCU\Software\Classes\.NET, HKLM\Software\Classes\.NET) creating or modifying AppDomain entries. Alert on modifications from non-system processes or those that load untrusted DLLs via AppDomainManager references.

suggestion.title: Suspicious COR_PROFILER and COMPLUS_* Environment Variable Injection
