suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'sophisticated .NET hijacking technique'—AppDomainManager hijacking often pivots on COR_PROFILER or COMPLUS_* environment variable manipulation to load malicious assemblies. No detection case captures this common execution path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process creation events where COR_PROFILER, COR_ENABLE_PROFILING, COMPLUS_ProfAPI_ProfilerCompatibilitySetting, or similar .NET CLR variables are set, especially pointing to non-standard DLL paths. Establish baseline for legitimate .NET profilers (e.g., Visual Studio, performance monitoring tools); alert on anomalous parent processes (e.g., Office, browsers).

suggestion.title: Malicious DLL Load via .NET CLR by Injected Profiler
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 12 SHA256 hashes—likely the malicious DLLs injected via AppDomainManager hijacking. Detection should target the DLL load phase when suspicious .NET processes load these artifacts from non-standard paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when .NET runtime processes (msbuild.exe, csc.exe, dotnet.exe) load DLLs from temporary directories, %APPDATA%, or web-downloaded locations. Correlate with the provided SHA256 hashes or with suspicious registry modifications setting up AppDomainManager or COR_PROFILER in the same session.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Network C2 Connections from .NET Runtime Processes
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies command-and-control domains (6 listed). Once hijacked, .NET runtimes execute attacker code and initiate outbound connections. Pipeline correctly noted domain IOCs but generated no network hunt template for this phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound connections from .NET runtime processes to the identified C2 domains, especially on non-standard ports or over encrypted protocols that obscure payload inspection. Baseline legitimate .NET domains (NuGet, Microsoft, CDNs); flag deviations.

suggestion.title: EDR Evasion via Tampered .NET Code Access Security Policy
suggestion.rationale: Article states goal is 'evade EDR detection'—AppDomainManager hijacking can disable .NET Code Access Security (CAS) or security manager restrictions. Pipeline did not generate a detection case for this defensive evasion step, which would be signature behavior for this attack chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect registry writes disabling .NET CAS or modifying CLR security policies (registry paths containing 'Security', 'CodeAccessSecurity', 'TrustedPath'). Alert on AppDomainManager security settings being weakened or removed, especially outside of system updates or legitimate administrative windows.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Installation from Untrusted Registry
suggestion.rationale: Article describes supply-chain compromise of Red Hat npm packages. Title establishes npm as distribution vector ('compromises Red Hat npm Packages'). Should detect unusual package source transitions, version jumps, or installs from non-official registries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install/ci commands for package sources deviating from package-lock.json registry baseline or pulling from secondary registries. Alert on successful installs of packages with recent timestamps or unusual author churn, especially for Red Hat-maintained packages.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting via Worm Payload Execution
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly mentions 'Credential-Stealing Worm.' Article should detail credential extraction mechanism. No detection for browser credential access, shell history, or environment variable enumeration for secrets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child processes spawned from npm or Node.js interpreters targeting credential stores: lsass.exe queries, chrome/firefox process handle operations, HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Internet Settings registry access. Flag outbound API calls from npm-sourced script to exfiltration endpoints.

suggestion.title: Anomalous npm Package Post-Installation Script Execution
suggestion.rationale: Worm delivery suggests malicious postinstall hooks. No use case covers arbitrary script execution via package.json scripts field after installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unsigned or obfuscated PowerShell/Node.js execution spawned from npm package directories or node_modules post-install. Correlate suspicious process lineage (npm → cmd/powershell → rundll32/certutil) with package freshness.

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration to C2 Over HTTPS
suggestion.rationale: Title implies stolen credentials must be exfiltrated. No detection for encrypted C2 callbacks or credential posting to attacker-controlled endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTPS POST requests from Node.js/npm processes to newly-registered or low-reputation domains, especially payloads containing base64-encoded credential formats (browser password store, token dumps). Monitor for DNS queries to C2 domains from compromised hosts.

suggestion.title: npm Package Propagation to Downstream Dependencies
suggestion.rationale: Worm behavior implies self-replication or lateral distribution via package dependencies. No detection for recursive/horizontal package installs or dependency chain manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for recursive npm install invocations or install trees exceeding normal depth/breadth for single developer workflow. Correlate package version bumps or lock-file changes with installation of secondary/previously-unused packages in monorepo or CI pipelines.

suggestion.title: Malicious npm Package Metadata or Binary Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks often inject checksums or replace binaries. Article doesn't surface detection for package signature verification failure, hash mismatches, or native module compilation anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm package integrity check failures (npm audit, npm verify mismatches). Monitor for native module (.node) compilation via gyp/node-gyp with unusual include paths or external source URLs. Flag failed signature validation on Red Hat-authored packages.

suggestion.title: npm Preinstall Script Execution with Credential Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'preinstall scripts [that] run automatically during npm install, before any of your own code executes' and payload that 'harvests secrets and credentials from the local environment and CI context: environment variables, ~/.npmrc tokens, SSH keys, GitHub tokens, and CI/CD secrets.' Pipe detection directly tied to the Miasma execution vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Node.js child processes spawned from npm package install context that access credential files (npmrc, SSH keys, GitHub token paths) or read environment variables containing secrets. Look for preinstall hooks executing obfuscated payloads or using eval().

suggestion.title: Suspicious Cloud Identity Enumeration from npm Install
suggestion.rationale: Article highlights 'new collectors for GCP and Azure that enumerate every identity the infected host can assume' as a key behavioral change. 'This one is oriented toward mapping and reaching the cloud control plane itself.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GCP (gcloud, Compute API) and Azure (az CLI, IMDS endpoint) enumeration calls originating from npm or Node.js processes, especially from CI runners or development workstations running npm install. Flag rapid identity discovery attempts.

suggestion.title: npm Package Republishing by Compromised Maintainer
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'It queries the registry for other packages the compromised identity can publish and republishes them, carrying the same payload, which is what turns a single compromised maintainer into a worm.' Clear propagation vector via npm registry automation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm publish operations for packages in @redhat-cloud-services and similar internally-managed namespaces; flag republishes of existing packages within short time windows, especially those lacking corresponding git commits or code review. Cross-reference against maintainer account compromise indicators.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated JavaScript Execution via eval() in npm Package
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'heavily obfuscated JavaScript file' that 'relied on eval() and ROT-based string decoding to hide the logic, a tradecraft pattern seen in earlier Shai-Hulud variants.' File analysis signal for malicious npm packages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Node.js processes executing large eval() statements with ROT or Base64 decoding chains in a single preinstall script. Correlate against npm package hashes and monitor for matching patterns in index.js files across @redhat-cloud-services namespace.

suggestion.title: GitHub OIDC Token Request from npm Publishing Workflow
suggestion.rationale: Article describes root cause: 'GitHub Actions workflow that...Requested a GitHub OIDC identity token via id-token: write.' This automated token issuance enabled package signing with valid SLSA provenance despite account compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag GitHub Actions workflows in RedHatInsights repositories that request id-token: write permissions without corresponding code review, especially those pushing directly to npm registry. Correlate OIDC token issuance timestamps against unexpected package publications.

suggestion.title: Malicious npm Package with Dune → Greek Mythology Rebranding
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'references to Greek mythology have replaced the original Dune-themed cosmetic elements' and notes 'Newly created attacker repositories carry the description Miasma: The Spreading Blight, which is a useful hunting signal.' Behavioral IOC for worm variant tracking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for newly created repositories or npm packages with 'Miasma: The Spreading Blight' description, references to 'spartan' in package metadata, or code structure matching the open-sourced Shai-Hulud framework. Cross-check against known Red Hat package maintainers.

suggestion.title: Process execution from node_modules post-npm install
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'credential-stealing malware' deployed via npm. Malware executes during package import or post-install hooks from node_modules. This is the actual execution vector for npm supply chain—missing entirely from generated UCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process creation from node_modules paths or npm post-install script execution (package.json 'install' field). Correlate with preceding npm install of @redhat-cloud-services packages within last 30 minutes. Flag execution of shell interpreters, curl, powershell originating from node_modules.

suggestion.title: Credential file access following npm package installation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'credential-stealing malware'—the core attack objective. Must detect correlation between npm package install and subsequent reads of ~/.aws/credentials, .ssh/config, .git/credentials, browser token caches.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for file read/access operations on credential paths (patterns: .aws/credentials, .ssh, .npmrc, .git/config, browser cache dirs) within 5-30 min after npm install events targeting @redhat-cloud-services. Low baseline expected; nearly all instances suspicious on dev machines.

suggestion.title: Suspicious network exfiltration post-npm package execution
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'worm' variant with credential stealing implies C2 callback for credential exfiltration. Pipeline detected zero exfiltration techniques (T1041, T1071). Must flag anomalous outbound connections from dev machines after npm execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify outbound HTTPS/DNS to rare/uncategorized destinations within 15 min of npm package execution. Flag traffic containing credential-like patterns (base64 keys, AWS/GCP/Azure secret prefixes). Correlate with WHOIS age (newly registered domains).

suggestion.title: npm token theft and unauthorized package operations
suggestion.rationale: Stolen credentials likely include npm tokens from ~/.npmrc. Attackers could use for lateral supply-chain poisoning. Article mentions 'over 30 packages'—supply chain control enables multi-package compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm registry API logs for token auth from new IPs/geolocations post-install. Flag publish/update attempts on other @redhat-cloud-services packages or org packages using exfiltrated tokens.

suggestion.title: Malicious npm Package Installation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title names 'codexui-android' as malicious npm package—primary attack vector. Pipeline generated zero use cases for package installation anomalies despite this being core delivery mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm/yarn install of 'codexui-android' or similar-named packages. Monitor for package installation from non-standard registries, packages with suspiciously low download counts, or recent package creation dates. Cross-reference against package blocklists and validate cryptographic signatures.

suggestion.title: OpenAI Authentication Token Exfiltration via Compromised Dependency
suggestion.rationale: Article describes stolen OpenAI Codex authentication tokens. Pipeline failed to generate detection for credential access or token exfiltration despite being core impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unauthorized reads of .env files, OPENAI_API_KEY environment variables, or credential stores by npm package processes. Monitor memory access patterns of dependency code reading sensitive configuration. Flag exfiltration of tokens to external domains.

suggestion.title: Anomalous OpenAI API Request Volume Post-Token Theft
suggestion.rationale: Stolen tokens enable unauthorized Codex API calls. Article impact is token compromise but pipeline generated no use case for detecting API abuse or resource consumption anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline OpenAI API request volume, geographic origin, and request types per API key. Alert on sudden >3-sigma increase in requests, calls from unexpected geographies, or API usage patterns inconsistent with known application behavior.

suggestion.title: Package Manifest Tampering and Transitive Dependency Injection
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain compromise typically modifies dependency trees. Article describes npm package injection but pipeline missed detection for altered package.json / package-lock.json.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor modifications to package.json, package-lock.json, and yarn.lock for new dependencies with zero stars, newly-registered authors, or suspicious transitive chains. Alert on lockfile changes that introduce packages not explicitly declared in manifests.

suggestion.title: Codex API Exploitation via Token Misuse
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically mentions 'OpenAI Codex' tokens stolen. Compromised tokens enable code-generation and execution via Codex API, but pipeline generated no execution or command-and-control use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound HTTPS to api.openai.com/v1/code* endpoints from processes outside development tooling. Alert on automated code generation workflows triggered by external API responses. Detect compilation/execution of Codex-generated code in non-dev environments.

suggestion.title: RAT Callback Detection from Post-ClickFix Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'remote access malware' and lists T1071 (Application Layer Protocol) but provides zero hunt for C2 communication. Article states malware 'infects' hosts and references 4 C2 IPs/domains, implying callback phase after initial execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate newly-spawned powershell.exe / mshta.exe processes (from ClickFix execution, parent=explorer.exe) with outbound network connections to non-RFC1918 destinations within 5 minutes. Filter out connections to known-good CDNs and legitimate download sites to isolate anomalous callback traffic.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated/Encoded Payload Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1027 (Obfuscated Files or Information) but no UC detects obfuscated payload decode/execution. ClickFix attacks typically deliver base64-encoded or compressed PowerShell; the article notes 'malicious script' without visible deobfuscation indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for powershell.exe / mshta.exe with command-line or script-block containing FromBase64String, DecompressString, ExpandString, or similar decode/decompress keywords, especially when parent is explorer.exe or browser (indicating clipboard-paste flow from fake CAPTCHA).

suggestion.title: RAT Persistence via Registry Autorun or Process Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'RAT malware' installation but lists no technique for post-execution persistence (T1055, T1547 are absent). RATs typically achieve persistence via registry autoruns or process hollowing to survive reboot.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious registry writes to HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\Run, HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\Run, or Services registries originating from powershell.exe / mshta.exe child processes within 2 minutes of ClickFix execution. Alternatively, hunt for anomalous process injection (e.g., powershell.exe opening handle to svchost.exe / rundll32.exe with memory write permission).

suggestion.title: Masquerading of Malicious Script as System/Security Tool
suggestion.rationale: Article states ClickFix lures victims via 'fake verification pages'—the script itself likely impersonates legitimate Windows or security tools. T1036 (Masquerading) is absent from the technique list but core to social engineering effectiveness.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for process creation with anomalous parent-child relationships (e.g., explorer.exe spawning system-tool names like 'svchost.exe', 'csrss.exe', 'lsass.exe' with unsigned or unusual file paths). Correlate to clipboard activity or recent downloads from phishing domains.

suggestion.title: Brute-Force Authentication Spike Against Web Password Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Brute-Force Attack'; pipeline failed to surface credential-access detection. Phrase: 'Dashlane Discloses Brute-Force Attack'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag >10 failed authentication attempts from a single source IP to password-manager-hosted endpoints within 5 minutes, especially from known botnet infrastructure. Correlate failed attempts to subsequent successful logons within the same session or source IP to identify compromised credentials.

suggestion.title: Bulk Vault Export or Multi-User Data Download
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Encrypted Vaults of Fewer Than 20 Users Downloaded'—explicit exfiltration of multiple user datasets. Pipeline missed this attack phase entirely. Phrase: 'Encrypted Vaults of Fewer Than 20 Users Downloaded'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for API calls or authenticated sessions requesting multiple vault exports, bulk user-data retrieval, or downloads exceeding baseline user data-access patterns. Alert on download payloads matching encrypted credential-store file signatures.

suggestion.title: Geographic or Device Anomaly During Successful Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Brute-force attacks typically involve IP/geo anomalies or non-standard access patterns. No baseline-deviation detection was suggested despite attack vector being stated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful authentications following brute-force attempts from geographies, IP ranges, or devices inconsistent with user baseline. Flag logons from residential proxies or known botnet infrastructure.

suggestion.title: File Hash Match: OverlayPhantom APK Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match' hunt in recommended-hunts section. Three SHA256 hashes provided. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this being a standard, trivial hunt template application.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on APK files with hash matching 9ef37376bfaa18e193cc72218924ad8ebf56d2667d348f0eae5ae6ec45ab8775, f8b614a2918378063d6e6655b676ceb52ae65b1510e2cc08087fcac31acb7aeb, or 8ddc1f2a75f3d5b5bd054a5367bd5015ebc90f3453d63c7cce438c12dc2ae86a. Flag particularly if package name spoofs legitimate banking/financial application.

suggestion.title: C2 Communication to OverlayPhantom Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Network connections to article IPs / domains' hunt (C2 phase, high confidence). IPv4 199.217.99.122 and domain bitlrewards-app.com listed as C2. Pipeline generated zero network-phase use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound network connections from Android devices to 199.217.99.122 or domains resolving to bitlrewards-app.com. Inspect TLS certificates for other domains sharing similar issuer/fingerprints. Flag even ephemeral connections from non-system apps.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Accessibility Service Permission Grant
suggestion.rationale: Article describes OverlayPhantom as uniquely abusing 'Accessibility Service to control devices' — this is the core attack vector and attack-phase threat. No use case generated despite article text explicitly highlighting this capability as 'particularly alarming.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on BIND_ACCESSIBILITY_SERVICE permission grants to non-system apps, especially those installed via sideload or phishing link. Cross-reference with app package naming against legitimate banking/financial app manifests to detect spoofed variants.

suggestion.title: Input Capture via Accessibility Service (Keystroke Logging)
suggestion.rationale: Accessibility Service in Android enables TYPE_VIEW_TEXT_CHANGED and input event capture — critical for banking trojan credential theft. Article states threat is 'placing banking credentials...at serious risk' but pipeline mapped no input-capture techniques (T1056).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for accessibility services from unknown publishers that request continuous active monitoring with event capture flags active when banking/financial apps are in foreground. Alert on suspicious memory access patterns consistent with keystroke hook implantation.

suggestion.title: Credential and Payment Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states malware targets 'banking credentials, financial data, and cryptocurrency accounts.' No exfiltration-phase use case generated. Pipeline missed T1533 (exfiltrate payment card information) and T1041 techniques.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on encrypted data uploads to 199.217.99.122 or bitlrewards-app.com following period of accessibility service activity. Monitor for abnormal file I/O patterns accessing Android credential storage (/data/data/*/databases, shared_prefs) or system keyrings followed by network egress.

suggestion.title: Dragon Weave Malware Execution Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article headline explicitly names 'Dragon Weave' as the threat actor conducting attacks against Czech Republic and Taiwan; any legitimate article text would describe attack execution methods, but pipeline returned empty kill chain and zero use cases, indicating complete failure to extract attack steps.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detection should look for process execution patterns, command-line obfuscation, and network callbacks consistent with Dragon Weave tooling. Typical patterns include scheduled task spawning, WMI process creation, or PowerShell invocation with encoded payloads.

suggestion.title: Czech Republic / Taiwan Targeting Campaign Initial Access
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates geographic targeting of Czech Republic and Taiwan, but pipeline returned zero IOCs and empty initial-access phase in kill chain. This suggests failure to extract phishing, supply-chain, or exploitation vectors that would establish entry points.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for email campaigns targeting .cz and .tw domains, unusual supplier communications, or exploitation of public-facing applications known to be leveraged in China-aligned intrusions.

suggestion.title: Dragon Weave Command & Control Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Threat actor name and geography specified in headline but zero IOCs extracted (no C2 domains, IPs, or beacons); pipeline should have surfaced C&C infrastructure if article contains any technical analysis or indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for outbound HTTPS or DNS queries to infrastructure associated with Dragon Weave campaigns; look for domains registered recently, privacy-protected, or previously tied to China-aligned groups.

suggestion.title: CVE-2024-21182 Patch Status Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Oracle WebLogic contains an unspecified vulnerability' with explicit guidance to 'match against your vulnerability scanner.' Core asset-exposure detection is absent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any system reporting Oracle WebLogic Server in software inventory AND flagged vulnerable to CVE-2024-21182 by Qualys/Nessus/Rapid7. Cross-reference patch date against federal deadline (2026-06-04) to escalate compliance risk.

suggestion.title: T3/IIOP Protocol Exploitation Attempts to WebLogic
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated attacker with network access via T3, IIOP' — named attack channels warrant protocol-specific detection rules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for inbound T3 protocol traffic (port 7001, RMI registry) to WebLogic servers from untrusted CIDR ranges or with payload anomalies. Alert on IIOP connections lacking corresponding authentication records in WebLogic audit logs within 10 seconds.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Data Exfiltration from WebLogic
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'complete access to all Oracle WebLogic Server accessible data' — exfiltration phase detection is completely absent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect WebLogic process initiating large outbound connections post-exploit. Flag bulk exports from weblogic/domains/ directories, database query volume spikes, or file reads to temp staging. Correlate with failed T3 authentication events in preceding hour.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated WebLogic Admin Access
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated attacker' accessing 'critical data.' Detection for authentication bypass to admin console is missing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful HTTP(S) requests to /console or /consoleapp endpoints (port 7001) returning 200 response without preceding valid credential submission. Monitor for privilege escalation or role-grant entries immediately after unauthenticated access logs.

suggestion.title: Federal Compliance Tracking: CVE-2024-21182 Patch Deadline
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Federal patch due: 2026-06-04.' Tracking mandatory compliance obligation and reporting for audit is absent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On 2026-06-04 and thereafter, escalate any remaining CVE-2024-21182 vulnerability to compliance alert. Track and report count of still-vulnerable systems. Enforce mandatory remediation workflow for post-deadline detections.

suggestion.title: WebLogic T3 Port Reconnaissance and Fingerprinting
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'known-exploited vulnerabilities' and 'actively exploited in the wild.' Pre-attack reconnaissance targeting WebLogic assets deserves early-warning detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect network scans or repeated connection attempts to port 7001 (T3) from external IP ranges. Alert on abnormal connection sequences to WebLogic endpoints. Flag HTTP User-Agent strings or requests attempting WebLogic version disclosure or diagnostic endpoints.

suggestion.title: Detect Privileged Container Deployment with Dangerous Capabilities
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_SYS_MODULE, CAP_SYS_PTRACE, CAP_NET_ADMIN as attack vectors under 'Privileged containers' section. These enable container escape and host compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Kubernetes pod specs with spec.containers[].securityContext.privileged=true or capabilities.add containing SYS_ADMIN, SYS_MODULE, SYS_PTRACE, NET_ADMIN. Monitor container runtime logs for --privileged or --cap-add flags at creation time. Correlate with process execution attempting ptrace or kernel module operations.

suggestion.title: Detect Container Escape Attempts via Kernel Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'Container escape followed by host compromise' as primary attack vector with dedicated section. Kernel namespace and cgroup isolation bypasses must be detected before host compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for kernel module loading (modprobe, insmod), namespace escape syscalls (unshare), /proc/sys modifications, ptrace to host processes, and cgroup escape patterns originating from container runtime. Alert on cross-namespace filesystem access or kernel memory mapping from container context.

suggestion.title: Detect Kubernetes API Reconnaissance and Secrets Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'Exploitation of orchestration APIs' as current vector and describes stealer 'loaded during KICS scanning process' to 'steal Kubernetes secrets and other sensitive data.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Kubernetes API calls to list/get secrets, describe service accounts, or RBAC queries. Alert on reads from /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/ or environment variable enumeration of Kubernetes credentials by non-system containers. Flag rapid sequential secret access or exfiltration to external IPs.

suggestion.title: Detect Supply Chain Compromise via Poisoned Container Image
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes TeamPCP 'poisoning a Docker Hub repository' with 'tainted images distributed a stealer' for Checkmarx KICS compromise. Supply chain entry point is the primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Docker Hub / container registry logs for unsigned image pushes, tag overwrites, and image pulls by scanning tools (KICS, Trivy). Detect unexpected process spawning during image execution (shell, network calls). Alert on images with modified layers containing injected payloads or stealer signatures.

suggestion.title: Detect Stealer Malware Behavior in Container Context
suggestion.rationale: Article states stealer 'loaded during KICS scanning process' to exfiltrate 'Kubernetes secrets and other sensitive data.' Behavioral detection of credential harvesting is essential during supply-chain execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file reads targeting /var/run/secrets, ~/.kube/config, /etc/kubernetes, or environment variable enumeration from unexpected processes during container startup. Alert on credential exfiltration (base64 encoding, zipping, network writes to external hosts). Correlate with KICS or similar scanning tool execution.

suggestion.title: Detect Host Kernel Vulnerability Exploitation from Container Runtime
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'Exploiting host system vulnerabilities' and 'Exploiting vulnerabilities in the host system and container runtime components' as primary vectors. Kernel CVEs (runc, containerd, cgroups) are exploitation paths to host.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for cgroups_release_agent exploit patterns (write to cgroup.procs and cgroup.release_agent). Alert on runc/containerd process memory access, /proc/sys/kernel modifications, or overlayfs manipulation from container context. Correlate with known CVE signatures (CVE-2021-30465, CVE-2021-22555).

suggestion.title: Magento Cache Plugin Exploit Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'unauthenticated PHP object injection flaw' allowing RCE. 'no login, configuration changes, or admin access required' establishes a public-facing attack surface with zero auth barriers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP requests to Magento installations targeting cache-plugin endpoints with serialized PHP payloads. Look for POST/GET patterns to common plugin paths with Base64-encoded object signatures or unusual parameter patterns in cache-warmer URIs.

suggestion.title: PHP Object Injection via Cache Mechanism
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability is 'PHP object injection flaw.' This is distinct from generic exploitation and requires targeted PHP deserialization payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PHP unserialize() calls on untrusted input in cache-warming contexts. Look for suspicious serialized object patterns (O:, s:, a: prefixes) in request parameters and POST bodies targeting Mirasvit plugin endpoints.

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution via Magento Caching Plugin
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes RCE as the impact: 'remotely execute malicious code.' This completes the kill-chain from initial access through execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate suspicious process spawning (PHP child processes, shell commands) with antecedent HTTP requests to Magento cache plugin endpoints. Watch for shell.exec(), system(), or proc_open() calls triggered by deserialized cache objects.

suggestion.title: Mirasvit Cache Warmer Vulnerability Scanning
suggestion.rationale: Plugin is identified as 'widely used' and vulnerable. Asset inventory detection is foundational.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all Magento installations running Mirasvit Cache Warmer plugin versions ≤ [version with fix]. Cross-reference against CVE-2026-45247 patch timeline to surface exposed assets.

suggestion.title: WordPress Plugin Exploitation - WP Maps Pro Unauthenticated Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Critical WP Maps Pro Flaw Actively Exploited' and body describes active exploitation in the wild. No endpoint patterns or payload signatures were extracted despite this being the initial attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to known WP Maps Pro vulnerable endpoints (/wp-content/plugins/wp-maps-pro/...) from external sources, especially POST requests without corresponding user-agent headers typical of interactive browsers. Track for 40x→20x response patterns indicating successful exploitation.

suggestion.title: WordPress Admin Account Creation - Unauthorized Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states outcome is 'Create Admin Accounts'. This is the persistence and privilege escalation mechanism, yet zero detection use cases address account creation anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on wp_users table inserts or wp_usermeta updates granting administrator role (meta_key='wp_user_level' or role='administrator') without corresponding legitimate admin UI activity in access logs within 5-minute window prior to account creation.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation WordPress Admin Activity - Suspicious New Admin Behavior
suggestion.rationale: Created admin accounts would immediately perform reconnaissance and data exfiltration. Article describes active exploitation but no detection hypothesis covers the post-compromise admin activity pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect newly created admin accounts performing bulk user enumeration (wp-admin/users.php with export-like requests), plugin enumeration, or configuration exfiltration within 1 hour of account creation. Baseline should show 0 admin accounts age <1 hour during normal operations.

suggestion.title: WordPress Plugin Vulnerability Scanning Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article states flaw is 'actively exploited' implying reconnaissance phase prior to exploitation. No detection addresses scanner traffic or fingerprinting requests targeting WP Maps Pro versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sequential GET requests to WP Maps Pro files (/plugin.php?action=..., /readme.txt, /wp-maps-pro.php) from single IP within 60 seconds, especially with User-Agent strings matching known WordPress vulnerability scanners or automated tools.

suggestion.title: WordPress Backdoor Installation via Admin Privilege
suggestion.rationale: Created admin accounts serve as persistence. Article's active exploitation status implies ongoing access maintenance, yet no detection covers backdoor plugin/theme installation by newly-created admins.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for plugin/theme installations in wp-content/{plugins,themes}/ by admin accounts created within past 24 hours, especially unsigned or externally-hosted payloads. Correlate with abnormal cron execution (wp-cron.php) from non-standard PHP processes.

suggestion.title: Database Credential Harvesting via WP-Config Disclosure
suggestion.rationale: WP Maps Pro exploitation may expose wp-config.php or database credentials. Article focuses on admin creation but credential theft is typical post-exploitation behavior requiring detection coverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on requests to /wp-config.php, /wp-config.php.bak, /.env, or similar files returning 200 status from external IPs. Also monitor for database connection strings appearing in web server logs or error_log files after WP Maps Pro-related 4xx errors.

suggestion.title: High-Volume Failed Login Spike per Account
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'trying multiple passwords in succession until the correct one is found' — core brute-force signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on >10 failed login attempts per account within 15 minutes from single source IP. Correlate SourceIP, TargetUserId, timestamp. Expected FPs: user password reset cycles, SSO sync delays, automation testing.

suggestion.title: Geographically Anomalous Login Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attempted logins from distant locations and unknown devices' — geographic distance is detection signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag logins from source IP geolocation >2000km from user baseline within 24 hours. Baseline from successful logins past 30 days. Expected FPs: business travel, VPN, proxy egress.

suggestion.title: Multi-Account Device Verification Storm
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'emails contained verification codes for legitimate account owners to register new devices' sent to multiple users — indicates credential-enumeration attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert if >5 distinct accounts receive device-verification challenges within 10-minute window. Correlate by time, verification trigger type, and scope. Expected FPs: organization-wide MFA enrollment, password-reset campaign.

suggestion.title: Account Lockout Preceded by Failed Login Cluster
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'suspension of those accounts as part of Dashlane's built-in security controls' — defensive lockout triggered by brute force is an impact indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate account suspension/lockout with preceding 15+ failed logins from multiple or single IP. Lockout event itself signals attack regardless of attacker success. Expected FPs: user password-entry failures before lockout threshold.

suggestion.title: Bulk Verification-Challenge Email Distribution
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Multiple Dashlane users...received notices of suspicious access requests from foreign countries' — mass notifications indicate non-targeted credential attack or enumeration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect if 8+ users receive device-verification emails within 1-hour window with no shared department/location/IP baseline. Indicates broad-based brute force. Expected FPs: scheduled security enrollment, policy rollout, credential reset campaign.

suggestion.title: Resumed Login Attempts on Unlocked Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'some users continue to report login problems' even after 'affected accounts have now been unsuspended' — post-lockout resumption suggests attacker monitoring or retry automation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag accounts receiving failed login attempts within 30 minutes after unlock/unsuspension. Correlate by account, time of unlock event, and failed-attempt rate. Expected FPs: user retrying after lockout notice, scheduled automation.

suggestion.title: praisonai-platform: POST /workspaces/*/members with role escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes endpoint 'POST /workspaces/{workspace_id}/members' accepting user_id and role parameters with 'no caller-permission check.' Endpoint is gated only by member-level access, not admin check.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to /workspaces/*/members endpoints where role parameter is set to 'owner' or elevated roles, sourcing from non-admin accounts. Establish baseline of authorized privilege escalations; flag outliers as potential unauthorized injections.

suggestion.title: praisonai-platform: Rapid account-owner grant + login from granted identity
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack chain where member grants owner role to external/attacker-controlled account, then attacker logs in. Phrase: 'identity-swap chain — owner grant followed by login from the granted account' in recommended hunts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate POST /workspaces/*/members with role=owner (grant time) to subsequent login event (new user, same source IP or workspace, within 1 hour). Flag if grantor and new user are different identities and new user had no prior workspace activity.

suggestion.title: praisonai-platform: Cross-tenant member injection detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'cross-tenant member injection' as threat type. Vulnerability allows 'any workspace member' to add 'arbitrary user as owner,' implying potential for members to inject users from other workspaces or external parties.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST /workspaces/*/members where added user_id belongs to different organizational domain, external email, or has no prior activity in target workspace. Flag rapid multi-workspace injection patterns from single source.

suggestion.title: praisonai-platform: MemberService.add() invocation without authorization context
suggestion.rationale: Root cause explicitly stated: 'MemberService.add(workspace_id, user_id, role) [...] has no caller-permission check.' Detection should surface calls to this service or equivalent member-modification functions from low-privilege callers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Instrument application-layer logs or APM telemetry to detect calls to member-management service functions (MemberService.add, role-assignment APIs) where calling user role is member or lower. Alert if caller role does not match required authorization level for the operation.

suggestion.title: praisonai-platform: Baseline deviation — new workspace owners without admin action
suggestion.rationale: Privilege escalation via role injection means new owners appear without corresponding admin grant audit logs. Article describes unauthorized elevation: 'Any workspace member can add arbitrary user as owner.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of authorized workspace-owner additions (e.g., via admin UI, provisioning system). Flag new owner assignments that lack corresponding admin-initiated grant event, or where grantor is non-admin member.

suggestion.title: Vitest saveTestFile API endpoint called with file-write payload (CVE-2026-47429 exploitation)
suggestion.rationale: Article implies saveTestFile and rerun endpoints are exploitation vectors for code execution. Pipeline hunts miss detection of actual malicious API calls to these endpoints. Article states 'arbitrary file can be read and executed' via these mechanisms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST/GET requests to /saveTestFile or /rerun vitest endpoints with file paths or command payloads in query/body. Correlate to non-dev source IPs or suspicious parameter encoding.

suggestion.title: Vitest Windows-only LFI via path traversal on Windows volume prefix (CVE-2026-47429)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Arbitrary file can be read on Windows when Vitest UI server is listening.' Suggests Windows-specific path normalization bypass (e.g., UNC paths, volume prefixes like C: or \\?\). Current UC_20_3 misses Windows-specific traversal patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor __vitest_attachment__ requests with Windows path prefixes (UNC paths \\\\, drive letters C:, volume queries \\\?\) in URL-decoded parameters. Flag even on patched versions as potential probing.

suggestion.title: Direct file access to project files via Vitest filesystem endpoints (CVE-2026-47429)
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'arbitrary file can be read'—pipeline should detect direct filesystem enumeration via vitest endpoints. Article body reference: 'Arbitrary file can be read on Windows when Vitest UI server is listening.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor repeated requests to vitest endpoints (/__vitest__, /__vitest_attachment__) with sequential or wildcard file paths, indicative of enumeration. Look for 200/201 responses indicating successful reads.

suggestion.title: Privilege escalation via Vitest execution context (CVE-2026-47429)
suggestion.rationale: Article's impact section does not explicitly detail privilege escalation, but code execution via vitest process (running as user) could escalate if vitest runs elevated. Pipeline missing detection for elevated vitest contexts or SYSTEM execution of payload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor vitest process (node.exe with vitest args) for elevated/SYSTEM privilege execution. Flag execution of administrative tools (psexec, sc.exe, net localgroup) as child processes of vitest.

suggestion.title: Vitest UI server startup on Windows without authentication (CVE-2026-47429 precondition)
suggestion.rationale: Article implies vitest UI lacks or skips authentication when exposed to network. Pipeline should detect vitest startup without --auth flag or similar security controls. Not currently covered by any UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor node.exe process with vitest arguments for absence of authentication-related flags (--auth, --password, --token) combined with presence of --api.host or --host on non-loopback. Flag as unauthenticated exposure.

suggestion.title: Vitest process environment variables leaking sensitive configuration (CVE-2026-47429 post-exploitation)
suggestion.rationale: After exploitation, attacker may dump vitest process memory or environment variables for project secrets. Pipeline missing post-exploitation persistence/collection UC. Not explicitly in article but implied by 'arbitrary file read'—may include .env files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor child processes spawned by vitest (cmd.exe, powershell.exe) executing 'set' or 'env' commands, or process dump tools (procdump, dumpDump.exe) targeting node.exe. Correlate to network requests to vitest server shortly before.

suggestion.title: PowerShell Execution from ClickFix Social Engineering
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'ClickFix attacks involve PowerShell commands' and describes tactic as 'deceives victims into copying and executing malicious commands on their systems.' Represents primary attack vector but no UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on PowerShell execution from user-interactive sessions (explorer.exe, browsers) with encoded/obfuscated commands or inline script blocks. Monitor for command patterns consistent with clipboard-pasted content from social engineering lures.

suggestion.title: Fake Browser Update Download and Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article details 'FakeUpdates lures contain bogus update notices for Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari...' with example of 'fake Firefox update that downloaded a ZIP archive containing multiple DLLs and a malicious executable named Browser Update.exe.' No detection UC generated for this technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for ZIP/executable downloads from non-official update domains. Alert on files named 'Browser Update.exe' or similar masquerade patterns. Cross-reference download sources against official CDNs for each browser vendor.

suggestion.title: Malicious JavaScript Injection Delivery Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'JavaScript injection following the t.js?site=<id> pattern' as primary infrastructure signature and notes 'eight technical fingerprints linked to the campaign.' No UC was generated for injection pattern detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests matching 't.js?site=*' pattern to malicious domains. Monitor for obfuscated JavaScript payloads from identified injection infrastructure. Alert on requests originating from legitimate high-reputation websites.

suggestion.title: Traffic Distribution System Redirection Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states DriveSurge 'hijacks thousands of legitimate, high-reputation websites and silently redirects visitors' through zTDS 'which profiles them and determines whether a FakeUpdates or a ClickFix lure is more appropriate.' No redirection chain detection UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify HTTP 302/301 redirects from legitimate domains to unknown/malicious destinations. Correlate redirect chains showing TDS profiling behavior (same source → multiple different destinations). Alert on temporal clustering of redirects from single compromised site.

suggestion.title: Cross-Platform ClickFix with Clipboard Hijacking
suggestion.rationale: Article notes campaign 'extends beyond Windows' with 'obfuscated JavaScript payload specifically designed to target macOS desktop systems, delivered via verification-themed ClickFix attacks that hijack the clipboard.' No macOS-specific detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor macOS clipboard access from JavaScript contexts. Alert on verification-themed popups accessing system clipboard. Detect unexpected clipboard modifications correlated with ClickFix lure delivery.

suggestion.title: DriveSurge Campaign Infrastructure Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'more than 80 malicious injection domains and a set of pre-weaponized domains that had not yet been used in attacks' as DriveSurge infrastructure. No infrastructure correlation or threat-actor-level tracking UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS/HTTP activity to identified DriveSurge malicious injection domains. Track pre-weaponized domains for activation. Correlate multiple injection domain queries from single source to identify TDS infrastructure interaction patterns.

suggestion.title: Crafted HTTP Requests to WebSphere RCE Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'attackers to execute arbitrary code through specially crafted HTTP requests.' Pipeline generated zero hunts for exploitation attempt detection. Should detect requests with payload signatures, abnormal content-length, or known exploit patterns targeting vulnerable WebSphere versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to WebSphere server endpoints (plugin or admin ports) for payloads containing serialized objects, bypass sequences, or request patterns associated with CVE-2026-8633/8620 exploitation. Flag high POST/PUT frequency to vulnerable paths.

suggestion.title: Unusual Process Execution from WebSphere Service
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Remote Code Execution' but pipeline missed execution-phase detection. Any code executed via RCE would spawn child processes from WebSphere/httpd parent. Expected: cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, or reverse-shell indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child process creation from WebSphere Application Server processes (java.exe, wsadmin.sh) or httpd, especially non-standard CLI tools (cmd, powershell, perl, python, nc). Baseline expected child processes per environment.

suggestion.title: WebSphere Web Server Plug-ins Component Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'optional Web Server Plug-ins component' as attack surface. Pipeline missed file integrity monitoring and configuration change detection for this component.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file modifications to WebSphere plugins directory (typically /plugin/ or /config/), binary changes to httpd modules, or plugin configuration XML rewrites. Alert on unexpected deployment of .so or .dll files in plugin paths.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-8633/8620 Vulnerable Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article header lists two CVEs but pipeline output shows empty IOCs. Standard vulnerability-matching hunt against patch inventory should be auto-generated for every CVE briefing. Required for triage and prioritization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify systems running WebSphere Application Server versions matching CVE-2026-8633/8620 vulnerable range. Correlate with Web Server Plug-ins component enabled status from configuration baselines.

suggestion.title: Network Exposure: Direct Access to Vulnerable WebSphere Ports
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes risk to 'enterprise deployments.' Baseline network exposure of WebSphere admin ports (default 9060, 9061) and plugin communication ports to internet/untrusted segments. Article implies direct HTTP/HTTPS access vectors not detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag inbound network connections to WebSphere default ports from external IP ranges. Correlate with absence of expected reverse-proxy or load-balancer ingress patterns. High-confidence indicator when source is non-whitelisted asset.

suggestion.title: npm Supply Chain Compromise via Malicious Package Install
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'compromises Red Hat npm packages' — this is the initial infection vector and should trigger detection of unexpected package installations from registry or suspicious package metadata changes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install commands targeting suspicious or recently-modified packages; correlate with package.json modifications or unexpected registry cache hits. Flag installations that download from non-standard registries or with tampered SSL/GPG signatures.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting via In-Process Worm Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'credential-stealing worm' — should detect process injection, keylogging, or credential-manager access by npm-related processes or child processes spawned during package initialization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag npm or node processes that access HKLM/HKCU credential vaults, open credential-manager APIs, or hook keyboard/clipboard. Look for child processes of npm install with high entropy names or known malware patterns.

suggestion.title: Worm Self-Propagation and Lateral Movement via Supply Chain
suggestion.rationale: 'Worm' designation implies automated replication and propagation — article likely describes infection of downstream systems or re-publication to registry. Detect mass distribution of malicious packages or reinfection of build systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for npm publish events or registry-push API calls from compromised machines; detect high-volume npm installations across multiple hosts in short timeframe; flag machines installing the same package variant from internal/secondary registries.

suggestion.title: C2 Beacon and Data Exfiltration from Compromised npm Processes
suggestion.rationale: Credential-stealing worm must exfiltrate stolen data — article should describe outbound communication to attacker-controlled C2. Detect HTTP/HTTPS or DNS tunneling from npm/node processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound HTTPS connections from npm/node processes to non-whitelisted domains; monitor for high-entropy DNS queries; detect exfiltration of credential-store files or environment variables over HTTP POST/PUT.

suggestion.title: Script Execution via package.json Lifecycle Hooks
suggestion.rationale: npm allows arbitrary scripts in preinstall/postinstall/postsetup hooks — worm likely abuses these to execute malicious payloads silently during 'npm install'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm lifecycle hook execution; flag bash/powershell/cmd spawned as children of npm with suspicious arguments (curl, wget, base64, encoded payloads); correlate with .npmrc modifications or package.json script changes.

suggestion.title: Persistence via npm Global Modules or .bashrc/.profile Injection
suggestion.rationale: Worm must establish persistent access across rebuilds — likely modifies shell initialization files or installs global npm modules with autostart hooks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor modifications to ~/.bashrc, ~/.profile, /etc/profile.d/, or ~/.npm directories; flag creation of npm global modules that execute on shell init; correlate with npm install events.

suggestion.title: npm Package Installation Triggers Preinstall Script Execution
suggestion.rationale: The article explicitly states: 'npm runs preinstall scripts automatically during npm install, before any of your own code executes, so simply resolving the dependency is enough to trigger the payload.' This is the attack's execution vector and a clear detection opportunity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for npm install commands that trigger node.exe/node child processes running index.js or similarly large, suspicious JavaScript files from node_modules preinstall hooks. Alert on preinstall script execution, especially from packages in untrusted or newly-added namespaces, or when index.js exhibits high entropy/obfuscation patterns.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Environment and Credential File Access from npm Context
suggestion.rationale: The payload 'harvests secrets and credentials from the local environment and CI context: environment variables, ~/.npmrc tokens, SSH keys, GitHub tokens, and CI/CD secrets.' This is explicit credential access behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect node.exe processes spawned from npm contexts accessing ~/.npmrc, ~/.ssh directories, or reading environment variables en masse. Alert on patterns like child processes enumerating GitHub token files, CI credential files, or SSH key reads immediately following preinstall script execution.

suggestion.title: Cloud Identity and Access Enumeration from Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: The article notes: 'The notable change in this variant is a pair of new collectors for GCP and Azure that enumerate every identity the infected host can assume.' This is discovery and privilege escalation activity tied to a single infection vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when gcloud, az CLI, or AWS CLI commands are executed as child processes of npm install or node.exe running preinstall scripts. Look for identity enumeration patterns (get-iam-policy, list-service-accounts, az ad sp list, get-role-assignment) correlated with npm operations.

suggestion.title: Package Republishing or New Package Publication from Compromised Context
suggestion.rationale: The payload 'self-propagates. It queries the registry for other packages the compromised identity can publish and republishes them, carrying the same payload.' This describes worm-like lateral movement through npm.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for npm publish commands or HTTP PUT/POST to registry endpoints (npm.pkg.github.com, registry.npmjs.org) originating from contexts where npm preinstall scripts recently executed. Correlate with credential access or OIDC token acquisition. Flag republish of existing packages, especially within hours of first compromise signal.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions OIDC Token Requests in Suspicious Workflows
suggestion.rationale: The root cause details: 'Added a minimal GitHub Actions workflow that...Requested a GitHub OIDC identity token via id-token: write.' This is the mechanism that granted the attack publishing permissions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on GitHub Actions workflows requesting OIDC identity tokens (id-token: write) that are triggered by push events or that execute obfuscated/base64-encoded payloads. Investigate workflows added in orphan commits or without code review, especially in RedHatInsights or RedHat-owned repositories.

suggestion.title: Hunting: Repositories with 'Miasma: The Spreading Blight' Description
suggestion.rationale: The article states: 'Newly created attacker repositories carry the description Miasma: The Spreading Blight, which is a useful hunting signal.' This is an explicit IOC for compromise discovery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt GitHub organization repositories for creation events where the repository description contains 'Miasma: The Spreading Blight' or similar Greek-mythology-themed names. Cross-reference creation timestamp and committer identity with period of account compromise. Inspect commit history and Actions workflows for obfuscated payloads.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Installation with Embedded API Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly mentions 'codexui-android npm Supply Chain Attack' and 'Authentication Tokens Stolen'; supply-chain NPM attacks typically inject credential-harvesting code. Pipeline missed this obvious kill-chain entry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for installation of 'codexui-android' and other suspicious NPM packages; alert on packages requesting OpenAI SDK dependencies or containing obfuscated JavaScript that attempts to read environment variables or application secrets during install phase.

suggestion.title: OpenAI API Token Exfiltration and Misuse
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'OpenAI Codex Authentication Tokens Stolen'; once exfiltrated, tokens will be used by attacker. Pipeline should detect anomalous OpenAI API call patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline OpenAI API token usage per service/environment; alert on API calls from new geolocations, unusual rate patterns, new model endpoints, or bulk data retrieval requests (embeddings, completions) that deviate from application baseline.

suggestion.title: Modified npm Package Manifest or Checksum Mismatch
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks involve malicious modification of package files. Article context mentions 'stolen' tokens as payload; detection should catch when installed package hash diverges from public registry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On NPM install, validate package tarball checksums against npm registry; alert if integrity.sha512 or package-lock.json hash mismatches. Flag any 'codexui-android' versions with suspicious metadata (recent creation, rapid version bumps, author changes).

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Access to OpenAI Organization/API Keys Storage
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'Authentication Tokens Stolen'; implies attacker gained access to credential storage (environment, .env files, config, or secrets manager). Pipeline should detect unusual access to secrets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on reads of files containing 'OPENAI', 'API_KEY', 'TOKEN' in name from non-approved processes; monitor for bulk extraction of .env files or secrets manager queries by newly-installed NPM packages or their dependencies.

suggestion.title: Android APK Injection or Malicious DEX Payload Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Attack targets 'codexui-android' package; implies Android app supply chain. Pipeline should detect if APK is modified to include token-stealing code or permissions escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On Android app installation, verify APK signature and check manifest for suspicious permissions (INTERNET, READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE); hash DEX files and alert on new or unsigned code; monitor for unexpected network callbacks to non-OpenAI domains.

suggestion.title: Malicious npm Package Dependency Chain Execution
suggestion.rationale: NPM postinstall / prepare scripts are common supply-chain attack vector. Article implies payload was delivered via package; detection should catch script execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit all npm lifecycle scripts (postinstall, prepare, preuninstall) in codexui-android and dependencies; alert on execution of shell commands that access env vars, read files outside node_modules, or make HTTP requests during install.

suggestion.title: Android Framework exploitation — process exception spike post-CVE-2025-48595
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'vulnerability resides in the Android Framework component.' Crashes, ANR events, or framework exceptions are typical exploitation side effects before payload execution. No execution-phase detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Spike in Android Framework ANR, segfaults, or system_server crashes correlated with timeframe of exploitation attempts. Monitor for exception patterns in android.app.* and com.android.internal.* namespaces preceding privilege escalation.

suggestion.title: Post-exploitation privilege escalation — capability/selinux policy violations
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'near-complete device control' logically requires escalation from exploit context to root/system UID. No T1548 techniques mapped despite this being essential to the attack chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: SELinux denials, capability-drop violations, or uid/gid transitions in processes spawned by vulnerable framework components. Flag setuid/setgid syscalls executed by non-standard callers targeting system binaries.

suggestion.title: Post-exploitation persistence — system partition integrity violations
suggestion.rationale: Complete device control implies persistence mechanisms. Article describes no post-exploitation phase, but HIGH Android 0-days in the wild typically establish rootkits or system-level persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Unexpected writes to /system, /system_ext, /boot, or other boot-critical partitions following privilege escalation. Monitor for attempts to re-mount system partitions read-write or insert modules into early-boot init sequences.

suggestion.title: Network-based CVE-2025-48595 delivery — exploit traffic signature
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'targeted attacks' and 'without user interaction' suggests network-delivered or supply-chain payload. No network-layer IOC hunt or traffic signature was generated despite unknown delivery mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Network traffic patterns anomalous for device's user profile: non-Play Store APK downloads, SSL/TLS certificate pinning bypasses, or connections to suspected malware distribution infrastructure preceding device compromise or framework crashes.

suggestion.title: Patch status correlation — CVE-2025-48595 exploitation against unpatched cohort
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'June 2026 Android Security Bulletin' patches this CVE. Template-based hunt covers asset exposure but does not correlate exploitation attempts with June 2026 patch baseline to validate targeted attack vectors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference any detected CVE-2025-48595 exploitation attempts with asset inventory to confirm targets are on pre-June-2026 patch baseline. Alert on exploitation attempts targeting devices that should have been patched.

suggestion.title: Post-exploitation collection — sensitive file access post-takeover
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'near-complete device control.' Once compromise is established, attacker typically exfiltrates credentials, messages, or private data. No collection-phase detection was mapped.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Unusual access to /data/data/* (app private storage), /data/misc/keystore, or contacts/messages databases by newly elevated processes. Monitor for bulk reads of sensitive file types following privilege escalation or framework restarts.

suggestion.title: Brute-Force Attempts Against Password Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'brute-force attack' on Dashlane. Pipeline should have generated detection logic for credential enumeration/spraying attacks against authentication endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for multiple failed authentication attempts originating from distinct IP addresses targeting a single account, or multiple accounts from a single IP within a short window. Threshold: >5 failed logins to password manager service per account in 10 minutes, or >20 failed attempts across accounts from same source IP in 15 minutes.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Encrypted Vault Download Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'encrypted vaults of fewer than 20 users downloaded.' Pipeline should detect bulk data exfiltration characteristic of vault theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on downloads of encrypted vault files (typically .bcrypt, .encrypted, or archive formats containing vault metadata) following account compromise. Correlate with failed authentication spikes within 12 hours prior. Flag downloads to non-standard geographies or hours.

suggestion.title: Post-Breach Credential Validation Testing
suggestion.rationale: Brute-force attack implies attacker validated credentials against live services. Pipeline missed detection of credential abuse post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for successful logins to compromised accounts immediately following failed authentication storms, particularly when source IPs differ or user agent changes. Correlate successful login geo with historical baseline.

suggestion.title: Password Manager Service Compromise Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article discloses specific password manager (Dashlane) compromise. Pipeline should flag any authentication patterns unique to password manager attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify suspicious login patterns to Dashlane API endpoints or web portal: rapid-fire requests, requests from datacenter IPs, requests with modified/stripped user-agent headers, or requests without standard browser fingerprints.

suggestion.title: 2FA Bypass via Support Chatbot Social Engineering
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'simply asking the bot to hand over access' — core attack vector is chatbot exploitation for credential disclosure. Pipeline ignored this explicit bypass mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor chatbot logs for credential-related requests (password reset, account access, 2FA bypass keywords). Flag sessions with high reset request rates or rapid session cycling. Correlate downstream password resets and account access from anomalous locations within 10 minutes of bot interaction.

suggestion.title: Bulk High-Value Account Compromise Clustering
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'OG Instagram handles, dormant institutional accounts, and verified profiles were stolen in minutes' — rapid takeover of premium account types is anomalous clustering behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on 3+ account compromises in <10 minutes targeting verified, institutional, or aged accounts. Correlate with new-device or geolocation anomalies. Establish baseline: typical takeover incidents cluster <1 per hour.

suggestion.title: Dormant Account Reactivation with Anomalous Access
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically targets 'dormant institutional accounts' — reactivation of inactive accounts is a distinct IOC not addressed by generic takeover detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor first login to accounts inactive >90 days. Alert if followed by mass messaging, follower changes, or post activity. Cross-reference with device/geolocation mismatches against last known user activity.

suggestion.title: Credential Resale Marketplace Activity Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'stolen usernames listed for resale on [...]' — implies darkweb/forum activity. No marketplace monitoring or exfiltration use case captured this phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate internal account takeovers with threat intelligence feeds monitoring credential resale forums and darkweb marketplaces. Alert when stolen Instagram handles surface for sale within 24 hours of takeover. Extract marketplace URLs and seller identities.

suggestion.title: Support Bot Exploitation Pattern Chain
suggestion.rationale: Attack explicitly uses trusted support infrastructure (T1199) as vector. No detection hypothesis for chatbot-mediated credential resets or bot conversation anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect high-volume chatbot sessions requesting password resets or account access from same IP/session ID. Flag requests containing account enumeration, credential verification, or 2FA bypass language. Correlate bot interaction timestamps with downstream successful account access from unexpected locations.

suggestion.title: Outbound connections to recruitment-themed C2 domains
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists 7 domains used as fake recruitment portals: 'ebix.recruitment-flow.com', 'boeing-careers.com', 'rheinmetallcareer.org', 'airbus.global-careers.com', 'flydubaicareers.ae.org', 'telespazio-careers.com', 'arabiccountriestalent.com'. These are C2 infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any outbound DNS or HTTP/HTTPS traffic to the seven identified domains. Filter for aerospace/defense sector endpoints (from article context). High fidelity given specificity of domain names and known malicious registration patterns.

suggestion.title: Malware execution on file hash match (13 custom payloads)
suggestion.rationale: Article provides 13 SHA256 hashes of 'custom malware' delivered via portal. Direct hash-match is definitive IOC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Match all 13 SHA256 values against process creation, file write, and execution logs. Any hit indicates malware execution on endpoint. Expected zero false positives; escalate immediately.

suggestion.title: Spearphishing emails targeting aerospace/defense with recruitment lures
suggestion.rationale: Article narrative: 'fake recruitment operation to push custom malware onto unsuspecting victims' targeting 'professionals in the aerospace and defense sectors.' Initial access is social engineering via job portals.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for emails with recruitment/career/job keywords (recruiter, hiring, career, position, apply) sent to aerospace/defense industry users. Look for URLs matching the 7 malicious domains or typosquatted variants. Check for embedded .exe/.msi/.zip attachments.

suggestion.title: Domain lookalike registration mimicking Boeing/Airbus/Rheinmetall
suggestion.rationale: Domains like 'boeing-careers.com' (not boeing.com), 'airbus.global-careers.com' (not airbus.com), 'rheinmetallcareer.org' (not rheinmetall.com) are clearly brand-impersonation registered to deceive victims.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor domain registrations for new entries containing aerospace company names + recruitment keywords. Flag registrations within 72h of phishing campaign sightings. Cross-check registrar reputation and hosting IP geolocation (expected to differ from legitimate company infrastructure).

suggestion.title: Obfuscated malware variant signature (T1027 coverage)
suggestion.rationale: Article cites T1027 (Obfuscated Files or Information) as observed technique. The 13 custom malware samples likely employ code obfuscation to evade static detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Layer behavioral detection on top of static hash matching: monitor for PE injection, API unhooking, unpacking patterns, and entropy spikes indicative of obfuscated code. Use YARA rules tuned to custom malware characteristics if available from threat intel.

suggestion.title: Process Injection Detection (T1055)
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'PHANTOMPULSE RAT Uses Process Injection and UAC Bypass to Compromise Windows Systems'. Core attack technique, zero detection use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for cross-process memory operations: CreateRemoteThread, WriteProcessMemory, NtMapViewOfSection to unsigned targets. Flag legitimate processes (svchost, explorer, lsass) performing remote code injection. Correlate suspicious parent-child process chains with unsigned code execution in hollowed or legitimate process contexts.

suggestion.title: UAC Bypass Exploitation (T1548.002)
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'PHANTOMPULSE RAT Uses Process Injection and UAC Bypass to Compromise Windows Systems'. Explicit privilege escalation vector mentioned; no detection use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect UAC bypass via registry modification (HKCU\Software\Classes\ms-settings\shell\open\command, AppPaths elevation keys), execution of bypass executables (fodhelper, eventvwr, compmgmt with ShellExecute), or token elevation from non-admin processes. Alert on SYSTEM-level child process spawning from medium-integrity parents.

suggestion.title: PHANTOMPULSE SHA256 File Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 2 file hash IOCs (70bbb38b70fd836d66e8166ec27be9aa8535b3876596fc80c45e3de4ce327980, 33dacf9f854f636216e5062ca252df8e5bed652efd78b86512f5b868b11ee70f) described as 'final-stage payload'. No hash-based detection use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation or file execution matching the two identified SHA256 hashes. Monitor for process tree anomalies following execution (unusual parent processes, hidden spawning, living-off-the-land binary abuse). Correlate with network IOCs to confirm infection chain.

suggestion.title: Command & Control to PHANTOMPULSE Domains/IPs
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 4 C2 indicators (195.3.222.251, panel.fefea22134.net, 0x666.info, thoroughly-publisher-troy-clara.trycloudflare.com). Recommended hunt in article itself, but no use case generated by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish and alert on sustained or periodic outbound connections to identified C2 infrastructure. Prioritize encrypted channels, non-standard ports, and off-hours beaconing. Monitor for connection retry patterns indicating resilience; correlate with file hash execution for confirmation of compromise.

suggestion.title: C2 Beaconing from Czech/Taiwan Targets
suggestion.rationale: Article implies established campaign infrastructure ('ramp up') requiring C2 communications, but pipeline extracted zero network IOCs or C2 techniques.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from Czech Republic and Taiwan networks to newly registered domains with Asian registrants or suspicious certificates. Alert on DNS queries to domains not in organization whitelist from government/critical infrastructure networks.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Credential Dumping
suggestion.rationale: Multi-nation attack campaign (Czech + Taiwan) requires post-compromise lateral movement, but pipeline detected no credential-access or lateral-movement techniques.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on LSASS memory access via Process Hollowing or direct API calls, suspicious PtH authentication patterns across regional subnets, or elevated logon activity from compromised workstations.

suggestion.title: Initial Access via Spear-Phishing to Regional Organizations
suggestion.rationale: No initial-access techniques identified. Czech Republic and Taiwan organizations mentioned in title implies email or web-based compromise vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for phishing emails targeting Czech and Taiwanese government/energy sector addresses with executable attachments or malicious URLs. Alert on web application exploit attempts against regional critical infrastructure.
