Correlate timing with user logins and file access patterns.

suggestion.title: Detect SideCopy Attribution Markers and Malware Signatures
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline output contains no mention of threat actor 'SideCopy' or Pakistan attribution despite article title explicitly surfacing it; missing IOC corroboration with known SideCopy samples.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference Xeno RAT sample hashes, encoding strings, and C2 domains against VirusTotal, abuse.ch, and internal SideCopy intelligence. Monitor for living-off-the-land (LOLBin) patterns: legitimate tools (certutil, msiexec, regsvcs) with suspicious arguments. Detect base64-encoded payloads and renamed executables matching past SideCopy artifacts.

suggestion.title: Process Injection Activity (T1055)
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Uses Process Injection...'. Pipeline generated zero hunts for this explicitly-named core technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for cross-process memory operations: CreateRemoteThread, WriteProcessMemory, VirtualAllocEx from suspicious parents into system processes. Flag unsigned executables or known-bad hashes injecting into critical services.

suggestion.title: UAC Bypass Attempt (T1548.002)
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'UAC Bypass to Compromise Windows...'. Pipeline captured zero privilege-escalation detections despite explicit technique in narrative.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on registry modifications to HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System, execution of fodhelper.exe/eventvwr.exe/services.msc from non-standard parents, or elevation via Comp-Mgmt DLL execution.

suggestion.title: C2 Callback to Known Malicious Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 3 C2 domains + 1 IP with explicit C2-phase recommendation ('Network connections to article IPs / domains'). Pipeline output IOCs field empty ({}); zero network hunts generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag DNS queries to or network connections to: panel.fefea22134.net, 0x666.info, thoroughly-publisher-troy-clara.trycloudflare.com, 195.3.222.251. Monitor for sustained beaconing or post-compromise callback patterns.

suggestion.title: Malware File Hash Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article provides 2 SHA256 hashes with explicit 'install phase' hunt recommendation. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs; no file-matching detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution or file creation with hash 70bbb38b70fd836d66e8166ec27be9aa8535b3876596fc80c45e3de4ce327980 or 33dacf9f854f636216e5062ca252df8e5bed652efd78b86512f5b868b11ee70f. Cross-correlate with user temp directories, script hosts.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Code Obfuscation & Deobfuscation
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'advanced approach' and obfuscation patterns (T1027). Pipeline captured T1027 in techniques but generated zero defense-evasion hunts from the finding.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for high-entropy memory regions, packed executables, or encrypted payload detonation. Flag script interpreters (PowerShell, cmd, rundll32) spawning from packed binaries or unusual parents.

suggestion.title: Remote Access Trojan Persistence Registry Modifications
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies PHANTOMPULSE as 'remote access trojan', implying persistence establishment. RATs typically modify Run keys, services, or scheduled tasks. Pipeline detected no persistence-phase techniques.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HKCU/HKLM Run key modifications from unsigned processes, service creation (WMI, sc.exe) with obfuscated names, or scheduled task creation in system namespaces by user-context processes.

suggestion.title: Unencrypted/Weak Wi-Fi Detection in World Cup Critical Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'evaluation of Wi-Fi hotspot security configurations and potential exposure risks'—implies specific insecure configurations were identified; hunt should detect deployment of WEP/WPA without strong encryption in identified cities.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Wi-Fi networks in Mexico City, Monterrey, Guadalajara with weak encryption (WEP, WPA without AES), broadcast SSIDs, or outdated firmware. Correlate against critical infrastructure locations (venue networks, government facilities, transportation hubs) to identify high-risk overlaps.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Wi-Fi Scanning Activity Near Event Venues
suggestion.rationale: Kaspersky explicitly conducted wardriving assessment to map regional security posture; hunters should detect similar reconnaissance patterns (passive probe requests, SSID enumeration) originating from non-authorized sources near identified vulnerable zones.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for rapid Wi-Fi SSID enumeration, high-volume probe requests from single MAC across multiple BSSID, or sustained scanning activity within 500m of World Cup venues. Establish baseline of authorized wardriving/security assessment traffic; flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Dragon Weave Initial Access via Phishing or Supply Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'Dragon Weave Hits Czech Republic & Taiwan' with no body content available to determine specific attack vector. Standard detection baseline for any named Chinese APT campaign should include phishing/social-engineering and C2 callbacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for email traffic to Czech Republic / Taiwan organizations with malicious attachment types or credential-harvesting payloads. Flag anomalous external domain registration overlapping with known Dragon Weave infrastructure patterns. Detect download + execution chains from suspicious web servers.

suggestion.title: Dragon Weave Command & Control Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: No specific C2 domains or IP ranges in article body, but any APT campaign requires C2 for post-exploitation. Should detect callbacks to known or suspected Dragon Weave C2 infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify outbound connections from Czech/Taiwan networks to Dragon Weave-attributed domains or ASNs. Correlate DNS queries to malicious domains with successful connection attempts. Flag TLS certificates signed by known malicious CAs used by Dragon Weave operations.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Execution Consistent with APT Tooling
suggestion.rationale: Article implies active intrusion activity but provides no technical details. Standard APT detection: Chinese state-sponsored groups often use LOLBins, encoded payloads, or living-off-the-land techniques.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on encoded/obfuscated PowerShell, cmd.exe launched by Office processes, or WMI execution without service request context. Baseline for APT-grade intrusions: process hollowing, DLL injection, or unsigned executable execution from temp directories.

suggestion.title: CVE-2024-21182 Vulnerability Scanner Alert
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies CVE-2024-21182 as the IOC; scanner hits are the baseline detection. Article: 'CVE-2024-21182 — match against your vulnerability scanner.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag any host identified by vulnerability scanner as vulnerable to CVE-2024-21182 within 24 hours of reporting. Cross-correlate with network exposure scans to identify public-facing unpatched instances.

suggestion.title: T3/IIOP Protocol Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack vector: 'unauthenticated attacker with network access via T3, IIOP.' Protocols are concrete indicators; should trigger network-level rules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unauthenticated connection attempts to Oracle WebLogic T3 (port 7002) or IIOP (port 7001) from untrusted networks. Correlate with failed authentication patterns or connection resets suggesting exploitation probes.

suggestion.title: WebLogic Service Exposure & Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes patch lag and public-facing exposure: 'worth one quick check across your fleet.' Detection should identify exposed instances before exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify publicly routable hosts responding on WebLogic ports (7001, 7002). Cross-reference against vulnerability scanner for CVE-2024-21182 status. Flag gap between discovery and patching.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Data Access via WebLogic Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article threat: 'complete access to all Oracle WebLogic Server accessible data.' Impact detection should capture post-breach data flows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WebLogic server logs for unusual authentication bypass, elevated-privilege queries, or bulk data exports from successful connections to vulnerable instances. Baseline normal access patterns.

suggestion.title: Federal Patch Due-Date SLA Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Federal patch due: 2026-06-04.' Alerts should close-of-business enforce compliance by deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: By 2026-06-04, ensure zero unpatched CVE-2024-21182 instances in fleet. Alert on any vulnerable host still present after due date. Escalate to Ops/compliance if deviation.

suggestion.title: Container Registry Poisoning Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'TeamPCP compromised Checkmarx KICS across multiple attack chains...poisoning a Docker Hub repository to later steal Kubernetes secrets.' Pipeline missed supply-chain detection entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor container image registries for unauthorized image uploads, unexpected layer additions, or signature mismatches. Alert on pulls of newly-modified images from trusted repos within deployment pipelines, especially if image timestamps postdate known repo compromise windows.

suggestion.title: Privileged Container Capability Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists dangerous capabilities: 'CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_SYS_MODULE, CAP_SYS_PTRACE, CAP_NET_ADMIN' as container escape vectors. Zero detection mapped for privilege escalation via capability misuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on container creation with dangerous Linux capabilities, especially CAP_SYS_ADMIN or CAP_SYS_MODULE. Monitor for kernel module loading, mount operations, or ptrace syscalls from containerized processes holding these capabilities.

suggestion.title: Kubernetes Secrets Enumeration & Theft
suggestion.rationale: Article: stealer 'loaded during the KICS scanning process' to 'steal Kubernetes secrets and other sensitive data.' No detection for secrets API access, bulk read patterns, or exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Kubernetes API audit logs for rapid secret enumeration or bulk reads. Alert on container processes accessing /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/ or calling Kubernetes API to list/get secrets from unexpected service accounts.

suggestion.title: Orchestration API Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'Exploitation of orchestration APIs' and 'Exploiting misconfigurations...of containerization and orchestration APIs' as distinct attack vector. Pipeline produced zero detection use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthorized Docker daemon socket access or containerd API calls from containers. Alert on kubeconfig exfiltration, abnormal API token usage, or API calls from containers attempting resource creation/modification outside normal workload scope.

suggestion.title: Code Injection via IaC Scanning Pipeline
suggestion.rationale: Article: tainted images distributed a stealer 'loaded during the KICS scanning process.' Missing detection for malicious code execution during artifact scanning/analysis stages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor KICS and similar IaC scanning tool processes for unexpected child processes, file writes, or credential/secret access. Alert on scanning process spawning network connections or accessing Kubernetes configs outside normal analysis workflows.

suggestion.title: Container Escape Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 'Container escape followed by host compromise' and 'Exploiting vulnerabilities in the host system and container runtime components.' No detection mapped for kernel exploit or namespace escape activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect container processes issuing escape-related syscalls (futex, bpf, userns, cgroup operations). Alert on unexpected process tree relationships between container and host namespaces, or processes spawning from containers with PIDs visible to host context.

suggestion.title: WP Maps Pro Plugin RCE / Privilege Escalation Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'critical flaw actively exploited'—signals remote code execution or equivalent vulnerability (T1190). Pipeline extracted zero initial-access detection despite explicit exploitation claim.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to /wp-content/plugins/wp-maps-pro/ containing SQL keywords, base64 payloads, or polyglot markers. Correlate with subprocess spawning from httpd/www-data processes or PHP execution within 10 seconds of the request.

suggestion.title: WordPress Admin Account Creation via Database Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states exploitation 'to create admin accounts'—direct persistence mechanism requiring INSERT/UPDATE to wp_users table. Pipeline missed this critical post-exploitation detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on INSERT or UPDATE against wp_users table setting wp_user_roles to 'administrator' or 'a:1' serialized role array, especially from PHP/web-server process context. Require correlation check: no matching wp-admin panel login from legitimate admin sources in prior 60 seconds.

suggestion.title: Unauth HTTP POST to wp-admin/user-new.php or wp-json/wp/v2/users
suggestion.rationale: Admin account creation can occur via REST API or admin form. Phrase 'actively exploited to create admin accounts' presupposes exploitation path reaching account-creation endpoint—critical detection gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag successful (200/201) POST requests to /wp-admin/user-new.php or /wp-json/wp/v2/users from IPs with no prior successful wp-admin authentication. Monitor Content-Type and user_login parameter patterns for indicators of bypass (SQL injection, parameter tampering).

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Admin Panel Access
suggestion.rationale: Once attacker creates admin account, they access /wp-admin. Pipeline should detect authentication from IPs previously linked to exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP 200 logins to /wp-login.php with source IPs that generated HTTP 40x/50x errors or WAF blocks to /wp-content/plugins/wp-maps-pro/ within prior 300 seconds. Flag successful logins as high-priority post-exploitation indicator.

suggestion.title: WP Maps Pro Plugin File Modification or Execution
suggestion.rationale: Plugin exploitation may involve in-place file modification or direct code execution within plugin directory. No file-system or execution-layer detection generated despite 'critical' vulnerability severity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation/modification under /wp-content/plugins/wp-maps-pro/ with timestamps within 60 seconds of HTTP requests to that path. Monitor for PHP or webshell process spawning from within the plugin directory.

suggestion.title: Multiple Failed Login Attempts from Single Source IP
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers attempted logins 'by trying multiple passwords in succession' and mentions 'threshold of failed attempts' triggering lockout. T1110.001 / T1110.004 baseline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect authentication service events where a single source IP or user agent triggers N+ failed login attempts against the same account within M minutes, followed by account lockout or suspension. Baseline by organization; Dashlane's systems flagged this automatically.

suggestion.title: Login Attempts from Geographically Distant Locations
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'attempted logins from distant locations' and 'unknown devices' as a red flag. Users received notices of 'suspicious access requests from foreign countries.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag login attempts where the geographic origin (IP geolocation) is inconsistent with the user's known baseline location or recent activity, especially when clustered in time with failed attempts or unusual device registrations.

suggestion.title: Device Registration Attempts from Anomalous Locations
suggestion.rationale: Article states emails contained 'verification codes for legitimate account owners to register new devices' as part of brute-force probe. Multiple device registration requests are a proxy for account compromise attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor device registration / enrollment requests (MFA device add, new device confirmation) where the source geography is unfamiliar, clustered with failed logins, or from known data-center IP ranges. Dashlane triggered lockout partly to prevent device registration post-compromise.

suggestion.title: Account Lockout Following Authentication Surge
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'account lockouts to block automated attacks after a threshold of failed attempts is reached' and accounts 'were locked out... resulting in the suspension of those accounts as part of Dashlane's built-in security controls.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect account lockout or suspension events preceded by authentication failure spikes. Correlate lockout timestamps with user-facing notification emails to confirm automated defensive response was triggered; absence of user-initiated password reset may indicate legitimate attack (not user lock-out).

suggestion.title: Verification Code Requests Without Corresponding User Action
suggestion.rationale: Article reports users 'received notices of suspicious access requests from foreign countries. The emails contained verification codes for legitimate account owners to register new devices' — users did NOT initiate these. Indicates detection of unauthorized device registration attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify verification code requests (MFA, device registration, email confirmation) where no corresponding user action precedes the request, or where the originating IP/location contradicts the user's session. High-signal indicator of account compromise attempt or credential-guessing attack.

suggestion.title: npm Package Malicious Version Installation (Supply Chain)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'codexui-android npm Supply Chain Attack'—package injection is the initial attack surface. No UC generated despite clear vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install/yarn add command execution with suspicious package names or versions not in approved registries. Correlate to unexpected package downloads or registry API calls from development machines. Alert on packages matching known typosquats or recently-registered names targeting popular utilities.

suggestion.title: OpenAI API Token Exfiltration via Process Monitoring
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'OpenAI Codex Authentication Tokens Stolen'—credential access and exfiltration are explicit attack outcomes. No detection logic provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process creation with environment variables or command-line arguments containing OpenAI API key patterns (sk-*). Monitor for HTTP POST/PUT requests from development environments to non-Azure, non-OpenAI domains containing Base64-encoded or plaintext token-like strings in request bodies or headers.

suggestion.title: npm Package Metadata Tampering Detection
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks often alter package.json, dist-tags, or version metadata to trigger automatic installations of malicious versions. Article context strongly suggests this but no UC created.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm registry audit logs for unusual metadata changes on packages matching target profiles (high-dependency packages, names similar to legitimate tools). Alert on version bumps that skip intermediate versions, ownership transfers, or re-publication of old versions with new code.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Registry Authentication and Publish Events
suggestion.rationale: Attacker must publish malicious package to npm registry. No IOC extraction of publishing account, IP, or timing anomalies despite being essential for supply-chain compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag npm publish operations from new or dormant accounts, unusual geographies, or non-standard CI/CD environments. Correlate account creation date, email domain, and publish history to detect compromised or newly-created attacker accounts. Alert on rapid package version releases (>3 versions in <24h).

suggestion.title: API Token Regex Matching and Outbound Data Transfer Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes token theft as outcome. Regex-based token detection paired with egress monitoring is fundamental gap—no suggestion provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Deploy regex signatures for OpenAI API keys (sk-[a-zA-Z0-9]{48}) across process arguments, environment variables, and HTTP request inspection. Correlate regex matches to outbound HTTPS connections to non-approved domains (esp. recently-registered or high-entropy hostnames) and flag within 10 seconds of process creation.

suggestion.title: npm Package Installation from Unexpected Source / Registry Substitution
suggestion.rationale: Attackers may host on alternative registries or use package-lock.json tampering. Title references 'npm Supply Chain'—registry origin validation is critical missing detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install/yarn operations for registry URLs differing from configured package-lock.json and .npmrc. Alert on installs from non-official registries, mirror domains, or IPs geographically inconsistent with legitimate npm CDN. Validate checksums against npm registry API.

suggestion.title: PAN-OS CVE-2026-0257 Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'enables attackers to bypass authentication mechanisms' and 'being actively leveraged in real-world attacks'—clear description of exploitation against public-facing firewall interfaces
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PAN-OS management interfaces (HTTPS/443) and API endpoints for exploitation signatures, unusual requests to CVE-2026-0257 vulnerable paths, and auth-bypass payloads.

suggestion.title: Inbound Connections from Known Threat IPs
suggestion.rationale: Article lists six IPv4 addresses under 'Indicators of Compromise' as part of active attacks; detection requires direct correlation with inbound network traffic
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on inbound connections from {104.207.144.154, 146.19.216.119, 146.19.216.120, 146.19.216.125, 209.99.191.137, 79.130.26.202} to any internal host or firewall interface.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable PAN-OS Inventory Against CVE-2026-0257
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'CISA has added...to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog'—asset inventory is the foundational hunt for triage and remediation prioritization
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset and vulnerability data for all PAN-OS instances running versions affected by CVE-2026-0257; prioritize internet-facing and management-network devices.

suggestion.title: CVE-2024-21182 T3/IIOP Protocol Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'can be exploited remotely by threat actors with no privileges in low-complexity attacks' via 'T3, IIOP' protocols, but pipeline extracted zero detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for inbound connections to WebLogic standard ports (7001, 7002) using T3 or IIOP protocol handshakes from untrusted networks. Alert on unauthenticated T3/IIOP sessions immediately followed by child process spawning or file system access beneath ORACLE_HOME.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Data Access on Compromised WebLogic Instance
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies successful exploitation results in 'unauthorized access to critical data or complete access to all Oracle WebLogic Server accessible data' but pipeline provided no exfiltration detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on WebLogic process performing bulk file reads from application directories or database JDBC queries returning large datasets immediately post-exploitation. Monitor outbound connections from WebLogic JVM to non-whitelisted destinations carrying serialized Java objects or plaintext credential material.

suggestion.title: WebLogic Version Inventory Against Shodan Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies exact affected versions: 'Shodan now tracks over 1,592 Oracle WebLogic servers exposed online' with '961 running version 12.2.1.4.0 and 631 running version 14.1.1.0.0'—asset-centric IOC requiring no extraction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference internal asset management database against public Shodan results for your organization's IP space. Flag any internet-facing WebLogic instances running versions 12.2.1.4.0 or 14.1.1.0.0 unpatched after June 4, 2026 CISA deadline.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-61884 SSRF in Oracle E-Business Suite
suggestion.rationale: Article cites secondary actively exploited vulnerability: 'unauthenticated server-side request forgery (SSRF) vulnerability (CVE-2025-61884) in Oracle E-Business Suite' with no detection guidance provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Oracle E-Business Suite HTTP handlers for malformed URL parameters containing localhost, internal IP ranges, or cloud metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254). Alert on unexpected outbound connections from E-Business Suite application context to internal systems.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-21992 RCE in Oracle Identity Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'critical unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability (CVE-2026-21992) in Identity Manager and Web Services Manager' released out-of-band; no RCE detection logic generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Oracle Identity Manager and Web Services Manager processes for unexpected child process spawning (bash, cmd.exe, powershell) or JAR execution. Alert on unauthenticated HTTP requests to web service endpoints immediately preceding abnormal process execution.

suggestion.title: Ransomware Campaign Targeting Oracle Vulnerabilities
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'CISA has flagged 43 vulnerabilities across various Oracle products as exploited in the wild, 12 of which have been abused in ransomware attacks'—indicating ransomware threat actor tooling targeting Oracle infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on encryption activity (bulk file modification, unusual file extension chaining, BitLocker/dm-crypt invocation) on systems hosting Oracle WebLogic, E-Business Suite, or Identity Manager post-exploitation. Monitor for mass file deletion or filesystem access patterns indicative of pre-encryption cleanup.

suggestion.title: Brute-Force Attack via Password Guessing
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Brute-Force Attack' as the attack method. Pipeline failed to surface credential-access detection despite this being the primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for rapid sequences of failed authentication attempts followed by successful login from a single source IP within a short time window. Dashlane incident involved brute-force; detection should trigger on >10 failed logins to same account in <5 min, especially if followed by vault/secret exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Abnormal Geographic Access to Credential Vault
suggestion.rationale: Encrypted vaults were downloaded after credential compromise. Article phrase: 'Encrypted Vaults of Fewer Than 20 Users Downloaded' indicates post-breach exfiltration requiring detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify vault access/download events from IP address geolocation inconsistent with user's historical pattern, especially within minutes of successful brute-force login. Flag bulk vault exports or unusual backup-download patterns post-authentication.

suggestion.title: Credential Stuffing Detection Against Password Manager
suggestion.rationale: Brute-force attacks on password managers typically use credential-stuffing (reused credentials from prior breaches). Pipeline should flag this attack pattern specifically.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for login attempts using known-compromised username/password pairs (from BREACH databases). Dashlane breach likely involved thousands of credential pairs; detection via auth logs + threat-intel feeds for known-bad pairs.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Encrypted Vault Access by Service Account
suggestion.rationale: Vaults were downloaded post-compromise. Need to detect if the exfiltration was automated via compromised service accounts or API keys rather than interactive user sessions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect non-interactive, high-volume vault/secret exports, or API token usage inconsistent with normal application behavior. Dashlane encrypted-vault downloads suggest large-scale automated exfiltration post-breach.

suggestion.title: Account Recovery / Password Reset After Brute-Force Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Users affected by brute-force attack would need to reset credentials. Detection should identify legitimate recovery patterns to differentiate from attacker cover-up attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After brute-force detection, correlate password-reset requests from compromised accounts. Legitimate users reset post-breach; attackers may attempt account-lockout circumvention or persistence via recovery codes.

suggestion.title: Vault Decryption or Credential Extract Post-Download
suggestion.rationale: Article states vaults were 'Encrypted' when downloaded, but pipeline missed detection of post-exfil decryption/parsing, which occurs during 'Collection' phase on attacker infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor attacker infrastructure (if identified) for cryptographic operations on Dashlane vault files, or DNS/traffic patterns consistent with credential-harvesting tools targeting password-manager exports. Off-network correlation needed.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via CVE-2025-48595 on Android 14+
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Local attackers can exploit...Android Framework vulnerability...to gain code execution and escalate privileges on devices running Android 14 or later.' Pipeline generated no detection for this active in-the-wild exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Android 14+ devices for suspicious process execution with privilege escalation or unexpected capability grants outside normal OS update contexts. Detect framework component abuse patterns preceding privilege escalation.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Android Devices Vulnerable to CVE-2025-48595
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies June 2026 patch levels (2026-06-01, 2026-06-05) as remediation but notes 'other vendors will often take longer.' Missing detection for devices not meeting patch baseline vulnerable to active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory Android 14+ devices by security patch level. Flag devices not running at least 2026-06-01 patches as vulnerable to active CVE-2025-48595 exploitation. Correlate against high-profile or high-interest target profiles.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Spyware Activity Following Android Framework Exploit
suggestion.rationale: Article notes similar framework flaws 'exploited in the past by commercial spyware and by nation-state operations targeting high-profile or high-interest individuals,' but pipeline generated no detection for post-compromise surveillance behaviors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-exploitation, flag anomalous access to device sensors (GPS, camera, microphone) and sensitive data enumeration (contacts, call logs, SMS) from unexpected processes or without user interaction. Correlate with vulnerable device populations and high-value targets.

suggestion.title: Critical Remote Code Execution via Android Framework Component
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'critical security vulnerability in the Framework component...remote escalation of privilege with no additional execution privileges needed. User interaction is not needed for exploitation.' Pipeline generated no RCE detection use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected privileged child processes spawned from Android Framework components (system_server, zygote). Flag framework-to-system process execution chains bypassing normal application sandbox and permission enforcement.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Compromise: Installation of TrapDoor Malicious Packages
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector: 'Hackers have planted 34 malicious packages across three major open-source ecosystems.' Pipeline completely missed the initial access / supply-chain compromise chain phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm/PyPI package registries for installation of known-malicious package names from TrapDoor campaign. Alert on new or recently-modified packages with suspicious maintainers, obfuscated code, or unusual dependencies. Correlate with artifact inventory systems to identify developer machines with installations.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Access to SSH Keys and Cloud Credential Stores
suggestion.rationale: Article payload: 'stealing cloud credentials, SSH keys, and blockchain wallet data'—describes local credential harvesting not mapped to any technique or kill-chain phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process file-system access to credential directories: ~/.ssh/, ~/.aws/, ~/.kube/, ~/.ethereum/, .ssh/config. Alert on npm/Python/Node.js processes reading these paths without legitimate package manager context. Flag simultaneous access to multiple credential stores from single process tree.

suggestion.title: Outbound Connection to TrapDoor C2 Domain
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies ddjidd564.github.io as C2 IOC for credential exfiltration. Pipeline output shows empty IOC extraction despite this being listed in 'Indicators of Compromise' section.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any outbound DNS queries or HTTPS connections to ddjidd564.github.io. Monitor npm/Node.js interpreter processes for unexpected network callbacks. Detect HTTP POST requests from developer machines containing base64-encoded or compressed credential material.

suggestion.title: Automated Exfiltration of Harvested Credentials to C2
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'quietly stealing...and [sending] from developers.' Implies automated post-compromise exfiltration behavior in malicious package code, no use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious network egress from package manager processes (npm, pip, node, python) to non-standard domains. Detect TLS/HTTPS handshakes from these processes to unrecognized IPs/domains. Alert on data volumes and patterns consistent with credential file uploads.

suggestion.title: Package Execution in Development Environment Post-Installation
suggestion.rationale: Malicious packages execute during install/import: 'poisoned packages spread across npm, PyPI' implies code execution via require()/import statements. Missing execution-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected child processes spawned from npm/pip/node interpreters during package installation. Flag node_modules/.bin scripts executing network tools (curl, wget) or credential accessors (ssh-keygen, aws-cli). Correlate package installation events with suspicious process trees.

suggestion.title: LNK file execution and malicious shortcut behavior
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly specifies 'Multi-Stage LNK and PowerShell Attack Chain' but zero detection for .LNK file execution or shortcut-spawned processes. LNK is the entry point mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag .LNK files executed by explorer.exe or user processes, particularly from Downloads/Temp directories. Alert on child processes (powershell.exe, cmd.exe, mshta.exe) spawned from LNK execution chains. Correlate with suspicious command line arguments or parent process context.

suggestion.title: Fake browser update delivery and execution
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'cleverly disguised fake browser update to trick users' but no detection for this social engineering initial access vector. Requires behavior-based hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect executable/MSI downloads with browser update semantics in filename from non-official sources, immediately executed by non-admin users outside standard patch windows. Correlate download URLs with C2 domains or suspicious origins.

suggestion.title: PlugX RAT C2 communication and beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Entire article is about PlugX RAT deployment but no PlugX-specific detection. C2 communication patterns are central to the attack and should be independently detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt outbound HTTP/HTTPS connections to IOC domains (fruitbrat.com, dalerocks.com, coastallasercompany.com) with periodic beaconing intervals. Flag data exfiltration patterns correlating with file hashes from the article and parent-child process trees showing PowerShell→rundll32/svchost relationships.

suggestion.title: Multi-stage loader execution and payload staging
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'multi-stage malware loader' but no detection for loader behavior. Stage-by-stage execution with credential/code download is core to this attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PowerShell/cmd.exe executing encoded commands followed by file creation and execution in temp locations. Flag parent-child chains (explorer/winrar→powershell→rundll32/regsvcs) indicative of staged loader behavior. Monitor for DLL injection into system processes.

suggestion.title: Anomalous parent-child process chains involving system binaries
suggestion.rationale: PowerShell spawning rundll32/svchost/regsvcs (not preceded by legitimate parent) is a signature behavior of RAT deployment chains. Missing from use cases despite being detectable from the narrative.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt PowerShell with non-standard parents (explorer, archive tools, documents). Flag PowerShell executing network activity (DNS/HTTP) followed by system binary execution (rundll32, regsvcs, certutil, mshta). Correlate command line content with obfuscation markers or base64 strings.

suggestion.title: Xeno RAT Process Execution & C2 Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'Xeno RAT' as the payload. RATs typically establish execution (cmd.exe, powershell) and spawn C2 callbacks. No use cases for RAT execution or network-based C2 detection were generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for Xeno RAT process creation patterns (common RAT markers: rundll32 with suspicious DLL, mshta execution, or direct executable spawn). Cross-correlate with outbound connections to known Xeno C2 domains or IPs. Monitor DNS queries for domains associated with Xeno RAT infrastructure.

suggestion.title: SideCopy Spear-Phishing & Document Exploit Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Article title identifies 'SideCopy' threat actor as the attacker. SideCopy is known for spear-phishing campaigns with malicious Office documents. No IOCs for phishing emails, attachment hashes, or initial access vectors were extracted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for Office document execution via Winword.exe, Excel.exe spawning child processes (cmd, powershell, rundll32). Monitor for macro-enabled document downloads from external sources. Check email headers for SideCopy-typical sender patterns or spoofed domains impersonating finance/government entities.

suggestion.title: Afghanistan Finance Ministry Lateral Movement & Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly targets 'Afghanistan Finance Ministry'—a critical government entity. No detection use cases for post-compromise persistence, lateral movement within government networks, or credential harvesting were generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious scheduled task creation (schtasks.exe), registry run-key additions, or service installation in AFG Finance Ministry network segments. Look for lateral movement using harvested credentials (logon type 3/9 from unexpected source IPs). Correlation: Xeno RAT spawn + persistence + lateral movement patterns.

suggestion.title: SideCopy-Attributed Infrastructure IOC Enrichment
suggestion.rationale: Article title identifies Pakistan-linked SideCopy group. Pipeline returned zero IOCs (domains, IPs, file hashes, email senders). SideCopy campaigns typically leave infrastructure signatures and malware hashes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Extract and correlate domain/IP C2 infrastructure associated with SideCopy group (reference VirusTotal, URLhaus, OSINT). Alert on DNS lookups or HTTP/HTTPS connections to known SideCopy control servers. Monitor email source reputation against SideCopy-attributed sending infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Browser Password Store Access by Python Process
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'steals browser passwords'—detection requires monitoring unauthorized access to Chrome/Firefox/Edge credential stores and password database files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when Python.exe or child process reads browser credential database files (%USERPROFILE%\AppData\Local\Google\Chrome\User Data\Default\Login Data, %APPDATA%\Mozilla\Firefox\*\logins.json) or accesses in-memory browser process handles. Flag if source is unsigned Python binary or PyInstaller stub.

suggestion.title: Keylogging Behavior by Python Process
suggestion.rationale: Article: captures 'keystrokes'—requires detection of Python process installing keyboard input hooks or calling WinAPI hooking functions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Python processes loading hooking libraries (pynput, keyboard, mouse modules) or calling SetWindowsHookEx, GetAsyncKeyState, or WH_KEYBOARD_LL. Alert if process spawns long-lived background threads persisting across multiple user sessions.

suggestion.title: Browser Cookie Database Extraction
suggestion.rationale: Article: steals 'cookies'—detection requires monitoring access to browser cookie storage and staging of exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Python process accessing browser cookie files (Cookies, Cookies-journal in Chrome/Edge profiles; cookies.sqlite in Firefox) combined with file copy operations to temporary directories or network connections to non-standard ports.

suggestion.title: Multi-threaded Concurrent Data Harvesting Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'multi-threading to carry out operations simultaneously'—behavioral signature distinct from single-threaded malware, enabling parallel credential and file harvesting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Python processes creating 4+ threads within 10 seconds, each accessing disjoint sensitive locations (password stores, browser data, document folders, registry). Threshold: 50+ file operations across disparate credential/document directories in 60 seconds.

suggestion.title: Sensitive File Bulk Collection by Python Malware
suggestion.rationale: Article: steals 'sensitive files'—requires detection of Python processes performing rapid enumeration and copying of documents, configs, and user data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when Python process accesses 50+ files across sensitive directories (Documents, Desktop, Downloads, %APPDATA%, .ssh, .aws) within 120 seconds, especially if followed by compression, staging to temp, or network exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Python Interpreter Executing Obfuscated Infostealer Code
suggestion.rationale: Article: malware uses 'Python libraries' and 'obfuscated'—detection requires monitoring Python execution environment for packed/scrambled payloads or suspicious module imports.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Python.exe and python.dll for loading obfuscated or compressed modules (PyInstaller bundles, base64-decoded strings in process memory). Alert on import of credential-access libraries (pynput, keyboard, requests, Crypto) combined with file-system reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: Suspicious PowerShell execution from Office applications
suggestion.rationale: State-sponsored groups targeting government infrastructure typically use Office macro-based exploitation. No PowerShell/scripting execution patterns were modeled despite 'attacks' against government targets being central to the article title.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for powershell.exe or cmd.exe spawned as child process of WINWORD.EXE, EXCEL.EXE, or OUTLOOK.EXE with command-line arguments indicative of encoded payloads, registry modification, or remote script download (iex, Invoke-Expression, -EncodedCommand).

suggestion.title: Suspicious WMI execution and lateral movement
suggestion.rationale: APT groups use WMI for command execution and persistence. No WMI-based activity patterns detected despite targeting government networks where WMI reconnaissance is standard tradecraft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on wmic.exe execution with class names (Win32_Process, Win32_Service, StdRegProv) or unusual WMI event subscriber creation. Flag cross-system WMI calls from non-admin source machines.

suggestion.title: Suspicious RDP authentication to government assets
suggestion.rationale: Czech Republic and Taiwan targets suggest government networks; RDP is standard lateral movement tool for APT groups. No RDP anomaly detection use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Event ID 4624 and 4625 for RDP logons from external IPs or unusual source->destination pairs within government IP ranges. Flag multiple failed RDP attempts followed by success from same source within short time window.

suggestion.title: Data exfiltration via suspicious HTTP/DNS patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'attacks' on government targets; no command-and-control or data exfiltration detection use cases generated. State-sponsored actors stage and exfiltrate intelligence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag DNS queries to newly registered domains or suspicious TLDs from government workstations. Monitor for large sequential POST requests to single external IP during off-hours. Alert on DNS queries for common C2 infrastructure patterns (domain-generation-algorithm signatures, known malware C2 domains).

suggestion.title: Unusual file staging and compression activity
suggestion.rationale: No collection-phase detection use cases generated. Attackers targeting government networks typically stage sensitive files before exfiltration using compression utilities.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual execution of 7z.exe, winrar.exe, or tar.exe on government workstations. Flag file write activity to temporary directories immediately preceding compression tool execution. Alert on bulk file access followed by archive creation.

suggestion.title: Malicious document delivery and macro execution
suggestion.rationale: Phishing with malicious attachments is Dragon Weave / China-aligned group tradecraft. Title mentions 'attacks' but no initial-access or delivery detection patterns were generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on emails with Office attachments delivered to government targets, especially from external or newly-registered sender domains. Flag macro-enabled .docm/.xlsm files with suspicious VBA code (WScript.Shell, CreateObject, DownloadFile). Monitor for file download following macro execution.

suggestion.title: CVE-2024-21182 Vulnerability Scan Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'CISA KEV entry' + 'Anything in CISA KEV is currently being exploited' + 'Federal patch due: 2026-06-04'—pipeline must surface scanner hits for this actively-exploited CVE across the fleet.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor vulnerability scanner reports for positive detections of CVE-2024-21182. Alert on any vulnerable WebLogic Server instances, prioritizing those accessible from untrusted networks given active exploitation in the wild.

suggestion.title: T3 Protocol Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated attacker with network access via T3, IIOP'—T3 is the explicit attack vector. Default ports 7001/7002 must be monitored for exploitation signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TCP 7001/7002 for T3 protocol traffic from external sources. Detect malformed T3 handshakes, protocol violations, or rapid connection attempts consistent with CVE-2024-21182 exploitation.

suggestion.title: IIOP Protocol Unauthorized Access
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'network access via T3, IIOP to compromise Oracle WebLogic Server'—IIOP (ports 7091/7092) is a distinct attack vector requiring separate detection coverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor TCP 7091/7092 for IIOP traffic from unexpected sources. Detect connection patterns consistent with reconnaissance or exploitation of the unspecified vulnerability.

suggestion.title: Oracle WebLogic Public Exposure Scan
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'KEV implies active exploitation against exposed assets'—organizations must identify misconfigured/exposed WebLogic instances on public networks before adversaries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan external IP space for WebLogic servers listening on T3 (7001/7002) or IIOP (7091/7092). Cross-reference against authorized asset registry to flag unauthorized public exposure.

suggestion.title: WebLogic Post-Compromise Data Access Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Successful attacks can result in unauthorized access to critical data or complete access to all Oracle WebLogic Server accessible data'—must detect exfiltration post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WebLogic logs for unusual data queries, large sequential data reads, or database connection anomalies following T3/IIOP exploitation attempts within a 1-hour window.

suggestion.title: Docker Hub Repository Supply Chain Poisoning Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'poisoning a Docker Hub repository to later steal Kubernetes secrets and other sensitive data'—core supply chain attack vector entirely missed by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor container runtime for unexpected modifications to pulled images, hash mismatches between registry-published and loaded images, or pulls from newly-created/low-reputation accounts. Alert on docker pull/push from non-standard hosts or layer integrity violations.

suggestion.title: Kubernetes Secrets Exfiltration from Container Context
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'steal Kubernetes secrets and other sensitive data' as primary exfiltration goal; no detection generated despite being core to attack success.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for reads of /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/* paths and environment variable extraction targeting Kubernetes API tokens or service account credentials. Alert on base64-encoded token strings exfiltrated to external IPs.

suggestion.title: Malicious Payload Execution During KICS Scanning
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'distributed a stealer that was loaded during the KICS scanning process'—build-time payload execution via compromised scanner requires detection at build phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected child processes spawned by KICS process (shell interpreters, curl, wget, nc, base64). Alert on file writes to /tmp or suspicious directories during scan execution, or network connections from scanner to non-repository hosts.

suggestion.title: Container Escape via Dangerous Linux Capabilities
suggestion.rationale: Article enumerates CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_SYS_MODULE, CAP_SYS_PTRACE, CAP_NET_ADMIN as escape vectors but provides no corresponding detection use cases for capability-based privilege escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on containers running with CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_SYS_MODULE, or CAP_SYS_PTRACE capabilities (via audit logs). Detect ptrace syscalls to host processes (PID 1 or host daemons), kernel module load attempts, or reads/writes to /dev/mem or /dev/kmem from container namespaces.

suggestion.title: Checkmarx KICS Build Tool Compromise Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'Checkmarx KICS' as the specific compromised scanning tool distributing stealer payloads, but pipeline generated no detection for suspicious KICS behavior or artifacts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected files, binaries, or scripts deposited in KICS output or configuration directories. Alert on KICS spawning non-standard child processes, establishing network connections to hosts outside known scanner repositories, or reading sensitive environment variables.

suggestion.title: TeamPCP Container Attack Pattern Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly attributes attack to TeamPCP APT group but pipeline failed to surface this actor or correlate their known TTPs: build tool compromise, Kubernetes targeting, credential stealer deployment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Checkmarx KICS execution with Kubernetes API enumeration commands (kubectl get secrets, get nodes, get pods) and credential exfiltration patterns. Alert on cluster reconnaissance from scanner/build contexts or suspicious service account token reads during container image scanning.

suggestion.title: WordPress Admin Account Creation via Plugin Exploit
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'actively exploited to create admin accounts'—this is the direct persistence mechanism and attack outcome. Pipeline entirely missed this.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WordPress for rapid user-to-admin privilege escalation events. Detect wp_usermeta or wp_users table writes creating accounts with admin caps immediately following failed/suspicious HTTP requests to wp-maps-pro plugin endpoints. Correlate creation timestamps with exploitation attempt logs.

suggestion.title: WP Maps Pro Plugin Exploitation (Unauthenticated)
suggestion.rationale: Article directly names 'WP Maps Pro' as the vulnerable plugin; 'actively exploited' indicates in-the-wild attacks. Pipeline should map this to T1190 exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on POST/GET requests to /wp-content/plugins/wp-maps-pro/ endpoints with suspicious parameters (file inclusions, serialized objects, SQL fragments). Match against known plugin CVE payload patterns. Detect followed by user-creation events within 60 seconds.

suggestion.title: Unpatched WP Maps Pro Plugin Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Threat is tied to specific plugin name and version. Pipeline should have surfaced inventory queries and version-pinning to prevent exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query for WP Maps Pro installations site-wide. Flag all instances below patched version threshold. Correlate against exploitation attempt timelines. Alert on plugin re-activation after update enforcement.

suggestion.title: High-Volume Failed Login Attempts Within Short Window
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers conducted 'brute force attacks...by trying multiple passwords in succession.' Detectable via authentication logs showing N+ failed attempts from single source IP targeting same user account within T seconds.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when >10 failed login attempts occur against same account from same source IP within 5 minutes. Correlate with account lockout events to confirm Dashlane-like automated defense triggering.

suggestion.title: Device Registration Verification Email Preceded by Failed Auth Spike
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'emails contained verification codes for legitimate account owners to register new devices' immediately after 'attempted logins from distant locations and unknown devices.' This sequence indicates credential-access escalation attempt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect time-correlated pairs: (1) failed auth spike against account followed within 15 min by (2) device registration verification email sent to same account. Flag if email geolocation mismatches failed login source.

suggestion.title: Account Lockout Following Multi-Attempt Authentication Failure Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article describes Dashlane's 'automated security controls' triggering 'account lockouts to block automated attacks after a threshold of failed attempts is reached.' Lockout event itself is a strong brute-force indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Generate alert when account lockout event occurs and pre-lockout logs show ≥5 failed login attempts within 10 minutes. Distinguish from user lockout via failed password entry by checking MFA success/failure patterns.

suggestion.title: Login Attempts from Geographically Disparate Locations Within Minutes
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'attempted logins from distant locations and unknown devices.' Geographic velocity—e.g., login from USA followed by login from distant country within 30 min—indicates brute-force tooling or credential stuffing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag login attempts where consecutive authentications span >1000 km within <X minutes (tunable per org baseline). Assign higher risk weight if one attempt fails and next succeeds.

suggestion.title: Multiple Device Registration Notifications to Same User in Short Period
suggestion.rationale: Article notes users 'received notices of suspicious access requests from foreign countries' with 'verification codes for legitimate account owners to register new devices.' Multiple notifications signal repeated device-registration escalation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when same account receives >3 device registration verification emails within 1 hour, or registrations are attempted from high-risk geolocations (particularly those matching failed-auth geographies).

suggestion.title: Support Ticket Surge for Account Access Issues Post-Brute-Force
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'some users continue to report login problems, mentioning that support is unresponsive.' Spike in account-access support tickets post-incident indicates either unresolved compromises or systemic service degradation requiring incident escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor support ticket creation rate for 'account locked' / 'cannot login' keywords; spike >2x baseline during/after known brute-force campaign indicates secondary compromise risk or incomplete remediation.

suggestion.title: POST /workspaces/*/members with role=owner
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly specifies UC_25_2 with complete Splunk/KQL. Core exploitation path: 'forwards the request body's user_id and role straight into MemberService.add(workspace_id, user_id, role), which has no caller-permission check'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on POST /workspaces/*/members returning 201 with role=owner in request body. Extract source IP, authenticated user, target workspace ID. Baseline for bulk owner assignments within short window.

suggestion.title: Owner escalation followed by login from newly granted account
suggestion.rationale: Article UC_25_3: 'identity-swap chain — owner grant followed by login from the granted account'. Detects post-exploitation account takeover consolidation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate POST /workspaces/*/members (201, role=owner) with subsequent authentication event where login source IP matches grant source IP and authenticated identity differs from grantor, within 3600 seconds.

suggestion.title: Backend process and file activity for member_service.py and deps.py
suggestion.rationale: Article UC_25_1 specifies behavioral hunt for member_service.py and deps.py—the backend components implementing the vulnerable MemberService.add() function. Behavioral baselines detect backend anomalies correlated with API exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal process execution and file I/O for member_service.py and deps.py. Flag process execution from unexpected parent processes, file modifications outside deployment windows, or file creation from non-deployment service accounts.

suggestion.title: Member enumeration followed by privilege escalation attempt
suggestion.rationale: Attack pattern: attacker queries workspace members (discovery phase) then immediately escalates. Article states gating enforced only by 'require_workspace_member(workspace_id)' with 'no caller-permission check'—any member can enumerate and escalate.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GET /workspaces/*/members* (member discovery) followed by POST /workspaces/*/members with role=owner from same source IP within 60–300 seconds. Indicates reconnaissance-then-escalation attack chain.

suggestion.title: Malicious JavaScript Injection Pattern Detection (zTDS)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes JavaScript injection following 't.js?site=<id>' pattern with unique ID per compromised site. Over 80 malicious injection domains identified. This is the primary compromise mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to domains matching t.js?site=* or zTDS-related callback patterns. Alert on requests from internal networks to known or suspected zTDS infrastructure. Correlate with webpage access logs to identify which sites are redirecting users.

suggestion.title: Fake Browser Update Prompt Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes FakeUpdates campaign impersonating Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari, Opera, Brave, Yandex, Vivaldi, Samsung Internet, and UC Browser with fraudulent update prompts. Users deceived into downloading malicious payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of suspicious update processes (Browser Update.exe, fake update executables) from temporary directories or user Downloads. Alert on process execution following HTTP download from non-canonical browser update domains (not official CDNs). Monitor for ZIP archives containing executable + DLL combinations matching fake update signature.

suggestion.title: PowerShell ClickFix Command Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article states ClickFix attacks involve PowerShell commands executed by victims deceived into copying malicious commands to Windows command prompt. Verification-themed attacks target both Windows and macOS.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PowerShell invocations preceded by user-visible prompts on compromised website redirects. Alert on scripts originating from copy-paste (high entropy, minimal white space). Correlate with web proxy logs showing visits to zTDS-compromised sites immediately before PowerShell execution.

suggestion.title: macOS Clipboard Hijacking via ClickFix
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions obfuscated JavaScript payload targeting macOS via clipboard hijacking in verification-themed ClickFix attacks, indicating campaign extends beyond Windows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for macOS processes accessing clipboard (pbpaste, /dev/clipboard) combined with unusual shell invocation. Alert on clipboard content matching known malicious command patterns. Correlate with web proxy logs showing macOS user-agent accessing compromised/zTDS-infrastructure sites.

suggestion.title: Traffic Distribution System (zTDS) Infrastructure Fingerprinting
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies zTDS (open-source since 2015, used by DriveSurge since Sept 2025) as central routing mechanism. Researchers identified eight technical fingerprints including JavaScript injection and domain patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify zTDS infrastructure through distinctive HTTP request patterns, URL parameter structures, and domain behavior (one TDS domain directing to multiple malicious lures). Monitor for bulk website compromises with identical JavaScript injection fingerprints. Correlate DNS queries and HTTP traffic to identify zTDS controller domains.

suggestion.title: Pay-Per-Install (PPI) Malware Distribution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states DriveSurge functions as initial access broker (IAB) using PPI model for follow-on attacks. This indicates staged malware delivery where initial payloads are dropped, then sold to other threat actors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for staging behaviors: initial executable drops multiple payloads, creates child processes invoking C2 callbacks, or exhibits rapid successive execution of unrelated malware families. Alert on single user/endpoint infected with multiple distinct malware lineages in short timespan.

suggestion.title: Compromised npm Package Installation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title specifies 'Red Hat npm Packages' compromised with worm payload. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs for malicious package names, versions, or installation indicators despite this being the initial-access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install operations for flagged malicious package names and versions. Alert when install-time dependency resolution pulls from non-standard registries or skips integrity verification. Correlate with package-lock.json entries containing known compromised hashes.

suggestion.title: Credential Theft via Worm Post-Execution
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'credential-stealing worm' but pipeline generated zero use-cases for credential access (T1555, T1187, T1003). Missing detection for browser/system credential harvesting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect node.exe spawning child processes targeting credential stores (LSASS dumps, SAM, browser profile DBs, SSH keys). Alert on DPAPI/credential manager API invocations from npm-spawned processes. Monitor for bulk file reads from %APPDATA%/Local/Google/Chrome or %USERPROFILE%/.ssh.

suggestion.title: Worm Lateral Movement via npm Dependency Chain
suggestion.rationale: Attack characterized as worm implies self-propagating behavior and multi-host infection. Pipeline failed to generate detection for lateral-movement phase (T1570, T1021) or infection chain propagation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for multiple machines installing same malicious npm package version within short timeframe. Detect node processes invoking npm install on UNC paths or to different registry hosts. Alert on command-line npm invocations with suspicious --registry or --cache-dir flags.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Code Execution from npm Module Cache
suggestion.rationale: Worm delivery via npm requires script execution phase (T1203, T1059). Pipeline produced no execution-phase use-cases despite npm postinstall scripts being a known worm vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on node.exe child processes spawning powershell, cmd.exe, or curl with encoded arguments during npm install. Detect DLL injection into node processes from non-system paths. Monitor for unsigned executable downloads to node_modules/.bin directory.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of Stolen Credentials via C2 Channel
suggestion.rationale: Credential-stealing worm must exfiltrate harvested credentials over C2. Pipeline generated zero use-cases for exfiltration phase (T1041, T1568) or C2 communication detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound HTTPS/DNS from npm-spawned processes to non-npm-registry domains. Alert on base64-encoded POST bodies resembling credential dumps. Detect connections to known malicious infrastructure or fast-flux domains correlating with credential theft timelines.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Package Integrity Verification Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Compromised npm packages imply tampering of manifest, lock files, or version control metadata. Pipeline extracted no IOCs or detections for integrity violations (T1195.003).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline integrity hashes of package.json and package-lock.json. Alert on cryptographic hash mismatches between registry-published and locally-installed packages. Detect npm ci/install with --force or --no-audit flags bypassing security checks.

suggestion.title: npm Package Preinstall Script Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Each compromised release adds an install-time hook. npm runs preinstall scripts automatically during npm install, before any of your own code executes' and identifies malicious index.js as the payload entry point. Zero preinstall-monitoring use cases generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm package.json manifests for preinstall script additions within @redhat-cloud-services or other high-trust namespaces. Flag preinstall scripts that invoke obfuscated JavaScript, particularly those using eval() or dynamic string decoding patterns. Correlate with package publish timestamps and account anomalies.

suggestion.title: GitHub OIDC Token Requests in Supply Chain Publishing
suggestion.rationale: Root cause explicitly describes 'Requested a GitHub OIDC identity token via id-token: write' in malicious GitHub Actions workflow 'Triggered on push to any branch.' No detection for this OIDC exfiltration or token abuse pattern generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on GitHub Actions workflows in publishing-critical repositories (e.g., RedHatInsights) that request id-token: write without corresponding legitimate publishing step. Flag OIDC token generation followed by push to main/release branches or orphan commits within short time windows.

suggestion.title: Cloud Identity Enumeration via GCP/Azure SDKs
suggestion.rationale: Article states payload 'enumerate[s] every identity the infected host can assume' via 'new collectors for GCP and Azure' to 'map and reach the cloud control plane.' No detection use cases for cloud identity discovery patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect enumerateServiceAccounts, listServiceAccounts, or equivalent GCP/Azure calls originating from npm install processes or CI/CD runners with unexpected privilege scope. Flag calls that enumerate identities reachable by the current principal without prior role-assumption pattern.

suggestion.title: Multi-Source Credential Harvesting in CI/CD Context
suggestion.rationale: Payload 'Harvests secrets and credentials from the local environment and CI context: environment variables, ~/.npmrc tokens, SSH keys, GitHub tokens, and CI/CD secrets.' Article notes blast radius reaches 'well beyond Red Hat's own pipelines.' No detection for coordinated credential access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In CI/CD contexts, alert on single process that reads ~/.npmrc, ~/.ssh/*, environment variables containing 'TOKEN', 'SECRET', 'KEY', or 'GITHUB' sequentially or in rapid succession. Preinstall scripts should not access credential files; flag npm-related PIDs accessing home directories.

suggestion.title: Package Republication by Newly-Compromised Maintainer
suggestion.rationale: Worm mechanism: 'It queries the registry for other packages the compromised identity can publish and republishes them, carrying the same payload, which is what turns a single compromised maintainer into a worm.' No lateral-movement or propagation detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm registry for multiple package versions published by the same account in a short window (< 1 hour) where account previously had low publish velocity. Flag republishes of existing package versions with modified preinstall scripts or matching obfuscation signatures. Correlate with account first-seen activity.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated JavaScript Patterns in npm Packages
suggestion.rationale: Article describes payload as 'heavily obfuscated JavaScript file' using 'eval() and ROT-based string decoding' as 'tradecraft pattern seen in earlier Shai-Hulud variants.' No static analysis or code-pattern detection for obfuscation in package manifests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan published npm packages for index.js or main entry points containing eval(), Function(), or atob() calls combined with string slicing, ROT cipher patterns, or XOR operations. Flag preinstall scripts with code complexity exceeding baseline for the package type; compare against historical releases by same maintainer.

suggestion.title: npm Post-Install Script Credential Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Authentication Tokens Stolen' via npm package; pipeline missed detection for processes spawned during package installation accessing credential stores. Core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm/node child processes accessing .openai, .env, .aws/credentials, shell_history, or invoking credential-manager APIs during install phase. Cross-correlate with unexpected network egress.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Install from Modified Lockfile
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain compromise implies injected dependency; detection should flag when installed package versions diverge from lockfile or when codexui-android (or similar typosquats) appears in manifests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm/yarn/pnpm install commands for package-name typosquats, packages installed from non-official registries, or version mismatches between package-lock.json and runtime installed versions.

suggestion.title: API Token Exfiltration via HTTP POST
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'OpenAI Codex Authentication Tokens' stolen, implying C2 callback. Pipeline failed to suggest detection for base64/obfuscated token patterns in outbound HTTP bodies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP POST requests from npm/node contexts with large payloads or base64-encoded bodies; match against OpenAI token patterns (sk-proj-*, sk-*) in network traffic or URL parameters.

suggestion.title: Malicious npm Package Version Detection
suggestion.rationale: Package codexui-android compromised; detection should cover known-malicious version publication and subsequent installation across developer estates.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest npm registry vulnerability feeds and cross-check installed versions against known-malicious releases; alert on npm install of codexui-android or near-homoglyphs in any environment.

suggestion.title: Unusual npm Registry Authentication Token Usage
suggestion.rationale: Attacker must publish malicious version; detection should cover compromised npm account tokens or unexpected publish operations from CI/CD contexts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor .npmrc file reads by unusual processes, npm publish/unpublish commands executed outside normal release workflows, or npm tokens appearing in process environment.

suggestion.title: Cloud Provider DNS Tunneling Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists T1071.004 (DNS) as observed technique and states attackers 'weaponizing trusted cloud infrastructure... to camouflage malicious traffic.' No UC provided for DNS-based C2 or DNS tunneling through cloud provider nameservers (Route53, Azure DNS, Google Cloud DNS).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect DNS query patterns to cloud provider authoritative nameservers with anomalies: high query volume to non-existent subdomains, unusual entropy/length in query names, or repeated NXDOMAIN responses. Correlate source process and timing. Cloud DNS abuse for C2 often manifests as subdomain enumeration or algorithmically-generated query streams.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Outbound to Cloud CDN from non-Standard Processes
suggestion.rationale: Article describes T1027 (Obfuscated Files or Information) and emphasizes attackers use cloud services 'to evade detection.' No UC detects obfuscated or suspicious execution chains originating from cloud CDN content (Cloudflare Workers, AWS CloudFront, Azure CDN).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process creation or file execution with parent process initiated by HTTP/HTTPS download from cloud CDN IP ranges. Flag if process is unsigned, missing certificate, or launched by unusual parent (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, wscript.exe). Correlate with rare destination ports or encrypted payload indicators.

suggestion.title: Cloud Service API Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Article phrase: 'sustain long-lived Command and Control (C2) operations' using cloud infrastructure implies persistence and credential theft. No UC detects unusual cloud API calls, token exfiltration patterns, or cloud provider credential misuse (AWS keys, Azure tokens, GCP service accounts in unexpected context).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect reads of cloud credential files (~/.aws/credentials, Azure config, GCP service account JSON) from non-standard processes or by processes not owned by cloud admin tools. Correlate with subsequent API calls from unexpected source IPs or regions. Monitor for exfiltration of credentials to external hosts.

suggestion.title: Multi-Hop Cloud Proxy Chain Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article lists abuse of AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, Cloudflare, GitHub as separate C2 channels but provides no UC for detecting multi-hop routing through multiple cloud providers in sequence. Attackers chaining clouds for redundancy and obfuscation is a natural implication of 'multiple trusted cloud infrastructure.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate outbound traffic across flow records: src → AWS IP range → then Azure IP range → then external destination, within short time window (< 60s). Use geolocation and ASN correlation. Compare cloud egress IPs against known cloud provider ranges; multi-hop exits are rare for legitimate traffic.

suggestion.title: Scheduled Task or Cron Referencing Cloud Storage
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes C2 persistence but provides no persistence-phase UC. Attackers sustaining long-lived operations via cloud services typically anchor jobs or scheduled tasks to cloud storage URLs or credentials for command fetching.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect scheduled tasks (Windows) or cron jobs (Linux) with command-line arguments or executables referencing cloud storage URLs (s3://, gs://, blob.core.windows.net), cloud API endpoints, or cloud provider CLIs used for credential exfiltration. Flag if task runs outside business hours.

suggestion.title: Asset exposure—vulnerable PAN-OS instances for CVE-2026-0257
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states CISA added vulnerability to KEV catalog with 'actively leveraged in real-world attacks' warning. Pipeline surfaced zero CVEs. Article phrase: 'CISA has added a critical Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS vulnerability to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, warning that the flaw is being actively leveraged in real-world attacks.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset databases for PAN-OS instances and version-match against CVE-2026-0257 affected versions. Flag internet-facing firewalls as critical. Cross-reference with inbound connection logs during exploitation windows.

suggestion.title: Network connections to attacker C2 IPs
suggestion.rationale: Six high-fidelity IPv4 IOCs provided in article 'Indicators of Compromise' section; pipeline extracted zero. These are explicitly mapped to C2 phase in article's recommended hunt template.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for any outbound connections from PAN-OS firewalls or vulnerable systems to: 104.207.144.154, 146.19.216.119, 146.19.216.120, 146.19.216.125, 209.99.191.137, 79.130.26.202.
