Flag successful connections for incident escalation. Correlate with CVE-2026-0257 exploitation indicators.

suggestion.title: PAN-OS administrative account abuse post-exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'enables attackers to bypass authentication mechanisms' yet pipeline generated zero use case for detecting unauthorized admin access. This is the core post-exploitation phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PAN-OS admin console logs for successful logins from the six IOC IPs, new admin account creation, or privilege escalation events. Correlate with network C2 connections for confirmation. Alert on logins outside normal geographic/time patterns.

suggestion.title: CVE-2024-21182 Exploitation via T3/IIOP Protocol Detected
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'can be exploited remotely' with 'network access via T3, IIOP'—this is the active attack vector cited as 'now actively exploited in attacks.' Pipeline generated no detection for protocol-level exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for T3 or IIOP protocol connections to Oracle WebLogic ports (7001, 7002, 7003) from external sources or untrusted networks. Flag handshakes from non-whitelisted IPs, connection attempts to versions 12.2.1.4.0 or 14.1.1.0.0, or payloads matching known exploitation signatures post-connection.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Oracle WebLogic Versions in Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article names specific vulnerable versions affecting '961 instances' (12.2.1.4.0) and '631 instances' (14.1.1.0.0) per Shodan. Pipeline missed version-based asset discovery and risk-layering detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query process inventory and WebLogic startup logs for version strings '12.2.1.4.0' or '14.1.1.0.0'. Cross-reference patch management to identify systems without July 2024+ patches. Flag as high-risk asset for lateral movement targeting.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Access to WebLogic Critical Data Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states successful exploitation 'can result in unauthorized access to critical data or *complete access to all Oracle WebLogic Server accessible data*.' No detection for impact-phase data access was suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of normal data access patterns per WebLogic application context (user, transaction, credential tables). Alert on bulk queries, exports, or unusual data volume spikes originating from exploited (unpatched) instances or shortly after external T3/IIOP connection events.

suggestion.title: WebLogic Server Exposed to Unauthenticated Network Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article highlights 'no privileges' required and lists 1,592+ instances exposed on Shodan. Pipeline did not surface exposure-based detection or network segmentation validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan external-facing network segments for accessible WebLogic ports (7001, 7002) without MFA or IP-whitelist gating. Alert if WebLogic instances respond to unauthenticated T3 protocol requests. Cross-reference with Shodan/Censys to confirm exposure visibility.

suggestion.title: Brute-Force Authentication Attempts Against Dashlane
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'brute-force attack' and discloses attack occurred against Dashlane's authentication layer. Pipeline failed to surface detection for repeated failed login attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect multiple failed authentication attempts (40+ in 5 min) targeting Dashlane login endpoints from single/clustered source IPs. Correlate with successful login immediately following failed attempts. Look for user-agent, SSL/TLS fingerprint consistency across attempts.

suggestion.title: Bulk Vault Data Exfiltration from Dashlane Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'encrypted vaults of fewer than 20 users downloaded'—direct evidence of data exfiltration. Pipeline provided zero exfiltration detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect large file downloads from Dashlane API endpoints (vault exports >5MB per user) occurring post-compromise. Baseline normal vault backup sizes; flag outliers. Correlate with credential-access phase (T1110 detection).

suggestion.title: Credential Manager Compromise - Account Takeover Post-Brute-Force
suggestion.rationale: Brute-force success implies valid credentials obtained. Article does not clarify if credentials were subsequently used for persistence or lateral movement, but account takeover is implicit in vault download scenario.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect logins using compromised Dashlane credentials to third-party SaaS or enterprise systems. Flag impossible-travel (login from attacker IP, then user's home IP within minutes). Correlate against vault-owner identity.

suggestion.title: SaaS Credential Manager Vault Access Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Fewer than 20 users affected. Pipeline should surface detection for unusual vault access patterns (e.g., downloads, decryption attempts, or sync events outside normal windows).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor vault access events (open, export, sync) grouped by user; flag sudden spike or out-of-hours access. Correlate with geographic anomalies and device fingerprint changes.

suggestion.title: Attack Infrastructure Enumeration - Dashlane Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Brute-force rarely succeeds without prior enumeration. Pipeline should detect scanning/OSINT activity against Dashlane login endpoints before credential attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequential HTTP requests to Dashlane endpoints (login, password-reset, account-recovery) from single source, testing response codes and timing patterns. Distinguish from legitimate user enumeration.

suggestion.title: LNK file execution by user process
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'Multi-Stage LNK' attack vector; body states 'fake browser update' delivery. Article describes trojanized .lnk file as initial entry point but no detection rule covers LNK execution. T1204.002 is core to this attack chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect .lnk file execution with CommandLine references to cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or system32 executables. Prioritize .lnk files launched from TEMP, Downloads, or ProgramData with parent process explorer.exe or svchost.exe (unusual). PlugX payloads are typically hidden in adjacent binaries invoked by trojanized shortcuts.

suggestion.title: PlugX RAT network signature
suggestion.rationale: Article names PlugX as the delivered payload and 'began communicating with a remote' indicates C2 post-execution. No detection rule provided for PlugX-specific command-and-control traffic. PlugX is signature tool of Mustang Panda; network-based detection is essential.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: PlugX uses HTTP POST or DNS tunneling to C2 server. Detect anomalous DNS queries with high entropy subdomains, or HTTP POST requests to suspicious domains with binary/encoded payloads. Look for connections to defanged IOCs (45.251.243.210, fruitbrat.com, dalerocks.com, coastallasercompany.com). Correlation with hash IOCs (79af67ed..., 106f4637..., 8421e799...) strengthens signal.

suggestion.title: Multi-stage loader execution chain
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'multi-stage malware loader' and 'quietly installed itself'. This indicates download-and-execution of secondary payloads; no behavioral detection rule covers this. Detect parent-child process chains indicative of staged download.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect powershell.exe launching with DownloadString, Net.WebClient, or IEX in parent chain; followed by execution of dropped binary from %TEMP% or AppData. Look for rapid file creation + delete patterns (staging). Correlation with C2 network IOCs increases confidence.

suggestion.title: Browser update spoofing installer execution
suggestion.rationale: Article opening: 'cleverly disguised fake browser update to trick users into downloading'. No detection covers this social-engineering vector. Behavior: user double-clicks fake update installer → .lnk drops PlugX. Detect installer files masquerading as legitimate browser updates.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect executable/MSI/LNK with file name or metadata claiming to be Chrome/Firefox/Edge update from non-official source (TEMP, Downloads, email attachment, USB). Verify signer (legitimate updates are signed by vendor). Trigger on execution from archive or email-temp locations.

suggestion.title: macOS Malvertising Campaign Initial Access Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'malvertising campaign targeting macOS users' as the delivery vector. Pipeline has zero initial_access phase. Need detection for malvertising traffic patterns, suspicious ad-network callbacks, or landing page indicators referenced in article.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious network connections to known malvertising infrastructure or ad-network abuse patterns. Look for macOS processes establishing connections to advertisement delivery networks preceding suspicious binary downloads.

suggestion.title: FlutterShell Backdoor Execution Detection (macOS)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies 'new backdoor FlutterShell, built using the Flutter framework' as payload. Pipeline has zero execution phase and no detection rule for FlutterShell execution. Must detect Flutter-framework binary execution with suspicious behavioral signals.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor macOS process execution for Flutter framework binaries spawned outside normal development contexts. Flag processes loading Flutter runtime libraries followed by unexpected child process spawning, network connections, or persistence setup.

suggestion.title: Flutter Framework Artifact Discovery (Defense Evasion Indicator)
suggestion.rationale: Article notes malware 'built using Flutter framework'—this is a known evasion technique (legitimate framework abuse). No pipeline coverage. Detect anomalous Flutter application signatures or suspicious Flutter runtime usage on macOS.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify unsigned or suspicious Flutter application bundles, Flutter .so library files with unusual entropy/signatures, or Flutter runtime invocations from non-standard paths (~/Downloads, /tmp, cache directories).

suggestion.title: macOS Backdoor Command & Control Communication Detection
suggestion.rationale: Implicit from 'backdoor' in article title—FlutterShell must establish C2. Pipeline has zero command_and_control phase. Need detection for FlutterShell C2 callbacks, exfiltration patterns, or command execution channels.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on macOS processes establishing outbound HTTPS connections to C2 infrastructure or showing abnormal HTTP/DNS request patterns consistent with backdoor callback behavior (periodic beaconing, command encoding).

suggestion.title: macOS Persistence via LaunchAgent/Daemon (FlutterShell)
suggestion.rationale: Backdoor malware requires persistence; article describes 'backdoor' but pipeline has zero persistence phase. Standard macOS persistence uses LaunchAgents/Daemons or cron. Must detect suspicious launch item creation by or for FlutterShell.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor creation/modification of ~/Library/LaunchAgents, /Library/LaunchDaemons, or cron job files with references to Flutter binaries, suspicious scripts, or C2 infrastructure. Alert on plist files containing persistence mechanisms created in same session as FlutterShell execution.

suggestion.title: Suspicious macOS Application Download via Safari/Browser
suggestion.rationale: Malvertising 'targets macOS users'; likely delivery via browser. Pipeline missing detection for user-clicked malvertising links and resulting downloads. Need to detect suspicious binary download chains from ad-networks to ~/Downloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate malvertising-network HTTP referrers with macOS .dmg/.app/.zip downloads to user Downloads folder, followed by immediate execution or Finder/Archive Utility activity. Flag if download parent process is browser and child is DMG mount or app execution.

suggestion.title: Xeno RAT C2 Beaconing Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title identifies 'Xeno RAT' as the attack payload. RATs inherently establish command-and-control communication; C2 beaconing patterns are the earliest detectable post-execution signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for network connections to known or suspected Xeno RAT C2 infrastructure. Xeno RAT variants typically establish HTTPS or custom-protocol C2 channels. Look for beaconing patterns (periodic connections at fixed intervals, characteristic TLS/SNI fingerprints, or unusual port assignments).

suggestion.title: Xeno RAT File Execution & Persistence
suggestion.rationale: The article describes a RAT deployment against a government finance ministry. Successful deployment requires local execution and likely persistence mechanisms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Xeno RAT parent-child process chains and execution artifacts. Detect suspicious .exe/.dll launches from User temp directories, AppData, or obfuscated paths. Monitor for registry Run-key or scheduled task persistence attempts common to RAT deployments.

suggestion.title: SideCopy Phishing/Initial Access to Finance Ministry
suggestion.rationale: Title identifies SideCopy as the attacker (Pakistan-linked group). SideCopy's historical TTPs include spear-phishing and malicious document delivery. This article describes *targeting* of Afghanistan Finance Ministry, implying initial compromise vector not yet detailed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for emails with SideCopy-attributed sender/domain patterns, macro-enabled Office documents, or suspicious attachment detonation. Correlate with any observed Office child processes (WinWord.exe → cmd.exe, WinWord.exe → powershell.exe) occurring in finance ministry user sessions.

suggestion.title: Credential Access on Finance Ministry Systems
suggestion.rationale: Targeting of a finance ministry with a RAT strongly suggests attacker intent to harvest credentials (banking access, administrative accounts, system credentials). No use case generated despite this being a clear attacker objective for this target class.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Xeno RAT spawning credential-dumping tools (mimikatz, LaZagne, comsvcs.dll + rundll32). Monitor for abnormal LSASS access, registry hive copy-outs, or WDigest/SamSam reads. Alert on login failures followed by successful lateral movement (anomalous lateral access patterns from compromised endpoint).

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion by SideCopy/Xeno RAT
suggestion.rationale: RAT campaigns targeting government ministries typically employ evasion (code injection, process hollowing, UAC bypass). Article context implies sophisticated adversary; pipeline generated zero evasion detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for suspicious remote thread creation (CreateRemoteThread), process injection targeting legitimate processes (svchost, explorer, WmiPrvSE), or UAC bypass attempts (eventvwr.exe, fodhelper.exe, wusa.exe). Correlate with parent process ancestry typical of Xeno RAT loaders.

suggestion.title: npm Package Installation: @redhat-cloud-services Versions Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'multiple packages published under the @redhat-cloud-services npm namespace'—threat is realized at `npm install` time. Detection must track installation/update of affected versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install/update operations for @redhat-cloud-services/* packages post-June 1, 2026. Correlate against affected version feeds. Flag installs by unexpected users, build service accounts, or outside normal patch windows.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Launch from npm Postinstall Script Execution
suggestion.rationale: 'Malicious code injected into frontend libraries' executes at npm postinstall time or app startup. Look for unexpected process spawns from node.exe or npm script contexts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect cmd.exe, powershell.exe, curl, wget spawned from node.exe parent or npm.exe; command-line obfuscation or encoding in npm script contexts; unexpected network callbacks from nodejs runtime.

suggestion.title: GitHub Repository Anomaly: Unauthorized Commits to Production Branches
suggestion.rationale: 'Compromised GitHub account was used to inject malicious code'—attack originates with account takeover. Monitor for anomalous commit patterns, unusual geolocations, off-hours activity, or bulk pushes to main/release branches.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag commits to Red Hat GitHub org main/release branches from: new/unusual IP ranges, service accounts during off-hours, bulk commit operations outside normal dev cadence, or commits immediately followed by npm publish.

suggestion.title: npm Registry Publish: Unexpected Version or Unauthorized Publisher
suggestion.rationale: Compromised account used to inject and then publish malicious versions. Monitor for package publishes from unexpected CI systems, revoked accounts, or unusual version jumps without changelog.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect publishes of @redhat-cloud-services packages with: non-sequential version numbers, published by accounts outside whitelist, published from CI systems not in approval matrix, or publishes outside scheduled release windows.

suggestion.title: APT C2 Beaconing Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes active attack by Dragon Weave against Czech Republic and Taiwan; implies command infrastructure and attacker-controlled C2 channels that must be detected during intrusion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for periodic outbound connections to low-volume or newly-registered domains, consistent with APT C2 heartbeat patterns. Flag encrypted tunnels and HTTP User-Agent anomalies associated with Dragon Weave infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Credential Theft and LDAP Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: APT 'Hits' against nation-state targets inherently involves reconnaissance and credential harvesting; article describes 'Ramp Up Attacks' indicating multi-stage intrusion with internal discovery phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify LDAP enumeration (net user queries, dsquery execution), credential dumping tool activity (mimikatz, secretsdump), and brute-force attempts against domain accounts following lateral movement indicators.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Administrative Shares
suggestion.rationale: High-severity China-aligned APT attacks crossing geographic boundaries require horizontal traversal through target networks; should detect SMB/RPC lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unusual SMB/RPC connections between internal hosts, especially ADMIN$ and C$ share access from non-admin source IPs. Detect use of lateral movement tools (psexec, wmiexec, smbexec) via command-line telemetry.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration Over C2
suggestion.rationale: APT targeting Czech Republic and Taiwan for 'Ramp Up' campaign implies intelligence collection objective requiring outbound data transfer detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect large-volume file transfers to C2-associated infrastructure, encrypted tunnels exfiltrating data, and anomalous outbound traffic patterns deviating from baseline user/host behavior.

suggestion.title: Initial Access via Email or Web Exploit
suggestion.rationale: Dragon Weave campaign described as hitting multiple geographies suggests distributed initial access mechanism, likely phishing or unpatched vulnerability exploitation targeting these regions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor email gateways for phishing payloads targeting Czech/Taiwan employees. Track exploitation of known CVEs in internet-facing applications and suspicious child processes spawned from Office macros or HTML applications.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Scheduled Tasks or Registry Modification
suggestion.rationale: Active APT campaign requires attacker persistence mechanisms to survive reboots and maintain access across the attack duration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect scheduled task creation with suspicious binaries, registry run-key modifications with obfuscated payloads, and WMI event subscription creation for persistent code execution.

suggestion.title: Asset Inventory: Oracle WebLogic Server Exposed (CVE-2024-21182)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated attacker with network access via T3, IIOP' and recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt'. Pipeline generated no asset inventory or vulnerability scan detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for Internet-exposed Oracle WebLogic Server instances running vulnerable builds, or scan logs for successful authentication bypass attempts targeting WebLogic administrative ports (7001–7002). Cross-reference vulnerability scanner output with network exposure data.

suggestion.title: Network: Suspicious T3/IIOP Protocol Activity to WebLogic Server
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'network access via T3, IIOP' as the attack vector. Pipeline did not generate protocol-abuse detection despite explicit mention.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound T3 or IIOP protocol connections to WebLogic infrastructure from external or untrusted networks. T3 (port 7001 default) and IIOP (port 7002 default) traffic from non-administrative sources may indicate exploitation attempts. Establish baseline of legitimate management connections and flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation: Unauthorized Data Access to WebLogic Configuration/Datasources
suggestion.rationale: Article states exploitation 'can result in unauthorized access to critical data or complete access to all Oracle WebLogic Server accessible data'. Pipeline did not surface detection for data exfiltration or unauthorized access patterns post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WebLogic log files and audit trails for unauthorized reads of sensitive configuration (datasources, encryption keys, domain credentials). Track large data transfers or unusual account access to RDBMS systems accessible via WebLogic connections. Flag access outside normal administrative windows.

suggestion.title: Process: Exploitation Shellcode/Payload Execution via WebLogic RMI/T3 Deserialization
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2024-21182 affects an 'unspecified' component but KEV context implies remote code execution potential. Pipeline did not model the execution phase common in WebLogic exploits (deserialization gadget chains).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for unexpected child processes spawned by Oracle WebLogic JVM (java.exe), particularly cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or reverse-shell payloads. Monitor for abnormal outbound connections from WebLogic processes post-initial-access, and correlate with T3/IIOP inbound traffic windows.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scan: WebLogic Service Detection and Version Identification
suggestion.rationale: Article is a CISA KEV entry; detection begins with asset discovery. Pipeline generated no asset-discovery or service-enumeration use case despite recommendation for 'asset-exposure hunt'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for open Oracle WebLogic Server ports (7001, 7002, 8001, 8002 default ranges) and perform banner-grabbing / version identification. Compare discovered instances against patch-history and deprecation timelines; prioritize instances running builds released before the patch cutoff for CVE-2024-21182.

suggestion.title: Docker Hub Repository Poisoning with Malicious Stealer
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'poisoning a Docker Hub repository to later steal Kubernetes secrets and other sensitive data. The tainted images distributed a stealer that was loaded during the KICS scanning process.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthorized modifications to container image manifests or repository metadata in Docker Hub/registries. Detect when images are pulled and executed with suspicious post-build modifications. Correlate to known stealer C2 beacon patterns and Kubernetes API enumeration.

suggestion.title: Container Escape via CAP_SYS_ADMIN/CAP_SYS_MODULE Capabilities
suggestion.rationale: Article details 'Privileged containers' section and enumerates CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_SYS_MODULE capabilities as primary escape vectors for privilege escalation from container to host.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on containers spawned with CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_SYS_MODULE, CAP_SYS_PTRACE, or CAP_NET_ADMIN capabilities. Correlate with process creation of kernel module loaders, namespace manipulation tools, or ptrace syscalls that indicate escape attempts.

suggestion.title: Kubernetes Secrets Exfiltration During Build/Scan Phase
suggestion.rationale: Article states attack chain 'steal Kubernetes secrets' following container compromise. Malicious stealer 'was loaded during the KICS scanning process', indicating secrets enumeration during automated build/scan phases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process execution of secret enumeration tools (kubectl, env, curl) within container during image scanning. Alert on unexpected outbound connections to credential stores or exfiltration of environment variables containing secret patterns.

suggestion.title: Malicious Payload Injection in KICS/SCA Scanner Execution Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article describes how 'a stealer was loaded during the KICS scanning process'—injection into trusted scanning tool execution is the delivery and execution mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor KICS/SCA scanner process hierarchy for unexpected child processes or library loads. Detect when scanner subprocess execution deviates from baseline (network calls, new binary execution, suspicious config file modifications).

suggestion.title: Orchestration API Exploitation Post-Container Escape
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'Exploitation of orchestration APIs' as a primary attack vector. After escaping container, attacker pivots to Kubernetes/Docker API for lateral movement or data exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on anomalous API calls to Kubernetes/Docker daemon (list secrets, create pods, exec into containers) originating from container process namespaces or suspicious service accounts. Correlate to compromised image metadata or supply chain indicators.

suggestion.title: Host Kernel Exploitation from Container Context
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 'Exploiting host system vulnerabilities' as primary vector. Containers share kernel with host, enabling privilege escalation via kernel CVEs targeting container namespace/cgroup mechanisms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect syscall patterns and kernel error signatures associated with known container-breakout CVEs (OverlayFS, cgroup_memory, nf_conntrack exploits). Alert on unusual privilege escalation calls originating from container processes.

suggestion.title: WordPress Admin Account Creation Following WP Maps Pro Interaction
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states flaw is 'actively exploited to create admin accounts.' Pipeline generated zero use cases. Detection should trigger on new admin user creation immediately after plugin requests or during vulnerability exploitation window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WordPress user creation events (wp_users table inserts or wp-admin/user-new.php POST requests) correlating with failed or suspicious WP Maps Pro REST API calls, multi-tool access, or unauthenticated requests to plugin endpoints. Baseline expected admin creation rates; flag outliers.

suggestion.title: Exploitation of WP Maps Pro Vulnerability (CVE-Unknown)
suggestion.rationale: Title identifies 'critical' and 'actively exploited' vulnerability. No IOCs extracted. Detection should identify exploitation patterns: non-standard request sequences, SQL injection markers, or privilege-escalation payloads targeting the plugin.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to /wp-content/plugins/wp-maps-pro/* endpoints with SQL injection patterns, PHP parameter tampering (e.g., action=xxx, role=administrator), or requests from non-admin IPs followed by privilege escalation. Alert on 40x→200 sequences within seconds.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Privilege Escalation via Plugin Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Title phrase 'create admin accounts' indicates post-exploitation persistence. No persistence-phase detection suggested. Detection should flag role elevation or capability grants tied to plugin directory access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate file modifications in wp-content/plugins/wp-maps-pro/ (especially admin.php, includes, or init hooks) with WordPress user meta changes elevating roles from subscriber/author to administrator. Unusual file timestamps or non-whitelisted actors modifying plugin code trigger alerts.

suggestion.title: Mass WordPress Admin Account Creation Campaign Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states flaw is 'actively exploited'—implies coordinated, likely mass-exploitation scenario. Pipeline provided no campaign-level detection. Detection should identify multiple admin creations across WordPress instances or suspicious naming/email patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: If monitoring multiple WordPress installations, detect correlated admin account creations within a time window (e.g., >3 admins created in <1 hour across different sites). Flag accounts with generic names (admin2, admin3, test, wp-admin), no email address, or email domains previously seen in exploitation campaigns.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to WP Maps Pro Administrative Functionality
suggestion.rationale: Critical flaw 'actively exploited' implies unauthenticated or low-privilege bypasses. Pipeline generated no initial-access detection. Detection should surface unauthorized WP Maps Pro endpoint access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on POST/GET requests to /wp-content/plugins/wp-maps-pro/ endpoints (especially **/admin.php, **/settings, **/api**) from non-authenticated sessions or with missing/invalid nonce tokens, or from IP ranges not in admin whitelist. Baseline access patterns during non-business hours.

suggestion.title: Multiple Failed Authentication Attempts Before Account Lockout
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers used 'brute-force attacks that attempted logins from distant locations'—textbook T1110.001. Pipeline failed to flag failed-auth-count spikes preceding account suspension.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor authentication logs for accounts exceeding threshold of failed login attempts (e.g., >5 in 15 minutes). Correlate with account suspension/lockout events. Alert when fail count spikes without corresponding successful login, indicating active brute-force campaign.

suggestion.title: Login Attempts from Geographically Distant Locations
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'suspicious access requests from foreign countries'—attackers geographically distant from user baseline. Pipeline did not capture this impossible-travel or geo-anomaly detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag login attempts originating from countries/regions that deviate from user's baseline. Alert if attempt originates from impossible-travel distance in short time window, especially when correlated with failed-attempt bursts.

suggestion.title: Device Registration Triggered During Failed Authentication Bursts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly: 'emails contained verification codes for legitimate account owners to register new devices' during brute-force. Pipeline ignored this persistence phase—attacker pivoting from credential-guessing to device enrollment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when device registration requests are initiated during or immediately after a burst of failed login attempts on the same account. Monitor for new device registration email notifications sent to users as proxy for attacker persistence.

suggestion.title: Account Suspension/Lockout Surge Indicating Brute-Force Campaign
suggestion.rationale: Article reports multiple users locked out; 'suspension of those accounts as part of Dashlane's built-in security controls' was the response. Pipeline should detect the precursor: sudden spike in account lockouts across users.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor account lockout event volume for deviations from baseline. Alert if lockouts cluster around same time window across distinct users (indicator of coordinated brute-force sweep rather than isolated failures).

suggestion.title: Verification Code Submission Failures (MFA Token Guessing)
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'verification codes' in context of brute-force—implying attacker obtained or attempted to guess OTP/MFA tokens. Pipeline missed detection for MFA token brute-force or reuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on multiple failed MFA challenges for same account in short time window. Flag if multiple distinct MFA tokens submitted in rapid succession (guessing). Monitor for verification code requests sent but not redeemed.

suggestion.title: POST /workspaces/*/members with role=owner (CVE-2026-47413 exploitation)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Any workspace member can add arbitrary user as owner via POST /workspaces/{id}/members' and describes the endpoint as 'gated only by require_workspace_member()' with no caller-permission check in MemberService.add(). This is the primary exploitation signature and should be the flagship detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to /workspaces/*/members with HTTP 200/201 responses, filtering for role=owner or 'role':'owner' in request body. Correlate source IP, user identity, and destination workspace. High fidelity: member adding external/unrelated user as owner; Medium fidelity: legitimate admin operations (baseline required).

suggestion.title: Workspace member enumeration preceding privilege-escalation attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'forwards the request body's user_id...straight into MemberService.add()' with no validation. Attackers must discover or enumerate valid user IDs before crafting the exploit POST. Missing detection for reconnaissance phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect burst GET requests to /workspaces/*/members, /users, or user enumeration endpoints from a single user/IP within 10 minutes, followed by a subsequent POST /workspaces/*/members with role=owner within 1 hour. Flag if new user_id in POST was absent from preceding GET enumeration responses.

suggestion.title: First login / account activation by newly-granted workspace owner (identity-swap validation)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes privilege escalation for 'account manipulation'. After the attacker adds an arbitrary user as owner, that user will authenticate to claim the role. Missing detection for the account activation/first-use pattern that validates exploitation success.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate workspace member additions (POST /workspaces/*/members role=owner) with first authentication or unusual login context (new IP, new user-agent, off-hours) for the newly-added user within 60 minutes. Flag if the login user is distinct from the granting user.

suggestion.title: Workspace permission and policy modifications within 24h of owner escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes the vulnerability enables 'account manipulation' and privilege escalation. Once an attacker gains owner role, they can modify workspace settings, member lists, and data access policies. Missing detection for downstream privilege abuse post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for permission/role changes within a workspace (member demotions, bulk additions, policy updates, data access changes) occurring within 24 hours of a detected CVE-2026-47413 exploitation event. Flag changes that alter data access scope or involve sensitive workspaces.

suggestion.title: Asset exposure: praisonai-platform instance detection and version enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 'Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)' as recon-phase hunt but provides only a template reference. Missing concrete detection for deployed praisonai-platform instances vulnerable to CVE-2026-47413.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference software inventory (installed praisonai-platform versions, container images, package manifests) against CVE-2026-47413 advisory. Probe candidate hosts for /workspaces, /healthcheck, or version endpoints to confirm API availability and deduce version. Flag all instances at or below affected version range.

suggestion.title: JavaScript Injection Pattern Detection (t.js?site parameter)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies 't.js?site=<id>' as fingerprint for DriveSurge infrastructure: 'JavaScript injection following the t.js?site=<id> pattern, where <id> is a unique value assigned to each compromised website.' This is a directly detectable indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests for t.js script tags with site parameter patterns. Alert on requests to malicious injection domains from multiple legitimate website sources. Correlate downstream with malware sandbox detections to confirm malicious intent.

suggestion.title: Fake Browser Update Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes FakeUpdates for Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari, Opera, Brave, Yandex, Vivaldi, Samsung Internet, and UC Browser, with concrete example: 'fake Firefox update that downloaded a ZIP archive containing multiple DLLs and a malicious executable named Browser Update.exe.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of update-themed executables (Browser Update.exe, ChromeUpdate.exe, etc.) from suspicious directories. Alert on ZIP archives containing mixed DLLs and executables downloaded via web. Correlate browser processes with non-standard update prompts or downloads.

suggestion.title: PowerShell ClickFix Command Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article states ClickFix attacks 'involve PowerShell commands' that trick 'victims into copying and executing malicious commands.' This is direct execution via command-line interface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PowerShell process creation from clipboard paste operations. Alert on suspicious command-line patterns immediately following verification-themed prompts or web redirects. Detect encoded/obfuscated commands attempting to disable security features or download payloads.

suggestion.title: Traffic Distribution System Redirect Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes zTDS infrastructure: 'DriveSurge hijacks thousands of legitimate, high-reputation websites and silently redirects visitors to malware, unbeknownst to the sites' owners.' zTDS profiles visitors and determines redirect targets, indicating detectable redirect patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected HTTP redirects originating from legitimate high-reputation websites. Detect variable redirect destinations based on visitor attributes (User-Agent, IP, etc.) indicating TDS profiling. Correlate with known zTDS infrastructure via domain pivoting.

suggestion.title: Mixed DLL-Executable Archive Download Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies distinctive artifact pattern: 'ZIP archive containing multiple DLLs and a malicious executable named Browser Update.exe.' This specific combination is detectable at network/file level before execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on ZIP archive downloads containing both DLL and executable files from web sources. Flag archives where executables are named after legitimate updates (Browser Update.exe, etc.). Correlate with browser activity and suspicious referrer domains.

suggestion.title: macOS Clipboard Hijacking via ClickFix
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies cross-platform targeting: 'obfuscated JavaScript payload specifically designed to target macOS desktop systems, delivered via verification-themed ClickFix attacks that hijack the clipboard.' Platform-specific execution vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor macOS for JavaScript execution followed by clipboard access operations. Alert on obfuscated scripts running in browser or system contexts. Detect unusual clipboard content (commands, URLs) being pasted into Terminal immediately following web activity.

suggestion.title: npm Package Installation from Untrusted Registry
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Red Hat npm Packages' were compromised in supply chain. Execution begins with end-user running 'npm install' on a malicious package. Need detection for package download/install anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm/yarn CLI execution with suspicious registry arguments or non-standard package sources. Detect installation of packages with recently-registered names or unusual download sizes. Alert on first-run installation of packages not previously seen in environment.

suggestion.title: Credential-Stealing Worm Code Execution During npm Install
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'Credential-Stealing Worm' behavior. npm package post-install scripts execute arbitrary code. Need detection for process spawning and credential access during npm module setup.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect shell/PowerShell spawned as child of node.exe or npm.exe, especially those attempting to access system credential stores, environment variables, or making outbound network connections. Correlate with package installation timeline.

suggestion.title: Browser Credential Harvesting from Node Context
suggestion.rationale: Worm is described as 'credential-stealing.' Malicious npm module code likely reads browser localStorage, cookies, or password manager exports. Monitor for unauthorized access to credential storage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on node.exe or child processes reading from %APPDATA%/browser credential directories, SQLite databases in Chrome/Firefox profile paths, or calling credential APIs. Monitor for unusual file reads targeting 'passwords', 'cookies', 'credentials', 'token' in path.

suggestion.title: Worm Self-Propagation via npm Dependency Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Worm' payload, implying automatic propagation. Supply-chain context suggests horizontal spread through project dependencies. Need detection for recursive/circular dependency injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm module attempting to modify package.json in parent/sibling projects, inject new dependencies, or spawn child npm install processes. Monitor for multiple npm registry API calls from single compromised module or repeated package-lock.json modifications.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of Stolen Credentials via C2 Channel
suggestion.rationale: Credential-stealing worm must exfiltrate data. Article likely references command-and-control infrastructure. Need detection for data exfil over HTTP/DNS/TLS from npm context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on node.exe or npm child processes making HTTP POST requests to non-npm-registry domains with JSON payloads (likely credential dumps). Monitor for DNS queries to newly-registered or suspicious domains from build processes. Correlate timing with npm install completion.

suggestion.title: Post-Install Script Execution with Privilege Escalation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Worm behavior suggests potential privilege escalation to persist or gain deeper access. npm post-install runs in user context but may attempt sudo/UAC bypass. Article context implies Red Hat environment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for sudo/su invocation from npm post-install scripts or node child processes, especially with nopass sudo. Detect 'sudo npm install' with embedded privilege escalation. Alert on failed UAC prompts from npm context on Windows.

suggestion.title: npm Preinstall Script Execution Detected During Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes the attack trigger: 'npm runs preinstall scripts automatically during npm install, before any of your own code executes, so simply resolving the dependency is enough to trigger the payload.' This is the direct execution vector and pipeline created no baseline detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for node.exe or npm.exe launching child processes (particularly index.js) during npm install execution. Alert on preinstall script execution from newly-added or recently-modified packages. Cross-reference with package.json modifications in the same timeline.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting from Environment and Local Configuration Files
suggestion.rationale: Core payload behavior: 'Harvests secrets and credentials from the local environment and CI context: environment variables, ~/.npmrc tokens, SSH keys, GitHub tokens, and CI/CD secrets.' No detection for this credential access pattern despite explicit description.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect node.exe or JavaScript processes reading ~/.npmrc, ~/.ssh/id_rsa, ~/.ssh/config files or enumerating process environment for CI_*, GITHUB_*, AZURE_*, GCP_* prefixed variables. Alert on eval() combined with rapid environment variable access. Flag these patterns within 10 seconds of npm install completion.

suggestion.title: Bulk Cloud Identity and Service Account Enumeration from CI/Build Environments
suggestion.rationale: Variant-specific capability: 'The notable change in this variant is a pair of new collectors for GCP and Azure that enumerate every identity the infected host can assume, not just static secrets.' No detection for cloud control-plane enumeration from compromised build infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk ListRoleAssignments, ListIdentities, GetServiceAccounts, or equivalent API calls from unexpected source IPs or CI/CD runner identities. Monitor for service-principal enumeration queries from GitHub Actions runners or npm CI contexts. Establish baseline of expected cloud enumeration from build agents.

suggestion.title: Rapid Republishing of Multiple npm Packages by Single Identity
suggestion.rationale: Self-propagation mechanism: 'It queries the registry for other packages the compromised identity can publish and republishes them, carrying the same payload, which is what turns a single compromised maintainer into a worm.' No detection for this lateral-movement/persistence pattern despite explicit description as key worm behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when a single maintainer identity publishes to more than 3 distinct packages within a 10-minute window. suggestion.title: Xeno RAT Process Execution Signature
suggestion.rationale: No execution-layer detections despite malware name in article. Should detect RAT process spawn, code injection, or module loading patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Xeno RAT execution via process hollowing, DLL injection into legitimate Windows processes, or spawning cmd.exe/powershell.exe from unusual parents. Monitor for unsigned or recently-added binaries with RAT behavioral signatures.

suggestion.title: Finance Ministry Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: RAT implants in finance ministry (high-value target for treasury, payment systems, budget data) trigger post-exploitation credential theft. No credential-access use cases despite context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect keylogging, clipboard hooks, LSASS memory access, or clipboard data exfiltration from compromised finance ministry systems. Flag suspicious tool execution (mimikatz, laZagne) or unusual registry edits for persistence.

suggestion.title: Bulk Data Exfiltration from Finance Ministry
suggestion.rationale: Targeting Afghanistan Finance Ministry implies theft of budgets, transaction records, payment schemes. No exfiltration-focused detections despite high-value data assets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for large outbound data transfers from finance ministry file shares, databases, or document repositories to external IP addresses. Detect encrypted tunnel usage (DNS-over-HTTPS, Tor) obscuring exfil payloads.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm package version / metadata anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'malicious code into frontend libraries maintained within a Red Hat GitHub organization' and 'published under the @redhat-cloud-services npm namespace'—directly implicating registry tampering. Pipeline should detect unexpected version jumps, backfilled timestamps, or hash mismatches on trusted packages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm registry for @redhat-cloud-services packages with unexpected version increments, publish timestamps inconsistent with team activity windows, or signature/hash deviations from known releases. Cross-reference lockfile changes in downstream projects.

suggestion.title: Unusual outbound connections from Node.js runtime processes
suggestion.rationale: Compromised npm packages will execute arbitrary JavaScript when installed. Article confirms 'malicious code' injected; pipeline must detect callback infrastructure. Hypothesis: code phones home to attacker C2.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound HTTPS/HTTP/DNS from node.exe or npm processes to non-standard domains (excluding npmjs.com, registry.npmjs.org, github.com). Prioritize destinations with low ASN reputation or geoIP anomalies.

suggestion.title: Code obfuscation and dynamic execution in JavaScript packages
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'injected malicious code' into production packages. Attackers obscure payloads. Pipeline should flag evals, Function constructors, base64 blobs, and minified/uglified code in source analysis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan package source (node_modules or build artifacts) for obfuscation markers: eval(), Function(), Buffer.from(base64), atob, require with dynamic strings, or code.split().join() patterns. Correlate with package publish delta.

suggestion.title: GitHub account anomalies on Red Hat organization repositories
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'A compromised GitHub account was used' to inject code. Pipeline must detect the compromise itself: unusual IP/geolocation, commits at off-hours, rapid repo modifications, or MFA disablement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub audit logs for Red Hat organization: logins from new geographies/IPs, commits to high-value namespaces (@redhat-cloud-services) from untrusted sessions, MFA policy bypasses, or commit timestamps clustering outside team work hours.

suggestion.title: Downstream package dependency on compromised @redhat-cloud-services versions
suggestion.rationale: Article does not specify which downstream projects auto-installed malicious versions. Pipeline should generate hunting prompts for package.json/package-lock.json containing @redhat-cloud-services in dependency trees within enterprise environments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query all npm install / ci / build logs for entries matching @redhat-cloud-services across any version during the compromise window (prior to remediation date). Flag any projects in production environments with matching lockfile entries.

suggestion.title: Malicious package auto-update or re-installation patterns
suggestion.rationale: npm can auto-update packages via caret/tilde versions. Detect re-execution of poisoned code on re-deployment or automated dependency refresh.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag npm install/ci/update operations pulling @redhat-cloud-services versions known to be compromised. Correlate with downstream container image builds and artifact repository updates.

suggestion.title: npm package install script executes suspicious external command
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly discusses CI/CD persistence and multi-stage payloads triggered during package installation—no detection for install script behavior captured. Install scripts are the primary execution vector in npm supply-chain attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for node.js or npm processes spawning child processes (curl, wget, powershell, bash) immediately after package install. Flag when curl/wget targets obfuscated or base64-encoded URLs. Correlate process tree: npm install → node → external download/execution.

suggestion.title: Credential harvesting via npm package code inspection
suggestion.rationale: Keywords cite 'Credential Harvesting' as attack objective; article describes exfiltration payloads in package source. No detection for suspicious string patterns (API keys, tokens, AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID) in package tarball contents or for credential exfiltration callbacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm packages containing credential-like patterns in source (process.env.AWS, process.env.GCP, TOKEN, SECRET, PASSWORD). Correlate with unexpected outbound HTTPS to external domains during install. Flag if package sends data from /home, /root, or .ssh directories.

suggestion.title: Worm-like package propagation via dependency injection
suggestion.rationale: Article keywords explicitly cite 'worm propagation'; description mentions self-replicating behavior across dependency trees. No detection for packages modifying package.json, package-lock.json, or auto-installing additional dependencies during install.
log_sources: git commit logs (if post-install runs git)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when npm install modifies package.json or package-lock.json to inject new dependencies. Flag packages that call npm install recursively or modify host system's npm config (.npmrc, npm-shrinkwrap.json). Detect behavioral signature: install → file write → new dependency added → next user's install inherits payload.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated payload detection in npm package source
suggestion.rationale: Keywords explicitly cite 'obfuscation' and 'payload'; article focuses on anti-analysis techniques. No detection for eval(), base64 decoding, hex decoding, or minified code patterns that bypass static analysis in package source.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag npm packages with high obfuscation entropy: suspicious eval() calls with dynamic strings, base64-encoded strings >500 bytes in install scripts, hex-encoded payloads, or minified code in package root. Alert if obfuscated code decodes to process execution or credential exfil signatures.

suggestion.title: Typosquatting or package name masquerading detection
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks via npm classically use typosquatting (lodash vs lo-dash, react vs reactjs). Article discusses attack surface and package compromise but no detection for install attempts against lookalike package names or rapid package creation patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when developer installs packages with edit distance <2 from popular packages (lodash, express, request, async). Flag package names containing special homoglyphs (𝙧eact vs react). Correlate with dev environment: if typosquatted package installed in CI/CD or production, escalate. Monitor for packages published same-day with name similar to trending libraries.

suggestion.title: npm package publishing from compromised GitHub accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions GitHub account compromise as attack vector. No detection for unusual publishing patterns: new maintainer added, version bump from new IP, API token issued, or publishing outside normal maintenance windows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm registry for version publishes from new IP addresses or geolocations inconsistent with historical publisher locations. Flag if GitHub Actions workflow modified to publish to npm without human approval. Alert if new maintainer added via API token immediately before package publish. Correlate GitHub 2FA changes with npm publishes.

suggestion.title: Device Code Phishing Flow Anomaly Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes device code phishing as 'industrialized PhaaS offering' with '18+ kits actively tracked' and notes it 'bypasses MFA and passkeys entirely.' Article: 'device code phishing, which abuses a legitimate OAuth flow to bypass MFA and passkeys entirely, has surged from a research curiosity to an industrialized PhaaS offering.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for device code authorization flows from atypical geolocations, rapid sequential device code attempts from the same user, and device code flows followed immediately by suspicious OAuth grants to AI tools or newly-registered apps. Correlate with failed sign-in attempts suggesting MFA bypass attempts.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized OAuth Permissions to AI Apps
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'average organization has...17 AI-connected OAuth integrations—most of them unapproved' and 'AI agents are requesting OAuth permissions.' This represents direct credential access and persistence vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect OAuth consent grants to unknown or unapproved AI applications, especially those requesting broad scopes (mail.read, files.read, user.read). Flag grants from non-standard applications or those with low reputation scores. Correlate with subsequent unusual data access patterns.

suggestion.title: AI Tool Data Exfiltration via File Upload & Clipboard
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly warns: 'Sensitive data leaves the organization through clipboard pastes and file uploads to AI tools that security teams didn't approve and can't monitor.' Also notes '38% of file uploads to AI tools are made from personal shadow accounts.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for POSTing of potentially sensitive files (documents with keywords like 'secret', 'confidential', 'password', 'API_KEY') to unauthorized cloud AI services. Track clipboard operations copying sensitive data to web-based AI tools. Correlate clipboard read events on AI tool domains with copy operations on sensitive file shares or document stores.

suggestion.title: Malvertising & Phishing Link Injection via Search & Social Channels
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'roughly 1 in 3 phishing payloads arrive via channels other than email' and 'ClickFix is an even clearer example, where 4 in 5 payloads arrive specifically through search engine results.' LLMShare campaign 'used legitimate chatgpt.com sharing links' for malvertising.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect clicks on suspicious search results or social media posts that resolve to phishing infrastructure. Monitor for legitimate AI sharing links (chatgpt.com/share) being used in ad campaigns or forwarded through email gateways. Analyze landing page behavior post-click: form injection, credential fields, mitmproxy signatures, rapid redirects.

suggestion.title: Browser Session Credential Theft & Script Injection Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'detection needs to operate at the browser session layer, analyzing page behavior, script execution, and malicious mechanics (session theft, malicious copy and paste, file downloads)' and notes 'many attacks now take place entirely inside the browser session without touching the endpoint.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for inline script execution on phishing-like pages (forms requesting credentials, suspicious DOM manipulation). Detect clipboard read/write patterns that correlate with sensitive-looking form fields. Flag session storage access and abnormal fetch/XHR calls to attacker-controlled domains or mismatched origins.

suggestion.title: AI Browser Extension Installation & Malicious Context Collection
suggestion.rationale: Article warns 'AI browser extensions collect browsing context from internal applications, creating a data exfiltration path that operates outside traditional DLP.' Organizations average '17 AI browser extensions' most unapproved. Extension as supply-chain vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for installation of unapproved AI browser extensions, especially from non-official stores. Track extensions requesting broad host permissions or high-sensitivity APIs (tabs, webRequest, cookies, storage). Correlate extension network traffic with sensitive domains (internal apps, cloud storage, AI tools) and flag data exfiltration patterns (large outbound payloads to unknown hosts).

suggestion.title: WordPress File Creation in Plugin/Content Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'malware campaign targeting WordPress websites'—requires execution and persistence. Article mentions malware 'works in two [truncated]', implying initial compromise. No detection for WordPress installation tampering. Phrase: 'campaign targeting WordPress websites'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected .php file creation in wp-content/plugins/, wp-content/uploads/, and wp-includes/ from web-server processes. Flag new files appearing outside maintenance windows or created by non-administrative processes.

suggestion.title: Web Process Outbound to Steam Community Profiles
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector: 'hiding command instructions inside Steam Community profile comments' and 'infected sites...command instructions inside Steam'. Article explicitly describes malware fetching from steamcommunity.com. Phrase: 'command instructions inside Steam Community profile comments'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect php-fpm, apache, or nginx processes initiating outbound connections to steamcommunity.com/id/* or steamcommunity.com/profiles/* endpoints. Correlate with WordPress directory in process working path. Flag presence of non-gaming User-Agent strings.

suggestion.title: Malware Domain hello-mywordl.info C2 Callback
suggestion.rationale: Article lists hello-mywordl.info as a defanged C2 domain; this is a high-confidence IOC that should trigger immediate alerting. Phrase: 'Domain (defanged): hello-mywordl.info'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any outbound connection to hello-mywordl.info from any process, especially web-server or WordPress-adjacent processes. Escalate if source is a WordPress installation directory. Zero tolerance for this domain.

suggestion.title: External Data Parsed as Commands (WordPress Context)
suggestion.rationale: Attack specifically fetches content from external URLs (Steam profiles) and processes them as commands. Requires detection for WordPress code paths that fetch, parse, and execute external content. Phrase: 'command instructions inside Steam Community profile comments'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WordPress logs and PHP error logs for eval(), exec(), system(), or passthru() calls operating on data fetched from steamcommunity.com or web requests. Flag any attempt to execute commands derived from external HTML/JSON parsing.

suggestion.title: Dragon Weave – Phishing Campaign (Czech Republic / Taiwan Targeting)
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly names Dragon Weave and geographic targets Czech Republic and Taiwan. Pipeline failed to generate any initial-access use cases despite this clear indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on phishing emails with sender domains impersonating government/critical infrastructure in Czech Republic or Taiwan. Monitor for URLs and attachments consistent with APT campaigns; correlate against known Dragon Weave malware families and infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Dragon Weave – Network C2 and Beaconing Detection
suggestion.rationale: Named APT actor indicates known infrastructure; pipeline should enable detection of command-and-control channels even without full article content.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound connections to Dragon Weave-attributed C2 domains, IP blocks, and SSL certificates. Flag beaconing patterns and DNS exfiltration attempts from hosts in Czech Republic or Taiwan government/defense networks.

suggestion.title: Dragon Weave – Lateral Movement and Persistence (Post-Compromise)
suggestion.rationale: APT 'ramping up attacks' indicates multi-stage operations; pipeline missed expected persistence and lateral movement indicators typical of sustained campaigns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious RDP, SMB, or SSH authentication attempts and lateral spread within target networks post-initial compromise. Alert on living-off-the-land binaries (LOLBins) and file-share enumeration from compromised hosts.

suggestion.title: Oracle WebLogic CVE-2024-21182 Unpatched Asset Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and directs substitution into `_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure` with CVE-2024-21182. Pipeline generated no use case despite this direct instruction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability management platform for unpatched CVE-2024-21182 across Oracle WebLogic instances. Flag any instance without patch applied before federal due date 2026-06-04. Correlate with asset inventory to confirm production criticality.

suggestion.title: Suspicious T3/IIOP Protocol Activity to WebLogic Servers
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'unauthenticated attacker with network access via T3, IIOP' but pipeline did not extract these protocol indicators or generate network-layer detection. T3 and IIOP are Oracle RMI protocols used in exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected inbound T3/IIOP connections to WebLogic default ports (7001, 7002, 8001, 8002). Establish baseline of legitimate internal traffic. Flag external sources or anomalous lateral connections as exploitation attempts, particularly before 2026-06-04.

suggestion.title: WebLogic RMI Deserialization Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article notes vulnerability 'could allow an unauthenticated attacker' to 'compromise' and gain 'complete access to all...accessible data.' Pipeline missed post-exploitation detection for data exfiltration or unauthorized access patterns via RMI.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WebLogic application logs for T3 protocol deserialization errors, RMI ClassNotFoundException, or unexpected object instantiation. Correlate with network events showing T3 handshakes. Watch for subsequent data queries or exports to non-standard destinations.

suggestion.title: Exposed WebLogic Server Console Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article implies network-accessible WebLogic instances vulnerable to unauthenticated attack. Pipeline should have detected exposure of admin console (port 7001/HTTP).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for publicly routable Oracle WebLogic Server instances via port 7001, 7002, 8001, 8002. Attempt banner grab to confirm WebLogic version. Cross-reference with CISA KEV to identify instances running vulnerable versions of CVE-2024-21182.

suggestion.title: Docker Image Registry Compromise / Supply Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'poisoning a Docker Hub repository to later steal Kubernetes secrets and other sensitive data. The tainted images distributed a stealer that was loaded during the KICS scanning process.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected image manifest changes in trusted registries, pulls of images with digest mismatches vs. signed manifests, and suspicious child processes spawned during image extraction or container initialization.

suggestion.title: Stealer Payload Execution in Container Context
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'stealer that was loaded during the KICS scanning process.' No detection mapped for credential exfiltration or C2 from container runtimes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child processes spawned from scanner/entrypoint with network exfiltration of environment variables, mounted secrets, or API credentials to external IPs.

suggestion.title: Kubernetes Secret Enumeration and Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'steal Kubernetes secrets and other sensitive data.' No detection for secret access from compromised container contexts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on list/get secret API calls from non-init containers, reads to /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token with subsequent exfiltration, or serviceaccount tokens used from unexpected namespaces.

suggestion.title: Container Escape via Dangerous Capabilities
suggestion.rationale: Article lists escape vectors: 'CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_SYS_MODULE, CAP_SYS_PTRACE, CAP_NET_ADMIN' and 'Exploiting host system vulnerabilities.' No detection for privilege-escalation attempts post-escape.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor containers with dangerous caps attempting to write /proc/sysrq-trigger, load kernel modules, mount /proc, attach ptrace to host PIDs, or execute eBPF programs.

suggestion.title: Orchestration API Reconnaissance and Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Exploitation of orchestration APIs' listed as attack vector. No detection for Kubernetes API enumeration or lateral movement via RBAC abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk secret/configmap list operations, cluster-admin RBAC binding changes, pod exec from non-standard clients, or API calls from unexpected IP ranges.

suggestion.title: Container Runtime Socket Access Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Exploiting vulnerabilities in the host system and container runtime components.' No detection for socket access or privilege escalation via runtime APIs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file access to /var/run/docker.sock, /run/containerd/containerd.sock from inside containers, followed by container creation or exec commands with escalated privileges.

suggestion.title: WordPress Plugin Exploitation via Unauthenticated RCE
suggestion.rationale: Article states the flaw is 'actively exploited'—implies remote code execution or similar vector. No detection UC was generated despite this being the attack trigger.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests targeting WP Maps Pro plugin paths (wp-content/plugins/wp-maps-pro/) with anomalous payloads or POST bodies. Correlate with unusual WordPress execution patterns or PHP errors indicating parameter tampering.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Admin Account Creation in WordPress
suggestion.rationale: Article headline explicitly names account creation as the impact: 'Create Admin Accounts.' No detection use case generated for this high-confidence attack outcome.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on wp_users table INSERT operations with role='administrator' or capability=manage_options where the source is unauthenticated HTTP request. Baseline normal admin creation cadence and flag out-of-pattern additions.

suggestion.title: WP Maps Pro Post-Exploitation Persistence via New Privileged Account
suggestion.rationale: Created admin accounts serve as persistence—attackers can use them for future access. No persistence-phase detection was suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track login activity from newly created admin accounts within 24h of account creation. Flag any logins from IP ranges not previously associated with legitimate admins, or at off-hours.

suggestion.title: WP Maps Pro Vulnerability Exploitation—Request Pattern Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article describes active exploitation but pipeline extracted no request signatures, malicious parameter names, or proof-of-concept payload patterns that would feed detection rules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest known WP Maps Pro exploit request signatures (from public PoCs or vendor advisories). Match against web access logs using regex/string matching on parameter names, function calls, or SQL keywords within query strings targeting /wp-content/plugins/wp-maps-pro/.

suggestion.title: High-Volume Failed Authentication Attempts on Cloud Identity Platform
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'brute force attacks' and 'multiple passwords in succession until the correct one is found.' Pipeline generated no detection use case for this signature attack pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for >5 failed login attempts in a 5-minute window per user account targeting password-manager or cloud-identity platform. Baseline user-account failure rates and alert on 3x deviation. Correlate with geographically distant or non-baseline source IPs to increase fidelity.

suggestion.title: Device Registration Following Failed Authentication Burst
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'The emails contained verification codes for legitimate account owners to register new devices.' Device registration following failed brute-force is indicator of account-hijacking workflow.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when device registration, MFA enrollment, or new authorized session occurs within 2 minutes following a burst of ≥5 failed authentication events on the same user account. Require synchronous user verification or block the device provisioning.

suggestion.title: Geographic Velocity Anomaly in Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attackers attempted logins 'from distant locations and unknown devices' and users received 'suspicious access requests from foreign countries.' Geographic anomalies are strong indicator of credential-stuffing or brute-force attacks, not legitimate user behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag login attempts from IP geolocation inconsistent with user's baseline geographic profile (e.g., login from US followed by simultaneous or near-simultaneous login from China/distant country). Assign medium confidence and trigger step-up authentication or account review.

suggestion.title: Account Lockout Spike Correlating with Brute-Force Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'suspension of those accounts as part of Dashlane's built-in security controls.' Account suspensions triggered by security threshold breaches are impact indicator. Detecting lockout spikes helps identify brute-force campaigns and assess security control effectiveness.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track account lockout/suspension events and identify clusters (multiple accounts locked in short window). Correlate lockout timestamp with spike in failed-authentication events. Log the account owner notified, suspension trigger threshold, and unlock actions taken. Escalate if pattern indicates coordinated mass-lockout attack.

suggestion.title: Verification Code Generation Rate Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'verification codes for legitimate account owners to register new devices' sent during attack. High-rate code generation or MFA code request spikes indicate attackers triggering legitimate verification workflows to enumerate accounts or prepare device registration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor rate of verification code generation per account per hour. Alert on >10 codes generated without user-initiated action or support ticket in 60 minutes. Block account temporarily after 3 consecutive failed verification attempts to prevent account enumeration and device registration abuse.

suggestion.title: praisonai-platform: API authorization bypass — member role adding owners
suggestion.rationale: Article states endpoint is 'gated only by `require_workspace_member(workspace_id)` (default `min_role="member"`) and forwards the request body's `user_id` and `role` straight into `MemberService.add(workspace_id, user_id, role)`, which has no caller-permission check.' This describes a missing authorization check. Detection should trigger when a user with 'member' role attempts to modify role or permissions (not owner role). Direct detection of the authorization bypass, not just the exploitation
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for API requests to /workspaces/*/members where the authenticated user's current role is 'member' and the request attempts to grant 'owner' or elevated role to any target user. Authorization bypass should trigger on role-elevation attempts by insufficiently-privileged accounts regardless of success status.

suggestion.title: praisonai-platform: Bulk owner escalation — multiple role-grant requests per session
suggestion.rationale: Article describes privilege escalation mechanism but does not address persistence tactic. Attacker would likely add multiple owner accounts in rapid succession to establish backdoors. Missing detection for 'multiple POST /workspaces/*/members role=owner from same src/user within short window', which is a hallmark of account-takeover campaigns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when a single authenticated user or source IP generates 3+ successful POST /workspaces/*/members requests with role=owner within a 5-minute window. Bulk-addition is a strong signal of adversarial account-takeover vs. legitimate onboarding workflow.

suggestion.title: praisonai-platform: Post-escalation account hardening — owner-grant followed by credential/auth changes
suggestion.rationale: UC_34_3 detects identity-swap (grant + login) but does not capture the next step: real account compromise involves securing the stolen account via password change, 2FA addition, or API-key generation. Missing detection for: owner grant → login from new account → immediate password/2FA/key-management API calls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful POST /workspaces/*/members (owner grant) with subsequent password-change, 2FA-modification, or API-key-generation API calls from the newly-granted account within 15 minutes. This pattern indicates actual account takeover vs. benign role management.

suggestion.title: praisonai-platform: Workspace enumeration + member list harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Article describes cross-tenant member injection risk but does not address reconnaissance phase. Before exploiting, attacker must either be invited to a workspace or gain initial member access. Missing detection for enumeration of workspaces and bulk-retrieval of member lists via GET /workspaces/ or GET /workspaces/*/members.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on GET /workspaces/* requests that retrieve large result sets (member lists with 10+ users) or repeated sequential workspace-enumeration requests from a single source. May indicate attacker mapping the target organization's workspace structure and role hierarchy before escalation.

suggestion.title: Malicious JavaScript Injection Pattern (t.js) Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes the attack vector: 'a JavaScript injection following the t.js?site=<id> pattern, where <id> is a unique value assigned to each compromised website.' This is the primary mechanism redirecting visitors from legitimate sites to malware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP responses containing 't.js?site=' pattern in JavaScript payloads or query parameters. Correlate injected-script execution with subsequent HTTP redirects to malware infrastructure. Flag cases where legitimate domains unexpectedly serve scripts matching zTDS patterns.

suggestion.title: Fake Browser Update Prompt and Executable Download
suggestion.rationale: Article details FakeUpdates for multiple browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari, Opera, Brave, Yandex, Vivaldi, Samsung, UC Browser) and cites specific indicator: 'a fake Firefox update that downloaded a ZIP archive containing multiple DLLs and a malicious executable named Browser Update.exe.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect browser processes downloading .zip or .exe files from non-official update URLs. Monitor for file creation of 'Browser Update.exe' or similar executable names in user directories post-download. Flag browser popups that claim to prompt for updates but originate from non-browser-vendor domains.
