suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect vitest process spawned with --ui or --browser combined with --api.host or api.host pointing to non-loopback address (excluding 127.0.0.1, localhost, ::1).

suggestion.title: Path-traversal exploit against /__vitest_attachment__ endpoint (CVE-2026-47429 PoC)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names the attack vector: 'path-traversal exploit hitting Vitest /__vitest_attachment__ endpoint'. No web-based or network-level exploitation detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt HTTP requests to /__vitest_attachment__ or /__vitest__ URIs containing path-traversal sequences (?\..\, %3F%5C..%5C, or equivalent) on ports associated with vitest.

suggestion.title: Shell spawned from vitest node.exe parent (CVE-2026-47429 RCE)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'arbitrary file can be read and executed', implying command-execution outcome. Pipeline generated no post-exploitation child-process detection for cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or scripting interpreters.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on cmd.exe, powershell.exe, pwsh.exe, cscript.exe, wscript.exe, or mshta.exe spawned from node.exe running vitest, excluding legitimate node worker child processes.

suggestion.title: Remote inbound TCP to Vitest UI port 51204 from external sources (CVE-2026-47429 delivery)
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes network exposure ('exposed to the network') as the attack delivery prerequisite. No network-based delivery-phase detection for non-loopback inbound connections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound TCP connections to port 51204 originating from non-loopback sources (excluding 127.0.0.1, ::1, 0.0.0.0, 127.0.0.0/8) where destination process is vitest.

suggestion.title: Windows file-discovery from vitest node.exe (CVE-2026-47429 Windows-specific file-read)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Arbitrary file can be read on Windows when Vitest UI server is listening' — Windows-specific discovery/access technique. No file-system discovery detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file-read operations initiated from node.exe running vitest targeting sensitive Windows directories (/Windows, /System32) or demonstrating parent-directory traversal patterns (..\..).

suggestion.title: Suspicious JavaScript Injection Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'a JavaScript injection following the 't.js?site=<id>' pattern, where <id> is a unique value assigned to each compromised website.' This is a highly specific, detectable indicator of TDS redirection infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web logs and proxy logs for HTTP requests to domains matching the pattern 't.js?site=*' or similar variations. Correlate with redirects to known malware infrastructure. On-host detection: flag JavaScript injection attempts that load external scripts with site identifiers, particularly on compromised web properties.

suggestion.title: Fake Browser Update Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'Downloads a ZIP archive containing multiple DLLs and a malicious executable named 'Browser Update.exe'.' This is a directly observable executable name that bypasses typical browser update mechanisms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process execution where the image name is 'Browser Update.exe', 'browser_update.exe', or similar variants, especially when launched from %TEMP%, %APPDATA%, or Downloads directories. Correlate with recent ZIP extractions or HTTP downloads of suspicious archives. Browser processes (Chrome, Firefox, Edge) should not spawn child processes with these names.

suggestion.title: ClickFix PowerShell Command Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'ClickFix attacks involve PowerShell commands.' Users are social-engineered into copying and executing malicious PowerShell one-liners. These often contain obfuscation, unusual parameter combinations, or encoded payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PowerShell process creation with encoded payloads (EncodedCommand flags), unusual download-execute patterns (DownloadFile, IEX, Invoke-WebRequest piped to execution), or clipboard-related operations. Flag one-liners pasted from user input or executed via cmd /c immediately after user interaction.

suggestion.title: Archive-to-Executable Deployment Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'fake Firefox update that downloaded a ZIP archive containing multiple DLLs and a malicious executable.' This two-stage pattern (archive download → extract → execute) is characteristic of malware distribution via fake updates.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate ZIP file downloads from non-standard sources (especially redirected traffic) with immediate archive extraction and child process spawning from extraction directories. Flag when executables within extracted archives have names mimicking legitimate software (e.g., 'Browser Update.exe', 'Update.exe', 'setup.exe') or when DLL files are written alongside executables in temp directories.

suggestion.title: macOS Clipboard Hijacking via JavaScript Payload
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'researchers discovered an obfuscated JavaScript payload specifically designed to target macOS desktop systems, delivered via verification-themed ClickFix attacks that hijack the clipboard.' This is a direct observable on macOS endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious clipboard access from web browsers or unexpected processes, especially when preceded by obfuscated JavaScript execution. On macOS, alert when processes read clipboard contents multiple times in rapid succession or when browser-based clipboard access is followed by command execution via Terminal or shell invocation.

suggestion.title: Compromised Website Visitor Profiling and Redirect
suggestion.rationale: Article explains: 'Visitors of compromised websites are redirected through a Traffic Distribution System (TDS) known as zTDS, which profiles them and determines whether a FakeUpdates or a ClickFix lure is more appropriate.' This describes the initial compromise and profiling stage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify when legitimate websites redirect to unexpected domains, especially through chain redirects. Monitor for inconsistent User-Agent handling, device fingerprinting queries (screen resolution, OS version, browser type in URL parameters), or redirect logic that branches based on system profiling. Detect when zTDS infrastructure domains appear in redirect chains from reputable sites.

suggestion.title: Malicious npm Package Post-Install Script Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'credential-stealing worm' embedded in npm packages—this implies malicious post-install scripts (postinstall, preinstall hooks in package.json). Pipeline missed the execution vector entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm/node processes spawning cmd.exe or powershell.exe immediately after npm install, especially with suspicious arguments (writing to temp, network exfil, credential access). Monitor npm cache directories and node_modules post-install behavior.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Network Exfiltration from npm-Spawned Processes
suggestion.rationale: Credential-stealing worm must exfiltrate credentials—article implies network-based C2 or exfil. Pipeline missed credential access and exfiltration phases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag network connections initiated by node.exe or child processes spawned from npm installs, especially to non-standard ports or C2 indicators. Correlate with credential access events (registry queries for stored passwords, token access).

suggestion.title: npm Package Repository Compromise—Suspicious Package Version Jump
suggestion.rationale: Article title mentions 'Red Hat npm packages' compromise—implies tampering at repository level or typosquatting. Pipeline missed supply-chain initial-access phase entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm package downloads for version anomalies (unsigned or newly-added versions from unvetted publishers), unexpected postinstall script additions in package.json, or hash mismatches vs. published checksums. Red Hat/official packages should only come from verified namespaces.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting from Installed npm Dependencies
suggestion.rationale: Malware named explicitly as 'credential-stealing'—article must describe credential access mechanism (env var theft, .npmrc stealing, SSH key access, browser storage). Pipeline missed credential access entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Node.js processes reading sensitive files (.npmrc, SSH keys, .aws/credentials, browser cookies, vault files) or accessing process environment variables (NPM_TOKEN, GIT_TOKEN, API keys). Flag access to %USERPROFILE%\.npmrc or ~/.ssh within npm install context.

suggestion.title: npm Dependency Tree Injection—Transitive Dependency Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks often use transitive dependencies (legitimate package depends on malicious dependency). Article should clarify if compromise is direct or transitive—no pipeline detection of dependency chains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Analyze npm dependency trees to detect unexpected new dependencies, version pinning changes, or dependencies from newly-created/low-reputation publishers. Compare lock files before/after for supply chain anomalies. Flag any Red Hat-signed packages with out-of-band publishers.

suggestion.title: Telegram API-Based C2 Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Telegram bot API–based external command and control (C2) mechanism that routed communication through Telegram's infrastructure rather than using direct connections.' This is the primary C2 infrastructure and observable attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTPS traffic to api.telegram.org from unexpected endpoints. Hunt for curl/wget/PowerShell execution with Telegram bot token patterns. Alert on non-standard Telegram API request rates from systems without legitimate business usage.

suggestion.title: Cobalt Strike Beacon with Custom HTTP Profiles
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Cobalt Strike profiles designed to make beacon traffic resemble legitimate web requests' as primary evasion mechanism while using a widely-detected toolkit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Cobalt Strike beaconing behavior: regular check-in intervals, characteristic HTTP response patterns, post-compromise metadata transmission timing. Profile legitimate traffic to distinguish authentic web usage from beacon patterns.

suggestion.title: Automated Active Directory Discovery Orchestration
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'an automated Active Directory (AD) discovery panel' where 'AD discovery is driven by collecting observations from completed tasks and selecting the next action from predefined choices'—programmatic enumeration via agents.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid-fire LDAP queries or Get-AD* cmdlet execution from Python/Go/Rust processes without human interaction delays. Alert on sequential domain trust, GPO, and group membership enumeration executed within seconds—anomalous velocity for manual discovery.

suggestion.title: Process Injection into Legitimate Executables
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Python-based malware development scripts for injecting shellcode into legitimate Windows executables while preserving original functionality.' The preserved legitimate behavior masks the malicious code execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag suspicious parent-child relationships where system binaries exhibit injection patterns (CreateRemoteThread, WriteProcessMemory). Monitor for image-integrity violations or unsigned DLL loads in protected process contexts. Alert on mismatches between declared and runtime process behavior.

suggestion.title: Multi-Layer Encryption and Evasion Stacking
suggestion.rationale: Article describes payloads with 'layers of encryption, evasion, and alternative execution techniques' tested against 70+ techniques across 80 modules—iterative obfuscation defeating detection across multiple EDR platforms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for high-entropy process memory (encrypted payloads). Alert on execution from temp/user-writable paths. Flag syscall alternatives or API hook detours. Detect repeated binary-loading failures indicative of EDR callback evasion attempts.

suggestion.title: Cloudflare Worker as C2 Front-End Redirector
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'Cloudflare Worker acting as a front-end redirector to obscure the actual backend C2 server'—infrastructure obfuscation leveraging legitimate CDN services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS and HTTPS traffic to *.workers.dev domains. Correlate Workers traffic originating from unexpected internal systems. Alert on traffic exhibiting C2-like patterns (regular beaconing, command-response cycles) despite legitimate CDN characteristics.

suggestion.title: Outbound to Cloud Service Providers — Suspicious Process Context
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers 'weaponizing trusted cloud infrastructure, including Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure, Cloudflare' to 'sustain long-lived Command and Control (C2) operations.' Detectable via process-to-destination anomalies: non-development processes (svchost, explorer, rundll32) initiating TLS connections to CDN ASNs or cloud provider IPs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for outbound connections from suspicious process contexts to Cloudflare, AWS CloudFront, Google Cloud, or Azure CDN IP ranges. Establish baseline for legitimate cloud usage per process; alert on anomalies. Supplement with certificate fingerprinting to detect traffic masquerading as legitimate cloud services.

suggestion.title: DNS Tunneling via Public Resolvers
suggestion.rationale: MITRE technique T1071.004 (DNS protocol) is explicitly listed. Article's emphasis on 'hiding malicious traffic' via 'trusted' infrastructure suggests DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH) covert channel to public resolvers (Cloudflare 1.1.1.1, Google 8.8.8.8) or DNS tunneling via subdomain queries to attacker-controlled domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect persistent DNS queries to unusual or newly-registered subdomains under legitimate domains, or abnormal query volume from a single host. Alert on HTTPS connections to 1.1.1.1:443, 8.8.8.8:443 from non-browser processes—indicative of DoH tunnel.

suggestion.title: GitHub API / Repository Access for Exfiltration or C2
suggestion.rationale: Article names GitHub explicitly among abused services. GitHub's API and webhook system are viable channels for C2 tasking and data exfil. Detectable via HTTPS POST/GET to api.github.com or github.com from suspicious process sources or unusual payload sizes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline legitimate GitHub usage (developers, CI/CD agents). Alert on HTTPS connections to github.com or api.github.com from processes outside development context (cmd.exe, powershell, notepad). Correlate with large POST requests (exfil) or periodic GET intervals (C2 polling).

suggestion.title: Cloud Infrastructure Reconnaissance and Persistence Setup
suggestion.rationale: For 'sustained long-lived C2 operations,' attackers must acquire or pivot through cloud infrastructure—requiring enumeration of cloud APIs and credentials. Detectable via unusual API calls to AWS STS, Azure AD, or GCP IAM from non-standard tool processes; or DNS lookups to cloud registrars.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor CloudTrail for API calls to credential retrieval (GetSessionToken, AssumeRole) from unusual principals or at unusual hours. Cross-correlate with subsequent CreateInstance or CreateDBInstance calls. Alert on failed enumeration attempts (repeated 401/403 responses to cloud APIs).

suggestion.title: TLS Certificate / SNI Mismatch Masquerading
suggestion.rationale: Article's T1027 (Obfuscated Files or Information) extends to traffic obfuscation. Attackers can mask C2 destinations by spoofing certificate subjects or using SNI mismatch—legitimate Cloudflare/AWS/GCP certificates but traffic sent to attacker-controlled backend. Detectable via certificate pinning validation or SNI anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Collect TLS handshake metadata (certificate subject, issuer, SNI hostname). Alert when SNI hostname does not match certificate subject (e.g., SNI=internal-staging.local but cert=*.cloudflare-cdn.com). Correlate mismatches with outbound traffic to known-malicious IP space.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated Payload over Legitimate Service Encryption
suggestion.rationale: T1027 (Obfuscated Files or Information) is marked. Beyond network-level obfuscation, payloads themselves may be encrypted or encoded within HTTPS streams to legitimate services, defeating content inspection. Detectable via statistical entropy anomalies or traffic pattern deviations from legitimate tool baselines.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline entropy and size distribution of legitimate cloud service traffic (Cloudflare, AWS, Azure). Alert on outbound HTTPS traffic to these providers with anomalously high entropy, unusual packet size distributions, or patterns inconsistent with browser/API client behavior—potential obfuscated payloads.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-0257 exploitation payload detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'being actively leveraged in real-world attacks'—requires hunt for characteristic exploitation attempts; direct signal of ongoing compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PAN-OS management ports (443, 8081) for HTTP requests with CVE-2026-0257 exploitation patterns; correlate failed auth followed by successful privileged action within 5 minutes as indicator of successful bypass.

suggestion.title: PAN-OS admin account creation post-exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacks are 'actively leveraged'—persistent remote access requires backdoor account creation, standard post-exploitation step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on new admin-privilege user accounts created on PAN-OS devices within 2 hours of exploitation window, especially outside scheduled change-control windows.

suggestion.title: Firewall rule disablement or modification on exploited appliances
suggestion.rationale: Article: attackers 'actively leveraged' flaw—post-compromise defense evasion typically involves disabling threat prevention; requires hunt for suspicious config changes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track PAN-OS security-policy modifications: rules whitelisting attacker infrastructure, threat-prevention disablement, or allow-all rules outside maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: Network beaconing to IOC IP addresses
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Network connections to article IPs / domains'—the six listed IPs (104.207.144.154, 146.19.216.119, etc.) are C2 or staging infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from PAN-OS appliances to 104.207.144.154, 146.19.216.119, 146.19.216.120, 146.19.216.125, 209.99.191.137, 79.130.26.202 across all ports; high-confidence post-exploitation signal.

suggestion.title: Failed authentication spike preceding successful admin actions
suggestion.rationale: Article: vulnerability 'enables attackers to bypass authentication mechanisms'—pattern is multiple failed attempts followed by successful privileged activity without successful login.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect 5+ failed auth attempts to PAN-OS management interface followed by successful admin API calls or config changes within 10 minutes, zero successful login in between.

suggestion.title: T3/IIOP Protocol Activity to WebLogic Ports
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated attacker with network access via T3, IIOP to compromise Oracle WebLogic Server.' T3 (default port 7001-7002) and IIOP are the direct attack vectors; network traffic on these protocols to WebLogic endpoints is a high-fidelity exploitation signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for inbound T3 protocol traffic (port 7001-7002) or IIOP protocol connections to systems running Oracle WebLogic. Unauthenticated T3 connections are highly suspicious given the vulnerability requires no authentication. Correlate with asset inventory to identify WebLogic endpoints.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Oracle WebLogic Version Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerable versions 12.2.1.4.0 and 14.1.1.0.0. 'Shodan now tracks over 1,592 Oracle WebLogic servers exposed online and vulnerable.' Detection requires knowing which processes are running vulnerable versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query software inventory and process telemetry to identify Oracle WebLogic instances running versions 12.2.1.4.0 or 14.1.1.0.0. Flag any process with these versions as immediately exploitable. Cross-reference with network egress to identify potential command-and-control or data exfiltration.

suggestion.title: CVE-2024-21182 Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article confirms 'actively exploited in attacks' and mandates patching by CISA 'Binding Operational Directive.' Exploit patterns for this RCE should be detectable in request logs or network streams.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WebLogic application and access logs for T3 protocol requests with payloads typical of CVE-2024-21182 serialization exploits. Look for abnormal command or script execution initiated by WebLogic service accounts immediately following network T3 activity.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Data Access from WebLogic Processes
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in unauthorized access to critical data or complete access to all Oracle WebLogic Server accessible data.' Post-RCE data exfiltration from WebLogic must be detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on WebLogic service account accessing or reading large volumes of sensitive files or databases post-exploitation. Detect unusual child processes spawned by WebLogic (sqlplus, powershell, curl) attempting data dump, compression, or exfiltration to external IP addresses.

suggestion.title: WebLogic Port Scanning and Service Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Attackers must discover and fingerprint vulnerable WebLogic instances before exploitation. Article implies reconnaissance via protocol-specific scanning to identify targets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for repeated connection attempts to ports 7001-7002 (T3) or 3700+ (IIOP) from external sources. Detect patterns consistent with nmap, Shodan-like enumeration, or manual port scanning targeting WebLogic infrastructure. Correlate source IPs against threat feeds.

suggestion.title: CISA BOD 22-01 Compliance Violation: Unpatched WebLogic
suggestion.rationale: Article mandates 'CISA ordered federal agencies to patch their WebLogic servers by midnight on Thursday, June 4.' Post-deadline, any vulnerable version running is a direct compliance breach.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset management and vulnerability scan results to identify any Oracle WebLogic 12.2.1.4.0 or 14.1.1.0.0 instances still running post-remediation deadline (June 4). Flag for immediate incident response and compliance audit.

suggestion.title: CVE-2022-0492 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2022-0492 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and references standard asset-exposure hunt templates. Pipeline generated zero UCs despite clear instruction to substitute this CVE into template detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag all assets matching CVE-2022-0492 in vulnerability scanner output. Prioritize internet-exposed Linux systems. Cross-correlate with patch-inventory systems to identify remediation lag.

suggestion.title: cgroups v1 release_agent Privilege Escalation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article describes specific attack surface: 'privilege escalation via the cgroups v1 release_agent feature.' This is the kernel-level abuse mechanism but was not mapped to any detection hypothesis or kill-chain phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes accessing cgroup release_agent files (typically in /sys/fs/cgroup/*/release_agent or /proc/*/cgroup). Flag unexpected cgroup manipulation, especially from unprivileged processes. Correlate with container/namespace context.

suggestion.title: CVE-2022-0492 Kernel Exploitation (cgroup Container Escape)
suggestion.rationale: Article implies container/cgroup context but pipeline did not establish detection for escape patterns. Relevant for containerized environments where cgroups enforcement is security boundary.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In Kubernetes/Docker environments, alert on processes exceeding their assigned cgroup limits or escaping container namespaces. Flag unexpected UID/GID privilege transitions correlated with cgroup manipulation.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Android Framework Devices — Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in [...] asset-exposure hunt' and emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer.' Pipeline generated zero UCs despite direct guidance on how to hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability management and asset inventory systems for Android devices vulnerable to CVE-2025-48595. Cross-reference patching status against federal due date (2026-06-05). Escalate any unpatched externally-facing Android devices as critical.

suggestion.title: Android Framework Integer Overflow Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'code execution' resulting from 'integer overflow vulnerability' but pipeline captures only T1190 without detection hypothesis for the actual exploitation payload or memory corruption indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Android Framework process logs and kernel audit trails for integer overflow exceptions, abnormal memory access patterns, or crafted input sequences targeting vulnerable code path. Correlate with unexpected code execution or process spawning from Framework context.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Privilege Escalation Following Framework Exploit
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'could allow for local privilege escalation' as final impact. Kill chain reconstruction was empty and no UC proposed for detecting privilege escalation post-code-execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect uid/gid changes, capability escalation, SELinux policy violations, or root-owned process spawning from untrusted Framework-spawned process context.

suggestion.title: Brute Force Attack on Password Vault Service
suggestion.rationale: Article headline explicitly states 'Brute-Force Attack'. Pipeline should map T1110 (Brute Force) variants and detect multiple failed authentication attempts in a short window against Dashlane or similar vault services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect repeated failed login attempts from single or multiple IPs targeting Dashlane user accounts within a narrow timeframe. Alert on 5+ failed authentications per user in 10 minutes, or 20+ distinct failed authentication events from single source IP in 15 minutes, with subsequent successful login from different geography or device.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Encryption Vault Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Headline specifies 'Encrypted Vaults of Fewer Than 20 Users Downloaded'. Pipeline should detect anomalous bulk data access or export of vault contents, even if encrypted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unusual download volume from vault-storage endpoints, retrieval of multiple encrypted vault containers in single session, or exfiltration of vault metadata (timing, structure) even if payload is encrypted. Baseline per-user vault access patterns and flag >3σ deviations.

suggestion.title: Credential Stuffing or Password Spray Against Dashlane
suggestion.rationale: Brute-force disclosure context suggests automated credential-testing attack (T1110.003 or T1110.001). Pipeline should surface detection for credential-reuse patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect spray pattern: many user accounts targeted from same source IP with same or similar passwords in short window (e.g., 50+ unique user targets from 1 IP in 30 minutes). Correlate with password-breach datasets (have-i-been-pwned, public leaks) to confirm credential-reuse attack.

suggestion.title: WinRAR CVE-2025-8088 Path Traversal Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'weaponization of CVE-2025-8088, a path traversal flaw in WinRAR, to launch an HTML Application payload.' No detection logic captured this initial access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WinRAR process spawning unusual child processes (rundll32, mshta, wscript). Detect extraction of .hta files from malicious RAR archives. Alert on WinRAR accessing path traversal sequences (..\) in archive listings.

suggestion.title: GammaPhish HTML Application Execution from User Temp/Downloads
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'HTML Application payload dubbed GammaPhish' as first-stage dropper. Typical attack flow: .hta file extracted and executed via mshta.exe.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect mshta.exe execution with .hta file from user-writable paths (Downloads, Temp, AppData). Alert on mshta spawning cmd.exe or wscript.exe children. Look for parent process WinRAR → mshta chain.

suggestion.title: VBScript Downloader (GammaLoad) Network Callbacks
suggestion.rationale: Article details 'intermediate Visual Basic Script (VBScript) downloaders codenamed GammaLoad' used to retrieve payloads. No UC captures VBScript-initiated network IOC callbacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on cscript.exe or wscript.exe making HTTP/HTTPS connections, especially to newly registered domains or IP addresses. Detect VBScript-spawned processes downloading and executing additional binaries.

suggestion.title: Scheduled Task Persistence via VBScript (GammaWorm)
suggestion.rationale: Article states GammaWorm 'establishes persistence via scheduled tasks.' Pipeline missed this critical persistence mechanism, a standard MITRE T1053 indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor schtasks.exe spawned by wscript.exe or cscript.exe. Alert on scheduled task creation with VBScript payloads or unusual run times. Correlate with process parent chain including mshta or rundll32.

suggestion.title: Telegram API Calls for Command & Control
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly notes GammaWorm 'uses legitimate platforms like Telegram for C2 communication.' No IOCs or detection logic for Telegram-based C2 channels were extracted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious processes (wscript, cscript, rundll32) making HTTPS connections to Telegram API endpoints (api.telegram.org:443). Alert on decoded Telegram bot tokens in process memory or network payloads. Monitor for Telegram file download/upload patterns from non-browser processes.

suggestion.title: AWS S3 Bucket Exfiltration via GammaSteel Information Stealer
suggestion.rationale: Article describes GammaSteel 'exfiltrates them to an Amazon Web Services (AWS) S3 bucket.' No UC captures the characteristic S3 API calls (PutObject, MultipartUpload) from suspicious processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes other than AWS CLI/SDKs making authenticated HTTPS calls to s3.amazonaws.com with AWS SigV4 signatures. Alert on PUT/POST requests with large payloads to S3 endpoints from unexpected child processes. Correlate S3 activity with prior file enumeration and VBScript execution.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-48595 Android Framework RCE Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'remote escalation of privilege with no additional execution privileges needed' and 'gain code execution' via CVE-2025-48595 on Android Framework. No detection use case generated despite this being the actively exploited threat.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected privilege escalation originating from Android Framework component without user interaction or additional execution privileges. Look for abnormal process spawning from system_server or framework-privileged processes, particularly on Android 14+.

suggestion.title: Android Device Spyware Post-Exploitation Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'similar flaws have been exploited in the past by commercial spyware and by nation-state operations targeting high-profile or high-interest individuals.' Pipeline missed behavioral detection for spyware post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag exfiltration patterns and C2 communication from patched Android devices post-exploitation. Monitor for covert tunneling or unusual inter-process communication (IPC) between framework components and background services.

suggestion.title: Qualcomm Display Driver Exploitation Chain (CVE-2026-21385)
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions separate zero-day in Qualcomm display component with 'limited, targeted exploitation.' No use case generated for this distinct attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal access to Qualcomm display driver interfaces or memory-mapped I/O regions. Flag privilege escalation attempts originating from display rendering processes.

suggestion.title: Targeted Attack Pattern: Limited Exploitation of Framework Zero-Days
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'indications that CVE-2025-48595 may be under limited, targeted exploitation' and mentions targeting of 'high-profile or high-interest individuals.' Pipeline failed to flag the narrow-targeting behavioral signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on spear-phishing or watering-hole campaigns targeting high-profile individuals or executives with Android devices. Correlate device patch status (Android 14+) with targeted messaging or malicious app delivery.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Android 14+ Device Inventory Gap
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability affects 'Android 14 or later' and notes exploitation difficulty 'enhancements in newer versions.' Pipeline did not surface asset-inventory or patch-compliance detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Generate alerts for unpatched Android 14+ devices in corporate inventory after June 2026 patch release. Prioritize devices owned by high-value targets (C-suite, researchers, diplomats) known to be targets of commercial spyware or APT operations.

suggestion.title: Detect Exploitation Attempts Against Actively Exploited Android CVE
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'One Actively Exploited' — this is the highest-priority detection gap. Pipeline must surface exploitation signatures, syscall anomalies, or capability-escalation attempts tied to this flaw.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal process execution patterns, unexpected system-level capability requests, or network beacons originating from processes attempting to trigger the known-vulnerable code path. Prioritize detections from low-privileged or sandboxed app contexts.

suggestion.title: Identify Unpatched Vulnerable Android Device Versions
suggestion.rationale: Article anchors on '124 Flaws' patched in June 2026 update — pipeline must invert this to detect pre-patch device versions for immediate inventory/remediation prioritization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate active device inventory against published vulnerable Android version list and alert on any system running a pre-patch build. Critical for prioritizing patch deployment.

suggestion.title: Android Privilege Escalation via Framework Vulnerability
suggestion.rationale: Android security bulletins routinely include PE flaws; '124 Flaws' almost certainly includes framework/kernel privilege escalation but pipeline generated zero privilege-escalation detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected elevation from user/app context to system/root via Android framework APIs, capability-request chains, or kernel module loading patterns consistent with CVE exploitation.

suggestion.title: Malicious App Installation Exploiting Android CVEs
suggestion.rationale: Context implies attack vector of malicious apps targeting these flaws; pipeline should generate detection rules for suspicious app behavior + exploitation indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on app installations followed by suspicious permission escalation, sensor access (camera/location), or system-level API abuse within minutes of install — hallmark of immediate post-install exploitation.

suggestion.title: Wasted Exploitation Attempts Post-Patch Deployment
suggestion.rationale: As devices patch, attackers waste attempts on already-fixed code; pipeline should flag exploitation attempts on confirmed-patched Android builds to track attacker lag.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect exploitation signatures or syscall anomalies on systems confirmed running June 2026 or later patch; filter via device version and timestamp to minimize FP. Valuable signal for measuring attacker operational tempo.

suggestion.title: Composer Package Hash Mismatch Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Every Tag Across Multiple Composer Packages Rewritten'—indicates malicious modification of package artifacts. Pipeline should detect when installed package hashes diverge from published lockfile or package registry metadata.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In CI/build environments, detect package installation where computed hash of installed artifact differs from expected hash in composer.lock or package.json. Monitor for downloads of versioned packages where SHA256 mismatches repository metadata.

suggestion.title: CI Environment Variable Exfiltration via Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states objective is to 'Steal CI Secrets.' Malicious package code would read and transmit secrets (GitHub tokens, AWS keys, deploy credentials) during install-time execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: During composer install/update, detect child processes spawned by PHP/Composer that access environment variables (reading CI_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, AWS_SECRET, etc.) and establish outbound HTTPS connections to non-whitelisted domains outside primary package registries.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Outbound Connections from Package Installation Phase
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks exfiltrate secrets over C2. Article describes theft mechanism but pipeline missed detection for anomalous network activity during the install phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP/HTTPS POST requests initiated by PHP interpreter or Composer process during package installation phase targeting domains not in whitelist (i.e., not packagist.org, github.com, gitlab.com, or known CDNs). Flag requests with Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded or JSON containing suspicious variable names.

suggestion.title: Package Repository Account Compromise Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates attacker rewrote tags across multiple packages, implying either account takeover of maintainers or repository access. Should detect abnormal login patterns or token usage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect login to Packagist/GitHub/GitLab accounts from unusual geographic locations or IP ranges compared to baseline. Identify API tokens used to push package versions from non-CI systems. Flag cases where package tags are created/modified without associated CI/CD pipeline execution or code review approval.

suggestion.title: Unexpected PHP Code Execution During Composer Install
suggestion.rationale: Composer allows arbitrary PHP execution via scripts defined in composer.json. Malicious packages would leverage this. Article doesn't detail mechanism but supply chain attacks commonly abuse install-time hooks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of PHP scripts from package vendor/ directories during composer install that were not whitelisted. Flag execution of scripts defined in composer.json 'scripts' section that spawn shells, make network calls, or read environment variables.

suggestion.title: Mass Package Version Rollback or Inconsistent Tag History
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'Every Tag Across Multiple Composer Packages Rewritten,' indicating attacker modified historical releases. Should detect impossible version histories or cryptographic signature failures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query package repository metadata: detect when multiple tags of the same package have identical or near-identical modification timestamps, or when GPG signature verification fails after previously passing. Alert on annotated tags being reassigned to different commits.

suggestion.title: Git credential exposure in CI/CD logs and build artifacts
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly references 'Securing code...across the development lifecycle' and keywords include GitHub. If article discusses credential management in pipelines, no detection use cases exist for token/key leakage in commit history, build logs, or artifact metadata.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor git and CI/CD tool processes (GitHub Actions, Azure Pipelines) for operations exfiltrating or committing secrets. Detect when build logs, environment variables, or artifact tags expose API keys, tokens, or certificates.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized AI model/agent deployment from untrusted source
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly includes 'agents and models' (Microsoft Agent 365). No detection hypotheses despite agent execution representing supply-chain and code-injection risk in development workflows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag execution or import of AI agents/models from non-canonical package sources, unsigned model weights, or agents executing shell/script commands outside sandboxed contexts.

suggestion.title: Development-to-production environment lateral movement
suggestion.rationale: Lifecycle security spans multiple tiers (dev, staging, prod). Article mentions securing across 'development lifecycle' but no detection for privilege escalation or lateral movement from development to production credentials or systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for service account or developer identity authentication across environment tiers. Alert on credentials issued in dev tier being used to access prod resources, or on build agents assuming production-scoped IAM roles.

suggestion.title: VS Code Extension Process Spawning Suspicious Child Processes
suggestion.rationale: Compromised extensions execute code in user's IDE context and typically spawn shells or binaries to exfiltrate data or establish persistence. Title establishes extension compromise but no detection use case for process execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child processes spawned by Code.exe or known VS Code extension processes (especially PowerShell, cmd.exe, curl, wget). Compromised extensions often shell out to steal environment variables, SSH keys, or .git credentials. Baseline normal extensions first; alert on anomalies.

suggestion.title: Sensitive File Access from VS Code Extension Context
suggestion.rationale: Extension compromises target developer credential stores and source code. Detection gap for suspicious file access (SSH keys, .aws, tokens, .git/config) from extension runtime.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on access to high-value paths (.ssh, .aws, AppData/Local/GitHub, npm config, .kube) by processes spawned from or associated with Code.exe. Cross-reference with network events to detect exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Network Egress from VS Code Process
suggestion.rationale: Compromised extension likely exfiltrates code or credentials over HTTP/HTTPS to attacker-controlled domain. No detection for outbound network activity from IDE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound HTTPS/HTTP connections from Code.exe or extension subprocesses to non-Microsoft, non-GitHub, non-npm domains. Flag connections to suspicious IPs or domains not previously observed in the organization.

suggestion.title: VS Code Configuration or Extension Manifest Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Persistence may involve modifying VS Code settings.json, launch.json, or extension metadata. Article title indicates compromise but no detection for config modifications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected modifications to .vscode/settings.json, .vscode/launch.json, or extension manifest files within user home directories. Establish baseline of expected modifications per user/team; alert on out-of-band changes.

suggestion.title: Extension Installation from Non-Official Sources or Unexpected Versions
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain compromise requires initial installation of malicious extension. Detection gap for marketplace or sideloading of unsigned/unexpected extensions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor VS Code extension directory (%USERPROFILE%/.vscode/extensions on Windows) for new installations or version changes. Cross-reference installed extension versions against known-good hashes or official marketplace metadata; alert on mismatches or installation from local/private sources.

suggestion.title: Credential Theft via Environment Variable or Token Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Compromised IDE extension runs in developer's context and can steal GITHUB_TOKEN, AWS_ACCESS_KEY, or other secrets from environment. Article premise establishes risk but no detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous reads of environment variables or config files containing tokens (GitHub, npm, AWS). Monitor for access to ~/.ssh, ~/.bash_history, or .env files from Code.exe subprocesses. Correlate with outbound network activity to suspicious domains.

suggestion.title: Malvertising Campaign: Drive-by Deployment Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'malvertising campaign targeting macOS users' and distribution of backdoor payload through ads—establishes T1189 drive-by compromise as initial access vector. No UC generated for this phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for download of unsigned executables or suspicious ZIP archives from ad-serving domains or unexpected secondary domains. Correlate with browser process execution and subsequent unsigned binary launch within seconds of ad click.

suggestion.title: Flutter-Based Malware Execution: Process and Library Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Malware is 'built using the Flutter framework'—distinctive execution signature (Flutter runtime, Dart VM, framework-specific libraries) should be detectable. No execution-phase UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unsigned Flutter or Dart runtime binaries executing outside expected app directories (/Applications). Monitor for suspicious library loads from non-standard paths (libflutter.so, libapp.so) combined with unexpected child processes or network connections.

suggestion.title: macOS Backdoor Persistence: Launchd/Cron Configuration Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'backdoor' with no details on persistence mechanism, but backdoors require staying resident—macOS-specific persistence via plist, launchd, or cron highly likely given target platform.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation or modification of ~/Library/LaunchAgents/*.plist, /Library/LaunchDaemons/*.plist, or crontab entries from newly-downloaded app bundles. Correlate with suspicious parent process (installer, downloader) and validate plist references legitimate vs. obfuscated binary paths.

suggestion.title: C2 Beaconing from FlutterShell Backdoor
suggestion.rationale: Backdoor with no C2 indicators extracted despite 'distributed' malware implying command infrastructure. Network communication pattern detection essential for backdoor families.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound HTTPS/HTTP from unsigned Flutter-based executables to non-standard ports or newly-registered domains. Identify periodic beaconing patterns (e.g., every 5-60 min) from suspicious process; correlate with malware delivery timeline.

suggestion.title: Unsigned or Self-Signed Binary Installation from Downloads Folder
suggestion.rationale: macOS malvertising typically delivers unsigned binaries disguised as legitimate apps. 'Operation FlutterBridge spreads FlutterShell backdoor' via downloads—gating on code signature validation is critical gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ~/Downloads for executable files lacking valid Apple developer signature. Alert when unsigned binary is executed or moved to /Applications. Correlate timing with browser history and ad/malvertising campaign indicators.

suggestion.title: Malicious JAR Download from SEO-Poisoned Domain
suggestion.rationale: Article states '240 distribution URLs' and '3,820 unique malicious JAR files' distributed via 'SEO poisoning promoting them.' No detection for JAR execution from non-official sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for JAR file downloads from domains matching Minecraft client names (Meteor, Radium, Wurst, LiquidBounce, etc.) that do NOT resolve to official GitHub or project domains. Correlate file hash against known malicious JAR SHA-256 signatures from campaign telemetry.

suggestion.title: Credential Extraction from Browser Profile Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies '36 browsers' targeted for password/cookie theft and '56 cryptocurrency add-ons.' No detection for credential access from local browser stores post-infection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag processes spawned by or child of java.exe or javaw.exe accessing browser credential stores (Chrome/Edge/Firefox roaming profiles, Local AppData secrets), cryptocurrency wallet directories, or Discord/Steam/Telegram token caches.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Wallet and Add-on Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Campaign targets '12 desktop cryptocurrency wallet apps' and '56 cryptocurrency add-ons.' Detection gap for reconnaissance of wallet software or browser extension enumeration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for enumeration of cryptocurrency wallet directories (Ledger, Trezor, Exodus, MetaMask AppData folders) or browser extension manifests by processes spawned from Minecraft installation paths or downloaded JAR archives.

suggestion.title: C2 Dashboard Registration and Exfiltration to MaaS Platform
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'MaaS operation...platform is hosted on the clear net...provides access to anyone.' No use case for detecting outbound connections to WeedHack dashboard or stolen data transmission.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP POST requests from compromised endpoints to known WeedHack C2 domains with JSON payloads containing stolen credential data (session IDs, cookie exfiltration format) or requests to /dashboard, /api/victims, /api/payload endpoints.

suggestion.title: Premium Tier Malware Capability Activation (Webcam, Keylogger, Remote Shell)
suggestion.rationale: Article notes premium tier features: 'webcam access, keylogger, remote shell, and remote file management.' No detection for unusual camera device access or shell process spawning from Minecraft context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on attempts to open video capture devices (/dev/video*, usb:vid_* webcam PIDs) from Minecraft or child processes. Monitor for cmd.exe/powershell.exe spawned with parent java.exe or JAR file name. Flag keyboard input capture APIs called from injected DLLs in browser or system processes.

suggestion.title: YouTube Download Link Extraction and JAR Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'drops download links in descriptions and comments' on YouTube videos with '7,500+ views.' Gap in detecting downloads from YouTube video metadata or direct JAR execution post-download.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate DeviceNetworkEvents showing YouTube domain visits followed by JAR file downloads to temp directories and immediate execution (java -jar). Alert if JAR hash is not signed by official Minecraft or mod project certificate.

suggestion.title: Xeno RAT Process Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names Xeno RAT as deployed malware. No process-based or behavioral detection was generated for the RAT's execution despite this being the core post-compromise indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of Xeno RAT binary or obfuscated scripts spawned by Office macros. Look for process chains where Office applications (winword.exe, excel.exe) spawn cmd.exe, PowerShell, or direct executable execution with encoded arguments or C2 callbacks.

suggestion.title: Macro-Enabled Office Attachment Execution
suggestion.rationale: SideCopy's primary attack vector is spear-phishing with macro-enabled attachments (established actor TTP). Article does not appear to contain countermeasures-focused detection rules for this initial execution vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Office macro execution originating from recently-downloaded or email-staged files. Flag Word/Excel enabling macros, especially when followed by spawning of unsigned executables, script interpreters, or registry modifications.

suggestion.title: Xeno RAT C2 Beaconing Detection
suggestion.rationale: RAT deployment requires persistent command-and-control communication. No network-layer detection for C2 callbacks was generated despite this being a continuous post-compromise indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP/HTTPS traffic from Finance Ministry hosts exhibiting periodic beaconing patterns, especially to newly-registered or known Xeno RAT C2 domains. Detect large data transfers over C2 channels and DNS requests for malware-associated domains.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Registry Run Keys
suggestion.rationale: Xeno RAT establishes persistence mechanisms to survive reboots. No persistence-layer detection for registry modifications or scheduled tasks was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious modifications to HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run or equivalent system-wide persistence mechanisms, especially when written by Office processes, PowerShell, or unsigned utilities. Correlate with malware-staging directories.

suggestion.title: Bulk Data Collection and Staging
suggestion.rationale: Attack on Afghanistan Finance Ministry implies objective of data exfiltration. No detection for archive creation, mass file reads, or data staging was generated despite this being the logical final attack phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk creation of archive files (.zip, .rar, .7z) by unexpected processes, especially originating from Finance-department shares or NTFS alternate data streams. Monitor for sequential reads of financial documents followed by immediate network transfers.

suggestion.title: Spear-Phishing Email Detection for Financial Targets
suggestion.rationale: SideCopy's documented TTP is targeted spear-phishing of government and financial entities. No email-borne malware or social-engineering detection was generated for the initial-access vector despite it being the documented attack entry point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails to Afghanistan Finance Ministry staff containing macro-enabled Office attachments, especially from spoofed or newly-registered domains. Flag emails with VBA projects, embedded objects, or OLE references typical of malware dropper campaigns.

suggestion.title: jqwik 1.10.0 Malicious Dependency Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names affected package and version: 'Package: net.jqwik:jqwik-engine Affected version: 1.10.0.' Pipeline extracted zero IOCs despite clear artifact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor dependency manifests and lockfiles for net.jqwik:jqwik-engine version 1.10.0. Query package managers and SCA logs for resolution of this package at exactly version 1.10.0 between 2026-05-25 and 2026-05-27 (pre-patch window). Correlate with build execution logs to identify projects that executed tests with the malicious JAR.

suggestion.title: ANSI Terminal Code Obfuscation in CI Logs
suggestion.rationale: Article describes technique: 'prints ESC [2K followed by a carriage return, twice... that sequence wipes the line before you can read it... But on any stream that records output as raw text instead of rendering it, those erase codes are just dead characters.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search CI/CD and test-runner logs for ANSI escape sequences ESC[2K (0x1B 5B 32 4B in hex) followed by carriage returns (0x0D). Particularly alert on sequences immediately following text containing agent-targeting language ('disregard previous instructions,' 'delete,' 'jqwik'). Baseline CI logs for normal ANSI usage and flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: Malicious Method Detection in Java Decompiled JARs
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies root cause: 'The malicious instruction lived in a new method called printMessageForCodingAgents() , inside the net.jqwik.engine.execution.JqwikExecutor class.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Decompile jqwik JARs and search for method net.jqwik.engine.execution.JqwikExecutor.printMessageForCodingAgents(). Alert on presence of this method and inspect its bytecode for prompt-injection patterns (hardcoded strings containing instruction-like content, ANSI code constants, carriage return sequences).

suggestion.title: AI Agent Rejection of Suspicious Test Output Instructions
suggestion.rationale: Article documents Claude Code's defensive response: 'In the documented field observation, Claude Code flagged the instruction on the first mvn test run, refused to act on it, and traced it back to its source in the JAR.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor agentic coding tool logs for suspicious instruction patterns in parsed test output: directives to disregard prior instructions, delete code/tests, or bypass standard workflows. Alert on agent self-rejection or anomaly flagging of such instructions. Correlate with jqwik test execution to identify exposure.

suggestion.title: File Deletion Following jqwik Test Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies intended payload: 'The payload told agents to disregard previous instructions and delete all jqwik tests and code.' and warns 'you're looking at anything from a minor annoyance to losing your source and test files with no useful audit trail.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate jqwik test execution (mvn test, gradle test) with subsequent file deletion events (rm, delete syscalls) targeting Java source files or test directories. Flag cascading deletions in the seconds following test execution completion, especially if agent processes are in the call stack.

suggestion.title: Maven Central Dependency Pull of Malicious jqwik Version
suggestion.rationale: Article describes delivery mechanism: 'On May 25, 2026, the maintainer of jqwik... released version 1.10.0 to Maven Central' and 'Any pipeline that pulled the dependency and fed test output back into an LLM agent could have triggered the prompt injection.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Maven Central repository queries for net.jqwik:jqwik-engine:1.10.0 downloads or cache hits during the May 25–May 27, 2026 window. Correlate with CI/CD execution contexts (GitHub Actions, Jenkins, Gradle daemon logs) to identify projects that resolved and used the poisoned JAR in automated builds.

suggestion.title: Preinstall hook executing unexpected subprocesses during npm install
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states payload 'fire via a preinstall hook on every npm install' but pipeline generated no detection for the hook execution itself. Preinstall hooks are the attack vector and should trigger before package code runs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm/yarn/pnpm parent processes for unexpected child process spawning during the install lifecycle. Preinstall scripts that spawn interpreters (node, bash, python) or reach network should trigger. Baseline legitimate hook behavior by package on baseline systems first.

suggestion.title: Credential harvester reading CI/CD environment variables
suggestion.rationale: Article states payload targets 'GitHub Actions secrets, AWS, GCP, Azure, Kubernetes, HashiCorp Vault, npm tokens, and CircleCI' but pipeline generated no detection use case for credential access. This is the core attack objective and should be detected at exfiltration or at read-time.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes spawned by npm/node reading sensitive environment variable patterns: AWS_*, GCP_*, VAULT_*, CIRCLECI_*, NPM_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, KUBECONFIG. Alert on env var enumeration followed by outbound network activity, or on direct access to ~/.aws, ~/.ssh, kubeconfig paths.

suggestion.title: Package installation from @redhat-cloud-services scope with anomalous version
suggestion.rationale: Article does not list 'normal' package versions, only the 32 compromised versions in the hunt; a detection for ANY @redhat-cloud-services installation event (before version blocklist) would provide real-time visibility at package pull time, not just at install execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm registry queries and package downloads from npm CDN (registry.npmjs.org) or internal mirrors for any @redhat-cloud-services/* package install attempts. Trigger on: package pull, version metadata fetch, or registry API calls from development / CI/CD infrastructure. Correlate with timestamp of article publication to identify potential infection window.

suggestion.title: npm package preinstall script writing to /tmp with obfuscated execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'sophisticated multi-stage credential harvester' and mentions obfuscation (T1027 is in the technique list). Pipeline missed detection of the obfuscated payload staging or execution, focusing only on known-hash match (UC_10_10).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm preinstall scripts writing executable or JavaScript files to /tmp or other writable locations outside node_modules. Alert on write-then-execute patterns, encoding/decoding function calls in Node.js context (atob, Buffer.from), or eval/Function constructor invocations with external input during install phase.

suggestion.title: Network exfiltration of harvested credentials post-npm install
suggestion.rationale: Payload harvests credentials per article; no detection UC for credential exfiltration to attacker infrastructure. This is the payload's ultimate action and must be detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound HTTP/HTTPS from npm install processes to non-standard or low-reputation domains post-install completion. Flag unusual traffic sizes, JSON payloads containing credential-like patterns (Bearer tokens, AWS key IDs, vault paths), or POST requests to unknown endpoints from CI/CD agents or development machines immediately after installing @redhat-cloud-services packages.

suggestion.title: npm package install with suspicious post-install script execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly discusses multi-stage attacks and payload delivery via npm; no detection for abnormal post-install hooks despite this being the primary npm attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for npm install commands followed by spawning of unexpected child processes (curl, wget, powershell, cmd) with encoded arguments, particularly targeting DNS exfiltration or reverse-shell patterns.

suggestion.title: Worm propagation through npm transitive dependencies
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically mentions 'worm propagation' in keywords; no detection for cascading malicious package installation through dependency trees.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate npm install events across multiple machines within a CI/CD pipeline; flag when a single compromised package triggers identical child process chains on multiple hosts, indicating worm-like spread.

suggestion.title: Credential harvesting from npm CI/CD environments
suggestion.rationale: Article keywords include 'credential harvesting' and threats target CI/CD systems; no use case for detecting exfiltration of secrets (API tokens, SSH keys) from npm scripts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm post-install scripts that read from ~/.npmrc, ~/.ssh, .env, or environment variables (process.env) and subsequently invoke network commands (curl, wget) without user context.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated JavaScript payload in npm package source
suggestion.rationale: Article keywords 'obfuscation' and 'payload'; no detection for deobfuscation or obfuscation patterns in published npm packages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag npm packages with minified/uglified code in source distribution or with function/variable names that exceed normal entropy thresholds; correlate with packages matching typosquatting patterns.

suggestion.title: npm registry abuse via account takeover or package republish
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks on npm require account compromise or package mutation; no detection for unusual publish activity, version rollbacks, or auth anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm account login from geographically impossible IPs, failed MFA attempts before successful auth, or package publishes that downgrade version numbers, alter maintainer metadata, or introduce new transitive dependencies.

suggestion.title: CI/CD pipeline persistence via npm package installation hooks
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly references 'CI/CD persistence' as a threat; no detection for post-install scripts that modify .github/workflows, Jenkinsfiles, or GitLab CI configs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install phases for subprocess activity that modifies CI/CD configuration files or injects steps into build pipelines; flag packages that spawn editors, git commands, or write directly to workflow definitions.

suggestion.title: Device Code Phishing OAuth Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'device code phishing, which abuses a legitimate OAuth flow to bypass MFA and passkeys entirely, has surged from a research curiosity to an industrialized PhaaS offering, with more than 18 kits being actively tracked in the wild.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual device code OAuth flows initiated from unexpected geographic locations or user agents. Monitor for rapid device code requests without corresponding user interaction, and track OAuth scope grants for device authentication patterns that deviate from normal user behavior.

suggestion.title: LLMShare Technique: Malicious Links via Legitimate AI Chat Sharing
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'LLMshare campaign used legitimate chatgpt.com sharing links, creating a convincing ad that is impossible to spot from just looking at the URL' and attackers 'malvertising the links via search engine ads.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag clicks on search engine ads and promoted results that resolve to phishing infrastructure. Detect when legitimate AI sharing domains (chatgpt.com, claude.ai) are used as redirects with unusual parameters or custom paths. Monitor for credential entry on pages reached via malvertised links.

suggestion.title: Multi-Channel Phishing Delivery via Malvertising and SEO Poisoning
suggestion.rationale: Article states: '1 in 3 phishing payloads arrive via channels other than email' and 'ClickFix: 4 in 5 payloads arrive specifically through search engine results.' Traditional email-only detection misses the majority of delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate users visiting search results, malvertising, and social media referrals to domains known for phishing. Establish baseline for each user's search engine click patterns and flag deviations toward high-risk domains. Detect search ad campaigns with shortened URLs or obfuscated parameters.

suggestion.title: Browser-Based Session Theft via Malicious JavaScript
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes: 'Attacks increasingly take place inside the browser, without touching the endpoint' focusing on 'session theft, malicious copy and paste, file downloads.' Detection must operate at browser script execution level.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect JavaScript accessing session cookies, authentication tokens, or localStorage from unexpected scripts. Flag clipboard read/write operations by non-standard scripts, especially those copying auth tokens or pasting malicious commands. Monitor for large file downloads to temporary directories initiated by script injection.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized AI Browser Extension Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'AI browser extensions collect browsing context from internal applications, creating a data exfiltration path that operates outside traditional DLP.' Pipeline data shows '17 AI browser extensions...most of them unapproved.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for browser extensions making requests to external domains while users are on internal/sensitive applications. Detect clipboard read operations by unapproved extensions during sessions with sensitive pages. Track data transfers by extensions that correlate with user access to sensitive content.

suggestion.title: Shadow AI Account Usage and Unauthorized OAuth Integrations
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: '67% using non-corporate accounts,' '17 AI-connected OAuth integrations — most of them unapproved,' and '38% of file uploads from personal shadow accounts.' Represents persistent credential access and data exfiltration vectors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify users authenticating to unauthorized AI platforms (ChatGPT, Claude, etc.) via personal accounts from corporate networks. Detect OAuth token grants to unapproved AI services. Track file uploads to cloud AI services and correlate file types/sensitivity with user role and data classification.

suggestion.title: Dragon Weave Targeting Detection — Czech Republic Infra
suggestion.rationale: Article headline explicitly names 'Dragon Weave Hits Czech Republic & Taiwan' but pipeline extracted zero targeting or actor indicators. Czech Republic is NATO ally; targeting its infrastructure is strategically significant and should trigger detection baselines.
