suggestion.title: China-Aligned APT Command & Control Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article title mentions 'China-Aligned Groups' conducting active campaigns. No kill-chain reconstruction provided. C2 communication is a core adversary TTPs for sustained access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for encrypted/obfuscated outbound connections to newly registered or fast-flux domains, anomalous DNS query patterns (e.g., heavy DNS tunneling), and process execution spawning uncommon network utilities from system binaries.

suggestion.title: Taiwan Infrastructure Targeting — Geo-Specific Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Title names Taiwan as a target alongside Czech Republic, establishing cross-continent APT campaign. Absence of exfiltration detection use cases is a gap in covering the attack lifecycle.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Taiwan-based hosts (.tw domains, government/telecom IP ranges) for bulk data movement to non-local destinations, file staging patterns indicative of pre-exfiltration compression/encryption, and anomalous SMB/WinRM session counts.

suggestion.title: Dragon Weave Malware Delivery — Weaponized Document Execution
suggestion.rationale: Threat-intel articles on named APT campaigns typically describe malware delivery chains. Article title establishes Dragon Weave as active threat, but zero execution/delivery detection rules generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track Office documents (Word, Excel) opened from untrusted sources spawning child processes, shell execution from document macros disabled-by-default, and unusual script interpretter invocations (PowerShell, VBScript) sourced from Office parent processes.

suggestion.title: Multi-Region Campaign Coordination Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly calls out simultaneous targeting of Czech Republic and Taiwan ('Ramp Up Attacks'), indicating coordinated multi-nation campaign. No cross-asset correlation or campaign-attribution use cases provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate suspicious authentication, phishing, or infrastructure reconnaissance activity across disparate geographies within a 30-day window; alert on targeting of entities in multiple allied nations in parallel (Czech + Taiwan + others), consistent with state-sponsored campaign operations.

suggestion.title: WebLogic Server T3 Protocol Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'network access via T3, IIOP' and explicitly recommends 'asset-exposure hunt.' T3 is WebLogic's proprietary RMI protocol (default port 7002). Exposed T3 listeners are the attack surface for CVE-2024-21182.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify inbound connections to WebLogic T3 port (7002) from external or anomalous internal sources. Baseline known administrative jump hosts. Alert on scanning activity or connection attempts from non-whitelisted source IPs. Correlate with vulnerability scanner findings for CVE-2024-21182 on the same asset.

suggestion.title: WebLogic Server IIOP Protocol Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists 'IIOP' as the second attack vector (default port 7003). IIOP (Internet Inter-ORB Protocol) is the CORBA-based interface and a parallel exploitation surface for the same unspecified vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on inbound IIOP connections (TCP/7003) from external sources. Monitor for IIOP protocol anomalies or handshake failures that may indicate exploitation. Cross-reference with scanner results identifying vulnerable WebLogic instances.

suggestion.title: CVE-2024-21182 Vulnerability Match in Scanner Output
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'CVE-2024-21182 — match against your vulnerability scanner.' CISA KEV entries are actively exploited; scanner hits must trigger immediate remediation workflow.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest vulnerability scanner data and alert on any CVE-2024-21182 findings. Enrich with asset criticality (federal civilian agencies are mandated remediation by 2026-06-04). Escalate exposures on internet-facing or DMZ assets immediately.

suggestion.title: WebLogic Server Post-Exploitation Data Access Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article states successful attacks result in 'unauthorized access to critical data or complete access to all Oracle WebLogic Server accessible data.' Post-exploitation data exfiltration is the impact phase and requires behavioral detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WebLogic Server logs for unusual data queries, bulk exports, or credential usage patterns post-exploitation. Alert on large data transfers initiated from compromised WebLogic processes or unexpected database access from application service accounts. Correlate timing with T3/IIOP exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: WebLogic Server Version/Patch Inventory Baseline
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'patch lag is the silent killer' and federal due-date is 2026-06-04. Inventory must distinguish patched vs. unpatched WebLogic versions to avoid false negatives from scanner gaps.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Asset inventory query: all WebLogic Server instances, version, build date, and patch level. Flag any version ≤ unpatched release date for CVE-2024-21182. Cross-correlate with scanner vulnerability reports to identify discrepancies (e.g., scanner reports 'vulnerable' but asset shows recent patch).

suggestion.title: T3/IIOP Exploitation Attempt Detection via Malformed Handshake
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'unauthenticated attacker with network access.' CISA KEV implies active exploitation attempts; protocol-level anomalies (failed T3/IIOP handshakes, malformed serialized objects) may precede successful compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: IDS/WAF signatures for malformed T3 protocol handshakes, unexpected RMI object deserialization attempts, or protocol version mismatches on WebLogic listeners. Alert on scanning tools probing T3/IIOP ports from external sources. Correlate with WebLogic error logs for exception patterns (e.g., serialization failures, ClassNotFound).

suggestion.title: Container Image Supply Chain Poisoning via Docker Hub Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'poisoning a Docker Hub repository to later steal Kubernetes secrets and other sensitive data.' This is the entry point of the attack chain and requires detection on unauthorized image manifest modifications and push anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor container registry (Docker Hub, ECR, GCR) for unauthorized image pushes or tag modifications to trusted repositories. Detect image pull activity from previously clean repos now serving tainted images. Correlate registry activity with downstream container runtime launches.

suggestion.title: Kubernetes Secret Extraction from Compromised Scanning Container
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'tainted images distributed a stealer that was loaded during the KICS scanning process' to 'steal Kubernetes secrets.' Detection must catch secret API access from container scanning contexts and credential exfiltration patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on containers executing KICS or build-scanning tools making unauthorized calls to Kubernetes secrets API (get, list, watch on secret objects). Detect base64-encoded secret values in container environment, process arguments, or outbound DNS/HTTP traffic.

suggestion.title: Privileged Container Capability Abuse for Host Escape
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists escape surface: 'Privileged containers CAP_SYS_ADMIN CAP_SYS_MODULE CAP_SYS_PTRACE CAP_NET_ADMIN' enabling 'container escape followed by host compromise.' Detection must catch capability-enabled syscalls and namespace crossing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor containers with dangerous capabilities for syscalls: ptrace() on host process PIDs (CAP_SYS_PTRACE), finit_module/delete_module (CAP_SYS_MODULE), eBPF operations (CAP_SYS_ADMIN). Detect attempts to access /proc/sys, cgroup manipulation, or host namespace file descriptor acquisition.

suggestion.title: Container Runtime Exploitation and Vulnerability Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Exploiting vulnerabilities in the host system and container runtime components' defines a broad vector. Pipeline must map known runc/containerd CVEs and detect exploitation patterns (cgroup escape, namespace confusion, syscall filters bypass).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect container processes invoking syscall patterns associated with published container runtime CVEs (e.g., runc cgroup escape, namespace leaks). Alert on unusual mmap calls targeting host kernel memory, ptrace on host PIDs, or cgroup path traversal in /proc/self.

suggestion.title: Silent Malware Injection via Tainted Container Image Layers
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'stealer that was loaded during the KICS scanning process'—malware embedded in container image layers executed transparently during build/scan orchestration, avoiding traditional runtime detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal KICS process execution, network, and file behavior. Alert on scanning containers spawning additional processes, accessing credential managers, exfiltrating environment variables, or establishing outbound network connections to non-standard endpoints.

suggestion.title: Orchestration API Reconnaissance and Cluster Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Exploitation of orchestration APIs' and 'insecure use of... orchestration APIs.' Compromised containers will probe Kubernetes API for lateral movement opportunity discovery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect container service accounts making unexpected API calls: list/get operations on deployments, services, configmaps, nodes, or namespaces; service account token enumeration; RBAC boundary probing via failed API attempts from single source.

suggestion.title: WordPress Admin Account Creation via Vulnerable Plugin Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states flaw is 'actively exploited to create admin accounts' — no detection UC exists for this attack outcome.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WordPress admin panel logs and database for rapid admin user_register or wp_user creation without corresponding WordPress admin dashboard session. Correlate with exploitation attempts against known WP Maps Pro endpoints. Alert on admin roles added to non-administrative user patterns.

suggestion.title: WP Maps Pro Plugin Vulnerability Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article title indicates active exploitation of specific plugin — detection should key on HTTP requests to the vulnerable endpoint pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP POST/GET requests to WordPress plugin directories matching /wp-content/plugins/wp-maps-pro/ endpoints known to be unauthenticated. Flag requests containing payload patterns for user creation or role escalation parameters.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via User Role Promotion in WordPress
suggestion.rationale: Creating admin accounts is explicit privilege escalation — no specific UC maps this in WordPress context despite being primary attack outcome.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor wp_usermeta table for rapid capability_wp_administrator assignments to previously non-administrative users. Alert on user creation immediately followed by role promotion in same database session.

suggestion.title: Suspicious WordPress wp-admin Access from New Admin Accounts
suggestion.rationale: After admin account creation succeeds, attacker will log in and operate with privileges — detect behavioral anomaly of new account immediate access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate WordPress admin user creation events with HTTP 200 responses to wp-admin/index.php login from same IP/user-agent within 5 minutes. Flag accounts created outside business hours with immediate privileged access.

suggestion.title: Bulk Admin Account Creation Pattern in WordPress
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions exploitation is active/widespread — batch indicators missing. Multi-account creation would be institutional IOC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on >2 admin user_register events within 60 seconds to same WordPress instance. Baseline legitimate admin account creation rates to identify anomalous batch additions.

suggestion.title: High-Volume Failed Authentication Attempts Against Single Account
suggestion.rationale: Article states attack mechanism as 'trying multiple passwords in succession until the correct one is found.' This is the core attack vector and should surface as failed login spike.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when a single account receives >10 failed authentication attempts within a 5-minute window. Correlate with successful account lockout/suspension events to confirm brute-force attack rather than user mistyping credentials.

suggestion.title: Authentication Attempts From Multiple Distant Geographies
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attempted logins from distant locations and unknown devices.' Geographic diversity in failed authentication attempts indicates distributed attack or credential-stuffing campaign.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For individual accounts, flag when failed authentication attempts originate from 3+ distinct countries within 24 hours, particularly if source IPs indicate datacenter/VPN infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Unsolicited Device Registration Verification Emails
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'users received notices...verification codes for legitimate account owners to register new devices' but 'had not initiated the requests.' Indicates attacker triggering device enrollment flows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when device registration verification emails are generated without a preceding successful authentication or password-reset request by the account owner. Cross-check email send logs against failed authentication patterns.

suggestion.title: Account Suspension/Lockout Correlated with Brute-Force Attack
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'accounts were targeted in a brute force attack...resulting in the suspension of those accounts.' Account suspension is the system's defensive response and indicates active attack detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for account suspension/lockout events and immediately correlate backwards 15-30 minutes for failed authentication clusters. Multiple suspensions within same service in short timeframe suggests coordinated campaign.

suggestion.title: Failed Authentication Followed by Legitimate Verification Email
suggestion.rationale: Article: attackers triggered device registration (unknown devices), causing system to email legitimate users verification codes. Gap between attack attempt and user receiving defensive email is detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequences where failed authentication attempts spike, then legitimate notification emails (MFA/verification codes) are auto-generated for same account without legitimate user action in preceding minutes.

suggestion.title: praisonai-platform: Failed or rejected ownership-grant attempts
suggestion.rationale: The article describes MemberService.add() performing the grant without caller-permission validation. Detection should also hunt for HTTP 403, 401, or 400 responses to /workspaces/*/members POST requests, catching either defender blocks or attacker probing for which accounts lack member privileges.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for 4xx/5xx responses to POST /workspaces/{id}/members. Spikes in 403 Forbidden may indicate attempted privilege escalation or membership checks by an attacker enumerating workspace structure.

suggestion.title: praisonai-platform: Rapid sequential ownership grants or multi-user elevation
suggestion.rationale: A single attacker adding multiple users as owners within a short window is consistent with workspace account takeover. The article emphasizes the lack of per-caller permission checks, meaning multiple grants could execute in rapid succession.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect >3 POST /workspaces/*/members requests with role=owner from the same source user within 5 minutes. Baseline normal membership onboarding to tune FP threshold.

suggestion.title: praisonai-platform: Workspace member POST /workspaces/*/members followed by workspace configuration changes
suggestion.rationale: After granting themselves or an accomplice owner status, the attacker can modify workspace settings, API keys, or integrations. The article's impact is workspace compromise, so detecting config changes correlated with prior ownership elevation is high-confidence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate POST /workspaces/*/members with HTTP 201 (success) followed within 2 hours by POST/PATCH to /workspaces/{id}/settings, /workspaces/{id}/keys, or /workspaces/{id}/integrations from the same or newly-elevated account.

suggestion.title: ClickFix PowerShell Command Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'the ClickFix attacks involve PowerShell commands' and describes how victims are deceived into 'copying and executing malicious commands on their systems.' This is a direct execution pathway requiring detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PowerShell process creation with obfuscation or suspicious encodings, particularly when parent process is browser or user-initiated. Correlate timing with clipboard operations (paste execution) and commands containing credential harvesting or lateral movement indicators. Filter legitimate Windows Update/security tool execution.

suggestion.title: Malicious Browser Update Executable Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Article documents specific payload: 'a fake Firefox update that downloaded a ZIP archive containing multiple DLLs and a malicious executable named Browser Update.exe.' FakeUpdates campaigns universally target Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari, Opera, Brave, Yandex, Vivaldi, Samsung Internet, and UC Browser.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on downloads of executables with names matching '*Browser*Update*', '*Chrome*Update*', '*Firefox*Update*' patterns or ZIP files containing suspicious DLL bundles. Correlate download source (redirected from legitimate site) with user seeing fake update prompts. Block execution of these payloads immediately.

suggestion.title: JavaScript Injection Detection via t.js Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies exact technical fingerprint: 'a JavaScript injection following the t.js?site=<id> pattern, where <id> is a unique value assigned to each compromised website.' Researchers identified 'more than 80 malicious injection domains' using this pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to any domain serving JavaScript from path 't.js?site=*' or matching variation patterns. Cross-reference requesting IPs/sites against silent-hijack indicators. Block or isolate sites triggering these injection payloads.

suggestion.title: zTDS Traffic Distribution System Redirection Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes silent redirection mechanism: 'Visitors of compromised websites are redirected through a Traffic Distribution System (TDS) known as zTDS, which profiles them and determines whether a FakeUpdates or a ClickFix lure is more appropriate.' zTDS has existed since at least 2015; DriveSurge used it since at least September 2025.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP 3xx redirects from legitimate, high-reputation websites to unexpected third-party domains, especially with profiling parameters (User-Agent, IP geolocation, referrer). Alert on users visiting single compromised site but receiving different redirect targets (evidence of conditional profiling).

suggestion.title: macOS Clipboard Hijacking via ClickFix Attacks
suggestion.rationale: Article reveals platform-specific campaign: 'an obfuscated JavaScript payload specifically designed to target macOS desktop systems, delivered via verification-themed ClickFix attacks that hijack the clipboard.' Indicates campaign extends beyond Windows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor JavaScript accessing macOS clipboard APIs (navigator.clipboard.readText, NSPasteboard) during web browsing sessions. Alert on verification-themed popups (fake app updates, system verifications) followed by clipboard access. Monitor for suspicious commands written to clipboard or read for credential exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Installation with Credential Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Credential-Stealing Worm'—core attack vector. Pipeline missed detection of npm package execution triggering credential harvesting, the fundamental malicious behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm process spawning child processes performing credential enumeration (registry queries, browser profile access, SSH key scanning) within 5 minutes of package install. Correlate with unexpected outbound connections from npm descendants to non-public IPs.

suggestion.title: Red Hat npm Package Registry Tampering—Unexpected Versions/Signatures
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Compromises Red Hat npm Packages'—indicates supply-chain poisoning. Pipeline failed to suggest detection of package manifest anomalies or version/signature mismatches indicating tampering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag npm install operations pulling unexpected package versions (major jumps, pre-release tags for stable packages), unsigned packages, or packages from non-standard registries. Alert on package-lock.json integrity mismatches indicating in-transit modification.

suggestion.title: Worm Persistence via npm Post-Install Scripts
suggestion.rationale: Worm designation requires persistence; npm supplies post-install script execution vector. Pipeline missed detection of suspicious post-install/post-uninstall hooks setting up scheduled tasks, registry modifications, or startup persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect package.json and package-lock.json 'scripts' fields for post-install commands. Alert on Base64-encoded, obfuscated, or PowerShell-invoked payloads. Correlate package installation timestamp with subsequent HKLM/HKCU Run key writes, Tasks folder modifications, or WMI event subscription creation.

suggestion.title: Credential Material Exfiltration to Attacker-Controlled Domains
suggestion.rationale: Title includes 'Credential-Stealing Worm'—stolen credentials must be exfiltrated. Pipeline lacked use case for detecting command-and-control communication carrying credential data or API calls leaking secrets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound HTTPS/HTTP from npm process or descendants to non-whitelisted domains, especially with POST payloads. Correlate timing with credential-harvesting process execution. Flag requests to newly-registered domains or IPs geolocated outside expected business regions.

suggestion.title: Miasma Campaign IoC Extraction—Package Names, Hashes, Domains
suggestion.rationale: High-severity article warrants named-campaign detection. Pipeline extracted zero indicators: no package names, versions, malware hashes, or C2 domains despite title naming the 'Miasma' campaign explicitly.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain threat-feed entries for Miasma-attributed packages by name and version; hardcode file hashes for known worm samples. Trigger alerts on attempted installation of blacklisted packages or process execution matching known Miasma malware signatures.

suggestion.title: Telegram Bot API C2 Communications
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Telegram bot API–based external command and control (C2) mechanism that routed communication through Telegram's infrastructure'. Explicit C2 channel descriptor.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTPS POST requests to api.telegram.org originating from non-browser processes. Identify bot token patterns (numeric_id:alphanumeric_string). Correlate with Python/curl parent processes and unusual child relationships.

suggestion.title: Cloudflare Worker C2 Redirector Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'A Cloudflare Worker acting as a front-end redirector to obscure the actual backend C2 server'. Infrastructure obfuscation pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTPS traffic to *.workers.dev domains from production endpoints with C2-like signatures: fixed payload sizes, 4-5 second intervals, auth failures followed by retries.

suggestion.title: Automated Active Directory Discovery Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'an automated Active Directory (AD) discovery panel' and 'AD discovery is driven by collecting observations from completed tasks and selecting the next action from predefined choices'. Iterative, programmatic enumeration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag rapid-fire LDAP queries (>50/min), Get-ADUser/Get-ADComputer/Get-ADGroup loops in PowerShell block logs, or sequential net user/group enum commands. Baseline per-user normal AD discovery rates.

suggestion.title: Shellcode Injection Preserving Process Functionality
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Python-based malware development scripts for injecting shellcode into legitimate Windows executables while preserving original functionality'. Injection technique with stealth requirement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unsigned code pages in signed executables, RWX memory in svchost/explorer/services, shellcode patterns (NOP sleds, ROP gadgets) in memory regions, or child process spawns with unexpected parent-binary mismatches.

suggestion.title: Cobalt Strike Beacon HTTP Profile Obfuscation
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'Cobalt Strike profiles designed to make beacon traffic resemble legitimate web requests'. Customized profiles bypass signature detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline per-user HTTP behavior and detect outliers matching Beacon signatures: fixed User-Agent consistency over days, 4-5 second callback intervals independent of user activity, anomalous HTTP header combinations.

suggestion.title: Russian-Language Malware Script Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'multiple Python scripts on the compromised host were written in Russian and generated with the help of AI tools'. Non-native language scripts in English-locale environments are anomalous.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Python invocations with Cyrillic characters in paths/arguments. Inspect script block logs for Russian comments/strings. Alert on script locale mismatch with system locale.

suggestion.title: Cloud Provider IP Beaconing — Legitimate Infra, Malicious Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'weaponizing trusted cloud infrastructure...to camouflage malicious traffic.' Beaconing UC is too generic; needs explicit cloud IP targeting. Phrase: 'sustained long-lived Command and Control operations' via AWS/GCP/Azure/Cloudflare.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify internal hosts with regular, periodic outbound connections to AWS (e.g., ec2, s3, lambda endpoints), GCP, Azure, or Cloudflare IPs where the traffic does not match known legitimate business application patterns. Focus on consistent time deltas between connections and small payload sizes.

suggestion.title: DNS Exfiltration via Public Resolvers
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists T1071.004 (DNS) technique but provides no hunt. DNS-based C2 is canonical evasion vector when hiding inside cloud provider infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS queries from internal hosts to public recursive resolvers (8.8.8.8, 1.1.1.1, Cloudflare, Google DNS) with anomalous patterns: unusually long subdomains, high-frequency queries to newly-registered domains, or consistent subdomain prefixes suggesting parameterized C2 requests.

suggestion.title: GitHub API Abuse for Command Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names GitHub alongside AWS/GCP/Azure as abused service. No detection for repository-as-C2-channel pattern where commits, issues, or repo metadata encode commands.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag internal users or service accounts with unusual GitHub API activity: rapid clone/fetch of suspect repositories, commit history parsing patterns, or API calls showing timing consistent with C2 polling. Correlate with process execution on same host to detect command parsing.

suggestion.title: T3/IIOP Protocol Exploitation Attempts to WebLogic
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'can be exploited remotely by threat actors with no privileges in low-complexity attacks' via 'T3, IIOP' to 'compromise Oracle WebLogic Server.' Pipeline produced no network-level detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor T3 (port 7002/7003) and IIOP (7001/7002) traffic to WebLogic from untrusted sources. Alert on unauthenticated T3 handshakes, serialized Java object transmission, or protocol sequences consistent with CVE-2024-21182 exploitation.

suggestion.title: Oracle WebLogic Vulnerable Version Identification
suggestion.rationale: Article names specific affected versions: 12.2.1.4.0 (961 Shodan instances) and 14.1.1.0.0 (631 instances). Pipeline failed to extract version-based asset indicators for 1,592+ exposed servers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify WebLogic Server instances running versions 12.2.1.4.0 or 14.1.1.0.0 via port 7001/7002 banner grabbing and process enumeration. Flag all unpatched instances as immediately exploitable per CISA directive.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Data Access via Compromised WebLogic
suggestion.rationale: Article states successful exploitation enables 'unauthorized access to critical data or complete access to all Oracle WebLogic Server accessible data.' Pipeline omitted impact-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected elevation of WebLogic service account privileges, unusual JDBC connections to backend databases, bulk data reads, or exfiltration of sensitive information accessible through WebLogic middleware.

suggestion.title: Malicious Java Deserialization in WebLogic T3 Channel
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'easily exploitable' active exploitation; typical WebLogic CVEs involve serialized gadget chains over T3. Pipeline did not generate execution-level detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Java deserialization gadget classes transmitted over T3 protocol. Alert on abnormal child process spawning from WebLogic JVM or memory allocation anomalies following unauthenticated T3 connections.

suggestion.title: WebLogic Server Reconnaissance and Capability Probing
suggestion.rationale: Shodan tracking of 1,592 exposed instances suggests active reconnaissance. Article implies attacker scanning for vulnerable versions before exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid-fire connection attempts to WebLogic T3/IIOP ports followed by version/capability probing. Flag port 7001/7002 banner grabbing from non-approved scanners or untrusted IP ranges.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scan for CVE-2022-0492 (Linux Kernel cgroups)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'CVE-2022-0492 — match against your vulnerability scanner' in Indicators of Compromise section. Pipeline generated no detection rule despite direct instruction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and patch-management systems for Linux Kernel versions vulnerable to CVE-2022-0492. Flag all unpatched systems. Enforce compliance by federal deadline 2026-06-05.

suggestion.title: Cgroups v1 release_agent Privilege-Escalation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies the exploit mechanism: 'privilege escalation via the cgroups v1 release_agent feature'. No detection generated for this specific attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process writes to cgroups v1 release_agent files (/proc/*/cgroup, /sys/fs/cgroup/*). Detect attempts to configure release_agent to point to user-writable paths or shell scripts. Correlate with subsequent privilege-elevation events.

suggestion.title: Unprivileged-to-Root Privilege Escalation (Post-Kernel Exploit)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes outcome as 'allow for privilege escalation'. No detection rule generated for privilege-elevation indicators following successful kernel exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unprivileged user processes spawning root-owned children without sudo/su/setuid. Flag capability grants (CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_SYS_MODULE). Correlate with cgroups-related syscalls on same host within same timeframe.

suggestion.title: Post-Deadline Patch Compliance: CVE-2022-0492
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies federal patch deadline: '2026-06-05'. Pipeline should generate compliance hunt, not just point-in-time vulnerability scan.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After 2026-06-05, query vulnerability scans for any systems still reporting CVE-2022-0492 as unpatched or unmitigated. Escalate findings for federal compliance audit.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Android Framework Devices (CVE-2025-48595)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and states 'it's worth one quick check across your fleet — patch lag is the silent killer.' Federal patch due date is 2026-06-05, making inventory visibility critical.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory to identify all Android devices with Framework versions vulnerable to CVE-2025-48595. Correlate against patch applied date to flag unpatched systems past 2026-06-05 deadline. Alert on any device with vulnerable version after federal due date.

suggestion.title: Patch Compliance Tracking for CVE-2025-48595
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'Federal due-date dates also frequently match the timing your organisation will be asked about by auditors / regulators.' Patch status tracking is compliance-critical for regulatory readiness.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track patch deployment timeline for CVE-2025-48595 across Android device estate. Measure compliance rate against 2026-06-05 deadline. Generate compliance reports for audit trail.

suggestion.title: Android Device Code Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability 'allows for code execution that could allow for local privilege escalation.' Code execution is the attack inflection point requiring immediate detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Android system logs and process events for suspicious code execution following attempts to trigger integer overflow in Framework libraries. Alert on unusual process spawning or unexpected elevated permissions immediately post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Android Framework Exploit
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'allows for local privilege escalation'—the post-execution payload objective requiring distinct detection rules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect privilege escalation attempts targeting Android Framework components following code execution. Monitor for calls to system APIs granting elevated permissions or protected resource access. Alert on unexpected privilege transitions on vulnerable versions.

suggestion.title: Brute-force attack detection against password manager service
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'brute-force attack'—core attack vector. Pipeline generated no detection for multiple failed login attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor authentication endpoints for > N failed login attempts targeting same user account within M-minute window. Flag patterns consistent with credential guessing: varying source IPs, rapid-fire attempts, common passwords. Dashlane auth logs should show spike in failed attempts preceding successful compromise.

suggestion.title: Bulk data exfiltration from compromised password manager accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'encrypted vaults of fewer than 20 users downloaded'—direct exfiltration. No detection UC generated for unusual vault access or bulk downloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual data volume or frequency of vault downloads/exports from single account within short timeframe. Correlate with prior authentication anomalies. Alert on bulk operations (export all vaults) or access from IP/geography inconsistent with account baseline.

suggestion.title: Compromised account usage post-credential exposure
suggestion.rationale: Brute-force success implies valid credentials obtained. No detection for subsequent abuse of compromised accounts (T1078).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-breach, monitor compromised accounts for login from atypical locations, times, or devices. Flag access that conflicts with account owner's known behavior profile. Correlate with vault access patterns (downloads, syncs) occurring outside normal windows.

suggestion.title: Detection of threat actor reconnaissance of password manager service
suggestion.rationale: Brute-force attack implies attacker had knowledge of Dashlane's auth endpoints and user base. No detection for reconnaissance or targeting indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for scanning/enumeration activity against Dashlane login endpoints (multiple requests with varying usernames, account validation probes). Detect credential stuffing tool signatures or automation patterns typical of brute-force campaigns.

suggestion.title: Service provider incident disclosure correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article is a security disclosure by Dashlane vendor. No detection use case for identifying affected customers or similar service compromises.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference employee/customer Dashlane logins during disclosed incident window (brute-force period). Alert on accounts with activity during attack window or access from previously-unseen geolocations. Trigger credential reset workflow for high-risk users.

suggestion.title: WinRAR Vulnerability Exploitation — Child Process Anomaly Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'Exploits WinRAR' — attack vector explicitly named. Pipeline generated zero detections despite WinRAR being the primary initial-access mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor rar.exe/unrar.exe with suspicious command-line arguments or parent processes. Alert on child process spawning within 5 seconds of WinRAR extraction, especially unsigned binaries or scripts from temp directories. Correlate with archive creation timestamps.

suggestion.title: GammaWorm/GammaSteel Malware Execution Signature
suggestion.rationale: Title names two specific malware families as payloads: 'GammaWorm and GammaSteel'. Pipeline provided zero process signatures, file hashes, registry artifacts, or malware-family detection rules for either.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on malware-family file hashes, known artifact paths, and behavioral patterns (e.g., registry key writes, service installation, C2 beaconing patterns) associated with GammaWorm and GammaSteel post-WinRAR extraction.

suggestion.title: Gamaredon Persistence via Registry and Scheduled Tasks
suggestion.rationale: Title identifies Gamaredon as actor. Pipeline did not surface Gamaredon's canonical persistence patterns (registry modification, scheduled task creation, LOTL abuse) or actor-attributed behavioral detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect scheduled task creation with batch/VBS launchers from temp directories or HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run writes with obfuscated paths. Chain detections with WinRAR extraction timeline and GammaWorm/GammaSteel process signatures.

suggestion.title: Spearphishing to Ukraine — Email-Based Initial Access
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'Against Ukraine' indicates geographic targeting. Gamaredon's primary vector is spearphishing; WinRAR delivery implies archive attachment. Pipeline missed email-layer detection or Ukraine-recipient geo-targeting rules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on .rar/.7z/.zip attachments to Ukrainian recipient domains from external/untrusted senders. Flag emails with government/military/critical-update lures. Correlate sender reputation, DKIM/SPF failures, and archive metadata timestamps.

suggestion.title: C2 Communication — Network-Layer Malware Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Both GammaWorm and GammaSteel are remote-access/infostealer malware requiring C2 communication. Pipeline surfaced zero network IOCs (domains, IPs, ASNs), preventing C2 detection or threat-intel enrichment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DNS queries and connections to Gamaredon-attributed C2 infrastructure. Alert on outbound connections from GammaWorm/GammaSteel processes to non-RFC1918 IPs on high-numbered ports. Correlate with malware execution timeline.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Android Framework Vulnerability
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Local attackers can exploit the actively abused high-severity Android Framework vulnerability... to gain code execution and escalate privileges on devices running Android 14 or later.' This is the primary impact; no detection rule exists for the privilege escalation step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process execution with unexpected elevated privileges on Android 14+ devices. Flag processes spawned from Framework context that attempt system-level capability access or UID elevation. Correlate with CVE-2025-48595 patch status to identify vulnerable devices.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-48595 Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: The zero-day is explicitly named as 'under limited, targeted exploitation' against high-value targets. Article provides no detection signature, but the vulnerability mechanics (Framework flaw, local trigger, RCE outcome) should define observable behaviors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Framework component crash dumps and stack traces for exploitation patterns (heap overflow, use-after-free, memory corruption signatures). Alert on Framework service restarts following abnormal process spawning on Android 14+. Cross-reference with unpatched device inventory.

suggestion.title: Targeted Device Compromise Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article notes CVE-2025-48595 is 'exploited in targeted attacks' and references historical abuse by 'commercial spyware and nation-state operations targeting high-profile or high-interest individuals.' This suggests behavioral IOCs for targeted campaigns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Android 14+ devices that are unpatched for CVE-2025-48595 and simultaneously exhibit suspicious installation attempts (sideloading, unsigned APKs, exploit delivery mechanisms). Prioritize devices matching high-value target profiles (executive, government, security researcher).

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution via Framework Component
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'The most severe of these issues is a critical security vulnerability in the Framework component that could lead to remote escalation of privilege with no additional execution privileges needed. User interaction is not needed for exploitation.' This RCE path should have dedicated detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for remote invocation of Framework services without standard user-interaction triggers. Flag network-to-Framework code paths that bypass normal intent mechanisms. Alert on Framework component spawning unexpected child processes with no corresponding user app activity.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Android 14+ Inventory at Risk
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'devices running Android 14 or later' are affected and mentions 'exploitation for many issues on Android is made more difficult by enhancements in newer versions.' Patch compliance detection is the baseline preventive control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory all Android 14, 15, and later devices lacking security patch level 2026-06-01 or later (issued June 1, 2026). Segregate high-risk device groups (enterprise, government, research) and prioritize patching timelines. Flag devices that defer patch installation >30 days.

suggestion.title: Android Vulnerability Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'one actively exploited' flaw. Pipeline extracted zero detection logic despite clear need to monitor for exploitation attempts against the patched vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on abnormal process execution, memory access patterns, or kernel panic signatures consistent with Android CVE exploitation. Correlate against known PoC code signatures for the actively exploited flaw once CVE is identified.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Android Device Inventory Query
suggestion.rationale: Article describes June 2026 update; no detection generated for devices not receiving patches within SLA window. Attackers routinely exploit delayed-patch gaps.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query MDM/EMM for Android build fingerprints older than June 2026 security patch level. Alert on corporate devices (COPE) running vulnerable versions >14 days post-release; escalate if >30 days.

suggestion.title: Android Privilege Escalation via Kernel Exploit
suggestion.rationale: 124-vulnerability patch set likely includes kernel-level flaws enabling PE. Article provides no attack-step granularity, but active exploitation suggests PE chain exists.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for capability/permission elevation attempts, syscall rate anomalies, or spawning of processes with elevated SELinux contexts on vulnerable Android versions. Flag shellcode or ROP gadget execution patterns.

suggestion.title: Malware Delivery Post-Android Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Actively exploited flaw serves as initial access vector for malware. Pipeline generated zero use cases mapping exploitation to subsequent payload delivery or persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful Android exploit indicators with subsequent app installation from unsigned sources, sideloading, or Play Store anomalies (unexpected app versions, permissions). Alert on file writes to /system or /data directories post-crash recovery.

suggestion.title: CVE-Specific Exploit Code Acquisition
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions active exploitation but provides no IOCs. Pipeline should have generated threat-intel use case for monitoring public exploit repos, GitHub, and PoC feeds for matching CVE numbers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on network requests to known exploit repositories, GitHub exploit-db mirrors, or paste sites containing Android CVE numbers from the June 2026 patch set. Flag compilation or download of exploit code in development environments.

suggestion.title: Android System Update Blocking or Evasion
suggestion.rationale: Attackers commonly disable or delay patches post-compromise. Pipeline failed to generate use case for detecting update suppression, rollback, or build fingerprint spoofing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for termination of system update services, modification of update config files (/system/update.conf), or false reporting of patch levels to MDM. Alert on network blocking of Google Update servers or version check manipulation.

suggestion.title: Compromised Laravel-Lang Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'Every Tag Across Multiple Composer Packages Rewritten'—core attack vector is malicious package delivery. Zero IOC extraction and zero UC generated for package-level compromise detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Composer installation of Laravel-Lang packages with version strings outside official release timelines or from non-standard repositories. Monitor for unexpected package installation triggering child process spawning (php, bash, curl) with suspicious arguments or environment variable access.

suggestion.title: CI Secret Exfiltration Following Package Install
suggestion.rationale: Attack explicitly targets CI secrets for theft ('Steal CI Secrets' in title). No UC covers credential access/exfiltration phase—the actual impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect subprocess spawning from PHP/Composer processes reading environment variables (GITHUB_TOKEN, AWS keys, etc.). Alert on base64-encoded or hex-encoded secrets sent to external IPs. Flag Composer install processes making unexpected HTTPS requests post-completion.

suggestion.title: Git Tag Rewrite / Repository History Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'Every Tag...Rewritten'—explicit defense evasion to hide malicious commits in release tags. No UC for git tampering detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on force-pushes or tag rewrites in Laravel-Lang repository, especially for release tags. Detect mass tag deletion/recreation in short timeframes. Monitor for unsigned commits or commits from new/anomalous GPG keys in stable release branches.

suggestion.title: Code Execution During Composer Install
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attack requires injected code execution during package install to exfiltrate secrets. No UC for post-install execution anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected process spawning (curl, wget, bash, sh) during Composer install/update with arguments containing URLs or credential patterns. Detect network activity from package directories. Flag scripts in vendor/ attempting credential file access.

suggestion.title: Package Version Anomaly vs. Official Release Metadata
suggestion.rationale: Compromised packages often have version strings that deviate from official releases. Article implies tag rewrite indicates version divergence from upstream.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when installed Laravel-Lang version in lock file does not match publicly advertised releases or checksum validation fails. Flag unusual pre-release identifiers, metadata, or tag structures. Correlate version mismatch with known compromise timeline if disclosed.

suggestion.title: Repository Maintainer Account / Write-Access Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Mass tag rewrite across multiple packages implies attacker obtained repository write access. No UC for upstream account compromise detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect login anomalies on Laravel-Lang maintainer accounts (new geography, device, off-hours). Alert on push activity from unexpected CI/CD systems or new SSH keys. Flag unsigned/newly-signed commits if GPG enforcement is policy.

suggestion.title: Development Agent Unauthorized Model Inference
suggestion.rationale: Article title emphasizes 'agents and models' security across dev lifecycle. If article discusses automated agents executing model calls or agents being compromised to modify model behavior, this represents lateral movement + resource hijacking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected API calls from development CI/CD agents to LLM endpoints with unusual model IDs, unusual frequency, or calls originating from new/unusual service principals. Alert on agent process spawning inference requests outside normal dev workflow patterns.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Compromise via Development Agent Injection
suggestion.rationale: Title references 'across the development lifecycle'—if article discusses threats to CI/CD agents or code commit signing, should detect when agents execute unsigned or malicious injected code before deployment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on git commits merged without required code review approvals, or commits signed with newly-created/unusual signing certificates. Monitor for agent workflows executing code from untrusted/newly-added branches or running with elevated permissions not matching baseline policy.

suggestion.title: Model Prompt Injection via Development Artifact
suggestion.rationale: Article likely discusses securing models in dev lifecycle. If it covers model-in-the-loop development tools, should detect injection of malicious prompts or system messages into model configuration files stored in version control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor development repos for suspicious additions to model configuration files (.env, .yaml, prompts/ directories). Alert on commits that modify system prompts, embedding injection vectors, or add new model endpoints outside documented allowlists. Flag changes from dev-external accounts or CI/CD principals.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via AI Agent Credential Theft
suggestion.rationale: Agents in dev lifecycle often have broad permissions (code read/write, model access, infrastructure). If article discusses agent security, should detect when agent-owned credentials are exfiltrated or misused.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unusual secret/token access from agent processes, especially read-all operations on credential stores. Monitor for agent-owned tokens used from IPs/geographies inconsistent with deployment location. Detect rapid sequential credential reads followed by external API calls.

suggestion.title: Development Model Exfiltration via Agent
suggestion.rationale: If article discusses securing model artifacts in dev workflows, should detect when agents download or copy proprietary models to external locations or new output paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual file transfers of .onnx, .pt, .pth, or other model artifact formats from dev agents. Alert on model files being written to unusual paths (temp, user home, cloud shares outside normal artifact repos). Flag uploads to external storage services from agent processes.

suggestion.title: Nx Console VS Code Extension — Malicious Version Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article title indicates 'Nx Console VS Code Extension Compromised'—a supply-chain attack on a development tool. No detection logic was generated for identifying installation or activation of malicious extension versions. This is the primary indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor VS Code extension installation logs and registry/filesystem for unexpected Nx Console extension versions, particularly those outside official release cadence. Track process execution spawned by the extension subprocess handler with abnormal parent-child relationships or command-line arguments.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Network Egress from VS Code Process
suggestion.rationale: Compromised extensions typically establish C2 or exfiltrate data. Article describes 'compromised' extension but no network-detection UC was generated. Need detection for unexpected outbound connections from code editors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on DNS queries or HTTP/HTTPS connections initiated by Code.exe (VS Code process) or its child processes to non-standard domains, particularly early in session after extension load. Establish baseline of legitimate Nx tooling domains and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Credential Access via Compromised VS Code Extension
suggestion.rationale: Compromised dev-tool extensions frequently harvest credentials from IDE context (git tokens, SSH keys, environment variables). Article does not indicate what attacker motivation is, but credential theft is standard for supply-chain compromises targeting dev teams.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Node.js child processes spawned by VS Code extension code reading ~/.ssh, ~/.git/config, or environment variables containing API tokens (GITHUB_TOKEN, NPM_TOKEN, etc.). Monitor for file I/O to .ssh/authorized_keys or credential stores.

suggestion.title: Nx Console Extension Privilege Escalation or RCE Execution
suggestion.rationale: Development tools running with user/build-system privileges can escalate to system access. Article states extension is 'compromised' but no execution-phase detection was built.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for powershell.exe, cmd.exe, or bash spawned with parent=Code.exe or grandparent=Node.js (extension runtime). Flag executions with obfuscated arguments, unusual directory changes, or attempts to invoke sc.exe, net.exe, or privilege-escalation tools.

suggestion.title: Nx Extension Package Manifest Tampering Detection
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain compromises often involve modified package.json or extension manifests. No detection was suggested for tracking package metadata or version anomalies published to VS Code Marketplace or npm.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference installed Nx Console extension version against official release history and digital signatures. Flag installations where version bump is unusually large, published outside normal cadence, or lacks expected maintainer signatures.

suggestion.title: Malvertising Campaign - macOS User Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article core finding: 'Operation FlutterBridge is a malvertising campaign targeting macOS users.' Pipeline extracted nothing about the initial access vector. Detection should monitor for ad-click or malvertising-related network behaviors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for macOS processes spawned following clicks on suspicious ad networks or landing pages known to serve malvertising. Look for process chains initiated by Safari, Chrome, or Firefox with command-line arguments indicating download of unsigned binaries or script execution via malvertising payloads.

suggestion.title: FlutterShell Backdoor Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'distributed the new backdoor FlutterShell, built using the Flutter framework.' Pipeline missed the malware name and execution phase entirely. Should detect Flutter-based malware instantiation on macOS.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Flutter runtime execution on macOS (libflutter.so or Flutter framework artifacts) spawning from unexpected parent processes or download directories. Flag processes with obfuscated command lines or attempt to access system binaries post-launch (indicators of Flutter malware unpacking native payloads).

suggestion.title: Flutter-based Malware C2 Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article describes a 'backdoor' capability but pipeline extracted no C2 infrastructure or command-and-control detection logic. FlutterShell as a backdoor implies persistent C2 communication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound HTTPS or HTTP connections from Flutter-runtime-spawned processes on macOS to unknown or newly-registered domains. Flag atypical C2 signaling patterns: periodic beaconing, encoded parameters, or connections to IP space without corresponding WHOIS registration history.

suggestion.title: macOS Unsigned Binary Persistence via Malvertising
suggestion.rationale: Malvertising campaigns often drop unsigned binaries for persistence. Article identifies persistent backdoor ('FlutterShell') but pipeline generated no persistence detection. Should monitor for unsigned executable placement post-malvertising compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unsigned Mach-O binaries written to standard persistence locations (~/.bash_profile, ~/Library/LaunchAgents, /tmp) following malvertising activity. Flag parent processes with unusual network connectivity immediately before binary placement.

suggestion.title: macOS Malvertising Ad Network Traffic Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'malvertising campaign' — this specific initial-access vector requires detection of ad-network traffic anomalies. Pipeline missed attack surface entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for macOS processes (web browsers) connecting to newly-registered or reputation-blacklisted ad-serving domains. Flag redirect chains: legitimate ad domain → intermediate tracker → malware delivery domain. Alert on failed SSL verification or cert warnings bypassed by browser plugins.

suggestion.title: Suspicious JAR Execution from Minecraft User Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies '3,820 unique malicious JAR files' distributed via 'malicious Minecraft mods, clients, cheats, and utilities.' JAR execution from Minecraft folders is the execution vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect java.exe spawning from user browser or file manager with JAR arguments pointing to %APPDATA%/Roaming/.minecraft or equivalent. Correlate with outbound network connections to non-Mojang infrastructure within 5 minutes of execution.

suggestion.title: Multi-Browser Credential Enumeration by Gaming Process
suggestion.rationale: WeedHack 'targets passwords across 36 browsers' and '56 cryptocurrency add-ons' plus 'Discord, Steam, and Telegram credentials.' Single gaming process accessing credential stores across multiple browsers is anomalous.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect java.exe or Minecraft launcher accessing Chrome/Firefox/Edge user data directories, password manager vaults, and cryptocurrency wallet directories in same process session. Flag when browser profile enumeration occurs outside normal launcher startup.

suggestion.title: Webcam and Input Capture Capability Installation
suggestion.rationale: Premium WeedHack tier includes 'webcam access,' 'keylogger,' and 'remote control with input access (mouse and keyboard)' — these are post-execution collection capabilities following initial infection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Minecraft/java.exe acquiring handles to camera devices, microphone drivers, or establishing keyboard/mouse hooks via user32.dll. Detect DLL injection patterns loading input capture libraries or hook utilities.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration to Clear-Net C2 Dashboard
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'WeedHack malware platform is hosted on the clear net and provides access to anyone for free' with victim overview dashboard. Network indicators should detect HTTP/HTTPS to C2 endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Minecraft process initiating HTTPS connections to unregistered or recently-registered domains with dashboard-like URI patterns (/victims, /exfil, /api/steal). Alert on Telegram API calls from java.exe context indicating credential exfiltration to attacker channel (800+ members per article).

suggestion.title: SEO-Poisoning Landing Page Access Preceding JAR Download
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'SEO poisoning promotion' and fake sites 'displaying a security notice warning visitors' mimicking legitimate GitHub/Discord. Detect malicious landing page chains leading to JAR delivery.

Correlate visit to fake security-notice page with immediate JAR file download.

suggestion.title: Minecraft Session Token and Launcher Profile Access
suggestion.rationale: WeedHack explicitly targets 'Minecraft session ID theft' and builds payloads for 'Minecraft versions 1.21.0 through 1.21.10.' Session token theft is primary credential objective.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect non-launcher processes accessing launcher_profiles.json, logintoken.bin, or .minecraft/launcher directory files. Flag file read attempts to Minecraft authentication token storage by unsigned or unsigned-by-Microsoft executables.

suggestion.title: Xeno RAT Process Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names Xeno RAT as the malware payload; no execution-phase detection suggested. Pipeline should flag process creation, DLL loading, or code injection associated with known Xeno RAT IOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process execution of Xeno RAT payloads (hash or behavioral patterns: suspicious DLL injection, unsigned executables in temp directories, child processes spawned from Office or browser). Correlate with known Xeno C2 infrastructure for confirmation.

suggestion.title: Phishing Campaign to Finance Ministry
suggestion.rationale: Article title and context imply initial access via targeted phishing to Afghanistan Finance Ministry; no initial_access detection suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect phishing emails to finance.gov.af or similar with malicious Office attachments, suspicious macros, or links to credential harvesting sites. Monitor for Document macro execution followed by child process spawning on affected hosts.

suggestion.title: Xeno RAT C2 Command & Control Communication
suggestion.rationale: No C2 detection use case generated despite malware-specific article; pipeline should identify network-layer IOCs and communication patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound connections to known Xeno RAT C2 domains/IPs (to be extracted from article and threat feeds). Look for suspicious DNS queries, HTTP POST requests to uncommon ports, or encrypted tunnels with beacon-like patterns.

suggestion.title: Xeno RAT Persistence Registry/Autostart Modifications
suggestion.rationale: RAT implants typically establish persistence via registry keys, scheduled tasks, or startup folder writes; no persistence-phase detection suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for registry writes to Run, RunOnce, or Startup folders correlating with Xeno RAT process execution. Flag unauthorized .lnk files in Startup directory or modifications to shell commands (ShellExecute hooks).

suggestion.title: SideCopy Lateral Movement Post-Compromise

suggestion.title: Maven Dependency Version: jqwik-engine 1.10.0 Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Package: net.jqwik:jqwik-engine Affected version: 1.10.0' and notes 'Follow-up release: 1.10.1'. Pipeline must detect exact version in manifests and lockfiles.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor build artifacts and dependency resolution logs for net.jqwik:jqwik-engine version 1.10.0. Alert on presence in pom.xml, gradle.build, or transitive dependencies during CI/CD runs. Distinguish from 1.10.1+ (patched) by examining Maven Central metadata or JAR checksums.

suggestion.title: ANSI Escape Code Anomalies in Test Output
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'prints ESC [2K followed by a carriage return, twice' and 'Watch for stray ESC[2K and carriage-return artifacts around your test summaries.' This obfuscation is the delivery mechanism.

Flag any raw ANSI erase-line codes in non-interactive log streams (GitHub Actions, Jenkins, GitHub workflows) as anomalous—they indicate obfuscation of tool output intended for agent processing.

suggestion.title: Prompt Injection in Maven/JUnit Test Output
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies the payload: 'The payload told agents to disregard previous instructions and delete all jqwik tests and code.' Detection should flag these directives in test logs fed to agents.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag test output containing prompt injection patterns targeting AI agents (e.g., 'disregard.*instruction', 'delete.*test', 'delete.*jqwik.*code'). Correlate with jqwik test runs. Monitor agent input pipelines for suspicious directives in tool output streams, especially from build/test phases.

suggestion.title: Suspicious CodingAgents Method in Compiled JAR
suggestion.rationale: Article reveals 'The malicious instruction lived in a new method called printMessageForCodingAgents() inside the net.jqwik.engine.execution.JqwikExecutor class.' Decompiled code inspection can identify this.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan downloaded JARs (especially jqwik-engine 1.10.0) for method names containing 'CodingAgents', 'Agent', or 'AIAgent' in combination with print/output methods. Decompile suspected JARs and grep for printMessageForCodingAgents() in net.jqwik.engine.execution.JqwikExecutor. Compare against known safe class structures.

suggestion.title: AI Agent Rejection of Crafted Tool Output
suggestion.rationale: Article documents: 'Claude Code flagged the instruction on the first mvn test run, refused to act on it, and traced it back to its source in the JAR.' Detect when agents properly reject injected directives.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor agent execution logs for rejection events where tool output contains prompt injection patterns. Log agent refusals to act on suspicious terminal output; these are successful defenses. Correlate with source JARs to identify supply-chain attack attempts that were mitigated.

suggestion.title: Commit 9dddcb5226 jqwik Repository Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies specific commit: 'That's the code snippet from commit 9dddcb5226' containing the ESC codes. Threat intel should track suspicious repository commits.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor jqwik repository commits for methods named printMessageForCodingAgents() or similar agent-targeting patterns. Flag commits that introduce ANSI escape codes (0x1B5B324B) combined with carriage returns in output paths. Cross-reference with Maven Central release timelines (May 25, 2026).

suggestion.title: npm preinstall hook spawning child processes
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'preinstall hook on every npm install' as attack vector. No detection for arbitrary process spawning from npm install phase. Detection gap for T1546.016 (Installer Packages).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes spawned from node/npm with parent command containing 'install' or npm process event with child spawning shell/Python/Node interpreters. Preinstall hooks typically execute synchronously during npm install; children from install phase are high-risk.

suggestion.title: Process accessing credential-related environment variables
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'targets GitHub Actions secrets, AWS, GCP, Azure, Kubernetes, HashiCorp Vault, npm tokens'. No detection for environment variable enumeration or reads. Maps to T1552.001 (Credentials in Files) and T1528 (Steal Application Access Token).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detection for process reading or enumerating variables: GITHUB_TOKEN, AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, GCP_*, AZURE_*, KUBECONFIG, VAULT_TOKEN, NPM_TOKEN, CIRCLECI_TOKEN. Higher confidence if sourced from preinstall hook context.

suggestion.title: HTTP metadata API access from build/CI environment
suggestion.rationale: Article lists AWS, GCP, Azure as credential targets. MITRE T1552.005 (Cloud Instance Metadata API) is mapped but no detection. Metadata services are primary lateral-movement credential vector in cloud CI/CD.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP(S) requests from npm/node processes to metadata endpoints: 169.254.169.254 (AWS IMDSv1/v2), 0.metadata.google.internal (GCP), 169.254.169.254:80/metadata/v1/instance (Azure). suggestion.title: Binary execution from node_modules directory during install
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'multi-stage credential harvester' payload. Typical supply chain attacks stage binaries or wrapped scripts in node_modules. No detection for stage-2 payload execution from package installation context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of binaries (non-JS, non-shell scripts) from node_modules or .bin directories with parent process = npm/node in install context. Second indicator: execution of scripts from node_modules with arbitrary permissions or obfuscation patterns.

suggestion.title: npm package integrity mismatch (expected vs. actual hash)
suggestion.rationale: Article states specific @redhat-cloud-services versions compromised. Detection should flag when installed package hash differs from npm registry manifest or package-lock.json. Covers T1195.002 (Supply Chain compromise) detection at install time.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare SHA256/SHA1 of installed @redhat-cloud-services packages against npm registry manifest or package-lock.json checksums. Flag mismatches during npm install. Correlate with network events fetching from unexpected CDNs or mirrors.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Installation with Obfuscated Payload
suggestion.rationale: Article keywords include 'obfuscation' and 'payload' in context of npm packages; supply-chain malware typically installs via npm install with hidden post-install scripts. Pipeline should detect installation of packages with suspicious post-install hooks or obfuscated code patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install / yarn add processes spawning child processes with suspicious names (powershell, cmd, bash with encoded arguments, curl/wget to external hosts). Correlate npm cache directory writes with network connections within seconds of installation.

suggestion.title: npm Package Exfiltration of Credentials or Environment Variables
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'credential harvesting' in npm context. Malicious packages commonly steal .env files, AWS keys, or CI/CD secrets during installation or at runtime.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm package processes reading .env, .aws/credentials, or CI environment files (BUILD_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, NPM_TOKEN), followed by DNS queries or HTTP POST to non-package-registry domains within the same process tree.

suggestion.title: Worm-like npm Package Self-Propagation via Dependency Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article metadata explicitly cites 'worm propagation' as a threat vector. Self-replicating npm malware injects itself into dependent packages' node_modules or modifies package.json to spread laterally.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for npm processes that modify package.json files outside their own directory, write to parent/sibling node_modules folders, or invoke npm publish/registry commands from a package's install script. Detect version increments in dependent packages shortly after a compromised package installs.

suggestion.title: CI/CD Environment Compromise via npm Package Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'CI/CD persistence' explicitly; npm packages in CI pipelines run with elevated permissions and can persist across builds via cached artifacts or registry poisoning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm package execution in CI runners (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins) that writes to cache directories, modifies CI configuration files (.github/workflows, .gitlab-ci.yml), or exfiltrates repo secrets to external infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Registry Metadata Tampering or Typosquatting Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attack on npm registry often involves fake/similar-named packages or version hijacking. Article discusses 'attack surface' of npm ecosystem, implying registry manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm install of packages with names similar to popular ones (levenshtein distance <3), packages with unusual version jumps, or packages from new publishers installing unusually large binary payloads relative to source code size.

suggestion.title: WordPress process HTTP requests to Steam profiles
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'polls Steam Community profiles for commands' and 'hides command instructions inside Steam Community profile comments'. Needs detection for w3wp.exe, php.exe, or apache processes initiating HTTP requests to steamcommunity.com URLs with repeated cadence.

suggestion.title: WordPress file system modifications preceding process execution
suggestion.rationale: Malware must be installed ('WordPress malware') implying file drop, plugin installation, or theme modification. Article describes two-stage attack with malware persistence on WordPress sites.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation or modification of WordPress plugin files (.php in wp-content/plugins/), theme files (wp-content/themes/), or wp-config.php within 10 minutes followed by child process spawning from web server (w3wp, httpd). Alert if files added post-deployment or modified outside change windows.

suggestion.title: Base64 or URL-encoded command injection from web requests
suggestion.rationale: Article describes commands 'hidden inside Steam Community profile comments'. Commands are likely encoded in comment text and decoded/executed by malware. Need detection for suspicious POST requests or process execution of base64-decoded payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PowerShell or cmd.exe child processes spawned with base64-encoded arguments, or monitor HTTP POST requests to Steam URLs containing base64 blocks in the request body. Correlate with web server process hierarchy.

suggestion.title: Unusual HTTP user-agent or missing headers in Steam requests
suggestion.rationale: Legitimate Steam browsing uses browser user-agents. Malware polling for C2 commands is likely to have atypical user-agent strings (or none) or absence of Referer/Accept headers typical of browser clients.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to Steam that lack browser-typical headers (Accept-Language, Referer, Cache-Control) or have non-browser user-agents (curl, wget, PowerShell, python-requests, etc.). Correlate source IPs with web servers.

suggestion.title: WordPress admin account creation or privilege escalation post-malware
suggestion.rationale: Malware infection of WordPress typically includes creation of backdoor admin accounts or modification of existing user roles to maintain access and execute commands.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WordPress user creation events (wp_users table inserts) or user_meta modifications that grant admin role, especially outside change windows or from non-admin IPs. Alert on creation followed within 1 hour by HTTP requests to Steam profiles.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of WordPress database or config over Steam side-channel
suggestion.rationale: Article implies bidirectional C2 (commands in, results out). C2 side-channel over Steam comments can carry exfiltrated data such as database dumps, WordPress config, or stolen credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect large POST requests from WordPress servers to Steam profiles (>100KB per request) or multiple POST requests in short window to same Steam profile. Monitor for mysqldump or wp-cli export processes preceding Steam HTTP POST activity.

suggestion.title: Dragon Weave C2 Beaconing Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'Dragon Weave' as the threat actor; typical APT campaigns involve C2 callbacks and encrypted communications that should be detectable via network signatures or behavioral patterns. No use case for C2 detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound connections to newly registered or bulletproof-hosted C2 domains with patterns consistent with Dragon Weave infrastructure (e.g., HTTPS on non-standard ports, beaconing intervals, TLS certificate anomalies). Correlate with regional targeting vectors against Czech/Taiwan entities.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Detection in Czech/Taiwan Government Networks
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates breaches of Czech Republic and Taiwan—both government-sector targets. No detection logic generated for inter-host lateral movement, which is standard in APT campaigns post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag RDP/WinRM authentication chains across government networks with Dragon Weave behavioral signatures (e.g., credential reuse, traffic to unusual target hosts, off-hours activity). Combine with suspicious process launches on destination hosts.

suggestion.title: Spear-Phishing and Malicious Document Delivery for Dragon Weave
suggestion.rationale: China-aligned groups commonly use phishing as initial access; article mentions attacks on Czech/Taiwan but provides no detection logic for email-borne compromise vectors. 'Ramp up Attacks' suggests increased phishing volume.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on phishing emails targeting Czech/Taiwan government domains with Office macro payloads, suspicious file extensions, or URLs hosted on newly spun-up domains. Correlate with file execution anomalies (e.g., Office spawning cmd.exe, PowerShell).

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration via Uncommon Protocols
